text: Accurate addresses reduce costs for the Department by reducing the amount of correspondence returned by Canada Post. To avoid a surcharge from Canada Post, addresses in ITRDS must meet the addressing guidelines provided by Canada Post. For more information, refer to Addressing Guidelines Internal link . Addressing Guidelines The most common mistake in address formatting occurs when the apartment or suite information is entered. The correct format for a Canadian address with apartment or suite information requires the apartment or suite number to appear: before the civic address number; with a hyphen in between; without spaces; without the word “Suite”; and without the “#” symbol. Table 1. Address Standards Correct Incorrect 401-70 ROYAL OAK PLAZA NW 401 70 ROYAL OAK PLAZA NW 7-2019 TRAWLEN WAY 7 – 2019 TRAWLEN WAY 2-805 CONCESSION ST 805 CONCESSION ST NO 2 5-302 NORTH RIVER RD SUITE 5, 302 NORTH RIVER ROAD 5-302 NORTH RIVER RD SUITE 5 5-302 NORTH RIVER RD 3-245 MONTREAL RD #3, 245 MONTREAL ROAD When a client has provided their civic address in addition to PO Box information, enter the civic address in the Home address fields and the PO Box information in the Mailing address fields on the Modify Address / Direct Deposit screen. The standard format of a Home address is the following: the client's name; their civic address; and municipality name, province or territory and postal code. The standard format of a Mailing address is the following: the client's name; their civic address or their PO Box number and the station information (if applicable); and municipality name, province or territory and postal code. When a client has provided their civic address in addition to PO Box information and both are within the same community (i.e. they have the same postal code and are in the same town or city), combine and enter the civic address and PO Box information in the Mailing address fields on the Modify Address / Direct Deposit screen. Once a client's address is changed, the old address information is moved to the Address History screen. Preferred official language When you modify a client's address, ensure that the address is entered in their preferred official language, which can be found in the Written Language field on the Client Profile screen in ITRDS . By using the client's preferred official language, the Department complies with the requirements of the Official Languages Act and avoids Official Language complaints. Address Guidelines for a Client's Preferred Language

An address cascade is when an update is made to one account and the change automatically transfers to another related account. The address cascades in ITRDS are based on the interrelationships in the client's account (i.e. related CPP child accounts with the same payee client identifier). Even if the interrelationship is no longer active, a change to the address on one account will continue to cascade to the related account until that relationship is severed or a new address is added to the related account. When changing the address, you must consider: If the client has an interrelated spouse, ensure that the spouse's benefits are not affected by the changes. Address changes for a child under the age of 18 (-18 child) cannot be made on the child's Client Profile screen. They must be made from the account of the person who is receiving the payment on the child's behalf, or on the child's Contact / Applicant screen.

topic_title: Release a suspended CPP benefit Updated
text: You must release a suspended benefit and take appropriate action in the following situations: Table 1. Situation Action A benefit was suspended until the date of death could be determined. It has been determined that the beneficiary has not died or has died some time after the benefit was suspended. If the beneficiary is alive, release the benefit. If the beneficiary has died some time after the benefit was suspended, release the benefit, then add the date of death. ITRDS will terminate the benefit. A benefit was suspended at the request of a beneficiary, who now requests a reinstatement of the benefit. Release the benefit. A benefit was suspended because the beneficiary's address was unknown, and the address has now been confirmed and entered into the system. Release the benefit. A benefit was suspended until a new payee could be determined. A trustee has now been approved. Refer to Trusteeship (Scenario) . Trusteeship (Scenario) Change the payee, then release the benefit. A disability benefit was suspended―pending an assessment of the case―and it is determined that the beneficiary: continues to be disabled; and ceased to be disabled some time after the benefit was suspended. Release the benefit, then terminate it the month after the beneficiary ceased to be disabled. The benefit of a child under 18 years of age was suspended pending determination of who has decision-making responsibility and parenting time of the child―and it has now been determined that: the current payee continues to have decision-making responsibility of the child; or a new payee is now eligible to receive the benefit on behalf of the child. Release the benefit or change the payee before releasing the benefit. The benefit of a child over 18 years of age was suspended on the date when the child left school or university because we were advised they left due to illness and the child has submitted: a Canada Pension Plan Illness Certificate (ISP-1403) form for the period of illness ; and a new Canada Pension Plan Child's Benefit Application and Declaration for a Student Over 18 Years of Age in Attendance at School or University (ISP-1402) form confirming they returned to full-time or part-time study immediately following the period of illness Release the benefit or add the new school declaration information, then release the benefit. A child's benefit was suspended on the date we received notice from a third party (someone other than the child) that the child left school or university, After contacting the child, they have: submitted a ISP-1402 form confirming they did not leave school or university; or confirmed their last date of attendance at school or university. Add the new school declaration information, if applicable, and then release the benefit; or release the benefit and then modify the School declaration screen with the date the child left school or university. The benefit will be terminated.

A legal representative can be one of the following: Table 1. Legal Representative Description An Attorney or Mandatary A Power of Attorney (POA) or mandate is a legal contract authorizing one or more individuals to act on behalf of the grantor or mandator regarding their property or personal care. CPP and OAS benefits are considered properties. Third parties that have been given power to make decisions for personal care only, cannot be accepted as contacts for CPP and OAS clients. Representation Agreements (British Columbia) The province of British Columbia provides authority to third parties named under their Representation Agreement Act to act on behalf of individuals with powers similar to those of a POA. These representations are recognized for CPP and OAS purposes. A Trustee Trusteeship is a legal process that gives an individual or agency the authority and responsibility to make financial decisions on an individual's behalf when they no longer have the capability to manage their affairs. This includes public trustee or Curateur public (in Quebec). For a list of approved public trustees, refer to Approved Public Trustees (Work Tool) . When there is no existing legally binding arrangement in place for another individual or agency to act on behalf of an incapable person, the Department can appoint a trustee to administer the client's CPP and OAS benefits. Approved Public Trustees (Work Tool) A Tutor (Quebec) A court-appointed individual that has the authority and responsibility to make financial decisions on an individual's behalf when they no longer have the capability to manage their affairs. A Committee A court-appointed individual in place of the public trustee, to manage the financial affairs of the incapable individual. A Guardian An individual appointed by the court or by the public trustee to care for and manage all property belonging to the incapable individual or the minor that is not otherwise held in trust. Where there is no legal representative, and no family or friends willing or able to act as a committee or private guardian, the public trustee may be appointed as statutory guardian. A Federal Department Indigenous Services Canada and Veteran Affairs Canada may inform the Department that they now administer the affairs of a client. An Executor / Liquidator (Quebec) An executor or liquidator named in a client's will has the authority to act and communicate on behalf of the estate. If a primary and a secondary executor or liquidator are identified in the will, only the primary executor or liquidator is identified on the payment. If the primary executor or liquidator is unable to carry out the required duties, the benefit can be paid to the secondary executor or liquidator. Evidence must be provided, indicating that the primary executor or liquidator has relinquished all rights as executor. A will can also name joint executors or liquidator. This means that they share equal roles. Estate Administrator An estate administrator appointed by the court when no will exists, has the authority to act and communicate on behalf of the estate. Temporary Representative (Quebec) A court-appointed individual that has the authority to perform a specific act on behalf of an incapable individual. At its discretion, the court may rule on the amount of time the temporary representative has to perform the act. The temporary representative must inform the represented person and the Curateur public once the act is completed. If the required court documents have not been provided, confirmation of the temporary representation can be obtained through the Public register of representation measures Internal link site. This site must be used only to validate that the third party is indeed the legal representative for the incapable individual and only when the third party has issued a request or application with the Department. Public register of representation measures For more information on the types of legal representatives, Legal Representation (Policy)

There are various levels of authority that can be granted to an individual by a client. When the Department receives documentation authorizing an individual, it is important to determine if the authorized representative named in the document is a legal representative or an authorized contact. In other cases, a capable client may grant another individual the authority to communicate on their behalf. These individuals are authorized contacts. For example, if a client requests to change their payment frequency from monthly to annually and wants the August monthly payment to be paid in August instead of being delayed until December, you can adjust the August monthly payment to be issued in August. Cancelling payment feature New You can cancel a non-monthly payable (e.g. quarterly paid) before it is sent to Standard Payment System. This can be done by selecting the Cancel Payment in the Payment History Details screen in CPMS . When you select Cancel Payment of a non-monthly payment, the system generates a supplementary payable for that month with a "Cancelled – Internal – In process to be paid" status. You then have the option to: change the status to pending (to issue it at the next monthly pay run); issue it as a priority payment (to issue it as a daily payment); split the payable (to issue to another payee); or apply it against a receivable. For example, the Cancel Payment option allows you to: stop payments that a client is not entitled to. A client calls, requesting that they receive one monthly payment sooner than the scheduled periodic payment. You have two options: you can either adjust the payment to pending and issue it on the next arrears run; or make it a priority payment and issue it as a daily payment.

topic_title: Is a client who only receives QPP benefits enquiring about the CPP PRB ? New
text: QPP RTR pension recipients aged 60 to 70 who are working or returning to work in Canada outside Quebec and made valid contributions to the CPP may be eligible for a PRB . For more information, Post-Retirement Benefit (Knowledge) Once the Department receives the client's earnings and contributions from Canada Revenue Agency, the CPP PRB for QPP-only clients begins processing. The system-generated letter and response form titled Payment of your Canada Pension Plan Post-Retirement Benefit / Method of payment for your CPP Post-Retirement Benefit (For Quebec Pension Plan Retirement Pension Recipients) (ISP-1019-1/ISP-1019-2) is automatically sent to the client. The client must complete, sign and send back the ISP1019-2 form using the enclosed return envelope. Once the Department receives the completed and signed ISP-1019-2 form, the client's payment destination information is added to their account. Subsequently, the client will receive a PRB Notice of Entitlement and payment for their PRB . Clients may call the Department to inquire about receiving the ISP-1019-1/ISP-1019-2 form and providing their address and direct deposit information. Ongoing monthly PRB payments will be issued separately because QPP-only clients do not receive any other CPP benefits. Therefore, the department requires their direct deposit information or mailing address to process the PRB .

topic_title: Is there a departmental, cross-program, third-party, or related receivable on the client's account in CPMS ? Updated
text: If yes, and there is recovery activity on the account, do not adjust the payment frequency. If an existing periodic payment is processed and a recovery activity is added to the account, the system will automatically revert the payment frequency to monthly on the next monthly pay run. CPMS will consider the recovery start date, not the date when you created the recovery. Therefore, all outstanding payables (supplementary and monthly) that have been accumulated and are marked as "Pending – In process to be paid” will be released to the client. CPMS considers the DOJ withhold start date. Therefore, all outstanding payables (monthly and supplementary) that have been accumulated and are marked "Pending – In process to be paid” in CPMS will be released to the client. For clients entitled to benefits, the standard payment frequency is monthly. For clients entitled to a supplementary payable, the standard payment frequency is weekly. In some cases, clients pay significant bank charges when negotiating their benefit payments with a financial institution. To minimize such expenses, the Department can combine their monthly benefit payments into one larger periodic payment by adjusting the frequency of a client's payment to a non-standard payment frequency. Non-standard payment frequencies can be adjusted to: bi-monthly; quarterly; semi-annually; or annually. Do not offer periodic payments to clients unless their monthly amount falls below the $2.00 threshold. In those cases, you may provide the periodic payment option to the client. Adjust the frequency of payments to bi-monthly, quarterly, semi-annually, or annually based on a request by the client or their authorized legal representative. Once a client has a non-standard payment frequency, it will apply to all payments - even supplementary payables, which are usually issued on a weekly payment frequency. Benefits must be paid at least once a year, and a payment must be issued in the December accounting month to ensure the T4 information is correct. Payments due in a calendar year must be paid during that calendar year. Do not accept payment frequency periods greater than one year. All required non-resident tax and OAS recovery tax withholds must be made from periodic payments.

While a death notification is sufficient to suspend or cancel a pension or benefit, proof of death is required in some situations. Proof may be obtained through documentary evidence or validation against a third-party source. Proof of death may be waived for OAS if certain criteria are met. Although documentary evidence may not be required, it can be requested at any time. A statement of death from a funeral home (e.g. a funeral director's statement of death) is considered an acceptable proof of death. However, an announcement of death (i.e. an obituary) from a funeral home or other source is not an acceptable proof of death. If there is any discrepancy when validating the DOD (e.g. the DOD in ITRDS received from the SIR source differs from the DOD received on a statement of death from a funeral home), you must request additional proof. For more information on documentary evidence required for proof of death and the criteria for waiving or validating the evidence, refer Documentary Evidence—Death (Policy) and Documentary Evidence—Death (Policy) Validate a Proof of Death (Action)

topic_title: Does the death notification meet the criteria to terminate the client's account and process any pension or benefit applications, including post-mortem benefits? Updated
text: When a death notification is received by fax, by phone or by mail, it must contain the following information: the client's SIN or Client Identification number; the client's full name and date of birth; the Date of Death (DOD) and the place where the death occurred; the name, address and phone number of the estate representative or next of kin; and the representative's name, phone number and relationship to the client (if different than above). You must also confirm that the death notification is received from someone other than the applicant (e.g. if the surviving spouse notifies the Department of their spouse's death and then applies for the SVR pension, you must use a source other than the death notification to validate the proof of death). If the death notification meets the criteria above, it may be used to process pension or benefit applications where proof of the DOD is an eligibility requirement (e.g. death benefit, SVR pension, ALWS benefit, or post-mortem applications). The information provided on the death notification must match the information on the application or additional proof will be required. Validate a Proof of Death (Action)

topic_title: Does the deceased individual have a spouse or common-law partner who may be entitled to the ALWS benefit? Updated
text: The ALWS benefit is available to individuals: who are the ages of 60 to 64; who have a low income; who live in Canada; and whose spouse or common-law partner is deceased. topic_title: Is the deceased a payee for a child under the age of 18?
text: If you receive a death notification for a payee of a Surviving Child's benefit or a Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit ( DCCB ) for a child under the age of 18 (-18 child) and the payee is not the disabled contributor, you must suspend the child's benefit based on the Date of Death (DOD). The entitlement to the child's benefit for a -18 child continues, but the benefit remains suspended until new payee information is received. An application form is not required to update the payee information for the child's benefit for a -18 child. However, the new payee must notify the Department that they have decision-making responsibility and parenting time of the child or children. Change in Decision-Making Responsibility and Parenting Time (Scenario)

topic_title: Is there a Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit on a deceased contributor's account?
text: If a Date of Death (DOD) is entered on a disabled contributor's account in ITRDS , any related benefits will end, e.g. Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit ( DCCB ) for a child under the age of 18 (-18 child) or for a child over the age of 18 (+18 child). For the deceased disabled contributor's -18 child to continue receiving benefit payments, the surviving spouse or common-law partner or other individual or agency with decision-making responsibility and parenting time of the surviving child must submit an application or request in writing. SVR Pension Application (Scenario) If a +18 child is in pay for a DCCB and the disabled contributor is deceased, the DCCB will only convert to a Surviving Child's benefit for a +18 child if a Canada Pension Plan Child's Benefit Application and Declaration for a Student Over 18 Years of Age in Attendance at School or University (ISP-1402) form is data captured by the month after death (i.e. the Surviving Child's benefit effective date). If the ISP-1402 form is not data captured by the month after the disabled contributor's death, the DCCB will not automatically convert to a Surviving Child's benefit for a +18 child. The +18 child must submit a Surviving Child's benefit application. For more information, Surviving Child's Benefit Application (Scenario)

topic_title: Results of entering a date of death
text: The same client data is used in each of the following examples: Client name: John Doe Current Benefit Status: In Pay Accounting Month: September 2018 Table 2. Example 3 Dates Rationale and results Date of death (DOD): August 25, 2018 Notification received: September 5, 2018 Client Profile modified: September 6, 2018 Next payment to be issued: September 2018 The DOD is in the current accounting month of September. The DOD is entered in ITRDS before the end of the September accounting month, even though the death occurred in August. After the DOD is entered in ITRDS , the benefit terminates with an end date of August 31, 2018. August is the last month in which the client is entitled to receive a regular monthly payment. ITRDS recognizes that the client is not entitled to the next payment. The September 2018 payment is not issued, and no receivable is created. Table 3. Example 4 Dates Rationale and results DOD: September 2, 2018 Notification received: September 5, 2018 Client Profile modified: September 6, 2018 Next payment to be issued: September 2018 The DOD is in the current accounting month of September. The client is entitled to the September 2018 payment because the client died in September. After the DOD is entered in ITRDS , the benefit terminates with an end date of September 30, 2018. September is the last month in which the client is entitled to receive a regular monthly payment. ITRDS recognizes that the client is not entitled to the next payment (October). The September 2018 payment is issued, and no receivable is created. Table 4. Example 5 Dates Rationale and results DOD: June 2, 2018 Notification received: August 5, 2018 Client Profile modified: September 6, 2018 Next payment to be issued: September 2018 The DOD did not occur in the current accounting month, and a receivable is created. CPMS displays the receivable in the Account Overview screen. After the DOD is entered in ITRDS , the benefit terminates with an end date of June 30, 2018, the month of death. June is the last month the client is entitled to receive a regular monthly payment. The account terminates in the September 2018 accounting month. No payment is issued for September because the death is entered before the end of the current accounting month. When the DOD is entered, a receivable is created for the July and August payments, which should not have been issued to the deceased client.

topic_title: Was a date of death entered on the client's account in error?
text: When it has been determined that a Date of Death (DOD) is entered on a client's account in error, it must be corrected as soon as it is discovered. You must immediately remove the DOD from the client's account and notify the Social Insurance Registry (SIR) and other program areas. For instructions on completing and sending an urgent email to notify the SIR and reinstating any suspended or cancelled benefits, Reporting an Incorrect Date of Death to the Social Insurance Registry (Action) To notify another program, follow your regional procedures.

topic_title: Was the incorrect date of death entered on the client's account? Updated
text: When there is a discrepancy in the Date of Death (DOD) entered on the client's account, you must: ensure the correct DOD has been validated; immediately correct the DOD in the applicable systems; and notify the Social Insurance Registry (SIR) if their DOD is incorrect. The error must be corrected for all programs as soon as it is discovered. If there is a DOD in Cúram and a new DOD is received from ITRDS that has a different month or year: the Death Details evidence will be updated in Cúram, but it will remain in an In Edit status; and a task will be created for staff to review the evidence and request proof of death, if required. For instructions on completing and sending an urgent email to notify the SIR about the discrepancy, refer to Reporting an Incorrect Reporting an Incorrect Date of Death to the Social Insurance Registry (Action) For more information on validating the DOD, Validate a Proof of Death (Action)

Outstanding benefit payments owed at the time of death are paid to the client's estate, another appropriate payee or nominee. To issue a payment to a deceased client's account, a hierarchy must be followed. For more information, Unpaid Benefits at Date of Death for CPP and OAS Pensions (Policy)

Entering a date of death When a date of death is entered into ITRDS , the account will automatically be readjudicated. Any interrelated accounts may also be readjudicated and should be reviewed to ensure accuracy. These readjudications could cause an earnings update or data adjustment, resulting in a payment owing after death or an overpayment on the account. Benefits for a child under the age of 18 unpaid at the time of death When there is a child's benefit payment owing at the time of death, you must determine the payee. If the child under the age of 18 (-18 child) is deceased, any payment owing after death can be issued to the person or agency (designated by the Minister) who had decision-making responsibility of the child immediately before the child's death. If the payee for the -18 children's benefit is deceased, any payment owing on behalf of the child can be issued to whoever assumes decision-making responsibility of the -18 child. If the -18 child has reached age 18 at the date of death of the payee, any unclaimed -18 child's benefit can be paid to the child who is now +18. Children's Benefits—Change in Decision-Making Responsibility and Parenting Time (Policy)

Once the date of death is added or updated on the Birth and Death Details evidence and activated, Cúram will run a reassessment to ensure that the account is in balance. A task will be generated for manual review if any of the following occurs during the reassessment process: the account is not in balance; the marital relationship of the spouse or common-law partner could not be updated; or there is a conflicting date of death received or the existing date of death is removed via the ITRDS Interface. Any interrelated accounts may also be reassessed and must be reviewed to ensure accuracy. These reassessments could result in a payment owing after death or an overpayment on the account. All CPP pensions or benefits and the OAS pension are taxable. However, income-tested benefits (i.e. GIS, ALW , ALWS ) are non-taxable. Tax slips inform clients, the CRA and Revenu Québec of the total amount of benefits paid and any amounts withheld during a calendar year. This includes: Regular benefit payments; Arrears payments; Underpayments; Tax withholds; and Overpayment recovery. For CPP accounts, tax slip information and credit slips originate from CPMS . For OAS accounts, tax slip information originates from Cúram. The reissuing and amending of tax slips are recorded through CPMS or Cúram. A CPP client will receive: a Statement of Canada Pension Plan Benefits T4A(P) (ISP-0136) form for periods when they are in receipt of a CPP pension or benefit and are a resident of Canada; a Statement of Amounts Paid or Credited to Non-residents of Canada NR4 (CPP) (ISP-0139) form for periods when they are in receipt of a CPP pension or benefit and are a non-resident of Canada; or a Reimbursement Of Benefit Paid During A Previous Year (ISP-1611) (credit slip) form when the recovery of an overpayment exceeds the total pension or benefit payments issued during the same calendar year. An OAS client will receive: a Statement of Old Age Security T4A(OAS) (ISP-0137) form for periods when they are in receipt of an OAS pension or an income-tested benefit and are a resident of Canada; a Statement of Old Age Security Pension Paid or Credited to Non-residents of Canada NR4(OAS) (ISP-0138) form for periods when they are in receipt of an OAS pension and/or an income-tested benefit and are a non-resident of Canada. CPP and OAS tax slips are generated at the beginning of January of a given calendar year. Tax slip mailing occurs the year following the tax year (e.g. in 2026 for the 2025 tax year). Clients will receive their tax slips by the end of February. Each year, some accounts are excluded from the automatic annual tax slip bulk mail-out because they do not meet the pre-set criteria. For CPP, these accounts are identified through scans and exception reports, which are used as the basis for specific instruction to staff. This annual instruction outlines the corrective action required to ensure clients who were excluded from the bulk mail-out will receive their correct tax slip by the end of February. Clients can view and print official copies of their tax slips for the current year and the past 6 years through My Service Canada Account (MSCA) for CPP and the Client Portal via their MSCA for OAS. The suspension of a CPP or OAS pension or benefit can occur either through an automated process or through manual intervention. Automatic suspension occurs by the applicable system depending on certain situations. While manual suspension is input by a processor to stop the system from issuing payments to allow for an ongoing eligibility review to occur. Before inputting a manual suspension, you must send a written notice to the client a minimum of 30 days before suspending their pension or benefit. However, a written notice is not required for a suspension if: you cannot locate the client; the client is non-compliant (during CPPD reassessment only); or you are waiting for confirmation of the date of death. text: When you have determined a client's eligibility to the DSB , you must cancel or withdraw the RTR pension in favour of the DSB . If the RTR pension's overpayment exceeds the DSB arrears amount, recover the excess amount owing from the monthly DSB payments. Departmental Receivables (Overpayments) (Scenario)

Effective September 21, 2020, to cancel a CPP pension or benefit, the client must submit a written request within 12 months of the due date of the first payment in the Standard Payment System. If you accept the cancellation request, the client must repay the CPP pension or benefit and all related benefits within 12 months after the Department approves the request. The following examples demonstrate how cancelling a pension or benefit impacts related benefits: Cancelling an RTR pension will terminate the PRB . Cancelling a DSB or PRDB will terminate any associated Disabled Contributor's Child Benefit ( DCCB ). Any federal voluntary tax or non-resident tax amounts withheld for the current tax year can be requested from the CRA and applied against the overpayment. If the cancellation request is received or processed after the year-end cut-off date, the client will be responsible to repay any tax amounts for the previous year. Refer to Tax Withhold—Reimburse or Recover (Scenario) for more information. Terminations can occur automatically by ITRDS or manually by processing staff based on information or documentary evidence received. The DSB and DCCB are automatically terminated by ITRDS . The PRDB is manually terminated by the PRDB Specialized Processing Centre. One of the separated legal spouses is deceased and the other spouse is in pay for an SVR pension from the same deceased spouse. SVR pension If the credit split application is approved, the separated legal spouse's SVR pension ceases at the effective date of approval of the credit split (i.e. the last day of the month in which the credit split application was received or in this case, the month of the event).

The Minister has the authority to refuse or cancel a credit split for a couple that is divorced, legally annulled or separated on or after January 1, 1987, when it is apparent upon data capturing or within 60 days after data capturing the credit split that negatively affects both spouses. When a request to split credits between former spouses upon divorce or annulment is approved, the credit split cannot be withdrawn by either of the individuals. With the exception of the Minister's power to refuse or cancel a credit split if detrimental to both individuals, the division of credits between former spouses upon divorce or annulment is permanent. text: If you simultaneously receive an RTR pension application and CPPD benefits application, you do not need to respond to the client. The applicant is aware of the deferral of the RTR pension's cancellation request until the disability determination is completed. Before the disability determination is completed, a client can also request a general cancellation of the RTR pension. If you receive a general cancellation request within 12 months of the first RTR payment, you must defer the cancellation until the disability determination is complete. You can contact and advise the client, if applicable. If the client insists on stopping their RTR pension, you can suspend the benefit payments until the disability determination is completed. You must release the RTR pension payments immediately if requested by the client. Cancel, Reinstate, Release, Suspend or Terminate a Benefit in ITRDS (Action)

topic_title: Termination of an SVR pension paid to a separated legal spouse after a credit split is approved with the same separated legal spouse
text: Effective January 1, 2025, when a credit split application is received and approved for separated legal spouses, there is no eligibility to a CPP SVR pension when one of the separated legal spouses dies. If a separated legal spouse is receiving an SVR pension and the Department receives a credit split application on or after January 1, 2025 for the same deceased separated legal spouse, the SVR pension ceases as of the effective date of the credit split approval. This applies regardless of whether it is the estate of the deceased contributor or the living separated legal spouse who applies for the credit split. An SVR pension that remains in pay awaiting processing of the credit split could result in an SVR pension overpayment. This overpayment is valid and collectable.

A client may request to change the effective date of a CPP RTR pension or an OAS pension because they want to receive the pension at an earlier or later date. You can change the effective date of a CPP RTR pension or an OAS pension when requested by the client in writing if the new effective date is 12 months or less from the date of receipt of application and the client has not received any payments. You can also change the effective date of a CPP, CPPD or OAS pension or benefit in the following situations: a protected date has been provided by using an International Social Security Agreement; a claim of incapacity is approved; a claim of erroneous advice or administrative error is approved; or it is recommended following an investigation by the Integrity Services Branch. For all other situations, the date of receipt of the application or the date of death determines the effective date. An RTR effective date cannot be earlier than the month after the receipt date of the application for applicants aged 60 to 64. RTR and OAS applicants 65 and over can receive retroactive benefits for up to 12 months if they qualify, but not for any months before they reached age 65. Requests for change to an effective date must be made in writing. topic_title: Change of address from Canadian to foreign or foreign to Canadian
text: If the client's home address changes permanently from a Canadian address to a foreign address, you may have to stop a federal voluntary tax withhold or update the non-resident tax withhold. Clients entitled to CPP or OAS benefits who are residing in another country can receive their payments by foreign direct deposit or by paper cheque if it is supported in the country in which the client resides. To determine if a country can support foreign direct deposit or paper cheques, refer to Countries of the world for a payment in the Standard Payment System Internal link . Countries of the world for a payment in the Standard Payment System CPP pension and benefits CPP clients are entitled to receive their CPP pensions and benefits, even when residing in a foreign country. There are no legislative or operational restrictions to send payments to a client's foreign address or foreign direct deposit account. There are only the tax implications mentioned above. OAS pension and benefits For OAS, non-portable OAS pensions and income-tested benefits (i.e. the GIS, ALW and ALWS ) cannot be paid outside of Canada for more than 6 months and the client may have to re-establish eligibility when they return to Canada. When a client requests a change of address, you must determine if the change is temporary or permanent as this will affect the requirements to resume payments when they return. Advise the client that their departure from Canada can result in a suspension of their benefits or the transfer of their file to International Operations. For more information, Client Departs from or Returns to Canada (Scenario)

text: When International Operations (IO) receives correspondence from a foreign institution that includes the client's address, they will advise the applicable processing site if the address differs from OAS or CPP records unless an information-sharing restriction is in place. IO will not validate the new address. You must contact the client to confirm that they have moved before making any changes in the applicable system. When there is an information-sharing restriction in place and the address information originates from any other source (e.g. client, next of kin), the information may be shared with all programs.

The mailing address is the location where the Department will send a client's correspondence and paper cheques if the client has not requested direct deposit. A mailing address is required for each client account. A client's home and mailing address can be the same. While a client's account can only have one home address, it can have multiple mailing addresses. For example, a client receiving both CPP and OAS benefits can request that the Department send correspondence for each benefit to a different mailing address. If you receive a request to send correspondence to a Canadian address and the client is residing outside of Canada, you must update the mailing address with the Canadian address information. This will not change the payment destination if the client receives benefit payments by direct deposit. This will not alter the Non-Resident Tax which is determined by the home address. For OAS and CPP pension and benefit payments, an account can have: the same payment destination for both; and different payment destinations for OAS and CPP payments. A payment destination can be: the client or their legal representative's mailing address if they receive payments by paper cheques; or the client or their legal representative's financial institution if they receive payments by direct deposit. The Government of Canada seeks to issue all federal government payments, including CPP and OAS benefits, by direct deposit. OAS and CPP payments can only be deposited into: the client's bank account; a bank account held jointly by the client and another person; or the bank account of a legal representative appointed to administer an incapable individual's financial affairs (e.g. a trustee, bulk payee, committee, or guardian). For more information, refer to Legal Representation (Policy) . The most common reasons are: the client lives in a remote location or country where the direct deposit service is not offered; the agency or provincial department (e.g. the public trustee) does not maintain a bank account for direct deposit; the client has a low income and cannot afford a bank account due to banking fees; and the financial institution refuses to open a bank account for a client.

topic_title: Recovery of a tax withhold after the final year-end update
text: After the year end cut-off date has passed, the net amount of a cancelled payment is reflected on the following year’s tax slip or credit slip. As a result, tax slip adjustments are not to be made for the previous year. As money withheld for the tax payment has already been sent to the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), only the net amount of the cancelled payment can be applied against the overpayment. You must request funds sent to CRA for the tax from the client or the estate, not from the Chief Financial Officer Branch (CFOB). Example The beneficiary died in November but was paid in December. Their account was cancelled in the January accounting month, but their December payment was returned and cancelled the following February, after the financial year end cut off. The net amount of the cancelled payment will be applied against the receivable amount in CPMS. Apply the net amount of the cancelled cheque, if applicable, against the overpayment amount. Refer to Adjust a Departmental Receivable Amount in CPMS . Adjust a Departmental Receivable Amount in CPMS Send a letter to the client or the client's estate to request the refund of the tax deduction, since you cannot request a reimbursement from CFOB. Include an explanation stating the amount of the tax withheld for the month of non-entitlement that appears on the previous year's tax slip, and can be claimed as a deduction when the client or estate prepares an income tax return for the current year. No further action is required. Update the client's notes in ITRDS to record details of your actions or decisions made on the account. Refer to ITRDS Notes—Review, Add and Delete (Action) . (KA-01651 Snippet 4.0 content. Do not modify or delete.) If the requested Federal Voluntary Tax Withhold (FVTW) or Non-Resident Tax (NRT) refund amount is received from the client, CFOB will apply the amount against the balance of the overpayment.

topic_title: Recovery of a withhold before the final year-end update where only the net portion is returned
text: You can only recover a Federal Voluntary Tax Withhold (FVTW) or Non-Resident Tax (NRT) from the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and apply it to an overpayment in the current year. You must do it before the year’s final update and before the tax slips are issued. After the final update, no further recovery can be made from the next remittance to the CRA for the previous year’s debt. Example The client died in October but was paid in November. The estate of the deceased client refunds the Department only the net portion of the overpayment amount in the following situations: Their account was cancelled in the December accounting month. Their November payment (gross amount $400.00, tax deduction $50.00, net amount $350.00) was negotiated. An overpayment amount of $400.00 is set up. A cash refund for the net November payment amount of $350.00 is received from the estate in late December, before the financial year-end cut-off. The Chief Financial Officer Branch (CFOB) will receive the incoming payment of $350.00 and apply the amount received against the receivable amount. You must: Determine how the payment was returned. For a cash refund in the Public Sector Collections and Disbursements system, refer to View Incoming Payments in CPMS . For payments returned through the Standard Payment System (SPS), refer to Returned Payment . View Incoming Payments in CPMS Returned Payment Request a reimbursement of the FVTW or NRT from the CRA by completing a Request for Manual Adjustment of Income Tax (ISP1607) form. Scan and email the form as directed on the form. See details Bring forward (BF) the work item. Refer to Bring Forward (BF) (Action) . (KA-01654 Snippet 7.0 content. Do not modify or delete.) You will receive an acknowledgement email when the form has been reviewed by CPP Operations National Headquarters (NHQ). You will be contacted if the form is incomplete or clarification is required and then asked to resubmit. When you receive the acknowledgement email from CPP Operations NHQ, refer to Adjust a Departmental Receivable Amount in CPMS . Use the reason "Withhold Adjustment Cancelled Payment". Adjust a Departmental Receivable Amount in CPMS Inform the client or the estate, in writing, of the amount of the FVTW or NRT that was recovered from the CRA applied against the overpayment. When an FVTW or an NRT is sent to the C RA Updated CPP monthly tax withhold dollar amounts are sent to the CRA by the 15th of the following month. The exception is December, when they are remitted around January 10. The Chief Financial Officer Branch (CFOB) sends taxes withheld from payments to the CRA. The total amount of tax withheld from a client during a calendar year is shown on the client’s annual tax slip. Dates are very important in determining how to process a request for reimbursement of income tax withheld from benefit payments. The tax slip and the CRA remittance adjust automatically if the cancelled payment is recorded in the Standard Payment System before the final update for the year. The January CPP Production schedule will provide the cut-off date for cancelled payment updates to tax slips in CPMS. If the cancelled payment is not recorded before the final year-end update: the client's tax slip is not adjusted; and the income tax amount withheld for any period of non-entitlement to a benefit is not recovered from the following year’s remittance to the CRA. As a result, the net amount of the cancelled payment is reflected on the following year’s tax slip or credit slip. Tax slip adjustments are not to be made for the previous year. Recovery of an FVTW or NRT from the CRA You may need to recover an FVTW or an NRT from the CRA and apply the amount towards an overpayment in the following situations: the beneficiary died and was paid benefits after the month of death; the beneficiary voluntarily cancelled their benefits and must repay them (the CRA will only reimburse tax amounts for the current year); the beneficiary is alive and had no entitlement to the benefits that were paid to them; or there was an existing overpayment and the FVTW or NRT should not have been withheld and remitted to the CRA . A departmental overpayment takes priority over an income tax withhold. For more information, refer to the Priority of Withholds—Set-offs, Withholds, Deductions, Reimbursements and Overpayments policy article. Priority of Withholds—Set-offs, Withholds, Deductions, Reimbursements and Overpayments You may need to recover an FVTW or NRT from the CRA and the amount may need to be reimbursed to the client in the following situations: the FVTW was applied against the wrong client; or the withhold amount was encoded as a greater amount than the client requested. You must submit a Request for Manual Adjustment of Income Tax (ISP1607) form before CFOB's financial year-end cut-off date to recover an FVTW or NRT amount. CFOB advises the network of the date, which is usually between January 5 and 10, but changes each year. After CFOB's year-end cut-off date has passed, the department cannot recover any amounts sent to the CRA. Tax slip adjustments are not to be made for previous years. For more information, refer to the policy on Voluntary Tax Withholds and Voluntary Deductions

A benefit is automatically readjudicated when a change to a client's information affects their benefit eligibility or entitlement. The changes may include: data capture sessions (completed and new); benefit status; interrelationship information (modifying or deleting periods or relationships); earnings information, refer to Record of Earnings Updates to CPP Benefits (Knowledge) ; Record of Earnings Updates to CPP Benefits (Knowledge) school attendance periods; survivor disability periods; personal client data (change to the date of birth, date of death or address); change in effective date; account that is in pay at less than the maximum rate supported with an application for the Child Rearing Provision; change as a result of a request for Credit Split; change as a result of a request for Pension Sharing; conversion of benefits ( DSB to the RTR pension); or record change (consolidate or deconsolidate accounts). When a client's data is updated (e.g. change to the date of birth) and the updated information directly affects benefit eligibility and entitlement, a readjudication is required and an event is created. When the event is created, ITRDS identifies the event and determines when and how it must be managed. Survivor under the age of 35 before January 1, 2019 When a survivor applicant is under the age of 35 before January 1, 2019, at the time of the contributor's death and is without a child or a disability qualifier, there is no pension payable until a qualifier is present or until the survivor reaches 65 years of age. When the SVR pension application is processed, the benefit displays the Eligible, No Entitlement status. ITRDS automatically readjudicates a SVR pension whenever qualifier information (dependency or disability) is updated. When a survivor reaches 65 years of age, the SVR pension is also automatically readjudicated. However, if the survivor is not in pay for a RTR pension, ITRDS changes the Eligible, No Entitlement status to the Suspended status with Requires SDA Intervention in the Reason field or Reason(s) field. This allows you to add a proper address and payment destination before release. Although the SVR pension displays the Suspended status, you must not use the Modify Benefits screen to release the benefit. After you have updated the address information correctly, you must click Re-adjudicate on the Benefits screen. Since the adjudication is triggered manually, the status automatically updates to In pay . Credit Split—Interrelationship data amended with subsequent benefit adjudication When you modify the spousal interrelationship data used in a completed Credit Split, a pop-up message notifies you that a readjudication of the Credit Split may be required. Since not all changes affect the Credit Split (i.e. may not affect the range of division), readjudication of the application is not always required. When a primary benefit (i.e. DSB or RTR pension) is processed, any existing Credit Split is also readjudicated. Any change to a DSB or RTR pension start or end date (e.g. beginning or terminating the benefit) readjudicates the Credit Split. This ensures that no earnings are divided during a period of benefit payment and that benefit rates are properly calculated. When both above scenarios occur on a client account, ITRDS cannot successfully readjudicate the Credit Split without your validation. The Credit Split is updated to display the Approved status with Requires SDA Intervention in the Reason field or Reason(s) field. Credit Split adjudication results are displayed on the Credit Split screen. Since Re-adjudicate is not displayed, you must access the completed Credit Split data capture session, update all mandatory fields and then select Submit . Benefit denial and data changes When a benefit is denied for any reason, ITRDS does not automatically change the status without your verification. When an application is denied, appeal rights are extended. Generally, a decision to deny an application can only be reversed through specific circumstances (e.g. reconsideration or appeal, administrative error) or through a new application. As a result, denial decisions cannot be reversed or changed without review. When a benefit has been denied and a readjudication determines that a benefit may be payable, ITRDS updates the benefit to display the Denied status with the Requires SDA Intervention in the Reason field or Reason(s) field. This allows you to determine if you have the authority to change the decision from Denied . Adding or modifying earnings CPP benefits that are denied for insufficient earnings may be affected when you add or update earnings. Following a change to the client's earnings, you may need to do a manual readjudication. Earnings—Add or Modify (Action)

topic_title: Client regains the ability to manage their own affairs Updated
text: When appointing a trustee, you must determine if you need to review the case later if the client's condition improves and terminates the trusteeship, if required. You must add a note in ITRDS and bring forward the account to the expected date of improvement indicated on the Certificate of Incapability-OAS/CPP (ISP-3505) form, if one was provided. When the trustee informs the Department of the client's regained ability to manage their affairs, you must request a new ISP-3505 form. Once the client's regained ability has been confirmed on the new ISP-3505 form, remove the trustee from the client's file and issue future payments directly to the client. If the public trustee is the appointed trustee, the Department will accept a letter from them stating that the client has regained the ability to manage their own affairs and that their trusteeship has ended on a specific date. You must remove the trustee's name from the client's file and issue future payments directly to the client. If the client informs the Department that they have regained the ability to manage their own affairs, contact the trustee and request a new ISP-3505 form.

Provincial or territorial courts can send the Department documents—such as court orders and certificates—appointing one or more individuals to act on behalf of an incapable client. The court appoints a guardian or committee only after considering factors that include whether the incapable individual had a personal directive in place before becoming incapable (e.g. an enduring power of attorney). Therefore, the guardian or committee takes precedence over all others who applied to become trustees on behalf of a CPP and OAS client. As a result, the Department will accept a court-appointed guardian or committee to act on behalf of a CPP and OAS client. Some court orders may pertain only to the personal care of the incapable individual and not their property. When a Department-appointed trusteeship ends for any reason other than death of the trustee, the trustee must return to the Department any CPP or OAS funds that they: received on behalf of the incapable individual; and have not yet disbursed to the incapable individual or expended on their behalf. This amount must be evident on the final accounting report the trustee is required to provide. Once received by the Department, any funds for which there is entitlement are to be issued to the client or their estate by priority payment. When the client dies, any type of trustee that was in place while the individual was alive ends and legal representation for the estate takes over. When the trustee dies, no effort is to be made to recover unexpended funds, as this becomes a civil matter between the new trustee and the former trustee's estate. For more information, including a complete list of the reasons a trusteeship could be terminated, Legal Representation (Policy)

topic_title: Trustee appointed by the Department Updated
text: When a person, agency or institution requests to act as a trustee for a client, the Department can only grant the appointment based on medical evidence indicating the client is incapable of managing their affairs due to infirmity, mental incapability or other causes. Municipalities, non-profit organizations and charitable organizations are only eligible to act as trustees for seniors when the following three criteria are met: the client must be incapable; the client must be homeless or at imminent risk of being homeless; and their benefits become payable at the age of 65. To appoint a trustee, the Department must receive the following completed forms: For an individual trustee: Certificate of Incapability-OAS/CPP (ISP-3505) form; and Agreement to administer benefits under the Old Age Security Act and/or the Canada Pension Plan by a Private Trustee (ISP-3506) form. For an agency trustee: ISP-3505 form; and Agreement to administer benefits under the Old Age Security Act and/or the Canada Pension Plan by an Agency or Institution (ISP-3507) form. For more information about when to appoint a trustee and any requirements that must be met, Legal Representation (Policy) Accounting from a Department-appointed trustee Department-appointed trustees are required to account for all CPP and OAS benefits received to ensure the monies are spent for the benefit of the client. The Trustee's Accounting Report (ISP-3509) form is required from the Department-appointed trustee at least every 2 years from the date of the last accounting request. A registered charity, non-profit organization or municipality appointed by the Department to administer benefits on behalf of a senior who is homeless or at imminent risk of being homeless, is expected to account yearly for monies received. These safeguards help to ensure that benefit payments are for the use and benefit of the client. You must also send an ISP-3509 form for completion in the following situations: there is a change in trustee; the client reports that they have regained the capability to manage their own affairs; the death of the client; the death of the trustee; there is doubt that the monies are being disbursed for the benefit of the client; or the Department receives a complaint that the trustee is not administering the benefits for the benefit of the client. Trustees must maintain yearly records of the monies received and spent for the client. If the Department deems it necessary to obtain an accounting report outside of the regularly scheduled reports, the trustee must be readily able to provide the requested documentation for the applicable years. CPP accounts CPP trustees are recorded in ITRDS as accounting or non-accounting to identify if an accounting report is required. A person or agency can legally act on behalf of an individual when it has been proven that the individual is incapable of handling their own affairs. This trustee can apply for, receive and administer benefits on behalf of the incapable individual. An individual cannot be considered incapable simply because they are: residing in a nursing home or institution; physically or terminally ill; or dependent on others for financial assistance. Trustees can be appointed by: a Canadian provincial, territorial or federal court; or the Department when the client is incapable of managing their own affairs and there is no: existing legally binding arrangement in place for another individual or agency to act on the client's behalf; or legal representative appointed under a provincial, territorial or federal court to act on behalf of an incapable client. Provinces and territories have their own jurisdiction for managing an individual's care, finances and property. Power of Attorney Legislation by Provincial or Territorial Statutes (Work Tool) A public trustee or public curator (in Québec) can be appointed to act on behalf of CPP and OAS clients in its care. For a list of provincial and territorial public trustees and curators, refer to the following applicable procedure: For CPP, refer to Approved Public Trustees (Work Tool) . Approved Public Trustees (Work Tool) For OAS, refer to the Bulk Pay/public trustee section of Third Party Contacts—Add, View, Edit, and Delete in Cúram (Action) . Third Party Contacts—Add, View, Edit, and Delete in Cúram (Action) Department-appointed trustees are required to account for all CPP and OAS benefits received to ensure the monies are spent for the benefit of the client. Court-appointed trustees are not accountable to the Department for benefits received. Protection Mandates and Tutorships (Québec) In Québec, a protection mandate is required to name one or more individuals to manage the mandator's property if they become incapable. The protection mandate can be produced on its own or included with a general Power of Attorney (POA) or mandate, while the person is capable. In both situations, the protection mandate will have to be homologated to become effective, which is a confirmation by the court of the incapability of the mandator. It involves assessments of the person's condition by medical professionals. Once the protection mandate has been homologated, the appointed mandatary: stays the same, but with new powers given by the protection mandate (if they were already acting as attorney or mandatary from a previous general POA or mandate document); or replaces the former attorney or mandatary (if a different third party was previously identified in the general POA or mandate document); or replaces a previously appointed Department trustee; and is added to the client's account in the same manner as a trustee, and benefits are redirected to the mandatary. You must confirm that all conditions have been met and that the required documentation has been received by the Department for a protection mandate to be valid. If an existing protection mandate is not in place when the client becomes incapable, a third party can be appointed by the court as a tutor to manage the incapable person's affairs. Prior to November 2022, this was referred to as a Curator. Once documentation for the tutorship has been validated, this legal representative is added to the client's account in the same manner as a trustee, and benefits are redirected to the tutor. As they are appointed by the court, mandataries (under a protection mandate) and tutors (tutorships) are not accountable to the Department. For more information on Protection Mandates and Tutorship, Legal Representation (Policy)

For example, if a pension or benefit is in pay for OAS and the name is correct, CPP must use the same name and vice versa. Name Mismatch Between Programs A name modification is required to: correct the spelling of the given name or surname; correct a name mismatch between all programs; add an initial; change a title; change a family name because of marriage or remarriage (not applicable in Quebec); revert from a married name to a name at birth; legally change a name; or correct an unexpected client name change following a QPP system update. topic_title: POA or mandate start date and end date
text: The POA or mandate document goes into effect on the date it was signed and witnessed, unless it is a springing POA or mandate that is not in force until the specified event occurs. There are many reasons a POA or mandate could end, such as: the death of the grantor; the attorney or mandatary no longer wishes to act on the client's behalf; or the bankruptcy of the grantor. For more information regarding the start and end dates, including a complete list of the reasons a POA or mandate could end, Legal Representation (Policy)

topic_title: Power of Attorney or mandate Updated
text: A Power of Attorney (POA) document is a legal contract between the client (grantor) and any authorized individual (attorney) named in the document. In Quebec, a Power of Attorney can also be called a mandate, in which the legal contract binds the client (mandator) and their legal representative (mandatary). When it is determined that the document is valid for CPP and OAS purposes, the legal representative has all the rights and responsibilities of the person they represent. The client can only grant POA or mandate to a third party when they are mentally capable and in control of their own affairs. If the client is not mentally capable, a trustee or tutor (in Quebec) may be appointed to administer their affairs. For more information, Trusteeship (Scenario) The Department will not accept different POA or mandate documents for the same grantor or mandator. There can only be one POA or mandate per client for both OAS and CPP. If two POA or mandate documents are received naming different parties, the documents will not be accepted. Confirmation as to which POA or mandate document to use for both programs is required. When an attorney or mandatary is on file, the client may continue to act on the account. The existence of a POA or mandate does not necessarily mean the client is no longer able or no longer wishes to administer their own affairs. You must review the document carefully to: identify who is being appointed attorney or mandatary. If there is more than one individual appointed, confirm whether they must act together (jointly) or can act alone (severally); identify if there is an alternate attorney or mandatary named, if the primary attorney or mandatary is unwilling or unable to act or dies. The Department will require written notification of the primary's resignation or proof of their death before the Department will recognize the alternate's authority to act on behalf of the grantor or mandator; ensure the type of POA or mandate document is recognized for the administration of CPP and OAS pension and benefits; ensure the type of POA or mandate document is recognized for the administration of CPP and OAS pension and benefits. The POA or mandate must be intended for property, not personal care; determine if the attorney or mandatary's authority will continue or end if the grantor or mandator becomes incapable. A POA or mandate in Quebec is not enduring. A protection mandate is required to name one or more individuals to manage the mandator's property if they become incapable and must be homologated (approved by a court) to become effective. Refer to Trusteeship (Scenario) for more information on protection mandates; and Trusteeship (Scenario) ensure that any required supporting documentation has been received by the Department. For more information, Legal Representation (Policy)

topic_title: Rights and responsibilities of an attorney or mandatary
text: The attorney or mandatary can: sign application forms; receive payments and correspondence on the client's behalf, including requests for duplicate payments. Refer to Duplicate or Replacement Payment (Scenario) ; Duplicate or Replacement Payment (Scenario) request information from the client's file via verbal and written requests, including written requests under the Privacy Act , using a Personal Information Request (TBC350-0058) form; sign a Consent to Communicate Information to an Authorized Person (ISP-1603) form, an Authorization to Communicate Information - Canada Pension Plan (ISP-1606) form or an Authorization to communicate Information - Old Age Security (ISP-3015) form to authorize a third party to obtain information on an ongoing basis or once a year. This information assists the attorney or mandatary in administering the client's CPP and OAS accounts. This does not allow the third party to make changes on the client's file. Refer to Third Party Contact—Non-Payee (Scenario) ; Third Party Contact—Non-Payee (Scenario) add or change an address or direct deposit information. If adding or changing direct deposit information, it must be to the client's bank account or a joint account with the client's name unless a homologated protection mandate is received. If a protection mandate is accepted, the mandatary is considered a trustee and the client's benefits are redirected to the mandatary. For more information regarding protection mandates, refer to Trusteeship (Scenario) ; or Trusteeship (Scenario) request reconsiderations. The attorney or mandatary must inform the Department of anything that can affect the client's eligibility for CPP and OAS benefits (e.g. updates to a CPP disability client's medical condition, residence status for OAS or death of the client). For more information, Legal Representation (Policy)

topic_title: Types of POA or mandate documents
text: Type Description Enduring Power of Attorney (POA) An enduring POA document remains in effect and the attorney continues to act if the grantor becomes incapable after appointing the attorney. Proof of the incapability is not required for the attorney to continue acting on behalf of the client. The client must sign the POA document before they become incapable. This provision does not apply to mandate documents established in Quebec. A protection mandate is required to name one or more individuals to manage the mandator's property if they become incapable. For more information regarding protection mandates in Quebec, refer to Trusteeship (Scenario) . Trusteeship (Scenario) General POA or Mandate A general POA or mandate document normally remains in effect until the grantor becomes incapable of managing their affairs. However, some older general POA documents contain a clause that the attorney will continue to act even if the grantor becomes incapable. Every POA document must be reviewed carefully for the powers, conditions and restrictions. Springing POA or mandate A springing POA or mandate document is not effective until the date a specific event detailed in the document occurs. The event can be any event described by the grantor or mandator (e.g. when the client becomes incapable, a specific date, client is out of Canada, etc.). Proof may be required to confirm that the event has taken place before the attorney or mandatary can exercise their authority (e.g. proof of departure from Canada). A springing event of incapability does not apply to mandate documents established in Quebec. A protection mandate is required to name one or more individuals to manage the mandator's property if they become incapable. For more information regarding protection mandates in Quebec, Trusteeship (Scenario) Trusteeship (Scenario) Special or limited POA or mandate This type limits or restricts the authority to specific duties (e.g. for banking purposes only). You cannot accept this type of POA or mandate for CPP or OAS purposes. Protection Mandate In Quebec, a protection mandate is required to name one or more individuals to manage the mandator's property in the event that they become incapable. The protection mandate can be produced on its own, while the person is capable, or included with a general POA or mandate. In both situations, the protection mandate will have to be homologated (approved by a court) to become effective. In the absence of an existing protection mandate, a tutor may be appointed by the court through a tutorship. A mandatary under a protection mandate and a tutor have the same authority as a trustee. Representation Agreements (British Columbia) The province of British Columbia (BC) has both a Power of Attorney Act and a Representation Agreement Act . The Representation Agreement Act provides authority to third parties to act on behalf of individuals who do not meet the capability requirements to appoint an attorney under the BC Power of Attorney Act . These representation agreements are treated like an enduring POA and are recognized for CPP and OAS purposes if it includes the following statement: Routine management of the adult's financial affairs, including, subject to the regulations, receipt and deposit of pension and other income. Proof of incapability is not required. Benefits continue to be paid to the client, despite any future incapability of the client. If the client has both a POA document and Representation Agreement in place, and a conflict or inconsistency arises between them, the authority given in the POA document will take precedence. It is important to record this information in the ITRDS client notes. For more information about the various types of POA, mandates or agreements and their conditions, Legal Representation (Policy)

Unclaimed payable for a -18 child's benefit In cases where a -18 child's benefit is retroactive and no payee exists for a period of entitlement, CPMS will identify this payable as Unclaimed with an assigned role of No Payee . When you issue an unclaimed payable, CPMS creates a new payable to the payee and an unclaimed receivable for the same amount. In CPMS , it is important to distinguish the difference between a payment and a payable: A payment is any issued monies. A payable is unreleased money owed to the client. Payables are entitlements that have been established, but not yet issued. Payables are modifiable until they are set to Completed status. CPMS sends the payment file to the Standard Payment System (SPS) to issue any supplementary payables according to the National CPP Production Schedule. On July 10, 2024, the Payment Frequency function was added to CPMS so that accurate information can be displayed to My Service Canada Account (MSCA) clients with payment frequency other than monthly. For more information, Periodic Payment (Scenario) When SPS issues the money, the payable will be displayed in CPMS as a payment. Monthly entitlements are also payables. However, they are payables for only a fraction of a minute (entitlement is not established until after the month ends). There will be a separate monthly payment run for bulk payments to public trustees. It will have the same payment due date as the regular monthly payments. Supplementary payables with a payable status of Pending , where the payee is a public trustee, are included in the monthly bulk net pay process. When the payee is a public trustee, the payable is actioned or viewed on the beneficiary's account as you cannot access the trustee's account. Once the payment run has been completed, you will be able to review payment information through accessing the Payment History screen under the beneficiary's account. When a Bulk Pay/Public Trustee role is added to the Contact / Applicant screen in ITRDS , there will be a new client identifier assigned to the payee in CPMS . All CPP payments issued with the same client identifier will be merged and issued as one regular bulk payment to the payee, instead of individual payments.

Individual calculation In CPMS , there is no functionality to automatically adjust the recovered amount of a receivable when a payable is created. Each action taken in ITRDS sends an individual calculation to CPMS . Multiple calculations If a single action in ITRDS causes multiple calculations to occur, CPMS combines the amounts and creates either one payable or one receivable.
When a payable is created in CPMS , the account has a credit (money owed to the client). The Department issues these payables to the beneficiary or payee and/or applies them to existing receivables.

ITRDS is the system of record for CPP benefits. It sends monetary information to CPMS . CPMS creates the payment files and manages the monetary transactions of these benefits. CPMS sends the payment files to the Public Services and Procurement Canada Standard Payment System to produce the payments. A client is a payee, a contributor, a beneficiary or a debtor. Every client has a client identifier in CPMS . The system links the beneficiary to a contributor, a payee or a debtor, if one exists.

text: Review the client's account to determine if the conversion of benefits will occur automatically in the system (i.e. without an application and using the information already on file) or if confirmation of information (e.g. address and payment destination) or an application is required. This will depend on the following conditions: the current ALW or ALWS benefit status (e.g. eligible and entitled, eligible but not entitled); the number of years of residence in Canada at the time of approval of the ALW or ALWS benefit; and the lifetime renewal designation. When the conversion of benefits does not occur automatically in the system, the client may be required to complete one of the following, depending on their situation: the Conversion Application (OAS/GIS) (ISP-3045) form; the Application for the Old Age Security Pension and the Guaranteed Income Supplement (ISP-3550) form; or the OAS, Conversion of benefits, Confirm Existence (ISS-0629) letter, if you are unable to reach the client by phone to confirm their address and direct deposit information. Conversion— ALW or ALWS to the OAS pension and GIS (Policy) Cúram will automatically convert a client's ALW or ALWS benefit to an OAS pension and the GIS when they reach age 65 if the following conditions are met: The client has 40 years of residence in Canada as of their most recent ALW or ALWS benefit application, determined by overrides or residence period evidence, in this order. The ALW or ALWS benefit is not suspended; and The client is eligible and entitled to an amount greater than $0 for the ALW or ALWS benefit in the current calendar month; or The client's account was not migrated from a legacy system and: they are eligible but not entitled (including excess income); and they meet the conditions outlined in the policy to waive the requirement to confirm the client's existence and information.
