text: Cúram automatically processes conversions from the ALW or ALWS benefit to the OAS pension and the GIS for clients who meet the eligibility criteria at age 65 and do not require further review. However, for cases requiring manual intervention, Cúram generates a task for manual review as follows: Table 2. Tasks for manual review Task Type Timing of task creation Criteria for task creation OAS-Application - Conversion Review 64 and 9 months On the first day of the month that the client turns 64 and 9 months, Cúram will create a task for review if the following criteria are met: The client is eligible for the ALW or ALWS benefit (regardless of entitlement); The client had less than 40 years of Canadian residence at their ALW or ALWS benefit approval date (assessed through overrides if present); There are no OAS/GIS Application Details; The client has an ALW / ALWS Conversion page and the Conversion Status is set to Pending ; and The account is not suspended. OR The client is eligible but not entitled (or entitled to $0) for the ALW or ALWS benefit; The client's ALW or ALWS benefit account was migrated from a Legacy system; The client had 40 years of Canadian residence at their ALW or ALWS benefit approval date (assessed through overrides if present); There are no OAS/GIS Application Details; The client has an ALW / ALWS Conversion page and the Conversion Status is set to Pending ; and The account is not suspended. OAS-Application - Conversion Review 65 years On the first day of the month that the client turns 65 years of age, Cúram will create a task for review if the following criteria are met: The client is eligible but not entitled (or entitled to $0) for the ALW or ALWS benefit; The client was eligible and entitled to an ALW or ALWS benefit with entitlement over $0 in the month they turned 64 and 9 months; The client's ALW or ALWS benefit account was migrated from a Legacy system; The client had 40 years of Canadian residence at their ALW or ALWS benefit approval date (assessed through overrides if present); There are no OAS/GIS Application details; The client has an ALW / ALWS Conversion page and the Conversion Status is set to Pending ; and The account is not suspended. OAS Intake - Conversion 3045 Once captured in Cúram When a Conversion Application (OAS/GIS) (ISP-3045) form is received, an Application Case is not created like other applications. The review and processing of the application occur on the Integrated Case, using the ALW / ALWS Conversion page. These tasks must be reviewed as a priority to ensure that the required information is obtained or that the ISP-3045 form has been sent or received, if applicable, so the conversion of benefits can proceed in Cúram where possible.

text: Reimbursement of DSB benefits are applicable only to private insurers with an existing Approval, Deduction and Payment Agreement with Employment and Social Development Canada. Refer to the National List of Status of Disability Insurers with an Existing Approval, Deduction and Payment Agreement with ESDC To reimburse a private insurer, the client must submit a written consent, or the following forms: Service Canada – Insurer: Disability Benefits Retroactive Payment and Information Sharing Consent (ISP1618A-B); Request to Deduct and Pay a One-Time Retroactive Payment to an Insurer (ISP1618C); and A copy of the private insurer's record of payment to the applicant. The Department can accept the previous standalone ISP1618A and ISP1618B forms if all of the conditions listed in the Reimbursement—Insurers/Provincial Administrators (Policy) are met. Doing so is in violation of the client's privacy rights. Instead, advise the private insurer to contact their client. Even if a valid ISP1618A-B form is received, you cannot release any information to the private insurer regarding the status of the client's CPPD benefits application. The reason to not proceed with the reimbursement must be communicated to the private insurer if: there is no agreement in place between the private insurer and the Department; the CPPD benefits, which might have been withheld for reimbursement, have already been paid to the client; the ISP1618C and record of payment were not received within the allotted time; The total amount of disability insurance benefits paid to the client over the retroactive period was less than $50.00; no disability insurance benefits were paid in the month of the effective date of the CPPD benefit or thereafter; or the CPPD benefit is the resumption of a previous period of entitlement, i.e. it is not considered a new CPPD benefits application.

A departmental receivable (overpayment) is any payment made to which there was no entitlement. This includes any cheques that were not negotiated. Typically, readjudication in ITRDS creates the departmental receivable. You can manually add a departmental receivable if there was a duplicate payment cashed or when the system failed to accurately create one (Duplicate Payment or Manually-Created Debt). Departmental receivables are usually recovered from monthly program entitlements and from payables related to the same program. However, if there is no monthly entitlement or not enough money payable from one program, you can recover the receivable from the other program. This is known as a cross-program recovery.

The assistance measure allows a person experiencing a difficulty to be assisted free of charge by one or two people of their choice. Officially recognized by the Curateur public du Québec, the assistant can then communicate with third parties (government services, financial institutions, businesses, service providers and professionals) on behalf of the assisted person. Assistants cannot sign or make decisions on behalf of applicants or clients. As an authorized contact, their scope is limited to communication. The authority of an assistant is similar to the authority granted to an individual through a Consent to Communicate Information to an Authorized Person (ISP-1603) form. Duration and termination The assistant is recognized for a maximum period of 3 years. After this period, a new application must be submitted to have the same person or up to 2 new persons recognized for an additional 3-year period. However, the assistance measure can be terminated at any time before the end of the three years in any of the following situations: at the request of the assisted person; when the Curateur public du Québec is informed that the assistant ceases to act; upon the death of the assisted person or the assistant; upon institution of a tutorship for the assisted person or for their assistant; following the homologation of the assisted person's or the assistant's protection mandate; following the appointment of a temporary representative for the assistant; or when the Curateur public du Québec decides to terminate it. Verification Assistants recognized by the Curateur public du Québec are officially registered in the Public register of assistants. You must consult the Public register of assistants whenever an assistant comes forward to communicate on behalf of the client. This register allows you to verify the identity of any assistant when they contact you to obtain information on behalf of the assisted person. Consulting the Public register of assistants is the only way to verify if an assistant is registered and if their recognition is still valid. To access the Public register of assistants, you will need the first and last name of the assistant and the measure number that the assistant will provide. The assistant will also be required to obtain and provide you with a security code. This code is valid for 72 hours and will allow you to see the identity (first and last name) of the assisted person. To verify the identity of an assistant when they contact you, refer to Public register of assistants External link . Public register of assistants

Payment request from a lawyer At times, a lawyer will advise a client to designate them as the recipient of their first benefit payment. All applications submitted by the applicant must be data captured in ITRDS. When a new or duplicate application is received, you must add the OAS pension application data capture session in ITRDS. You will modify data captured information for a previously submitted, incomplete or force denied OAS pension application when: there was insufficient information captured to adjudicate the application; you receive additional or updated information from the applicant; or a submitted data capture session requires correction. Once all mandatory and optional information from the OAS pension application is data captured, ITRDS will adjudicate the application and determine if the applicant: qualifies for a full OAS pension (40/40); qualifies for a partial OAS pension (x/40); or does not qualify for an OAS pension.

topic_title: Determine the duration of hardship New
text: When a debtor's financial situation meets the criteria of undue hardship, you must consider the expected duration of their hardship to determine when to reassess the debtor's financial situation. Verify if the debtor's financial situation will change based on receiving additional income or the end of a loan or mortgage term. Undue hardship occurs when the repayment of an overpayment (in whole or in part) causes financial stress for the debtor because of limited household income. Hardship exists when the debtor is unable to repay a portion of the overpayment without being deprived of the necessities of life such as food, shelter, medical services, clothing and utilities (water, electricity and heating). When an overpayment is established on a debtor's account, they are notified of the amount and recovery rate. The proposed recovery rate is based on the Recovery Guidelines (Work Tool) When the debtor or their legal representative claims financial difficulty and cannot repay the debt at the proposed recovery rate, you can accept or negotiate an amended recovery rate without requesting a Statement of Income and Expenses (ISP-0100) form. However, you must ensure that the overpayment can be recovered within the applicable 5- or 10-year period. For more information, Overpayments—Recovery and Collection (Policy) If the overpayment cannot be recovered within the 5- or 10-year period, the debtor must indicate their inability to afford repayment on the ISP-0100 form or in a written statement, including their income and expenses. The income stated on the ISP-0100 form or written statement should be current amounts, and if the debtor is married or living common-law, the spouse or common-law partner's income must also be included. Other household members' income should not be included (e.g. children, parents, etc.). Use your judgment to determine if the expenses listed are reasonable. If an expense appears too high, you must contact the debtor to request clarification or supporting documentation. For example, if a client has 2 people in their household and claims $5,000.00 per month in grocery expense, you must request clarification. When a new recovery rate is set or the recovery is deferred, you must send a letter to notify the debtor. You must assess each undue hardship case on an individual basis.

text: Once the settlement offer is accepted and the payment has been received and cleared, the Collections Litigations and Advisory Services will send a letter to the debtor or their legal representative. This letter confirms that the remaining debt no longer needs to be repaid. These periods determine if the individual can claim the CRP. When you process a new benefit application with the CRP, a notice of entitlement is produced to advise the client that the CRP has been applied to the benefit calculation. When you add the provision to an existing benefit, you must send a letter to the client to inform them of any resulting changes to their benefit rate. If the client was already receiving the benefit at the maximum rate payable, or, if there is no change in the client's benefit rate after processing the CRP request, you must send a letter to the client to explain that the CRP was applied to their account, but that it did not change their benefit rate. For children who were born or who lived outside Canada before age 7, you must complete the Period of Ineligibility field. The ineligible period begins the month after birth and ends with the month the child arrived in Canada. Proof of the child's date of arrival in Canada must be obtained from the client.

The preferred income is the income source that ITRDS will use to calculate benefit entitlement. On the View Income screen in ITRDS, a Preferred Source field will be displayed for every year in which there is an income record. If there is only one source of income, the Preferred Source is set to Default and cannot be modified. If there are 2 sources of income, the Preferred Source can be updated to either Default , CRA or Client Reported by selecting Yes to the applicable source. If the Preferred Source is set to Default , ITRDS will determine the preferred income as the one with the highest total income. If both incomes match, Canada Revenue Agency will have its Preferred Source field displayed as Yes .

A Protected status will identify that the income data is available, but ITRDS will not use it to adjudicate or recalculate the benefit. Income will be in Protected status when: the account has been identified by Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) under GIS Take-up, but the client has not yet submitted their application for benefits. Income remains in Protected status until the application is received and data captured; there is bankruptcy information on the account; bankruptcy an income exception flag exists on the account; CRA income is received and client-reported income exists on the account for the same income year and is being used to pay benefits . This includes changes to the income for the base calendar year where an option has been approved to determine entitlement. Income can be taken out of Protected status as required.

This procedure demonstrates how to perform an ITRDS data capture simulation to estimate the dollar amount for the Pension Sharing (PNSH) provision.

Click Simulation from the institutional bar in ITRDS . The Simulation Selection screen opens. Click the radio button next to Pension Sharing (PNSH) in the Provision Selection block. Click the radio button next to the client's interrelated spouse/common-law partner with whom the client's RTR pension will be shared. Click Continue . The Simulation - PNSH screen opens. Complete the Simulation Dates block as follows: Table 1. Simulation Dates Field Direction Date of Application Enter the date when the application was received. YYYYMM Earliest Month Check the box if the client has requested the PNSH to begin the earliest possible month. or Start Date Enter the start date of the PNSH requested by the client. YYYYMM Click Submit . The Simulated Benefits screen opens. Click PNSH in the CPP block to expand and review the simulated benefit calculation results. There are multiple scenarios possible, depending on if one or both spouses or common-law partners made enhanced contributions: Double base PNSH: Both spouses or common-law partners are contributors and both display RTR and PNSH benefit rows. The RTR row displays the contributions and calculation details for the base component. If the contributor made enhanced contributions, it would also display the first additional and second additional amounts for the spouse or common-law partner from whose account the simulation is performed. The PNSH row displays the contributions and calculation details of the base amount received from the other spouse or common-law partner's account. If the other spouse or common-law partner made enhanced contributions, it will also display the first additional and second additional amounts. Residence periods are the amount of time a client has resided in and outside of Canada. You will data capture all residence periods a client has declared from age 18 to present. The data capture in ITRDS must be complete and accurate in order to determine the client's: eligibility (to approve or deny the application); and entitlement (to avoid an incorrect payment). Once all residence periods are captured, ITRDS calculates the total years of residence based on: total periods of valid Canadian residence to date; total periods of creditable foreign residence to date; or a combination of both. When entering periods on the Residence screen, ITRDS will determine the client’s eligibility to the OAS pension and benefits based on the following: Residence period Included in the residence calculation Excluded from the residence calculation Period in Canada Residence Presence Unknown Period outside of Canada Deemed residence Absence Unknown For any residence period outside of Canada, you must select a Reason for Absence associated with the Type of period.

In most cases, the Department pays a benefit directly to the client. However, there are situations where the Department can authorize the payment to a legal representative, also known as a third party payee. The Department can authorize a legal representative to receive benefit payments on a client's behalf in the following situations: A client becomes incapable of managing their own affairs. An individual or organization with legal authority can act and make decisions, give or receive information and receive benefit payments on the client's behalf. A child under the age of 18 (-18 child) is eligible for benefits. The individual or organization who has decision-making responsibility and parenting time of the child receives the payment. A client is deceased. A one-time payment paid to an authorized third party. Under certain circumstances, approved provincial administrators of social assistance, private insurers or Provincial Workers' Compensation Program Agencies can receive repayment of benefits. ITRDS uses the data in the client's profile with the information that you enter when you perform a data capture simulation. A simulated data capture performed in ITRDS does not affect any of the client's current benefits. Data capture simulations in ITRDS allow you to: calculate a single or combined benefit estimate dollar amount; determine the potential eligibility for a benefit; or determine the Minimum Qualifying Period for benefit eligibility purposes. ITRDS can only simulate the data capture of one benefit at a time. As of August 25, 2025, the data capture simulation results have been updated to include the calculations of the second additional earnings and contributions of the CPP enhancement. The PRB estimate includes only the CPP portion, even when you perform a simulation on a client's account with both QPP and CPP data present. ITRDS provides an estimate of the PRB base, the first additional and the second additional dollar amounts using: the client's age; the effective date (actual or hypothetical) of the client's RTR pension; and the dollar amount of the base, the first additional and second additional pensionable contributions. You can also perform a PRB simulation for contributors over the age of 65 that indicate they made an Election (Opt-out) or Revocation (Opt-in), which permits a more precise calculation of the PRB . When a client requests a simulation for a PRB in a future year where that year's CPP rates are unavailable, ITRDS will use the latest CPP rates to calculate the PRB simulation. ITRDS will also include the earnings and contributions, or unadjusted pensionable earnings provided by the client and entered by the user. Therefore, the benefit amounts for future PRBs are calculated in current dollar amounts. When a client requests a simulation for a PRB with a past effective date, the PRB will be escalated to the current accounting month.

Translation requests are sent to internal translation units first, then to the Translation Bureau—Public Services and Procurement Canada, if necessary. You can accept documents translated by Canadian federal, provincial or territorial governments, foreign missions (e.g. embassies, consulates, High Commissions) and certified translators for the purpose of administering CPP and OAS benefits. You do not have to translate documents provided by clients in a foreign language if the material is not relevant to the consideration of the application or the ongoing receipt of benefits. For example: A client who came to Canada in 1988 attaches a copy of his foreign passport from 1980 to 1985 while he did not reside in Canada. A client indicates in a letter the nature of attached documents and you know they are not relevant. You must not assume the nature of the documen ts, the client must specify it in writing . Departmental employees can review and edit translated work. For technical translations of one or two words, employees can use a program lexicon to identify the word in the other official language. Best practices You must send translation requests as early as possible before the deadline in order to reduce costs. A minimum 24-hour turnaround time is required for all requests sent to the Translation Bureau. Translating l ong documents can take several weeks. Ensure that you follow the Government of Canada’s security directions Internal link on how to classify and transmit documents. For example, client documents can require Protected B classification and transmittal. Government of Canada’s security directions You should provide: translated reference material with related vocabulary in both languages. Providing existing translations improves accuracy and reduces timelines; a clean copy with few questions or clearly marked revisions (e.g. tracked changes, yellow highlighting). For revision, include the original translation; and content that is clear and professional with proper punctuation, grammar, names, titles, etc.

When determining if an application for the OAS pension, GIS, ALW or ALWS benefit must be transferred to International Operations (IO), you must always review the first possible effective date of the pension or benefit and the applicant's requested start date, if applicable. If an applicant requests a specific start date for their OAS pension, only transfer the application to IO if an agreement is needed as of that date. You must transfer an application to IO in the following situations: the applicant has a Canadian address with less than 10 years of Canadian residence at the earliest possible effective date and has lived or worked in a country with an International Social Security Agreement (ISSA) ; the applicant has a Canadian address with less than 10 years of Canadian residence at the earliest possible effective date and has lived or worked in a country with an International Social Security Agreement (ISSA) the applicant has a foreign address with less than 20 years of Canadian residence at the earliest possible effective date and has lived or worked in a country with an ISSA ; the applicant has a foreign address with less than 20 years of Canadian residence at the earliest possible effective date and has lived or worked in a country with an ISSA the applicant meets the residence requirement without an ISSA; however, based on the receipt date of their application, they may qualify with an earlier effective date by using an ISSA ; the applicant meets the residence requirement without an ISSA; however, based on the receipt date of their application, they may qualify with an earlier effective date by using an ISSA an OAS pension or benefit application is awaiting adjudication in IO for the applicant and/or their spouse or common-law partner, if applicable; the applicant is currently receiving an OAS pension or benefit through IO and reapplies for the same pension or benefit; or the applicant's spouse or common-law partner is in pay for an OAS pension or benefit through IO. Situation The applicant has a Canadian address, less than 10 years of Canadian residence at the earliest possible effective date and lived or worked in a country that has an ISSA in force with Canada. Example An applicant submits an ALW benefit application dated December 15, 2023, that states residence in Canada from December 2020 to the present. They have also indicated 15 years of residence in Croatia. The application must be transferred to IO because: the applicant meets the age and legal status criteria; at the earliest possible effective date of January 2023 (11 months retroactive from the date of application), the applicant has less than 10 years of residence in Canada; and Canada has an ISSA in force with Croatia. Situation The applicant has a foreign address, less than 20 years of Canadian residence at the earliest possible effective date and has lived or worked in a country that has an ISSA in force with Canada. Example An applicant submits an OAS pension application dated January 15, 2024, that states residence in Canada from May 2016 to July 2022. They have also indicated: The application must be transferred to IO because: 25 years of residency in Japan, where they currently reside; and they want their OAS pension to start as soon as they are eligible. the applicant meets the age and legal status criteria; at the earliest possible effective date of February 2023 (11 months retroactive from the date of application), the applicant has less than 20 years of residence in Canada; and Canada has an ISSA in force with Japan. Situation The applicant meets the residence requirement without an ISSA; however, based on the receipt date of their application, they may qualify with an earlier effective date by using an ISSA. Example An applicant submits an OAS pension application dated April 15, 2024, that states they: In this situation, the applicant would qualify without an ISSA, with an effective date of February 2024 (the month after the month in which they obtained 10 years of residence in Canada) for regional processing. However, the application must be transferred to IO because: have resided in Canada since January 15, 2014; have 20 years of residence in Italy; and would like their OAS pension to start as soon as they are eligible. at the earliest possible effective date of May 2023 (11 months retroactive from the date of application), the applicant had less than 10 years of residence in Canada; and Canada has an ISSA in force with Italy. For all benefit types, do not send the application to IO if the applicant: does not meet the legal status requirement; has less than one complete year of residence in Canada after age 18; or does not require an ISSA but has a spouse or common-law partner whose OAS pension, GIS or ALW benefit application is pending a final decision in IO. IO will request the transfer of the file and adjust the marital status, as required. When the OAS pension or benefit application is transferred to IO to determine eligibility under an ISSA, the following will occur: Situation IO can qualify the applicant or beneficiary under an ISSA. Result IO will inform the applicant of the decision and take over the administration of the OAS account. Situation IO cannot qualify the applicant under an ISSA due to the client not having any foreign creditable periods. Result If the applicant resides in Canada and needs an ISSA to qualify, IO will deny the application and return the file to the regional processing centre. If the applicant resides outside of Canada and needs an ISSA to qualify, IO will deny the application and retain the file. If the application was sent to IO to review for an earlier effective date under an ISSA, but the applicant could qualify without an ISSA using that application date, IO will return the application to the regional processing centre. Situation IO cannot qualify the applicant under an ISSA due to the client not having sufficient foreign creditable periods. Result If the applicant needs an ISSA to qualify, IO will deny the application and retain the file. If the application was sent to IO to review for an earlier effective date under an ISSA, but the applicant could qualify without an ISSA using that application date, IO will return the application to the regional processing centre.

topic_title: Transfer a file after the CPP pension, benefit or provision has been approved
text: After a regional processing centre approves a CPP pension, benefit or provision, an update to the client's earnings and contributions may result in the client now requiring an International Social Security Agreement (ISSA) to qualify. When the CRA updates earnings and contributions on the contributor's Record of Earnings, the client's eligibility may change if they no longer have sufficient contributions to qualify for a pension or benefit. In this situation, if the client lived or worked in a country with an ISSA, you must forward the benefit application file to International Operations (IO). IO will determine if eligibility can be established using the client's foreign creditable periods.

topic_title: Transfer a file after the OAS pension or benefit has been approved
text: After an OAS pension, ALW benefit or ALWS benefit has been approved, a client will no longer qualify: for the OAS pension when they permanently move outside of Canada with less than 20 years of accumulated residence in Canada; for the ALW benefit or ALWS benefit when they have been absent from Canada for 6 months after the month of departure; or when a residence review determines that additional 40ths were awarded to the client in error, and the client now requires an ISSA to qualify. In these situations and if the client has lived or worked in a country with which Canada has an ISSA in force, forward the file to IO to determine if eligibility or portability can be established. Once the account has been reviewed and if eligibility or portability: can be established, IO will take over the administration of the OAS account, including the recovery of any applicable overpayment; cannot be established, IO will return the file to the originating office. That office must advise the client of the overpayment amount (if it has not already been done) and begin overpayment recovery.

topic_title: Transfer an initial CPP pension, benefit or provision application
text: You must send an initial CPP pension, benefit or provision application to IO in the following situations: Retirement Retirement Death Death Survivor / Surviving Child's benefit Survivor / Surviving Child's benefit Pension Sharing Pension Sharing Child Rearing Provision Child Rearing Provision Benefit or pension Retirement Situation The applicant is currently in pay or was previously in pay for a CPP benefit (e.g. DSB , SVR pension or Pension Sharing) with IO. Benefit or pension Death Situation The deceased was previously paid a CPP benefit through IO. The deceased does not meet the Minimum Qualifying Period (MQP), has at least one valid contribution to the CPP and has lived or worked in a country with an International Social Security Agreement (ISSA). Benefit or pension Survivor Surviving Child's benefit Situation The deceased does not meet the MQP, has at least one valid contribution to the CPP and has lived or worked in a country with an ISSA; The deceased was previously paid a CPP benefit through IO; or The applicant for a SVR pension is receiving or was previously paid a CPP benefit through IO. Benefit or pension Pension Sharing Situation The applicant is currently in pay for a CPP RTR pension with IO. Benefit or pension Child Rearing Provision Situation The applicant is currently in pay or was previously in pay for a CPP benefit with IO. If the applicant or beneficiary qualifies for the CPP pension, benefit or provision, IO informs the applicant or beneficiary of the decision and takes over administration of the account, including the recovery of any overpayment. If the applicant or beneficiary does not qualify due to insufficient foreign creditable periods, IO informs the applicant or beneficiary of the denial and retains the file. If the applicant or beneficiary's CPP account needs to be combined with an existing IO CPP account, IO must request that the region transfer the file to them. Do not send the application to IO if the applicant: does not have at least one year of valid unadjusted pensionable earnings; does not have at least one valid CPP contribution; or has never lived or worked in a country with an ISSA, with the exception of an RTR pension applicant whose application is being sent to IO due to having previously been paid an SVR pension with IO.

topic_title: Transfer an initial CPPD benefits application
text: You must send an initial CPPD benefits application to International Operations (IO) in the following situations: The applicant has insufficient CPP contributions to meet CPPD benefits contributory requirements but has at least one valid CPP contribution and indicates they lived or worked in a country with which Canada has an ISSA in force. The applicant has sufficient CPP contributions to calculate a Latest Possible Date of Onset (LPDOO) or Minimum Qualifying Period (MQP) and has lived or worked before or after their LPDOO or MQP in a country with which Canada has an ISSA in force. However, the Regional Medical Adjudicator cannot deem the applicant disabled by their LPDOO or MQP. The Regional Medical Adjudicator deems the applicant is disabled and the applicant is receiving a CPP benefit or pension with IO. The Regional Medical Adjudicator deems the applicant is disabled and the applicant previously received CPPD benefits with IO. If the applicant or beneficiary qualifies for a CPPD benefit, IO informs the applicant of the decision and takes over administration of the account including any overpayment. IO notifies the region if the applicant or beneficiary's regional SVR pension or Early Retirement pension account needs to be combined and paid through IO. When IO is not able to establish or improve the LPDOO or MQP under an ISSA, IO will return the CPPD benefits application to the region to make a decision and administer the file. Do not send the CPPD benefits application to IO if the applicant: does not have at least one valid CPP contribution; has never lived or worked in a country with which Canada has an ISSA in force; or has an LPDOO or MQP into the future (i.e. beyond the date of determination or decision).

IO processes benefit applications using provisions set out in the International Social Security Agreements (ISSA) to assist individuals to qualify for Canadian benefits to which they would not otherwise be entitled. These agreements coordinate the administration and operation of the CPP and OAS programs with the comparable social security program of another country. When determining eligibility for an OAS pension or benefit, an ISSA allows periods of residence and/or contributions in a country with which Canada has an agreement in force to be added to an applicant's years of residence in Canada after reaching age 18 to meet the minimum residence requirements to qualify. While an ISSA can assist in qualifying a client for an OAS pension, the client's entitlement (40th) will be based only on their actual number of years of residence in Canada. An ISSA can also allow periods of residence and/or contributions in a country with which Canada has an agreement in force to be added to an applicant's CPP contributions to meet the minimum contributory requirement for a CPP pension or benefit. In all cases, the terms and provisions of an ISSA can only be applied on or after the entry into force date. An agreement enters into force when the terms and conditions of the ISSA take effect. To confirm the status of Canada's ISSAs with other countries, the entry into force date and the responsible IO processing centre, refer to the International Social Security Agreement Country List (Work Tool) CPP OAS Accounts returned from International Operations A CPP or OAS benefit or pension or CPPD benefit application transferred to IO will be returned to the regional processing centre if the following occurs: IO determines the applicant qualifies for benefits under domestic legislation without an ISSA or an ISSA cannot be used to qualify the applicant at an earlier effective date; there is no ISSA in force that can assist the applicant to qualify for benefits; the contributor does not have at least one valid contribution; the client does not qualify for benefits with or without an ISSA and there is an existing overpayment on the account; IO determines that the CPPD benefit applicant's Latest Possible Date of Onset or Minimum Qualifying Period cannot be established or improved with an ISSA after investigating foreign creditable periods; or the applicant resides in Canada and did not qualify for an OAS pension or benefit under an ISSA as they did not have any valid foreign creditable periods (i.e. residence and/or contributions).

This procedure provides instructions on how to review, add and delete notes on a client's account in ITRDS .

Notes ITRDS notes are an important part of a client's file. A clear and concise record of actions taken on a client's account directly impacts client service and improves communication between processing staff, in-person staff, and call centre staff. The Privacy Act gives the client the right to request the contents of their file and ITRDS notes may be released to the client or their representative, when requested. You must enter a note in ITRDS when you take any action on an account, make a decision or attempt to contact the client. You must also enter a note on any related accounts directly affected by the action or decision. You must include: the impact of the action or decision (e.g. the results when the application is approved or denied); any underpayment or overpayment amounts created and the period; and a reference (e.g. Client ID number) to the account on which the decision or action took place; information provided to a foreign institution (e.g. sending a foreign benefit application or responding to a request from the foreign institution), if applicable; information received from a foreign institution, if applicable; or if International Social Security Agreement restrictions prevent International Operations (IO) from sharing client information. A note can contain up to 500 characters (case insensitive and accent neutral) in length, including spaces and dashes. You must avoid using abbreviations or acronyms whenever possible. You must respect the following criteria when adding a note in ITRDS . It must accurately capture and convey client information in a way that is easily understood by anyone accessing the file internally (e.g. other processing agents, in-person agents, call centre agents, or Integrity agents) or externally for SST appeals, Ministerial enquiries or Access to Information and Privacy requests from a client or their representative. It must be written in a professional manner. It must be written in plain language and respect the client's language of choice on file. It can include only the Department's acronyms and abbreviations found in the ITRDS List of Acronyms, Initialisms and Abbreviations (Word, 78.8 KB) Download link . List of Acronyms, Initialisms and Abbreviations You must add a note to the client's account if you send any correspondence. If referring to forms and letters in notes, you must include: the form number and name; or the letter number and a brief description of the content of the letter being sent to the client. The following are common examples of ITRDS notes and the information that must be included: An application has been reviewed but requires: further information or supporting documentation from the applicant; further information from other regions or a foreign institution; or a transfer to another region or to IO For a CPP, OAS, or CPPD non-medical determination, a decision has been made to approve, deny, terminate or suspend the benefit, pension or provision. The note must include: the effective date of the approved benefit, pension or provision; the reason for the denial of the benefit; and/or the date the benefit, pension or provision is suspended, terminated, or cancelled and the reason. For a CPPD medical determination, at the time of the decision, the note must include: Initial decision made; Reconsideration decision made; or Reassessment decision made. For a CPPD medical determination when releasing the decision to approve, deny or terminate, do not include the reason for a denial or termination of the request in the note. The reason(s) for a denial or termination decision is documented on a worksheet and communicated to the client in the decision letter. The note must include: the effective date of the approved benefit; or the decision and the decision date for the denial or termination. An overpayment or underpayment is calculated. The note must include: the reason for the overpayment or the underpayment; the dollar amounts and payment periods; that a letter was sent to the client notifying them of the underpayment or overpayment details; the lump sum payment information for notional tax purposes; and the date when an underpayment will be released and whether any confirmation was sent to the client; or the date when the Department will start recovery of the overpayment and the recovery rate. An explanation of a BF. The note must include: the reason for the BF; and the review date. A foreign benefit application is sent to the client or to the foreign institution. The note must include: the type of benefit; the name of the country of Agreement; that the documents were sent with the application, if applicable; and that the letter was sent to the applicant. A foreign liaison is sent or received. The note must include: information received from the foreign institution (e.g. creditable periods, date of death); information sent to a region (e.g. foreign pension information, date of death, current address); and information requested from the foreign institution and the information sent to the foreign institution in response to a liaison request. A CPP benefit application is denied in a region and after review by IO, the client is still not eligible. The note must include: the type of benefit; the name of the applicant and any relevant third party information; the name of the country of Agreement; the reason for the denial; that a liaison was sent to the country of Agreement to notify of the denial; and that a letter was sent to the applicant informing them that they still do not meet the Minimum Qualifying Period. Prescribed notes If instruction is provided in a procedure regarding notes (e.g. using a specific note format or including specific content), you must follow the prescribed format and include the required information when adding your note to a client`s account. The prescribed note is used to identify or review files of a particular nature at a later date. If you are participating in a pilot or test project you may be provided prescribed notes by the project administrator. If so, you must follow the prescribed format and include the required information. Important or Archived notes The Notes block displays 2 separate blocks: important and regular notes. The Archived block displays archived notes. Important notes are listed at the top of the Notes screen. The Type column indicates if the note was flagged as Important or was added systematically. The text of an important note is bolded . You can add multiple important notes per program (CPP, OAS and IO) and they are displayed from the most recent to the oldest. Important notes should be limited to only information that is required before taking action or releasing information. An important note is used to communicate such things as: authentication information; special instructions regarding payments; warnings (e.g. ca llers trying to impersonate the client); or files being reviewed by the Integrity Services Branch. This is not an exhaustive list. You can use the Demote Selected note feature to remove the Important flag and move the information to a regular note. A systematic important note can be demoted, but cannot be deleted. The Archived block is located at the bottom of the Notes screen, and contains archived notes that were recorded in the CPP, OAS and International Agreements Legacy systems. To assist you in deciphering older ITRDS notes, refer to the Common Reference Tool's list of Unofficial Abbreviations Internal link . Unofficial Abbreviations Deleting notes You cannot modify or delete notes. Ensure you review all notes you add for clarity and accuracy before saving. Only authorized designates can delete notes in ITRDS . You can submit a request to delete an ITRDS note in the following situations: the note can lead other agents to provide incorrect information to the client; an error in calculating a payment amount is possible due to the information in the note; the client has requested that personal information be deleted from a note; or the note was added to the wrong account.

When processing an application or a statement of income for an income-tested benefit, you must request the respective income from the CRA for the client and their spouse or common-law partner, if applicable, to determine entitlement. Before submitting a request to the CRA , determine if the required income is already on file by reviewing the following screens: the CRA Income ( CRA ) screen in OAS Online; the Income screen or Income History screen in ITRDS ; the Future Income (INF) screen in the International Agreements (IA) system; and the notes screen in ITRDS to determine if a manual request has been sent to the CRA . In OAS Online, you can request income online for the current base calendar year and up to 3 preceding calendar years. If the income is available, the CRA will send it via the two-way feed process on the Tuesday following the next system update. If you cannot request the required income online, you must request the required Income Tax Benefit and Returns for the client and their spouse or common-law partner, if required, or send a manual request to the CRA for the income. In the IA system, the CRA income feed is only initiated when you approve an income-tested benefit application in the system. Once approved, the CRA will begin sending the income annually for the renewal of benefits. You cannot request specific income years (i.e. current or previous) through the IA system. You must request the required Income Tax Benefit and Returns for the client and their spouse or common-law partner, if required. You can also send a manual request to the CRA for income. To request income manually, you must complete and send the Request for Information for Guaranteed Income Supplement purposes (ISP-3090) form to the CRA as per regional procedures. You can request income manually for the current year and up to 3 preceding calendar years. In February of each year, the CRA starts switching their systems to the present taxation year. To prepare for this, the Department enters a period of CRA unavailability at the end of January until the beginning of March. During this period, income enquiries can still be submitted but CRA income will not be received until this period is over. This procedure provides guidance on how to manually add, adjust, modify or cancel a third party receivable on a client's account in CPMS .

CRA , Employment Insurance (EI) and Veterans Affairs Canada can each submit a request to the Department to recover a debt on their behalf. The Department recovers a third party receivable from benefits currently payable to a CPP client in CPMS . Depending on the client's benefit status in ITRDS , the Receivable Status field in CPMS is set to the following: Table 1. Receivable Status Benefit status Receivable status In pay Active —Recovery begins immediately. Not in pay Inactive —Recovery does not begin as there is no benefit to recover the debt from. Future (In Pay, but has a future Benefit Start Date) Pending —Recovery begins the later of the two following dates: The Benefit Start Date ; or The Recovery Start Date . If the Department adds a third party receivable and a recovery rate to a client's account during the current accounting month, debt recovery will begin in the next payment cycle. The Department can recover a third party receivable, in whole or in part, from any monthly or supplementary CPP payment payable directly to the client. However, upon the death of the client, the third party receivable on the account ceases. A client's account can have only one third party receivable per department (i.e. CRA , EI, Veterans Affairs Canada). When a client's account has an existing third party receivable, and another third party receivable request is received from the same department, you must cancel the existing receivable and add a new third party receivable with the new amount. The Start Date field reflects the start date on which the first deduction will occur. Third-party recoveries must always start in the accounting month they are entered. When the Receivable Status field is Active or Inactive , you are able to: adjust the debt amount; modify the recovery rate and recovery start date as needed; and change the status of the debt. Adjustments to the third party debt amount is not permitted if the Receivable Status field is marked as Completed or Cancelled . If you modify the recovery rate results, the following changes will be made in CPMS : If you enter a current rate start date: the Recovery Rate field displays the new percentage or dollar amount; the Start Date field displays the current accounting month; the Receivable Status field remains active, and CPMS automatically applies the new recovery percentage or dollar amount; and the Recovered Amount field updates after the payment run. If you enter a future rate start date: the Recovery Rate and Start Date fields remain the same; the Future Start Date field displays the future date entered; and the Future Rate field displays the future recovery percentage or dollar amount. The Department can only change the status of a third party receivable to Cancelled . When a third party receivable is cancelled, the system: keeps the current or future recovery rate; sets the recovery status of the receivable to Cancelled ; and stops the debt recovery immediately. Once a third party receivable is Cancelled , it cannot be reinstated. If a third party receivable is Cancelled in error, you must add a new one.

ITRDS uses the data in the client's profile with the information that you enter when you perform a data capture simulation. A simulated data capture performed in ITRDS does not affect any of the client's current benefits. Data capture simulations in ITRDS allow you to: calculate a single or combined benefit estimate dollar amount; determine the potential eligibility for a benefit; or determine the Minimum Qualifying Period (MQP) for benefit eligibility purposes. ITRDS can only simulate the data capture of one benefit at a time. As of August 25, 2025, the data capture simulation results have been updated to include the calculations of the second additional earnings and contributions of the CPP enhancement. When a data capture simulation for combined benefits is required and one benefit is already in pay, ITRDS can simulate the data capture of the other benefit and provide a combined benefit amount. When a data capture simulation for combined benefits is required and no benefits are in pay, you must perform separate data capture simulations for each benefit. The results from the individual simulations can then be used in the Canada Pension Plan Calculation Module for manual calculations to obtain the combined benefit dollar amount. International Operations processing staff will use ITRDS to simulate a single benefit amount or use the Retirement For Benefit Calculation for benefits that do not require an agreement to meet the MQP. The results from the simulation may then be used in the Canada Pension Plan Calculation Module to calculate a combined benefit amount.

text: To determine the appropriate supporting documents required to establish the validity of third party post-mortem contacts, refer to: Third party post-mortem contact roles in ITRDS —Supporting documents Administrator Appointed By The Courts A written statement declaring that the appointed administrator is responsible for the administration of the estate and providing payment address information. ITRDS uses the data in the client's profile with the information that you enter when you perform a data capture simulation. A simulated data capture performed in ITRDS does not affect any of the client's current benefits. Data capture simulations in ITRDS allow you to: calculate a single or combined benefit estimate dollar amount; determine the potential eligibility for a benefit; or determine the Minimum Qualifying Period (MQP) for benefit eligibility purposes. ITRDS can only simulate the data capture of one benefit at a time. As of August 25, 2025, the data capture simulation results have been updated to include the calculations of the second additional earnings and contributions of the CPP enhancement. When a data capture simulation for combined benefits is required and one benefit is already in pay, ITRDS can simulate the data capture of the other benefit and provide a combined benefit amount. When a data capture simulation for combined benefits is required and no benefits are in pay, you must perform separate data capture simulations for each benefit. The results from the individual simulations can then be used in the Canada Pension Plan Calculation Module for manual calculations to obtain the combined benefit dollar amount. International Operations processing staff will use ITRDS to simulate a single benefit amount or will use the Retirement For Benefit Calculation for benefits that do not require an agreement to meet the MQP. The results from the individual simulation may then be used in the Canada Pension Plan Calculation Module to calculate a combined benefit amount.

Add, modify, stop or delete a Federal Voluntary Tax Withhold (FVTW) on a client’s account in CPMS.

A client can request an FVTW to withhold a dollar amount or percentage from their benefits for federal tax purposes. You can accept a request for an FVTW when the client: is entitled to a benefit; is a resident of Canada or is deemed a resident by CRA; and provides a written or verbal request to withhold a voluntary tax. A client can request an FVTW at the time they apply for a benefit or after their benefit has been approved. The client must determine the dollar amount or percentage of the tax withhold. When the client is in pay, the FVTW will start in the current accounting month or at a future date chosen by the client. The start date cannot be: later than the end date ; before the current accounting month; or more than 12 months in the future. If there is no end date entered, the tax withhold will continue until the benefit ends or until the client submits a new request. You can add a maximum of 2 FVTWs with non -overlapping start and end dates to allow for a future dated withhold. CPMS will set the end date of the first FVTW to the month before the start date of the second FVTW. The FVTW will automatically stop when a client is no longer entitled to a benefit or when their address changes from domestic to foreign. For non-resident tax withholds, you can add an FVTW only when the client’s account is identified as a: Deemed (the client is a deemed resident of Canada by CRA for tax purposes); Client-Exception (the client resides in Canada , but their contact resides outside of Canada ); or Deemed-Exception (the client is a deemed resident, but their contact resides in Canada or in a different country than the client). You can modify an existing, active or future dated FVTW as well as any FVTW that has ended or been modified within the current tax year. If a client’s account has an overpayment and an accumulated FVTW, you can apply all or a portion of the current year’s FVTW amount to the overpayment. A client can request a PVTW to withhold a dollar amount or percentage from their OAS benefits for provincial tax purposes. Arrêter The Department does not have a process in place with Revenu Québec to seek reimbursement of Quebec provincial tax from the previous year. Therefore, as of January 15, 2018, you cannot set up a PVTW until the client has been in pay for more than 6 months. The Department can now better apply the cancellation provision under the Old Age Security Act , since a pensioner can request to cancel their OAS pension if they notify the Department in writing within 6 months from the pension start date. You can accept a request for a PVTW when the client: Old Age Security Act is entitled to a benefit; is a resident of Quebec; and provides a written or verbal request to withhold a voluntary tax. The client must determine the dollar amount or percentage of the tax withhold. Note that you cannot enter a percentage over 100% or a dollar amount greater than the client’s benefit entitlement. The PVTW will start in the current accounting month or at a future date chosen by the client. The start date cannot be: later than the end date; before the current accounting month; or more than 12 months in the future. If there is no end date entered, the tax withhold will continue until the benefit ends or until the client submits a new request. You can add a maximum of 2 PVTWs with non-overlapping start and end dates to allow for a future dated withhold. CPMS will set the end date of the first PVTW to the month before the start date of the second PVTW. The PVTW will automatically stop when a client is no longer entitled to a benefit or when their address changes from domestic to foreign. You can modify an existing, active or future dated PVTW as well as any PVTW that has ended or been modified within the current tax year. When there are 2 PVTWs on the client’s account, you must modify them in separate sessions. The PVTW amount can be reimbursed to a client only under one of the following conditions: the PVTW is applied to an incorrect client account; the amount withheld is more than the amount requested; or there is an administrative error.

There are scenarios that prevent an OAS pension or benefit from being automatically adjudicated in ITRDS due to either: system limitations; or insufficient client data merged from legacy systems. Processing agent intervention is required in such situations and the pension or benefit will be considered to be in protected status. A pension or benefit is in protected status in the following scenarios: OAS pension applications where the applicant qualifies under transitional rules (10 year rule or 3 for 1 rule); Marital status changes before July 1, 1999; Options calculations before July 1, 2008; Pension income split changes to base calendar year income for a partial pay period; Benefits are converted from legacy systems; or Payments are issued that are not related to changes in monthly entitlement. A notification appears at the top of the Client Profile screen in ITRDS to warn you that the account has a protected status benefit in pay. The Program Exception Process (PEP) Status column on the Benefits screen will indicate with a Yes or a No if a benefit is in protected status. Such accounts appear in ITRDS as protected status benefits as follows: For OAS pensions and income-tested benefits that were converted from the OAS On-line system as PEP benefits before the July 2020 to June 2021 payment period, the following data elements from the OAS On-line system were carried over into ITRDS: start date; number of 40ths; number of deferral months; rate table; and payment income. For OAS pensions and income-tested benefits that were converted from the International Agreements legacy system as Super-PEP benefits before the July 2020 to June 2021 payment period, only the: start date; benefit type; and amounts from the International Agreements legacy are carried over into ITRDS. These benefits continue to be paid and escalated in ITRDS based on this carried-over data. If certain client data is updated on an account with a protected status benefit, ITRDS re-adjudicates the protected status benefit based on the initial eligibility and entitlement overrides entered. A cash receipt refers to all payments (e.g. personal cheques, money orders) received from a debtor or their representative to repay an amount that they were not entitled to receive. Cash receipts are recorded in CPMS with a status of Unapplied . The status changes to Partial or Completed when the funds are partially or completely applied to a debt (receivable). Any excess amount withheld from a benefit payment to pay a receivable can only be refunded to the debtor if no other receivable exists for that client. A client is in a dire need situation if a delay in benefit payments will cause them to suffer severe financial hardship. Severe financial hardship is defined as a risk of being unable to satisfy basic needs, such as food, medical services or housing. Examples of factors demonstrating dire need situations include: an inability to pay medical bills or expenses (including medications) or to pay for the transportation required to access medications or medical services; an inability to buy food; a risk of eviction from housing due to an inability to pay the rent or mortgage; a risk of disconnection of utilities. Every individual’s circumstances are unique. A situation that seems dire need to one individual may not seem dire to another. You must make every effort to ensure that the client’s situation meets the following dire need criteria. An inability to satisfy basic needs such as food, medical services or housing. The benefit application's status has been verified in ITRDS, OAS Online or in the International Agreements (IA) system. All required supporting documents have been submitted . There is no pattern of past claims of dire need. Review the claimant's file to see if there is a history of such claims. Dire need situations must be escalated on an urgent basis. If a client who is in receipt of ongoing benefits has not received their payments due to an error by Service Canada: You must apologize to the client for any inconvenience caused. You must issue a priority payment immediately; an. You do not need to assess dire need criteria. Dire need notifications received by email or telephone When an email is received from either an in-person centre or a call centre with “Dire Need” in the subject line: Review the file immediately . Contact the client within 24 hours to tell them: the outcome of the review; and when they will likely receive their CPP or OAS payment. If you can issue a payment to the client, follow existing procedures to issue a priority payment within 72 hours of receiving the notification. If the situation requires faster delivery of the payment, discuss arrangements with your manager. Dire need notifications received by mail There are instances when correspondence is received in the mail processing centre indicating that the client is in dire need. In such cases, you must: Review the file immediately ; Contact the client within 24 hours of file review; If you can issue a payment to the client, follow existing procedures to issue a priority payment within 72 hours of receiving the notification.

You must validate the need for a manual priority payment before you prepare one. A manual priority payment may be issued in the following situations: there has been a delay in the processing of the client's pension or benefit and the client is in dire financial need; there is a system limitation that does not allow the release of the payment; the client's payment was cancelled, suspended or interrupted in error; there is a reimbursement owing to a third party (e.g. Family Orders and Enforcement, provincial agency, private insurer); cancelled payments for a non-resident need to be reissued and duplication of the Non-Resident Tax (NRT) withhold needs to be avoided; or a payment has been returned or cancelled in the Standard Payment System (SPS) and needs to be reissued but this cannot be done through the SPS. the payment was issued from the OAS Online system or International Agreement system before migration; or the refund of a deduction withheld in error or on request (e.g. CRA refund of the NRT). The following forms must be completed to issue a manual priority payment : For CPP payments, complete the Canada Pension Plan Requisition for Manual Priority Payments (Canadian Funds) (ISP-1669-CPP) form. For OAS payments, complete the Old Age Security Requisition for Manual Priority Payments (Canadian Funds) (ISP-1669-OAS) form. For International Operations (IO)-OAS and IO-CPP payments, complete the International Operations Requisition for Manual Priority Payments (Canadian Funds) (ISP-1669-IO) form. The Overpayments / Underpayments for Approval (ISP-0118) form, if applicable. The completed ISP-0118 form must be attached to the applicable ISP-1669 form when sending for review and approval. Refer to Delegation of Authorities (PDF, 263 KB) Download link . Delegation of Authorities You must also validate the requisition form to ensure it is accurate and complete. The forms will also need to be prepared, verified, and approved by the appropriate delegation of authority. To ensure you have the required level of authority, refer to Delegation of Authorities (PDF, 263 KB) Download link . Delegation of Authorities Ensure any necessary tax slip adjustments are completed after the manual priority payment is issued. Tax Slips (Scenario)

topic_title: Power of Attorney and Mandate Validation Examples (Work Tool)
text: Power of Attorney Validation Examples Situation Direction The Department receives an application for OAS with a recently dated Power of Attorney (POA) or mandate document. Information exists on file that the public trustee currently administers the client's affairs. Contact the public trustee and ask them to apply for OAS on behalf of the client. A public trustee is only responsible for a client who is incapable of caring for their own property. A public trustee takes precedence over an attorney or mandatary. Refer to Trusteeship (Scenario) . Trusteeship (Scenario) The Department receives one or more documents bearing different dates and naming separate individuals as attorneys or mandataries for a client. Program records indicate that there is no incapability on the part of the client. Contact the client and ask if you can send them the attorney or mandatary documents for verification or confirmation. The Department appoints a person or agency as a trustee for a client. The Department then receives an enduring POA or mandate document naming an independent third party to act on behalf of the client. The POA or mandate is dated earlier than the date of the Department-appointed trustee. Review the POA or mandate document to ensure its validity. Advise the Department-appointed trustee that the trusteeship is cancelled and they must complete a final trustee accounting report. Do not give the trustee appeal rights. The trustee appointment is under the Department's legislation and made at the Minister's discretion. Refer to Trusteeship (Scenario) . If requested, correspondence and payments can be sent c/o the valid attorney or mandatary. Trusteeship (Scenario) The Department receives a springing POA for a mentally capable client. The springing POA comes into force only if the client becomes incapable of managing their own affairs. As long as it meets all legislative criteria, this POA is valid even if the client is still capable. However, it is not yet in force and the attorney cannot exercise their authority with the Department. If the client becomes incapable of managing their own affairs, the attorney must submit confirmation of the incapability (i.e. an assessment from a medical professional, a court document, a Certificate of Incapability (ISP-3505) form) to support the springing POA document and begin exercising their authority with the Department. Refer to Validate a Certificate of Incapability (Action) . Validate a Certificate of Incapability (Action)

This procedure explains the steps of how to manually create and issue a tax slip (i.e. T4, NR4 and credit slips) when one was not produced by the system.

After you create the tax slip, its status will automatically be set to: Requested (the transaction has been queued for processing); then to Issued (the tax slip is posted in TISO and forwarded for printing and mail out).

Tax slips reflect benefit and payment information for an entire calendar year. They are issued on an annual basis for monthly CPP and OAS benefits and for the one-time death benefit payment received within a calendar year. T4As are issued to a CPP or OAS client for periods during which they were a resident of Canada. NR4s are issued to a CPP or OAS client for periods during which they were not a resident of Canada. Credit slips are issued when a client refunds a sum of money that was deposited during the previous tax year to offset an overpayment. For CPP, you must create a manual tax slip ( T4A (P) Statement of Canada Pension Plan Benefits (ISP-0136), NR4 (CPP) Statement of amounts paid or credited to non-residents of Canada (ISP-0139) or Reimbursement Of Benefit Paid During A Previous Year (ISP-1611) (credit slip)) in CPMS or E-Forms when the system has not produced one for various reasons. These reasons are identified during the year-end T4A and NR4 scans. For OAS, you must create a tax slip ( T4A (OAS) Statement of Old Age Security (ISP-0137) or NR4 (OAS) Statement of Old Age Security Pension paid or credited to non-residents of Canada (ISP-0138)) in Cúram. There should never be a systematic reason where an original tax slip for 2023 or later could not be generated in Cúram. If you encounter a situation where a tax slip cannot be created, you must create a National Service Desk ticket to report the issue.

An executor is an individual appointed in a will to manage the estate of the deceased by carrying out the disposition of assets and the requests of the will. Hierarchy of payment CPP and OAS pension and benefit applications share the same rules (except for Credit Split) regarding the payment of post-mortem benefits, in the following priority: Estate of the contributor (Executor, Administrator or Legal Representative) Institution or individual paying for the funeral Surviving spouse Next of kin If the Estate has not applied for the CPP Death (DTH) benefit within 60 days after the death of the contributor, the next applicant on the hierarchy of payment becomes eligible. For more information, refer to Paying the Death Benefit and the policy on Paying the Death Benefit Payee for the Death Benefit Required documentation You must receive: an Application for CPP Death Benefit (ISP1200) indicating there is an estate; letters of probate where there is a probated will; relevant pages of an original or certified copy of the will showing the name of the executor; letters of administration where an administrator has been appointed; or evidence indicating that the primary executor has relinquished all rights as executor, if applicable. You do not need: funeral receipts, contracts, invoices or specified letters; or a 60-day hold for the DTH benefit application, if the executor is validated. It is possible that one primary and one secondary executor are identified in the will. Only the primary executor is identified on the payment. If the primary executor is unable to carry out the required duties, the benefit can be paid to the secondary executor. Evidence must be provided, indicating that the primary executor has relinquished all rights as executor. You can also have a will which names joint executors. This means that they share equal roles. If any conflict arises about who the executor is, letters of probate, a certified copy of the entire will or letters of administration can be requested to identify the executor. Executor The Executor can receive: DTH benefit and DTH benefit information; benefits and provisions made by post-mortem application received within one year of the date of death for the DTH benefit, RTR benefit (after age 70), SVR benefit, Child Rearing Provision (CRP), Credit Split, Surviving Child benefit and OAS pension; information in writing or verbally (in-person or by telephone); tax slips; amounts payable on the deceased client's account. The executor cannot: waive their rights (assign benefit) in favour of someone else. This procedure demonstrates how to validate a next of kin applicant. This information determines their eligibility to receive a Death ( DTH ) benefit and the amount payable.

Review the DTH benefit application to confirm the applicant is applying as the next of kin. Review any DTH benefit applications on file or in PWS to determine if another applicant in the payment hierarchy is eligible. Determine if the applicant indicated there is a will. If no , ensure that: the individual or institution responsible for the funeral expenses provided a written statement indicating that they are not applying for the DTH benefit; there is proof that the funeral was pre-paid or the body was donated to science, if applicable; there is a statement from the spouse indicating that they will not be applying for the DTH benefit, if applicable. If yes , ensure that: more than 60 days have passed since the date of death; there are statements indicating that the executor, administrator or the individual or institution responsible for paying the funeral expenses are not applying for the DTH benefit; there is a statement from the surviving spouse or common-law partner indicating that they will not be applying for the DTH benefit, if applicable.

If eligibility to a DTH benefit is approved, payment can be made to the next of kin when: there is no estate; the executor or administrator of the estate has not applied for the DTH benefit within 60 days after the date of death; or the executor or administrator of the estate provided information on the Application for CPP Death Benefit (ISP-1200) form indicating they will not apply for the DTH benefit; or a signed written statement indicating they will not apply for the DTH benefit. the individual or institution who is responsible for paying the funeral expenses provided: information on the ISP-1200 form, stating that they will not be applying; or a signed written statement indicating they will not be applying; proof the funeral was prepaid by the deceased, or the body was donated to science (e.g. pre-paid contract, or a letter from the medical examiner indicating the body was donated); there is no eligible spouse or common-law partner; or a signed written statement was received from the surviving spouse or common-law partner stating that they will not be applying, if applicable. For more information, refer to: Paying the Death Benefit (Work Tool) ; Paying the Death Benefit (Work Tool) Payee for the Death Benefit (Policy) ; or Payee for the Death Benefit (Policy) Payment in Special Circumstances—Death Benefit (Policy) . To determine what information must be provided by the next of kin, Third Party Contact or Applicant After a Client Dies—Add, Modify or Delete in ITRDS (Action) Documentation required To consider the next of kin as the eligible applicant, you must receive the following documents: a DTH benefit application where the applicant applies as the next of kin; and a signed written statement from one or more of the following, if applicable, stating that they are not applying: the executor or administrator; the individual or institution responsible for the funeral expenses; or the surviving spouse or common-law partner. text: The Authorization to Communicate Information - Canada Pension Plan (ISP-1606) and Authorization to communicate Information - Old Age Security (ISP-3015) forms allow a person, body or authority (e.g. accountant, lawyer or social worker) to receive benefit information on behalf of the client on an annual basis. The consent remains valid unless cancelled in writing and it is only valid if the Department receives one of the forms within one year from the date it is signed. The consent is not valid if more than one request for information concerning the same client is made in the same year and is to be communicated to the same person or authority.

topic_title: Consent for Service Canada to collect personal information Updated
text: The consent that allows the Department to collect personal information (medical and non-medical) about the client. This includes for the purpose of assessing incapacity for CPP, CPPD and OAS pensions and benefits, at all levels of adjudication and for all medical conditions. Consent can be provided in a standalone Consent for Service Canada to Collect Personal Information (ISP-2502) form or embedded in the following forms: Application kit for Canada Pension Plan Disability benefits (ISP-1151) form; Medical Report for a Canada Pension Plan Disability Benefit (ISP-2519) form; Terminal Illness Application Kit for Disability Benefits under the Canada Pension Plan (ISP-2530A) form; and Terminal Illness Medical Attestation for a Disability Benefits Application under the Canada Pension Plan (ISP-2530B) form. Once one of the forms is completed, the consent remains valid for the period indicated on the form from the date it is signed by the applicant or authorized representative, unless cancelled in writing. However, the consent is valid only for the lifecycle of the application for which it was submitted and does not extend to subsequent applications received. If a subsequent application is submitted, new consent is required for the subsequent application even if the period indicated on the original consent has not expired. Verbal confirmation (i.e. documented phone call) from the client is needed to use the consent provided with the application for the reassessment process, even if the period indicated on the original consent has not expired. If verbal confirmation cannot be obtained, a new consent is required.

topic_title: Consent to Communicate Information to an Authorized Person (ISP-1603)
text: The Consent to Communicate Information to an Authorized Person (ISP-1603) form allows a person (e.g. spouse, partner, family member or friend) to give and receive benefit information on behalf of the client on an ongoing basis. The consent remains valid unless cancelled in writing and it is only valid if the Department receives this form within one year from the date it is signed. It is revoked in the event of the death of the client. The ISP-1603 form is intended for authorizing an individual and not for use by an organization.
