Proceed as follows: Ask the client for: their full name; their SIN or Client Identifier number; their date of birth (day, month and year); the name of the unauthorized third party. Obtain the client's verbal consent to continue the conversation with the unauthorized third party. Ask the third party to confirm their relationship with the client (e.g. friend, relative or translator). Complete the rest of the security check process with the assistance of the third party. Go to the Authenticating a client or authorized representative section above. Update the client's notes in ITRDS to record details of your actions or decisions made on the account. If the client would like to provide authorization for this third party to communicate with the Department on an ongoing basis, send a Consent to Communicate Information to an Authorized Person (ISP1603) form to the client for them to complete and return.

topic_title: Privacy and protection of client information
text: Clients may be hesitant to provide the information required to authenticate their identity due to concerns of identity theft or scams. When you call a client or their authorized representative, you may identify yourself as calling from one of the following programs: Service Canada—Old Age Security; Service Canada—Canada Pension Plan; or Service Canada—International Operations. For CPPD , only identify that you are calling from “Service Canada—Canada Pension Plan”. Identifying “ CPPD ” or “Disability” could acknowledge the existence of the account. If, after you have identified yourself, a client is still hesitant to provide the information required to validate their identity, invite them to call the Service Canada Call Centre to confirm that you are a representative of Service Canada. Once the individual on the phone confirms that they are the client or the authorized representative you need to speak with, you may provide them with general details of why you are calling before initiating the security check. General details include stating: that the call is about information, documentation or a request that was received from the client or their authorized representative; or the month and year the information, documentation or request was received. Do not provide specific details of the information, documentation or request received until the client or their authorized representative is authenticated. Providing information on file or acknowledging the existence of a file before an individual is authenticated may result in a privacy breach. For suggested wording to use when speaking to a client before they are authenticated, Script Examples—Authenticating a Client or Their Authorized Representative

The security check is completed in 2 parts. Failure to complete these 2 parts constitutes a breach of security. Security Check—Part I Updated If a call centre staff member transfers a caller to you, ask them to provide the caller's name and to confirm if they have authenticated the caller's identity. If yes, you do not need to authenticate the caller again. If the caller has not been authenticated or if you made the call, the client or their authorized representative must correctly answer all questions in Part I of the security check, which includes providing their full name and details about their account number (i.e. their SIN or Client Identifier number). As an added security measure, a client or their authorized representative may request that a password be added to their account. A password can be added on the account only after the client or the authorized representative has been authenticated and is added as an important note in ITRDS . If a password has been added to the ITRDS notes, it must be provided by the client or their authorized representative during Part I of the security check. If you call the client or their authorized representative, you must obtain the last 3 digits of the client's account number. However, you must obtain the full account number when: you receive an Enquiry work item in PWS or a task in Cúram and call the client or their authorized representative back at a phone number that is not on the account; someone calls you directly; or a caller is transferred directly to you without prior interaction with call centre staff. Do not read aloud the information appearing in the systems (e.g. ITRDS , Cúram, PWS ) or on a client's file that you are using for authentication. You must ask the individual on the phone to provide the information or they must volunteer it. Do not acknowledge the existence of a client's CPP or OAS account before the completion of a successful security check. Only provide general information. Security check—Part II Updated If the client or their authorized representative successfully answers the questions in Security Check—Part I , you must obtain additional details about their CPP or OAS account. The client or their authorized representative must successfully answer at least 2 of the questions in Security Check—Part ll . Information from any available system (e.g. ITRDS , Cúram, PWS , Client Correspondence Tool (CCT), Government On Line (GOL)) can be used to authenticate the caller; however, the following restrictions on the release of information apply: For CPP, a PWS barcode or work item ID (prefaced by the letter "W") must not be used to authenticate the caller. For OAS, a task must not be used to authenticate the caller. Medical information cannot be disclosed by telephone. Do not call the client or their authorized representative if the systems are unavailable. If the client or their authorized representative calls you during a time when the systems are unavailable, advise them to call back later, when their identity can be authenticated. To review the list of possible questions, go to the Authenticating a client or their authorized representative section in the What you need to do of the Step by Step tab. Failed security check If an individual fails any part of the security check or confirms that they are an unauthorized third party, you must inform them that client information can only be given to the client or an authorized representative. If the individual requires further assistance, direct them as follows: If the individual called you directly, advise them to go to a Service Canada Centre to authenticate their identity. If you called the individual, advise them that you will contact the client or authorized representative that is on file by mail to obtain or provide the required information. For specific direction, go to the Failed security check section in the What you need to do of the Step by Step tab.
The following procedure provides guidance on authenticating individuals to ensure you are speaking with the correct client or their authorized representative during a phone call.

Client information cannot be provided to unauthorized third parties without the client's consent or valid documentation on file. Advise the individual that is seeking to become or claiming to be the client's authorized representative of the documentation that is required before the Department is able to communicate with them. Refer to Third Party Requests (Scenario) . Alternatively, advise the individual that the client can give their verbal consent to allow us to speak with them, if they call back with the client present and once the client is authenticated. Go to the Client asks that you speak with an unauthorized third party section above. Third Party Requests (Scenario) Update the client's notes in ITRDS to record details of your actions or decisions made on the account. Refer to ITRDS Notes—Review, Add and Delete (Action) . ITRDS Notes—Review, Add and Delete (Action) Complete the Telephone Call (ISP0112) form or relevant CPPD form to record: the date and time of the call; the reason for the call; the name of the third party; the third party's relationship to the client; that the third party was not authenticated; and the information provided to the individual during the call.

It is important to authenticate an individual before releasing personal information as a privacy breach occurs when there is improper or unauthorized disclosure of personal information. For more information, Privacy and Personal Information (Scenario) You may need to call a client or their authorized representative to obtain information about their CPP or OAS application or to clarify information on the file. You may also receive a voicemail or a call from a client or their authorized representative requesting information. Before discussing any information related to a client's account, you must conduct a security check to authenticate the individual's identity. You must also ensure that a third party is authorized to obtain information on a client's account. Third Party Requests (Scenario)

topic_title: Deeming a receipt date for a benefit due to incapacity
text: An application can be deemed to have been received on an earlier date when the incapacity provision is applied. The incapacity provision is extended to a child under the age of 18 (-18 child) or a child over the age of 18 (+18 child) who is listed on a CPPD benefits application when the disabled contributor is granted an earlier date of application due to incapacity. For a child aged between 18 and 25, the incapacity provision under the disabled contributor can only be applied if the child submits their own application within the prescribed timeframe. The incapacity provision can also be applied to the +18 child based on their own Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit application and claim of incapacity. topic_title: Protective dates under International Social Security Agreements
text: The protective date provision applies to most of Canada's International Social Security Agreements (ISSA). The provision stipulates that the date that a benefit application is received in one country is considered the date of application for the corresponding benefit in the other country, provided certain conditions are met. International Operations (IO) processing staff validate protective dates received under the ISSAs by ensuring the various conditions are met. Therefore, a protective date may only be considered as the receipt date of the application if it has been validated and provided by IO.

topic_title: Receipt date of an OAS or CPP benefit application
text: An applicant may request OAS or CPP benefits by completing and signing: an application for OAS or CPP benefits; or a written request for CPP benefits. For more information, Determine if an Application is Valid (Scenario) The date of receipt for paper applications is the date stamped on the application or written request for CPP benefits. For more information, Applications Date of Receipt (Policy) For information about the application, written request and supporting documents for a CPPD benefit application containing the signature of the applicant that can also conditionally protect the date of application, Applications Date of Receipt (Policy) To request the missing documents or information, CPPD—Determine if an Application or Request for Reconsideration is Complete (Scenario) If you subsequently receive the required information for a valid CPPD benefit application, within the applicable bring forward periods, use the initial date stamp on the application, written request or supporting document to protect the receipt date. Refer to Bring Forward (BF) (Action) and to Bring Forward (BF) (Action) Determine if an Application is Valid (Scenario) When Service Canada receives a paper OAS or CPP benefit application or a written request for CPP benefits, it is date stamped at the Service Canada Centre or Mail Processing Centre. A duplicate payment is issued to replace an original payment that a client reports as: lost; stolen; destroyed; not received; or not deposited into the designated account by the payment due date. You must also verify the following in the SPS and in the processing systems (e.g. Cúram, ITRDS or CPMS ): Standard Payment System user guide the original payment attempt status was Issued for the month or period for which the client claims non-receipt; the client is entitled to the payment; the payment has not been returned; the payment has not been cancelled; the payment has not already been replaced; and the payment address or direct deposit information is correct. a provincial government or a private insurer has not requested any portion of the payment. For more information on reimbursement to a province or municipality, refer to Reimbursement to Provincial Social Services Agencies, Workers' Compensation Program Agencies or Private Insurers (Scenario) . Reimbursement to Provincial Social Services Agencies, Workers' Compensation Program Agencies or Private Insurers (Scenario) If the client claims they have not received the payment, you can issue a duplicate payment if the original payment status is Issued or the original foreign cheque status is Returned (with reason Reclaimed Foreign Cheque and the Correspondence Indicator is N ). If the original payment status is Redeemed and the client requests a duplicate payment that was issued by cheque, you cannot issue a duplicate payment before the IRGOD investigates who redeemed the original payment. For Redeemed payments issued by direct deposit, the duplicate payment can be re-issued without requesting an IRGOD investigation. If a client redeems both an original and a duplicate payment (i.e. by cheque or direct deposit), the IRGOD will automatically investigate the situation and notify the Department to create an overpayment on the client's account. If the IRGOD sends a Journal Voucher Advice Notice to the Department, you must initiate the recovery of the overpayment immediately. Undertaking and indemnity declaration Before you can issue a duplicate payment, the client must complete and sign a PWGSC-TPSGC 535 form or a PWGSC-TPSGC 536 form when: the payment is for an OAS or a CPP benefit with a Cancelled or Suspended status; the payment is issued to a foreign bank account; the payment was issued to a client living outside of Canada; the payment is a one-time lump sum or an arrears payment; an estate claims non-receipt of a payment issued to the estate; the payment attempt status is Returned with reason Reclaimed Foreign Cheque and the Correspondence Indicator is N ; or the duplicate payment amount is more than $5,000. In this situation you must also obtain the following signed forms based on the method of payment: Original payment issued by cheque: Affidavit For Cheques over $5,000 issued by the Receiver General (PWGSC-TPSGC 540) form; and PWGSC-TPSGC 535 form. Original payment issued by direct deposit: Affidavit For Direct Deposit payments over $5,000 issued by the Receiver General ( PWGSC-TPSGC 546-3 (PDF, 1.7 MB) Download link ) form; and PWGSC-TPSGC 546-3 PWGSC-TPSGC 536 form. In all other cases, you can issue a duplicate payment without obtaining any signed form or written documentation from the client. By completing and signing any of the applicable forms, the client agrees to return the original, non-negotiated payment to the Receiver General of Canada if the payment comes into their possession. If the client claims their cheque is mutilated, the PWGSC-TPSGC 535 form serves as the client's confirmation that the original payment was destroyed and cannot be negotiated. Advise the client that if they cash both the original and duplicate payments, it will create an overpayment on their account. Undertaking and indemnity forms are processed as soon as they are received at the appropriate mail processing centre. Duplicate payments are created and loaded into the SPS immediately, unless an IRGOD investigation is required.

If the contributor meets the MQP, the amount of the DTH benefit depends on when the contributor dies. When the date of death is: On or after January 1, 2019 , the DTH benefit amount is a flat-rate amount of $2,500. On or after January 1, 2025 , if the deceased contributor did not receive a CPP or QPP RTR pension or DSB and there is no SVR pension payable as a result of their death, the DTH benefit also includes a top-up amount of $2,500 in addition to the flat-rate amount. This increases the maximum DTH benefit payment to $5,000. The deceased can have a Surviving Child's benefit payable. In addition, when a surviving spouse or common-law partner exists but does not apply for an SVR pension, the DTH benefit includes the top-up amount as there is no SVR pension payable. Between January 1, 1998 and December 31, 2018 —the DTH benefit amount is 6 times the amount of the deceased contributor's RTR pension at age 65, up to a maximum of $2,500. Before January 1, 1998 — the DTH benefit amount is the lesser of 6 times the amount of the deceased contributor's RTR pension at age 65 or 10% of the year's maximum pensionable earnings for the year in which the contributor died. For more information, refer to Amount of Death Benefit (Policy) and Amount of Death Benefit (Policy) Payment in Special Circumstances—Death Benefit (Policy)

text: If the applicant indicates that the deceased contributor had children born after December 31, 1958, you must determine if you need to send the applicant a post-mortem Request for a Child Rearing Provision (ISP-1640) form. Child Rearing Provision (Scenario)

topic_title: Does the applicant indicate the deceased contributor is divorced or separated?
text: If the applicant indicates the deceased contributor was divorced or separated and they do not meet Minimum Qualifying Period (MQP), send the Supply: Sending applications and information (ISS-6191) letter and How to Apply for a Canada Pension Plan Credit Split (ISP-1901A) form to the applicant if: there is no credit split in ITRDS or PWS ; and ITRDS notes do not indicate that the Department previously sent credit splitting information to the applicant. The Death ( DTH ) benefit is a flat-rate amount for all deceased contributors who meet the MQP with entitlement to an additional top-up amount when the deceased contributor meets the top-up eligibility criteria. A credit split has no effect on the amount of the DTH benefit with the exception of when there is the requirement of an International Social Security Agreement to qualify for the DTH benefit. The intent of the onus policy is to inform contributors who are separated or divorced of the credit split and the possible effect to their benefits. In this situation, you do not need to send a credit split information sheet. Refer to Application Management—Onus (Policy) and to the procedures for Application Management—Onus (Policy) Credit Split Application (Scenario)

topic_title: Does the applicant wish to withdraw their application?
text: If the applicant wishes to withdraw their DTH benefit application, the request must be received before the payment is issued. Withdraw an Application (Scenario)

topic_title: Does the application indicate the funeral was prepaid or the body of the deceased was donated to science?
text: If the applicant indicates the funeral was prepaid or the body of the deceased was donated to science, you must determine if you require additional documentation. Paying the Death Benefit (Work Tool)

topic_title: Does the application indicate there is a surviving spouse or common-law partner, but they have not yet applied for an SVR pension?
text: Effective January 1, 2025, if you receive a Death ( DTH ) benefit application indicating there is a surviving spouse or common-law partner, you must send an SVR pension application. Sending an application is not required if there is indication that one has already been sent or that the surviving spouse or common-law partner is already aware of applying for the SVR pension. After sending the SVR pension application, follow the bring forward guidelines to determine if you can pay the top-up amount when: the contributor meets the Minimum Qualifying Period for a DTH benefit; the deceased contributor did not receive a CPP or QPP RTR pension or DSB ; and an SVR pension application has not been received in PWS . In cases where the surviving spouse or common-law partner has passed away after the date of death of the deceased contributor, you must send a post-mortem SVR pension application to the surviving spouse or common-law partner's estate representative, individual representative or heir. Sending an application is not required if there is indication that one has already been sent or that the estate representative, individual representative or heir is aware of the benefit. If the DTH benefit flat-rate and top-up amounts are paid and an SVR pension application or post-mortem SVR pension application is received and approved, the top-up amount is considered an overpayment on the DTH benefit amount and must be recovered. Refer to Bring Forward (BF) (Action) and Bring Forward (BF) (Action) Departmental Receivables (Overpayments) (Scenario)

topic_title: Does the application indicate there is an estate but the applicant is not the executor?

topic_title: Does the application indicate who represents the deceased contributor for the purposes of filing income tax?
text: If the applicant provides their own personal contact information on the Application for CPP Death Benefit (ISP-1200) form or the online Death benefit application, the Deemed Person to Represent the Deceased Client for the Purpose of Issuing a T4A (OAS), T4A(P) and NR4 (ISP-1202) form is not required. You can set the applicant as the post-mortem business contact and indicate as an important note that the post-mortem business contact is only for tax slips purposes. If the applicant provides information for a third party, follow the normal process to determine the person to issue a T4 for filing the deceased contributor's income tax. If there is no ISP-1202 on file, send the form to the third party and update the notes; there is no requirement to bring forward for the return of the ISP-1202. For more information, Post-Mortem Applications and Forms (Scenario)

topic_title: Does the deceased contributor have valid QPP contributions?
text: If the deceased contributor has CPP and QPP contributions but was previously in pay for an RTR pension or a DSB from QPP, the DTH benefit amount must not include the top-up amount. If the deceased contributor had valid QPP contributions and if one of the following conditions applies, you must move the work item in Pensions Workload System Guide Internal link to the Dual Processing Unit, in Timmins, ON for processing: Pensions Workload System Guide The deceased contributor had QPP earnings only. The deceased contributor was in pay for an RTR pension or DSB at QPP at the time of death. The deceased contributor was not in pay at the time of death, but had a previously terminated DSB at QPP. The deceased contributor was already in pay for a CPP benefit and had dual contributions. The deceased contributor had QPP and CPP earnings and lived in Quebec at time of death. The deceased contributor had dual CPP and QPP earnings, lived outside Canada and their last province of residence was Québec. If you cannot confirm that the last province of residence was Québec, but can determine that their last contribution made was a QPP contribution, transfer the file to the Dual Processing Unit. Refer to the Pensions Workload System Guide Internal link and Dual Workflow Charts for CPP and CPPD Processors (PDF, 301 KB) Download link . Pensions Workload System Guide Dual Workflow Charts for CPP and CPPD Processors If all of the following conditions apply, you can process the application if the deceased contributor: had dual CPP and QPP earnings; was not in pay for an RTR pension or DSB benefit at QPP; was not in pay for a CPP benefit at Dual; and did not live in Québec at time of death. Complete the work item in PWS . If the deceased lived in Québec at the time of their death and had solely CPP contributions, move the application in PWS to the Fredericton processing centre for processing. For information on the Death ( DTH ) benefit eligibility requirements, Eligibility Requirements—Death Benefit (Policy) The MQP is met if the deceased contributor had unadjusted pensionable earnings in the lesser of: one third (1/3) of the total number of years in their contributory period, when it is 9 years or greater; 10 years; or 3 years, when the contributory period is less than 9 years. When a contributor does not appear to meet the MQP, you can use any of the following to help them meet it, if applicable: Disability exclusion; Child Rearing Provision; Credit Splitting; +65 Age Qualification Provision; or Social Security Agreements. Calculation of CPP Benefits (Knowledge) You must deny the application if: the full benefit has already been paid to the eligible applicant or applicants; the applicant submits a second application for the same deceased contributor; the deceased contributor did not meet MQP; the applicant did not submit the required documentation; or the applicant is not considered the eligible payee, based on the order of priority of payment. A deceased contributor who does not have enough CPP and QPP contributions to meet the MQP but lived or worked in another country that has an International Social Security Agreement (ISSA) with Canada may meet the MQP with the help of the agreement. These applications must be transferred to International Operations after the application has been processed in ITRDS . To determine if there is an existing ISSA with a country named on the DTH benefit application or if the agreement will help an applicant to qualify for the DTH benefit, refer to the Overview tab of the applicable country. To be an eligible payee for the Death ( DTH ) benefit, the applicant must be one of the following (in order of priority): The contributor's estate representative (executor, administrator, or legal representative). The institution or individual paying for the funeral (if no estate exists). The surviving spouse (if there is no estate or payer of funeral expenses). The next of kin (if there are none of the above). Where there is an executor, administrator, or legal representative of the estate, payment must be made to: The Estate of (the deceased contributor's name), c/o (the name of the executor, administrator, or legal representative). For all other applicants, payment is made to: For the Estate of (the deceased contributor's name). Payment is never made payable directly to the person's name only. If there is an estate, you can only make payment to someone else if the estate has not applied within 60 days of the contributor's death. However, you can make the payment before 60 days if the estate has submitted a letter stating that they will not be applying for the DTH benefit. If the contributor died before January 1, 2019, you can make the payment of the DTH benefit immediately to someone other than the estate if the amount is less than $2,387.00. You must still follow the order of priority for determining the payee. An applicant cannot waive their right to payment in favour of another payee. They must withdraw their application or provide a letter indicating they will not be applying for the DTH benefit. topic_title: International Operations—Is the Minimum Qualifying Period met without an International Social Security Agreement?
text: You must keep the Death benefit application for processing if one of the following applies: an International Social Security Agreement (ISSA) is required to meet the Minimum Qualifying Period (MQP); or the deceased contributor was in receipt of an RTR pension or a CPPD benefit by International Operations (IO). You must transfer the application to the Dual Processing Unit when: the deceased contributor falls under the jurisdiction of QPP and an ISSA is required to meet the MQP requirements; or the deceased contributor falls under the jurisdiction of QPP and an ISSA is not required to meet the MQP requirements. The Dual Processing Unit will transfer the application to Retraite Québec. topic_title: Is the application from a funeral home?
text: Canada Pension Plan legislation prohibits any attempt to assign the Death ( DTH ) benefit payment. CPP administration is under no obligation to pay a funeral home for expenses incurred. Payment of the DTH benefit to a funeral home is only done under extremely rare circumstances. When a funeral home insists on applying for a DTH benefit, it must provide details regarding the reasons, along with the name and address of the person who would be responsible for the funeral expenses. If you receive an application from a funeral home, send an enquiry for direction to the Business Expertise Request Tool (BERT) Internal link . Business Expertise Request Tool

text: The client's date of death must be recorded in the applicable system ( ITRDS or Cúram) as soon as the Department is informed. The date must match (year and month) for all programs. If the date of death has not been recorded or does not match for OAS, you must update ITRDS and notify the affected program, if applicable. For more information, Death Notification (Scenario)

topic_title: Is the death benefit applicant deceased?
text: A Death ( DTH ) benefit application cannot be processed if the applicant is deceased. An Indemnity Agreement (Old Age Security and Canada Pension Plan) (ISP-0425) form cannot be used to determine eligibility to the DTH benefit in scenarios when the DTH benefit applicant has since passed away. If you receive information that the DTH benefit applicant is deceased, you must administratively close the application. Review the contributor's file to determine if there is someone else who may be eligible for the DTH benefit and invite them to apply. Payee for the Death Benefit (Policy) For more information on how to administratively close an application, Determine if an Application is Valid (Scenario)

You must consider a presumption of death when a client disappears and remains absent from their customary location or home for an extended period, with or without apparent reason. When the Department confirms a client is dead, you must confirm the date of death and issue a Presumption of Death Certificate (ISP-3511) form to approve or stop certain CPP and OAS benefits. A Service Canada manager has the authority to issue an ISP-3511 form and declare the date on which a client's death is presumed to have occurred. Presumption of Death (Action)

topic_title: Is the deceased contributor over the age of 70 and eligible for a post-mortem RTR pension?
text: Effective January 1, 2025, if you receive a Death ( DTH ) benefit application and the deceased contributor is over the age of 70 and eligible for a post-mortem RTR pension, you must send a post-mortem RTR pension application to the deceased contributor's estate representative, individual representative or heir. Sending an application is not required if there is indication that one was already sent or that the deceased contributor's estate representative, individual representative or heir is aware of the benefit. After sending the post-mortem RTR pension application, follow the bring forward guidelines to determine if you can pay the top-up amount when: the contributor meets the Minimum Qualifying Period for a DTH benefit; the deceased contributor did not receive a CPP or QPP RTR pension or DSB ; and there is no SVR pension payable to a surviving spouse or common-law partner. If the DTH benefit flat-rate and top-up amounts are paid and a post-mortem RTR pension application is received and approved, the top-up amount is considered an overpayment on the DTH benefit amount and must be recovered. Departmental Receivables (Overpayments) (Scenario)

topic_title: Is there a CPPD benefits application on hold?
text: If there is a CPPD benefits application on hold in ITRDS awaiting a medical adjudication, contact the CPPD processing unit. You must advise them that the client is deceased and that there is a Death ( DTH ) benefit waiting to be processed. The CPPD application must be adjudicated before you can data capture the DTH benefit application. If the deceased contributor is eligible for the CPPD benefit, they are only eligible to receive the DTH benefit flat-rate amount and are not eligible for the top-up amount.

topic_title: Is there an application from a trust company or law office acting on behalf of an Estate or another Death benefit payee?
text: If you receive an application from a trust company or a law office acting on behalf of an estate, person responsible for the funeral expense, survivor or next of kin, the eligible applicant must sign the application. However, you can communicate with the trust company or law office if you have authorization from their client. Third Party Contact—Non-Payee (Scenario)

topic_title: Is this an application from a public guardian or public trustee?
text: A Public Guardian or Public Trustee may apply for the Death ( DTH ) benefit in one of two ways: as an administrator appointed by the court; or as the organization responsible for funeral expenses. If they apply as the administrator appointed by the court, then there is an estate even if there is no will. The DTH benefit cheque is made payable to " The Estate of (the deceased contributor's name)" in care of the administrator appointed by the court. If they are applying as the organization responsible for funeral expenses, the payment is made to the Public Guardian or Public Trustee, " For the Estate of (the deceased contributor's name)".

topic_title: Did the Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit eligibility requirements cease after the disabled contributor turned 65?
text: Effective January 1, 2025, when a DSB converts to RTR or when the PRDB ends at the age of 65, a child in pay at that time remains entitled to the Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit ( DCCB ), provided they continue to meet all eligible criteria. If the eligibility requirements cease any time after the disabled contributor turns 65, there is no longer entitlement to the DCCB (i.e. the child-contributor relationship between the child and the +65 disabled contributor ends or the +18 child is no longer in full-time or part-time attendance). text: -18 child's benefit To receive a -18 Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit ( DCCB ), the payee must be: a disabled contributor who has decision-making responsibility of the child and a minimum 20% of the parenting time; the other parent, custodian, guardian or agency who has decision-making responsibility and parenting time of a disabled contributor's child when the child lives less than 20% of the time with the disabled contributor; or a -18 child who is not living with a parent, custodian, guardian or agency who exercises normal parental control, under exceptional circumstances. For more information, go to the Is the -18 child requesting to be paid directly? section below. The disabled contributor is presumed to have decision-making responsibility of the -18 child unless they have less than 20% of the parenting time. For more information on determining the payee for a child -18, Payee for the Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit (Policy) Initial application When you receive an initial application, complete one of the following actions, depending on the situation, to identify the payee: Situation Action Initial application with the disabled contributor's attestation of decision-making responsibility and parenting time. When the disabled contributor applies for the DCCB indicating they have decision-making responsibility and parenting time of the child, call them to determine if the applicant has full or shared or joint decision-making responsibility and parenting time, if additional information on living arrangements is not submitted with their application. If the disabled contributor has full decision-making responsibility and there is no evidence to the contrary, pay the child's benefit to the disabled contributor. If the disabled contributor has shared or joint decision-making responsibility, you must send the Development – Decision Making Responsibility (ISS-4511) letter to determine if the disabled contributor has at least 20% parenting time, if additional information on living arrangements is not submitted with their application. Situation Action Initial application without the disabled contributor's attestation of decision-making responsibility and parenting time. When it is not indicated who has decision-making responsibility and parenting time, contact the disabled contributor to confirm. If the disabled contributor confirms they have full decision-making responsibility and parenting time, a written statement or an official legal document attesting this may be accepted. Situation Action Initial application and the disabled contributor does not have decision-making responsibility and parenting time. When the disabled contributor indicates they do not have decision-making responsibility and parenting time of the child, refer to Protection and Disclosure of Personal Information for Disabled Contributors . The DCCB is a monthly flat rate benefit payable to the dependent child directly, the disabled contributor or the person or agency who has decision-making responsibility and parenting time of the disabled contributor's dependent child. A DCCB is paid to or on behalf of a: child under the age of 18 (-18 child); or child over the age of 18 (+18 child). The child is always the beneficiary and remains so regardless of their age and who the payee is. The tax slip is always issued in the child's name. As of January 2025, if the disabled contributor has a dependent child under the age of 25 receiving a DCCB , their dependent child may still be entitled to receive the DCCB even after the disabled contributor's CPPD benefit ends at age 65.

To protect the privacy and personal information of the disabled contributor, you may only initiate contact with the child or the individual or the agency that has decision-making responsibility and parenting time for the child when the disabled contributor has provided their written consent. If you receive a DCCB application from a child, the individual or agency who has decision-making responsibility and parenting time of said child, and the disabled contributor did not provide written consent, you must process the application. This procedure demonstrates how to validate the individual or institution responsible for the funeral expenses and the amount of the funeral expenses. This information determines who is eligible to receive the DTH benefit and the amount payable.

Review the DTH benefit application to confirm the applicant is applying as the individual or institution responsible for the funeral expenses. Review any other DTH benefit application on file or in PWS to determine if another applicant in the payment hierarchy may be eligible for the DTH benefit or if a split payable is required. Determine if the applicant indicated there is a will. If no , go to Step 4 . Step 4 If yes , ensure that one of the following situations apply: more than 60 days passed since the date of death and the executor or administrator has been sent a letter inviting them to apply for the DTH benefit; there are written statements on file indicating that the executor or administrator are not applying for the DTH benefit; or the executor or administrator chose the option not to apply in question D2 on the Application for CPP Death Benefit (ISP-1200) form. Determine if the applicant is applying as the individual or institution responsible for the funeral expenses by reviewing: question C2 on the ISP-1200 form; an applicable question on the XXX/Canada Agreement - Application for Canadian Old Age, Retirement and Survivor's Benefits (ISP-5054-XXX) form; or the online application field question Are you the person responsible for the funeral expenses? . If applicable, review all funeral invoices, written statements, receipts and contracts the applicant provided to ensure they include the following information: name of the funeral home; name of the deceased; individual or institution responsible for the funeral expenses; type of expenses incurred; and amount of the funeral expenses incurred. If the applicant indicates the funeral was pre-paid or the body was donated to science, ensure there is proof on file (e.g. pre-paid contract or a letter from the medical examiner indicating the body was donated).

If eligibility to a DTH benefit is approved, a payment in the amount of the expenses can be made to the individual or institution responsible for the funeral expenses when: there is no estate; the executor or administrator of the estate has not applied for the DTH benefit within 60 days after the date of death; or the executor or administrator of the estate provided: information on the Application for CPP Death Benefit (ISP-1200) form indicating they will not apply for the DTH benefit; or a signed written statement indicating they will not apply for the DTH benefit. On or after January 1, 2019, the DTH benefit payment is a flat-rate amount of $2,500 when the contributor meets the Minimum Qualifying Period for the DTH benefit. Effective January 1, 2025, if the deceased contributor did not receive a CPP or QPP RTR pension or DSB and there is no SVR pension payable as a result of their death, the DTH benefit also includes a top-up amount of $2,500 in addition to the flat-rate amount. This increases the maximum DTH benefit payment to $5,000. The deceased can have a Surviving Child's benefit payable. In addition, when a surviving spouse or common-law partner exists, but does not apply for an SVR pension the DTH benefit includes the top-up amount as there is no SVR pension payable. The maximum amount the Department can pay to an individual or institution responsible for the funeral expenses is $5,000. The Department cannot exceed that amount. When eligibility to the DTH benefit is established by using an International Social Security Agreement, entitlement to the flat rate may be prorated based on the deceased contributor's actual number of contributory years. Entitlement to the top up is also prorated, if applicable. A write-off under the Financial Administration Act is an accounting action that removes, in whole or in part, a legally enforceable debt from the accounts receivable records. A write-off does not mean that the debt is forgiven. Since the debt will continue to exist, a write-off simply defers the recovery so that the debt can be collected in the future, except if you are recommending a write-off in any one of these 3 situations: a balance remains after a compromise settlement is accepted; a balance remains after the closure of a consumer proposal; or a balance remains after a bankruptcy discharge is granted. Once the debt or any remaining balance is written off, it cannot be collected at a future date as the debtor is released from the obligation to repay the debt and the debt no longer exists. For more information, refer to Compromise Settlement (Scenario) and Compromise Settlement (Scenario) Bankruptcy (Scenario) An overpayment should only be written-off when every possible effort to recover or collect the debt is exhausted. For more information, refer to Overpayments—Write-Offs (Policy) and Overpayments—Write-Offs (Policy) Overpayments—Key Principles (Policy) To write off a debt, you must make a recommendation to the Chief Financial Officer Branch (CFOB) via the CFOB F&A Portal External link . Only the CFOB has the authority to approve the write-off of a debt. CFOB F&A Portal Once approved, the recommendation is sent directly to the Public Sector Collections and Disbursements system. The following are common examples of when to recommend a write-off as there is potential to recover the debt in the future: the debtor is deceased and there is no known estate or person responsible for the deceased debtor's affairs (e.g. no response to the Department's request for repayment when sent to the deceased's last known address); the debtor is a non-resident (e.g. debtor resides outside of Canada and currently does not have residential ties with Canada) and there are no apparent means of collecting the debt at this time; the debtor cannot be located; the debtor is experiencing long-term hardship with the possibility of future recovery; the Department determined the debt was the result of misrepresentation and it cannot be recovered despite all collection attempts; or the debtor has a debt arising from a conviction of fraud and it cannot be recovered despite all collection attempts.

If the write-off request is for multiple overpayments, complete a separate form for each program and each benefit. Refer to the following examples to determine if you must submit multiple forms: If a client is in pay for an OAS pension and the Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS) benefit and payments are made after their date of death, the total amount of the OAS pension and GIS benefit is one benefit payment. If a client has a GIS benefit and Allowance benefit overpayment determined due to a change in marital status, the amount of each debt is treated separately as they are separate benefit payments. If a client has a Disability benefit and a Retirement ( RTR ) pension overpayment due to a change to their Record of Earnings (ROE), the amount of each debt is treated separately as they are separate benefit payments. If a client is in pay for a combined RTR and Survivor ( SVR ) pension and payments are made after their date of death, the total amount of the RTR pension and SVR pension is one benefit payment. If a client has an RTR pension and Post-Retirement Benefit ( PRB ) overpayment due to a change to their ROE, the total amount of the RTR pension and PRB is one benefit payment. If a client has an RTR pension and Post-Retirement Disability Benefit ( PRDB ) overpayment due to a change to their ROE, the total amount of the RTR pension and PRDB is one benefit payment. If a client has a combined RTR / SVR pension and PRDB overpayment due to a change to their ROE, the total amount of the RTR pension, SVR pension and PRDB is one benefit payment.

text: If the contributor's or the child's account has a Program Exception Process (PEP) status, you must determine if the surviving child's benefit application must be transferred to the Program Exception Processing Unit. Confirm the Office of Control (OCON) on the Client Status screen. If the deceased contributor has an International Operations (IO) OCON, transfer the application to the applicable IO office. The IO unit will take any required follow-up action. If the Death ( DTH ) benefit has a PEP status only because it was paid the DTH benefit top-up by the Triennial reform processing team, do not transfer an SVR pension or Surviving Child's benefit application to the Program Exception Processing Unit. You must process these applications in your region. text: A -18 Surviving Child's benefit application can be submitted by: the individual or agency who has decision-making responsibility and parenting time of the child; or the -18 child of a deceased contributor. The portion of the benefit that is payable when the child reaches age 18 is made directly to the child if they are in part-time or full-time attendance at a recognized educational institution.

Add, adjust, modify, approve, remove or reactivate a departmental receivable write-off in CPMS.

A departmental receivable is also referred to as a debt or an overpayment. A write-off is the removal of a full or partial uncollectible dollar amount from the accounts receivable. The debt is removed from the accounts receivable until the Department is able to recover it. You can only write off the debt when every attempt to collect the departmental receivable has been made. You can apply any combination of write-offs and remissions to the same departmental receivable. Separate users must add and approve a write-off. You must complete the Overpayment Remission and Write-off Decision Under $25,000 (ISP0102) form or the Remission or Write-Off Review Request Summary Over $25,000 (ISP0106) form using the appropriate Remission and Write-Off Authority Reason Codes . The completed form must be verified and approved by the delegated authority. Refer to ADM BISB Assigned Canada Pension Plan and Old Age Security Functions (PDF, 677 KB). Remission and Write-Off Authority Reason Codes ADM BISB Assigned Canada Pension Plan and Old Age Security Functions Add a write-off When you add a write-off, CPMS sets its Status to Pending and its Status Reason to N/A until it is approved. A pending write-off does not impact the following: Original Debt Amount ; Adjusted Debt Amount ; Recovered Amount ; Balance Owed ; Projected End Date ; or Receivable Status . The Remission/Write Off indicator updates to Y on the Departmental Receivables Summary screen and the Account Overview screen. Adjust a write-off This is the amount by which you increase or decrease the write-off. For example, if the original amount is $200.00, but should be $250.00, the adjustment amount is $50.00. Approve a write-off When you approve a write-off, its Status changes to Granted , and the write-off appears in the Write Offs block of the Departmental Receivable Remissions/Write Offs screen. The Original Debt Amount , Recovered Debt Amount and Balance Owed do not change when you approve the write-off. Remove a write-off When you remove a write-off, CPMS sets its Status to Removed and its Status Reason to User Error . To view the original write-off reason, click on Reason Details or Expand All within the Write Offs information block. The Remission/Write Off indicator on the Departmental Receivables and Account Overview screens displays Y . The Receivable Status changes to Active when a benefit is in pay. The recovery of the receivable then resumes, and the recovery rate automatically applies to all pending payables. Reactivate a write-off Reactivating a write-off makes the funds accessible to the user for collection or remission.

topic_title: An individual applies for an RTR pension after their DSB application is denied
text: If an individual applies for an RTR pension within 90 days of being informed that their DSB application has been denied, the DSB application can be used to deem and protect the RTR pension application receipt date. All conditions of eligibility for the RTR pension must be met at the effective date. If the individual appeals the denial of the DSB , you must extend the 90-day time limit for submission of the RTR pension application and protect the effective date for each level of appeal that the individual chooses to raise. The effective date should be the later of the month after the DSB application was received or the month after the client reached aged 60. For more information, Applications Date of Receipt (Policy)

topic_title: An individual applies for an RTR pension and appeals the DSB cessation decision
text: If an individual applies for an RTR pension within 90 days of being informed that their DSB has been terminated, the month in which the DSB ceased can deem and protect the date of the application for the RTR pension. If the individual appeals the cessation of the DSB , you must extend the 90-day time limit for submission of the RTR pension application and protect the effective date for each level of appeal that the individual chooses to raise. When an individual submits an RTR pension application and requests a reconsideration of the decision leading to the cessation of the DSB , you must process the RTR pension application immediately. All conditions of eligibility for the RTR pension must be met at the effective date. You must recover the overpayment of DSBs from the RTR pension arrears payment. If the reconsideration of the decision is in favour of the individual and you must reinstate the DSB , you must also cancel the RTR pension according to the CPP regulations and collect the RTR overpayment from any DSB arrears payment. As of January 1, 2019, the Department began phasing in the CPP enhancement, a new component of the CPP. The enhancement is not a separate benefit, but rather a top-up to the original, now referred to as the base component of the CPP. This means working Canadians will receive higher benefits in exchange for making higher contributions. Before January 2019, the RTR pension replaced one quarter (25%) of the average monthly pensionable earnings. This average is based on an individual's work earnings up to the year's maximum pensionable earnings set by CPP. The CPP enhancement increases this to one third (33.33%) of the average pensionable earnings. Individuals will not see the full impact of enhancement before 2065, but their pension will increase based on how much and for how long they contribute to the enhanced CPP. Individuals will get the full increase if they make the maximum contributions to the enhanced CPP for 40 years. The enhanced and base components of the CPP are intended to work seamlessly together. That means there is no separate application process to receive the enhanced component of CPP benefits. The eligibility criteria for CPP benefits are not affected by the enhancement as only the base component is used to determine eligibility and the minimum qualifying period for CPP benefits. The current formula used to calculate the combined benefits under the base CPP continues to apply. However, there is no maximum placed on the enhanced component of a combined SVR and RTR pension or of a combined SVR pension and DSB . For more information, CPP Enhancement (Knowledge)

topic_title: Scenarios requiring Program Exception Processing status
text: The following special handling cases require the application to be forwarded to the Program Exception Processing Unit in St. John's NL for processing. Transfer Files and Work Items (Scenario) Retirement QPP DSB start date incorrectly used in CPP RTR pension calculation When a client applies for a CPP RTR pension and was in receipt of a DSB through QPP only, ITRDS incorrectly includes the first month of DSB in the contributory period rather than excluding it. The Program Exception Process (PEP) will be required. Beneficiary turns 65 during DSB waiting period When a client is granted a DSB , the contributory period ends with the Date of Onset (DOO) for calculating that DSB entitlement. There is a 4-month waiting period before the DSB begins to be paid. When a client turns 65 during the waiting period, there are no DSBs payable. The month after the DOO to the month of the 65th birthday should be excluded from the contributory period when calculating entitlement to any future benefits (e.g. RTR pension, Death benefit and/or SVR pension); this is the Disability Exclusion. When the RTR pension is calculated, ITRDS is not dropping the DSB months after the DOO to the month of the client's 65th birthday in the calculation. PEP intervention is required. All benefits Accounts identified by the Federal Courts Whenever a Federal Court ruling determines that a benefit or pension will be paid despite not meeting eligibility requirements, the file must be forwarded to the Program Exception Processing Unit as ITRDS rules must be overridden. Account with any benefit pre-1983 with refunded contributions on record of earnings Before 1983, contribution refunds were not considered when calculating Unadjusted Pensionable Earnings (UPE). When calculating the UPE, ITRDS doubles some earnings. In addition, subsequent benefits may also be incorrectly calculated. Benefits with credit split and previous DSB before 1987 When a credit split is approved, earnings for any month within the joint contributory period are divided. If a DSB is or was payable, the contributory period ends with the DOO. Before 1987, the contributory period ended with the start of the DSB . If the DSB was effective before 1987, ITRDS incorrectly excluded the 3 months between the DOO and effective date of the DSB from the credit splitting process. Any benefits (e.g. RTR pension) processed subsequently will be incorrectly calculated or re-calculated. Benefit where re-adjudication would remove eligibility—Investigation required Scenario 1 Accounts currently in pay are re-adjudicated in a pre-production environment to determine the impact of a re-adjudication (i.e. to determine the impact of new earnings). These accounts require review before terminating or denying a benefit as a result of re-adjudication. If an account is re-adjudicated and the client's benefit is denied or terminated, the only solution to change the benefit (including related benefits) to in pay status is to PEP the account. Scenario 2 During ongoing adjudication and maintenance of accounts, client benefits will automatically re-adjudicate. This can result in the denial of an existing in pay benefit. Additional investigation is required to determine the validity of the denial and the only solution to change the benefit back to in pay status is to PEP the account. Scenario 3 When an account is either identified in advance (as in Scenario 1 above) or through ongoing adjudication (as in Scenario 2 above), and the affected benefit is not in pay status (i.e. it is inactive), denial of that inactive benefit as a result of re-adjudication can affect the benefit rate of subsequent benefits. Any valid receivables are sent to Public Sector Collections and Disbursements for collection. To prevent confusion and to protect benefit rates, the denied benefit must be set-up as a PEP account.

topic_title: When can an applicant or third party apply?
text: The applicant or third party can submit an application up to 12 months before the date they want their RTR pension to start. For more information, Eligibility Requirements—Retirement Pension

You must build a relationship between the primary contributor's account and the beneficiary's account. This interrelationship is required because eligibility is based on contributions made by the primary contributor. For example, a CPP contributor dies and their spouse submits an SVR pension application and a Surviving Child's benefit application. The spouse has decision-making responsibility and parenting time of the deceased's children. To process the applications, the following interrelationships are needed: a spousal interrelationship between the deceased contributor and the spouse (survivor); and a Dependent to Parent interrelationship between each child and the deceased contributor. After creating an interrelationship, it must be updated whenever there is a life change (e.g. separation, change in decision-making responsibility and parenting time) as it may impact adjudications. You must fully understand how and when interrelationships are used in the adjudication process to properly maintain existing accounts. For example, depending on the nature of a child-contributor relationship, when decision-making responsibility and parenting time for a child changes, you may need to modify the interrelationship as well as maintain payee information. When a survivor is receiving a benefit and the child is used as the qualifier for the benefit, the interrelationship between the parent and the child may remain but the dependency can end. This means that the child may have gone to live with someone else, left school (e.g. child is over the age of 18 (+18 child)), died, etc. Therefore, the dependency period ends between the survivor and the child, but the interrelationship remains. topic_title: Is there a marital status discrepancy between programs? New
text: When the Department receives information on an updated marital status, it is important to make the updates for the marital status on both the individual's account and the associated account. It must also match the marital status found in OAS and CPP. If the marital status is not recorded or does not match for all programs, you must notify the other programs by following your existing procedures. Changes to an individual's marital status can result in an underpayment or overpayment to an individual's account or associated accounts. If there is conflicting information obtained from a client, the file may need to be sent to the Integrity Services Branch for further investigation. For more information, Referral Process for Administrative Investigations (Scenario)

The interrelationship must be updated when life events change the client's interrelationships, as they will continue to affect both eligibility and entitlement. Modify an interrelationship to: add an end date to a relationship (needed if a new relationship type is identified); correct information that was previously captured (e.g. incorrect date of marriage); and add a new relationship or marital status (e.g. contributor goes from married to divorced). When a date of death is added to a client's profile, the system will use the date of death to update the end date for all spousal relationships existing on the client's record and related accounts. If the interrelationship is added after the date of death is entered on the deceased's client profile, you must manually enter the end date for all affected relationships. When establishing and entering relationship periods, ensure you are entering the correct dates. The system will prevent overlapping periods within the same interrelationship but not between non-interrelated individuals (e.g. Fred and Wilma's marriage period could overlap with Fred and Betty's).

When you change or add information to a client's account (e.g. date of divorce), ITRDS readjudicates the account and the results are visible immediately. If the amended data creates an adjudication event, you must review the account's Benefits screen where the change was made, as well as all related accounts, to ensure that you achieved the expected results. You must also review CPMS to identify any accounts that may have been affected by the update to the amount of the benefits from accounts related to that of the client. ITRDS does not automatically readjudicate accounts with benefits that have a Program Exception Process (PEP) or Super PEP status. The deceased contributor must meet the Minimum Qualifying Period for a spouse or common-law partner to qualify for a Survivor's Benefit. You can perform a Survivor's Benefit simulation on the surviving spouse's account to: determine if the deceased contributor has sufficient earnings; calculate entitlement; and identify which is the greater of the two survivor benefits. ITRDS uses the data stored in the client's profile with the information that you enter when you perform a data capture simulation. A data capture simulation performed in ITRDS does not affect the client's current benefits. ITRDS can only simulate the data capture of one benefit at a time. As of August 25, 2025, the data capture simulation results have been updated to include the calculations of the second additional earnings and contributions of the CPP enhancement. When a data capture simulation for combined benefits is required and one benefit is already in pay, ITRDS can simulate the data capture of the other benefit and provide a combined benefit amount. When a data capture simulation for combined benefits is required and no benefits are in pay, you must perform separate data capture simulations for each benefit. The results from the individual simulations can then be used in the Canada Pension Plan Calculation Module for manual calculations to obtain the combined benefit dollar amount. You must create all interrelationships before performing the Survivor’s Benefit data capture simulation. If the proof required to support the interrelationship is unavailable at the time of the simulation, add an unproven interrelationship to allow a simulation session. You must detach the interrelationship once you complete the simulation. The child's birth certificate must identify the contributor as a parent. Natural child of a disabled contributor A natural child is considered the child of a disabled contributor, born before or after the date when the contributor's disability benefit was approved. Child who becomes a ward of an agency, such as Children's Aid or Social Services, after birth A child cannot be considered for a child's benefit based on the death or disability of a foster parent. The foster parent is paid by the agency to care for the child. The benefit cannot be paid to the foster parent or parents because they do not have decision-making responsibility of the child—it is the agency that has decision-making responsibility of the child. An agency can be considered for a child's benefit on the death or disability of a legal parent. The child's benefit can be paid to the agency or authority that has decision-making responsibility on behalf of such a child if all other requirements are met.

Students who cannot remain at school or university full-time or part-time because of an illness can still be eligible for benefits. To determine if they are eligible, the student must submit the Canada Pension Plan Illness Certificate (ISP-1403) form. If a student was unable to resume full-time or part-time attendance at the start of an academic year, entitlement to benefits can still exist. To be entitled, the student must submit an ISP-1403 form and resume attendance immediately after the period of illness. If the student is absent for the entire year, they will only be entitled to benefits if they resume full-time or part-time attendance in the following academic year and submit a second ISP-1403 form to support the entire period of the absence (including the vacation period). If a student has not started an education program (instead of being unable to resume attending one), there is no entitlement to benefits, regardless of health. Absences that occur within an academic year If the student was absent due to an illness occurring within an academic year, they must submit a new Canada Pension Plan Child's Benefit Application and Declaration for a Student Over 18 years of Age in Attendance at School or University (ISP-1402) form confirming that they have resumed full-time or part-time studies. If the student does not return to school after the illness, they are only entitled to the benefits during the period of illness. Absences that last until the end of an academic year The student is entitled to benefits if their ISP-1403 form is valid until the end of the academic year, including the normal school vacation period. Absences that extend into the next academic year The student is entitled to benefits if their ISP-1403 form is valid for the entire current academic year, including the normal school vacation period. The student is also entitled to benefits from the start of the next academic year until the end of the period of illness if they resume full-time attendance sometime during that academic year. To confirm they have returned to full-time or part-time attendance, the student must submit a new ISP-1402 form. When a contributor's CPPD benefit stops while the dependent child is absent from school or university due to illness As of January 1, 2025, when a disabled contributor's CPPD benefit ceases because they reach age 65, the eligibility to the Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit ( DCCB ) may be extended for the disabled contributor's child. For more information, Children's Benefits After CPPD Beneficiary Reaches Age 65 (Scenario) In all other situations, when a contributor is no longer eligible for the CPPD benefit, the DCCB also stops. If a disabled contributor's child was absent from school due to illness but was receiving the benefit because they submitted the ISP-1403 form, payment stops the same month that the CPPD benefit ends. If a contributor's CPPD benefit stops and their child is absent from school or university due to illness, the child is eligible for benefits up until the cessation date of the CPPD benefit. To be eligible they must: resume full-time or part-time attendance during that year or the next school year; and submit an ISP-1403 form. A child turns 25 while absent from school or university due to illness If a child who is turning 25 years old in the academic year but is unable to start school or is absent due to an illness, they are eligible for a child's benefit from the start of that school year until the month of their 25th birthday. To maintain eligibility, they must: submit an ISP-1402 form to prove that they resumed full-time attendance during that year or the next school year; and submit an ISP-1403 form.

There are situations that fall under the category of alternative schooling. The following situations are just some of these types of schooling. Off-site attendance The Department can consider a child as being in full-time or part-time attendance without the child being physically present at the institution. CPP considers the child to be in full-time attendance through the use of technology if the school considers them to be full-time. CPP considers the child to be in part-time attendance when the school confirms that the student is taking courses that make up 20% of a full course load through the use of technology. Online courses Students have the opportunity to complete their courses via the internet. The students are closely monitored to ensure that they are fulfilling the course requirements within the specified timeframes. Students participating in courses taught via the internet must usually meet the same deadlines and write the same tests or exams as students taking the same courses in a classroom setting. In these situations, CPP usually considers the full-time course load requirements to be the same for both students. Correspondence courses If a student is taking correspondence courses, they must submit the Canada Pension Plan Child's Benefit Application and Declaration for a Student Over 18 years of Age in Attendance at School or University (ISP-1402) form at the beginning of the course and at every 4-month interval. The school must also provide a written statement proving that the student is taking correspondence courses. Home schooling When a child is home schooled, the parent or guardian acts as the child's primary educational facilitator. The school or school board must approve the student's home-schooling program and provide the curriculum and examinations. Students who are home schooled must follow the same requirements for full-time or part-time school attendance as students that are attending in person. Evening courses Students taking evening courses must meet the same requirements as those taking courses during the day to be considered in full-time attendance. That is, they must be enrolled in courses that constitute a full-time course load recognized by the educational institution. Students taking evening courses must meet the same requirements as those taking courses during the day to be considered in part-time attendance. That is, they must be enrolled in courses that make up at least 20% of a full course load recognized by the educational institution. Multiple institutions - day and evening A child who attends more than one educational institution or who is enrolled in a combination of daytime and evening courses can be considered to be in full-time attendance. If additional guidance is needed to determine whether the child meets the full-time attendance requirements, send an enquiry via the National Business Expertise Tool (NEXO) Internal link . Apprenticeship programs will now be accepted as eligible full-time or part-time school attendance.

If a child does not have enough credits to complete the requirements for a certificate, diploma or degree, they may need to enroll in additional courses to graduate or complete the program. The child is considered to be in full-time attendance if they are deemed to be full-time by an acceptable educational institution, regardless of the number of enrolled courses. The child is considered to be in part-time attendance if they are enrolled in courses that make up at least 20% of a full course load as recognized by an acceptable educational institution.

topic_title: Did the child leave school or university?
text: If you received notification from the child that they are no longer attending school and that their absence is unrelated to a period of illness, you must: modify the relevant school attendance period on the School Declaration screen to terminate the child's benefit at the end of the month of their last day of attendance; and send the Benefit Status - Cancel or Terminate (ISS-4559) letter or Benefit Status - Cancel or Terminate - DSB non-medical (ISS-4592) letter notifying the child of the termination. When you cannot modify the relevant school attendance period, you must notify the following units in the following circumstances: If the child's benefit has a Program Exception Process (PEP) status, you must notify the Program Exception Processing Unit in St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador. If the child's benefit is being paid under an International Social Security Agreement and an International Operations (IO) processor must modify the relevant period of full-time or part-time attendance, you must notify the responsible IO processing unit. If the child is receiving a Disabled Contributor's Child Post-Retirement benefit or Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit by manual priority payment, you must notify the responsible specialized processing centre. The responsible processor must then terminate the benefit and send the ISS-4559 letter or ISS-4592 letter to notify the child of the termination. The benefit is terminated at the end of the month when the student last meets the full-time or part-time requirements. Modifying the school attendance end date terminates the benefit. Declaration of Attendance at School or University—Add, Modify or Delete in ITRDS (Action) If you receive notification from someone other than the child that they are no longer attending school full-time or part-time, or you have received notification that the child left school due to illness but you have not received a completed Canada Pension Plan Illness Certificate (ISP-1403) form, you must suspend the child's benefit. Send the child the Development - School Attendance (ISS-4512) letter and request completion of Canada Pension Plan Child's Benefit Application and Declaration for a Student Over 18 years of Age in Attendance at School or University (ISP-1402) form and a completed ISP-1403 form, if applicable, from the child to confirm their attendance or that they have left school or university. topic_title: Did the child's attendance change from full-time to part-time or vice versa?
text: If you receive notification from a child that their attendance changed from full-time to part-time or vice versa, you may need to forward the information to another processing unit to update the child's account. A change in attendance must be handled by the following units in the following circumstances: If the child's benefit has a Program Exception Process (PEP) status or a Super PEP status, the file must be sent to the Program Exception Processing Unit in St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador. A Super PEP user must modify the child's benefit entitlement and attendance from full-time to part-time. If the child's benefit has a PEP status and is paid under an International Social Security Agreement, the file must be sent to the responsible International Operations (IO) processing unit. An IO processor must modify the relevant period of attendance. If the child is receiving a Disabled Contributor's Child Post-Retirement benefit or Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit by manual priority payment, the file must be sent to the responsible specialized processing centre. To change the child's benefit entitlement based on their attendance, the responsible processor must: modify the relevant full-time school attendance period on the School Declaration screen by adding an end date, if applicable; add a new part-time school attendance period on the School Declaration screen, if applicable; and send a letter to notify the child of the change to their monthly entitlement.

topic_title: Extension of eligibility to the Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit after the disabled contributor turns 65
text: Effective January 1, 2025, eligibility to the Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit ( DCCB ) can be extended for the child of a disabled contributor who was receiving a DSB or PRDB and has their 65th birthday in January 2025 or later. For DCCB to continue, the child must be entitled to the benefits in the month of the disabled contributor's 65th birthday. A +18 child must be attending school or university full-time or part-time, or if absent, their absence was due to illness and they have submitted supporting documentation. If the child was not entitled to DCCB the month of the disabled contributor's 65th birthday, there is no entitlement to DCCB even if the child returns to school sometime after the contributor reaches age 65. The DCCB must be denied. For more information, refer to Children's Benefits After CPPD Beneficiary Reaches Age 65 (Scenario) and Children's Benefits After CPPD Beneficiary Reaches Age 65 (Scenario) Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit Application (Scenario)
