The OAS pension, ALW benefit and ALWS benefit are based, in part, on the applicant's years of Canadian residence (actual or deemed). The applicant must meet the minimum residence requirements to be eligible for the pension or benefit. When an applicant applies for an OAS pension, ALW benefit or ALWS benefit, their declared residence can be accepted without the need for further review or additional documents if: a signed, complete residence statement is provided; there are no inconsistencies between the residence statement and documentation on file; the applicant has a permanent Canadian legal status (e.g. Landed Immigrant, Permanent Resident or Canadian Citizenship); and the applicant did not declare any absences from Canada after the later of; their 18th birthday; or their initial arrival into Canada. An International Social Security Agreement (ISSA) may allow an applicant to meet the minimum residence requirements to be eligible for a pension or benefit under the OAS program. Table 1. Pension or benefit type and description Pension or benefit type Description Full OAS pension Residence rules are used to establish whether the applicant is eligible to receive a full or partial pension. An applicant may be eligible for a full pension under one of the following rules: 40-Year Rule: An applicant may be eligible under this rule if they have 40 or more years of residence in Canada from age 18 to the present . Refer to Example—40-Year Rule . Example—40-Year Rule 10-Year Rule: If an applicant does not have 40 or more years of residence in Canada but they meet certain residence criteria on or before July 1, 1977, and were resident in Canada for the 10 years immediately before the approval of their application, they may still be eligible for a full pension under the 10-year rule. Refer to Example—10-Year Rule . Example—10-Year Rule 3-for-1 Rule: If an applicant does not meet the criteria of the 10-year rule because they did not reside in Canada for the full 10 years before the approval of their application, they may still be eligible for a full pension under the 3-for-1 rule if additional criteria are met. Refer to Example—3-for-1 Rule . Example—3-for-1 Rule Example—40-Year Rule Example—10-Year Rule Example—3-for-1 Rule Partial OAS pension under domestic rules An applicant may be eligible for a partial pension if they meet one of the following minimum residence requirements: 10 years of residence in Canada after their 18th birthday, if they are applying while residing in Canada; or 20 years of residence in Canada after their 18th birthday, if they are applying from outside of Canada. Entitlement to a partial pension is calculated based on 1/40th for each complete year of residence in Canada after the applicant's 18th birthday. Once the pension is approved, the 40ths do not increase with continued residence in Canada. However, the client can continue to accrue years of Canadian residence towards the portability of their pension. Partial OAS pension under an ISSA If an applicant does not meet the minimum residence requirements for a partial OAS pension under the domestic rules above, they may still be eligible to receive a partial pension if they: have worked or resided in a country with which Canada has an ISSA in force. To view the countries with an ISSA in force, refer to International Social Security Agreements Countries ; and International Social Security Agreements Countries have sufficient creditable periods (e.g. contributions and/or residence) in the other country that can be added to their actual Canadian residence to allow them to meet the minimum residence requirements. Foreign creditable periods are only used to determine if an applicant meets the minimum residence requirements and are not used to calculate the applicant’s entitlement (i.e. entitlement is based solely on the applicant’s years of residence in Canada after age 18). Entitlement to a partial pension is calculated based on 1/40th for each complete year of residence in Canada after the applicant's 18th birthday. Once the pension is approved, the 40ths do not increase with continued residence in Canada. However, the client can continue to accrue years of Canadian residence towards the portability of their pension. International Social Security Agreements Countries Full ALW or ALWS benefit An applicant may be eligible for a full ALW or ALWS benefit if they have a minimum of 10 years of residence in Canada after their 18th birthday. Partial ALW or ALWS benefit under an ISSA If an applicant does not meet the minimum residence requirements stated above for a full ALW or ALWS benefit, they may still be eligible to receive a partial benefit if they: have worked or resided in a country with which Canada has an ISSA in force. To view the countries with an ISSA i n force, refer to International Social Security Agreements Countries ; and International Social Security Agreements Countries have sufficient creditable periods (e.g. contributions and/or residence) in the other country that can be added to their actual Canadian residence to allow them to meet the minimum residence requirements. Foreign creditable periods are only used to determine if an applicant meets the minimum residence requirements and are not used to calculate the applicant’s entitlement (i.e. entitlement is based solely on the applicant’s years of residence in Canada after age 18). The partial benefit is calculated based on 1/10th for each complete year of residence in Canada after the applicant's 18th birthday. When the benefit is approved, the partial benefit will increase by 1/10th upon reaching another full year of Canadian residence until they are payable at the full rate. If the client did not have 40 years of Canadian residence at the time the ALW or ALWS application was approved, you must review and validate the client’s residence up to the OAS pension effective date. However, the client can continue to accrue years of Canadian residence towards the portability of their pension if they had less than 20 years of residence in Canada at approval. topic_title: Partial remission of debts as a result of Erroneous Advice/Administrative Error
text: Example A When the client's GIS was processed, the income used to calculate the benefit was $12,050.00 instead of $18,050.00 as they indicated on their application. While the error was an encoding error on Service Canada's part (i.e. an administrative error), the client's award letter also indicated that the income used to calculate their benefit was $12,050.00. The client should have noticed that the incorrect income was used to calculate their benefit and notified Service Canada of the error. In this situation, a partial remission of 50% can be considered based on the facts of the case. Example B The client completed their residence information on their OAS application and accidentally omitted a period of time where they were not a resident in Canada. There was documentation on file about the absence, however, the Service Canada employee did not consider it when the application was processed. It was later determined that the client was overpaid for a period of time, since the absence from Canada reduced the aggregate for their pension from 40/40ths to 35/40ths. While the client's error was the original cause of the overpayment, the Service Canada employee should have been aware of the error and corrected it. In this situation, a partial remission of 50% can be considered based on the facts of the case. Example C New On March 8, 2023, the Department received a letter from a client asking for their Date of Birth (DOB) to be corrected. The letter included: their correct DOB of August 1, 1957; a certified copy of their birth certificate; and an explanation that they were aware that the Social Insurance Registry (SIR) had an incorrect DOB on file for them. They stated that their mother applied for their SIN in 1973 providing an incorrect DOB of January 8, 1955, which made them age 18 and able to work overseas. Timeline of events Date Description 1973 Mother entered the incorrect DOB as January 8, 1955 when applying for a SIN for the client. Client states being aware that the SIR had the wrong DOB. Refer to event dated March 8, 2023, below. December 2018 The client created a My Service Canada Account (MSCA) using the incorrect DOB of January 8, 1955, as the system could not match their actual DOB. February 2019 The client received their OAS auto-enrolment form as the system estimated they would be 65 in January 2020. The client declined the OAS auto-enrolment stating that they did not want their OAS at this time. They did not mention their incorrect DOB or request to have it corrected. August 2022 The client applied for an RTR pension through their MSCA requesting a start date as soon as possible. The system used the incorrect DOB of January 8, 1955. September 2022 (October accounting month) The system: used the DOB from the SIR of January 8, 1955; processed the RTR pension application effective September 2021 based on the August 2022 receipt date; released a retroactive payment of $12,000.00 for the period of September 2021 to September 2022. The client received this payment and knows it is incorrect as their financial planner advised them there is no retroactive entitlement before age 65. March 8, 2023 The client writes a letter to the Department including a certified copy of their birth certificate. In this letter the client stated the following: Their DOB is August 1, 1957; and They knew their DOB was incorrect with the SIR as their mother provided an incorrect DOB when applying for the SIN in 1973. March 25, 2023 (April accounting month) A Department employee updates the client's DOB, but only changes the year of birth. The DOB is changed to January 8, 1957. This change results in a change to the client's RTR pension effective date to February 2022 and an overpayment of $15,000.00 for the period of September 2021 to March 2023. An overpayment letter is sent to the client explaining that their DOB has been changed which resulted in a change to their RTR pension effective date and resulted in an overpayment. However, the letter does not specify the updated DOB. April 30, 2023 The client requests a reconsideration of the overpayment amount. May 15, 2023 (June accounting month) The client's file is reviewed due to the reconsideration request. Since the client is appealing the overpayment amount and not the reason for the overpayment, the request is denied. However, during the review, the Department employee notices that the client's DOB was updated incorrectly in March 2023 and corrects it to August 1, 1957. This results in a change to the effective date to September 2022 and an additional overpayment of $2,000.00 for the period of February 2022 to May 2023. The total of the 2 overpayments on the client's account is now $17,000.00. For Example C, use the chart below to determine if a portion of the overpayment should be remitted: Table 2. Overpayment period Overpayment Amount Who is responsible for the overpayment? (Department, client, other?) Investigation Rationale Sept 2021 -March 2023 $15,000.00 The client: admits that they knowingly used an incorrect DOB; and failed to inform the Department until March 2023. You must verify the client's file to determine if the Department knew about the incorrect DOB before receiving the client's letter. Since this client applied for their RTR pension via their MSCA, the DOB from the SIR was used and the system automatically put them into pay. The DOB from the SIR was the only source available on the Client Profile screen in ITRDS when the RTR pension was released into pay. The client's paper file only contains the client letter from March 8, 2023, with the certified copy of their birth certificate. The client was aware of the incorrect DOB with the SIR and the earliest entitlement to the RTR pension. Therefore, the client is fully responsible for debt during this overpayment period and must repay this entire portion of the overpayment. February 2022 to May 2023 $2,000.00 The Department updated the client's DOB incorrectly after being notified of the correct date by the client. Since the Department erred, you must verify if the client could have been aware of the error. In this case: the letter sent to the client did not provide them with their updated DOB; and ITRDS Notes and the file has no records of any phone calls with the client regarding the update to their DOB. Since the Department erred and the client was found not to be aware of the error, the Department is responsible for increasing the overpayment amount. Therefore, the Department is fully responsible for this portion of the overpayment, and it should be remitted using the reason due to Erroneous Advice/Administrative Error.

topic_title: Partial remission of debts as a result of the OAS time bar provision
text: Example A The client was overpaid from March 1985 to September 1993 in the amount of $12,000.00. The overpayment was discovered and set up in December 1993. This is a debt to the Crown and is recoverable because it was established and set up before the removal of the time bar provisions of April 1, 1994. Example B The client was overpaid from June 1990 to September 1995 in the amount of $25,000.00. The overpayment was not discovered and set up until September 1995. The overpayment for the period from June 1990 to March 1994 of $15,000.00 is not considered a debt due to the Crown. Neither is it recoverable because it was not established and set up before the removal of the time bar provisions of April 1, 1994. The total overpayment amount that is considered a debt due to the Crown is from April 1994 to September 1995 in the amount of $10,000.00. The entire amount of the overpayment ($25,000.00) must be set up in the system. The $15,000.00 for the period of June 1990 to March 1994 must be remitted, but the $10,000.00 for April 1994 to September 1995 must be recovered in full.

topic_title: Releasing the benefit at the entitlement date
text: Cúram will automatically determine entitlement to the income-tested benefit when the applicant or their spouse or common-law partner, if applicable, reach their entitlement date if the following conditions are met: the applicant is still eligible for the benefit; income information is available for the payment period in which there is entitlement to the benefit. Income can be received from the CRA or a statement of income; and there are no outstanding issues, evidence or tasks in Cúram. When adding the Sponsorship Agreement evidence to Cúram, a Sponsorship Review task must be manually created to review the account 6 months before the entitlement date. GIS Before entitlement to the GIS can be determined, the account must be reviewed to confirm that: the applicant is in pay for an OAS pension; the applicant's ITB for Life status continues to be set to Yes ; the applicant has a Canadian address and there is no indication on file that they may no longer be residing in Canada; and CRA Income evidence has been received for the payment period in which the applicant is entitled to begin receiving the GIS. If any of the above cannot be confirmed, the applicant must be contacted to: confirm that they are still residing in Canada; confirm their current address and banking information; obtain an updated residence statement for the most recent 5 years; obtain income information for the applicable payment periods, if applicable; and confirm any other information that is required to determine eligibility and entitlement. ALW benefit and ALWS benefit Before entitlement to the ALW benefit or ALWS benefit can be determined, the applicant must be contacted to: confirm that they are still residing in Canada; confirm their current address and banking information; obtain an updated residence statement for the most recent 5 years; obtain income information for the applicable payment periods, if applicable; and confirm any other information that is required to determine eligibility and entitlement. Payments will begin in the month of the sponsorship breakdown if: the applicant is still eligible for the benefit; income information is available for the applicable payment periods where there is entitlement to the benefit. Income information can be received from CRA or a statement of income; and there are no outstanding issues, evidence or tasks in Cúram. A sponsored immigrant is an individual who is legally admitted to Canada under a sponsorship agreement. A sponsor is an individual who meets the Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) requirements and has agreed to financially support the sponsored immigrant while they live in Canada. The sponsor is responsible for supporting the sponsored immigrant for the duration of the sponsorship agreement which is also known as the undertaking period. Under a sponsorship agreement, the sponsor and the sponsored immigrant both agree to certain responsibilities for the duration of the undertaking period. The sponsor agrees to provide basic needs (e.g. food, clothing, shelter) to the sponsored immigrant and the sponsored immigrant agrees to make every effort to support themselves and their accompanying family members. Even if a sponsored immigrant obtains Canadian citizenship, their sponsorship agreement is in effect for the duration of the undertaking or until there is a sponsorship breakdown. For more information, Sponsorship Agreement (Policy) Sponsorship categories and undertakings The undertaking period starts on the day the sponsored immigrant becomes a permanent resident. The category and the length of the undertaking depend on: the sponsored immigrant's age; the sponsored immigrant's relationship to the sponsor; and where the sponsorship agreement was signed. Table 1. Sponsorship categories and lengths of undertakings Category Length of undertaking Family class code Spouse 3 years FC1 Common-law partner 3 years FCC Conjugal partner 3 years FCE Parents and Grandparents (PGP) 20 years FC4 Other relative 10 years FC7 Sponsored refugee Varies from 1 to 3 years N/A

topic_title: Sponsorship agreements signed with the province of Québec
text: The Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration is responsible for approving sponsorship undertakings for sponsors residing in Québec. After Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) confirms an individual's eligibility as a sponsor, the sponsor must meet Québec's sponsorship requirements and sign an undertaking with the province of Québec. Although IRCC determines sponsor eligibility and grants permanent resident status to sponsored immigrants, IRCC cannot determine or confirm the duration of sponsorship undertakings signed with Québec as it is administered by that province. Table 2. Sponsorship categories and lengths of undertakings for sponsors residing in Québec Category Length of undertaking Spouse 3 years Common-law partner 3 years Conjugal partner 3 years Parents and grandparents 10 years Other relative 10 years If an applicant entered Canada with a sponsorship agreement signed with Québec and confirmation of the duration of their sponsorship undertaking is required, the applicant must provide documentation to verify their sponsorship details. The Department and IRCC do not have an understanding with Québec to access this information. Documentary Evidence—Sponsorship Agreements (Policy)

topic_title: Sponsorship and entitlement to GIS, ALW benefit and ALWS benefit
text: Sponsorship agreements restrict entitlement to income-tested benefits, but they do not affect eligibility. An applicant is not entitled to an income-tested benefit if they are a sponsored immigrant. However, an application for an income-tested benefit cannot be denied for that reason. The ALW benefit must not be paid to the spouse or common-law partner of a pensioner for any period during which the pensioner is not entitled to the GIS because they are under a sponsorship agreement. For more information, Eligibility Requirements— ALW Benefit New Business (Policy) Grandfathering rules In January 2014, amendments were made to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) regulations to increase the undertaking length for Parents and Grandparents (PGP) sponsorship agreements from 10 years to 20 years. Although the amendments came into force in January 2014, sponsored immigrants did not begin entering Canada under the 20-year PGP sponsorship agreements until approximately January 2016. In October 2025, amendments made to the Old Age Security Act (OAS Act) came into force, limiting entitlement to income-tested benefits for sponsored immigrants for the duration of their sponsorship, regardless of their years of Canadian residence. If the income-tested benefit effective date is: October 1, 2025 or later, applicants will be subject to the new OAS Act amendments. Prior to October 1, 2025, the benefit will be assessed using the previous entitlement criteria for sponsored immigrants, regardless of when the application is received. Benefit effective date is October 1, 2025 or later If the effective date of the income-tested benefit is October 1, 2025 or later, a sponsored immigrant is not entitled to the benefit for the entire duration of the sponsorship agreement, unless there is a sponsorship breakdown. If all other eligibility requirements are met, sponsored immigrants are entitled to receive income-tested benefits in the earlier of: the month that a sponsorship breakdown occurs; or the month after the sponsorship agreement ends. Benefit effective date is prior to October 1, 2025 If the effective date of the income-tested benefit is prior to October 1, 2025, a sponsored immigrant is not entitled to receive any income-tested benefit for the entire duration of the sponsorship agreement, unless: there is a sponsorship breakdown; or the sponsored immigrant accumulates 10 full years of residence in Canada after the age of 18. If all other eligibility requirements are met, sponsored immigrants are entitled to receive income-tested benefits in the earlier of: the month that a sponsorship breakdown occurs; the month after they accumulate 10 years of residence in Canada after the age of 18; or the month after the sponsorship agreement ends. For more information, Sponsorship Agreement (Policy) Sponsorship evidence in Cúram When an Application Case for an income-tested benefit is authorized and the applicant's Sponsorship Agreement evidence is added in Cúram, the applicant will be eligible but not entitled. The system will not calculate any entitlement for the duration of the sponsorship agreement unless: there is a sponsorship breakdown; or the benefit's effective date was prior to October 2025 and the applicant has accumulated 10 years of Canadian residence before their sponsorship end date. When an Application Case for an ALW benefit is authorized and the Sponsorship Agreement evidence for the spouse or common-law partner is added in Cúram, the system will not calculate any entitlement for the duration of the spouse or common-law partner's sponsorship agreement unless: there is a sponsorship breakdown; or the spouse or common-law partner's GIS effective date was prior to October 2025 and they have accumulated 10 years of Canadian residence before their sponsorship end date.

A sponsored immigrant may be entitled to income-tested benefits (i.e. GIS, ALW benefit, ALWS benefit) before the end date of their sponsorship agreement if there is a sponsorship breakdown. A sponsorship breakdown will occur if the sponsor: dies; is convicted of an offence under the Criminal Code in respect of the sponsored immigrant; becomes bankrupt; or is sentenced to a term of imprisonment of more than 6 months. In any of these situations, a sponsored immigrant could be entitled to income-tested benefits in the month of the sponsorship breakdown if all other eligibility requirements are met and the required income is received. For more information, Sponsorship Agreement (Policy) In all cases, documentary evidence is required to validate a sponsorship breakdown. For more information, Documentary Evidence—Sponsorship Agreements (Policy)

topic_title: When to determine if a GIS, ALW benefit or ALWS benefit applicant is under a sponsorship agreement
text: When an application for an income-tested benefit is received for an applicant who was not born in Canada, determine if the applicant is under a sponsorship agreement if the conditions below apply. The effective date is prior to October 1, 2025 If the effective date of the income-tested benefit is before October 1, 2025 and if, at that effective date, the applicant has less than 10 years of residence in Canada after age 18, determine if the applicant is under a sponsorship agreement. The effective date is October 1, 2025 or later If the effective date of the income-tested benefit is October 1, 2025 or later and if, at that effective date, it has been less than 20 years since the date the applicant became a permanent resident, determine if the applicant is under a sponsorship agreement. Required information If the application form does not allow the applicant to provide this information or the applicant does not answer the sponsorship agreement questions, and there is no supporting documentation on the file to confirm the sponsorship agreement details, request it by phone or mail. Request Documentation or Information by Phone or Mail (Action) Request the following sponsorship agreement details: The category of the sponsorship agreement. Whether the sponsorship agreement was signed with the province of Québec. The length of the sponsorship undertaking in months or years. The date the applicant became a permanent resident in Canada. The applicant's Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) Unique Client Identifier number. The applicant may not be able to provide all the above information. However, they must provide enough information for you to confirm: whether they are under a sponsorship agreement; the category of the sponsorship agreement; and the length of undertaking for the sponsorship agreement. In some cases, applicants may not know the category of their sponsorship agreement but are able to provide information about their relationship with the sponsor. This information can be used to determine the sponsorship category (i.e. if the sponsor is the applicant's child, they would have entered Canada under the parents and grandparents sponsorship category).

Information used to make the decision Date of birth: March 15, 1952 65th birthday: March 15, 2017 March 15, 1970, to June 4, 1972: Japan June 5, 1972, to April 5, 1974: Canada April 6, 1974, to February 1, 2002: United Kingdom February 2, 2002, to present (March 14, 2017): Canada 10-year period: March 15, 2007 to March 14, 2017 Application receipt date: February 2017 Approval date: March 15, 2017 Effective date: April 2017 at 40/40 Decision Since the applicant was 25 years of age on July 1, 1977, had Canadian residence after age 18 and before July 1, 1977, and resided in Canada for the 10 years immediately preceding the day of approval of their application, they will be considered for an OAS pension under the 10-year rule.

An applicant may qualify under the 10-year rule if: on July 1, 1977, they were 25 years of age or over; and resided in Canada or , if they did not reside in Canada: they resided in Canada after the age of 18; or they possessed a valid Canadian Immigration Visa; and they had resided in Canada for the 10 years immediately preceding the day of approval of their application (10-year period).

Information used to make the decision Date of birth: May 28, 1946 65th birthday: May 28, 2011 May 28, 1964, to March 18, 1980: Canada March 19, 1980, to December 31, 1990: Brazil January 1, 1991, to December 21, 2000: Canada December 22, 2000, to January 14, 2003: Korea January 15, 2003, to present (May 27, 2011): Canada 10-year period: May 28, 2001, to May 27, 2011 Application receipt date: April 2011 Approval date: May 28, 2011 Effective date: June 2011 at 40/40 Decision The applicant was 25 years of age on July 1, 1977, was a resident of Canada on July 1, 1977, and resided in Canada for one continuous year immediately before the day the application was approved. As they were not a resident in Canada for the entire 10-year period, their previous residence after age 18 and before the 10-year period (25 years and 286 days) is 3 times greater than the absences in the 10-year period (4 years and 331 days). Therefore, the applicant will be considered for an OAS pension under the 3-for-1 rule. Calculation The applicant was absent from Canada during the 10-year period from May 28, 2001 to January 14, 2003 = 1 year and 232 days. Therefore, their required make-up time is: total absences (1 year and 232 days) x 3 = 4 years and 331 days. The applicant resided in Canada from May 28, 1964, to March 18, 1980 = 15 years and 296 days. January 1, 1991 to December 21, 2000 = 9 years and 356 days Total: 25 years and 287 days

An applicant may qualify under the 3-for-1 rule if: on July 1, 1977, they were 25 years of age or over; and resided in Canada or , if they did not reside in Canada: they resided in Canada after the age of 18; or they possessed a valid Canadian Immigration Visa; and they had resided in Canada continuously for at least one year immediately preceding the day of approval of their application. If there are absences during the 10-year period, the applicant must have been present or resident in Canada after age 18 and before the 10-year period, for periods that total at least 3 times the length of their absences in the 10-year period.

topic_title: A selected person applies for an OAS pension, the GIS, or an ALW or ALWS benefit
text: When an application for an OAS pension, the GIS, or an ALW or ALWS benefit is received after the client has been selected for automatic enrolment, the action required depends on the type of application submitted and when it is received during the autom atic enrolment process. OAS pension or GIS application received before age 65 If an OAS/GIS Application Case is present and it has not been authorized, the client will be excluded from the automatic enrolment process upon receipt of a new application. The OAS/GIS Application Case must be closed and a new Application Case will be created in Cúram. The applicant's eligibility will be determined based on the manually submitted application alone. OAS pension or GIS application received after age 65 If the application is received after the selected person's 65th birthday and the OAS pension and the GIS have been authorized, the requirement to submit an application has already been waived. Therefore, you must review the new application for any discrepancies and update the applicable evidences, as required. If there are no changes to the applicant's eligibility or entitlement, manually send a letter to the applicant to acknowledge the application and advise that the OAS pension and/or GIS has already been approved under the automatic enrolment process. You must also close the outstanding Application Case. ALW or ALWS benefit application received A person who was selected for automatic enrolment of the OAS pension and GIS can apply separately for the ALW or ALWS benefit. Residence and legal status requirements for approving the OAS pension are only met on the client’s 65th birthday. If the ALW or ALWS benefit application is received, you must process the application as usual. Refer to ALW Benefit Application (Scenario) or ALW Benefit Application (Scenario) ALWS Benefit Application (Scenario) If you encounter and resolve a marital relationship evidence issue while processing the ALW application, ensure you change the automatic enrolment status on the Application Case to Waiting for Authorization , if applicable.

Up until their 65th birthday, a selected client may opt-out of the automatic enrolment process for: the OAS pension and the GIS at the same time; the GIS alone; or the OAS pension alone after they have already opted-out of the GIS. By choosing to opt-out of the automatic enrolment of the OAS pension, the client is also choosing to opt-out of the automatic enrolment of the GIS. However, the client may opt-out of the automatic enrolment of the GIS only and continue with the automatic enrolment of the OAS pension. If the selected client continues to be eligible on the day of their 65th birthday, the requirement to submit an application is considered to have been waived and the OAS pension and the GIS, if applicable, have been authorized. Therefore, a request to opt-out of the automatic enrolment process must be received before the day of their 65th birthday in order to be considered valid. A selected client can opt-out of the automatic enrolment process by: requesting to opt-out on their Client Portal through their My Service Canada Account (MSCA); sending a letter to the Department requesting to opt-out of the automatic enrolment process of one or both benefits; returning the notification letter to the Department with a note (separate or made directly on the notification letter) requesting to opt-out of the automatic enrolment process of one or both benefits; or submitting an Application for the Old Age Security Pension and the Guaranteed Income Supplement (ISP-3550) form where the following criteria are met: the applicant indicated that they do not want to apply for the GIS (i.e. they checked the box in question C1); the applicant has not responded to any of the questions in Section C (i.e. questions C2 to C11); and you have obtained confirmation from the applicant by phone or mail that they wish to opt-out of the automatic enrolment process for the GIS. Refer to Request Documentation or Information by Phone or Mail (Action) . Request Documentation or Information by Phone or Mail (Action) If the selected client requests to opt-out of the automatic enrolment process through their Client Portal, Cúram will automatically process the request. All other requests will require manual processing in Cúram before the client’s 65th birthday to ensure that the Application Case is closed. The received date of the notification of the person's intention to opt-out is: the date of the MSCA opt-out transaction. This date is populated in the Withdrawal Date field of the Application Details evidence in the Application Case; or the date the Department received the incoming correspondence. If the client is excluded from the automatic enrolment process and wishes to receive the OAS pension and the GIS in the future, they must submit an application. If the client submits a request to opt-out of the automatic enrolment after their 65th birthday, proceed as follows: For a combined OAS pension and GIS, or for an OAS pension alone: If no payments have been issued, treat the request to opt-out as a withdrawal request. For more information, refer to Withdraw an Application (Scenario) . Withdraw an Application (Scenario) If the request is made within 6 months of the first payment being issued, treat the request to opt-out as a cancellation request. For more information, refer to Cancel or Terminate Pensions or Benefits in ITRDS (Scenario) . Cancel or Terminate Pensions or Benefits in ITRDS (Scenario) If the request is made more than 6 months after the first payment was issued, the pension and benefit, if applicable, will continue and the client can no longer request to opt-out. However, the client may request a cessation . Refer to Cessation OAS Pension and Benefits (Policy) . Cessation OAS Pension and Benefits (Policy) For the GIS alone, treat the request to opt-out as a cancellation request.

topic_title: Automatic enrolment process and letters sent
text: The following table describes the automatic enrolment process and the letters sent at the various stages between the selected person's 64th and 65th birthday. Table 1. Automatic enrolment process and letters sent Client's age System process System-generated letters 64 The client is screened based on the selection criteria for the OAS pension. If the client does not meet all of the selection criteria, they are excluded from the automatic enrolment process and will not be re-selected for it in the future. If the client meets the selection criteria, an Application Case is automatically created in Cúram. If the client meets the selection criteria, the system will send one of the following letters, as applicable: OAS Automatic Enrolment Notification letter (ISP-3009) for category 1 and 3; or OAS Automatic Enrolment Notification letter (ISP-3030) for category 2 and 3. These letters include the Department's intent to: waive the requirement to submit an OAS pension application; and obtain information from the CRA to waive the requirement to submit a GIS application. They also provide the selected client with: the date of birth, residence and legal status criteria used in the selection process; and direction on how to opt-out of the automatic enrolment process, or how to notify the Department of any incorrect information before they reach age 65. 64 and 9 months The GIS automatic enrolment process is initiated and Cúram will attempt to manage the entire process. A request is made to the CRA to obtain income and spouse details, if applicable. Cúram will create a profile for the spouse if one does not exist. If Cúram encounters any issues, a task will be created to indicate that manual intervention is required to continue the automatic enrolment process. System-generated letters are sent based on the marital relationship and the GIS AE Status set in Cúram. If the GIS AE Status is set to Waiting for Authorization , the OAS/GIS Auto-Enrolment Notification to GIS Auto-Enrolment Client 64 +9 months (ISP-3108) letter is sent to the selected client. The OAS/GIS Auto Enrolment - Spouse's Notification re GIS Client at Age 64+9 (ISP-3115) letter will be sent to the selected client's spouse or common-law partner, if applicable. These letters include: the Department's intent to waive the requirement to submit a GIS application. the information that will be used to determine the entitlement to the GIS; and direction on how to notify the Department of any incorrect information before they reach age 65. 65 The client is automatically enrolled for the OAS pension and, if applicable, the GIS, provided that: there is no opt-out date in Cúram; the account has not been flagged for further review; or the Integrated Case's status is not set to Suspended . If any part of the process is incomplete and the account does not reach the Waiting for Authorization stage, the client will be excluded from the GIS automatic enrolment process, but the OAS pension automatic enrolment process will continue. A system-generated OAS/GIS Notification of Entitlement letter, 65 + 1 month (ISP-3092) letter will be sent to the client. This letter provides the client with: the effective date of their OAS pension and the amount of their payment. the amount of the GIS payment, if the client is eligible and entitled to it. If the client’s income is in excess, the amount of the GIS payment will be zero; or a notification that a GIS payment amount is not stated because: the client opted to not receive the GIS; or there was not enough information to determine their eligibility. A system-generated Application for the Guaranteed Income Supplement with Statement of Income (On Demand) (ISP-3025B) form will be sent to the client if they are excluded from the GIS automatic enrolment process.

A person is selected for automatic enrolment of the OAS pension and the GIS when there is sufficient data available to the Department to presume eligibility for the OAS pension (i.e. age, legal status and residence), and the GIS (i.e. income and marital status). For more information on the selection criteria and reasons why a person would be excluded from the automatic enrolment process, Eligibility Requirements—Automatic Enrolment (Policy)

topic_title: Correction to the automatic enrolment data elements
text: Corrections to the following data elements can impact the automatic enrolment process: date of birth; name; home address; Canadian legal status; Canadian residence; marital status; income; legal representation; and requested start date for an OAS pension. Correction of data elements received before age 65 If you need to obtain additional documents or information to validate a reported change or correction to a data element, you must set the automatic enrolment status to Manual Intervention in Cúram while you wait to receive the required documents or information. If documents or information are needed but are not received before the selected client’s 65th birthday, the client is excluded from the automatic enrolment process and they will have to submit an application. If certain errors are corrected before the client’s 65th birthday and the correction does not affect their eligibility or effective date, they can continue to be automatically enrolled. If updates are made to any of the following data elements before age 65, the client may be excluded from the automatic enrolment process for the OAS pension and the GIS, depending on the update made: Table 3. Change or correction reported and consequence Change or correction reported Still eligible for automatic enrolment No longer eligible for automatic enrolment Date of birth The change in the date of birth does not affect the effective date (i.e. only the day of birth is incorrect). The change in the date of birth affects the effective date (i.e. the month or year of birth is incorrect). Canadian residence The change in residence results in 40 or more years of residence in Canada. The change in residence results in less than 40 years of residence in Canada. Legal status The person reports that they have a valid Canadian legal status. The person reports that they do not have a valid Canadian legal status. Address The person reports a domestic to domestic address change. The person reports a domestic to foreign address change. If a selected person no longer qualifies for automatic enrolment because of any of the above changes, they will have to submit an application in writing or online. Correction to automatic enrolment data elements received after age 65 If the notification of a correction is received after the person's 65th birthday, the requirement to submit an application has already been waived as the person has been automatically enrolled. Therefore, any correction to the eligibility criteria or other data elements would need to be reviewed and updated as usual after the approval of a pension or benefit.
There are no exceptions or special cases. (KA-01098 Snippet 12.0 content. Do not modify or delete.)

At the age of 64, t he automatic enrolment process is triggered to see if the requirement to submit an application for OAS pension can be waived. topic_title: Selected client requests a duplicate notification letter
text: The directions to issue a duplicate notification letter depend on whether or not the client has received an OAS pension payment. If a selected client who has not received a payment wishes to receive a duplicate notification letter, they have the option to print the letter themselves from the Client Portal through their My Service Canada Account. The request can be made: in writing; by calling the Service Canada Call Centre; or in person at a Service Canada Centre. The duplicate letter can also be sent if: the notification letter was returned as undeliverable, and a new address has been obtained; or the notification letter was sent to the selected client, but the Department has received Trustee, Power of Attorney or Mandate documentation before the client reaches age 65. For more information, refer to the Legal representatives and the automatic enrolment process section below. If a client who has received an OAS pension payment wishes to receive a duplicate notification or award letter, the request must be made in writing.

topic_title: Changes to existing estimated income or event details Updated
text: If you receive information about an option that affects the existing option details or the related base calendar year income, you must amend the existing estimated income evidences. Do not create a new Statement of Estimated Income evidence record. Amendments to estimated income and event details are necessary in situations where: a change to the estimated income or event is required; a change to the base calendar year income is received; a new event is reported; and a return to work is reported. Once you have validated the new information, modify the estimated income or event details in Cúram for the affected option. This involves updating the existing Statement of Estimated Income evidence record and creating new (or amending original) Estimated Income and Estimated Income Data evidence records to reflect any changes. Cúram will perform a recalculation of the option. If the recalculation results in a change to the estimated income, the entitlement for the client and their spouse or common law partner's affected payment periods, if applicable, will be recalculated. The client and their spouse or common-law partner must be notified in writing of any changes to their entitlement. Return to work reported Updated If it has been determined that the client has not retired, but an option was granted for retirement, Cúram must be updated to indicate that this event did not occur as originally planned. This applies if the person returns to the same job shortly after termination (within one month), not months or years later. In most cases, where a return to work is reported by the client, the conditions will have changed (e.g. a lower salary, a reduction in hours) and the new employment may be considered as secondary or temporary employment. The original retirement remains an optionable event, however, the estimated income evidence must be updated to include the income from the new employment source. Once you have validated the new information, update Cúram as required: If it is determined that there is no longer an optionable retirement event, edit the Statement of Estimated Income evidence to indicate that there is no retirement event. You may have to also edit the Estimated Income and Estimated Income Data evidences to reflect that an event is excluded or non-optionable. If it is determined that the client retired but the retirement date has changed, edit the Statement of Estimated Income evidence to indicate the updated retirement date. You may have to also update the Estimated Income and Estimated Income Data evidences if the expected employment income has changed. If the client returned to work but the retirement event still exists and is optionable: edit the Estimated Income evidence and Estimated Income Data evidence for the affected option to include the employment income earned after the retirement event if the source of employment income is the same (e.g. the client went from full-time hours to part-time hours at the same job); or create a new Estimated Income evidence and Estimated Income Data evidence to reflect the new employment income received after the retirement event. Once the option details have been updated, Cúram will perform a recalculation of the option. If the recalculation results in a change to the estimated income, the entitlement for the client and their spouse or common-law partner's affected payment periods, if applicable, will be recalculated. For more information, Examples—Changes to Estimated Income or Event Details

topic_title: Income to be included in the estimated income calculation Updated
text: When the estimated income is calculated, only pension income, employment income, and self-employment income are included. Income and deductions from all other sources from the actual income reported in the base calendar year is combined with the estimated income. This combined total option income is used to calculate entitlement. Refer to Options (Policy) for more information regarding the income to include in an option calculation. Options (Policy) If the base calendar year income is not available at the time of the option calculation, defer the Estimated Income 3041 task in Cúram until you receive the income information to determine the income-tested benefit entitlement for the period affected by the option. If the required income is not received after the appropriate bring forward periods, stop review of the option. Add an Is not entitled override to the income-tested benefit in the system for the current payment period to prevent Cúram from automatically calculating entitlement when the income is received. Once the required income is received, a task will be generated to review the account and determine entitlement for the base calendar year. Once the entitlement for the base calendar year has been determined, the option can be processed. If the client’s base calendar year income is received too late and they are not entitled to income-tested benefits for the period affected by the option, they are not entitled to the option for this period either. Special income considerations When you are reviewing and processing an ISP-3041 form, the following income types have special considerations: Seasonal Work; CPP/QPP Pension Sharing; CPP/QPP Credit Splitting; PRB ; PRB CPP/QPP lump sum payments ; CPP/QPP lump sum payments CPP/QPP Enhancement ; CPP/QPP Enhancement Wage Loss Replacement Income; Child or Spousal Support Payments; Pension Split Income ; Pension Split Income Foreign Pension Income; Pension Income Unduly Received ; Pension Income Unduly Received Provincial workers' compensation benefits (e.g. La Commission des normes de l'équité de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) in Quebec, Workplace Safety Insurance Board (WSIB) in Ontario); La Commission des normes de l'équité de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) Employment Insurance (EI) Benefits; Employment Insurance COVID-19 Emergency Benefits ; COVID-19 Emergency Benefits Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP) Income; Registered Retirement Income Fund (RRIF) Income (including transfers from a RRSP); Registered Retirement Income Fund (RRIF) Income Lump Sum Pension Income ; and Lump Sum Pension Income Option Following the Retirement of Fishing Licences. For more information regarding these special considerations, Options (Policy) PRB When you are reviewing income and see that a PRB is in pay, you must ensure that the individual has included this amount in their CPP or QPP monthly rate. The receipt of PRB retroactive payments is generally not an optionable event, unless the lump sum payment includes income for the previous year and the notional tax provision does not apply. Refer to Options—Post-Retirement Benefit (Action) to determine if the lump sum payment can be considered an optionable event and how to ensure the correct rate is used in the estimate when the income must be included in the estimate calculation. Options—Post-Retirement Benefit (Action) CPP/QPP lump sum payments A record of earnings (ROE) update or a delay in processing a pension or benefit can result in a retroactive lump sum payment. If the CPP or QPP lump sum is a retroactive payment that includes entitlement for a previous year and the amount is not considered under the Notional Tax Provision (i.e. less than $300.00 of the underpayment extends to a previous calendar year), entitlement to an option can be considered. For more information, refer to Options (Policy) and Options (Policy) Examples—Calculating Options with Lump Sum Payments CPP/QPP enhancement As of January 1, 2019, the Department began phasing in the CPP enhancement; a new component of the CPP. The enhancement is not a separate benefit, but a "top-up" to the original, now referred to as the base component of the CPP. The CPP enhancement is called "Additional CPP". As of January 1, 2019, the QPP was also enhanced in a way that mirrors the CPP enhancement. Provisions were made in both provincial and federal legislation to ensure coordination of the enhanced portions of the CPP and the QPP. Gradual increases to CPP or QPP contribution rates will take place over a 7-year period (2019 to 2025). Starting in June 2022, clients who made valid contributions in January 2019 or later will start to receive the first additional component of their benefit, including any retroactive amounts. Those who begin receiving a benefit in June 2022 or later will be paid the first additional component as part of their regular monthly amount. The lump sum payments received are to be treated as described in the CPP/QPP Lump Sum Payments section above. In CPMS , the Account Overview, the Payables and the Receivables screens will display the breakdown of the base and first additional benefit amounts; however, the payment will be sent to the client as one total amount. Be sure to use the total CPP monthly amount when estimating CPP benefits. For more information, Payment of the first Additional Portion of the CPP Enhancement Pension income splitting Updated To lower a couple's joint tax liability, the Income Tax Act allows a senior to share their pension income with a lower-income spouse or a common-law partner. The eligible pension income is restricted to funds from private pension sources. The pension income splitting provision can have a negative impact on certain couples who are having their benefits calculated based on an estimate of their current income but elected to split their pension income in the base calendar year. When a couple is disadvantaged by the pension income split, the income reported on Line 11600 of the spouse or common-law partner who is not reporting an event must be manually removed from the base calendar year if the option is approved. It is effective the same month as the effective date of the option. Before the income is removed, the spouse or common-law partner who has the income on Line 11600 must submit a new statement of income or a GIS or ALW (Pension Income Splitting - Option situation - Consent to remove a transferred amount ) (ISP-3034) form to consent to the removal of the pension income split amount. If the option is cancelled (e.g. the client did not retire or it is determined that an optionable event has not happened), you must manually return Block 2 ( CRA income from Line 11600) of the spouse or common-law partner’s base calendar year income back to the original income amount that was declared. Cúram will perform a recalculation of the entitlement using the base calendar year income. This may result in an overpayment for the client and their spouse or common-law partner. Pension income unduly received Updated If a client has reported that they are repaying or have repaid pension income that was unduly received, an option may be granted for the reduction or termination of the pension if : the repayment is in a subsequent year to the event. the client is negatively impacted by the receipt of the benefits when calculating an option for another event. If the client received and repaid benefits in the same year and there is no other event, an option is not granted because the benefit and repayment offset each other and the client has not suffered a loss of pension income. The granting of an option also depends on how the repayment will appear on the client’s T4, because this can affect how an estimate is calculated. If the repayment is made while the client is still in receipt of the benefit, the net amount of benefits will appear on the T4 on the benefit line. If the repayment was made after the benefit ended, the repayment amount will appear in a separate box on the T4 and may be on a separate line for CRA income. If the repayment of benefits in the CRA income appears in Block 9, it is treated like all other income appearing on Block 9 and is not to be included in the estimated income. For example, for CPP pension income, generally the repayment of benefits happens by monthly recovery while the pension is still in pay. Therefore, the net amount of the benefit will appear on Line 11400 of the CRA income (Block 1). However, for Employment Insurance (EI) benefits, if the repayment occurs while the client is still in receipt of benefits, the net amount will appear on line 11900 of the CRA income (Block 3) and can be included in the estimate. If the repayment happens after the benefits have ended, the repayment will appear as a deduction on Line 23200 of the CRA income (Block 9) and is not included in the estimate, but will appear in the applicable base calendar year income. For more information, refer to Options (Policy) . For examples of the various ways this repayment can affect an option, Options (Policy) Examples—Options with Pension Income Unduly Received La Commission des normes de l'équité de la santé et de la sécurité du travail La Commission des normes de l'équité de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) is the provincial workers’ compensation benefits program in Quebec. CNESST is paid biweekly and calculated using a daily rate. The annual amount received is reported in Block 10 on the T5007 slip. If the accident that has resulted in the receipt of benefits occurs before the beneficiary is 64 years of age, they will continue to receive regular benefits until they reach 65. Beginning on the beneficiary’s 65th birthday, the benefit will begin to decrease by 25% for the next 4 years, ending at age 68. Each 25% reduction is an optionable event. CNESST is adjusted each year on the anniversary date of the day the worker became unable to work as a result of the accident. This adjustment is called the annual revalorization. The calculation of this adjustment takes into account the consumer price index, as well as the amount of gross annual income that was used as a basis for calculating the benefit, which is specific to each client. These 2 factors are used every year to set a client's adjustment rate. Generally, this increases the benefits. However, for some years, the small increase in the consumer price index contributes to the reduction of benefits for some CNESST recipients. This reduction is not optionable. If the accident that has resulted in the receipt of benefits occurs after the beneficiary is 64 years of age, they will receive benefits for 4 years after the date of the accident. The decrease of benefits at 25% per year will begin after the first year, on the anniversary date of the day the worker became unable to work as a result of the accident. The annual adjustment of benefits and the decrease will occur at the same time. Employment Insurance benefits Updated EI benefits are calculated on a weekly basis and paid bi-weekly, in arrears. An individual will therefore receive their benefit payments after the entitlement period it covers. For example, a benefit payment received on July 15, 2022 is for the entitlement period of June 26 to July 9, 2022. When calculating an option for an event (e.g. retirement from employment) and EI benefits are included in the estimate calculation, you must include the amount of benefits received after the event and not the entitlement periods. When reviewing Full Text Screens (FTS) for EI information, use the amount that appears in the Gross column not the Net column, even if the client did not receive the gross amount for that payment. Using the net amount could put the client in an overpayment situation when the reconciliation is performed. When the reconciliation is performed, the net amount (plus taxes) will be used. If the client did not receive the gross amount for each payment, they will receive an underpayment at this time. Alternatively, when processing an option and EI benefit payments ending is the event, the EI benefits are considered terminated when the entitlement period ends, not when the last payment is received. The event date and the effective date for the termination of EI benefits are the first month of no entitlement. If entitlement to EI benefit payments ends in December, but the final payment is received in January of the following year, the final payment is not included in the estimate calculation. As this income will also appear in the base calendar year for the payment period immediately following the option periods, you must create and defer a Manual – Evidence Verification Request task to manually remove it immediately before the affected payment period. For more information on estimating EI income, Options (Policy) FTS FTS is the system used by the EI program for all EI claim-related information. Access to FTS is available to designated staff in the regions to obtain EI information for option processing. To determine the entitlement weeks and payment dates for an individual, review the Payments tab in FTS. The entitlement weeks are in the Report Week column. The dates found in the Date Processed column identify payments that will be reflected on the Statement of Employment Insurance and Other Benefits (T4E) slip. This date is considered the date the payment was received. All payments processed in a particular year will be displayed on that year’s T4E. For example, if a payment for a reporting week in 2021 was not processed until 2022, the payment is considered income in 2022 rather than 2021 and will appear on the 2022 T4E slip. COVID-19 emergency benefits In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, the Government of Canada introduced emergency benefits to support Canadians by providing temporary income support for workers (employed and self-employed) who were directly impacted by the pandemic. These emergency benefits are: Employment Insurance Emergency Response Benefit (EI ERB); Canada Emergency Response Benefit (CERB); Canada Recovery Benefit (CRB); Canada Recovery Caregiving Benefit (CRCB); Canada Recovery Sickness Benefit (CRSB); and Canada Worker Lockdown Benefit (CWLB). For income-tested benefits, this income is treated differently depending on the year it is received. If you are processing an option that is affected by emergency benefits, refer to COVID-19: Interim Measures—Emergency Benefits (Action) for information on how to treat the income. COVID-19: Interim Measures—Emergency Benefits (Action) Registered Retirement Income Fund payments An individual must convert all the money in their Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP) into retirement income by December 31 of the year they turn 71 years old. The individual can choose one or a combination of the following retirement income choices: cash the RRSP; purchase a retirement annuity; convert the RRSP to a Registered Retirement Income Fund (RRIF). Many individuals choose to convert the RRSP to a RRIF. An individual may have as many RRIFs as they want and they may transfer money from one RRIF to another at any time. An individual must withdraw a minimum amount from the RRIF(s) each year, according to the formulae included in the Income Tax Act. There is no maximum withdrawal limit. An individual can determine their own withdrawal rate and schedule (i.e. annual, semi-annual, quarterly, monthly or weekly withdrawal periods). An individual may also change the rate and schedule of their withdrawals at any time during the course of a year. Most individuals make monthly withdrawals. A RRIF payment year is always a calendar year that is divided into periods. The period is based on the frequency of payments. For more information regarding RRIF payments and options, refer to Options (Policy) and Options (Policy) Examples—Calculating Options with RRIF Payments Lump Sum Pension Income Updated Lump sum payments that fall under the definition of pension income may qualify for an option. However, these lump sum payments are treated differently than regular pension income payments. Lump sum payments are often declared on Line 13000 (other income) of a pensioner’s Income Tax and Benefit Return. These payments can include a retroactive lump sum payment, an amount replacing future payments or a one-time payment. When you are determining whether to include or exclude the lump sum payment income in the estimate calculation, you must consider: when the lump sum payment was received; and whether other optionable events happened during the same calendar year or are being calculated in the same payment period. For more information, refer to Options (Policy) and Options (Policy) Examples—Calculating Options with Lump Sum Payments

Cúram will perform the option calculation based on the estimated income details that have been data captured. Cúram will use the estimated income evidences to calculate blocks 1, 2, 3, 7, 8 and 9. You must capture all income from these blocks as estimated income evidence, including non-optionable income from Block 9 received in the base income year. This income is automatically combined with the base year income for blocks 4, 5 and 6 to determine the total estimated income. This total estimated income is compared to the total base year income and the most advantageous income is used to calculate entitlement for the income tested benefit during the option period. You must review and analyze the provided information to ensure it is as complete and accurate as possible. You must ensure that the details of all the applicable events have been recorded to avoid overpayments when the estimated income is compared and reconciled with the actual income in the following year. Generally, when an option is processed for an event, two statements of estimated income are required. A current year option calculation is performed for the statement of estimated income that coincides with the calendar year that the event occurs in. Then a previous year option calculation is performed for the statement of estimated income that follows the calendar year that the event occurs in. The exception to this is when an option is effective January. As mentioned previously, only one statement of estimated income is required when an option is effective January, but depending on the type of event, the calculations to perform are different. If the individual retired from employment or self-employment in the month of December, the event is considered to have occurred in December but the option is effective January. Since the event occurred in the calendar year immediately before the year of the statement of estimated income, a previous year option calculation is performed for January to June and again for the period from July to the following June, resulting in only 2 previous year option calculations. If the individual’s pension income reduced or terminated in January, the event is considered to have occurred in January and the option is effective January. Since the event occurred in the same calendar year as the year of the statement of estimated income, a current year option calculation is performed for the period from January to June and again for the period from July to the following June, resulting in only 2 current year option calculations. Post-mortem option calculations When performing the option calculations for the year that the individual passed away, the estimated income is prorated or calculated for the entire year, as though the individual is still alive. This ensures that the estate receives the correct entitlement of benefits that would have been paid if the death did not occur. Current year option calculation Pension income The estimated pension income for a current year option is calculated using a proration formula. This formula uses the income that was received after the optionable event and prorates it over a full year. The following basic proration formula is used for pensions and benefits that are received monthly : For pensions and benefits that are received bi-weekly , quarterly , semi-annually , annually or irregularly , an additional calculation is required to convert the payment into a calculated monthly payment amount before using the basic current year proration formula above. The following calculation formula is used to convert the payment into a calculated monthly payment amount: For pensions and benefits received semi-monthly , the following proration calculation formula is used: For pensions and benefits that are received weekly , the following proration calculation is used: An additional calculation is required to determine what the maximum annual amount would be if the individual received the weekly pension or benefit for the full calendar year. The following calculation is used: Cúram will compare the result of this calculation to the result of the proration calculation and the lesser of the two calculations is used in the estimate calculation. This ensures that the estimate will never be higher than what the client could actually receive in a year. For examples of prorating using the formula, Examples—Current Year Option Prorating Calculations Employment and self-employment income If the event is not retirement, the full amount of employment or self-employment income the client expects to receive in the calendar year, minus the calculated earnings exemption, is included in the calculation. If the event is a reduction of employment income (e.g. reduced hours, new position at a reduced rate of pay), only the employment and self-employment income that the client expects to receive after the month of retirement, minus the calculated earnings exemption, will be included in the calculation. If the event is retirement, any employment income related to the retirement that is received in the same calendar year must be excluded from the calculation, such as: severance pay; vacation pay; sick leave benefits; retroactive salary adjustments; bonuses and commissions; and disposition of business assets. If the individual has retired from employment but is on leave immediately following their retirement date (e.g. sick leave, vacation leave), they are still receiving a regular income until the leave has ended. The event date for the retirement in this situation is the last day for which the individual receives regular salary or wages. If the individual receives income from more than one employment source and has retired from only one, the full amount of employment or self-employment income the individual expects to receive from the other employment sources in the calendar year, minus the calculated earnings exemption, is included in the calculation. If this breakdown is not provided on the ISP-3041 form, you can obtain the information over the phone. Other income Include all other income from the base calendar year in the estimate calculation. If there is income in the base calendar year and you are unsure of the source (e.g. Line 13000), review the file or contact the individual to clarify and confirm what the source is. If the income is a pension income that is affected by the option, remove it from the base calendar year income and include it in the estimate calculation as applicable. For example, if the individual has retired from employment or self-employment, retiring allowances (severance pay), disposition of business assets and profit sharing would appear in Line 13000. Although this employment income is found in Block 9, it cannot be used as part of the estimated income when calculating an option based on retirement and must be removed from the base calendar year income. Once you have confirmed the source of income in Block 9, you must manually enter it into Cúram when you enter the pension and employment incomes. You must identify whether the income is non-optionable annual income from the base calendar year or optionable income that must be included in the estimated income calculation (e.g. alimony or support payments). Previous year option calculation Pension income The estimated pension income for a previous year option is not prorated. All pension income that is received for the calendar year is estimated as it is expected to be received. The following formula is used for the calculation: Employment and self-employment income If the event is not retirement, you must include all employment and self-employment income received for the calendar year as it is expected to be received. If the event is retirement and the individual has reported subsequent employment income related to the retirement on the previous year option form, do not include it in the previous year option calculation. When the subsequent employment income related to the retirement, is included in the individual’s income for the payment period immediately following the previous year option, remove this income from the base calendar year by updating the manually entered income and excluding this amount. If the subsequent income is received more than a year after the last option ending, it cannot be removed from the base calendar year income and must be included as income in the calculation of income-tested benefits. For self-employment, there are situations where an option can be granted for equipment sales related to the business in the following year or years after retirement. For more information, Options (Policy) Other income All other income from the base calendar year is included in the estimate calculation. If there is income in the base calendar year and you are unsure of the source (e.g. Line 13000), review the file or contact the individual to clarify and confirm that it is not a pensionable income that should be removed from the base calendar year and, if applicable, estimated. For example, if the individual retired from employment or self-employment, retiring allowances (severance pay), disposition of business assets and profit sharing would appear in Line 13000. Although this employment income is found in Block 9, it cannot be used as part of the estimated income when calculating an option based on retirement. Once you have confirmed the source of income in Block 9, you must manually enter it into Cúram when you enter the pension and employment incomes. You must identify whether the income is non-optionable annual income from the base calendar year or optionable income that must be included in the estimated income calculation (e.g. alimony or support payments).

Option Continuation is the process where a current year option is processed and the event happens between the months of January and June. Effective July, Cúram will calculate the option for the new payment period if the base calendar year income is received using the estimated income to renew the income tested benefit if it is still to the client's advantage. If you are processing an option between January and June that requires a manual review of the income before it can be calculated for the next payment period (e.g. income exists in block 9) and the required income information is not received yet, create a Manual – Evidence Verification Request task and defer it to review the income immediately prior to the next payment year.

If it is determined that a deceased client would have benefited from an option, a Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form can be sent to the estate for completion and processed after the client’s death only once documentation supporting the income for the year being estimated (e.g. Income Tax and Benefit Return) is received. When processing the option, you must reconcile the estimated and actual incomes using the information reported on the ISP-3041 and the actual income provided on the supporting document. The death of an individual is not an optionable event. For more information on the documentation required to process an option post-mortem, Options (Policy)

A client who was granted an option must provide their actual income information for the following payment period by: completing an Income Tax and Benefit Return so the income can be provided by the CRA ; or submitting a Statement of Income for the Renewal of the Guaranteed Income Supplement, the Allowance or Allowance for the Survivor for payment period of July (20XX) to June (20XX) with Information Sheet (ISP-3026) form. Reconciliation is required to validate the actual income against the estimated income that was previously calculated. You must review and question any discrepancies that you are unable to resolve by reviewing the information on file, to assure the accuracy of the benefit rate paid. The only option situation that does not require a reconciliation is the option granted to a client who has since passed away and the required actual income has not been received by the Department. As statements of income may be waived, the income information received from the CRA is treated as a statement of income. When actual income is available at the time that the estimate is being processed, you must manually reconcile the estimated and actual incomes before activating the evidence in Cúram. It is expected that the actual income required to perform the reconciliation should be received by July following the year of the estimate for the renewal of the income-tested benefit. If the required income is not available at the time of processing and it should be, defer the Estimated Income 3041 task until October. If by October the actual income is not received and the appropriate requests for the income have been sent, the client will no longer be entitled to the option until they submit the required information. The entitlement for the option period must be recalculated using the base calendar year income. Add an Is not entitled override to the system for the current payment period. Once the income is received, a task will be generated to review the account. When the required income information is received, the override must be removed and the option can be processed again along with the reconciliation for the affected period. Refer to Option Reconciliation—Follow-up Income not Received (Action) for the procedures to follow-up on these accounts. topic_title: Requirement for the Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form
text: When there is an optionable event, a completed and signed Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form must be received by the Department before an option can be granted, even if the actual income for this year has already been received. Generally, an ISP-3041 form must be completed for each estimated calendar year. No other forms are acceptable. The ISP-3041 form has all the information that is required to calculate the estimated income. It also tells the individual that they are responsible for estimating their income as accurately as possible, and that the consequence of underestimating their income may be an overpayment that they must repay. Refer to Options (Policy) for more information regarding the requirement for an ISP-3041 form. Options (Policy)
