text: Once you have reviewed the estimated income evidence details and have resolved any issues, proceed with an eligibility check before applying the estimated income evidences. The Check Eligibility function is accessed from the Product Delivery Case. To determine whether the estimated income will be used to calculate the client’s benefit entitlement, you must analyze the amounts displayed under the Income tab of the applicable Coverage Period . Review the Total Payment Income field to determine if entitlement is based on the estimated income or the base year income. This field could include a combination of the client and the spouse or common-law partner’s base year income or estimated income, as applicable. If the results are as expected, apply all evidence changes and Cúram will automatically reassess entitlement. Proceed according to the result displayed on the Determinations tab of the Product Delivery Case. Table 2. Results of the option calculation or recalculation Result Description Cúram The option is to the client's advantage The option has been granted and is to the client's advantage because the estimated income is lower than the income in the base calendar year. The Total Payment Income that entitlement is calculated on includes the client’s total estimated income. The options is not to the client's advantage The option has been granted but is not to the client's advantage because the income in the base calendar year is lower than the estimated income. The Total Payment Income that entitlement is calculated on uses the base income and does not include the client's estimated income. The option is denied The option is denied for one of the following reasons: No potential optionable event declared; Time limit is not met. The Total Payment Income that entitlement is calculated on uses the base income and does not include the client's estimated income. Cúram will perform a benefit entitlement recalculation for the applicable option's payment period, for both the client and their spouse or common-law partner if applicable, when: an option is granted; an option that was previously granted is now modified or denied based on a change to the original information; or an option that was previously granted is no longer to the client’s advantage due to a change to the base calendar year income. This recalculation may result in an overpayment that must be collected, or an underpayment that you must either apply to an existing overpayment or issue to the client. The client and their spouse or common-law partner must be notified in writing of any changes to their entitlement and resulting overpayment or underpayment.
An option can be applied retroactively if it is determined that the individual is eligible for income-tested benefits for the option period. For more information, Options (Policy)

topic_title: Review and analyze the estimated income Updated
text: Cúram will perform the option calculation based on the estimate details that have been data captured. Therefore, when you receive a Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form, you must review and analyze the information provided to ensure it is complete, accurate and that the details of all the applicable events have been recorded. This step is also important to avoid overpayments when the estimated income is reconciled with the actual income in the following year. You must ensure that the applicant has reported income amounts from all the sources that they expect to receive income from for the estimated year by comparing the income that is reported on the ISP-3041 form to the income that was received in the previous year. Once you confirm that all income sources have been estimated on the ISP-3041 form, confirm that the benefit rates and payment amounts reported on the statement (if converted to an annual amount) are consistent with the annual amount reported in the previous year. Allow for fluctuations due to cost of living increases or exchange rates. If the related previous or current year option has already been processed, compare the information that is provided on the current statement with the information that was previously provided and investigate any discrepancies, such as: event type; event date; benefit amounts; and sources of income. Examples—Options With Missing Information and Discrepancies In the payment period following the estimate year, the client must provide the actual income for the estimate year. When the actual income is available at the time the estimate is being processed, you must compare the actual income information with the estimate details and manually reconcile the incomes before data capturing the information in Cúram. For more information on how to manually reconcile the income and to indicate in Cúram if this has been done, go to the Reconciliation of an option section below. If you are processing the option after renewal in the year following the estimate year and the actual income has not been received yet, you must request it before finalizing the option. If the income has still not been received by October after renewal, advise the individual that the option cannot be processed until the actual income is received. Process the option as usual after the required client income information is received. If the required income is not received by October, add a Is not entitled override to the income-tested benefit in the system for the current payment period to prevent Cúram from automatically calculating entitlement when the income is received. Once the required income is received in Cúram, a task will be generated to review the account, process the option, remove the override and determine entitlement for the affected payment period. For more information about the reconciliation process that occurs in the year after the option was processed, go to the Reconciliation of an Option section below.

text: The date of the event determines which estimate year must be completed. In most cases, 2 Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) forms are required for one optionable event. An ISP-3041 form is required for: the calendar year when the event occurred, which is the current year option; and the calendar year immediately following the event, which is the previous year option. The following are 2 exceptions where only one statement is required for an optionable event: When the event is effective in January: Retirement occurs in the month of December. In this situation, an ISP-3041 form for the following calendar year is required. The pension income is reduced effective January (i.e. January is the first month the reduced pension is received). In this situation, an ISP-3041 form for the current calendar year is required from the client. The pension income is terminated effective January (i.e. January is the first month the pension income is not received). In this situation, an ISP-3041 form for the current calendar year is required from the client. The only reported event is due to a lump-sum payment receipt that meets the criteria to be granted an option. In this situation, only a previous year option is required. If a current year option is entered in Cúram with an effective date between February and December, the applicable previous year option form will be automatically sent in March following the year the event occurred even if the current year option was not used to calculate entitlement (e.g. the option was not to the client’s advantage). This allows the client to estimate their income for the second year of the process. Refer to GIS Statement of Income Mailout (Cyclical)—March 20XX for information regarding the annual form mailout. GIS Statement of Income Mailout (Cyclical)—March 20XX If you are processing the current year option after March following the year the event occurred, you must send the previous year option form manually. An authorized representative can also submit an estimate on behalf of an individual by using the prescribed form. They must also provide documentation to prove that they are authorized to act on the individual's behalf, if it has not already been provided to the Department. For more information, Third Party Requests (Scenario) Individuals can obtain an ISP-3041 form: from a Service Canada Centre; by calling Service Canada; or from a regular mailing process from Service Canada. This form is not available online. The Department must mail the form to the client or their spouse or common-law partner.

topic_title: Time limits to submit a Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form Updated
text: The Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form must be received by the Department within the timeframes established by legislation. These time limits are based on the timing of the optionable event. The time limits for the current year and previous year options are as follows: timeframes Current year option: The Department must receive the ISP-3041 form no later than the end of the second payment period following the payment period in which the event occurs. Previous year option: The Department must receive the ISP-3041 form no later than the end of the payment period following the payment period in which the effective date of the previous year option occurs. If an ISP-3041 form is received too late to grant a current year option, a previous year option may still be granted in the following payment period if that form is received within the prescribed time limit for the previous year option. Examples—Time Limits for Submission of a Statement of Estimated Income If it is determined that the ISP-3041 form was not received within the prescribed timeframes, the statement of estimated income form and event details must still be data captured in Cúram. Once the event details are data captured, Cúram will: continue to calculate entitlement using the base calendar year income; and display No in the Time Limit Met field of the Estimated income data evidence. For more information, refer to Options (Policy) and Options (Policy) Time Limit Tables for Submission of a Statement of Estimated Income

Entitlement to income-tested benefits (i.e. GIS, ALW and ALWS benefits) is based on the income that was received for the previous calendar year (i.e. base calendar year income). When a client or their spouse or common-law partner retires from employment or self-employment, or suffers a loss of pension income, their current income may no longer be as high as it was in the previous calendar year. To lessen the financial impact of this income reduction, clients can choose to have their benefit entitlement calculated with an estimate of their income for the current calendar year (after the retirement or loss) instead of with their income for the base calendar year, if it is to their advantage. This choice is called an option. A retirement, cessation of a business, and a loss or reduction of pension income are all known as events. Since these events relate to the types of income that can be granted an option, they are called optionable events. For more information, Options (Policy)

topic_title: When to send a Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form to a client Updated
text: The client may declare an optionable event. However, if you have reason to believe that an optionable event has occurred and the client did not declare it, a Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form must be sent. You may discover optional events during a review of: a GIS application or statement of income; an ISP-3041 form submitted for a different event; CPP and if available, QPP pension or benefit entitlement in ITRDS ; income received from the CRA ; a task created in Cúram due to an income variance; annual pension amounts provided by the foreign institution; or information that a client provided by letter, by telephone, or during a visit to a Service Canada Centre. In the case of a couple, the ISP-3041 form is sent to the individual who experienced the loss or reduction, even if they do not receive OAS benefits. When determining if you need to send an ISP-3041 form, you must verify whether the event has already happened or if the event will happen in the future. If the event has already happened and the time limits for submitting a statement of estimated income have not elapsed, you must immediately send the required forms to the individual who experienced the loss. Time Limit Tables for Submission of a Statement of Estimated Income If the event has not happened yet, there are situations where a form can be sent to the individual before the event or can be accepted as reported on a completed ISP-3041 form. Future Optionable Events—Sending and Accepting the ISP3041 Form Before the Event When an event is going to happen in the future and the client does not know the details at the time of reporting, it is preferred that the necessary forms are sent when the event has actually occurred. When multiple events happen in the same calendar year, a single ISP-3041 form can be used if the dates of all the events within that year can be accurately recorded on the form. If the client has another event that has not been recorded, then you must obtain another ISP-3041 form for the same calendar year. If the event is related to CPP income, all information for a CPP-related event is available in ITRDS and CPMS . Therefore, if a CPP-related event is identified and not included on the form, you can include: the event in the Statement of Estimated Income evidence in Cúram; and the details of the event in ITRDS notes. It is important that the Department has an ISP-3041 form that accurately reflects the client’s estimated income for the applicable calendar year. An ISP-3041 form is automatically sent by Cúram when an event occurred in the current month or a future month and a Retirement or Pension Reduction evidence record is created. If the event is for a future month the form will be sent at the beginning of the month in which the event occurs. If the event date has already passed and is within the prescribed timelines, you must send the applicable form manually. Cessation At any time after the OAS pension payments begin, a client can request to cease payment of their OAS pension provided the request is made in writing. Cessation of the OAS pension also results in the cessation of other related benefits (GIS and ALW benefit). If the benefits for the spouse or common-law partner are affected, they must be notified in writing. The client can request in writing to have their OAS pension reinstated at any time without having to reapply. However, no retroactivity will be paid earlier than the received date of the reinstatement request. Entitlement resumes the later of: the month following the month the written request is received; or the date indicated on the request. For more information, refer to: Cessation—OAS Pension and Benefits (Policy) ; and Cessation—OAS Pension and Benefits (Policy) Reinstatement (Policy) . Reinstatement (Policy) Cancellation A client can request to cancel their OAS pension provided the request is made: in writing; and within 6 months after the day the OAS pension began. If the request is granted, the pension and any related benefits (GIS and ALW benefit) must be repaid no later than 6 months after the day on which the cancellation request was granted. If the client does not repay the amounts within the 6 months, the pension and any related benefits are reinstated and any recovered amounts are returned to the client and their spouse or common law partner, if applicable. Once an OAS pension is cancelled, the application is deemed to have never been made and the individual will have to reapply if they wish to receive the OAS pension. They will continue to accumulate residence or to increase their OAS pension through an actuarial adjustment. For more information, refer to: Cancellation (Policy) ; and Cancellation (Policy) KA-05344 Cancellation—OAS Benefits (Scenario) (article not available).

text: Portability refers to a pensioner’s ability to receive their pension outside of Canada. The portability rules also determine the length of time that the Department can continue to pay the entitlement if a pensioner leaves Canada after their pension has been approved. The portability of the OAS pension depends on the years of Canadian residence, or the combination of residence in Canada and creditable periods in a country with which Canada has an International Social Security Agreement (ISSA) in force, that the applicant has accumulated up to their date of departure from Canada . If the total residence in Canada, or the combination of residence in Canada and creditable periods in a country with which Canada has an ISSA in force, equals: more than 20 years , the client is entitled to continued payment of the OAS pension when they leave Canada. The client is only entitled to continued payment of the GIS, ALW or ALWS benefit for a period of 6 months after the month of departure from Canada. less than 20 years , the client is only entitled to continued payment of the OAS pension and GIS, ALW or ALWS for a period of 6 months after the month of departure from Canada. topic_title: Determining eligibility under an International Social Security Agreement
text: Under an International Social Security Agreement (ISSA), an applicant’s eligibility can be determined using foreign creditable periods (e.g. contributions and/or residence) in a country with which Canada has an ISSA is force. International Social Security Agreement Country List (Work Tool) An application will be considered under an ISSA when the applicant has lived or worked in a country with an ISSA with Canada and: does not meet the minimum residence requirement to qualify for an OAS pension; or meets the minimum eligibility requirements, however they could have an earlier effective date under an ISSA. The terms of most ISSAs allow for foreign creditable periods to be added to residence in Canada to meet the minimum residence requirements. This is known as "totalization" and it is completed by staff in International Operations (IO). While totalization can assist an applicant to meet the minimum residence requirements, entitlement is still based on actual years of residence in Canada. For more information on when to transfer an OAS pension application to IO, Transfer a Client's File to International Operations (Action)

The OAS pension can be paid retroactively to a maximum of 11 months before the receipt date of the OAS pension application. The OAS pension cannot be paid to an applicant for any month earlier than 11 months before: the OAS pension application is received or deemed to be received; or the month in which the requirement to submit an application for the OAS pension was waived or deemed to have been received (age 65). For more information, Retroactivity (Policy) Effect of retroactive OAS entitlement on the spouse or common-law partner's GIS When a retroactive OAS pension payment is made, an automatic recalculation of the spouse or common law partner’s GIS will be completed if they are already in pay for the GIS. Once the applicant is entitled to the OAS pension, the rate table that their spouse or common-law partner's GIS is based on may change as their spouse is now a pensioner and not a non-pensioner spouse or in receipt of the ALW benefit. If the recalculation results in an overpayment, do not solicit the applicant or their spouse or common-law partner to have the applicant's OAS underpayment applied directly against the overpayment. When a client is entitled to an OAS pension, there may be situations where the pension is subject to a tax withhold or the client can request one. Non-resident tax Clients that do not live in Canada may be subject to non-resident tax. Tax treaties between Canada and other countries allow varying percentages of Canadian tax to be deducted. The country in which a client resides determines whether or not non-resident tax is applicable and, if so, the percentage of tax to be withheld. For more information, Non-Resident Tax (Scenario) OAS recovery tax The OAS recovery tax applies to higher-income OAS pensioners who file an income tax return and whose individual net income (for a given base taxation year) is above the threshold set by the Department of Finance. OAS pensioners who receive an OAS income-tested benefit (GIS, ALW and ALWS benefits) are not subject to the OAS recovery tax. For more information, refer to KA-04549 OAS Recovery Tax (Scenario)(article not available). Voluntary tax withhold The OAS pension is a taxable benefit. However, it is not automatically subject to a federal or provincial (e.g. Quebec) tax withhold. Pensioners can request a withhold amount on their OAS application by written request, or online through their Client Portal. For more information, Voluntary Tax Withhold (Scenario)

topic_title: Voluntary deferral and pension choices Updated
text: Voluntary Deferral Situations exist where individuals can choose to voluntarily defer receipt of their OAS pension to a later date. Voluntarily deferring the start of the OAS pension allows the individual to accrue actuarial adjustment which increases the amount of their monthly entitlement. For more information, refer to: KA-01986 Deferral of an OAS Pension (Action) (article not available); and Entitlement—Voluntary Deferral and Pension Choices (Policy) . Entitlement—Voluntary Deferral and Pension Choices (Policy) Pension choices If all of the following criteria are met, an applicant may have various choices regarding their OAS pension entitlement and effective date: the applicant is not entitled to or does not wish to apply for GIS; transitional rules may apply (i.e. the applicant was resident in Canada after age 18 and on or before July 1, 1977, or was in possession of a valid Canadian Immigration visa on July 1, 1977); and the applicant did not provide a chosen start date. If any of the above criteria are not met, Cúram will determine the most advantageous choice for the applicant and send a system generated letter. This could include calculating increased residence in Canada, actuarial adjustment of the initial partial pension, or actuarial adjustment of initial full pension. For more information, refer to: KA-01997 OAS Pension Choices (Action) (article not available); and Entitlement—Voluntary Deferral and Pension Choices (Policy) . topic_title: When can an individual or their legal representative apply?
text: An individual or their legal representative can submit an application up to 12 months before their 65th birthday or before the date on which they want their pension to start. If an individual applies up to 12 months before becoming eligible, the application remains valid. However, in some cases, you may have to verify additional periods of residence at the time the application is approved (e.g. partial pension applications approved before age 65 where an additional 40th will be attained with continued residence up to age 65). If an individual applies more than one year before their 65th birthday, deny the OAS pension application as the age requirement has not been met. If the individual applies more than one year before the date they wish their OAS pension to start, they must withdraw their application and submit a new application no more than 12 months before that date. Withdraw an Application (Scenario)

An applicant can request to withdraw their OAS application, either in writing or online via the Client Portal. The Department will approve the withdrawal request if it is received before any payments are issued to the applicant. Once an application is withdrawn, the applicant must submit a new application if they decide they want to receive the pension. For more information, Withdraw an Application (Scenario)

Example 1—Retroactive entitlement owing before incarceration date An OAS pension application is submitted and approved in February 2024 with an effective date of April 2023. After observing an ITRDS note indicating that the client is impacted by Bill C-31, and confirming with the Incarceration team that the applicant has been incarcerated since December 12, 2023, retroactive entitlement is limited to the months of April 2023 to December 2023 only. The applicant’s account is suspended effective January 2024 until the month of their release. Example 2—No retroactive entitlement An OAS pension and GIS application is submitted on January 15, 2024. The applicant’s 65th birthday is on September 20, 2024. When processing the application in November 2024, an ITRDS note is observed indicating the client is impacted by Bill C-31. Confirmation is received from the Incarceration team that the applicant has been incarcerated since August 8, 2024. Therefore, the OAS pension application can be approved effective October 2024, but the client is not entitled to receive any retroactive entitlement for the month of October. Payments are suspended effective November 2024 until the month of their release. Example An ALW benefit application is received in December 2023 and is processed with an effective date of January 2023. After observing an ITRDS note indicating that the client is impacted by Bill C-31, it is confirmed with the Incarceration team that the applicant’s spouse was incarcerated in December 2023. The entitlement for the ALW benefit is calculated as usual at the MS5 (rate table 4) rate based on the couple’s combined income for the period of January 2023 to December 2023. Effective January 2024, the spouse’s OAS pension and GIS are suspended and the applicant’s ALW benefit is paid at the MS5 (rate table 4) rate based on either the couple’s combined income or on the ALW benefit applicant’s individual income, whichever is higher. The retroactive entitlement (and subsequent monthly payments) must be paid by priority payment as the system will not issue an ALW benefit payment if the related OAS account is suspended. Example In March 2024, the Department receives a GIS application and relevant statements of income. The applicant indicates on the application that they have been incarcerated in a federal correctional facility since July 2020 and were released in August 2023. Before their incarceration, the applicant was in receipt of an OAS pension only, which was suspended effective July 2020. A review of the GIS application and the file confirms that the applicant meets all the GIS eligibility requirements and is eligible for the GIS effective April 2023. In addition, the monthly transfer of information from the Correctional Service of Canada confirms July 12, 2020, as the date the applicant was incarcerated in a federal correctional facility, and that they were released on August 11, 2023. The details provided by the applicant match. Based on the above information, the applicant's GIS application is approved effective April 2023. However, since they were incarcerated at this time, the benefit entitlement would not begin until August 2023, the month of release. The applicant will receive retroactive entitlement for the period of August 2023 to March 2024. The OAS pension is also reinstated, and retroactive entitlement is issued for the same period.

topic_title: Applicant applying from outside of Canada
text: An applicant's residency status can impact their eligibility or entitlement if they submit a GIS application when they reside outside of Canada. Refer to the following situations and outcomes: Situation 1 Outcome The applicant left Canada more than 6 months before the GIS effective date. The application will be denied because there is no eligibility or entitlement to the GIS outside of Canada beyond the 6 months after the month of departure. If the applicant returns to reside in Canada permanently, they must submit a new GIS application. Situation 2 Outcome The applicant left Canada within 6 months of the GIS effective date. The application will be approved if all the eligibility criteria are met. The applicant can receive payments for the remainder of the 6-month period after the GIS effective date. For more information, Eligibility Requirements—GIS New Business (Policy)

topic_title: Applicant's spouse or common-law partner's income or signature is not received
text: The spouse or common-law partner of a GIS applicant must provide their: income information; and signature on the: initial GIS application; statement of income form; Spousal Consent and Declaration GIS (ISS-0954A) letter; or a separate written statement that includes their personal information and their income. If both the income information and the signature are not received, the applicant can be approved if they meet the eligibility requirements. However, they will not be entitled to receive the benefit until the spouse or common-law partner provides their income information and signature. The spouse or common-law partner cannot be placed on the CRA Lifetime List if their signature is not received, as their consent was not received to obtain income information from the CRA . If the spouse or common-law partner's income is received in the future, the applicant can be paid retroactively for the payment period of the application, then the lifetime renewal criteria would apply for each payment period thereafter. topic_title: Cessation and cancellation of the GIS
text: Cessation At any time after the GIS payments begin, a client can request to cease the payment of their GIS provided the request is made in writing. When a client chooses to cease the payment of the GIS, the lifetime renewal designation ends. If the benefits for the spouse or common-law partner are impacted when the request to cease the GIS is approved, they must be notified in writing. If the client wishes to receive the GIS in the future, they must submit a new application. topic_title: Client departs from and returns to Canada after approval
text: Portability refers to a client's ability to receive their pension or benefit outside of Canada. The GIS is not portable. topic_title: Income is received for the wrong income year
text: When a valid application for the GIS is submitted, it protects the date of the application (and possible retroactivity) based on the date the application was received. If the statement of income or the income information received from the CRA is not for the correct base calendar year, the requirement for the statement of income is met. However, entitlement to the GIS cannot be determined until the required income for the applicable payment period is obtained from the CRA or the applicant. To determine which base calendar year income is required, you must consider the earliest possible effective date of the GIS. Refer to the examples below: Example: Situation 1 Direction A client has been in pay for an OAS pension since June 2021. They submit an Application for the Guaranteed Income Supplement (ISP-3025) form on July 2, 2023. The GIS application is processed on July 24, 2023. The GIS application can be approved with an effective date of August 2022 (11 months before the application was received). To pay the full retroactive entitlement of August 2022 to July 2023, the following statements of income are required: 2021 (July 2022 to June 2023 payment period); and 2022 (July 2023 to June 2024 payment period). The CRA income feed has been received for 2022; however, the 2021 income is not available from the CRA . The requirement for the statement of income is met and payments for the client's GIS can begin effective July 2023. The period of August 2022 to June 2023 is date protected and can be considered once the 2021 income has been obtained from the client or the CRA . Example: Situation 2 Direction An Application for the Old Age Security Pension and the Guaranteed Income Supplement (ISP-3550) form is received on October 2, 2023. The applicant's 65th birthday is at a future date of August 5, 2024. The application is processed on November 13, 2023, and the OAS pension is approved with an effective date of September 2024. In this case, the client is being considered for the GIS at the same time as the OAS pension (i.e. in November 2023). Once an individual indicates that they wish to receive the GIS, a request is made to the CRA for the applicant's income information. Since the application is being processed in the July 2023 to June 2024 payment period, the income for 2022 is received from the CRA feed. The requirement for the statement of income has been met; however, entitlement cannot be determined until the income that coincides with the payment period of the effective date (2023) is received. Since the 2023 income is not available at the time of processing, the application will have to be held until the 2023 income is available and entitlement can be determined. The payment period of the effective date is date protected. However, any subsequent payment year is reviewed individually and is subject to the conditions of the lifetime renewal designation.

When a partial OAS pension application is approved, the entitlement of the pension does not increase with additional years of residence in Canada. However, if the applicant has resided in Canada for less than 10 years at the effective date and they are eligible for the OAS pension under an International Social Security Agreement, the applicant may be entitled to a prorated GIS, provided all eligibility and entitlement criteria have been met. Entitlement to prorated income-tested benefits is calculated at 1/10th of the benefit rate for each year of residence in Canada and increases with each additional year of residence in Canada after approval of the benefit, up to a maximum of 10 years. You can validate the marital status declared by the applicant on the GIS application using the marital status information received from the CRA . CRA Marital Status Evidence—View in Cúram (Action) Applicants who meet the definition of separated or divorced before their earliest effective date are treated as single and documentation is not required to prove their marital status. If the marital status has changed between the time the OAS pension was approved and the GIS going into pay, proof must be obtained to validate when the marital status changes occurred to ensure any retroactive entitlement is calculated using the client's correct marital status. Documentary Evidence—Marital Status (Policy) For more information regarding marital status, Marital Status (Scenario) For GIS Take-Up applications, proof of marital status is not required for married or common-law pensioners as they have already self-identified as a couple on their Income Tax and Benefit Return. For more information, GIS Take-Up Applications (Knowledge) Marital status rate tables A rate table provides a listing of income ranges and corresponding monthly entitlements to income-tested benefits according to a predetermined maximum allowable income level for a specific marital status. There are 5 rate tables. They are used to determine the monthly benefit entitlement for the GIS, the ALW and the ALWS benefits based on the applicant's income level and marital status. Under most circumstances when the non-pensioner spouse or common-law partner becomes eligible for an OAS pension and the GIS, the couple will receive more GIS between them than they did when only one of them was a pensioner. However, there are situations where the combination of income levels and years of entitlement results in a lower combined amount. Bill C-31 was enacted on April 1, 1996, and allows the Department to pay a married or common-law couple using separate rate tables to ensure their total benefits are not less than they were receiving before the non-pensioner spouse became a pensioner. In this situation, Cúram will calculate the future and any retroactive entitlement according to the appropriate rate table. For more information on the rate tables and how to calculate retroactive entitlement under Bill C-31, refer to: Marital Status and Rate Tables for Income-Tested Benefits ; and Marital Status and Rate Tables for Income-Tested Benefits Paying Two Pensioners at One Pensioner Rate (Policy) . The minimum income guarantee increases the maximum amount of the GIS payable to individuals who are eligible to a partial OAS pension to ensure that all GIS clients receive the same minimum level of income under the OAS program. For example, if an applicant is approved for a partial OAS pension and the GIS, they will also receive additional monies commonly known as the GIS top-up . Cúram will automatically calculate the amount of the GIS top-up and add the amount to the client's regular GIS entitlement. The amount is equal to the difference between the maximum OAS pension and the amount of the client's partial pension.

The GIS can be paid retroactively to a maximum of 11 months before the receipt date of the GIS application. The GIS cannot be paid to an applicant for any month earlier than 11 months before: the GIS application is received or deemed to be received; or the month in which the requirement to submit an application for the GIS was waived or deemed to have been received (age 65). A sponsored immigrant will only be eligible for the GIS if they meet all eligibility requirements. However, they will not be entitled to receive the GIS. In October 2025, amendments to the Old Age Security Act came into force limiting entitlement to the GIS for the duration of the sponsorship agreement, unless there is a sponsorship breakdown. Before October 2025, a sponsored immigrant was not entitled to receive the GIS for the duration of the sponsorship agreement, unless there was a sponsorship breakdown or the sponsored immigrant accumulated 10 full years of residence in Canada after the age of 18. In certain circumstances, an applicant's sponsorship agreement details must be validated and documentary evidence provided before authorizing the GIS application case. A Sponsorship Review task must be created to review the account 6 months before the entitlement date to confirm eligibility and entitlement. Entitlement to an ALW benefit is based on the combined net income of the OAS pensioner and the ALW benefit applicant. An ALW benefit application must be approved if the applicant has met the eligibility criteria. However, there will be situations where an application is approved with no entitlement to the benefit. An application is approved with no entitlement when: the applicant is a sponsored immigrant at the effective date; the applicant has a spouse or common-law partner who is eligible to the GIS but not entitled to it as they are a sponsored immigrant; the combined income of the applicant and their spouse or common-law partner is in excess; or the applicant is incarcerated. An application will be approved but entitlement to the benefit cannot be determined in situations when: eligibility has been met; and required information or documentation has not been received to determine the entitlement amount (e.g. clarification of their or their spouse or common-law partner's income, documentation required to confirm foreign pension, documentation to confirm sponsorship agreement details).

text: An applicant's residence status can affect their eligibility or entitlement if they submit an ALW benefit application when they reside outside of Canada. Refer to the following situations and outcomes: The applicant left Canada more than 6 months before the ALW benefit effective date The applicant left Canada more than 6 months before the ALW benefit effective date The applicant has at least 20 years of residence in Canada after age 18 and left Canada within 6 months of the ALW benefit effective date The applicant has at least 20 years of residence in Canada after age 18 and left Canada within 6 months of the ALW benefit effective date The applicant has at least 10 years but less than 20 years of residence in Canada after age 18 and left Canada within 6 months of the ALW benefit effective date The applicant has at least 10 years but less than 20 years of residence in Canada after age 18 and left Canada within 6 months of the ALW benefit effective date At the effective date, the applicant has less than 10 years of residence in Canada after age 18, has lived or worked in a country with which Canada has an ISSA in force, and left Canada within 6 months of the ALW benefit effective date At the effective date, the applicant has less than 10 years of residence in Canada after age 18, has lived or worked in a country with which Canada has an ISSA in force, and left Canada within 6 months of the ALW benefit effective date At the effective date, the applicant has less than 10 years of residence in Canada after age 18, has not lived or worked in a country with which Canada has an ISSA in force, and left Canada 6 months or more before the ALW benefit effective date At the effective date, the applicant has less than 10 years of residence in Canada after age 18, has not lived or worked in a country with which Canada has an ISSA in force, and left Canada 6 months or more before the ALW benefit effective date Situation 1 Outcome The applicant left Canada more than 6 months before the ALW benefit effective date. The application will be denied because there is no eligibility or entitlement to the ALW benefit outside of Canada beyond the 6 months after the month of departure. If the applicant returns to Canada permanently, they must submit a new ALW benefit application and statement of income. Situation 2 Outcome The applicant has at least 20 years of residence in Canada after age 18 and left Canada within 6 months of the ALW benefit effective date. The application will be approved if all the eligibility criteria are met. The applicant can receive payments for the remainder of the 6-month period after the effective date. Situation 3 Outcome The applicant has at least 10 years but less than 20 years of residence in Canada after age 18 and left Canada within 6 months of the ALW benefit effective date. The application will be approved if the applicant was residing in Canada on the day before the application's approval date. The applicant can receive the payments for the remainder of the 6-month period after the effective date. Situation 4 Outcome At the effective date, the applicant has less than 10 years of residence in Canada after age 18, has lived or worked in a country with which Canada has an ISSA in force, and left Canada within 6 months of the ALW benefit effective date. The application must be processed by staff in International Operations (IO) who will determine eligibility and communicate the approval or denial to the applicant. IO staff: The application will be approved if totalization is possible under the applicable ISSA and all eligibility criteria are met. The applicant can receive payments for the remainder of the 6-month period after the effective date. Situation 5 Outcome At the effective date, the applicant has less than 10 years of residence in Canada after age 18, has not lived or worked in a country with which Canada has an ISSA in force, and left Canada 6 months or more before the ALW benefit effective date. The application will be denied. For more information, Eligibility Requirements— ALW Benefit New Business (Policy)

topic_title: Cessation and cancellation of the ALW benefit
text: Cessation At any time after the ALW benefit payments begin, the client can request to cease the payment of their ALW benefit provided the request is made in writing. When a client chooses to cease the payment of the ALW benefit, the lifetime renewal designation ends. If the benefits for the spouse or common-law partner are impacted when the request to cease the ALW benefit is approved, they must be notified in writing. If the client wishes to receive the ALW in the future, they must submit a new application. For more information on ceasing the ALW benefit and the requirements to reinstate it, refer to: Cessation—OAS Pension and Benefits (Policy) ; and Cessation—OAS Pension and Benefits (Policy) Reinstatement (Policy) . Reinstatement (Policy) Cancellation Although the client cannot request a cancellation of the ALW benefit in the same way that an OAS or GIS pensioner can, their benefits are affected if the OAS pensioner requests to cancel their OAS pension or GIS. For more information, refer to: Cancellation (Policy) ; and Cancellation (Policy) KA-05344 Cancellation—OAS Benefits (Scenario) (article not available).

topic_title: Client departs from and returns to Canada after approval
text: Portability refers to a client's ability to receive their pension or benefit outside of Canada. The ALW benefit is not portable. The ALW benefit is no longer payable when a client has been absent from Canada for a period longer than 6 months after the month of their departure from Canada. When a client has been absent from Canada temporarily, their ALW benefit payments can resume in the month they return to Canada. If the absence was not temporary, the client must reapply for the ALW if they wish to receive it when they return. For more information, refer to: Client Departs from or Returns to Canada (Scenario) ; and Client Departs from or Returns to Canada (Scenario) Entitlement—Portability of OAS Pension and Benefits (Policy) . topic_title: Determining eligibility under an International Social Security Agreement
text: Under an International Social Security Agreement (ISSA), an applicant's eligibility can be determined using foreign creditable periods (e.g. contributions and/or residence) in a country with which Canada has an ISSA in force. International Social Security Agreement Country List (Work Tool) An application will be considered under an ISSA when an applicant has lived or worked in a country with an ISSA with Canada and: does not meet the minimum residence requirement to qualify for an ALW benefit and has completed creditable periods in an ISSA country; or meets the minimum eligibility requirements, however they could have an earlier effective date under an ISSA. The terms of most ISSAs allow for foreign creditable periods to be added to residence in Canada to meet the minimum residence requirements. This is known as "totalization" and is completed by International Operations (IO) staff. While totalization can assist an applicant to meet the minimum residence requirements, entitlement is still based on actual years of residence in Canada. For more information on when to transfer an ALW benefit application to IO, Transfer a Client's File to International Operations (Action)

topic_title: Determining eligibility using the data elements of automatic enrolment
text: The automatic enrolment criteria that establish eligibility for the OAS pension can be used to confirm the legal status and residence eligibility requirements for the ALW benefit, only if you are processing the ALW benefit application after the applicant has been automatically enrolled for an OAS pension and the GIS at age 65. Eligibility Requirements— ALW Benefit New Business (Policy) Although documentation to support residence or legal status may not be required in these cases, the Department retains the right to request documentary evidence at any time before or after the approval of the ALW benefit application. You cannot hold applications that are received more than one month before the applicant's 65th birthday to be processed after the eligibility criteria have been met. topic_title: Income is received for the wrong income year
text: When a valid application for the ALW benefit is submitted, it protects the date of the application (and possible retroactivity) based on the date the application was received. If the statement of income or the income information received from the CRA , is not for the correct base calendar year, the requirement for the statement of income is met. However, entitlement to the ALW benefit cannot be determined until the required income for the applicable payment period is obtained from the CRA or the applicant. To determine which base calendar year income is required, you must consider the earliest possible effective date of the ALW benefit. Example: Situation 1 Outcome An applicant submits an Application for the Allowance or Allowance for the Survivor – Under the Old Age Security Program (ISP-3008) form on July 2, 2023. The ALW benefit application is processed on July 24, 2023. The ALW benefit application can be approved with an effective date of August 2022 (11 months before the application was received). To pay the full retroactive entitlement of August 2022 to July 2023, the following statements of income are required: 2021 (July 2022 to June 2023 payment period); and 2022 (July 2023 to June 2024 payment period). The CRA income feed has been received for 2022; however, the 2021 income is not available from the CRA . The requirement for the statement of income is met and payments for the client's ALW benefit can begin effective July 2023. The period of August 2022 to June 2023 is date protected and can be considered once the 2021 income has been obtained from the client or the CRA . Example: Situation 2 Outcome An Application for Allowance Under the Old Age Security Program (ISP-3033) form is received on October 2, 2023. The applicant's 60th birthday is at a future date of August 5, 2024. The application is processed on November 13, 2023, and the ALW benefit is approved effective September 2024. Once an individual applies for the ALW benefit, a request is made to the CRA for the applicant's income information. Since the application is being processed in the July 2023 to June 2024 payment period, the income for 2022 is received from the CRA feed. The requirement for the statement of income has been met; however, entitlement cannot be determined until the income that coincides with the payment period of the effective date (2023) is received. Since the 2023 income is not available at the time of processing, the application will have to be held until the 2023 income is available and entitlement can be determined. The payment period of the effective date is date protected. However, any subsequent payment year is reviewed individually and is subject to the conditions of the lifetime renewal designation.

When an ALW benefit application is approved with 10 years of Canadian residence, the entitlement of the benefit does not increase with additional years of residence in Canada. However, if the applicant has resided in Canada for less than 10 years at the effective date and they are eligible under an International Social Security Agreement, the applicant may be entitled to a prorated ALW benefit, provided all eligibility and entitlement criteria have been met. Entitlement to prorated income-tested benefits is calculated at 1/10th of the benefit rate for each year of residence in Canada and increases with each additional year of residence in Canada after approval of the benefit, up to a maximum of 10 years. This is known as the special qualifying factor or proration of income-tested benefits. For more information, Special Qualifying Factor (Work Tool)

topic_title: Paying an ALW benefit when the spouse or common-law partner does not wish to receive the GIS
text: To be eligible and entitled to receive an ALW benefit, the applicant's spouse or common-law partner must be eligible to the GIS. However, there may be instances where they are entitled to receive the GIS, but do not wish to receive it. This choice will not affect the payment of the ALW benefit to their spouse or common-law partner, provided all the conditions of eligibility are met. In these cases, the spouse or common-law partner must still apply for the GIS, but can advise in writing or by completing the statement attached to the letter that they do not wish to receive it. Once eligibility to the GIS has been determined, continue processing the ALW benefit application. Eligibility and entitlement overrides will be required on both accounts. For more information, Marital Status—Income-Tested Benefits Entitlement (Policy)

The ALW benefit can be paid retroactively to a maximum of 11 months before the receipt date of the ALW benefit application. The ALW benefit cannot be paid to an applicant for any month earlier than 11 months before the ALW benefit application is received or deemed to be received. When an applicant has already applied for the ALW benefit for the current payment period and there may be retroactive entitlement for a previous payment period, you can obtain the relevant income from the CRA . If the CRA income is not available, the applicant must complete and submit a statement of income. A new ALW benefit application is not required. For more information, Retroactivity (Policy) Using a GIS application or statement of income form to date protect the ALW benefit entitlement If the applicant has not applied for an ALW benefit, the receipt date of the following forms can conditionally date protect a subsequently received ALW benefit application: Application for the Guaranteed Income Supplement (ISP-3025); Application for the Guaranteed Income Supplement with Statement of Income (ISP-3025B); Statement of Income for the Guaranteed Income Supplement, the Allowance or Allowance for the Survivor for payment period of July (20XX) to June (20XX) with Information Sheet (ISP-3026); Application for the Old Age Security Pension and the Guaranteed Income Supplement (ISP-3550); Combined OAS and GIS online application and GIS standalone online application; and GIS Take-up applications: GIS Take-up Applications (T1) Pensioner, Exclusively for Processing Centres (ISP-3042); GIS Take-Up Application (T2) SPS/C-L, Exclusively for Processing Centres (ISP-3043); or GIS Take-up Applications (T3) Pensioner, Exclusively for Processing Centres (ISP-3044). To be date protected, applicants must submit a valid ALW benefit application within 60 days of: the GIS application or statement of income form received date; or the date the ALW benefit application was sent to the applicant for completion, if one was sent while processing the GIS application or statement of income form. For more information and to review the conditions to date protect an ALW benefit application, Applications Date of Receipt (Policy) Effect of retroactive ALW benefit entitlement on the spouse or common-law partner's GIS When a retroactive ALW benefit payment is made, a recalculation of the spouse or common law partner's GIS is required if they are already in pay for GIS benefits as a pensioner married to a non-pensioner spouse. Once the applicant is entitled to the ALW benefit, the rate table that their spouse or common-law partner's GIS is based on will change. The result of this calculation is always an overpayment for the spouse or common-law partner if they were receiving GIS payments. Depending on the couple's level of combined income, the overpayment will be equal to or less than the amount of the ALW benefit underpayment. Do not solicit the applicant to have their ALW benefit underpayment applied directly against their spouse or common-law partner's overpayment. Each person is entitled to their own benefit. text: An individual or their legal representative can submit an application up to 12 months before their 60th birthday and up to 11 months after their 65th birthday. topic_title: Assessing the client’s primary place of residence
text: To continue receiving a non-portable OAS pension or an income-tested benefit after approval, the client’s primary place of residence must be in Canada. The client may leave Canada temporarily and may also have a second home that they visit often, but Canada must be where they make their primary home and normally live. When a client leaves Canada after their benefits have been approved, you must determine whether the absence is temporary or permanent as this can affect their entitlement to benefits. It can also affect the requirements to reinstate the benefit when they return. When a client regularly visits a second home outside of Canada, you may also have to confirm that Canada is still their primary place of residence. Portability refers to a client’s ability to receive their pension outside of Canada. The OAS pension is only portable once the client has accumulated at least 20 or more years of residence in Canada after the age of 18 or has met the 20 years through a combination of Canadian residence and foreign creditable periods in a country with which Canada has an International Social Security Agreement. If a client was originally approved for an OAS pension with less than 20 years of Canadian residence, they can continue to accumulate residence after approval to allow portability of their pension. Therefore, if a pensioner leaves Canada, you must reassess their residence history to determine if they have acquired the necessary years of residence to deem their pension portable. However, the rate of entitlement does not increase with additional years of residence after the approval of the pension. For examples on portability, Examples—Portability If the client was approved for their OAS pension with less than 20 years of Canadian residence after the age of 18, you must request an updated residence statement in writing if it appears they have continued to live in Canada and may now meet the 20-year requirement for portability. Portability only applies to the OAS pension. The GIS , ALW benefit and ALWS benefit are non-portable benefits. The payment of a non-portable OAS pension, GIS , ALW benefit or ALWS benefit are limited to 6 months after the month the individual left Canada, regardless of whether the absence is temporary or not. If the pensioner is absent from Canada and their GIS is suspended in the 7th month after their departure from Canada, the ALW benefit is also suspended even if the ALW benefit recipient is still in Canada. For more information, Entitlement—Portability of OAS Pension and Benefits (Policy)

To qualify for a credit split, legally separated spouses and common-law partners must be separated for a period of at least one year. Currently, ITRDS will deny applications with a receipt date before the required one-year period of separation date. If a credit split application for legally separated spouses or common-law partners is received and the couple is separated for less than one year, you must determine: if the application is received more than 3 months from the one year period of separation date, deny the credit split and send the appropriate denial letter. if the application is received within 3 months or less of the one year period of separation date, you must BF the file until the former spouses or common-law partners have been separated for a full year. once the 12 month separation period has ended, contact the applicant to confirm their relationship status: if the applicant is no longer separated after 12 months, you must deny the credit split as per the legislation. if the applicant is still separated after 12 months, follow the normal procedures to process the credit split application and apply the following exception: When data capturing the credit split application in ITRDS , you must enter in the Date stamp field the 1st day of the month, following the month in which the 12-month period of separation is reached.

The effective date of the approval of the credit split is the last day of the month in which the request or application is received. Pensionable Earnings will be attributed the month following the month in which the credit split is approved. When an existing benefit in pay is to be adjusted or a new benefit is put into pay as a result of earnings from a credit split, the effective date will be the month following the month the credit split is approved. A benefit that was not payable in the absence of the credit split cannot be paid for any months before the month in which the earnings are attributed. For example, if a request or application is received in March, the earnings resulting from the approval of the credit split will be attributed to the record of earnings effective April. For information on the effective date of the attribution of pensionable earnings, Credit Splitting (Policy)

topic_title: Child Rearing Drop-In and credit split Updated
text: As of January 2019, the Child Rearing Provision includes the Child Rearing Drop-In (CRDI). The CRDI adds Unadjusted Pensionable Earnings (UPE) to periods of low or zero earnings in the first or second additional contributory period for the time when the child was under 7 years of age. As CRDI amounts are UPE, they are subject to credit splitting upon divorce or separation. The CRDI UPE amount is determined using earnings from the 5 years before the birth or adoption of the child, or the date the contributor gained decision making responsibility and parenting time of the child. If a credit split occurs before the CRDI calculation and any earnings from the 5 years before the child's birth, adoption or date they came under the decision making responsibility and parenting time of the contributor were split, the divided earnings are used in the CRDI calculation. If a credit split occurs after CRDI amounts are attributed, and the credit split changes any of the earnings amounts in the 5 years prior to the birth or adoption of the child, the CRDI amounts that were originally attributed within the period of cohabitation are not recalculated, however, they are divided along with the other UPE. If a credit split occurs after CRDI amounts are attributed, the credit split changes any of the earnings amounts in the 5 years before the child's birth, adoption or date they came under the decision making responsibility and parenting time of the contributor, and the CRDI period extends past the period of cohabitation, then CRDI amounts for the post-cohabitation period are recalculated taking into account the newly divided earnings. For an example of a CRDI subject to the division of UPEs, Examples—Child Rearing Drop-In Calculation

The applicant must meet the credit split eligibility requirements. To be eligible for a credit split: The Department must be informed of the dissolution of a marriage by separation, divorce or legal annulment, or the dissolution of a common-law union by separation. An application must be submitted, unless the divorce or legal annulment took place on or after January 1, 1987. The couple must have cohabited for a period of at least one continuous year. Documentation must be provided to support dates of cohabitation. At least one former spouse or former common-law partner must have CPP credits. The combined CPP credits must exceed twice the Year's Basic Exemption (YBE). Conditions within the terms of any written spousal agreements may affect the ability of CPP to split the credits of the couple. These conditions are also dependent on the date of the spousal agreement and the province in which it was signed. The separation, divorce or legal annulment must have taken place within the required time frames: Table 1. Credit split eligibility requirements Situation Minimum Period of Cohabitation Minimum Period of Separation Time limit to apply A divorce or an annulment granted before January 1, 1987 36 consecutive months N/A 36 months from the date of the divorce or annulment A divorce or an annulment on or after January 1, 1987 1 year None No time limit A separation of legally married spouses 1 year 1 year beginning on or after January 1, 1987 No time limit A separation of legally married spouses if former spouse is deceased 1 year 1 year beginning on or after January 1, 1987 3 years from the date of the former spouse's death A breakdown of a common-law relationship 1 year 1 year beginning on or after January 1, 1987 4 years from the date of separation A breakdown of a common-law relationship if former partner is deceased 1 year Can be less than 1 year beginning on or after January 1, 1987 4 years from the date of separation For situations that require a minimum period of separation as an eligibility condition, the applicant and their former spouse or common-law partner must meet this requirement at the time of application, and must still be living separate and apart at the time the credit split application or request is made. Former (divorced or annulled) or separated legal spouses or common-law partners who have reconciled and resumed cohabitation are not eligible for a credit split if they are reconciled and living together at the time of the credit split application. When a minimum of one year of separation is required and you receive an application before the 12th month of separation, go to Applications received too early in the Exceptions and special cases section below. A credit split is not permitted for: a year in which the combined pensionable earnings of the former spouses or common-law partners was not more than twice the YBE; the period before one of the former spouse or common-law partner reach age 18 or after they reached age 70; the period when one of the former spouses or common-law partners was a beneficiary of a Retirement pension under CPP or QPP; or any months that were excluded from the base contributory period of one of the former spouses or common-law partners because they were considered to be disabled for the purpose of the CPP or QPP disability benefit. For more information on eligibility requirements, Credit Splitting (Policy)

topic_title: Is the applicant or non-applicant in pay for an SVR pension from the same deceased separated legal spouse? New
text: Effective January 1, 2025, when a credit split application is received and approved for separated legal spouses, there is no eligibility to a CPP SVR pension when one of the separated legal spouses dies. If a separated legal spouse is receiving an SVR pension and the Department receives a credit split application on or after January 1, 2025 for the same deceased separated legal spouse, the SVR pension ceases as of the effective date of the credit split approval. This applies regardless of whether it is the estate of the deceased contributor, or the living separated legal spouse who makes the application or request for the credit split. An SVR pension that remains in pay awaiting processing of the credit split could result in an SVR pension overpayment. This overpayment is valid and collectable. To avoid an overpayment situation for the SVR recipient you must: ensure you screen the credit split application at the time of receipt; and suspend or terminate the SVR pension. In some situations, you must suspend the SVR pension before continuing to review the credit split application or request. Suspension of the SVR pension should only occur when more information is required to determine eligibility to the credit split. Some examples of when you must suspend are (this is not an exhaustive list): when the credit split application meets the criteria to be processed by the Dual Processing Unit in Timmins, ON; when there is a CPPD application in PWS or on hold in ITRDS ; when a letter of representation must be sent to the deceased separated legal spouse's estate; when the period of separation is less than 12 months; when the applicant has indicated they have a spousal agreement with their legal separated spouse but did not provide it, and it was signed: before June 4, 1986; in British Columbia on or after July 1, 1995; in Quebec on or after July 1, 1989; in Saskatchewan on or after January 1, 1987; or in Alberta on or after October 1, 2005. For information on contacting the client to notify them of the suspension of the SVR pension, as well as instructions on how to suspend the SVR pension, Suspend Benefits (Scenario) When no additional information is required to determine eligibility to the credit split, or you have requested and received the required information, you must terminate the SVR pension before continuing to process the credit split application or request. A credit split application will be denied when a spousal agreement signed before June 4, 1986 has a general clause releasing the former spouse from any property claims, present and future. In this situation, the Kempling remedy may be applied. The Kempling remedy allows the applicant to have the amount of pension credits added to their record of earnings, which they would have received if the credit split had been approved. The non-applicant's record of earnings is not adjusted. The remedy is only applied if it is to the applicant's advantage. To apply the Kempling remedy to a credit split, the Erroneous Advice/Administrative Error Submission (ISP0506) form must be prepared and signed and approved at the regional level according to the Delegation of Authorities (PDF, 262 KB) Download link , however, the form does not need to be sent to National Headquarters for approval. Delegation of Authorities If you are unsure if the Kempling remedy can be applied to a credit split, submit a Business Expertise Request Tool enquiry to be escalated to CPP Operational Policy for review. topic_title: Periods of separation during the cohabitation period
text: After January 1, 1987, former legal spouses or former common-law partners may have their credit split range of division impacted if they have periods of separation during their cohabitation. Living arrangements where former legal spouses or former common-law partners are living separate and apart but in the same residence are considered to be separated. However, if the couple lived apart for reasons beyond their control, those periods of separation are to be included in the cohabitation period. The Interrelationships will need to reflect the periods of separation, based on the following: Table 2. Periods of separation during the cohabitation period Separation Period Period after Resuming Cohabitation Is Period of Separation included in Period of Cohabitation? Less than 90 days No specific time period Included. Between 90 days and 12 months Less than 90 days Not included. Cohabitation ends with 1st date of separation. Between 90 days and 12 months Greater than 90 days Included. Greater than 12 months Less than 12 months Not included. Cohabitation period ends with 1st date of separation. Greater than 12 months Greater than 12 months Not included. This would require two periods of cohabitation. When processing the credit split, it will result in two ranges of division. For example: Marriage Date: May 1995 1st Separation Date: January 2007 Date of Reunion: May 2010 2nd Separation Date: September 2015 Divorce Date: October 2016 For more information on Interrelationships, go to Update the applicant's information section below.

topic_title: Special handling situations (Dual Processing Unit only)
text: Divorce before to July 1989 RRQ credit split eligibility rules state that for divorces before July 1989, the Department must receive the application within 3 years (36 months) of divorce. If you do not receive the application within the 36-months, you cannot divide the RRQ earnings. Currently, ITRDS only applies the 36-month period if the date of divorce is before January 1, 1987 (CPP rules). This results in incorrect division of RRQ earnings. One client RRQ only, second client CPP only with RRQ inquiry When at least one of the clients on a credit split application has CPP contributions, ITRDS should not deny the application for reason “Jurisdiction RRQ”. Currently, if the Contributions screen identifies one CPP client as “CPP Contributor with RRQ Inquiry”, and the other client is “RRQ contributor only”, ITRDS incorrectly denies these applications for reason "Jurisdiction RRQ". Dual only—Credit split withdrawn by RRQ When the Dual unit processed a Credit Split application, ITRDS receives information from RRQ on which years to divide, then it updates the earnings record. If RRQ withdraws that division, ITRDS has insufficient rules to determine which years should be “undivided” and the division remains on the client's records. For information on other historical special handling cases, Special Handling History (Knowledge)

A couple may enter into a spousal agreement before a legal marriage or common-law relationship or upon the breakup of a legal marriage or common-law relationship. Spousal agreements or court orders dated on or after June 4, 1986, may affect eligibility depending on when and where the agreement was signed. The credit split application cannot be approved if the agreement: specifically mentions CPP; indicates the intention of the spouses that there be no division of credits; has not been invalidated by a court order; and was signed in one of the following provinces on or after the following dates: British Columbia, July 1, 1995; Quebec, July 1, 1989; Saskatchewan, January 1, 1987; or Alberta, October 1, 2005. Spousal agreements dated before June 4, 1986 may be binding on the Minister for the purposes of a credit split if the agreement contains a special release clause. The credit split application cannot be approved when the spousal agreement contains: a waiver to all claims to CPP credits and benefits; and the intention, by both parties, to reach a final disposition of all marital matters. For more information on spousal agreements, Credit Splitting (Policy)

Credit splitting is a provision that allows CPP pension credits (unadjusted pensionable earnings) to be divided equally between 2 individuals following the dissolution of their relationship. CPP credits that were earned during a period of cohabitation in a marriage or common-law union can be divided between former spouses or former common-law partners, except for Post Retirement earnings. Post Retirement earnings are considered outside of an individual's contributory period and cannot be included in the division of earnings following a request for a credit split. As of January 1, 2019, the CPP enhancement was implemented and former spouses or former common-law partners who apply for a credit split will divide both their base and first additional CPP credits; as of January 1, 2024 second additional CPP credits will be divided as well. In order to divide first additional and second additional CPP credits, at least one of the former spouses or common-law partners must have made enhanced contributions during their cohabitation period. Credit splitting can only take place after: divorce; legal annulment separation from a legal marriage; or separation from a common-law union. A credit split is mandatory for divorces or legal annulments that occurred on or after January 1, 1987. Effective January 1, 2025, when a credit split application is received and approved for separated legal spouses, there is no eligibility to a CPP SVR pension when one of the separated legal spouses dies. If a separated legal spouse is receiving an SVR pension and the Department receives a credit split application on or after January 1, 2025 for the same deceased separated legal spouse, the SVR pension ceases as of the effective date of the credit split approval. The effective date of the credit split approval is the last day of the month in which the credit split application or request was received. Pension credits are attributed the first day of the month after the effective date of the credit split approval. For more information on credit splitting and CPP enhancement, refer to CPP Enhancement (Knowledge) and Calculation of CPP Benefits (Knowledge) . topic_title: Are there contesting applications (legal spouse vs common-law partner)?
text: If the SVR pension application has been processed and you receive an application from another applicant, you must determine who is eligible to the SVR pension. The new applicant must provide evidence that they are the surviving spouse of the deceased contributor as defined by CPP. For more information, Survivor's Pension—Contesting Applications (Policy) If you initially obtained substantial information and evidence, the decision to change the SVR pension from one individual to another should rarely occur. To make this change, the evidence submitted to support the second application must challenge the information that was submitted by the first applicant. In cases where another individual submits a contesting application for an SVR pension already in pay, you must: review the original decision and all supporting documentation; review the new application and documentary evidence; and analyze and compare the applications to determine who is eligible. If you determine that there are anomalies or discrepancies in either applicant's information, refer the file to the Integrity Services Branch. Referral Process for Administrative Investigations—CPP (Scenario) Only one person can be the survivor for the purpose of the CPP SVR pension. If the information and evidence collected establish the eligibility of the second applicant as the survivor, you must terminate the first SVR pension. You must send the Benefit Status - Cancel or Terminate (ISS-4559) letter to the first applicant to notify them of the decision to terminate the SVR pension, provide details of any receivables generated from the termination and give reconsideration rights. Departmental Receivables (Overpayments) (Scenario) As only one person can be the survivor for the purpose of the SVR pension, payments made to any other person—regardless of whether they were thought to be the survivor at the time of approval—are payments to which the person was not entitled. The overpayment is a debt to the Crown and as such must be recovered. The overpayment cannot be automatically remitted. Review the evidence and information on the file. An overpayment can only be considered for remission, in full or in part, in cases where the Minister is satisfied that a person meets one of the 4 conditions, as set out in the remission provisions. Remit an Overpayment (Scenario) This direction is for all new cases effective November 17, 2020. Closed cases will not be overturned or reviewed.
