topic_title: Changing the date of death based on new evidence
text: A Service Canada manager is not bound by the issuance or cancellation of a death certificate by any authority other than the CPP and the OAS Act. However, the manager does have authority to change the presumed date of death based on new evidence or information. If a manager is satisfied that the date of death is different from the one already determined, the client is considered to have died on this new date. You must review all benefit applications on a client’s file and on that client’s survivors’ files. This allows you to identify if: the client’s survivors are currently receiving CPP or OAS benefits; the client has ever been in receipt of or has made an application for a benefit under OAS, CPP or QPP. Following the findings of these reviews, Service Canada staff must adjust the affected benefit dates, based on the client's new presumed date of death.
Declaration Disappearance Presumption of death Proof of death

The following documentation is required before Service Canada can issue a presumption of death certificate: Evidence describing the circumstances surrounding the person’s disappearance (e.g. newspaper clippings, police reports, search and rescue reports, eye witness statements, private insurance companies’ reports); A court order issued in a province that has a Presumption of Death Act ; or A detailed report received from a Service Canada centre or a mail processing centre (e.g. date of relevant incident or accident, date when the person was last seen). These reports must provide information to help the Service Canada manager make a presumption of death.

To apply for a DTH, SVR, ALWS or Children's benefits, an eligible survivor of the presumed dead contributor must submit: a death certificate; or a Statutory Declaration—Haïti (ISP1813) form as evidence to confirm that the presumed date of death of the contributor is January 12, 2010 . An individual applying for a DTH, SVR, ALWS or Children's benefits, who has not submitted proof of death, but provided sufficient information on the circumstances, place and date of death of the deceased contributor, is not required to complete the ISP1813 form—the application can be accepted without it.

topic_title: Internships, Articling and Practical Working Experience
text: Individuals wanting to obtain their university diploma and become a full member of their profession, must: write an examination and complete an internship in a hospital (doctors); article in a law firm (lawyers); or gain practical work experience in an accounting firm (chartered accountants). Other than during the vacation period that immediately follows the academic year, a graduate student is not entitled to child's benefits if they are completing an internship or articling. Generally, child's benefits are not paid during internships that follow the attainment of a diploma, degree or certificate. The only possible exception is in the field of Dietetics.
Students are entitled to payment for the entire vacation period if they have been in full-time attendance at school or university immediately before a vacation period within April 1 and September 30.

If a student is taking correspondence courses, the student must submit a Declaration of Attendance when courses start and at 4-month intervals. The school must also provide a written statement proving that the student is taking correspondence courses. The student must notify CPP immediately if they reduce their full-time participation by: deciding to withdraw from the program; or failing to complete assignments or write examinations. The benefit is stopped or ceased at the end of the month when the student last meets the full-time requirements. Full-Time Attendance Examples

Some school boards offer selected students the opportunity to complete high school via the Internet. The students are closely monitored to ensure that they are fulfilling the course requirements within the specified timeframes. Students participating in courses taught via the Internet must usually meet the same deadlines and write the same tests or exams as students taking the same courses in a classroom setting. In these situations, CPP usually considers the full-time course load requirements to be the same for both students.
When you determine full-time attendance, you must judge evening courses by the same criteria as daytime courses.

In cases of home schooling, the parents act as the their children`s primary educational facilitators. The school provides the curriculum and expects the student to write the same examinations as the students following the in-school program. The school or school board must approve the student's home schooling program, and the program must satisfy CPP's full-time attendance requirements.
Students who attend more than one institution or who take a combination of daytime and evening courses can be considered to be in full-time attendance if they are taking 60% of a full course load.

With new technologies (e.g. live television, pre-recorded video, computers), it is now possible to be considered a full-time student without being physically present at the institution. CPP considers the student to be in full-time attendance when the school confirms that the student is taking courses that make up 60% of a full course load through the use of technology. Full-Time Attendance Examples

If a student attends school or university full-time for 8 consecutive months of a calendar year and their vacation period does not fall within April to September, they may be considered to be in full-time attendance during their chosen vacation period. Full-Time Attendance Examples

Students are entitled to payment for the entire vacation period if they have been in full-time attendance at school or university immediately before a vacation period within April 1 and September 30. Full-Time Attendance Examples

text: If the client's affairs are being administered by a public trustee, the public trustee must provide documentary evidence of legal status or initiate a search of immigration records for applicants that were not born in Canada. If the trustee's search is unsuccessful, they can: complete the Consent to Exchange Information with Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (ISP-3210) form to be sent to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC). Refer to Validate and Submit a Consent to Exchange Information with Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (ISP-3210) Form (Action) ; or Validate and Submit a Consent to Exchange Information with Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (ISP-3210) Form (Action) contact IRCC directly on the client's behalf. However, they cannot request documentation related to the client's sponsorship status. If information cannot be obtained from IRCC, the public trustee can complete the Statutory Declaration - Confirmation of Canadian Citizenship (ISP-1899) form on the client's behalf.

The requirement for documentation to support legal status will be waived when processing all initial OAS pension, ALW or ALWS benefit applications, if the applicant meets one of the following criteria: The applicant is selected for automatic enrolment of the OAS pension; The applicant is not selected for automatic enrolment but submits a paper application and has their eligibility for an OAS pension determined by a combination of automatic enrolment data elements. Refer to Eligibility Requirements—Automatic Enrolment (Policy) ; or Eligibility Requirements—Automatic Enrolment (Policy) The applicant meets certain criteria to have this requirement waived. Refer to Documentary Evidence—Legal Status (Policy) . Documentary Evidence—Legal Status (Policy) Once the client's legal status has been confirmed for the ALW or ALWS benefit, it does not need to be confirmed again when converting the benefit to the OAS pension, unless there is an indication that the legal status has changed. Although documentation to support legal status may not be required, documentary evidence can be requested at any time before or after approval of the OAS pension and ALW or ALWS benefits. When validating the declared legal status, examine the documents you receive from the applicant to ensure they are valid (e.g. the document is acceptable, the document is not expired on the day legal status is required). If there are discrepancies between the provided documents and the information on the application or in the file, you must request clarification from the applicant before making a decision. For more information, Documentary Evidence—Legal Status (Policy) Acceptable documentation There are multiple legal status categories and a vast number of documents exist to support proof of legal status. For more information on the various types of acceptable documents to support legal status, Documentary Evidence—Legal Status (Policy) Foreign-born applicants The Landed Immigrant document or the Permanent Resident card can be used to confirm legal status in Canada, even if the individual has subsequently obtained their Canadian citizenship. If the applicant indicated on their application that they are a Canadian citizen, but only provided their Landed Immigrant document (e.g. IMM 1000) or Permanent Resident card, they do not need to provide proof of Canadian Citizenship if they: originally entered Canada as a permanent resident or landed immigrant and have provided acceptable proof of this status; have no absences from Canada where legal status may have been lost; are currently residing in Canada; and have no discrepancies or conflicting information on their account.

For applicants with multiple periods of residence in Canada, you do not need to confirm their legal status for each period of residence in Canada. An applicant who applies when residing in Canada must have a valid legal status in Canada on the day before an OAS pension or an ALW or ALWS benefit application is approved. The date of approval is the day the applicant meets all of the eligibility requirements for the pension or benefit. Approval Date—OAS Pension and Benefits (Policy) An applicant who applies from outside Canada must have had a valid legal status on the day before the day they ceased to reside in Canada for the last time. If the applicant does not meet the legal status requirements, the application is denied. Deportation If the applicant ceased to reside in Canada because they were deported for being in Canada illegally (i.e. entered illegally or let their permit expire), they did not have legal status on the day before the day they left Canada and cannot be approved for an OAS pension or an ALW or ALWS benefit. If the applicant had legal status in Canada before being deported for a different reason, you must confirm if they left Canada by the date of the removal order: If the applicant left Canada before or on the removal date, they had legal status on the day before the day they left Canada. If the applicant left Canada after the removal date, they did not have legal status on the day before the day they left Canada. You must review the file to determine if there is any evidence that the applicant lost their legal status (e.g. long absences reported in the residence statement, stamps in passport). An applicant who has lost their legal status must prove that it has been reinstated before the application's approval. Before February 15, 1977, Canadian citizens could not have a dual citizenship. If a Canadian citizen was absent for a period greater than 5 years or became a citizen of another country before or by this date, they may have lost their Canadian citizenship. If there is any indication on the file that the applicant may have lost their legal status during an absence before February 15, 1977, they must either: complete a statutory declaration confirming that they were not granted citizenship in another country during their absence over 5 years; or provide a Canadian citizenship certificate as proof that their Canadian citizenship has been restored. Applicants who are Canadian citizens and became citizens of another country on or after February 15, 1977, do not lose their Canadian citizenship. They hold dual citizenship. For more information, refer to Legal Status—Examples and Legal Status—Examples Defining Legal Status (Policy) Applicants resuming residence in Canada Applicants who resume residence in Canada and apply for an OAS pension, ALW benefit or ALWS benefit must meet the legal status requirement on the day before the application is approved. An applicant who lost their citizenship due to departing Canada and becoming a citizen of a foreign country before February 15, 1977, may have had their Canadian citizenship automatically reinstated under the amendments to the Citizenship Act that came into force on April 17, 2009. In this case, citizenship is reinstated back to the day the applicant was born or the day they lost their citizenship, depending on the situation. These applicants do not have to apply for citizenship but may need to request a Canadian Citizenship certificate. For more information, Defining Legal Status (Policy)

text: Referring applicants to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada Under no circumstances can the Department provide applicants with interpretations of immigration legislation. If an applicant questions their citizenship or wants a duplicate immigration document, advise them to: use the self-serve options on the IRCC website; contact an IRCC Call Centre, if they are in Canada, at 1 (888) 242-2100; visit an IRCC office in Canada; or visit a Canadian Visa office, if outside of Canada. Requesting a Verification of Status from IRCC If you determine that proof of Canadian legal status or sponsorship is required, you can request it directly from IRCC if the applicant: cannot provide documentary evidence of their legal status or sponsorship; or is present in Canada with an undetermined legal status. Before sending the request to IRCC, ask the applicant to complete the Consent to Exchange Information with Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (ISP-3210) form. text: A CPP SVR pension or Surviving Child's benefit is separate from the deceased contributor's account. You cannot request to recover a deceased contributor's overpayment from either payment. You can only recover the overpayment if the survivor or child voluntarily offers to repay it.

You can apply a Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit or Surviving Child's benefit underpayment to an existing overpayment on the child's account only if the underpayment amount is being paid: to or on behalf of that same child; and to the same payee who has the overpayment.

As a result, you cannot apply the DTH benefit against the deceased contributor's overpayment.

This procedure provides direction on identifying indicators of incapacity, the process for requesting a medical determination of incapacity and applying the new earlier deemed date to the application when incapacity can be applied.

Incapacity means that an individual is or was incapable of expressing an intention to make an application. The incapacity provision allows an application for benefits that was filed late, due to incapacity, to be deemed received at an earlier date. For clarity, "applicant" used in this article is defined as the individual or their legal representative whether the benefit is in pay, or the application for benefits is in process.

The incapacity provision can be reviewed at any stage of the application process—initial, reconsideration or appeals to the SST , but must be tied to an active application. When you receive a claim of incapacity without an application for benefits, you must contact the applicant or their legal representative and inform them that incapacity can only be reviewed with an active application. For more information, refer to Determine if an Application is Valid (Scenario) and to Determine if an Application is Valid (Scenario) Valid Applications (Policy) When you receive a claim of incapacity with an application for benefits or after a decision has already been made on an application, proceed as follows: Table 1. Criteria to perform a review of incapacity when a claim (this includes an indicator of incapacity) is noted Situation Decision A claim of incapacity is received with an application for benefits or while processing an application. The eligibility and the claim of incapacity are reviewed at the same time. The applicant must be given a decision on their benefit application with their right to reconsideration or appeal. The decision on incapacity itself does not have reconsideration or appeal rights. A decision was made at initial application and the applicant is within the 90-day period for requesting a reconsideration. The claim of incapacity can be reviewed if a reconsideration request is submitted within 90 calendar days of the initial decision letter and it is accepted. Refer to Reconsideration (Scenario) . Reconsideration (Scenario) A decision was made at initial application and the applicant is outside the 90-day period for requesting reconsideration. The claim of incapacity can be reviewed if a late request for reconsideration is received and an extension to the 90-day time limit is granted. Refer to Extension of the 90-day Time Limit to Request a Reconsideration (Scenario) . Extension of the 90-day Time Limit to Request a Reconsideration (Scenario) A decision was made at reconsideration and the applicant is within 90 days of receiving the decision letter. The claim of incapacity can be reviewed if an appeal is submitted to the SST within the 90-day deadline and they accept it. A decision was made at reconsideration and the applicant is outside of the 90 days after receiving the decision letter. The claim of incapacity can be reviewed if a late appeal is submitted to the SST , and they grant an "extension of time" and allow the appeal to go to the next step. For more information, refer to Examples—Incapacity Provision (Work Tool) and to Examples—Incapacity Provision (Work Tool) Incapacity (Policy)

topic_title: CPP disability benefit reassessment—Use of Facebook
text: Situation specifics Description Scenario The Medical Adjudicator (MA) responsible for reassessing a person’s DSB benefit recalls seeing an advertisement for the person’s family business on Facebook and decides to “friend” the person to get a sense of how involved they are in the day-to-day running of the business. The MA notices many business-related pictures of the person and determines that these images are evidence that the person is capable of regularly pursuing substantially gainful occupation. Issue The MA is unauthorized to seek out or collect personal information about the person’s business activities from social media sites (e.g. Facebook). The MA is unauthorized to discuss extraneous information with the person or to use that personal information to determine the person’s ongoing eligibility for a DSB benefit. Authorized approach The person did not provide sufficient evidence to support their ongoing eligibility for a DSB benefit. The MA must follow up with the person to request more information. Referral to Integrity Services Branch (ISB) The MA confirms the person has provided conflicting information. The MA refers the file to Integrity Services Branch (ISB) for investigation.

topic_title: CPP survivor’s pension application—Use of obituaries
text: Situation specifics Description Scenario John Smith is a Service Canada Benefits Officer (SCBO) processing an application for a CPP survivor’s pension from a person claiming to be the common-law partner of the deceased contributor. John notices that the person has submitted insufficient evidence confirming their common-law relationship at the time of death. A search on the Internet for an obituary that named the common-law partner would likely render determinative evidence to support the processing of a survivor’s pension. Issue John is not authorized to seek out or collect personal information (e.g. an obituary) about the person’s marital status from search engines or Web sites. John is not authorized to use that personal information to make a determination about the person’s eligibility for a CPP survivor’s pension. Authorized approach The person did not provide sufficient evidence to support the status of the common-law partner. John must obtain additional information from the person. With this new information, John determines the person’s eligibility for the survivor’s pension.

Situation specifics Description Scenario John Doe is an SCBO processing an application for an OAS pension and the GIS. The person has indicated in their application that they have been a resident of Canada for 25 years. The person provided insufficient information to support 25 years of residence. The person has also indicated that he owned his house and ran a business for the period in question. John accesses the municipal property assessments to confirm that the person did own his house for 20 of the 25 years. John also accesses the provincial enterprise register to confirm that the person ran his business for 19 of the 25 years, as they indicated. John processes the OAS and GIS benefits application and grants the benefits based on 20 years of residency. Issue John is unauthorized to collect personal information about the person’s residence from public sources, including property assessments and enterprise registries to determine eligibility. Neither is John authorized to use that information to determine the person’s eligibility for OAS benefits. Authorized approach The person did not provide sufficient evidence to support their application. John must contact the person to request clarification and additional documentation that can substantiate their residence in Canada. John can share the contact information from the public sources, including the property assessments and enterprise registries.

Situation specifics Description Scenario Jane Doe is an SCBO processing an application for an OAS pension and the GIS. The person has less than 20 years of residence in Canada and a history of multiple travels to their home country. Jane, having noticed that the person is not residing in Canada, accesses the person’s Facebook profile. There are many pictures and posts documenting the person's current stay in their home country—pictures with family over the Christmas holidays, buying furniture for their house, comments from their friends in Canada saying they miss them. Jane establishes that the person does not ordinarily reside in Canada and is thus ineligible for OAS benefits. Issue Jane is unauthorized to seek out or collect personal information about a person’s residence from social media platforms. Jane is unauthorized to use that information to determine the person’s eligibility for OAS benefits. Authorized approach There are inconsistencies in the person’s residence history. Jane must contact the person to request clarification and further documentation to substantiate their residence in Canada. Jane cannot access publicly available information, such as Facebook pages, to collect and use information for the administration of the OAS program. Referral to ISB The person provided conflicting information. Jane must refer the file to ISB for investigation.

Situation specifics Description Scenario A person’s notice of entitlement for a retirement pension is returned to the Department by Canada Post by reason of “moved, no forwarding address”. No further updates are available from other sources available to the Department (e.g. hard file, ITRDS Notes). Issue The SCBO is allowed to seek out or collect the person’s address from Canada411 to contact them. This approach is consistent with the initial collection and posting of information by Canada411. However, the information is unreliable because the person bearing the name might not be the one the SCBO is trying to reach. Authorized approach An SCBO obtains a person's address via Canada411.ca. The SCBO must: confirm the address before mailing information to the person; confirm verbally that the person is the person whom the Department is trying to reach. Obtaining information for this purpose is consistent with legislation. The information serves only to contact a person and not to make an administrative decision regarding eligibility.

topic_title: Social Security Tribunal submission—Information obtained via Internet put on file
text: Situation specifics Description Scenario The MA provides the Minister’s submission to the Social Security Tribunal - General Division (SST-GD) regarding a person whose DSB benefit ceased. The MA finds information on the Internet confirming that the appellant is working as a self-employed owner of a bed and breakfast (B&B). This information was used in the reassessment decision. The information on file from the Internet shows that the CPPD appellant is the owner—with the same address and phone number—and that booking a room is possible on the Internet. In looking at available reservation bookings printed from the Internet that were used in the initial decision, the MA sees that the B&B had very few openings available in the upcoming months. However, in documentation received from the appellant, it is stated that they only had a few people use their B&B and that they were mainly family and friends. In completing the submission to the SST, the MA argued that the appellant was working, based on the information on file that was used in the reassessment decision. The MA then used this information in the submission to the SST-GD in support of the Minister’s decision to cease the benefits based on the work-related information posted on the Internet. Issue Improperly collected unauthorized information cannot be used to determine eligibility for benefits (e.g. information about the B&B obtained from search engines or web sites, used to determine the person’s ongoing eligibility for a DSB benefit). The MA cannot complete the submission by referring to documentation taken from the Internet showing on file. The Minister’s submissions must be based on facts obtained from the appellant, their physicians or other approved sources (with valid consent). Authorized approach The person did not provide sufficient evidence to support their argument that the appellant ceased to be disabled. The MA must obtain additional information from the person by: requesting income tax returns from the appellant; obtaining detailed earnings information from CRA under the terms and conditions of the Information Sharing Agreement. With the additional information from CRA, the MA determines if the case can proceed to a hearing or a settlement offer. The MA cannot use public personal information to make a new determination on the appellant’s eligibility. Such documentation and information must be retained on file and clearly labelled as having been obtained through unauthorized methods.

The CPP legislation requires the Minister to notify applicants of a decision in writing. The Minister must also advise them of their right to request a reconsideration or to appeal this decision within 90 days of the notification date. For more information, Notice of Decision on Applications (Policy) Applicants may request a decision letter in writing, by phone or in-person. If the request is made by phone or in-person, the applicant's identity must be authenticated. Authenticate a Client or an Authorized Representative During a Phone Call (Action) When an applicant requests a decision letter, you must determine whether the applicant received the original decision letter or not. When they did not receive the original decision letter: the applicant is not aware of the decision made in their case, their right to request a reconsideration or appeal, and the time frame for that request; and you must issue the appropriate cover letter that carries the current date, along with a copy of the original decision letter that provides the applicant with information on how to request a reconsideration or to appeal the decision. When they received the original decision letter: the applicant is aware of the decision in their case, their reconsideration or appeal rights and the time frame to make that request; and you do not provide the applicant with a new 90-day reconsideration or appeal period. When the request is for an alternate format Applicants may request an alternate format of the decision letter. Requesting or Receiving Forms, Publications or Letters in Alternate Formats (Action) When the location of the letter is unknown On rare occasions, you may not be able to determine the location of the decision letter or the letter may be inaccessible. text: You must follow regular adjudication procedures, in addition to the procedures below, when determining if the applicant meets the severe and prolonged criteria for PRDB and DSB , if applicable. When adjudicating PRDB independent of DSB , follow the regular adjudication process. Use the information that was received with the Application for a Canada Pension Plan Post-Retirement Disability Benefit (ISP-1170) form, along with the information that was received with the CPPD benefits application. For more information, Medical Adjudication (Scenario) When verifying the Earnings and Contributions (E & C) information, if the applicant is in receipt of an early RTR pension and there is no E & C Worksheets for PRDB , return the file to the SCBO for review before proceeding with an adjudication. If the applicant meets the severe and prolonged criteria for the PRDB , the Date of Onset (DOO), or established DOO for late applicants, will determine which legislation applies. For more information, refer to Medical Adjudication for PRDB (Policy) and the Date of Onset section below. Medical Adjudication for PRDB (Policy) If the applicant does not meet the severe and prolonged criteria for PRDB and has a Latest Possible Date of Onset (LPDOO) listed for both legislative rules, the decision letter will only mention the most recent LPDOO. Requests for reconsideration To process a request for reconsideration, it must be clear which benefit the request is intended. When it is not clear which benefit the reconsideration is for, refer to the PRDB and Reconsideration SharePoint link Work Tool. PRDB and Reconsideration If the applicant is in pay for their early RTR pension when the request for reconsideration of their DSB decision is received, you must send an Application for a Canada Pension Plan Post-Retirement Disability Benefit (ISP-1170) form. No Bring Forward timeframe is required. You must complete the following fields before saving the ISP-1170 form to your regional printing folder: Region SIN Date Applicant Name Early RTR pension effective date (use the first day of the effective month and year). For more information, refer to Medical Adjudication for PRDB (Policy) and to Post-Retirement Disability Benefit Workflow when DSB is at Reconsideration, located on the KMT EReference Library page, under Work Tools, CPPD, PRDB , Flow Maps. Medical Adjudication for PRDB (Policy) EReference Library Adjudication documentation at initial and reconsideration At the initial and reconsideration levels, complete the appropriate decision summary form. If adjudicating a PRDB and DSB simultaneously, you must clearly demonstrate that each benefit was considered separately. If the PRDB and DSB are at different levels of adjudication (e.g. when an early RTR pension begins after the DSB decision and there is an active appeal regarding this decision), PRDB must be adjudicated separately on a new decision summary form, depending on the level of adjudication. For information on saving the decision summary form, Naming and Saving Files to the National Common Drive Rationale If adjudicating a PRDB and DSB simultaneously, follow the regular requirements to complete your rationale. You must clearly indicate the decisions for each benefit. For more information, Document Rationale (Knowledge) Date of Onset If you determine the applicant meets both severe and prolonged for the PRDB , you must set the DOO. If the applicant has sufficient E & C under both legislative rules, the DOO will determine which rules apply. For more information on how to determine the DOO, Medical Adjudication for PRDB (Policy)

If an applicant is receiving an early RTR pension, the SCBO will determine the Latest Possible Date of Onset (LPDOO) for the PRDB under both the previous and current legislation. If the severe and prolonged criteria are met for the PRDB , the DOO or the established DOO in the case of a late applicant will determine if the 2019 or 2023 legislation is used. The SCBO will also calculate and provide the LPDOO for DSB , if applicable. When adjudicating the PRDB and the DSB simultaneously, a separate decision must be made for each benefit following the regular adjudication process. The decision letter must communicate both decisions to the applicant and include the appropriate appeal rights. For more information, Medical Adjudication for PRDB (Policy)

IO also processes the payments when the PRDB must be combined with an existing RTR pension or combined RTR pension and SVR pension paid with an ISSA. For PRDB and DCCPR benefits that do not require an ISSA, the account is referred to the responsible specialized processing centre for all other CPP and dual contributors. The responsible IO processing centre or specialized processing centre issues the monthly PRDB and DCCPR benefit payments by manual priority payment. topic_title: PRDB monthly amount and combined benefits
text: The monthly amount for a PRDB is a flat rate which is equal to the DSB monthly flat-rate amount. When an applicant becomes entitled to a PRDB while in receipt of an early RTR pension and an SVR pension, the greater of the DSB or SVR pension flat rate is paid to the applicant. At this time, the DSB flat-rate amount is greater. The combined RTR pension and SVR pension payments continue to be sent by CPMS to the Standard Payment System. The specialized processing centre reduces the PRDB amount (i.e. the DSB flat-rate amount) by the SVR pension flat-rate amount when preparing the manual priority payment and issues the difference. International Operations (IO) processes payments for applicants who qualify for PRDB with an International Social Security Agreement (ISSA). When an ISSA is used to determine eligibility, the flat-rate amount may be lower based on the applicant's actual number of years contributed to CPP and/or the number of foreign years used to meet the Minimum Qualifying Period. For more information, Calculation of CPP Benefits (Knowledge)

topic_title: Previously in pay for DSB within 5 years, currently in pay for an early RTR pension and not eligible for Fast-Track reapplication for DSB
text: When an applicant applies under a fast-track reapplication within 5 years of their DSB being ceased, has since gone into pay for an early RTR pension and is not eligible under the DSB fast track criteria, initial processing staff will make a determination on eligibility for both DSB and PRDB . If the applicant is granted a PRDB , the 4-month waiting period is waived. The benefit effective date is then determined to be the month following the DOO. For more information, Effective Date—CPP DSB and PRDB (Policy)

Initiate a PRDB Return to Work in the Rules Based Reassessment System If this is the first time a beneficiary has self-reported a Return to Work (RTW) while in receipt of a PRDB , a request must be made to load the assessment into the Rules Based Reassessment System ( RBRS ). Any subsequent self-reported RTW while in receipt of a PRDB is an available choice within RBRS . For more information, Opening a PRDB Return to Work Assessment in Rules Based Reassessment System To complete a PRDB RTW in RBRS following regular procedures, you must: Complete the steps to have an RTW- PRDB assessment loaded into RBRS , if required. Ensure the RTW- PRDB is selected as the assessment type. Complete the assessment. Suspend the PRDB Following regular procedures, you must: Complete the interim suspend decision in RBRS . Email the appropriate specialized processing centre General Delivery box, if applicable. In the subject line write “Suspend PRDB ”. In the body of the email include “Request to suspend PRDB ” and the “Effective date”. Attach the appropriate benefit instruction sheet. Send the suspension letter to the beneficiary. The SCBO must action the cease following regular procedures and send the cease letter to the beneficiary. The specialized processing centre or the responsible International Operations processing unit will calculate the PRDB overpayment and related Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit, if applicable, and manually create the debts in CPMS following their procedures.. (KA-01651 Snippet 4.0 content. Do not modify or delete.) Automatic reinstatement A beneficiary can only be reinstated for the same benefit for which they were previously in pay. For example, a PRDB cannot be reinstated if the DSB was previously in pay. A request for Automatic Reinstatement (AR) will be completed following regular procedures. For additional information refer to Automatic Reinstatement—CPPD Benefits (Policy) and to Automatic Reinstatement (Scenario) (article not available). Automatic Reinstatement—CPPD Benefits (Policy) If a beneficiary is denied AR for DSB because the Date of Onset (DOO) cannot be established before the initiation of an early RTR pension, the Medical Adjudicator (MA) sends an Application kit for Canada Pension Plan Disability Benefit (ISP-1151) form or Terminal Illness Application Kit for Disability Benefits under the Canada Pension Plan (ISP-2530A) form with the appropriate decision letter. The signed AR form protects the date of the subsequent application for an Initial determination. Once the ISP-1151 form or ISP-2530A form is received, the application will be held in abeyance until the appeal period for AR expires, following regular procedures. Once the appeal period for AR is complete, the ISP-1151 form or ISP-2530A form is considered an application for both DSB and PRDB . The Medical Adjudicator will adjudicate following regular procedures, in addition to procedures specific to PRDB adjudication as outlined within this guidance. For more information, refer to Automatic Reinstatement (AR) and PRDB Workflow, located on the KMT EReference Library page, under Work Tools, CPPD, PRDB , Flow Maps. EReference Library Fast Track Reapplication An applicant previously in receipt of DSB and now in receipt of an RTR pension cannot be granted as a fast-track if the DOO cannot be established to be before the effective date of the RTR pension. Within reassessment, consider an early RTR pensioner for fast-track if they were previously in receipt of a PRDB and meet all the other criteria. For more information, refer to Fast Track Reapplication (Policy) and Process a Fast Track Reapplication (Scenario) (article not available). Fast Track Reapplication (Policy) Applicants who are ineligible for DSB fast-track are forwarded for initial determination following regular procedures. Initial processing staff will consider the Fast Track Reapplication, as an application for both DSB and PRDB and follow regular adjudication procedures, in addition to procedures specific to PRDB adjudication, as outlined within this guidance. For more information, refer to Fast Track and PRDB Workflow, located on the KMT EReference Library page, under Work Tools, CPPD, PRDB , Flow Maps. EReference Library

Reassessment and vocational rehabilitation for a beneficiary in pay for a PRDB are handled in the same manner as those in pay for a DSB . A request for automatic reinstatement is not an official application as it can only be used for the purpose of reinstating a benefit. A new application is therefore required for a PRDB , specifically the Application kit for Canada Pension Plan Disability benefits (ISP-1151) form, Terminal Illness Application Kit for Disability Benefits under the Canada Pension Plan (ISP-2530A) form or an international agreement-specific application XXX/Canada Agreement - Application for CPP Disability Benefits (ISP-5053-XXX) form.
This procedure provides the steps to follow when processing a PRDB independently or simultaneously with a DSB .

topic_title: Was a CPP RTR pension application received within 90 days of the DSB denial letter date?
text: A CPP RTR pension application received within 90 days of the DSB denial letter date is not considered a simultaneous application for PRDB . An Application for a Canada Pension Plan Post-Retirement Disability Benefit (ISP-1170) form is required.

The PRDB and DSB are 2 distinct benefits. The PRDB came into effect January 1, 2019. It provides disability coverage for CPP Early Retirement pensioners who meet the legislative criteria of severe and prolonged and have not reached age 65. A legislative change to the PRDB came into effect in May 2023. The Date of Onset (DOO) or established DOO will determine which legislation applies.

topic_title: How to use NATS letters temporarily stored on the KMT and E-Reference Library
text: How to use NATS letters temporarily stored on the KMT and E-Reference Library In the NATS Catalogue, access the applicable blank template: ISS 880 (no cover page) or ISS 881 (with cover page). Access the letter temporarily stored on the KMT. Select and copy (Ctrl + C) the body of the letter. Do not select the salutation or the signature block . If you include them, the add-ins may not work. Paste (Ctrl + V) the content you have copied into the body of the blank template (ISS 880 or 881). If you wish to reduce the amount of manual selections, you can remove any (v) variable paragraphs before selecting the add-ins (e.g. the overpayment variable paragraphs). Complete one of the following actions: From the Add-ins menu (at the top), click Paragraph , then click Return to letter . This will automate the variable paragraph and choices of text. If the Add-ins menu does not work, manually select the variables by completing the following: Choose the applicable words found between brackets { } and [ ]. Remove the { } and [ ] brackets. Fill in the date, year, period of time or amount (as indicated in the template) between the symbols < >. Remove the < > symbols. Replace "&PRGRM_BNFT_NME&" with the applicable benefit name. Replace "&CLNT_NME&" with the applicable client, contributor or beneficiary name. Choose the applicable (V) variable paragraphs and text as required and delete those that are not. Remove the (V) paragraph numbers and headings. Remove the (P) paragraph numbers. Remove any highlighting. If your letter has the "If you have any questions" or the "If you disagree with our decision" paragraph, use the newest version. These versions can be found in the denial letters. These paragraphs will also be available on the Forms and Letters page shortly. If you are writing to a third party, remove the first bullet from the reconsideration paragraph ("If you disagree with our decision") which reads: "log into your My Service Canada Account (MSCA) at canada.ca/msca, and choose Canada Pension Plan/Old Age Security and Request for reconsideration; or ". Third parties are not eligible to use My Service Canada Account for their clients. Remove the telephone number block at the end of the letter if it also appears in the body of the "If you have any questions" paragraph. To remove the telephone number block: Click File from the MS Word menu. Click Protect Document , then select Restrict Editing from the drop down list. In the Restrict Editing Pane on the right side of your screen, click Stop Protection at the bottom. Click into the telephone number block to highlight and delete the information. Read the letter to ensure it flows logically and that there is no extraneous text remaining. To see the final letter format: Click Print from the NATS Add-ins menu. When the Print Options box opens, select View Final Letter Format . Ensure the font is Times New Roman (12 point font for the text and 14 point for headers). Ensure the paragraphs are aligned. Print the letter.

Adjudicate a CPPD benefit application with a possible prorate date.

You will adjudicate the file following normal processes. For more information, Medical Adjudication (Scenario) Earnings and contributions The SCBO will provide the Earnings Investigation Worksheet for DSB and PRDB , if applicable. This worksheet must include: the Latest Possible Date of Onset (LPDOO) using years of valid contributions (if they have sufficient Earnings and Contributions (E & C)) without proration; and the possible prorate date. There will be instances in which an applicant does not have sufficient E & C to establish an LPDOO and only the possible prorate date will be provided. For more information, CPPD Earnings and Contributions Criteria (Scenario) Medical adjudication The medical adjudicator will incorporate the following guidance into the 5-step adjudication process to determine if the applicant was disabled according to the Canada Pension Plan legislation. For more information, Medical Adjudication (Scenario) If the applicant has a LPDOO, using years of valid earnings, you must first determine if the severe and prolonged criteria were met at the LPDOO. If the applicant is not found to be disabled at the LPDOO, you must then determine if the applicant was disabled on or before the end of the possible prorate period and continuously thereafter.

The proration of Unadjusted Pensionable Earnings (UPE) may be used to assist an applicant in conditionally meeting the Earnings and Contributions (E & C) requirements for CPPD benefits. For more information, Proration of Unadjusted Pensionable Earnings (Policy) Applicants considered for the proration of UPE for CPPD purposes may qualify for a year in which: the Date of Onset (DOO) occurred in a month other than December and before 1998, where the earnings are equal to or below the year's basic exemption; or in January 1998 and later, where the earnings are below the Disability Basic Exemption (DBE). The applicant will qualify for DSB if they became disabled on or before the end of the possible prorate period and continuously thereafter. There are considerations when determining if it is appropriate to prorate a contributor's earnings for the purpose of DSB . For more information, refer to Proration of Unadjusted Pensionable Earnings (Policy) . A review of the E & C on disability files where there is a possibility of proration must include, but is not limited to, the following: Proration of Unadjusted Pensionable Earnings (Policy) objective medical evidence that indicates that the applicant meets the CPP criteria for disability by the end of the possible prorate period; and evidence from the employer, the Employment Insurance record of employment or the CRA regarding the monthly earnings in that year. You need to consider: the date the applicant states they stopped work due to the disability; the date the applicant indicates they are disabled; the months during which employment earnings were earned; and any employment earnings earned after that date. Without evidence to support that the applicant was disabled by the period extended by the UPE below the DBE, the applicant will not qualify. If the applicant is found disabled on or before the end of the prorate period and continuously thereafter, the DOO will end the contributory period. This will allow the Department to use prorated earnings to extend the Latest Possible Date of Onset (LPDOO). The Department can only extend the LPDOO if the DOO is set during this time. For more information, refer to Determine and Record the Date of Onset (Action) or Determine and Record the Date of Onset (Action) Determine and Record the Established Date of Onset (Action)

topic_title: Cessation and cancellation of income-tested benefits
text: When a client requests to cease the payment of the GIS or the ALW or ALWS benefit, the lifetime renewal designation ends. They are no longer eligible for income-tested benefits; if they want to receive them in the future, they must submit a new application. When the GIS is cancelled, the GIS application is considered to have never been made and the client no longer has a lifetime renewal designation, an d they are considered to have never been eligible. If they want to receive the GIS in the future, they must submit a new application. For more information, refer to: Cessation—OAS Pension and Benefits (Policy) ; and Cessation—OAS Pension and Benefits (Policy) Cancellation (Policy) . Cancellation (Policy)

topic_title: Client departs from and returns to Canada
text: Income-tested benefits are no longer payable when a client has been absent from Canada for a period longer than 6 months after the month of their departure from Canada. When a client has been temporarily absent from Canada, their income-tested benefit payments can be reinstated the month they return to Canada. If the absence was not temporary, the client will not be eligible for renewal of the income-tested benefit; they must reapply for the benefit if t hey want to receive it when they return. For more information, refer to: Client Departs from or Returns to Canada (Scenario) ; or Client Departs from or Returns to Canada (Scenario) Entitlement—Portability of OAS Pension and Benefits (Policy) . Income-tested benefits are renewed in July each year based on: the income received for the previous calendar year (i.e. base calendar year income); and marital status. After eligibility is established based on an initial application for income-tested benefits, entitlement to benefits can be renewed every year without the client having to reapply, if they provide the required income information. The renewal of the client's entitlement to benefits can be automatic if their income information is received directly from the CRA .

topic_title: Accepting income information by phone for the renewal of income-tested benefits
text: The Call Centre will renew income-tested benefits using income received by phone if the following conditions are met: There are no notes in ITRDS indicating that the processing centre is already working on the renewal of the client's income-tested benefits. A Statement of Income for the Guaranteed Income Supplement, the Allowance the Allowance for the Survivor for payment period of July (20XX) to June (20XX) (ISP-3026) form has not been received. The client's ITB for Life status is set to Yes in Cúram and they received income-tested benefits for the month of June. The client or their spouse or common-law partner, if applicable, does not indicate that they are entitled to a partial or complete tax exemption. The Call Centre employee has the correct financial authority. If the above conditions are met, the Call Centre employee will: add and apply the income information received by phone in Cúram as Manually Entered Income evidence; advise the client that they must file their income tax or submit a statement of income within 30 days for the benefits to continue; forward a follow-up template to National Headquarters; create an Income - GIS Renewal Telecentre Contact Report (3088) enquiry task in Cúram indicating that income information was accepted over the phone and has been applied to the client's account; send a Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form, if applicable; update ITRDS notes indicating the actions taken on the account; and send the applicable letter to the client: Table 1. Letter title and description Letter Description GIS/ ALW / ALWS Entitlement Letter (ISP-3057) This letter is sent by the system when the benefit is automatically renewed by Cúram for the July accounting month. It informs the client of: their new entitlement amount; the total income used to calculate the entitlement; and the marital status used to calculate the entitlement. GIS Renewal Entitlement Letter (ISP-3819) This letter: is automatically sent by the system if the income source is CRA Income and there is an arrears payable; or must be sent manually when: the income source is Manually Entered Income ; and there is an arrears payable or an overpayment that is being recovered from the arrears. It informs the client of: the date of the benefit change; the new monthly entitlement amount; and the retroactive payment amount. GIS/ ALW / ALWS Non-Entitlement Letter (ISP-3056) This letter: is automatically sent by the system if the income source is CRA Income ; or must be sent manually when the income source is Manually Entered Income . It informs the client: that they are not entitled due to excess income; that they will be notified if they become entitled in the future; and of the marital status used to determine entitlement. When the Income - GIS Renewal Telecentre Contact Report (3088) task is assigned to a processing centre employee within 60 days, the employee will review the task and the account to determine if confirmation of the income information has been received. When a Call Centre employee is unable to renew the income-tested benefit due to not meeting one of the conditions above, income information can still be accepted over the phone but will not be recorded in Cúram. The Call Centre employee will record the client's income information received by phone using the GIS Renewal Telecentre Contact Report (ISP 3088) form and advise them to file their income tax or submit a statement of income within 30 days. The ISP-3088 form is added to Cúram as an attachment and an Income - GIS Renewal Telecentre Contact Report (3088) task is generated. To ensure the income information received over the phone is urgently reviewed by a processing centre employee, the Call Centre employee will mark the task as High priority. The request is expected to be processed in 5 business days (10 business days for International Operations). The Call Centre employee will advise the client of the timeframe. If the task is not processed within the expected timeframe, the Call Centre will follow up with the processing centre via an urgent enquiry. For more information regarding the information obtained and assessed by the Call Centre employee, as well as the required actions to be taken, refer to Accepting Income over the Phone for GIS Renewal Internal link on the Common Reference Tool. Accepting Income over the Phone for GIS Renewal

Clients' income-tested benefit can be automatically renewed if: their income is received through the CRA income feed; and they have a lifetime renewal designation. Clients may also renew their benefits by providing a statement of income (i.e. a Statement of Income for the Guaranteed Income Supplement, the Allowance the Allowance for the Survivor for payment period of July (20XX) to June (20XX) (ISP-3026) form or written statement of income). Renewal of income-tested benefits (Policy) If income information has not been received from the CRA income feed or from the client directly by the July accounting month, the client's entitlement to income-tested benefits will not be renewed in Cúram in time for the new payment period. Starting in the July accounting month, these clients may be able to provide their income information by phone. The renewal of benefits by phone is a temporary measure to help pensioners maintain entitlement to their income-tested benefits until the CRA income feed or a statement of income is received. If income information is accepted by phone, the client is advised that they must provide a statement of income or file their income tax return within 30 days. This requirement also applies where the income of a spouse or common-law partner is provided over the phone. Clients (or their spouse or common-law partner) who have reported their income by phone will continue to receive their income-tested benefits until the account is reviewed by the processing centre to confirm the income. If confirmation of the income information has not been received within 60 days (to allow for mailing time or CRA tax assessment beyond the 30 days), the income information received over the phone must be manually deleted from Cúram. Cúram will then recalculate the client's entitlement and create an overpayment for any payments received within the applicable payment period. The client must be notified in writing that their entitlement has stopped and of the overpayment details. The deleted income can be viewed in the manually entered income history on the Integrated Case.

The CPMS monetary and payment reports are all accessible in the Enterprise Reporting System , in the folder found via the following path: Enterprise Reporting System Team Content Canada Pension Plan CPP Operational Reports CPMS reports The Department of Justice and CPP currently share information for the purpose of Family Orders Enforcement (FOE) garnishment. The FOE information comes from an electronic exchange of files within the monthly and arrears (supplementary) payment processes. Confirmation of the actual amount of FOE withholds are only known once the payments are issued. The process is completely automated for CPP, OAS and International Operations. The CPMS process is as follows: On a daily basis, the Department of Justice sends a file identifying individuals with an FOE garnishment notice against them to: CPP; Employment Insurance; and Canada Revenue Agency. CPP matches the Department of Justice list by beneficiary social insurance number to those clients who are scheduled to receive a CPP payment. Refer to the Funds withholding and payment section below. The pre-determined CPP priority of withholds is applied to the forthcoming CPP payment. CPMS calculates the required garnishment amount by using the formula that the Department of Justice provides. If funds are available to divert, the FOE amount will be displayed on the CPMS Preview Payment screen. The FOE amount is displayed as follow s: DOJA —Department of Justice Arrears DOJF —Department of Justice Fees CPP then diverts the garnishment amount from the CPP client’s payment and sends the information electronically to the Department of Justice. When the payment is issued, the FOE amounts are displayed in CPMS on the Payment History and Year to Date screens.

Branch policy states that the withholding and payment of funds are processed in the following order: Program-specific overpayment recoveries; Non-resident tax (NRT) withholds; Cross-program recoveries (i.e. OAS from CPP, CPP from OAS); Contracts (i.e. Reimbursements to Province, Workers' Compensation Board, Insurers , Department of Veterans' Affairs); Monies owed to other federal departments (Set-off); Family Orders and Agreements Enforcement Assistance Act ; Voluntary Tax Withholds (VTW). Example The dollar amount that can be garnished is the current monthly entitlement amount of the CPP or OAS pension or benefit payment added to any retroactive entitlement minus any: Program-specific overpayment recoveries; NRT withholds; Cross-program recoveries; Contract recoveries; and/or Other Crown debt recoveries. CPMS has up-to-date information regarding FOE on the Preview Payment screen before the payment is issued. No information should be released to clients as CPP does not have the authority to do so. The amount of the FOE withhold on the Preview Payment screen can change daily. Confirmation of the actual amount of FOE withhold is final when the information appears on the Payment History Details screen.

The Family Orders and Agreements Enforcement Assistance Act allows for garnishment of federal monies. A spouse or common-law partner may petition a court for a judgment order. These petitioning documents are submitted to the Minister of Justice. The Department of Justice then requests the search of all eligible funds which can then be intercepted, including the following payments: OAS pension; Allowance benefit; Allowance for the Survivor benefit; Guaranteed Income Supplement benefit; and/or CPP pensions and benefits, excluding: benefits payable in respect to children; benefits payable on behalf of a beneficiary to a province, territory or municipality; and the Death benefit. The Department notifies the Department of Justice of the dollar amounts and dates of current and future applicable pensions and benefits. The Family Orders and Agreements Enforcement Assistance Unit The Family Orders and Agreements Enforcement Assistance Unit at the Department of Justice: evaluates the funds available against the financial terms of the garnishee summons; and instructs the source program (i.e. OAS, CPP or International Operations) to transfer all or some of the money to the Department of Justice . The transferred funds are deposited into a trust account and a cheque is issued to the court or enforcement service which issued the garnishee summons. The Department of Justice is responsible for transferring the funds to the creditor. Tracing requests are processed through an electronic exchange of data between the Department and the Department of Justice. The Department does not release information directly to a creditor. The creditor must contact the court or enforcement service that issued the garnishee summons for information. The Department also does not deal directly with clients regarding garnishments. The Department of Justice is responsible for notifying clients in writing with respect to garnishments. The client is not advised from which department the monies will be intercepted, and therefore, any client inquiries must be referred to the Department of Justice website where the client will find contact information relevant to their province or territory. An application for CPP Retirement Pension Sharing must be processed even if the garnishment action has started because the Department cannot terminate the processing of an application if there is entitlement. The amount that can be garnished may change as a result of the application for Pension Sharing. Department of Justice

The Family Orders and Agreements Enforcement Assistance Act provides for the garnishment of designated federal monies to satisfy support orders or provisions. Under this Act, the Department of Justice provides weekly information that allows the Department to withhold money from our payments. Throughout the Department's automated CPP monthly processes, the garnishment amounts are withheld based on a hierarchy of recovery. The Department commonly refers to this withholding process as Family Orders Enforcement (FOE).

The enforcement of family orders and agreements is a provincial and territorial responsibility. The Family Orders and Agreements Enforcement Assistance Act provides the following remedies for common enforcement problems: allowing the release of information from designated federal information banks to help trace missing persons; removing the legal barriers preventing the garnishment of federal monies to satisfy support orders or support divisions; assisting provincial and territorial enforcement services to: carry out support orders; and support divisions by denying certain licences to family orders debtors who are in persistent arrears. The Department of Justice has a Family Orders and Agreements Enforcement Assistance Unit which performs the following services: information tracing; and interception of the OAS or CPP payment . When the Department of Justice determines that an application for a trace is valid, they request to search the Department's computer files. They can search: CPP Record of Earnings ; CPP Retirement and Survivor's pensions and the Disability and Death benefits; and International Operations' domestic and foreign benefits. The following limited information can be released to the Department of Justice on individuals who have: breached a family order or family agreement; or been charged with parental abduction: the address of the individual; the name and address of that individual's recent employers; the address of every child named in an application; the name and address of the employer of every child named in an application.

Consider the factors above when analyzing the following examples: 1. Likely to be long continued and of indefinite duration Situation: A client diagnosed with a brain tumour is expected to undergo surgery in the next 2 to 3 months. Functional limitations of fatigue, weakness, shakiness and dizziness related to seizures and treatment have been identified. The outcome of surgery and the prognosis are uncertain. Assessment: Even though surgery is expected in the next few months, there is no reasonable end in sight due to the uncertain prognosis. The disability is likely to be long continued, and of indefinite duration, thus the prolonged criterion is met. 2. Not likely to be long continued and of indefinite duration Situation: A client with severe osteoarthritis of the right hip is expected to undergo a total hip replacement within the next 6 months followed by 6 to 8 weeks of recovery and rehabilitation. The surgeon notes the prognosis following this is favourable. Functional limitations include difficulty with prolonged walking, standing and sitting. Assessment: Although the disability is currently severe, it would not be prolonged because it is reasonable to anticipate improvement with surgery. The disability is not likely to be long continued and of indefinite duration or to result in death. 3. Likely to be long continued and of indefinite duration—favorable prognosis Situation: A 49-year-old client was diagnosed with breast cancer and underwent surgery and chemotherapy. Their prognosis for recovery is favourable, but they will require hormonal therapy with tamoxifen for 10 years. The client has a secondary diagnosis of moderate depression requiring treatment, with limited response thus far. As a result of the breast cancer treatment, they face limitations due to: peripheral neuropathy in their dominant hand; chemo fog, fatigue; side effects from Tamoxifen; and the oncologist reporting that it is unknown when the side effects may resolve. Assessment: Even though there is a favourable prognosis for the breast cancer, the client's ongoing depression and limitations resulting from the cancer treatment make it more likely than not that they are incapable of regularly pursuing any kind of work. The prolonged criterion is met because the disability is likely to be long continued and of indefinite duration.

Determine if the client meets the prolonged criterion, only after the severe criterion is met.

If the client meets the severe criterion, determine if their medical condition(s) also meets one of the prolonged components: Are the medical conditions likely to be long continued and of indefinite duration? If yes , the prolonged criterion is met. If no , the prolonged criterion is not met. Are the medical conditions likely to result in death? If yes , the prolonged criterion is met. If no , the prolonged criterion is not met.
