topic_title: Selection of individuals for proactive enrolment of an RTR pension at age 70 or older
text: There are 2 categories of proactive enrolment that allow the Minister to waive the requirement for a CPP RTR pension application. Individuals who meet the following criteria: Contributors aged 70 or older who are in receipt of at least one of an OAS benefit and/or a Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS) or a CPP Survivor’s pension; Contributors aged 70 or older who are not in receipt of an OAS benefit, a GIS or a CPP Survivor’s pension, but who have recently filed taxes with Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). On an ongoing basis, individuals will be enrolled using the following criteria: Contributors who turn age 70, who are in receipt of at least one of an OAS benefit and/or GIS or a CPP Survivor’s pension; Contributors who turn age 70, who are not in receipt of an OAS benefit, a GIS or a CPP Survivor’s pension, but who have recently filed taxes with CRA.

Previously, the processing network had to obtain lists of accounts from EDS or Cognos/IRIS that were identified in various operational reports and that required action. The SharePoint site has been designed to filter out any reports where action is not required.

You must no longer access the 6 CPP and 16 OAS operational reports from either the Electronic Document System (EDS) or Cognos/IRIS. Instead, NHQ will automatically upload any accounts that require action to PWS as work items. The regions will manage and assign the work items, and you are responsible for those that have been assigned to you. You can access a list that includes all reports in Wave 1, their current report name and number and the new PWS work items. Each PWS work type can have multiple associated barcodes to help identify the action required. list Once a PWS work item is assigned to you, look up the account in the SharePoint Digital Repository by entering the client’s social insurance number (SIN) or account number. The SharePoint Digital Repository has been designed to eventually capture all reports for that client. For now, the functionality includes a subset of accounts. For example, a client could appear on 4 CPP credit reports and 2 CPP debit reports. Likewise, a client could appear on the OAS Reject report and the Marital Status Incompatible report. This functionality will allow you to action all reports at the same time. The SharePoint Digital Repository also removes any duplication between a daily, weekly or monthly version of a particular report. Therefore, only one PWS work item will be created regardless if it previously appeared on both a weekly and monthly operational report. When one spouse or common-law partner receives or would receive an OAS pension and a Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS) benefit under Rate Table 3, and the other spouse or common-law partner’s OAS pension (and possibly a GIS benefit) is approved, the first spouse or common-law partner continues to be entitled to receive the GIS benefit amount as calculated under Rate Table 3 minus the second spouse or common-law partner’s OAS pension (and a GIS benefit, if applicable) amount as determined under Rate Table 2. Before considering or adjusting a payment based on Rate Table 1, the following situations must be determined: Any couple such as individuals living apart for reasons beyond their control; A separation; or The death of one spouse or common-law partner during the payment year. Once the most beneficial rate is determined, the resulting amount must be compared with the benefit on Rate Table 1. The most beneficial rate can then be determined by verifying if the rate on Rate Table 1 is greater than the rate calculated by determining the adjustment.

The pensioner who receives the adjustment is determined as follows: Circumstance Adjustment recipient Entitlement to the (Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS) exists for both pensioners. The pensioner with the greater number of 40ths of OAS pension entitlement receives the adjustment. Both pensioners have the same number of 40ths of OAS pension entitlements and neither has a "special qualifying factor". As defined under the OAS Act, the pensioner with the earliest effective date for the OAS pension receives the adjustment. No entitlement to the GIS exists for one pensioner, or one pensioner is only entitled to a pro-rated GIS. The other pensioner receives the adjustment. Unless otherwise requested, a discretionary decision can be made in cases where both the number of 40ths and effective dates of OAS pensions are the same for both spouses or common-law partners.

The couple must fall within a specific income range for the protection to benefit the couple. Rate Tables 2 and 3 are examined to determine at what level of income the combined OAS pension and Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS) benefit amount in Rate Table 3 first becomes greater than twice the combined OAS pension and GIS benefit amount in Rate Table 2. The high e nd of the income range is the largest combined income amount at which Rate Table 3 pays more than the total basic OAS pension received by the couple.

This policy ensures a married or common-law couple will at least maintain a total amount of benefits at a rate equivalent to what they would receive or were receiving as a spouse or common-law partner of a non-pensioner. When it is to their advantage, the spouses of a married or common-law couple who are both pensioners may be paid using separate rate tables. This can occur when the non-pensioner spouse or common-law partner becomes eligible for an OAS pension and a Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS) benefit. For example, one spouse or common-law partner receives an OAS pension and a GIS benefit at Rate Table 2, while the other spouse or common-law partner receives an OAS pension and a GIS benefit at Rate Table 3, less the OAS and GIS amounts received by the other spouse or common-law partner. The right for both pensioners to receive a pension is protected, and this protection ensures that each pensioner’s right to receive a pension is not detrimental to the other spouse or common-law partner’s current benefit. The total OAS pension and GIS entitlement paid to one pensioner at the rate of a married or common-law pensioner with a non-pensioner spouse is also protected.

This protection may also apply to some cases where one or both spouses, or the common-law partner is a "specially qualified individual" (i.e. someone who is not eligible for full Guaranteed Income Supplement entitlements because they are a sponsored immigrant or they do not have 10 years of residence in Canada after reaching age 18).

Deductions allowed by Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for income tax purposes are also allowed for the purposes of the OAS Act. In addition, deductions specific only to the OAS Act are allowed. Although deductions used for the purposes of the OAS Act should generally be the same as those declared under the Income Tax Act , there are exceptions. The Federal Court of Appeal ruled that if a deduction is allowed under the Income Tax Act but is not claimed, it may still be allowed as a deduction under the OAS Act. All documentation required to support the deduction claim must be provided. The allowable deductions are as follows: Deductions allowed to reduce employment and self-employment income Deductions allowed to reduce employment and self-employment income Deductions allowed to reduce rental income Deductions allowed to reduce rental income Deductions allowed to reduce other income Deductions allowed to reduce other income Deductions allowed to reduce Canadian dividends Deductions allowed to reduce Canadian dividends Deductions allowed to reduce employment and self-employment income EI premiums Contributions to the CPP or QPP The definition of Income in Section 2 of the OAS Act specifies that contributions to the CPP or QPP must be deducted from employment and self-employment earnings. Beginning July 2020, enhanced contributions made by a person to the CPP or QPP from employment or self-employment earnings are deducted from their respective earnings when determining entitlement to income-tested benefits. Pensioners 65 to 70 years of age can choose to cease contributing to the CPP. At age 70, they are no longer able to contribute. These enhanced contributions are reported to CRA separately from the base contributions for employment earnings. For self-employment, the enhancement and the base contributions are reported on the same line. Earnings Exemption Before July 1, 2020, the first $3,500.00 of employment earnings was exempted from inclusion in employment income for determining the amount of an OAS income-tested benefit. This earnings exemption did not apply to self-employment income. Beginning July 1, 2020, the earnings exemption is extended to include self-employment earnings for the first time. It continues to apply to each individual member of a couple to determine combined income for the purpose of OAS income-tested benefits. EI premiums and contributions to the CPP or QPP, including enhanced contributions, for the year, must be deducted from their respective employment earnings and self-employment earnings before applying the earnings exemption. EI premiums and contributions to the CPP or QPP, including enhanced contributions, must be deducted from their respective employment earnings and self-employment earnings before applying the earnings exemption. Only self-employment earnings that exceed zero dollars will be used to calculate the individual's total earnings for the purposes of the exemption. The exemption is calculated by combining an individual's employment and self-employment income after EI premiums and CPP or QPP contributions, including enhanced contributions, have been deducted (total earnings) and deducting up to $5,000.00 from their total earnings for the year. In addition, if the individual's total earnings are more than $5,000 for the year; their total earnings can be further reduced by applying a deduction of 50% to earnings greater than $5,000 but not exceeding $15,000. The total amount of the exemption cannot exceed $10,000. Deductions allowed to reduce rental income When calculating income for the GIS, ALW and/or ALWS , a capital cost allowance deduction cannot result in a net rental loss or increase the total rental loss. However, a net rental loss may be used to reduce the total amount of income. The following deductions and expenses are allowed to reduce rental income: capital cost allowance (major repairs); electricity; heat; insurance premiums; maintenance (such as snow removal); other expenses allowed for income tax purposes; property taxes; repairs (such as roof and windows); and water. Deductions allowed to reduce other income The following deductions are allowed and are used to reduce other income: amount paid to refund an overpayment of EI, CPP or QPP benefits ( except when the amount is recovered from current benefits); annual union, professional or like dues; attendant care and other disability supports deductions; business investment loss; carrying charges; child care expenses; child support payments under a court order or agreement made before May 1997; Quebec Parental Insurance Plan premiums on self-employment income; exploration and development expenses; moving expenses related to employment; other employment expenses; clergy residence deduction; Registered Pension Plan contribution; Registered Retirement Savings Plan contribution; First Home Savings Account contribution; spousal support payments; deduction for elected pension split income; and other deductions permitted by CRA. If an individual claims spousal or child support payments as a deduction and the spouse or common-law partner receiving these payments is also in receipt of a GIS, ALW , and/or ALWS , ensure that the individual receiving the support payments has reported them as income. Deductions allowed to reduce Canadian dividends A dividend is considered income for the year in which it is received. It is considered received on the day it is paid. All taxable dividend income received from taxable Canadian companies must be reported as income. The taxable amount of dividend income is indicated on the dividend taxation slip issued by the company issuing the dividend. If the individual does not have a dividend taxation slip from which to obtain their taxable dividend income, it must be manually calculated. An amendment to the OAS Act in June 1999 allows for a beneficiary or an applicant to deduct an amount equal to 3 times the unused portion of their federal dividend tax credit from their income. This deduction may further enable an individual to become eligible either to receive the GIS, ALW or ALWS or to receive a higher benefit payment amount. The unused portion of the federal dividend tax credit deduction became effective starting with the July 2000—June 2001 payment period. It is not possible to calculate the unused portion of the federal dividend tax credit of an individual who has not filed an income tax and benefit return. The only way for an individual to apply the unused portion of their federal dividend tax credit for OAS purposes is to file an income tax and benefit return. CRA income feed provides the values necessary for the system to calculate the correct amount of the benefit. If the CRA feed is not available, a copy of the individual's income tax and benefit return must be requested from the CRA to manually calculate the unused portion of the individual's federal dividend tax credit. Income is determined in accordance with the Income Tax Act allowing for certain exceptions. Capital gains are not an exception. CRA provides the amount of taxable capital gains, which CRA calculates after all losses and exemptions are applied. When the income is reported in Block 5 of the CRA screen, accept the amount.

Entitlement to income-tested benefits under the OAS Act such as the GIS, the ALW and the ALWS is based on: the beneficiary's current marital status; and net income received in the base calendar year. When the beneficiary has a spouse or common-law partner, their combined income is used for calculating their GIS and/or ALW . Exceptions occur when: the couple is separated for reasons beyond their control; or one of them is incarcerated. Income under the OAS Act is calculated in accordance with the Income Tax Act . The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) assesses income on an annual basis from the filing of income tax and benefit returns. The income used to assess income-tested benefits is from the previous calendar year and the benefit is paid on that amount for the next payment period, which runs from July 1 of the current year to June 30 of the following year. Income-tested benefits are adjusted on an annual basis. However, certain sources of income, as outlined under the Income not considered section below, are excluded from the calculation under the OAS Act. Although some sources of income are not taxable, they are still defined as income under the Income Tax Act and, therefore, must be considered as income under the OAS Act. Deductions allowed by CRA for tax purposes are also allowed under the OAS Act to reduce a beneficiary's income. Some additional deductions specific to the OAS Act may further enable a beneficiary to become entitled to receive a GIS, ALW or ALWS or a higher benefit payment amount. When an individual's income decreases due to retirement or a reduction or loss of pension income, the GIS, ALW or ALWS entitlement may be calculated based on an estimate of certain sources of income for the current calendar year rather than on the base calendar year income. This is referred to as an 'option'. This estimated income is added to any other type of income from the base calendar year.

The following sources of income are considered when calculating entitlement to income-tested benefits under the OAS Act. For ease of reference, the order in which the information is provided in this document is presented in the same way as on the Statement of Income (blocks 1 through 9). Refer to the detailed procedures to ensure that the proper amount is considered for each of the following sources of income: payments from CPP or QPP, excluding Death ( DTH ) or Child's benefits; other pension income from Canadian and foreign sources; Employment Insurance (EI) and provincial and territorial Workers' Compensation Board benefits; net interest and other investment income, including foreign dividends; Canadian dividends and capital gains; net rental income; net employment income; net self-employment income; and/or other income.

topic_title: Sources of income not considered Updated
text: Certain sources of income are not considered when calculating entitlement to income-tested benefits. Benefit and assistance payments Certain social assistance payments paid from a municipal, provincial, territorial or federal government are not considered as income for the calculation of OAS program income-tested benefits. The following are no t considered income for OAS income-tested benefits purposes: amount issued to fishers abandoning lobster fishing after return of permit; assistance payments from a municipal, provincial, territorial or federal government; Bell Canada Death benefits for Needy Dependants; benefits paid by La Société de l'assurance automobile du Québec (the exception: benefits paid directly to a third party for personal assistance to the accident victim are considered as employment income); compensation received from a province or territory for a motor vehicle accident; Canada Child Benefit (CCB) payments as well as those from related provincial or territorial programs; CPP and QPP DTH and Children's benefits; Charles Massey Employees Aid Fund; Child support payments received under a court order or written agreement made after April 30, 1997; Child support payments received under a court order or written agreement made before May 1997, if certain CRA conditions are met; compensation payments made by the Quebec government to salmon fishers; disability payments considered to be non-taxable in the U.S.; Dutch Supplementary Allowance as of April 1, 2004, when the revised international agreement between Canada and the Netherlands came into force; OAS ALW ; OAS ALWS ; OAS GIS; OAS pension; Employment Insurance Emergency Response Benefit (EI ERB) received in 2021 or later; Canada Emergency Response Benefit (CERB), Canada Recovery Benefit (CRB), Canada Recovery Sickness Benefit (CRSB), Canada Recovery Caregiving Benefit (CRSB) and Canada Worker Lockdown Benefit received in 2021 or later; Canada Dental Care Plan (CDCP) payments; Canada Disability Benefit; payments made by a provincial or territorial government to indigenous people who live from hunting and fishing; strike fund payments; Universal Child Care benefit effective July 2006; and/or voluntary spousal or child support payments (where no formal written agreement or court order exists). Grants, rebates, refunds, programs and credits The following grants, rebates, refunds, programs and credits are not considered income for OAS income-tested benefits purposes: Climate Action Credit (British Columbia only , beginning summer 2008); Energy Cost Benefit Program—payments began January 12, 2006; excise gas tax refunds and rebates; federal sales tax credits; fire insurance rebates; Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) credits and rebates; grants received under the Home Adaptations for Seniors' Independence program introduced by Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation; income tax rebates or refunds (excluding any interest received, which must be considered as income); municipal tax rebates; Natural Gas Vehicles Program grants; and/or one-time payment for older seniors (OAS Pensioners age 75+) (2021); one-time payment for persons with disabilities (2020); one-time payment for seniors (2020); one-time grant for GIS recipients who received Pandemic Benefits (2022); and/or provincial grants received under the program for improvement of housing (in Quebec, LOGIRÉNOV). War service pensions, retribution payments and ex gratia payments The following war service pensions, retribution payments and ex gratia payments are not considered income for OAS: Agent Orange lump-sum payments; Assistance Program for HIV/AIDS secondaries; Common Experience Payment, which is part of the Indian Residential Schools Settlement Agreement; Ex gratia payments from the Canadian government: to each living Hong Kong veteran or their survivor, for the forced labour they were made to endure while prisoners of the Japanese during the Second World War; to each living veteran or their survivor, who, as Canadian airmen, were held captive and suffered atrocities for 3 months in 1945 in the Buchenwald Concentration Camp; Ex gratia symbolic payment: Chinese Head Tax and Historical Recognition Initiatives for Head Tax payers who were living as of February 2006, effective August 29, 2006; Chinese Head Tax and Historical Recognition Initiatives for persons who were in a conjugal relationship with a Head Tax payer who is now deceased, effective November 30, 2006; Extraordinary Assistance Program for HIV/AIDS Primaries; First Nations Veterans Package; Indemnities paid by a provincial or territorial go vernment to victims of criminal acts; Merchant Navy Veteran Special Benefit; Pension payments made by the Federal Republic of Germany as compensation to victims of National Socialist persecution; Pension received from the U.S. as a result of the death of a son in the Vietnam War; Province of Quebec National Program of Reconciliation with the Duplessis Orphans; Redress payments to Japanese Canadians; The 86-90 Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) Settlement Agreement; U.S. Veterans' Administration disability pensions, generally called Compensation, which is a service connected disability pension; War service pensions or retribution payments on account of disability or death paid by Commonwealth countries and countries that were allies of His Majesty during World War I (1914-1918) and World War II (1939-1945); and War Veterans Allowance or Civilian War Allowance, disability or widow's pension based on war service or certain war service pensions from other countries. Other payments The following other types of payments are not considered income for OAS income-tested benefits purposes: Aboriginal people tax-exempt income; inheritances; lottery winnings; most amounts received from a life insurance policy following someone's death; Registered Disability Savings Plan; reverse mortgage initial cash payment; support or gifts from relatives, registered charities or other organizations; Tax-Free Savings Account; wage loss replacement benefits paid under a private insurance plan to which an employee was the sole contributor. Court settlement payments for damages with respect to personal injury or death; and, First Home Savings Accounts withdrawals (as long as the income is used to purchase a home).

topic_title: Special circumstances in income sources and situations faced by individuals
text: Income exemption under section 87 of the Indian Act For purposes of the tax exemption under section 87 of the Indian Act , CRA uses the term “Indian” because it has a legal meaning in the Indian Act . This term is defined in the Indian Act as a person who is registered as an Indian or is entitled to be registered as an Indian. Determining whether an individual is entitled to be registered as an Indian is a question of fact. Any taxable income received by an indigenous person is considered as income for the OAS program unless they are eligible for the tax-exemption under Section 87 of the Indian Act . That exemption applies to the income of an Indian that is earned on a reserve or that is considered to be earned on a reserve. It also applies to goods bought on or delivered to a reserve. Determining income for OAS purposes under section 87 of the Indian Act Income that is exempt under section 87 of the Indian Act must not be considered as income for the purpose of calculating OAS income-tested benefits. The exemption in question applies to the personal property of individuals who are registered as Indians under the Indian Act . Personal property includes: employment and employment-related income earned on a reserve or considered to have been earned on a reserve; and goods that are bought on or delivered to a reserve and are therefore tax-exempt. To determine the income of an individual who may be exempt from taxation under section 87 of the Indian Act and who has filed a federal income tax and benefit return, confirm with CRA how the income was treated to ensure correct calculation. If the beneficiary did not file a federal income tax and benefit return, accept the information provided, subject to the Indian Act Exemption for Employment Income Guidelines External link . This guideline is an administrative tool developed by CRA to assist in determining whether the personal property (including income) of the individual is considered to be situated on a reserve and therefore tax-exempt. Indian Act Exemption for Employment Income Guidelines Employment income CRA's Indian Act Exemption for Employment Income Guidelines are used to determine whether the employment or other income related to the employment of an indigenous person is considered or not for the purposes of the OAS Act. Other employment-related income The following benefit payments received by an indigenous person will usually be excluded from the calculation of their income when received as a result of employment income that was not considered as income under the OAS Act: CPP and QPP payments; EI benefits; Registered Pension Plan benefits; Retiring allowances; and Wage loss replacement benefits. Interest and Investment Income To determine whether interest and investment income is tax-exempt, consider the location of the financial institution and where the income is generated. If the financial institution is on a reserve, but the financial activities that generate the income are not, the interest or investment income must be declared as income. Treaty money or band funds CRA must confirm if this type of income is tax-exempt or not. If it is tax-exempt, it is not considered income for OAS purposes. Payments of retroactive CPP or QPP benefits—Notional tax considerations Income is generally considered income in the year in which it is received. However, the retroactive payment of certain CPP or QPP benefits may be treated differently. Retroactive lump sum payments of CPP or QPP benefits from both the previous and current calendar years are considered income for the year in which they are received. However, when portions of the lump sum payment from the previous years are $300.00 or more, notional tax considerations are applied. This means that any portions of the lump sum payment from previous years are subtracted from the base calendar year amount. Any portion of the lump sum from the current year is considered income in the year in which it is received. Under the OAS, accounts where retroactive payments of CPP or QPP benefits paid are identified and the amounts broken down by year, such information is provided to CRA through a supplementary tape sent along with the T4 information tape. CRA then uses this information to apply the notional tax provision automatically for all beneficiaries receiving retroactive CPP or QPP benefits. If this action reduces the tax liability, the provision is applied by CRA. However, if the provision does not benefit the beneficiary for taxation purposes, CRA does not subtract previous years' portions from the base calendar year amount the beneficiary received. For OAS, retroactive CPP or QPP benefits are treated in a different way. Notional tax considerations are applied for all beneficiaries who receive retroactive CPP or QPP benefits regardless of tax considerations. This means that portions of the retroactive lump sum payment that apply to previous years and are $300.00 or more are always subtracted from the base calendar year income when calculating entitlements to income-tested benefits. The income removed from the current year is not retroactively applied to previous years and is not considered income for the previous years. Unusual sources of income When it is unclear or there is doubt as to how a source of income is treated for income tax purposes, and when such information is not already available on file, it is the responsibility of the beneficiary to obtain the necessary information or confirmation from CRA. Bankruptcy In the case of bankruptcy, the amount to be taken into consideration is the applicant or beneficiary's income for the entire calendar year and not the adjusted amount calculated by CRA after bankruptcy. Cessation of or decrease in income due to retirement or to a reduction or loss of pension income In situations where a client's income decreases due to retirement or to a reduction or loss of pension income, their entitlement to the GIS, the ALW or the ALWS benefits may be calculated based on an estimate of income for the current year (this provision of the OAS Act is also referred to as an option ) rather than the base calendar year income. Only optionable income (i.e. all employment, self-employment or pension income) will be estimated. This will be added to all non-optionable income from the base calendar year to establish the income used for calculating the income-tested benefit. A decrease in the following types of income may give rise to an option: CPP and QPP Disability benefits and Survivor's pension Employment Insurance benefits and provincial and territorial Workers' Compensation Boards benefits; Income assistance benefits (paid under certain government programs); Other pension Income from Canadian sources; Other pension Income from foreign sources (except for decrease due to currency exchange rate); Registered Retirement Income Fund payments Rental income (only if CRA confirms that the income is from a business); Self-employment income (if the individual has stopped working or has sold the business that generated the income); Support payments; and/or Wage loss replacement benefits (paid under a private insurance plan to which both the employer and the employee contributed). Receipt of income information When an individual has made an initial application for GIS, ALW or ALWS , they will be determined to have qualified for lifetime renewal. Income information must be provided by CRA or through a Statement of Income (ISP-3025B or ISP-3026 form). If this information is received more than 11 months after the beginning of a payment period, the usual 11-month retroactivity period applies for payment purposes (unless another provision applies e.g. incapacity). The individual continues to be considered a lifetime applicant, but the Minister reserves the right to request a further application. The 11-month retroactive period begins from the date on which the application or income information becomes available to us, even if the Department is awaiting confirmation of income from CRA. topic_title: Data elements used to waive an OAS pension application and presume eligibility requirements
text: The combination of the following data elements of age, residence, legal status and a Canadian residential address allows the Minister to waive the requirement for an OAS pension application and substantiate eligibility for the OAS pension. Age Under Category 1 , the date of birth will be the age that was established to approve CPP and/or QPP benefits. Under Category 2 , the date of birth will be the age established under the Social Insurance Registry (SIR) validated with the date of birth from the CRA. Residence CPP and/or QPP information For the purpose of presuming residence, 40 years of participation to the CPP and/or QPP programs will be considered as 40 years of residence for a full pension under the 40-Year Rule. Participation is defined as: 40 years of CPP and/or QPP contributions after age 18; or a combination of valid CPP and/or QPP contributions as of the age 18 (i.e. years when the individual had Unadjusted Pensionable Earnings (UPE) above the year's basic exemption), years in which: a Child Rearing Provision or a division of UPE provision (also referred to as a Credit Split) were applied; or previous years in receipt of a CPP or QPP RTR pension or CPPD benefit. Additional residence data elements required for Category 2 Because Category 2 individuals are not already in pay for a CPP or QPP benefit, CPP or QPP participation alone is not sufficient to demonstrate residence. Residence must be demonstrated with a combination of CPP or QPP participation in conjunction with tax filings as a Canadian resident for each year of participation for a minimum of 40 years. The individual must also have filed an income tax return as a Canadian resident in the last possible tax year before their 64th birthday. These 40 years of residence are assessed within a 46-year window which is based on the maximum number of years that an individual can contribute to the CPP or QPP from age 18 until age 64. Even if an individual only needs 40 years of residence to qualify for an OAS pension under the automatic enrolment process and considering that not everyone will have worked or filed their tax returns for 40 consecutive years, the 46-year window is used in the selection process to provide a longer period in which the minimum 40 years of CPP or QPP participation and tax filings can be matched. A 45-year window applies to individuals for whom tax data is not available for the year before turning 64. This could happen if the individual's birthday falls within the months of January to April. Taxes filed CRA information In order for a CPP or QPP year to be considered as a year of residence for the selection process, the individual must have filed federal taxes as a Canadian resident for that year. Although the combination of CPP or QPP participation and tax filing information for 40 years is required to presume residence in Canada under the Category 2 automatic enrolment selection, tax filing information will not be available before 1972 and may not be available in the year before the individual's 64th birthday. CPP or QPP participation for 40 years and tax filing for 38 to 39 years (depending on when the individual turned 64) will be sufficient to presume residence in Canada during the transitional period when: individuals are turning 64 in the years 2017 and 2018; and the tax filing window is less than 45 years. If the year 1971 is required to meet the 40-year residence requirement, CPP or QPP participation alone will be considered as sufficient evidence to presume residence in Canada for that year. In 2019, tax information will be available for the full 45 to 46 year window and, at that time, the 40 years of CPP or QPP participation along with the tax filing information in each year since 1972 to their 64th birthday will be required in order to presume residence for Category 2 automatic enrolment. Latest tax year filed The individual must have resided in Canada and filed taxes as a Canadian resident with a valid Canadian residential address (i.e. not a commercial, government or institution address) in the last possible tax year before they turned 64. This means that for individuals who turn 64 in 2017, the latest tax filing available before the individual turns 64 is either 2016 or 2015 (2015 if the individual's birthday falls within January to April). Legal status When selected for automatic enrolment, an individual's legal status in Canada will be presumed from age 64 up until the day before the application is approved (i.e. their 65th birthday) provided they meet the eligibility requirements of residence and they have a Canadian residential address.

topic_title: Data elements used to waive the GIS application
text: Statement of Income At age 64 + 9 months, the Department will obtain the CRA income year data for the payment period for the month after the GIS application will be waived. Marital status At age 64 + 9 months, the Department will leverage the CRA data to identify the individual's marital status. When the CRA tax information identifies that the individual is married or in a common-law relationship, it is required that the spouse or common-law partner's identity and information are known to the Department in order to be automatically enrolled for the GIS. For the purposes of GIS automatic enrolment, "known to the Department" means that Service Canada has data in ITRDS for the spouse or common-law partner received from the CPP program or the SIR.

topic_title: Declining automatic enrolment for the GIS benefit
text: If the individual does not wish to be automatically enrolled, they must notify Service Canada that they wish to decline receipt of the GIS benefit before their 65th birthday. If the individual wishes to receive the GIS benefit at a future date, they must submit a new application. If an individual notifies Service Canada that they wish to decline automatic enrolment after their 65th birthday, they can choose to cease or cancel the GIS benefit. In the absence of any response or corrections from the individual and their spouse or common-law partner, if applicable, the requirement for the GIS benefit application will be waived and the supplement will be approved on the individual's 65th birthday. Payment will be effective the month after the individual's 65th birthday. Once the GIS benefit application is waived, the individual is considered a GIS for Life applicant, unless the waiver is cancelled for a future payment period. A Notice of Entitlement letter will be sent to the individual after age 65 outlining the date that the pension and supplement become effective and of their right to request a reconsideration.

topic_title: Declining the OAS pension automatic enrolment
text: If the individual does not wish to be automatically enrolled, they must notify Service Canada in writing or through My Service Canada Account that they wish to decline receipt of the OAS pension before the day of their 65th birthday. If the individual wishes to receive an OAS pension at a future date, they must submit a new application. If an individual notifies Service Canada that they wish to decline automatic enrolment after they turn 65, but before a payment is issued, this will be considered a withdrawal of their deemed OAS application. In the event that an OAS pension payment has been issued, the individual can choose to cease or cancel their OAS pension.

topic_title: Exclusions for automatic enrolment for the GIS benefit
text: Individuals will be screened out of the automatic enrolment process and invited to complete an application for the GIS benefit when they: have not been selected for Category 1 or Category 2, or have been selected but have chosen to decline automatic enrolment; have not filed an income tax return for the base calendar year; have a spouse or common-law partner, but the spouse or common-law partner is unknown to the Department; have a foreign address or a foreign tax withhold on their account at age 64; have a SIR warning flag on file; and were selected for automatic enrolment where an OAS pension application is not deemed to have been made and approved at age 65. Additionally, individuals will not be automatically enrolled if, before their 65th birthday, they: will no longer be automatically enrolled for the OAS pension; notify Service Canada that they have ceased or will cease to reside in Canada; report inaccuracies in the marital status information on the notification letter and do not correct it before their 65th birthday; or decline the GIS benefit. In all of the above situations, the individual will be notified that an application is required.

topic_title: Exclusions for automatic enrolment of the OAS pension
text: Individuals with the following will not be selected for automatic enrolment: a foreign residential address or a foreign tax withhold; a warning flag on file at the SIR (warning flags identify issues such as possible fraud, lost or stolen cards, or dormant files); a power of attorney on the individual's CPP file (each power of attorney agreement provides different rights and limitations). Additionally, selected individuals will not be automatically enrolled if, before their 65th birthday: they notify Service Canada that they have ceased or will cease to reside in Canada; they report inaccuracies in the information on the OAS Automatic Enrolment Notification letter (ISP-3009) or the OAS Automatic Enrolment Notification letter (ISP-3030) and no longer meet the eligibility requirements; or they decline the pension. In all of the above situations, the individual will be notified that an application is required.

The GIS notification letters for an individual selected for automatic enrolment and for their spouse or common-law partner, if applicable, outline the obligation to correct any inaccuracies in the income and the marital status before the day the individual turns 65. Inaccuracies in the GIS notification letter The individual and their spouse or common-law partner must make any corrections before the selected individual's 65th birthday, if applicable. If the reported inaccuracies are corrected before their 65th birthday and the individual still meets the eligibility requirements, they may continue to be automatically enrolled. If they do not meet the eligibility requirements, they will be required to submit an OAS pension and a GIS application. The Minister retains the right to request an application at any time before the individual's 65th birthday to determine eligibility and entitlement for the OAS pension and the GIS.

topic_title: OAS pension application is waived and the pension approved
text: In the absence of any response or corrections from the individual, the requirement for an application will be waived and the pension will be approved on the individual's 65th birthday. Payment will be effective the month after their 65th birthday. A Notice of Entitlement letter will be sent to the individual after age 65 outlining: the date that the pension becomes effective; the individual's responsibilities to the Department; and their right to request a reconsideration.

topic_title: OAS pension automatic enrolment notification letter
text: If an individual is selected for automatic enrolment, they will be notified in writing in the month following their 64th birthday of the Department's intent to waive the application for an OAS pension and to provide the individual with the information that the Minister intends to use to determine their eligibility for the pension. Inaccuracies in the OAS pension notification letter The individual is obligated to correct any inaccuracies in the information provided in the notification letter. The individual must make any corrections in writing before their 65th birthday. If reported inaccuracies are corrected before an individual's 65th birthday and the individual still meets the eligibility requirements, they may continue to be automatically enrolled. If they do not meet the eligibility requirements, or the corrections affect the eligibility requirements originally established for automatic enrolment (i.e. the effective date), they will be required to submit an OAS/GIS integrated application. In the case of an incorrect date of birth (month/year), the individual would not meet the criteria for automatic enrolment because their effective date would be amended to either before or after the 65th birthday we originally used to select them. The only situation where a corrected date of birth would result in an individual meeting the criteria for automatic enrolment would be if the day was incorrect but the month and year were correct. The Minister retains the right to request an application at any time before the individual's 65th birthday to determine eligibility for the OAS pension.

Automatic enrolment for the OAS pension Automatic enrolment for a full OAS pension allows the Minister to waive the requirement for an application at the age of 65 based on available information. The application is only waived if the Minister is satisfied that an individual is presumed to have met all of the eligibility requirements (age, residence and legal status) in the absence of evidence to the contrary. The Minister retains the right to cancel the automatic enrolment process and to request an application before the individual's 65th birthday. The Minister may also request documentary evidence (e.g. proof of age, residence or legal status) at any time before or after the approval of the OAS pension. OAS pension applications that meet the data elements to be automatically enrolled Individuals who submit a paper or online application to apply for a full OAS pension and who meet all the data elements to substantiate eligibility may have their eligibility to the OAS pension determined using the same rules and information. Automatic enrolment of the GIS Automatic enrolment for the GIS allows the Minister to waive the requirement for a GIS application at the age of 65 based on information that is made available. The application can only be waived if the Minister is satisfied, based on the information collected, that an individual meets the eligibility and entitlement criteria for the benefit. The Minister retains the right to cancel the automatic enrolment process and to request an application before the individual's 65th birthday. Individuals who are selected for the automatic enrolment of the OAS pension (Categories 1 and 2) will be screened for GIS automatic enrolment. In order to waive the requirement for a GIS application, the Minister must: be able to obtain a statement of income from the CRA; and determine the marital status of an individual and the identity of the spouse or common-law partner, if applicable, by leveraging existing data from the CRA and within the Department. The Department will obtain income and marital status information from the CRA to determine entitlement to the GIS. In order to waive the requirement for a GIS application, the selection of individuals for the GIS automatic enrolment can only occur if, at age 64 + 9 months, these individuals are single, widowed, divorced or separated and, for those individuals who are married or in a common-law relationship, their spouse or common-law partner's identity and information are already known to the Department.

topic_title: Selection criteria for the OAS pension
text: Selection criteria for the OAS pension (Category 1) Individuals are selected for a Category 1 automatic enrolment if they meet the following criteria at the age of 64: They have a Canadian residential address; They are in receipt of or are approved for payment of a CPP or QPP RTR pension, CPPD benefit or SVR pension; and They have 40 or more years of participation to the CPP or QPP program. Selection criteria for the OAS pension (Category 2) Individuals are selected for a Category 2 automatic enrolment if they meet the following criteria at the age of 64: They have a Canadian residential address; They have 40 or more years of participation to the CPP or QPP program and are not in receipt of or have not been approved for payment of a CPP or QPP RTR pension, CPPD benefit or SVR pension; and They have CRA tax filing data for each year of CPP or QPP participation since 1972 or later, up to the year before the individual reached age 64.

topic_title: Actuarial adjustment for the deferral of a full OAS pension
text: A full pension is increased by a factor of 0.6% for each month an individual defers receipt of their OAS pension up to and including the month of approval of their OAS pension. The actuarially adjusted pension is based on the pension rate at the effective date of the full pension.

topic_title: Actuarial adjustment for the deferral of a partial OAS pension
text: Depending on the situation, pensioners approved for a partial pension can receive additional 40ths for accumulated periods of residence or an actuarially adjusted pension based on the number of 40ths at the earliest date of eligibility. Unless they decide otherwise, you must calculate each additional 40ths and actuarially adjusted pension to provide the individual with the most beneficial rate. As of July 2013, applicants who qualify for a partial pension and who have voluntarily deferred their pension or have applied late, must be advised of the amount of their pension with an actuarial adjustment and accumulated residence for the same period of time. If deferral is chosen by the individual, o r is the most advantageous payment option, the partial OAS pension is increased by a factor of 0.6% for each month an individual defers receipt of their OAS pension after the month of initial eligibility up to and including the month of approval of their OAS pension.

Individuals who have not applied for the OAS pension will be able to accrue months towards a deferred pension starting the month after the month in which they first become eligible to receive a pension under the Old Age Security Act until the month they turn 70 years old. The deferral period ends in the month of approval, and payments commence the month after the month of approval.

topic_title: Eligibility to a full pension during the period of deferral
text: An individual who qualifies for a partial pension at age 65 may become eligible for a full pension during their period of deferral. For instance, an individual who qualifies for a partial pension may accumulate residence to become eligible for a full pension under the 10-year rule or the 3 for 1 year rule. These individuals can accrue an actuarial adjustment on their full pension from the month after the month they are eligible for a full pension.
Old Age Security Act Section 7.1—Voluntary deferral

Periods for which an individual would not have been entitled to an OAS pension cannot be applied towards a deferred pension. Individuals cannot voluntarily defer their OAS pension and have an actuarial factor applied for periods that fall under the following situations: Individuals incarcerated in a federal penitentiary or in a provincial correctional facility, are not eligible to accrue an actuarial adjustment for the months they are incarcerated (i.e. the month after the month of incarceration up to the month before release). However, incarcerated individuals are entitled to payment of the OAS pension for their first month of incarceration, therefore, that first month of incarceration may be applied towards a deferred pension. Voluntary deferral will be available to the incarcerated individual the month of their release. Periods in which an individual spent time outside of Canada, for which there is no enti tlement to the OAS pension, cannot be applied towards a deferred pension. This limitation applies to individuals with less than 20 years of residence . Voluntary deferral will be available to the individual the month they return or resume residence in Canada.

As of July 1, 2013, individuals may choose to voluntarily defer receipt of their OAS pension starting the month they are entitled to receive the pension. Individuals will only get credit for deferral from this month onward. Individuals who are eligible to receive a full pension may choose to defer their pension start date to receive the increased actuarial adjustment. Those who are eligible for a partial pension may also choose to defer their pension, and in some cases are given the choice of increasing their benefit amount based on: the actuarial adjustment; or additional 40ths for the accumulated periods of residence in Canada. Individuals are able to defer the start of their pension for a maximum of 60 months up to the month they turn 70 years of age . Individuals who choose to defer receipt of their pension will not be eligible to receive the Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS). I n addition, their spouse or common-law partner will not be eligible for the Allowanceduring the deferral period. The actuarially adjusted pension is based on the pension rate at the effective date of the full pension.

topic_title: When to offer a pension choice
text: A “pension choice” refers to offering an applicant the choice of when the OAS pension is to begin. Generally, applicants qualify for and start receiving their pension the month after their 65th birthday. Some individuals do not apply at that time because they: may not have accumulated sufficient residence to entitle them to either a partial or full pension; are unaware of the pension; or choose to delay receipt of the pension to receive an actuarially adjusted amount. In these cases, determine whether a choice should be offered. As there are several ways that residence in Canada may give rise to eligibility (full pensions, partial pensions, 10-year rule and 3 for 1 rule), making the right choice may be confusing for applicants. For this reason, the Department must provide information to applicants about the possible pension choices available and the significance of them. There is no requirement to offer pension choices to applicants where there is entitlement to the GIS. For applicants where there is no entitlement to the GIS or where they do not wish to receive the GIS, you must offer them the following pension choices: When an applicant resides in Canada and was a resident in Canada on July 1, 1977, or earlier (or was in possession of a valid Canadian Immigration visa on July 1, 1977); and when an applicant has no entitlement to the GIS, they have the choice to: receive a partial pension at the earliest effective date; o r a full pension under the transitional rules (10- year and 3 for 1 rule) at a future effective date. If the applicant applies after their first date of eligibility, the applicant also has the choice to accumulate residence (i.e. more 40ths) or receive an actuarially adjusted partial pension at the effective date. When an applicant resides outside of Canada and was resident in Canada on July 1, 1977, or earlier (or was in possession of a valid Canadian Immigration visa on July 1, 1977), they have the choice to: receive a partial pension at the earliest effective date; or return to reside in Canada for the period of residence that is necessary to qualify for a full pension under the transitional rules at a future effective date. If the applicant applies after their first date of eligibility, the applicant also has the choice to receive an actuarially adjusted partial pension at the effective date, or return to reside in Canada for the period that is necessary to qualify for a full pension under the transitional rules at a future effective date. For voluntary deferral, those eligible for a partial pension will be paid the greater of their accumulated residence (i.e. the most 40ths) or an actuarially adjusted amount, with some exceptions. Beneficiaries must be notified in writing: of the rate; why that rate was chosen; and that they have the option to choose the lower rate.

topic_title: Applications deemed to be received at an earlier date Updated
text: Applications for pensions and benefits are deemed received at an earlier date under the following circumstances: Post-mortem applications are deemed to have been received on the individual's date of death when the application is received by Service Canada within a year of the date the individual died. A CPPD benefits application is denied and the individual requests an RTR pension within 90 days of receiving the initial CPPD letter or appeal letter. The RTR application is deemed to have been received on the CPPD benefits application date. A DSB is ceased and the individual applies for an RTR pension within 90 days of the date they were advised that their DSB has been ceased. The RTR application is deemed to have been received in the month the DSB ceased. For CPP Children's benefits: when the children (under the age of 18, or aged 18 to 25 years old) are listed on the contributor's application for CPPD benefits or SVR pension application; and when the parent or guardian who has decision-making responsibility of the child under the age of 18 submits the Child's benefit application; or when the child aged 18 to 25 years old submits an Application for a Canada Pension Plan Child's Benefit form (ISP-1400) and a Declaration of Attendance at School or University form (ISP-1401) or a Canada Pension Plan Child's Benefit Application and Declaration for a Student over 18 years of Age in Attendance at School or University form (ISP-1402) within the prescribed timeframes. The Department applies the incapacity provision, the deemed date of an application is the later of: the month before the earliest month the relevant benefit could have started; or the month the latest period of continuous incapacity started; The Minister is satisfied and determines that erroneous advice and/or administrative error has occurred. Discretion is used to evaluate, on a case-by-case basis, those paper applications received late due to circumstances which are beyond the applicant's control (such as postal delays), and for which the applicant requests that an earlier date of receipt be accepted by the Department.

Applications for CPP and OAS pensions or benefits are waived under the following circumstances: An automatic enrolment for the OAS pension occurs at age 65 based on: information made available to the Minister; and the Minister being satisfied that the individual meets the eligibility and entitlement criteria for the pension. An automatic enrolment of the GIS occurs at age 65 based on: information made available to the Minister; and the Minister being satisfied that the individual meets the eligibility and entitlement criteria for the benefit. An automatic conversion of the ALW to the ALWS occurs the month after the month that the spouse or common-law partner of the ALW recipient dies. The ALW must have already been in pay or payable at the time their spouse or common-law partner died. An automatic conversion of ALW or ALWS benefits to an OAS pension along with the GIS occurs at age 65. An automatic payment of CPP PRB to the recipient of a CPP and/or QPP RTR pension occurs effective January 1 of the year after the year in which contributions are made. An automatic conversion of a DSB to an RTR pension at age 65 occurs. An automatic conversion of a Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit (DCCB) to a Surviving Child's benefit for a child 18 years of age or over occurs effective the month after the disabled contributor's death when the child is already receiving a DCCB from the disabled contributor's parent at the time of their death and all conditions of eligibility for the Surviving Child's benefit are met. A CPPD benefits application submitted by an RTR pension beneficiary is considered an application for both the DSB and the PRDB. The requirement for a separate PRDB application is waived.

As of November 1, 2016, changes were made to the application screen of the online application to make it easier for applicants to know when they have successfully submitted and applied for their pension or benefit. Applicants receive a confirmation message that their online application has been received. If they do not receive such a message, they know that their attempt to complete an online application was not successful. Before November 1, 2016, an individual submitting an online application did not receive confirmation that their application was received. When an individual claims they submitted an online application for an RTR pension before this date, and the Department has no record of receipt, date protection can still be applied when: the individual informs the Department of the date they submitted their RTR online pension application (and it is before November 1, 2016); and the Department subsequently receives an online or paper application within a time frame communicated to the individual; and the Department confirms the individual accessed My Service Canada Account (MSCA) on or about the date the applicant claims. When all of these conditions are met, the RTR pension application is considered received on the date the individual initially accessed MSCA. The pension start date can then be determined based on this date of receipt.

topic_title: Date of receipt—Applications submitted online through My Service Canada Account
text: An electronic application is made online when it is submitted through the applicant's My Service Canada Account (MSCA). Applications made online via MSCA are submitted through the server located in Moncton, New Brunswick. If the applicant does not receive a message to confirm that their online application was received, then they did not complete the process of applying for the pension or benefit and no application was submitted. Online applications submitted on the last day of any given month could, in some instances, be date and timestamped on the first day of the following month. This depends on the date and time zone from which the individual submits the online application. For example, if an individual applies online from British Columbia on April 30 at 8:03 p.m. for an Early Retirement pension, because of the time zone difference, the server in Moncton will stamp it May 1 at 12:03 a.m. In this case, the individual would be eligible to receive their benefit effective June 1 instead of May 1. Before January 2020, only an RTR pension application for CPP could be submitted online.

All applications that are received by the Department are date stamped. A paper application is deemed to have been received when: it physically arrives in any Service Canada Centre; it is received by one of its employees while on duty outside the office; or it is received by a social security institution of a country with which Canada has a Social Security Agreement in force. When a paper application for a CPP or an OAS pension or benefit is received unsigned , it is not a valid application. However, the date it is stamped as received conditionally protects the date of receipt of the application for retroactivity purposes if the signature of the applicant or the applicant's legal representative is subsequently received within the requested time frame. If the valid application is not received within the requested time frame, the file is administratively closed and the date of receipt is no longer protected. A certified true copy or original application does not need to be requested in cases where a signed photocopy, a fax or an email with a scan is received. A wet signature is not required unless the validity of the application or the signature is in question. Additionally, most of Canada's International Social Security Agreements contain a protective date provision which provides that the date of receipt of an application for a pension or benefit from one country can be considered the date of the corresponding pension or benefit application from the other country (i.e. CPP or an OAS pension or benefit). This provision varies from agreement to agreement. For more information, Foreign Benefits CPPD benefits The date stamp on any supporting documents for a CPPD benefits application containing the signature of the applicant can also conditionally protect the date of application for CPPD benefits provided the following are subsequently received with the signature of the applicant within the allotted time: An Application for Canada Pension Plan Disability Benefits (ISP-1151) form from the Application kit for Canada Pension Plan Disability benefits; An Application for a Canada Pension Plan Post-Retirement Disability Benefit (ISP-1170) form; A Terminal Illness Application for Disability Benefits under the Canada Pension Plan (ISP-2530A) form from the Terminal Illness Application Kit for Disability Benefits under the Canada Pension Plan ; or A written request for CPPD benefits. CPPD supporting forms Forms to support a CPPD benefits application include: the Questionnaire for Disability Benefits - Canada Pension Plan (ISP-2507) form; the Consent for Service Canada to Collect Personal Information (ISP-2502) form; or the consent embedded within the Medical Report for Canada Pension Plan Disability Benefits (ISP-2519) form; and the consent embedded within the Terminal Illness Medical Attestation for a Disability Benefits Application under the Canada Pension Plan (ISP-2530B) form from the Terminal Illness Application Kit for a Disability Benefits under the Canada Pension Plan strong>. CPPD supporting forms require the applicant's or the applicant's legal representative's signature for date protection. The ISP-2507 and ISP-2502 forms that are part of older CPPD benefits application kits are stand-alone forms. These stand-alone forms are not applications because they do not contain a declaration that they are an application for CPPD benefits and are considered supporting forms. If these supporting CPPD forms are signed and received first, they can conditionally protect the date of receipt of the CPPD benefits application only when a valid CPPD benefits application is subsequently received within the allotted time frames. For date protection, a photocopy, fax or scan of the supporting form with signature is acceptable. If there is no signature on the supporting form, it cannot be used to date-protect the application. CPP pension or benefit Date stamps on requests and applications for CPP Credit Splitting are treated differently from other applications. The date stamp is not used to protect the retroactivity of payment of benefits, but it does determine the date that pension credits are attributed to both parties. The only time that a date stamp on a credit splitting application or request affects eligibility is when there is a time limit in which to submit the request or application. This occurs in cases of separation of common-law partners, or legal spouses where one of them has died. In such cases, the date stamp will only protect the application date for a period of one year from the date indicated on the stamp. QPP application When an application for a CPP pension or benefit is received by a Retraite Quebec centre, it is date-protected for CPP retroactivity purposes to the date that it was received in that office. A QPP application that is received by the Department that demonstrates the applicant's intent to apply for the equivalent CPP benefit will date-protect the CPP benefit. ALW and ALWS benefits The date stamp on any signed initial application for the GIS or on a signed Statement of Income can conditionally protect the date of application for the ALW or ALWS benefit for an applicant, their spouse, or their common-law partner. This date stamp therefore protects the retroactivity of the individual's benefit entitlement. The statement of income form must be completed by both OAS pensioners and their spouse or common-law partner, both must have signed it. The signed ALW or ALWS application must be received within the required time frame to be considered date protected. If it is not received within this time frame, it cannot be used to date protect the GIS statement of income date. Applications received after the required time frame will not be considered date protected and regular processing rules will apply, meaning only 11 months from the date stamp on the ALW or ALWS application.

topic_title: How long is the date stamp valid?
text: A date stamp on a valid application protects the date of application for all benefits included on the application (e.g. Children's benefits included on a CPPD benefits application) until the final decision is made on that application. This includes decisions made at reconsideration and appeal levels. When the final decision is made, the date stamp cannot be used to protect the date of receipt for subsequent applications that are received by the Department. Applications that are not valid have no rights to reconsideration; when the file has been administratively closed, the date stamp can no longer be used as a protective date for future applications.

Surname field includes multiple names in one record (often a middle name). Change to the client’s surname due to the start or end of a marriage or common-law relationship. Typographical error in the date of birth field (e.g. year and month are reversed or day and month are reversed). You can then use the CRA income information to renew the income-tested benefit.

The evidence required to establish the conditions of eligibility include the following: The contributor is deceased. The contributor has unadjusted pensionable earnings for the minimum qualifying period. The child is the child of the deceased contributor. In addition to being the deceased contributor's child, the child must be the dependent child of the deceased contributor. An application for the benefit is submitted in the prescribed manner and at the prescribed location. Applications for a Surviving Child's benefit may be made by: the surviving parent for a child under the age of 18 (-18 child), if the child is under their decision-making responsibility; the person or agency having decision-making responsibility of the -18 child; the child who has reached the age of 18; or a surviving -18 child in exceptional circumstances. If the child is aged 18 (+18 child) or over but less than the age of 25, they must also submit a CPP Child's Benefit Application and Declaration for a Student Over 18 years of age in Attendance at School or University (ISP-1402) form to confirm full-time or part-time attendance at school.

The CPP Surviving Child's benefit is a monthly flat-rate benefit which is adjusted annually. The CPP pays benefits to dependent children of deceased contributors provided they meet the specified eligibility requirements.
Canada Pension Plan Section 74(2)—Commencement of payment of benefit

For Children under age 18 , the surviving child’s benefit begins the later of : the month after the contributor’s death; the month after the child is born; the 11th month before the month the application is received; or For Children who are 18 to 25 years of age and attending school on a full-time or part-time basis, the surviving child’s benefit begins the later of : the month after the contributor’s death; the 11th month before the month the children’s benefit application is received; or the month in which classes begin (a school vacation may be considered part of the full-time or part-time attendance class period). The date of application is protected for all children who are identified on a CPP Survivor’s pension application, in addition children over the age of 18 must submit their own application within the prescribed timeframes. A written request applying for a children’s benefit which contains all the required information is also acceptable. You may also find the following other User ID s for IA Legacy system converted data: IACPP MERGE for data moved to the History screen by the Merge process (i.e. if 2 pieces of data existed for a client for both Source IA and Source CPP when the accounts were merged into 1 Source CPP client). These benefits have Super Program Exception Process (PEP) status and will not recalculate except for yearly escalation. You can modify the Data Capture Session for these accounts if required. Post-Retirement Benefit ( PRB ) Post-Retirement Benefits in IA Legacy system were added to the RTR pension amount and identified with a PRB Indicator. At IA migration, all existing accounts with a PRB indicator were manually updated to remove the PRB amount from the RTR amount. Then, ITRDS automatically calculated the PRB . Arrears payments generated in CPMS as a result were suspended. PRBs are the only benefits from IA Legacy system which were not put in Super PEP status. After IA migration, ITRDS will automatically adjudicate new PRB for CPP-IA clients. Child Rearing Provision (CRP) information CRP is not recorded in the IA Legacy system. For this reason, no data conversion occurred for the CRP. Upon verification, CRP information can be entered if necessary. Instead, this data will be available in CPMS on the Archived IA Payment History screen. Since Release 4 (November 2003), payment details and history have been available in the ITRDS . Before Release 4, this information had not been loaded into the Enterprise Database. The priority payment date will not be visible on the ITRDS . Calculation and Recalculation for OAS/GIS/SPA 1I5 IA - I.M.F. Account Enquiry 1S1 ROECIS - INQUIRY MENU 1S2 ROECIS - RELEASE MENU 1S3 ROECIS - FORM LETTER MENU 1S4 ROECIS - DATA INVESTIGATION MENU 1S5 ROECIS - BROWSE RELEASES 1S6 ROECIS - MAINTAIN USER ACCESS TABLE 1T7 Payment History and Tax Information 3A OAS DATA CAPTURE Substituted value Certain data that may not have been present in the Legacy system but would have been used to pay the benefit is required in ITRDS for adjudication. According to the prescribed rule above, substituted value is data that the conversion program has contained in the ITRDS conversion program and placed in fields on client accounts. For more information, go to the Explanation of Substituted or Derived Converted Values section below. Example of a substituted value: A proof of a child-contributor relationship would exist where the Child's benefit is paid in the IA Legacy system, but the Legacy system does not record the type of relationship. ITRDS requires a valid relationship for rules-based adjudication. Therefore, on the Interrelationships screen, the value Child , Valid Custody will be substituted as the Relationship. If you try to modify any data on that interrelationship in ITRDS , you must select a valid relationship from the drop down (e.g. Natural , Legally Adopted ). Derived value In other instances, ITRDS requires data for adjudication because it is not available in the IA Legacy system and ITRDS is not able to populate a substituted value. In these cases, ITRDS uses existing data to derive data. A derived value is a value that the conversion program has calculated based on information available on the account. For more information, go to the Explanation of Substituted or Derived Converted Values section below. Example of a derived value: ITRDS requires the start date of an interrelationship between a deceased contributor and a surviving child to data capture a surviving child's benefit; ITRDS derives a start date equal to the child's date of birth, since the actual start date of the interrelationship is not recorded in the Legacy system. The Interrelationships screen displays this date as Start Date . +18 children—child's last name In the IA Legacy system, the child's last name was not stored as part of the contributor's account but it was possible to record a payee name. When the information was converted from the IA Legacy system, the contributor's last name was defaulted as the child's last name. If the child has a different last name, you can update this information on the Modify Client Profile screen. The last name provided by the child on the Canada Pension Plan Child's Benefit Application and Declaration for a Student Over 18 Years of Age in Attendance at School or University (ISP-1402) form is considered as sufficient evidence. If you have reason to question the name provided by the child, you may: verify previous payments; or search for a Social Insurance Registry record for the child to confirm the last name. The hard file containing the original application may also be requested. Interrelationships In the IA Legacy system, the benefit and client information were accessed through the contributor's account. The interrelationship existed if related benefits (i.e. SVR pension, Disabled Contributor's Child Benefit ( DCCB ) and Surviving Child's benefits were present). In ITRDS , these interrelationships are more defined, but the required detail was not always available in the IA Master File. At IA migration, no interrelationship data was converted or derived. Interrelationship data such as relationship types and start or end dates are derived from existing information. For children's interrelationships, the start date is set as the child's date of birth and the type of relationship as Parent , Valid Custody . The data requires updating only if it results in incorrect adjudication (i.e. the child-contributor relationship began after the child's birth). Processing the majority of ISP1402 forms does not result in any modifications to the Interrelationships section. School attendance periods School start and end dates from IA Legacy system (i.e. DT str: and End: ) are already available for review in ITRDS on the School Declaration screen. No conversion was necessary for this data. Entering the school end date lets you enter the future end date of a +18 benefit. The school end date is updated when the benefit is terminated.

topic_title: Interpreting Converted Data on ITRDS Screens (Work Tool)
text: At ITRDS Release 21, every CPP benefit contained in the International Agreements (IA) Legacy system was converted to ITRDS , regardless of account or benefit status. In past releases (i.e. for ITRDS Release 7.0) the data conversion program either substituted or derived a value for data that was not available in the Legacy system but was required to perform adjudication in ITRDS . The substituted or derived value was inserted into the applicable account record in ITRDS . For more information on substituted or derived data, refer to version 1.0 of this procedure. As all CPP International Operations accounts will be processed using the Super Program Exception Process functionality, which bypasses the ITRDS adjudication process, there is no requirement to substitute or derive a value for any missing data from the IA Legacy system. Only data available in the IA Legacy system will be converted to ITRDS . You must ensure that you review, verify and update all available data on the CPP-IA client's account and any related accounts before adjudication.
