topic_title: OAS pension and benefits applications Updated
text: An application for an OAS pension and benefits can be made on the Department's prescribed form. In certain circumstances, an application is not required, i.e. when it is waived under the OAS automatic enrolment process or when another acceptable form has been submitted. Refer to: Eligibility Requirements—Automatic Enrolment (Policy) ; and Eligibility Requirements—Automatic Enrolment (Policy) Eligibility Requirements—GIS New Business (Policy) (go to the section GIS application form and the statement of income ). Eligibility Requirements—GIS New Business (Policy)

A valid application for OAS purposes is a departmental OAS pension application form with the applicant's signature. A valid application for CPP benefits is a departmental application form or a written request that clearly identifies the applicant, the CPP benefits requested and the applicant's signature. OAS and CPP provisions are not considered applications. OAS options are considered a statement, while CPP provisions are considered a request.

The signature on an application is required to confirm intent to apply, authenticate the identity of the applicant for integrity purposes, and to validate the applicant's declaration that the information they have provided in their application is true and complete. A signature also provides evidence of the applicant's intent to be legally bound by the content of the application. The signature also confirms that the applicant accepts the obligations for the receipt of the benefit, e.g. the responsibility to report income. An unsigned application protects the effective start date of the benefit. However, payments will not be made until a signed application is received. A signed application includes the following signed documents: an original; a certified true copy; or a photocopy received by mail, fax or email with scan. A certified true copy or original application does not need to be requested in cases where a signed photocopy, an email with scan or a fax is received. A wet signature is not required, unless the validity of the application or the signature is in question. When an applicant submits a completed and signed application form that is uploaded or scanned and emailed to the Department, it is an electronic document and subject to the Department of Employment and Social Development Act and the Electronic Documents and Electronic Information Regulations. For it to be accepted, it must: be sufficiently readable to be usable for subsequent reference; be in a format that does not prevent it from being retained; and have the time and date of receipt recorded by the system used to accept the transmitted document. If the Department receives the signed application on, or before the applicant's death, the application is considered a valid application that can be processed post-mortem.

If the applicant cannot sign their name, a mark on the application, e.g. an "X", thumbprint or other symbol, that is duly witnessed will be considered a signature. The application form provides further instructions on how a mark should be made and witnessed.

topic_title: Valid applications with insufficient or missing information or documentation
text: When a valid application is received, a decision must be made. If, after reasonable attempts have been made to obtain further information or documentation, an applicant fails to provide the information required to prove they are eligible to receive the requested benefits, a decision must be made using the information provided. If an applicant can prove eligibility for benefits for a period or portion of entitlement, that period or portion can be approved. For example, this applies when determining: residence under the OAS program, e.g. paying a partial pension or benefit; income for periods of OAS income-tested benefit entitlement; periods of custody and control for CPP children's benefits; periods of school attendance for CPP children's benefits; cohabitation periods for CPP credit splitting and pension sharing; Child Rearing Provision periods; and periods of incapacity for CPP and OAS pensions and benefits. If the decision is to deny the benefit, the reason for denial provided in the letter must indicate which specific criteria were not met, and note that information or documentation is missing, if applicable. Reconsideration rights are included when a valid application for a benefit has been received. Refer to the appropriate benefit, pension or provision for the applicable eligibility requirements.

DARS was developed in the 1990s as a single cross-program account receivable and collection system for debts owed to and recovered by the Department. Due to the age of this system, it was not adaptable to the current modern business environment and had to be replaced. The PSCD system will modernize and enhance the processing of the Department's receivables to increase functionality and meet the growing needs of the Department.

As of April 6, 2021, the following processes are changing for CPP staff only: You will no longer record and apply cash receipts in CPMS. The Chief Financial Officer Branch will now be responsible for applying incoming payments to all CPP receivables in PSCD. Once processed in PSCD, the information will feed back to CPMS automatically. incoming payments You will no longer use Manual Priority Payments to issue refunds to clients for over-recovery. Refunds will be managed in PSCD by the CFOB - National Accounts Receivable (NAR) unit. NAR will check the ITRDS, CPMS, OAS Online and IA systems to ensure there are no overpayments before refunding the client; Manual Priority Payments You will no longer add and approve remissions in CPMS. Once CFOB receives and processes the information in PSCD, it will feed back into CPMS automatically; and remissions You may need to request a lock to be placed on certain debts if there is a reconsideration or an appeal on the account or if it is under investigation to stop Canada Revenue Agency from collecting. request a lock In addition, the following processes will impact CPP, OAS and International Operations staff: You will no longer remit overpayment balances remaining after a compromise settlement , a bankruptcy discharge is granted or a consumer proposal is closed . You will request a write-off from the CFOB to have these balances permanently removed. compromise settlement bankruptcy discharge is granted or a consumer proposal is closed write-off The Remission and Write-Off Authority Reason Codes have been updated to align with PSCD. Effective April 6, 2021, the Public Sector Colle ctions and Disbursements (PSCD) system replaces the Departmental Accounts Receivable System (DARS) and will manage all CPP Departmental receivables. All new CPP receivables and adjustments calculated in CPMS will now be sent to PSCD as part of a daily interface. In addition, receivable (overpayment) information from client accounts in the OAS Online and the International Agreements systems can, however, be manually added by the Chief Financial Officer Branch (CFOB) to PSCD when: the receivable arises due to a conviction of fraud; the Integrity Services Branch determines there has been misrepresentation; or a garnishment is being applied to a debt. For more information, Public Sector Collections and Disbursements System The following receivables will be managed in PSCD: CPP active and inactive accounts; CPP and OAS active and inactive accounts with penalties, including those paid under an International Social Security Agreement (ISSA); CPP and OAS active and inactive fraud accounts, including those paid under an ISSA; and CPP and OAS debts where a garnishment is being collected, including those paid under an ISSA.

As of May 28, 2021, individuals can apply for ALW and ALWS benefits online through My Service Canada Account portal if they: are aged 59 + 1 month to age 65 + 11 months; and do not have a third party representative (trustee or power of attorney) on file. If any of the above criteria are not met, the applicant is directed to an "Unable to continue" page indicating why they cannot apply online. The message offers a "contact us" link that points to the Department's website and provides contact information, as well as information on how to submit a paper application. If all of the above criteria are met, the applicant can complete and submit their application online. Domestic addresses and telephone number updates through the online application are captured directly into ITRDS . Applicants with a foreign address on file are advised that an incorrect address may result in payment or follow-up letters not being delivered correctly. They are advised to contact the Department to update their address information before using the online service. When an individual applies online, the information is captured in a date stamped PDF file and applicants are presented with a confirmation page. The confirmation page contains the following information: the applicant's name; the date and time stamp; a list of documents that the applicant is requested to submit as supporting evidence based on answers they provided on the application (e.g. legal status, marital status, immigration); the address of the mail processing centre where the documentation must be sent; a phone number for foreign residents to provide direct deposit information and a link to the applicable direct deposit form; and for ALWS benefit applications, information regarding the CPP Survivor's pension and Death benefit. Where the applicant is required to mail in supporting documentation (e.g. legal status, marital status), they are advised to: attach the documentation to either: a printed confirmation page; or a separate piece of paper that includes their name and social insurance number; or mail everything to the appropriate regional mail processing centre.
There are no exceptions or special cases. (KA-01098 Snippet 12.0 content. Do not modify or delete.)

When an individual is applying online for an ALW benefit, their spouse or common-law partner must provide consent to obtain their information from the Canada Revenue Agency ( CRA ) and declare that the information provided about them is true. The spouse or common-law partner's consent and declaration are considered obtained through their GIS application process if: the details of their marital status match the information provided on the online ALW benefit application you are processing; the CRA Marital Status flag and the CRA Spousal SIN found on the CRA Income ( CRA ) screen in OAS Online, match the information provided, if available; and one of the following conditions are met: both spouses or common-law partners have signed a previously submitted paper OAS / GIS or paper GIS application; the spouse or common-law partner previously submitted an online OAS / GIS or online GIS application and a signed Spousal Consent and Declaration (ISS0954) letter or a Spousal Consent and Declaration GIS (ISS0954A) letter was received; the spouse or common-law partner has been approved for automatic enrolment of the GIS (i.e. the process is not in Pending status); or the spouse or common-law partner has also submitted an online OAS / GIS or online GIS application that is being processed at the same time as the applicant's online ALW benefit application. If there are any discrepancies between the information provided in the spouse or common-law partner's GIS application process, the CRA Income ( CRA ) screen, and the information provided in the online ALW benefit application you are processing affecting eligibility and entitlement, they must be resolved according to regular procedures, before processing the online ALW application. If the spouse or common-law partner's consent and declaration have not been obtained through the GIS application process, this consent can be obtained by sending the Spousal Consent and Declaration ALW (ISS0954B) letter to the spouse or common-law partner to complete. The ISS954B letter allows the spouse or common-law partner to provide: confirmation that the information provided on their behalf is correct; and consent for the Department to request and use their CRA income information to determine their spouse or common-law partner's entitlement for the ALW benefit. If all other eligibility criteria are met, the online application can be approved without the consent and declaration from the spouse or common-law partner; however, the applicant's ALW benefit entitlement cannot be calculated until the consent and declaration are received from the spouse or common-law partner.
This procedure provides the guidance necessary to retrieve and process an online ALW or ALWS benefit application.

topic_title: Accommodated and sheltered or inclusive employment
text: Accommodation allows applicants or beneficiaries with disabilities to participate fully in the workplace. An example of accommodation can include a flexible schedule or fewer work hours than others are afforded. Use the same approach for these applicants or beneficiaries when assessing work activity as any applicant or beneficiary with paid work. For an example of workplace accommodations , go to example 1 in the Case Examples section below. Accommodated work is different from sheltered or inclusive work, which is for therapeutic reasons to keep a social connection, rather than provide an income. Sheltered or inclusive work is an exception occurring in rare circumstances.

Once you have established work activity (hours and predictability of attendance) and earnings, look at them in combination to determine the overall work capacity. The more hours and earnings an applicant or beneficiary has, the more it increases the likelihood the applicant or beneficiary is demonstrating work capacity. For an example of assessment of overall work capacity , go to the Case Examples section above. Scenarios for assessing work capacity Table 3. Scenarios for assessing work capacity Work activity (predictability of attendance + hours of work) Earnings Scenario Less than 15 hours per week Below the Substantially Gainful Occupation (SGO) benchmark A 32-year-old applicant or beneficiary works at a boutique clothing store 12 hours a week. Attends scheduled shifts regularly but cannot increase hours due to child rearing reasons. Holistic review Diagnosis: Noninsulin-dependent diabetes mellitus and recent decreased renal function. Experiences mild fatigue. Has specialist appointments every 6 months. While there are limitations from the medical condition, work hours are predictable. The reason for low hours of work is due to personal choice. Outcome The information shows this applicant or beneficiary is demonstrating work capacity. Less than 15 hours per week Above the SGO benchmark A 40-year-old applicant or beneficiary with diabetes and decreased renal function works as a lawyer 12 hours a week. Review The applicant or beneficiary maintains 12 hours per week regularly and is predictable in attendance. Earnings are above the SGO benchmark. There has been no recent changes in hours of work. Outcome The information shows they are demonstrating work capacity. Between 15 and 30 hours a week Below the SGO benchmark A 45-year-old applicant or beneficiary works 25 hours at a grocery store. The employer cannot offer more than 25 hours but accommodates with night shifts. Attends night shifts regularly. Holistic review Diagnosis: Schizophrenia with social anxiety. Recently diagnosed but currently stable on medications. Unable to work with the public. Can only work nights due to social anxiety. One month of work was missed due to the illness. The employer offers workplace accommodation of working night shifts and confirms that attendance is regular and predictable. Outcome While earnings are below SGO, working 25 hours a week is demonstrating work capacity. The limited hours are due to availability of work, not from the medical conditions and functional limitations. Over 30 hours a week Above the SGO benchmark A 52-year-old office worker suffers from chronic pain from a back surgery. Works 37.5 hours a week. Uses a sit-stand desk and can work from home 3 days a week. Flexibility for breaks. Review Works over 30 hours a week and is able to be predictable in attendance through workplace accommodations. Though earnings are noted to be above SGO, work capacity is demonstrated through work activity alone. Outcome The employer is able to accommodate the worker to work within their functional limitations. This demonstrates work capacity. Between 15 and 30 hours a week Above the SGO benchmark A 32-year-old applicant or beneficiary works at a boutique clothing store 16 hours a week. Work attendance is not reliable due to time off for treatments and symptoms. Employer is accommodating as the beneficiary has been with the company for many years prior to the disability. Holistic assessment Diagnosis: End-stage renal failure with a history of insulin-dependent diabetes. Receives hemodialysis 3 days a week and is on the transplant list. Experiences constant moderate fatigue. Outcome Earnings are above the SGO benchmark, but the work activity is not predictable. However, the employer is accommodating the unpredictable schedule. The evidence supports the work is accommodated, so the beneficiary is able to participate in the workplace and demonstrate work capacity. Above 30 hours per week but unpredictable 2 or more years at or above the SGO benchmark 40-year-old applicant or beneficiary with multiple sclerosis works at an information technology help desk. Returned to work after child-rearing years with 3 years of earnings after the LPDOO. Review Works 30 hours a week but due to the medical condition, she frequently missed work. Experience flare-ups resulting in temporary blindness, leading to periods of time missing work. The pattern of relapses is every 2 years. All three years of earnings after the LPDOO were above the SGO benchmark. Outcome While the applicant or beneficiary has relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis causing periods of unpredictable attendance to work, the presence of 2 or more years above the SGO benchmark is an indicator of work capacity.

Assess hours and predictability of attendance to establish work activity. The following provides a general framework to assess work activity by evaluating hours of work and predictability of attendance. Assess hours and predictablity of attendance Review the file or call the applicant or beneficiary to assess: the actual average hours of work per week they have been able to attend; any workplace accommodations; and their ability to attend work on a regular basis: have their hours changed? have they missed work and why? Assess hours of work When assessing hours of work, it is important to establish actual hours worked versus scheduled hours, as absences due to illness could be disguised through paid leave arrangements such as vacation leave, etc. Do not consider other factors such as availability of work, labour market conditions, or lifestyle choice. While these may result in limited hours, they are not related to the functional limitations from the medical condition. Assess predictability of attendance Determine if their attendance is predictable. The information on file may state that they are scheduled to work a certain number of hours a week (e.g. 29 hours) but if the attendance is unpredictable due to functional limitations from a medical condition, then the hours do not support work activity. Predictability in attendance supports the ability to regularly pursue work. Work activity may be predictable . Below are some indicators to consider when establishing the predictability of work activity: Table 1. Indicators of predictable work activity WHEN WHY Working scheduled shifts for periods of months or years. Demonstrates the applicant or beneficiary is able to consistently report to work as required and meets the expectations of the job. Little or no absences related to the medical condition. Demonstrates that the medical condition is not affecting the applicant or beneficiary's ability to report to work on a regular basis, or that no medical intervention is required (tests, appointments, etc.). A medical professional provides clearance for a return to work approving medical capacity for work. Demonstrates the medical professional does not identify any functional limitations that would prevent the applicant or beneficiary from working on a regular basis. A self-employed applicant or beneficiary continues to perform their business responsibilities. Responsibility for the day-to-day operations to maintain the business demonstrates predictability. Work accommodations allow regular attendance which may not be possible without the accommodation. While the accommodation may be the reason for success in predictable attendance, it demonstrates the ability to do some type of work within their limitations. A seasonal worker applies while working but the season ends shortly after the Date of Application but they were able to regularly attend work and complete the season. Demonstrates predictability during work with no indication of functional limitations from the medical condition preventing the ability to work during the season or at the time of decision. Work or work-like activity may be unpredictable: Table 2. Indicators of unpredictable work activity WHEN WHY Periods of absence are related to functional limitations from the medical condition. Demonstrates frequent follow-up (tests, appointments) or symptoms causing functional limitations from the medical condition, which may interfere with predictability of attendance. The medical condition has sporadic or cyclical flare-ups (e.g. mental health disorder, multiple sclerosis). Demonstrates the functional limitations from the medical condition may interfere with predictability of attendance. Assess work activity Determine the presence of work activity: If you cannot establish the presence of work activity, complete a holistic assessment . If you can establish work activity (work hours are predictable), refer to the following guide to view how the hours relate to work capacity: Work activity assessment guidance If work activity hours are: Then: less than 15 hours per week Applicants or beneficiaries participating in paid employment less than 15 hours per week are usually not demonstrating work capacity. Further assessment is required. If work activity hours are: Then: between 15 and 30 hours per week Applicants or beneficiaries participating in paid employment between 15 and 30 hours per week may be demonstrating work capacity. Further assessment is recommended. If work activity hours are: Then: over 30 hours per week Individuals participating in paid employment over 30 hours per week are likely demonstrating work capacity, unless the evidence on file supports otherwise.

Workplace accommodations Scenario 1 Scenario 2 Assessment A police officer with a diagnosis of post-traumatic stress disorder returns to work with medical accommodations for non-operational duties of office work with no direct contact with the public and no requirement for the use of a personal firearm. These accommodations are longstanding unless changed by attending health practitioners. A fast-food worker with chronic pain is scheduled for shifts in the drive-thru taking orders. This accommodates the need for the worker to switch from sitting to standing. The employer also gives the worker shifts earlier in the day with frequent breaks. Determine their work capacity by assessing work activity (predictability and hours of employment) and earnings. If earnings are below the Substantially Gainful Occupation (SGO) benchmark and hours are below 30 hours a week, complete a holistic assessment. Assessment of overall work capacity Scenario Assessment A 35-year-old applicant or beneficiary with high school education works as a customer service representative. He has a diagnosis of severe Crohn's disease resistant to multiple biological agents, a history of multiple bowel resections with frequent bowel movements, and secondary arthritis affecting both knees. He reported a return to work in September 2025 after reaching allowable earnings of $7,100.00. He earned $11.50 per hour working 12 to 15 hours per week (gross earnings of $690.00 per month, which is below monthly SGO). Attempts to increase hours of work have been unsuccessful due to significant fatigue and arthritic pain. Accessibility to a washroom is not always possible when providing client service. Work attendance is under review due to frequent sick leaves for illness and frequent medical appointments. Unless the beneficiary is able to increase the number of hours worked, it is reasonable to continue the benefit. He will continue to meet the eligibility criteria for CPPD benefits based on hours of work at or below 15 hours per week, below SGO earnings and the demonstrated limited work capacity. Evaluate the potential for a vocational rehabilitation referral due to the beneficiary's young age and motivation to return to work. The beneficiary would be advised during personal communication and a decision letter of his responsibility to notify the Department if there are changes to the work activity (i.e. increase in the hours of work, or salary) or medical condition. Income without work activity (self-employment) Scenario Assessment A 61-year-old applicant or beneficiary with a diagnosis of Parkinson's disease works as a fisherman. The applicant or beneficiary owns a business with above SGO gross earnings. He indicates on his application that he is self-employed and will declare as a self-employed person for income tax purposes but does not list a Date Stopped Work. After developing for more information, it was discovered he owns a fishing enterprise. The business is a family-run enterprise that remains in the applicant's name only, and as the original owner of the business. He has a profit-sharing agreement in place with his sons, which explains the earnings. The applicant has no roles or responsibility in the business; his sons maintain the business. Medical reports indicate the applicant has advanced Parkinson's disease and despite earnings above the SGO benchmark, he has no work activity. The medical condition is advanced and progressive in nature with significant mobility impairment. This precludes him from engaging in any employment and this was evidenced by the medical information and the self-employment questionnaire. This information supports the applicant is demonstrating no work capacity.

If after considering all of the evidence, a decision cannot be made regarding eligibility or continuing eligibility for a CPP disability benefit, further assessment is required through consultation. Send an enquiry to receive further instructions. Go to the Enquiries section below. Enquiries

Work may be evident when: the application states that the applicant is still working; income is posted on ITRDS ; a triggered reassessment occurs; or a beneficiary self-reports a return to work or work-like activity. Income can be from reasons other than work, such as a payout. Ensure earnings are from work activity to determine work capacity.

topic_title: Is the applicant or beneficiary self-employed?
text: Assess the Client's Self-Employment Work Capacity (Action)

Paid employment includes regular employment, self-employment, seasonal and accommodated work. This applies to: applicants: at or after the date of application; at the Latest Possible Date of Onset (LPDOO) for late applicants; or with valid earnings after the LPDOO. beneficiaries: who report a return to work, including seasonal work; or with work or work-like (i.e. educational or volunteer) activity or earnings discovered post-grant. Work capacity Work capacity consists of two indicators: Work or work-like (i.e. educational or volunteer) activity, which is determined through hours and predictability of attendance; and Gross earnings from employment or gross business earnings from self-employment. While both indicators of work capacity are reviewed and described in the rationale, work capacity can be demonstrated by either work, work-like activity or income earned for work activity, or both. Work Activity To ensure the applicant or beneficiary is engaged in work or work-like activity, a review of hours and predictability of attendance is required. Hours It is important to assess what the reported hours of work or work-like activity means in the context of the applicant or beneficiary. If an applicant or beneficiary is only working or participating in work-like activity a few hours of work each week (e.g. less than 15 hours) this may be all they can manage due to the functional limitations from the medical condition, but it may also be an indication of lifestyle choices, seasonal employment or other factors such as labour market conditions. Applicants or beneficiaries working or participating in work-like activity more than 30 hours per week are likely exhibiting work capacity. Predictability of attendance Predictability of attendance demonstrates the applicant or beneficiary's ability to regularly pursue work or work-like activity. The ability to regularly pursue work or work-like activity means the applicant or beneficiary is reliable and dependable in attending the workplace, volunteer activity or educational activity. If predictability is not evident on file or through a phone conversation with the applicant or beneficiary, development for medical, employment, volunteer or educational information may be necessary. Absences need to be explored to determine if they are due to the medical condition or other factors, such as lack of childcare. Self-employment and accommodated jobs may allow for flexibility to the work schedule. Flexibility should not be considered as unpredictable work. An applicant or beneficiary with an unpredictable medical condition may have periods of time where they are unable to work; however, they may have patterns of earnings over a sustained period. Earnings at or above the substantially gainful occupation amount (SGO) in 2 or more consecutive years usually demonstrate regular capacity for work. Earnings For the purposes of this guidance, earnings refer to a payment an employee or self-employed applicant or beneficiary receives for services provided. When assessing an applicant or beneficiary's earnings from regular employment, you must use their gross earnings. For self-employment, you must use their gross business earnings. Earnings above the maximum annual amount an applicant or beneficiary could receive as a disability benefit defines an SGO. This benchmark is consistent and transparent for the Department, Social Security Tribunal, courts and CPP disability applicants and beneficiaries, which allows for equitable treatment. While increasing earnings may indicate increasing work capacity, decreasing earnings may not indicate decreasing work capacity. Decreasing earnings may be related to lifestyle choice rather than functional limitations from the medical condition. During adjudication, determine whether the applicant or beneficiary is earning below or above the SGO benchmark. Holistic review Once you establish work activity and earnings, if the earnings are below the SGO benchmark or the hours per week are under 30 hours, a holistic assessment may need to occur. A holistic assessment can include a review of the following items: work history such as multiple employers; earnings history to identify gaps or changes; patterns in the work activity such as repetitive seasonal work; the medical condition(s); the functional limitation(s) and their impact on the applicant or beneficiary's ability to work; and personal characteristics.

Rationale when work is demonstrative of work capacity Consider the applicant or beneficiary has work capacity when: work activity is between 15 and 30 hours per week and there is predictability of attendance; earnings are above Substantially Gainful Occupation (SGO) from work activity; or both. Even though work capacity can be determined with either the work activity or earnings alone, the rationale needs to refer to both indicators of work capacity. When writing the rationale, refer to: hours of work and predictability of attendance; and earnings. Rationale when work is not demonstrative of work capacity If a decision cannot be made with the work activity and earnings, ensure that the rationale explains how the following were considered and factored in your decision: Work activity (hours and predictability) Earnings below the SGO benchmark Functional limitations related to the medical conditions Personal characteristics
There is no reference material. (KA-01423 Snippet 14.0 content. Do not modify or delete.)

When an applicant or beneficiary is working under 30 hours a week, continue the assessment of work capacity by reviewing earnings. Earnings from work activity above the Substantially Gainful Occupation (SGO) level likely indicate work capacity on a predictable basis, unless there is evidence that supports otherwise. Review gross earnings or gross business earnings from work activity for all employment income. For applicants with valid earnings after the Latest Possible Date of Onset (LPDOO) and beneficiaries during a triggered reassessment, check the ITRDS earnings screen. For applicants with a current LPDOO and beneficiaries who report their return to work, obtain their current earnings. Determine if earnings from work activity are above or below SGO benchmark. If earnings are above SGO benchmark: consider that work capacity is likely being demonstrated; and make a decision. If earnings are below SGO benchmark, complete a holistic assessment. The decision should reflect that earnings above the SGO benchmark likely support work capacity, even if the hours are under 15 hours a week. You have established the earnings are from work activity through hours and predictability of attendance. For earnings below the SGO benchmark, consider the following: If the reason is due to: then the likely relation to work capacity is: personal preference; or labour market conditions. unrelated—it is not due to the functional limitations from the medical condition. If the reason is due to: then the likely relation to work capacity is: functional limitations from the medical conditions in combination with: personal characteristics; required treatments; multiple failed work attempts due to functional limitations from the medical conditions; or the nature and progression of the medical conditions. related—it is due to the functional limitations from the medical condition—requires a holistic assessment.

Seasonal work is assessed the same as any applicant or beneficiary in paid work by reviewing earnings and predictability of attendance. If the applicant or beneficiary stopped working, you need to determine if the work activity was aligned with the season or due to any functional limitations from a medical condition or a combination of both. For assessing self-reported seasonal employment, Assess Self-Reported Seasonal Employment at Reassessment (Action) For more information, refer to policy Severe Criterion—Work Activity and Earnings (Policy)

A self-employed applicant or beneficiary is assessed the same as applicants or beneficiaries working for an employer with minor differences due to the nature of the work. Review the work activity hours that lead to producing a product or service for the purpose of generating income. Review the gross business earnings from the work activity. For more information, refer to Assess the Client's Self-Employment Work Capacity in addition to this guidance. Assess the Client's Self-Employment Work Capacity For an example of self-employment , go to example 3 in the Case Examples section below. For more information, Severe Criterion—Work Activity and Earnings (Policy)

Sheltered or inclusive work is an exception occurring in rare circumstances. This is a highly supportive work environment with no or significantly low pay. While hours and predictability may be met, this alone does not demonstrate work capacity. If identification of sheltered or inclusive work requires further assessment, Severe Criterion―Impact of Medical Condition(s) and Functional Limitations on Work Capacity (Scenario)

The severe criterion for the CPPD benefit is met when an applicant or beneficiary's medical condition causes functional limitations preventing them from regularly pursuing any substantially gainful occupation. When applicants and beneficiaries are engaged in paid work, the focus is on the work activity and earnings. The medical adjudicator determines if the work activity and earnings support their capacity to work. Paid work consists of regular employment, self-employment, seasonal and accommodated work.

As of November 2019, individuals can apply for the OAS pension or the OAS pension and GIS together online through the My Service Canada Account portal if they: are aged 64 + 1 month or older; are not already in pay or pending for the OAS pension; are a Canadian resident (have no current foreign address on file); and do not have a third party representative (trustee or power of attorney) on file. If any of the above criteria are not met, the applicant will receive a message indicating that they are unable to apply online along with the reason. If all of the above criteria are met, the applicant can complete and submit their application online. Domestic addresses and telephone number updates through the online application are captured directly into ITRDS . When an individual applies online, the information is stored in an internal database within our Department, Government On-Line (GOL) Support Services. An individual can submit multiple online applications for the OAS pension or for the OAS pension and the GIS combined. All submitted applications are stored in the GOL Support Services database indefinitely. The system reads the home postal code the applicant enters and determines where the online application should be sent for processing. The address of the appropriate mail processing centre is recorded in the GOL Support Services database.
There are no exceptions or special cases. (KA-01098 Snippet 12.0 content. Do not modify or delete.)

Review PWS to identify and retrieve any correspondence items related to the applicant that have been received. Place any correspondence items related to the application into the folder. Change the status of all items in PWS that have been matched to the folder to Complete . Repeat these steps for all future incoming correspondence. After the online application has been processed and no further actions are necessary. Change the status of the online application work item in PWS to Complete . OAS and GIS Application—Details screen The OAS and GIS Application—Details screen in Government On-Line (GOL) is the first screen you will be presented with to view an applicant's application details. This screen contains all of the information the applicant submitted on their online application in a question and answer format in the order in which you will use to enter it into the OAS Online System when creating a client record. While the OAS and GIS Application—Details screen looks very different from the standard paper application, the information is generally the same as in a standard paper application. A list of documents will be displayed at the bottom of the screen, if applicable. The applicant must submit these documents as supporting evidence based on answers they provided on the application (i.e. legal status, marital status, immigration, etc.). This list will be helpful to the processing agent as it will identify which supporting documents the applicant has been advised to mail in. Processing summary The Processing Summary in GOL shows the information an applicant provided on their online application in a printable format. Confirmation page When an individual applies online, the information in the application is received instantly and applicants are presented with a confirmation page. The confirmation page contains the following information: the applicant's SIN ; the date and time stamp; a list of documents that the applicant is requested to submit as supporting evidence based on answers they provided on the application (e.g. legal status, marital status, immigration, etc.); the address of the mail processing centre where the documentation must be sent; a list of benefits for which the applicant may be eligible for based on answers they provided on the application. Where the applicant is required to mail in supporting documentation (e.g. legal status, marital status), they are advised to: a ttach the documentation to either: a printed confirmation page; or a separate piece of paper that includes their name and SIN . mail everything to the appropriate regional mail processing centre.

Online applications are labelled in PWS the same as paper applications; however, the following Source fields are displayed: Processing : for paper applications Online : for online applications. When an individual is married or in a common-law relationship and is applying online for the GIS , their spouse or common-law partner must provide consent to obtain their information from the Canada Revenue Agency ( CRA ) and declare that the information provided about them is true. The spouse or common-law partner's consent and declaration are considered obtained through their GIS or ALW application process if: the details of their marital status match the information provided on the online OAS / GIS application you are processing; the CRA Marital Status flag and the CRA Spousal SIN found on the CRA Income ( CRA ) screen in OAS Online, match the information provided, if available; and one of the following conditions are met: both spouses or common-law partners have signed a previously submitted paper OAS / GIS or paper GIS application; the spouse or common-law partner previously submitted an online OAS / GIS or online GIS application, and a signed Spousal Consent and Declaration (ISS954) letter or Spousal Consent and Declaration GIS (ISS954A) letter was received; the spouse or common-law partner has been approved for automatic enrolment of the GIS (i.e. the process is not in Pending status); or the spouse or common-law partner has also submitted an online OAS / GIS , online GIS or online ALW application that is being processed at the same time as the applicant's online OAS / GIS application. If there are any discrepancies between the information provided in the spouse or common-law partner's GIS or ALW application process, the CRA Income ( CRA ) screen, and the information provided in the online OAS / GIS application you are processing affecting eligibility and entitlement they must be resolved according to regular procedures before processing the online OAS / GIS application. If the spouse or common-law partner's consent and declaration have not been obtained through their GIS application process, this consent can be obtained by sending the ISS954A letter to the spouse or common-law partner to complete. The ISS954A letter allows the spouse or common-law partner to provide: confirmation that the information provided on their behalf is correct; consent for the Department to request and use their CRA income information to determine their spouse or common-law partner's entitlement for the GIS ; and advise the spouse or common-law partner that, if they have already been deemed eligible for the OAS pension, their partner's online application for the GIS will also be considered their application for the GIS , if applicable. If all other eligibility criteria are met, the online application can be approved without the consent and declaration from the spouse or common-law partner; however, the applicant's GIS entitlement cannot be calculated until the consent and declaration are received from the spouse or common-law partner.

This knowledge article describes the allowable earnings exemption amounts to employment and self-employment income for determining entitlement to income-tested benefits.

In 1989, the Old Age Security Act was amended to introduce an earnings exemption which allowed individuals and their spouse or common-law partner to exempt up to $500 from their employment income when determining entitlement to an OAS income-tested benefit. In 2008, this exemption was increased to $3,500. The earnings exemption did not apply to self-employment income. As of July 2020, the amount of the earnings exemption increased from $3,500 to $5,000 and is applied to earnings from employment and self-employment when calculating income for all income-tested benefits (i.e. the GIS, the ALW benefit and the ALWS benefit). Furthermore, when the combined employment and self-employment income is between $5,000 and $15,000, an additional exemption of 50%, up to $5,000, is applied. The maximum total deduction is $10,000. The full amount of these exemptions applies to both the client and their spouse or common-law partner based on their individual earnings. When income information is received from the CRA or manually added as income evidence, Cúram automatically calculates the earnings exemption and deducts the amounts from the employment and self-employment income, as required. As of March 15, 2020, applicants are no longer instructed to deduct the earnings exemption from their employment income and self-employment income when completing the Application for the Guaranteed Income Supplement with Statement of Income (ISP-3025B) form or the Statement of Income for the Guaranteed Income Supplement, the Allowance or Allowance for the Survivor for payment period of July (20XX) to June (20XX) with Information Sheet (ISP-3026) form. If you are processing a statement of income or an application form for the July 2020 to June 2021 payment period (2019 income year) or later, you must enter any net employment income in Cúram prior to the earnings exemption being applied so that Cúram can accurately calculate it. Manually Entered Income Evidence—Add, Edit, View and Delete in Cúram (Action) For applications and statements of income received for the July 2019 to June 2020 payment period (2018 income year) and earlier, the $3,500 earnings exemption is applied to the employment income. For more information about the earnings exemption and how it is calculated, refer to Calculating Income (Policy) and Calculating Income (Policy) Examples—Earnings Exemption Calculations (Work Tool)

The allowable earnings work incentive is only provided to beneficiaries who self-report their return to work and remain compliant throughout the reassessment process. Allowable earnings are a beneficiary's total gross earnings from all work in a calendar year that is equal or less than the Disability Basic Exemption (DBE). The DBE is the minimum amount of earnings a contributor must make for these earnings to count as valid contributions for CPPD benefit purposes. Generally, it increases each year along with the DBE amount. The allowable earnings amount resets in January of each year. Once this amount is reached, it is counted towards any work trial started in that calendar year. In cases where beneficiaries reach allowable earnings in December, the observation month would be in January of the following year, followed by the work trial. The following are not included in the yearly allowable earnings amount for all jobs in that calendar year: vacation pay; wages in lieu of notice; and all monies paid on termination of employment.

topic_title: What happens between allowable earnings and the Substantially Gainful Occupation threshold Updated
text: The onus of proof is on the Department when considering a beneficiary's continuing eligibility for CPPD benefits. The Department must show that a beneficiary who returned to work has regular capacity to pursue any Substantially Gainful Occupation (SGO). Application Management—Onus (Policy) Reported earnings that exceed the allowable earnings amount but are less than the SGO threshold can trigger the Department to contact the beneficiary. However, the evidence on file must show the beneficiary has demonstrated work capacity either through paid or unpaid (i.e. educational and volunteer activities) work activity, an improvement in their medical condition, or a combination of both, before benefits may be ceased. Severe Criterion—Work Activity and Earnings (Policy)

The observation month is a work incentive offered only to beneficiaries who self-report their return to work and reach the allowable earnings benchmark while remaining compliant during the reassessment process. The observation month is a one-month period after the month the beneficiary reaches the allowable earnings amount. If the allowable earnings have already been reached for the calendar year, the month the beneficiary returns to work is considered an observation month. For more information on the allowable earnings, Allowable Earnings (Policy) Beneficiaries are not required to earn the monthly substantially gainful occupation amount. When the beneficiary is able to work regularly and predictably during the observation month, the 3-month work trial begins the following month, regardless of earnings.

topic_title: Beneficiaries who have not reported their return to seasonal work New
text: There may be times when a beneficiary does not report their RTW and is instead identified by the Department as a beneficiary earning above the SGO benchmark amount. If a beneficiary demonstrates work capacity through seasonal work but does not report their RTW, they are not entitled to allowable earnings or an observation month. However, they are eligible for the 3-month work trial if they are compliant throughout the reassessment process. The first year the beneficiary returns to seasonal work, their benefits cease. For information on allowable earnings and the observation month, refer to Allowable Earnings (Policy) and Allowable Earnings (Policy) Observation Month (Policy) If the beneficiary does not comply, refer to the Non-Compliance During the CPP Disability Benefit Reassessment Process (Policy)

The Department provides an observation period to beneficiaries who report participation in educational or volunteer activities. The observation period is 4 months long to mimic the length of the observation month and the 3-month paid work trial provided to beneficiaries who self-report a return to work. The observation period is provided after the beneficiary reports 4 months of participation in educational or volunteer activities at 15 hours or more per week.

topic_title: Numerous attempts to return to work due to a recurring disability Updated
text: The 3-month paid work trial is not a one-time entitlement. Each time a beneficiary attempts a reported Return to Work (RTW), they are given a 3-month paid work trial. This work trial becomes effective: the month after the observation month (i.e. allowable earnings reached, observation month, 3-month paid work trial); or the 1st month after the beneficiary's RTW, if the allowable earnings have already been reached for the calendar year (i.e. observation month, 3-month paid work trial). The month the beneficiary returns to work is considered the observation month. For more information on allowable earnings or the observation month, refer to Allowable Earnings (Policy) and Allowable Earnings (Policy) Observation Month (Policy)

A 3-month paid work trial is available to all CPPD beneficiaries who are engaged in paid work and are compliant with the reassessment process. For beneficiaries who report their Return to Work (RTW) to the Department, the 3-month paid work trial begins when the beneficiary: reaches the allowable earnings amount; and demonstrates work capacity during the observation month. Monthly Substantially Gainful Occupation (SGO) earnings do not need to be met in each month of the work trial for it to be considered successful. The Department also removed the requirement to meet monthly SGO earnings before the 3-month work trial begins. For more information, Observation Month (Policy) For beneficiaries who do not report their RTW to the Department but remain compliant during the reassessment process, the 3-month paid work trial begins: the month following the month they returned to work if the RTW date is known; or January 1st of the first year of SGO earnings if the RTW date is unknown. Beneficiaries who report their RTW are entitled to all work incentives including: allowable earnings; an observation month; a 3-month paid work trial starting the month after the observation month; an automatic reinstatement; and a fast-track reapplication.

The purpose of a 3-month paid work trial is to establish that the beneficiary has regained capacity to work and is able to sustain this capacity before ceasing their CPPD benefits. The work trial period supports a return to the work force without risking immediate loss of access to CPPD benefits.

Determining how the work trial of a seasonally employed beneficiary is assessed depends on whether the beneficiary has reached the annual Substantially Gainful Occupation (SGO) benchmark amount. Seasonal earnings below the annual SGO amount During the Return to Work (RTW) assessment, if: the 3-month paid work trial was not completed before the end of the season and the beneficiary's earnings are below the annual SGO amount, the work trial may be paused, and the remainder of the work trial will be carried over to the next season or year. the second work season ends before the end of the continued work trial period and the beneficiary's earnings remained below the annual SGO amount, a holistic review is required. Seasonal earnings above the annual SGO amount During the RTW assessment, if: the beneficiary earns the annual SGO amount or more during the work season, cease their benefit at the end of the work trial. the season ends before the end of the work trial and the beneficiary has earned the annual SGO amount or more, cease their benefit at the end of what would have been the third month of the work trial. For more information, Assess Self-Reported Seasonal Employment at Reassessment (Action)

If a beneficiary is not able to continue working due to their medical condition and is not able to complete their 3-month work trial, their CPPD benefits continue without suspension or cancellation. In cases where the work trial was not completed or was deemed unsuccessful for reasons not related to the medical condition and functional limitations, the benefit may be ceased if capacity is demonstrated. A holistic assessment should be undertaken to determine overall work capacity when necessary.

The purpose of creating an NPS account is to allow for the receipt of the NPS' income from the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). This allows the pensioner to continue receiving the GIS without having to complete a statement of income every year. The signature and receipt of income for a non-pensioner spouse on their spouse or common-law partner’s GIS application does not constitute an application for a future GIS for the NPS. Creating an NPS account in OAS Online is similar to creating an ALW account. Once created, the account is automatically added to the CRA Lifetime List, initiating the one-way income feed from the CRA. For more information, refer to KA-01866 CRA Lifetime List and Lifetime Renewal Designation (Action) (article not available). Do not create an NPS account if the NPS: has not provided consent for the Department to obtain their income from the CRA by signing one of the following: Application for the Guaranteed Income Supplement (ISP-3025) form; Application for the Guaranteed Income Supplement with Statement of Income (ISP-3025B) form; Statement of Income for the Guaranteed Income Supplement, the Allowance or Allowance for the Survivor for Payment Period of July (20xx) to June (20xx) (ISP-3 026) form; Application for the Old Age Security Pension and the Guaranteed Income Supplement (ISP-3550) form; or Spousal Consent and Declaration GIS (ISS-0954A) letter. has submitted an ALW or OAS pension application. If an application has been received, an account will be created in the system when the application is processed. does not have a SIN. The pensioner’s account in OAS Online will remain a stand-alone account and they must submit a statement of income annually for the renewal of their GIS. Once the NPS account is created, do not release it. The account must remain in an incomplete status until the NPS applies for an OAS pension or benefit. At that time, the account will be adjusted for the pension or benefit being applied for, as required. Setting a system review date and code to bring forward the account When an NPS account is created, you must set a system review date with review code 09 to bring forward the account at a specific time for 2 reasons: To prevent the account from appearing on the Monthly Reference Report as an incomplete ALW account; and To send one of the following applications to the NPS, if required: Application for the Allowance or Allowance for the Survivor - Under the Old Age Security Program (ISP-3008) form; or Application for the Old Age Security Pension and the Guaranteed Income Supplement (ISP-3550) form. Once you create an NPS account in OAS Online, the NPS will be excluded from the automatic enrolment process for the OAS pension and the GIS as they now have an account in OAS Online. Therefore, it is important to review the account at the BF dates to ensure the NPS receives an application to apply for benefits. Depending on the age of the NPS at the time the account is created, you will set the following system review dates: the month of their 59th birthday; and the month of their 64th birthday. On the review date, the account will appear on the Month End Monthly BF report to send the ISP-3008 form or the ISP-3550 form as applicable, if one has not already been sent or received.

topic_title: Assessing incapacity at reconsideration and appeal levels
text: The incapacity provision can be assessed at any active level of the process. If the applicant is granted a benefit at the reconsideration level, but the incapacity request is not applied, it can be assessed by the SST if an appeal is accepted. If a claim of incapacity is made at the SST level or if the SST requests that the incapacity be reviewed, you must review the information on file and, if required, develop the file to get additional information. For CPPD benefits: If the incapacity provision can be applied prior to the SST hearing, proceed with an agreement offer. If the agreement offer is not accepted, you must complete a submission. If the incapacity provision is denied, you must complete an addendum or submission to address the issues at the SST level. An addendum is sometimes required if the non-medical determination is at the SST level. For CPP or OAS benefits, you must provide the Incapacity Addendum to the SCBO . For more information, refer to the CPP/CPPD/OAS Appeals Sharepoint External link site. CPP/CPPD/OAS Appeals Sharepoint

topic_title: Assessing the applicant's ability to apply for benefits
text: The intent of an incapacity assessment is to determine if the applicant was unable to apply for benefits earlier than they did because they could not express the intent to submit an application. Evaluate the following information on file to make a medical determination of incapacity: the medical evidence (i.e. the diagnosis and cognitive limitations); the Power of Attorney (POA) or legal representative documents including: the effective date of the POA or court documents; and the date the application was signed. the claimed period of incapacity on file with medical evidence; and the applicant's ability to perform activities that support whether they had the capacity to express an intention to apply for benefits. The following activities may support the applicant's ability to apply. This list is not comprehensive as there may be additional activities not mentioned here: managing their affairs of daily living, such as: travelling unaccompanied; working with earned income; attending school; participating in training programs; or managing personal or family finances. calling Service Canada or going to a Service Canada Centre to inquire about their application; living independently and maintaining their own health by going to medical tests or treatments; maintaining their driver's license; being the primary caregiver for a young or disabled child or other family members; engaging in volunteer activities; or signing a POA. The date a POA document is signed may not impact when an incapacity date can be determined, as long as the medical evidence supports the claim of incapacity. The POA signature and date are part of the incapacity evidence to be considered with any medical or other evidence before a determination of incapacity can be made. Submit a request through the National Business Expertise Tool (NEXO) External link when it is difficult to make a medical determination due to a complex medical condition or medical evidence, or where relevant daily activities are not determinative of incapacity. National Business Expertise Tool

topic_title: Deemed receipt date of an application Updated
text: For CPP and OAS applications, if the incapacity provision can be applied, the Medical Adjudicator provides the date the last period of continuous incapacity started and the date the incapacity ended, if applicable. In ITRDS , the SCBO will calculate the earlier deemed date of application, if applicable. For CPPD benefits applications, you must determine if: the incapacity provision would be beneficial for the applicant; the requirements of the incapacity provision have been met; and the applicant has or had a "severe and prolonged" disability on or before their latest possible date of onset. If the incapacity provision can be applied, the earlier deemed receipt date of the application is the later of: the month before the 1st month the CPPD benefit could have begun; or the month the last period of continuous incapacity started.

topic_title: Determine if the period of incapacity was continuous and within the time limits for submitting an application for benefits
text: Continuous Continuous means there were no periods of time when the applicant was capable of expressing an intention to apply for pensions or benefits. Persons with certain medical conditions can have periods when they are clearly incapacitated and other periods when they recover to a point of being capable. Evaluate all dates related to: the medical condition; cognitive and physical functional impairments; earnings; and signatures on documents. If necessary, request supporting documentation for the claimed period of incapacity. For more information, CPPD—File Development (Scenario) Time limits for submitting an application for benefits If the applicant's incapacity ended, determine if the application was submitted within the prescribed time limit. If a leap year occurred, count February 29. If the incapacity provision can be applied, provide the date the last continuous period of incapacity started on the Incapacity Adjudication Summary template, then return the file to the applicable processing area. Processing staff will then determine the new earlier deemed date of application. For CPPD benefits applications, the applicant must be continuously disabled on or before their Latest Possible Date of Onset or Minimum Qualifying Period, and into the future to qualify.

An application meets the eligibility criteria for the incapacity provision when the period of incapacity was continuous. In a case where the applicant regains capacity, the incapacity provision may be applied if the benefits application was submitted within the following time limits: within one month if the period of incapacity was less than 30 days; within the number of days the person was incapacitated, if the period of incapacity was less than 365 days (e.g. if the period of incapacity was 45 days, the applicant must submit their application within 45 days of regaining capacity); or within one year if the period of incapacity was more than 365 days. For more information, refer to Incapacity (Policy) and to Incapacity (Policy) Examples—Incapacity Provision (Work Tool)

There must be medical evidence on file to make a medical determination of incapacity and to support the dates provided. The automation process is designed to assist the regional processing centers with processing overpayment work items. During this process, the automation process will calculate the recovery rates, apply them to the accounts and send a letter to the client advising them of the recovery rate and the start date. These automated letters are saved in the Corporate Correspondence Tool letter vault and are accessible by specific authorized individuals. The accounts identified for this process are active (in pay) accounts where the client has an overpayment or several overpayments which are not being recovered, and has a work item in Auto status in PWS . The automation process will proceed as follows: Identify monthly overpayment work items in PWS that are Unassigned with an Auto status. Use the client’s SIN and search PWS for other active or on hold work items matching the work type list: Integrity Investigation Request (0414); Integrity Case (0415); Integrity – Direct; Reconsideration (3134); Agreement Offer; Death Notification; Notif. Cash Receipt (1671); Payment Advice Notice; SST Appeal; Statutory Set off; Bankruptcy; REU-Enquiry; Consent Deduct/Payment (3010); Enquiry – Payment Related; Enquiry – Death Notification; and Monthly Overpayment. If a work item matching the work type list is found, the automated process will complete the work item and add this note to the PWS work item: “Monthly OAS / GIS overpayment work item completed by Process Automation because there is another work item with active or on hold status”. Assign the work item in PWS to the automated process. The automation process usernames contain "UiPath" or "Pensions" followed by a number. Apply the exception criteria in OAS Online to determine if the automation process can continue: If yes , the automation process will go to Step 5. If no , the automation process will flag the work item as an exception for manual processing. Verify the overpayment on the Deductions (DED) screen in OAS Online and determine the path to follow: The automation process will flag the work item as an exception for manual processing if: an overpayment exists but the code is not 1, 3 or 5; or an overpayment exists for codes 1, 3 or 5 and the Outstanding field is $25,000 or more. The automation process will complete the work item in PWS if: no overpayment exists; an overpayment exists for codes 1, 3 or 5 and the Outstanding field is blank; or an overpayment exists for codes 1, 3, or 5 and the Monthly Recovery Rate or % field is populated. Store the date the overpayment was added to the account on the HISTORY (HST) screen in OAS Online. Use the date the overpayment was added to the account in ITRDS to perform a keyword search to determine if the client has repaid the amount of the overpayment or expressed financial hardship. If no , the automated process will go to Step 8. If yes , the automated process will flag the work item as an exception for manual processing. Check for CPP receivables (overpayment) in CPMS . Determine the recovery rate based on all of the client’s current monthly entitlements under both CPP and OAS pensions and benefits using the current benefit amounts listed in ITRDS under the BENEFITS tab. Set the recovery rate based on current policy Recovery Guidelines in OAS Online. Recovery Guidelines Add a note in ITRDS from the user "BRPA". Send the appropriate overpayment letter to the client, giving them 30 days to reply. Complete the work item in PWS with the following note: “Work item processed by Automation.” The automation tool uses delegated authorities that are in line with those of an SCBO .
There is no reference material. (KA-01423 Snippet 14.0 content. Do not modify or delete.)

As of June 4, 2021, individuals can apply for the GIS online through the My Service Canada Account portal if they: are age 64 + 1 month or older; are in pay for or will be in pay for an OAS pension; are not already in pay for or will not be in pay for the GIS; and do not have a third party representative (trustee or power of attorney) on file. If any of the above criteria are not met, the applicant is directed to an "Unable to continue" page indicating why they cannot apply online. The message offers a "contact us" link that points to our Department website and provides contact information, as well as how to submit a paper application. If all of the above criteria are met, the applicant can complete and submit their application online. Domestic addresses and telephone number updates through the online application are captured directly into ITRDS. Applicants with a foreign address on file are advised that an incorrect address may result in payment or follow-up letters not being delivered correctly. They are advised to contact the Department to update their address information before using the online service. When an individual applies online, the information is captured in a date stamped PDF file and applicants are presented with a confirmation page. The confirmation page contains the following information: the applicant's name; the date and time stamp; a list of documents that the applicant is requested to submit as supporting evidence based on answers they provided on the application (e.g. marital status, proof of death); the address of the mail processing centre where the documentation must be sent; a phone number for foreign residents to provide direct deposit information and a link to the applicable direct deposit form; and a list of OAS or CPP benefits for which the applicant may be eligible for based on answers they had provided in the application. Where the applicant is required to mail in supporting documentation (e.g. marital status), they are advised to: attach the documentation to either a: printed version of their confirmation page; or separate piece of paper that includes their name and social insurance number. mail everything to the appropriate regional mail-processing centre.
