topic_title: Is the applicant or beneficiary a business owner who generates income but does not work in the business?
text: An applicant or beneficiary may be the owner of a business that generates income, however, staff or family run and manage the business. The applicant or beneficiary may also be in a limited partnership or have an incorporated business where their involvement is strictly financial. In such situations, determine if the applicant or beneficiary is engaged in work activity. Work activity for a business owner can involve the following: strategic planning; making financial decisions; and providing advice. If the business earnings do not correlate to any work activity, refer to Severe Criterion—Impact of medical condition(s) and functional limitations on work capacity . If the business earnings correlate to any work activity, continue to the What you need to do section of this procedure. Severe Criterion—Impact of medical condition(s) and functional limitations on work capacity
Assess the self- employed individual's capacity for work.

Assess w ork activity When you assess the client 's work activity, review the hours spent contributing to the business and the predictability of the client's attendance. This information can be obtained through telephone co ntact with the client and recorded in the Development Call record Calculate the ho urs that the individual contributed to the business including hours spent : producing the product or providing the service; managing the operation of the business; managing and hiring staff; accounting; marketing; scheduling; consulting; maintaining or establishing client relationships; and providing advice and guidance to the business. Ensure the hours worked are predictable and that the individual is able to regularly continue the hours of work. Refer to Severe Criterion—Work Capacity (regular employment, self-employment, seasonal and accommodated) . Assess gross business earnings After work activity is established through an assessment of hours and predictability, assess the gross business earnings as follows: Severe Criterion—Work Capacity (regular employment, self-employment, seasonal and accommodated) Consider the type of business. Calculate the gross business earnings for partnerships or corporations based on the percentage of the individual's share of the business. For example: If the individual is in a partnership with a 40% share of the business, calculate 40% of the gross business earnings as follows: $40,000 gross business earnings multiplied by 40% = $16,000 gross business earnings for the individual. Determine if the individual's gross business earnings are above or below the s ubstantially gainful occupation threshold . Refer to Severe Criterion—Work Capacity (regular employment, self-employment, seasonal and accommodated) . Severe Criterion—Work Capacity (regular employment, self-employment, seasonal and accommodated)

The assessment of the work capacity of a self-employed individual who continues to work is the same as that used for individuals working for an employer. However, additional factors must be considered due to the nature of the self-employed work. Refer to Severe Criterion—Work Capacity (regular employment, self-employment, seasonal and accommodated) in combination with this procedure. Severe Criterion—Work Capacity (regular employment, self-employment, seasonal and accommodated) The following lists the differences in responsibilities between self-employment and employment. A self-employed individual invoices others for services rendered or goods sold; oversees their own work activities; sets their own work hours; chooses business clients and partners; can accept or refuse work; provides and maintains their own work tools and equipment; and has a relationship with the payer for a specific job. An employer pays the employee's wages; oversees work activities; determines the schedule or priority of work; assigns work clients; decides what work the employee does; supplies work tools and equipment; and maintains a relationship with the employee that is usually continuous. The following lists the differences between a self-employed individual and one who is an employee. A self-employed individual has capital investment in their business; determines the overall direction of the business; pays taxes as a self-employed person or is paid by a business which they own; and can hire, manage and pay staff. An employee typically has no capital investment in the business; cannot determine the direction of the business; is paid by the business that they do not own; and does not hire or pay others to do the work. To assess work capacity, consider the followin g factors:

Work activity hours Self-employment hours are th e hours of work activities that lead to producing a product or delivering a servic e to generate i ncome . Include all work activity hours relating to the business including hours spent to make the product or to deliver the service in the determination of hours. For example, the self-employed person may spend 2 hours a week taking pictures of families as a photographer. However, they spend 8 hours a week advertising, talking to current or potential clients, editing the pictures and managing the finances. All of which goes towards the current or future product or service. Predictability Unlike an employee, a self-employed individual may not have a schedule they must follo w . Self-employed individuals may have flexibility to choose when and how often to work. This flexibility may allow the person to change their work hours to suit any functional limitations they may have as a result of one or more medical conditions. For example, the person may work split hours so that they can rest or they may adjust their work hours to accommodate their medically induced functional limitations. When the applicant or beneficiary is the only person working in the business, they must be able to manage finances, staff, market, brand, plan and execute on a predictable basis to keep a business operating. Because of the flexibility of work for some self-employment, it would be difficult to determ ine if th e work was unpredictable for an active business. Therefore, the assessment of work activity for these self-employed individuals is determined by the number of work activity hours.

text: RTR pension Effective June 1, 2024, once the applicant applies for the RTR pension in MSCA, their date of birth from ITRDS will be displayed for them to verify by selecting Yes or No. If the applicant selects No, they will be stopped from applying online and instructed to contact the Department to apply for the RTR pension. When the applicant submits an online RTR application, the information transfers to ITRDS and the following occurs: All sections completed by the applicant during the online application process are downloaded onto ITRDS and can be viewed in the Application Status screen. Effective June 1, 2024, My Service Canada Account (MSCA) was updated to allow DTH benefit and SVR pension and Child(ren)'s Benefits online applicants to submit supporting documentation using the MSCA Document Upload Solution service. CPPD benefits online applicants can also submit supporting documentation using the Document Upload Solution service. MSCA allows students to submit information about their attendance at school or university and proof of enrolment in support of their Child's benefit. Students must upload: a Canada Pension Plan Child's Benefit Application and Declaration for a Student over 18 Years of Age in Attendance at School or University (ISP-1402) form with Section E signed by their educational institution administrator; or proof of enrolment obtained from their online school or university portal. The proof of enrolment must include the following information to be acceptable: Student's name; School official's original or electronic signature; Degree; Program; Semester(s), term(s) or school year; Student ID number; Start and End dates for each semester(s), the term(s), or school year; Name and address of the school or university (logo or watermark accepted); and Enrolment status for each semester(s), term(s) or school year (e.g. full-time or part-time). Students will be required to upload the ISP-1402 form with Section E signed by the school or university or a proof of enrolment obtained from their student online portal with the following information: Student's name; Student identification number or date of birth; Program of study; Name and address of school or university; Start and end dates for semester, term or school year enrolled in; and Enrolment status for the semester, term or school year (full-time or part-time). Applicants and students are still able to provide their documentation by mail or at a Service Canada Centre. For more information, Document Upload Solution (Scenario)

topic_title: Viewing the online application in PWS
text: When applicants submit an online application, the following occurs: MSCA compiles the applicant information from the online application into a PDF format and sends that information to PWS and the Digital Repository where they will be stored in a secure and protected environment. a corresponding PWS work item is auto-generated with a link to the PDF document for each application submitted using existing work types. This work item is loaded into the appropriate regional processing centre's inventory based on the applicant's or contributor's latest province of residence for distribution and processing. If a PWS work item does not contain a link to retrieve the document, you should change the Document Status of the online document from Active to Any to see all documents regardless of the Repository Status in PWS. For more information on how to create suggested views in PWS and on PWS work types, refer to Pensions Workload System Guide Internal link . Pensions Workload System Guide Dual contributors Transfer the file to Timmins, Ontario Dual Processing Unit and move the work item or file in PWS if the applicant or their spouse or common-law partner is: a Dual contributor; or a QPP contributor only. For more information, Dual Accounts (Knowledge) International Operations accounts The system will not automatically create a work item for International Operations (IO) accounts in Alberta or New Brunswick offices. The Regional staff must review all incoming online applications. For IO accounts, regional staff will change the PWS work item to IO-WT or IO-ATL program. Transfer a Client's File to International Operations (Action) Accounts with Program Exception Processing status If the applicant's, their spouse or common-law partner's account has Program Exception Processing (PEP) status, transfer the account to the PEP Unit for processing. The PEP Unit in St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador takes any required follow-up action. For more information, CPP Program Exception Process Accounts (Knowledge)

topic_title: Viewing the online Death benefit application in ITRDS
text: In ITRDS, you can access the downloaded data from the online DTH benefit application through the Application Status screen under the Online Application section. If the data integration is successful, a DTHA link will display. When you click the DTHA link, the Online Application screen opens. You will see the following sections, which will display the populated data, if applicable: Application for a Canada Pension Plan Death Benefit (ISP-1200) SECTION A - Information about the Deceased Contributor SECTION B - Information about the Settlement of the Estate SECTION C - Information about the Applicant Additional Info

My Service Canada Account (MSCA) allows applicants to submit an online application for the following CPP benefits, pensions and provisions: Benefit or Pension Child's benefit Death benefit Disability benefit Post-Retirement Disability benefit Retirement pension Survivor's pension Provision Child Rearing Provision Credit Split Pension Sharing My Service Canada Account (Knowledge) Receipt date The official receipt date is the date the database receives the online application and supporting documents. Online applications and supporting documents are date and time stamped in Atlantic Standard time and must not be altered. This date is located at the bottom of the PDF document of the application and supporting document. Access the online CPP application in PWS

The Transfer a Client's File to International Operations procedures have been updated to include the procedures relating to CPP D isability benefits applications where the applicant has indicated they lived or worked in a country with which Canada has an International Social Security Agreement in effect. The information found in the Kool Tool (2015) was included into the procedures. These procedures will allow you to identify the different situations when a CPPD benefits application must be transferred to International Operations and include the process to complete the adjudication. Contact: Transfer a Client's File to International Operations Operational Service Desk

Currently, Service Canada receives all PNSH applications by paper or written communication only. Both or either one of the spouses or common-law partners can apply for PNSH on the same application form. If two applications are received, the information is verified and treated as one application. If only one spouse or common-law partner signs the application, the other spouse or common-law partner must be informed in writing of the application. Third party contacts may apply on behalf of the applicant if the third party administrator provided the supporting documentation with the paper application.
If additional guidance is required, send an enquiry via the Business Expertise Request Tool by following normal channels. Business Expertise Request Tool

The online application for PNSH is a manual process and staff must follow current procedures. Pension Sharing Processing agents must retrieve the information in PDF form in the documents section of PWS. There is no automation (e.g. auto data capture, interrelationship established in ITRDS, or auto adjudication) with the online application of PNSH during this e-Service implementation.

Effective October 29, 2021, applicants will be able to apply for CPP Pension Sharing (PNSH) through their My Service Canada Account (MSCA). Although applicants have the option to submit an online application, the processing of the PNSH remains the same. The online application for PNSH is viewable in PWS. It contains a series of questions grouped into 5-step sections, which reflects the Application for Canada Pension Plan Sharing of Retirement Pension(s) (ISP1002) form. The online application does not replace the ISP1002 form. The online version offers an alternate option to submit their application. Before beginning the application process, the applicant must provide the following 2 mandatory pieces of information in the General Information page in MSCA: their marital status; and the date of birth of their spouse or common-law partner. The applicant's responses will determine if they meet the eligibility criteria to apply online, and set the next relevant questions to display. For more information, Online Applications for Canada Pension Plan

The Digital Repository is a secure environment where all online applications and forms are safely stored after they are received in the system. When an applicant submits an online CPP Child’s benefit application, it is stored within the Digital Repository. You can view the application via the associated work item in PWS under the contributor’s account.

CPP Child’s benefit provides monthly payments to the dependent children of disabled or deceased CPP contributors. To qualify, the child must be 18 to 25 years old and in full-time attendance at a recognized school or university. Service Canada currently receives CPP Child’s benefit applications only on paper via the Application for a Canada Pension Plan Child’s Benefit (ISP1400) form or by written communication. Effective October 22, 2021, individuals can choose to apply for the CPP child's benefit online using their My Service Canada Account (MSCA). The online CPP Child’s benefit application does not replace the ISP1400 form. It is another channel eligible applicants can use to apply for the benefit. The online CPP Child’s Benefit application has a dynamic component that displays appropriate application questions based on the information input by the applicant. Individuals can now apply online for CPP Child’s benefit using their My Service Canada Account (MSCA). Existing clients can log into their MSCA account, while new clients must register for an account to access the online application form. MSCA-authenticated clients must agree to the following: Privacy Notice for MSCA: Your information is used for the purpose of registering and authenticating yourself before enrolling in various online services accessible through MSCA. Terms of Use for MSCA: You are responsible, accountable and liable for all use and misuse of MSCA associated with your user ID and password. You must use the services provided via MSCA solely for the purposes for which they are offered and for no other purpose including for no improper or illegal purpose or activity. You must not use MSCA on behalf of anyone else and you must not allow anyone else to use your MSCA. You must access and use MSCA only as yourself. A registered trustee, guardian, or other legal representative may only act on your behalf in person, by mail or by phone, not online. The eligibility criteria to apply for a CPP Child’s benefit online are as follows: The applicant must be logged in to their MSCA and have been authenticated; The applicant must be between 18 and 25 years old at the time they make the application; There must be no authorized legal representative such as a trustee or power of attorney on the applicant’s record; The applicant must be a Canadian resident. If the applicant does not meet the above eligibility criteria, the system displays an Unable to continue message. If the applicant meets the above eligibility criteria, they can apply for the CPP Child’s benefit online. The applicant’s electronic signature is captured when the application is made to ensure their: identity is established through their Social Insurance Number; and intent is established through their: confirmation of the accuracy of the information; and agreement to the terms and conditions. Processing staff must review the accounts that appear on this report and validate the income variance. A variance in income can indicate that a client forgot to report sources of income on their Income Tax and Benefit Return or statement of income. It can also indicate a reduction in income where an option situation exists. If the variance in income is a result of a reduction or loss of pension income, employment income or self-employment income and meets the criteria for an option, a Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form is sent to the client to complete and return. Once the option is received, it is manually processed. Since August 2, 2021, an automated process actions accounts appearing on the yearly variance report. A reduction in CPP income is the only optionable event considered for automation. The accounts will fall under one of the following two scenarios: CPP accounts where there was a reduction in the CPP income and CPP is the only source of income; or CPP accounts where there was a reduction in the CPP income and the client had multiple sources of income, but all other sources increased (i.e. you can assume that the client only suffered a loss in CPP income).

The automated process is designed to assist the regional processing centers with processing accounts from the CRA yearly variance report. During this process, the income is adjusted, underpayments are issued and a letter is sent to the client. These automated letters are then saved in the Corporate Correspondence Tool vault and are accessible by processing staff. The accounts considered for this process automation are active MS1 , MS2 and MS3 accounts with a Variance Rreport work item in Auto status in PWS. The automated process will proceed as follows: Identify the Variance Report work items in PWS that are Unassigned with an Auto status. Assign the work item in PWS to the automated process. The usernames used by the automation process contain "UiPath" or "Pensions" followed by a number. Apply the exception criteria below to determine if the automated process can continue: If yes , the automated process will go to Step 4 . Step 4 If no , the automated process will flag the work item as an exception for manual processing. In OAS Online, go to the CRA Income (CRA) screen to obtain the income needed from the estimated year and from the base calendar year. In ITRDS, determine if the client is in receipt of CPP benefits: If yes , the automation will access CPMS to obtain the client's monthly CPP rate for the years in review. If no , the automated process will flag the work item as an exception for manual processing. Calculate the new estimated income total. On the Re-Calculation Input (CAL) screen, determine the payment period and validate that the account status, marital status and payment income on the Re-Calculation screen were consistent. Add the new estimated total income to the Payment income field. Determine if there are any changes in the client's or the spouse or common-law partner's entitlement. If the recalculated net amount is positive , the automated process will do the following: Perform the following steps in OAS Online: On the Deductions (DED) screen, the automated process will verify for any existing outstanding overpayments for codes 01, 03 or 05 and remove any existing recovery rate for these codes. On the Cash receipts (CSH) screen, the automated process will apply the underpayment to any existing overpayment, if applicable. If the outstanding balance remaining is an overpayment, the client will be notified of the new outstanding amount. If the outstanding balance remaining is an underpayment, it will be released online and the client will be notified. On the Underpayment (OVP) screen, the automated process will issue the full balance of the underpayment. Send the appropriate letter to the client to notify them of the actions taken. Add notes in ITRDS from user "BRPA" with details of the actions taken. If the recalculated net amount is NIL (i.e. results in no change to the beneficiary's entitlement), the automated process will add notes to ITRDS by user "BRPA" to indicate the recalculation was completed. Complete the work item in PWS with the following note: "Work item processed by Automation // Article de travail traité par Automatisation."
This procedure provides guidance on the automated process applied to active accounts that appear on the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) year-to-year variance report where an option situation exists.

The automated process is designed to assist regional processing centres in processing P Option Recalculations. During this process, income is adjusted and an overpayment or underpayment letter is sent to the client. These automated letters are saved in the Corporate Correspondence Tool (CCT) vault and are accessible to processing staff. The accounts considered for this process are the active MS 1, 2, 3, 8 and 9 with an Options – Recalculations work item in Auto status in PWS . The automated process will: Identify Options – Recalculations work items in PWS that are Unassigned with an Auto status. Assign the work item in PWS to the automated process. Usernames used by the automation process contain “UiPath” and/or “Pensions” followed by a number. Apply the exception criteria below to determine if the automated process can continue: If yes, the automated process goes to Step 4 . Step 4 If not, the automated process flags the work item as an exception for manual processing. In OAS On-line, go to the CRA INCOME screen to obtain the income needed from the estimated year and from the base calendar year. Calculate the new total estimated income. On the RE-CALCULATION screen, determine the payment period and verify that the account status, marital status and payment income are consistent. Add the new estimated total income in the payment income field. Determine if there is any change in the entitlement of the client, their spouse or common-law partner. If the recalculated net amount is negative , the automated process will: Add the overpayment on the DEDUCTION screen in OAS On-line. Send the appropriate overpayment letter to the client. Add notes in ITRDS from user BRPA with details of the actions taken. If the recalculated net amount is positive, the automated process will: Perform the following steps in OAS On-line: On the DEDUCTIONS screen in OAS On-line, check for any existing outstanding overpayments for codes 01, 03 or 05. Read and store any existing recovery rate for these codes. On the CASH RECEIPTS screen, apply the underpayment to any existing overpayment, if applicable; and If the outstanding balance is an overpayment, the client will be notified of the new outstanding amount. If the outstanding balance is an underpayment, it will be released online, and the client will be notified. On the UNDERPAYMENT screen, issue the full balance of the underpayment. Send the appropriate letter to the client to notify them of the actions taken. Add notes in ITRDS from user BRPA with details of the actions taken. If the recalculated net amount is NIL (results in no change to the beneficiary’s entitlement), the automated process will add notes to ITRDS by user BRPA to indicate the recalculation was completed. Complete the work item in PWS with the following note: “Work item processed by Automation // Article de travail traité par Automatisation.”

The actual income for the estimated income year must be reviewed against the statement of estimated income previously made. Any discrepancies that cannot be resolved by reviewing the information on file must be questioned to ensure the accuracy of the benefit rate paid. If the income or the date of the event has been changed, a recalculation of the option must be made, and the entitlement for the GIS , ALW or ALWS must be adjusted. If the comparison of the submitted income to the actual income for the base calendar year results in an underpayment or an overpayment, the account must be balanced and the client must be notified of the outcome. You must proceed as follows: Retrieve the estimated income calculation from the Option Calculator tool and recalculate the option with the income from the CRA screen in OAS On-line . Perform the following steps in OAS On-line: On the RE-CALCULATION screen, update the fields to determine any underpayment or overpayment, if applicable. Release the underpayment or apply it to an existing overpayment, if applicable; or On the DEDUCTION screen, add the overpayment, if applicable. Send the applicable letter to inform the client of the outcome. Update ITRDS Notes and PWS .

Effective October 29, 2021, individuals can choose to apply online for CPP Pension Sharing (PNSH) through their My Service Canada Account (MSCA). PNSH is a provision that lets spouses or common-law partners apply for, share or assign a portion of their CPP Retirement pension with their spouse using a set formula. The online CPP Pension Sharing application does not replace the ISP1002 form. It is another channel eligible applicants can use to apply for the provision . The online CPP Pension Sharing application contains a dynamic component that displays appropriate application questions based on the information input by the applicant. Individuals can now apply online for PNSH using their My Service Canada Account (MSCA). Existing clients can log into their MSCA, while new clients must register for an account to access the online application form. MSCA-authenticated clients must agree to the following: Privacy Notice for MSCA: Your information is used for the purpose of registering and authenticating yourself prior to enrolling in various online services accessible through MSCA. Terms of Use for MSCA: You are responsible, accountable and liable for all use and misuse of MSCA associated with your user ID and password. You must use the services provided via MSCA solely for the purposes for which they are offered and for no other purpose including for no improper purpose or activity. You must not use MSCA on behalf of anyone else and you must not allow anyone else to use your MSCA. You must access and use MSCA only as yourself. A registered trustee, guardian, or other legal representative may only act on your behalf in person, by mail or by phone, but not online. The eligibility criteria to apply online for PNSH are as follows: The applicant must be logged into to their MSCA and have been authenticated; The applicant must be married or in a common-law relationship; Both the applicant and spouse or common-law partner must be 60 years old at the time of the application; There must be no authorized legal representative such as a trustee or power of attorney on the applicant’s record; The applicant must be a Canadian resident. If the applicant does not meet the above eligibility criteria, the system displays an Unable to continue message. If the applicant meets the above eligibility criteria, they can apply for PNSH online. Before starting their online application, applicants must answer 2 mandatory questions from the General information screen. They must enter: their marital status; and the date of birth of their spouse or common-law partner. For certain countries' benefit applications, you will not be required to ensure that the application has been fully completed. In others, you must review what sections or fields are mandatory and request their completion if not already done so by the applicant. If the applicant did not complete any of the required sections, you must return the entire original copy of the application to them (retain a certified copy on file) and clearly indicate in the accompanying letter what needs to be completed. If the applicant does not return the application after the bring forward process, the certified copy will be sent to the other country as is.

topic_title: Completion of the liaison and forwarding the application
text: Once the foreign benefit application has been reviewed and all possible information and documentation has been collected, a liaison form must be completed to be sent with the application to the other country. When completing fields related to the applicant or deceased contributor, only enter information that has been verified through information in ITRDS, or documentation in the regional or International Operations file. If a certain data element cannot not be validated (e.g. date of death, citizenship), do not provide that information on the liaison form. Once the liaison has been completed and the application is ready to be sent, the package can be sent by mail, through Canada Post's Connect or both.

topic_title: Did the applicant die before their foreign benefit application was transferred to the other country?
text: If the applicant died before their application was transferred to the other country, treat the application as you would for a living client. However, on the liaison form, you must state the applicant's date of death as well as any verified estate or legal representative information. To enter a date of death, if required, Manage a Person Record in Cúram (Action)

The documentation requirements for a foreign benefit application will vary by country and by benefit type. You must review the country's requirements to determine when documents are required: to be sent with the application to the other country; or to validate a client's information. Documents to be sent to with the application In some cases, the other country does not require the Department to obtain all of the necessary documents needed to process the application as they will contact the applicant directly for any missing information or documents. In other cases, you may be required to contact the applicant to obtain documentation. If the applicant does not respond to requests for the documents, or does not provide everything that is required, the application will be sent without the requested documentation. In all cases, if the applicant submits any supporting documentation, it must be sent to the other country along with the application. If the applicant submits original documents, certified copies must be sent to the other country and the originals returned to the applicant, unless the other country requires the original documents. Normally, this information can be validated through ITRDS, Cúram or documentation on the IO) file. In certain situations, the other country may require validation of certain data elements that cannot be validated through ITRDS or the IO file. In these cases, you must first determine if the information could be located in the regional processing centre file. If not, the applicant must be contacted to request that they provide the required documentation to validate the information. However, if the other country does not require the completeness of documentation, you will not need to request documents (from the applicant or regional file) to support the validation of the applicant or deceased's information. Only information that is readily available will be provided on the liaison form.

topic_title: Responsibility of the Bureau des ententes de sécurité sociale
text: All International Social Security Agreements contain a provision that permits the concluding of "understandings" with provincial governments. Quebec is the only province to enter into understandings under social security agreements. Quebec has its own provincial pension plan, the QPP, which is Quebec's counterpart to the CPP. In certain situations, you will be required to forward the application to the Bureau des ententes de sécurité sociale. For more information, Determine responsibility of foreign application or information request (Action)
This procedure provides the steps to follow when you review and transfer a foreign benefit application to a foreign institution.

If validation of residence in Canada on the liaison form is required, you must determine if the applicant's Canadian residence has already been validated and, if it has, if updated information is required. If the applicant's Canadian residence has not already been reviewed, you will need to obtain a residence statement if one was not received with the application. A client's residence statement can be accepted and validated as stated, unless there are inconsistencies or discrepancies with information or documents on file or in the system. When reporting Canadian residence to the other country, there may be limitations to the periods you enter on the liaison form based on the applicant's CPP creditable periods (i.e. CPP contributions and periods in receipt of a DSB, when applicable). Therefore, you must always review the benefit type's requirements for reporting Canadian residence, as it may not need to be validated if it doesn't need to be reported. All confirmed periods of Canadian residence must be added to Cúram.
For more information on foreign benefits, liaisons and Cúram, refer to the Cúram Work Tool

A foreign benefit refers to any pension or benefit that is paid by a social security administration of a country other than Canada. Benefits from other countries are comparable to Canada's social security benefits and include retirement, old age, disability and survivor benefits. International Operations staff provide information to be sent with foreign benefit applications to assist the foreign institution in determining whether the individual is eligible to that country's benefits based on the terms of the social security agreement. An individual's Canadian creditable periods (i.e. Canadian residence and/or CPP creditable periods) may assist the individual to meet the eligibility criteria of the other country's pension scheme when an International Social Security Agreement exists between Canada and that country. In all cases, the foreign institution determines an applicant's eligibility. The action that you will take with a foreign benefit application is dependent on the foreign institution's requirements. You may be required to: verify that all of the required documents and information have been received prior to forwarding the application; or send the application without verifying the completeness of documentation or the application, in which case the foreign institution will communicate directly with the applicant to obtain the required information or documents .

topic_title: Examples—Periods not considered residence in Canada
text: Example 1 Table 1. Example 1 - Situation and Residence determination Situation Residence determination An applicant indicates on their residence statement that they have lived in Canada from 1989 to the present (February 2024). They also indicated that they worked in Italy between March 1996 and November 1996. After requesting clarification from the applicant, you determine that this period was a temporary absence from Canada as they: had maintained their abode in Canada; intended to return to Canada after the end of the employment period; and maintained strong ties to Canada. You verify that Canada has an International Social Security Agreement (ISSA) with Italy in force and send a request to International Operations (IO) to verify the Italian contributions. IO responds that the applicant made valid contributions in Italy from March 1996 to July 1996. Therefore, this period is not considered residence in Canada for the residence calculation. This period is considered an absence from Canada, even though the applicant would have normally been considered a resident of Canada during the absence. Example 2 Table 2. Example 2 - Situation and Residence determination Situation Residence determination An applicant indicates on their residence statement that they were born in Canada but lived in Spain from January 2010 to May 2020 while performing missionary work for the Salvation Army. They also indicated that from November 15, 2011, to November 15, 2019, they worked in Spain and made contributions to Spain’s social security scheme. You verify that Canada has an ISSA in force with Spain and send a request to IO to verify the Spanish contributions. IO responds that the applicant has made valid contributions in Spain from November 15, 2011, to November 15, 2019. Although performing missionary work outside of Canada can be considered deemed residence, the period of November 2011 to November 2019 is considered an absence from Canada as the applicant made work-related contributions in Spain during that time. However, the period of January 2010 to November 14, 2011, and November 15, 2019, to May 2020, will be considered deemed residence if all other conditions are met. Example 3 Table 3. Example 3 - Situation and Residence determination Situation Residence determination An applicant indicates on their residence statement that they resided in Germany from June 2000 to May 2015. They also indicate that they worked in Germany during that time. A review of the spouse's account shows that they were considered a deemed resident of Canada during this period in Germany as they were working for Canadian Armed Forces during this time and did not contribute to the German pension program. After confirming that the applicant was accompanying their spouse during the period together in Germany, you verify that Canada has an ISSA in force with Germany and send a request to IO to verify the German contributions. IO responds that the applicant made valid contributions in Germany from August 2000 to February 2015. While their spouse was deemed to be a resident of Canada during the entire period in Germany, the period of August 2000 to February 2015 must be removed from the applicant's residence calculation as the applicant made work-related contributions in Germany during that time. However, the period of June 2000 to August 2000, and February 2015 to May 2015 will be considered deemed residence if all other conditions are met.

Foreign insurance numbers are the most efficient tool used by foreign institutions to locate client records. It is essential that attempts are made to obtain the foreign identifier when it is not found in the client’s file. Sending a liaison to a foreign institution without this identifier will often result in delay ed responses or non-responses. For clients who have previously submitted CPP or OAS pension or benefit applications, a request can be sent to the responsible regional office to verify if the foreign number was provided on the application form. This is particularly recommended for cases of deceased or incapacitated clients who may have provided their foreign numbers at the time of application for Canadian benefits but had not made this information available on the current application. In cases where it is not possible to obtain the foreign institution number, you must provide as much client information as possible on the liaison request (e.g. name at birth, alternate names, specific place of birth).

topic_title: Guidelines for communicating with a foreign institution
text: When communicating with a foreign institution using a liaison form, adhere to the below guidelines: Do not use abbreviations (e.g. DOD, NOK). Avoid handwritten comments. A separate liaison form must be prepared for the first and second requests for information. Always indicat e on the form that it is a second request. Indicate "unknown" in the foreign reference number field on the liaison if the number cannot be obtained. If certain elements of a client's data are unknown or not clear, review the documentation in the file to determine if the information can be located (e.g. a client's date or place of birth could be located on a passport or a spouse's name could be found on a marriage certificate). Always use standard phrasing in the Other or Other remarks field of the form when it's available.

text: Many of the European Union countries will request that International Operations respond to their request using the Certificate concerning insurance history in <Country> (E 205) form , which is a form used within the European Union Agreements to exchange information such as creditable periods. The Request for information, communication of information, request for forms, reminder on an employed person, self-employed person, a frontier worker, a pensioner, an unemployed person, a dependant (E 001) form is often attached to the letter for requesting that the Department provide the E 205 form. As long as an International Social Security Agreement exists with the country making the request, complete a liaison in response and provide the information to the foreign agency address. For all other situations (i.e. requests that are not received on the E 205 form), return the request with a liaison including the following in the Other or Other remarks field: "Please note that form <form code or name> is not applicable under the Canada/<name of the requesting country> Social Security Agreement. topic_title: Receiving information from a foreign institution
text: When a liaison is received from a foreign institution, it must be reviewed to determine if the information provided is in response to a request made b y International Operations (IO) or a request made on behalf of a regional processing centre. If not, you must determine if the information impacts the administration of a CPP or OAS pension or benefit, paid in either IO or a regional processing centre. If the information could impact a Canadian pension or benefit administered in a regional processing site, you must send an email that outlines the information to the applicable site's general delivery mailbox. Example A foreign survivor benefit protective date is received from the other country. You must review the effective date of the Canadian IO-SVR pension to determine if the client could be eligible for an earlier effective date based on the protective date. Example A non-restrictive country provides a decision advising that the client's foreign retirement pension application was approved. A review of ITRDS shows that the client is currently in pay for a GIS benefit through a regional processing centre. As most income from foreign pensions is considered in the calculation of GIS benefits, an email must be sent to the applicable processing cen tre to provide any information that was received (e.g. effective date of the benefit, current or historical rates). If the information was received from a liaison from an International Social Security Agreement partner with sharing restrictions (i.e. Jamaica, Japan and the United States), the information ca nnot be shared outside of IO. For more information, International Operations—Sharing information obtained under an International Social Security Agreement (Knowledge) If foreign creditable periods (contributions and/or residence) are received from the foreign institution, they must be added to Cúram. If new client information is received (e.g. updated address, date of death) for a client that has Canadian benefit activity, you must continue to update the International Agreements system in addition to updating Cúram.

topic_title: Responding to a request for information from a foreign institution
text: The foreign social security offices will require information from Canada that will allow them to determine eligibility to one of their benefits or to maintain payment of existing benefits. The foreign institution will use their own liaison form to request any of the following: periods of contribution to the CPP and/or periods in receipt of a DSB ; periods of Canadian residence; Canadian pensions and benefit decisions and rates; date of receipt of a Canadian pension or benefit application (protective date); date of d eath and authorized representative information; current address; medical information on file; request for a medical examination to be arranged and a medical report be provided to the agreement country; and request to "start intergovernmental proceedings" (for the Austria agreement only). When responding to a request for information from a foreign institu tion, International Operations is responsible for: requesting clarification from the other country when their information request is not clear; collecting the requested information from the applicable system or client file; contacting the client for the requested information, if required; validating that the collected information is accurate; and sending the information on a completed liaison form to the appropriate social security agency and the correct office address. If the foreign institution is requesting more than one type of information, provide any information that is readily available or that will be available within a reasonable time frame. If you are unable to provide responses to all of the requests on the form, always advise the other country that the outstanding information will follow.

Canada Pension Plan (CPP) Enhancement - Questions & Answers for Service Canada Staff

On January 1, 2019, the Government of Canada began implementing the legislative changes to enhance the Canada Pension Plan (CPP). The legislative changes will be gradually implemented over a seven year period from 2019-2025. The QPP is being enhanced in a similar way as the CPP, allowing for alignment of enhanced benefits. The CPP and QPP are very similar by design, but are not identical.

If additional guidance is required, send an enquiry via the Business Expertise Request Tool by following normal channels. Business Expertise Request Tool If client enquires about the QPP enhancement, refer them to: RQ Website: https://www.rrq.gouv.qc.ca/en/programmes/regime_rentes/Pages/regime_rentes.aspx https://www.rrq.gouv.qc.ca/en/programmes/regime_rentes/Pages/regime_rentes.aspx Québec Pension Plan (QPP) Toll-free Telephone Number: 1 800 463-5185 If you receive correspondence in reference to QPP enhancement, follow existing procedure for transfer to Retraite Québec.

For information about the payment date of the enhanced portion of CPP benefits, please advise CPP recipients that, if they made valid contributions in 2019 or later, they will receive the enhanced portion of the CPP benefits, as well as any retroactive amounts from when they began to collect their benefit once system changes are implemented.

Effective October 29, 2021, Retraite Québec (RQ) will begin paying first additional enhanced QPP benefits, as well as any retroactive amounts, to eligible clients. Details of the enhanced QPP payment roll-out will be posted on the RQ website in the coming weeks. Work is ongoing to implement all necessary system changes related to the CPP enhancement (for more details please refer to SDB-795 - Enhancement to the Canada Pension Plan ). SDB-795 - Enhancement to the Canada Pension Plan While the implementation timelines for the enhanced portion of the CPP and QPP may vary due to jurisdiction, legislative and system differences, CPP recipients will receive the enhanced portion of the CPP benefits, as well as any retroactive amounts from when they began to collect their benefit (if they made valid contributions in January 2019 or later) once system changes are implemented.

topic_title: Accepting and processing the ISP3041 form when received before the event occurs
text: The following table provides you with guidelines for accepting and processing a Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP3041) form that is received before the event. Table 2 Type of Optionable Event Guidelines for accepting and processing the ISP3041 Retirement Do not accept the ISP3041 if you are processing it before the event occurs. A client can change their mind and decide to postpone or cancel their retirement. If they do not advise the Department, this could result in an overpayment. If the ISP3041 was received before the event and the event date has not passed at the time of processing: Complete the work item in PWS. Return the ISP3041 along with the Option, includes estate (129) denial letter to the client, advising them to resubmit the form once they have retired. Update ITRDS Notes. If the ISP3041 was received before the event but the event date has passed at the time of processing: Contact the client to confirm that they did retire and that any other information provided on the statement is still accurate. Complete a Telephone Call (ISP0112) form with the details of the conversation: If they did retire, continue processing the option. If they did not retire, deny the option request. Update ITRDS Notes. Reduction in CPP or QPP Pension Income For a CPP beneficiary, you can accept the ISP3041 form before the event. You can confirm the amount of the CPP entitlement and date of change in ITRDS. Bring Forward (BF) the ISP3041 until the event date. After the event has occurred, confirm the details of the event with ITRDS. Call the client to confirm any other information reported on the statement, if required. Continue processing the option. For a QPP beneficiary, you can accept the ISP3041 before the event if the client received written notification from the QPP Pension Office and has the date of the reduction details and the new amount. Refer to Reduction in other pension income below. Reduction in other pension income For reductions in other pension income, you can accept the ISP3041 before the event if the client indicates by telephone or in writing, that they have received a written notice (e.g. Registered Retirement Income Fund statement or letter of notification from the other pension office) that provides the effective date (i.e. future date) of the reduction and the new reduced pension amount. Scenario no. 1 The event is in the future and is recorded on the option form. Call the client and confirm the event date. Ask the client if they received a notification letter from their pension office outlining the details of their event (effective date and reduced amount). Complete an ISP0112 form and ask the client to send in the notification letter. BF the option until the effective date of the event. Review ITRDS Notes or PWS to determine if the notification letter or response from the foreign agency (for IO only) has been received. If yes , continue processing the option. If no , call the client to confirm the details of the event (i.e. event date and benefit rates) and any other information provided on the statement. Complete an ISP0112 form and continue processing the option. If you are unable to reach the client by phone, or are unable to confirm the event details, send a letter requesting a copy of the notification letter and indicate that the option cannot be processed until that confirmation has been received. Once you receive confirmation, or if the client calls in to the call centre and confirms the event details, continue processing the option. Scenario no. 2 The event is in the future and is not recorded on the option form: Add a Future Option Date to the system or set a manual BF to send a new form to the client when the event has actually occurred. The entitlement will then be recalculated when the option has been returned. Scenario no. 3 The form was received prior to the event, but the event has now occurred and is recorded on the option form. If the notification letter has been received confirming the details of the event, continue processing the option. If the notification letter has not been received, call the client to confirm the details reported on the statement. Complete an ISP0112 form and continue processing the option. If you cannot reach the client by phone, or were unable to confirm the details on the statement during the call, send a letter requesting confirmation of the event details (i.e. a copy of the notification letter) and indicate that the option cannot be processed until that confirmation has been received. Once confirmation is received or if the client calls in to the call centre and confirms the event details, continue processing the option. Simplification Improvement Strategies—Options and Income

topic_title: Sending the ISP3041 form before the event occurs
text: The following table provides you with guidelines for sending out the Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP3041) form prior to an event or not. Table 1 Type of Optionable Event Guidelines on sending the ISP3041 Retirement Do not send the ISP3041 prior to the event occurring. A client can change their mind and decide to postpone or cancel their retirement. If they do not advise the Department , this could result in an overpayment. Reduction in CPP or QPP Pension Income For a CPP beneficiary, you can send the ISP3041 form prior to the event. You can confirm the amount of the CPP entitlement and the date of the change in ITRDS. For a QPP beneficiary, do not send the ISP3041 form prior to the event if the details cannot be confirmed. Quebec processing staff do not have access to view the QPP entitlement or the effective date. However, if the client is receiving both QPP and CPP (dual), these details can be confirmed in ITRDS. If the client received written notification from the QPP Pension Office and has the date of the reduction details and the new amount, go to Reduction in other pension income below. Reduction in other pension income If a client indicates by telephone or in writing, that they have received a written notice (e.g. Registered Retirement Income Fund statement or letter of notification from the other pension office) that provides the effective date (i.e. future date) of the reduction and the new reduced pension amount, you can send the ISP3041 form prior to the event. In this case, you must ask the client to return a copy of their statement or letter of notification with the completed ISP3041 form. Update ITRDS notes to show that the ISP3041 form was sent prior to the event as the client has supporting documents that they will provide when returning the ISP3041 form to Service Canada. If you receive only a copy of the client’s statement or letter of notification and it includes the details described above, you can send an ISP3041 form to the client prior to the reduction occurring. Update ITRDS notes to show that the ISP3041 form was sent prior to the event as the client has provided supporting documentation that contains the effective date of the reduction and the new reduced pension amount. In both Steps 1 and 2 , the copy of the client’s statement or letter of notification from the pension office will allow you to verify if the client correctly estimated their income. This will avoid an overpayment situation.

topic_title: Client automatically enrolled for a RTR pension or OAS pension
text: When the corresponding pension is an RTR pension or OAS pension, a protective date cannot be obtained if the requirement to submit the application was waived. An applicant is not required to submit an application when they are proactively enrolled for: an RTR pension through RTR70 Proactive Enrolment; or an OAS pension through Automatic Enrolment. The Department proactively enrols clients who are aged 70 or over and have not yet applied for an RTR pension to which they are entitled. When the client has been proactively enrolled, it will be indicated in ITRDS notes. When a client is automatically enrolled for an OAS pension, the enrolment process (i.e. selection criteria) does not obtain or capture the client's record of foreign residence or work. Automatic enrollment can be identified when the value is Yes i n the OAS Automatic Enrolment field on the OAS Automatic Enrolment screen in ITRDS.

To apply the protective date provision, the client must have applied for a Canadian benefit that corresponds to the benefit in the other country. When the foreign institution requests the date of receipt or date of claim of an application for Canadian benefits, they will identify the type of foreign benefit on the liaison form. When providing a foreign institution with the date of receipt of an application for Canadian benefits, you must first identify the type of benefit(s) for which the client has applied for in the agreement country. Many protective date provisions include a requirement that states that the applicant must have indicated periods of residence or employment under the legislation of the other country on the application for the corresponding pension or benefit. This is known within International Operations as "intent". Depending on the terms of an International Social Security Agreement, intent is e stablished when an applicant: indicates they lived or worked in the other country on their corresponding Canadian pension or benefit application; or requests that the application be considered an application under the legislation of the other country. There are several ways a client can demonstrate intent on a Canadian benefit application. OAS and CPP pension and benefit application forms contain specific fields that question if the applicant has resided or worked in another country. This includ es separate residence statements received during the course of processing, as these statements are considered a part of the application once they have been receive d.

For paper applications, the date of receipt is the earliest Department date stamp on the corresponding Canadian pension or benefit application, or a deemed date of application that has been established. The date of application for an online application is the timestamp on which the applicant submitted it through their My Service Canada Account. For more information, Applications Date of Receipt (Policy) Paper applications The receipt date of a paper application is normally found in PWS or on the ITRDS Benefits screen. If the receipt date cannot be determined through either system, it must be requested from the appropriate processing center or determined based on the application in the International Operations (IO) file. If intent is required, the application must be reviewed to determine if the client indicated the applicable country on the application. This includes applications that were processed in IO and a reg ional processing centre. Online applications The details of an online application, including information provided by the applicant regarding periods of work and employment in another country, ma y be available through ITRDS or PWS . If the application cannot be accessed online, a request for the information must be sent to the applicable regional processing centre. OAS pension applications made online can be retrieved by selecting the GoL (Government Online) link in ITRDS on the applicable client's account. The application details can be viewed on the OAS and GIS Application(s) - Details screen in GoL . For more information on accessing online C PP applications, Online Applications for CPP (Knowledge)

The protective date provision stipulates that the date on which an application for a benefit is received in one country is considered the date of application for the corresponding benefit in the other country, if certain conditions are met. For more information, Protective Date Provision Under an International Social Security Agreement (Knowledge) Protective date information can be provided to foreign institutions to accompany foreign benefit applications or in response to a liaison request. Foreign institutions will use this information to establish the effective date for a benefit in that country. When a client is in pay for a corresponding pension or benefit under the jurisdiction of QPP and an Understanding is in force, the Bureau des ententes de sécurité sociale is responsible for reporting the protective date for that pension or benefit to the foreign institution. Denial or approval of a Canadian pension or benefit application has no bearing when providing a protective date to a foreign institution. If the conditions of the protective date provision have been met, a protective date can be provided to the foreign institution regardless if the application has been approved, denied or is under review. To report a valid protective date to a foreign institution, you must ensure that the date meets all of the conditions as outlined by that country's International Social Security Agreement (ISSA).

International Operations (IO) staff provides an individual's personal information such as address, date of death and legal representation after death: to be sent with an individual's application for foreign benefits; when sending a request for information to the foreign institution; or in response to requests from foreign institutions. All countries paying social security benefits want to ensure that they maintain accurate and current information for all of their clients. When an International Social Security Agreement (ISSA) partner is unable to contact a client, the liaison agency will contact IO to obtain current information for that client. In some situations, the liaison agency has been unable to contact the client as that client is now deceased. As a result, agreement countries may need information about a client’s date of death and/or their estate information. Request to provide a client's address Foreign institutions of agreement countries will request confirmation of a client's current address when they are unable to contact the client at the address that they have on their file. A foreign institution may also request confirmation of a client's address to ensure that their records are accurate. When they request information, the foreign institution will normally provide the address of the client from their records. When providing an address to the foreign institution, you must provide both the home and mailing address if they differ. If the client's mailing address is set up in care of a trustee, you must also provide the trustee's name with the address. Request to provide date of death or legal representation after death information In Canada and in most ISSA countries, social security benefits are available to the spouse, children or the next of kin of a deceased contributor or pensioner. As a result, agreement countries may request the deceased’s date of death and the contact information of the legal representative. When the date of death is validated by CPP, OAS or IO, the information will appear in ITRDS on the Client Profile screen. If the date of death is provided by provincial vital statistics, ITRDS will display the source as SIR-PRV C . When the date of death is validated by one program, it can be accepted by another unless there is an indication of a discrepancy. If legal representation after death has been validated, the information will be captured on: the Address block on the Client Profile screen in ITRDS; the Contact / Applicant screen in ITRDS; the Evidence tab in Cúram as Third Party Contact evidence; and ITRDS notes.

Canadian residence under the OAS Act will already be established when: the client is in pay for an OAS pension, ALW or ALWS benefit; or residence information was previously provided to a foreign institution. Canadian residence established for an OAS pension If a client's application for an OAS pension was approved, or there is an application in progress, residence information will be available from the client's file (either within International Operations (IO) or a regional processing centre). If residence information is being requested from a regional processing centre, you must request that they electronically provide you the start and end dates of all residence periods that were used to determine the client's eligibility. When providing Canadian residence on the liaison form, the last day reported will be: the day prior to the OAS effective date, if the applicant was living in Canada at the effective date; or the last day of residence in Canada, if the applicant was living outside of Canada at the effective date. Canadian residence previously validated for an ALW or ALWS benefit When Canadian residence has already been established for an ALW or ALWS benefit, residence in Canada will continue to accumulate beyond the effective date of the benefit, as long as the client continues to reside in Canada. For that reason, you may be required to validate the client's residence to the present date before providing the residence on the liaison form. Canadian residence can only be provided to the current date if it has been confirmed that the client continued to reside in Canada after the effective date of their ALW or ALWS benefit. Canadian residence previously validated for foreign benefit or liaison purposes A client’s residence information may be present in the IO file if a foreign institution previously requested the same information. When this occurs, you must ensure that the residence information on the file is accurate and up to date before providing a response.

topic_title: Reporting Canadian residence on the liaison form
text: In certain cases, the periods of residence reported on the liaison form is impacted by the client's CPP contributions. Based on the terms of the agreement, reporting periods of Canadian residence could be limited by: the overlap with CPP creditable periods; or the number of CPP creditable years. Example A request is received from the Spanish foreign institution for a client's Canadian residence and CPP creditable periods. The client's residence in Canada is established from September 15, 1990, to December 15, 2000, and they have valid CPP contributions from 1991 to 2000. Since Spain will not consider periods of Canadian residence that overlap with CPP contributions, the residence will be reported on the liaison form from September 15, 1990, to December 31, 1990. Any periods after that date would overlap with the CPP contributions. When Canadian residence is required as part of a liaison request, review the liaison form to determine if the foreign benefit type the information is required for is stated. If the benefit type is known, refer to the applicable country's Foreign benefit manual tab and follow the Canadian residence guidelines for that benefit type. If the foreign benefit is unknown, provide all periods of residence in Canada after age 18.

International Social Security Agreements (ISSA) may establish eligibility to a foreign pension by giving consideration to periods of residence in Canada that have been established under the OAS Act. Unless instructed otherwise under the terms of an ISSA, all periods of residence that meet the definition of "residence" under the OAS Act must be provided to foreign institutions when transferring a foreign benefit application or when responding to a request for this information. This includes periods during which a client does not fulfill the Canadian legal status requirement or periods that are not long enough to establish the right to an OAS pension or benefit (i.e. periods of less than one year). Many ISSAs contain a provision within the administrative arrangements which allows a country to request the preparation of a medical examination for an applicant or beneficiary residing in the other country. The country requesting the medical examination will use this information to establish entitlement to a benefit or to maintain entitlement to an existing benefit. Foreign institutions will req uest that Interna tional Operations (IO) arrange medical examinations for clients residing in Canada. When a medical examination request is received, IO will be responsible for: communicating the request to the client on behalf of the foreign institution; acknowledging the receipt of the request by completing the appropriate section of the liaison form; communicating the progress of the medical examination to the foreign institution; sending the medical report to the foreign institution; and forwarding the doctor's invoice to facilitate payment and reimbursement from the foreign institution. Under the terms of the medical examination provisions, the cost of the medical examination will be the responsibility of the requesting country. When a medical report is received from the doctor or spec ialist, they must also provide the Department with an invoice for the cost of performing the examination. Upon receipt of the invoice, IO National Headquarters will arrange reimbursement from the foreign institution. When a client is under the jurisdiction of the QPP and an Understanding is in force, the Bureau des ententes de sécurité sociale is responsible for responding to the medical examination request. However, if the client is under the jurisdiction of QPP and there is no Understanding in force, IO will arrange the medical examination request. Arranging medical examinations When a medical examination request is received in IO, you must ensure that the foreign institution specifies the type of doctor or specialist that will conduct the medical examination. The client will be advised to schedule an appointment with the required type of doctor or specialist, or obtain a referral from their family doctor for the required type of doctor or specialist, if required. The foreign institution may also specify certain requirements in their request for the medical examination. This can include that the medical examination be completed by an independent doctor (i.e. by a doctor that has not previously treated the client) or that the doctor complete specific medical report forms (e.g. the Austrian Care Benefit Expert's Report form). The Foreign Medical - Acknowledge appointment to client (ISS-6600) letter advises the client of the medical examination request and any specific requirements requested by the foreign institution. The letter includes the following forms that must be completed by the client: Medical Examination Authorization Service Canada’s copy form; and Medical Examination Authorization Physician's copy form. The Medical Examination Authorization forms obtains the client's consent to undergo the medical examination and the authorization to release their medical information to the Department and foreign institution. This consent and authorization must be obtained in order to facilitate the medical examination request. Once advised of the medical examination request, the client will be responsible for: obtaining a referral for a specialist or independent doctor (if required); scheduling the medical examination appointment; and forwarding the required forms to the doctor.

text: There are various ways to report pension or benefit rates, depending on the country you are reporting to and the situation. topic_title: Provide a Canadian pension or benefit decision
text: A "decision" refers to the outcome (i.e. approval or denial) of a Canadian pension or benefit application. You must provide a decision to an agreement country when: a liaison form from the foreign institution requesting notification of decision has been received; or the terms of the agreement requires International Operations to inform the other country of decisions. In certain cases, you will only need to send the decision if the application for Canadian pension or benefits has originated from a foreign institution. Applications for Canadian benefits that are forwarded through the foreign institution will normally be on an agreement-specific application form and may: have a liaison form attached; have a foreign liaison agency date stamp; have the client's biographical data certified on the application form by the foreign institution; and/or be accompanied by documentation that is certified by the foreign institution. A decision may also be required for OAS or CPP pension or benefit applications that did not require an International Social Security Agreement to qualify. In cases where the application was transferred to a regional processing centre, the decision must still be sent once the application has been finalized. When providing the decision for a finalized application, you must provide the decision as well as all Canadian pension and benefit amounts that the client is receiving and identify those that are currently suspended. If the foreign institution requests the status (or "decision", "outcome", etc.) of a specific Canadian pension or benefit that is not in pay, you must provide the reason why.

topic_title: Respond to a request for Canadian pension or benefit rates
text: When Canadian pension or benefit rates are requested by a foreign institution, you must provide information for all pensions and benefits in pay, including those that are currently suspended. You must also advise the foreign institution when a Canadian pension or benefit application has been received but is not yet finalized; however, you are not required to place the liaison on hold while awaiting completion of the application. If the foreign institution does not specify from what date they require the rates from, provide the current amounts only. When you are reporting retroactive rates to the foreign institution, report the current rate or rate at the effective date (as required) on the liaison form and attach a record of historical rates.

topic_title: Sending Canadian pension and benefit information with a foreign benefit application
text: When sending Canadian pension or benefit information with a foreign benefit application, you must provide all Canadian pension and benefit amounts that the client is receiving and identify those that are currently suspended. You must also advise the foreign institution when a Canadian pension or benefit application has been received but is not yet finalized; however, you are not required to place the liaison on hold while awaiting completion of the application. Each country outlines the Canadian pension or benefit information you must provide to the responsible foreign institution along with a foreign benefit application. You may be required to provide: the current rate of payment; the rate from a specific date; or the rate from the effective date.

text: The XXX/Canada Agreement - Application for a Canadian Old Age, Retirement and Survivors Benefits (ISP-5054-XXX) form may be used to apply for multiple pensions and benefits at the same time. When a benefit or pension does not require an ISSA to meet eligibility requirements, you must send the original ISP-5054-XXX form to the responsible region.
