The date on which an application is received can impact the applicant's effective date. This protective date provision is only beneficial to applicants who do not apply within 11 months of their first possible effective date and will therefore not receive the maximum retroactive payments to which they could have received if they had applied on time. Example A client would have been eligible for an OAS pension in M ay 2021 based on their Canadian residence, legal status and age. However, they did not submit an application until April 15, 2023. If a protective date is not applied, the earliest effective date for the pension is May 2022 (i.e. 11 months prior to the date of application). The ISSA country confirms a protective date of August 9, 2021. Using this date as the date of application for the OAS pension, the applicant's pension can be approved effective May 2021. There are no limitations associated with how long the protective date predates the first possible effective date. As long as the protective date is after the date of entry into force of the agreement, it can be applied to the corresponding Canadian benefit application. Example The applicant applied for an OAS pension in May 2023 at age 68, but would have met the eligibility requireme nts (i.e. age, residence and legal status) had they applied in March 2020, the month in which they turned 65. The other country provides a protective date of January 11, 2016. Despite the applicant having applied for the corresponding foreign benefit at age 60, the protective date can still be applied to the OAS pension application. Since a protective date is deemed to be the date of receipt of a Canadian pension or benefit application for administration purposes, the same rules surrounding retroactivity will apply using that date.

topic_title: Deferral of Canadian pensions and benefits
text: Although a foreign institution may provide the Department with a valid protective date for the corresponding foreign benefit, it cannot be used if the applicant selected a start date after their first possible eligibility date, unless a protective date would be required to approve the application at the requested start date. Example A client applies for an OAS pension on June 15, 2023. On the application, they request a pension start date of January 2022. After reviewing the file, it is determined that the applicant could have been eligible in November 2021, the month after the month in which they had obtained 10 years of residence in Canada (and met the age and legal status requirements). Based on OAS retroactivity rules, the pension could normally only be effective July 2022. A protective date based on a foreign retirement application is received with the date October 15, 2021. Using this date as the date of the OAS application, the pension can be effective in January 2022.

Under OAS and CPP legislation, there are limitations based on when an application for pensions or benefits can be submitted on behalf of a deceased individual. If an application is not received within the prescribed time-frame for that pension or benefit (normally one year from the individual's death), the application would normally be denied. For more information, Post-Mortem Applications (Policy) However, if the deceased had applied for the corresponding foreign benefit prior to their death, a protective date could be applied. If there is a valid protective date that predates the date of death or the date of receipt of the post-mortem application, that date is considered to be the date of application when determining eligibility and entitlement. Example A post-mortem RTR pension application is received on March 15, 2023, on behalf of an individual that died on November 9, 2021. The foreign institution provides a protective date of April 23, 2020. For administrative purposes, including those related to system input, the date of application is now April 23, 2020.

Under certain International Social Security Agreements (ISSA), the only applicable condition is that the client must have applied for the corresponding benefit in the other country. However, most ISSAs will also contain one or more of the following conditions to establish a valid protective date: At the time of application, the applicant must have indicated periods of employment or residence in the other cou ntry (i.e. show ing "intent" on an application). Example An appli cant submits an Application for Canada Pension Plan Disability Benefits (ISP1151) form and indicates a period of residence in the applicable country. The applicant is not required to provide any additional information or details on the application form to satisfy to the conditi on. The applicant requests that the Canadian pension or benefit application be considered an application under the legislation of the other country. Example An applicant submits an Application for the Old Age Security Pension and the Guaranteed Income Supplement (ISP3550) fo rm. On the application, the applicant states that they wish to use the ISP3550 form to also apply for a German retirement pension. The date of receipt of an application for benefits must be after the date of entry into force of the agreement. Example The Canada/Albania ISSA came into force on August 1, 2022. A client applies for an Albanian survivor pension on February 15, 2020, and indicates periods of employment in Canada on the application. Since the Albanian pension application was received before the agreement came into force, it cannot be considered a valid protective date when establishing eligibility to a Canadian SVR pension.

A protective date provided by a foreign social security institution under an International Social Security Agreement (ISSA) with Canada can assist clients in qualifying for a benefit earlier than the effective date based on the date stamp of their application.

A protective date provision is included in many of Canada’s ISSAs. In general, this provision stipulates that the date on which an application for a pension or benefit is received in one country is deemed to be the date of application for the corresponding benefit in the other country, if certain conditions are met. The protective date provision varies by agreem ent, and each agreement will outline the conditions that must be met for the protective date provision to apply. If an ISSA does not contain a protective date provision, the date of receipt is established with OAS a nd CPP rules only. To determine if an ISSA contains a protective date provision, International Social Security Agreement Country List

This process will focus on single ( MS1 ) and widowed ( MS8 and MS9 ) clients who make up about 45% of clients submitting options. Entitlement to income-tested benefits is based on the income received for the previous calendar year. If a client or their spouse or common-law partner retires or suffers a loss of pension income, their current income may not be as high as it was in the previous calendar year. To lessen the financial impact, the OAS Act allows the client or their spouse or common-law partner to request to have their benefit entitlement calculated based on an estimate of their income for the current calendar year instead of their income from the previous year. This is called an option and it is granted if it is to their advantage.

The CPP Credit Split is a provision allowing the equal division of CPP contributions accumulated by both the applicant and their former spouse or common-law partner while they were living together. Service Canada currently receives applications for the CPP Credit Split only via the paper Application for Canada Pension Plan Credit Split (upon separation or divorce) (ISP1901) form or by written communication. Effective October 29, 2021, individuals can choose to apply online for the CPP Credit Split using their My Service Canada Account (MSCA). The online CPP Credit Split application does not replace the ISP1901 form. It is another channel eligible applicants can use to apply for the provision. The online CPP Credit Split application contains a dynamic component that displays appropriate application questions based on the information input by the applicant. The automated process is designed to assist the regional processing centres with processing Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Reassessment reports. During thi s process, the income is adjusted and an overpayment or underpayment letter is sent to the client. These automated letters are saved in the Corporate Correspondence Tool letter vault and are accessible by specific authorized individuals. The accounts considered for this process are active MS 1 , 2 , 3 , 8 and 9 with a 3017 work item in Auto status in PWS. The automated process will: identify 3017 work items in PWS that are Unassigned with an Auto status; assign the work item in PWS to the BOT, which means Robotic Process Automation. The list of grave medical conditions was introduced in 2012 to assist in identifying files of applicants with grave medical conditions to expedite their application process. The list represents severe and rapidly progressive conditions that have been found to have a high probability of meeting the eligibility requirements for CPP DSB benefits. Income and Social Security Development’s Medical Expertise Division reviews the list every 2-3 years to ensure continued medical relevance and accuracy. The review methodology for these revisions included analysis of the fast-track processes in other jurisdictions (e.g. United States and Australia), stakeholder feedback and grant rates by medical condition. The addition of these conditions is not expected to impact the Department’s ability to meet service standards. A minimal increase in the volume of grave condition applications is anticipated (estimated at approximately 2000 additional files per year). The impact of these changes will be closely monitored and evaluated post implementation. If additional guidance is required, send an enquiry to the Operational Service Desk

The Minister can rescind or reduce a penalty amount, after the penalty has been imposed, in the following situations: on the presentation of new facts; on being satisfied that the penalty was imposed without knowledge of some material fact, or on the basis of a mistake; on being satisfied that the penalty cannot be collected within the reasonably foreseeable future; or on being satisfied that payment of the penalty will cause undue hardship to the debtor. A penalty amount can be reduced to zero, but the penalty is still considered to have been imposed.

text: Employment and Social Development Canada currently has 61 Information Sharing Agreements (ISAs) with federal, provincial and territorial partners under the CPP and OAS programs. These agreements (irrespective of them being identified as an agreement, arrangement, memorandum of understanding, letter of agreement, letter of concurrence, etc.) are considered written records of understanding between government parties that outline the terms and conditions, including the specific data elements, under which personal information is shared between the parties. The CPP and OAS Delivery Support team has created tools to ensure standards related to the disclosure of personal information are in place for federal, provincial and territorial agreements. These documents will provide guidance on information sharing practices with federal, provincial and territorial partners. Service Canada employees must protect the personal information of clients and are responsible for ensuring that the collection, retention, use and disclosure of client information comply with all standards and directives as they pertain to the protection of sensitive information. Employees must review the tools before responding to enquiries from federal, provincial or territorial partners under an ISA. Information shared outside the scope of an ISA is considered a privacy breach. topic_title: Examples—Assessing the mitigating circumstances and determining the penalty percentage reduction amount
text: Table 3. Situation Mitigating circumstances Level of significance % Reduction amount Rationale for % Reduction amount The individual admits to the misrepresentation immediately and offers to repay the overpayment. During the investigation, the individual expresses genuine remorse and fully cooperates. Factors present at the time of the misrepresentation: none Factors present at the time of the investigation or when the penalty is being imposed: immediately admits to the misrepresentation; offers to repay the overpayment; expresses genuine remorse; and fully cooperates during the investigation. Moderately significant 40% The individual's actions from the beginning of the investigation were positive. Their immediate admission of the misrepresentation, the offer to repay the overpayment and cooperation and the offer to repay the overpayment saved the Department a lot of time, effort and money. Their genuine remorse indicates that they have been deterred from committing subsequent misrepresentations. The individual reluctantly admits to the misrepresentation at the end of the investigation after they are presented with all of the evidence. Factors present at the time of the misrepresentation: none Factors present at the time of the investigation or when the penalty is being imposed: admits to the misrepresentation but only after all of the evidence is presented Moderately significant 10% The fact that the individual eventually admitted to the misrepresentation saved the Department some time, effort and money in building the case. However, further reduction is not warranted given they had several opportunities to confess during the investigation but only admitted once all of the evidence was presented. The individual admits to having misrepresented their marital status halfway through the investigation. They promise that they deeply regret the whole thing and will not do it again. The individual states that they misrepresented because they had recently became unemployed and were going to lose their home. This is where they care continuously for their mentally and physically disabled sister who has no income of their own. The individual thoroughly describes the circumstances surrounding their various hardships and how they viewed their misrepresentation as their only way out. Situations or factors present at the time of the misrepresentation: they became unemployed; they were going to lose their home where they care for their sister; their sister is mentally and physically disabled and has no income of their own; and due to their various hardships, they felt it was their only way out. Situations or factors present at the time of the investigation or when the penalty is being imposed: admits to the misrepresentation halfway through the investigation; they regret their actions but felt it was their only way out at the time; and promises they will not do it again. Significant 60% The fact that the individual admitted to the misrepresentation halfway through the investigation saved the Department time, effort and money in building the case. The genuine remorse and promise not to misrepresent again makes a subsequent misrepresentation unlikely. The individual's statements on their financial, employment, housing and family situations describe serious challenges that significantly help explain why they misrepresented. The individual states they did not disclose their foreign income to the Department for 10 years because they were in the hospital. When asked how long they were in the hospital and why, they stated they were in the hospital for 4 months because they had liver issues. Situations or factors present at the time of the misrepresentation: none Situations or factors present at the time of the investigation or when the penalty is being imposed: none No mitigating circumstances 0% Although the individual stated they were in the hospital for 4 months, it does not help explain why they did not disclose their foreign income to the Department for 10 years. Therefore, it is not a mitigating circumstance and it does not warrant a reduction of the penalty amount. During the investigation, it was discovered that the individual misrepresented their martital status as separated to receive more GIS. However, their husband states they are still together. The individual never admits to the misrepresentations and maintains they are separated. Family members state they are being manipulated by their son who has severe addiction and mental health issues and is completely alienated from the rest of the family. The family states that they are using the extra money to provide for their son. A thorough assessment of both types of mitigating circumstances is important to establishing the penalty percentage reduction amount. You must use your judgment and critical thinking to determine the level of significance of the circumstances. All decisions are made on a case-by-case basis. If an individual claims the same mitigating circumstances on a subsequent misrepresentation, you have the discretion to accept or deny them as valid in each case. You must consider the individual's particular situation and all relevant circumstances, as a whole , when assigning a percentage. When assessing mitigating circumstances consider the following: state of mental health, illness or depression (consider the severity); personal medical circumstances; illness of a family member; addiction (e.g. gambling, alcohol or drug related); dealing with a death of a spouse, relative or close friend; individual's admission (e.g. Did they admit to the misrepresentation? If so, was it early in the investigation or at the end? ); individual's remorse (e.g. Did they express any regret about the misrepresentation? If so, to what degree? ); cooperation and assistance with the investigation (e.g. Did they cooperate during the investigation or were they resistant in providing information? ); offers repayment; and other debt obligations. Once you have determined the mitigating circumstances, you will use the scale below to assess the significance of these circumstances in the individual's situation, from no mitigating circumstances to very significant. This scale is broken down by 10% increments: Table 2. Level of significance % of reduction increments No mitigating circumstances 0% (full penalty amount) Moderately significant 10% to 40% (reduction of penalty amount) Significant 50% to 70% (reduction of penalty amount) Very significant 80% to 100% (reduction of penalty amount)

topic_title: Situations or factors present at the time of the investigation or when the penalty is being imposed
text: There may also be situations or factors that are present at the time of the investigation or when the penalty is being imposed. The following situations or factors can be considered as mitigating circumstances when the individual: expresses genuine regret or remorse; admits to the misrepresentation without resistance or further misrepresentation; or cooperates or assists in the investigation (e.g. providing documentation or information). There may also be cases where you will not find any mitigating circumstances after reviewing the Report of Investigation. However, you must also consider situations or factors that may develop after the misrepresentation occurred but are present when the penalty is being imposed. You must determine if the penalty should be reduced based on the circumstances of each case. For example, an individual becomes medically incapable or incapacitated and now lacks the ability to understand right from wrong. In this case, a 100% penalty reduction may be applied as imposing a penalty to this individual would not be considered as a deterrent. You will still impose the penalty, but the amount would be $0.00.

topic_title: Situations or factors present at the time of the misrepresentation
text: There must be clear indication that mitigating circumstances existed.The information surrounding these circumstances must be identified and documented by the Integrity Services Branch in their Report of Investigation. To be considered a mitigating circumstance, the situations or factors must: be present at the time of misrepresentation; be credible; and help explain the individual's actions. The following examples are situations or factors that can be considered as mitigating circumstances that may support the reduction of a penalty amount: Table 1. Category Mitigating circumstance examples Physical or mental illness serious illness of an immediate family member or close relative; medical circumstances or conditions of the individual; or compulsive disorders (e.g. addictions, gambling, drug or alcohol dependency). Emotional death of a spouse, common-law partner, immediate family member or close relative; physical, mental or financial abuse by a spouse, partner, family member etc.; or loss of income due to separation from spouse or common-law partner. Other individual demonstrates an urgent need for money due to personal or family circumstances; personal theft; other debt obligations; or state of emergency (wildfires, flooding, earthquakes, etc.).
Mitigating circumstances need to be assessed to determine the reduction to be applied to a penalty amount.

topic_title: Jurisdiction to medically adjudicate a subsequent application Updated
text: When reviewing a subsequent application, you must determine if you have the jurisdiction to adjudicate it. You have full jurisdiction to adjudicate a subsequent application if the following apply: the decision on the last application, assessment or reassessment is final; the period to request a reconsideration or an appeal is expired; and the Minister was the last decision-maker. You do not have jurisdiction to adjudicate a subsequent application if the earlier application is still active. An application is active if the decision is pending or the reconsideration or appeal period has not expired at the following stages: an application; an assessment or reassessment; a request for an extension of the 90-day time limit to request a reconsideration; a request for new facts; or a claim of Erroneous Advice/Administrative Error. If a previous decision-maker was the SST , the former Review Tribunal, or the former Pension Appeals Board, you may not have jurisdiction to adjudicate or you may have limited jurisdiction. You do not have jurisdiction if a tribunal has already determined the applicant did not meet the severe and prolonged criteria by the Latest Possible Date of Onset (LPDOO) on that application and the LPDOO is the same on the subsequent application. The decision is res judicata . Additionally, there is no jurisdiction if a tribunal considered a cease decision on a previous application and the LPDOO on the subsequent application is before the cease effective date. If the LPDOO considered by the tribunal was after the hearing date or has changed with the subsequent application, you have limited jurisdiction called a jurisdictional window. You must determine if the severe and prolonged criteria were met within the jurisdictional window. Refer to the Adjudicate the subsequent application when the previous application was denied—Medical Adjudicator section below or to Medical Adjudication of a Subsequent Application (Policy) KA-04735 (article not available). If the tribunal only considered the DSB , there may be full jurisdiction for the PRDB . If you require assistance in determining if you have jurisdiction on a subsequent application, submit a request through the Business Expertise Request Tool (BERT) Internal link . Business Expertise Request Tool If the applicant meets the eligibility criteria on the subsequent application, the Date of Onset (DOO) must be tied to the application being adjudicated. The DOO cannot be more than 15 months prior to the receipt date of the current application, or 12 months for applicants who received a CPPD benefit within the last five years. National Headquarters: prior to National Administrative Penalties Committee review Prior to the National Administrative Penalties Committee (NAPC) reviewing the proposed recommendations to impose a penalty, staff in CPP and OAS at National Headquarters (NHQ) will: Review the Report of Investigation (ROI), the electronic versions (not scanned) of the final Administrative Penalty Recommendation (ISP-0114) form and the draft of the penalty notification letter and recommend changes, if applicable. Prepare the agenda and cover page for the NAPC meeting. Upload these documents in the NAPC Meetings section of the SharePoint site along with the ROI, the ISP-0114 form, the draft of the penalty notification letter and all related attachments. Send a meeting reminder to the NAPC members, including the link to the NAPC SharePoint site, 5 business days prior to the meeting. National Administrative Penalties Committee Case presenters make recommendations based on relevant legislation, policies, investigations and evidence on file for each case presented. They also refer policy or legislative clarifications to the appropriate NAPC member, if required. Director Generals review and determine if a penalty case should be developed further before making a final decision. They may also endorse the penalty recommendations. National Headquarters: After National Administrative Penalties Committee decision Prepare the meeting minutes and upload them to the NAPC SharePoint site. Inform the Benefits Delivery Services's (BDS) Business Expertise Consultant (BEC) of the NAPC's decisions for action on the file by sending them the signed cover page. Input the penalty and related overpayment information in the Penalties Access database. Return the file to the appropriate BDS BEC. If the NAPC determines that a penalty case needs to be developed further before making a final decision, NHQ staff will coordinate with the appropriate area and ensure the file returns to the NAPC as soon as possible. Benefits Delivery Services Region: After National Administrative Penalties Committee decision After the NAPC's decision, the BDS BEC will do the following: Review the NAPC's decision and contacts BDS NHQ if clarifications are required. Every year, tens of thousands of seniors have their Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS), Allowance (ALW) or Allowance for the Survivor (ALWS) benefit increased or decreased to reflect changes in their net income. As these benefits are calculated on the basis of the previous year's income, any change in income in a given year will result in an adjustment of benefits in the following July to June payment period. Pandemic-related benefits, such as the Canada Emergency Response Benefit (CERB), the Employment Insurance Emergency Response Benefit (EI ERB) and the Canada Recovery Benefit (CRB) are considered taxable income. This means that CERB or CRB benefits that were received in 2020 could impact a person's GIS, ALW, or ALWS benefit entitlement for the July 2021 to June 2022 payment period. On December 14, 2021, the Government of Canada announced that a targeted one-time payment will be issued to assist seniors who have had their GIS, ALW, or ALWS benefit entitlement impacted negatively by pandemic-related benefits. Details of the one-time payment (e.g. the amount and issue date) are in the process of being determined and will be communicated at a later date.
A one-time payment will be issued to income-tested benefit recipients whose entitlement was negatively impacted by receiving pandemic-related benefits.

The operational policy Documentary Evidence—Marital Status was updated as a result of feedback received. An individual does not have to be in receipt of the GIS in order to be approved for the GIS. An individual who is approved for the GIS and has the GIS for Life Status may not be in receipt of the GIS (e.g. due to excess income). Foreign marriage dissolution —This section was added as it was missed when the information was transferred from the Functional Guidance Procedure to the KMT platform. Acceptable documentary evidence for living separate and apart while under the same roof —Information was added in a note to clarify that for situations where the documentary evidence obtained for the separation contains sufficient information to support the claim of living separate and apart while under the same roof, no additional documentary evidence is required.

The Re-calculation Input (CAL) screen summarizes payment and entitlement details, both historical and current, for OAS clients. Therefore, the CAL screen must be as accurate as possible at all times. The account is in balance when the Re-Calculated Net value at the bottom of the CAL screen shows NIL . An account is out of balance when the Re-Calculated Net value is not NIL . Out of balance accounts must be reviewed for mispayments, underpayments and overpayments. You must review each case individually and follow the Delegation of Authority (PDF, 677 KB) as per usual business processes. Delegation of Authority Out of balance OAS Online accounts In certain situations, an out of balance OAS Online account is acceptable and will be considered balanced. An account can only remain out of balance if it contains one of the following exceptions: a valid underpayment exists and the client cannot be located; a valid underpayment exists and no designated payee has been established (may apply to both deceased and living clients); a valid overpayment amount of $100,000 and over exists and the account is not being recommended for remission or write off; or the account is a Bill C-31 account with manually calculated retroactive adjustments and the adjustments have not yet been made in the system. An Out of Balance CAL screen may indicate one of the following possibilities (not an exhaustive list): the revised entitlement criteria or adjustments were entered inaccurately, but all payments issued were accurate; the account is a Bill C-31 account and retroactive adjustments were manually calculated; the client may have outstanding underpayments; the client may have outstanding overpayments that have not been identified on the Deductions (DED) screen for collection, remission or write-off; an adjustment has been made to the account for periods prior to January 1998; or the system may have created an invalid out of balance issue if the account was dropped from the Masterfile and was later recreated. When the account is recreated, an invalid underpayment is created for each January that the account was missing from the Masterfile. In certain situations, clients were at risk of financial instability due to circumstances beyond their control and the required income was not received in order to renew their income-tested benefits, e.g. in the Guaranteed Income Supplement, Allowance and Allowance for the Survivor. In these cases, either the payment income or the payment amount was carried forward from the prior payment period in order to minimize the impact. These situations resulted in temporary mispayments that you must adjust if it is not already resolved. The dates for these situations are: April to June 1998, implementation of the modified payment period. 1997 income had not yet been received and 1996 income was brought forward to pay income-tested benefits. July to December 2020, COVID-19: Guaranteed Income Supplement Renewal 2020 Measures—Procedures 2019 income had not yet been received and the June 2020 payment amount was brought forward to pay income-tested benefits. The CPP Record of Earnings (ROE) work items will be sent for automation. These items are then placed in Auto status in PWS . Where possible, re-adjudication of benefits, monetary actions, and resulting client letters, will be automated. Automated process For CPP ROE work items in PWS with Auto status, the automated process will complete the following: Search PWS for any other work items that exist on the account with Active or On Hold status. Review ITRDS notes for Third Party , Integrity and Remission keywords. Re-adjudicate CPP benefits. Validate the monetary in CPMS : Release suspended payables. Apply payables to pending or active receivables. Set a recovery rate on pending receivables of 25% (10% if income-tested benefits are in pay) of the total CPP benefit amount payable to the client. Send a letter advising the client of underpayments or overpayments and planned recovery start dates. Add a note in ITRDS . Update the work item status in PWS to: Active , if manual intervention is required; BF , if any receivable was adjusted by $0.01; or Completed , if no manual intervention is required. Review manually to adjust the recovery rate and start date after the 60-day BF Period . text: The client began withdrawing quarterly payments from their Registered Retirement Income Fund (RRIF) in 2017. In July 2020, the client reduced the amount of their quarterly RRIF payments. The following payments were received from 2019 – 2021: Regular and Predetermined RRIF Payments: 2019 Month RRIF Withdrawals January $500.00 April $500.00 July $500.00 October $500.00 Total for year 2019 $2,000.00 Regular and Predetermined RRIF Payments: 2020 Month RRIF Withdrawals January $500.00 April $500.00 July $400.00 October $400.00 Total for year 2020 $1,800.00 Regular and Predetermined RRIF Payments: 2021 Month RRIF Withdrawals January $400.00 April $400.00 July $400.00 October $400.00 Total for year 2021 $1,600.00 The current year option was processed effective the beginning of the quarter in which the first reduced payment was received. Since the first reduced payment was received in July 2020, the option is effective July 2020. A previous year option was also processed effective July 2021.

topic_title: Example 2—Regular and Predetermined RRIF Payments (Quarterly with Change to Monthly)
text: The client began withdrawing quarterly payments from their Registered Retirement Income Fund (RRIF) in 2019. In June 2020, the client reduced the amount of their payments and changed the payment frequency to monthly. The following payments were received from 2019 – 2021: Regular and Predetermined RRIF Payments: 2019 Month RRIF Withdrawals January $1,000.00 April $1,000.00 July $1,000.00 October $1,000.00 Total for year 2019 $4,000.00 Regular and Predetermined RRIF Payments: 2020 Month RRIF Withdrawals January $1,000.00 April $1,000.00 June $250.00 July $250.00 August $250.00 September $250.00 October $250.00 November $250.00 December $250.00 Total for year 2020 $3,750.00 Regular and Predetermined RRIF Payments: 2021 Month RRIF Withdrawals January $250.00 February $250.00 March $250.00 April $250.00 May $250.00 June $250.00 July $250.00 August $250.00 September $250.00 October $250.00 Novemer $250.00 December $250.00 Total for year 2021 $3,000.00 In this scenario, the client changed their quarterly payments to monthly. The client has also reduced their RRIF income. A current year option was processed effective July 2020. Although the client began receiving a lesser rate starting in June 2020, their option was effective in July 2020 because they had been receiving payments in quarterly instalments, and the payment for the April to June quarter had already been received in addition to the monthly payment for June. Therefore, the client's option was effective the first quarter in which a loss was suffered. A previous year option was also processed effective July 2021.

The client began withdrawing annual payments from their Registered Retirement Income Fund (RRIF) in 2019. In August 2021, the client withdrew the final payment, depleting the fund. This option was calculated again and applied for July 2022 to June 2023. Since this event is effective in January, there is no option for the July 2023 to June 2024 payment year.

When a lump sum payment is not the only optionable event in the current payment period, it is considered a multiple event lump sum payment. Since there are multiple events in the same calendar year, the lump sum payment can be considered an event in this year. However, processing of an option depends on when the lump sum is received in relation to the other events. Example 1—Lump sum payment received prior to another Optionable Event The following table shows the events and their options: The lump sum payment was received in February 2020. The pension was reduced in July 2020. The pension ended effective December 2020 (the final payment was received in November 2020). The current and previous year options are being processed together in August 2021. Table 3. Multiple event lump sum payments—Example 1 Event Option Event 1: Lump Sum Payment The client received the lump sum payment in February 2020, which is in the July 2019 to June 2020 payment period. Their entitlement to income-tested benefits for this period is based on their 2018 income. Therefore the client's entitlement is not affected by the lump sum payment at this time. The current year option is not calculated at the time the lump sum payment is received. The lump sum is considered a single event lump sum payment until another optionable event takes place in the same calendar year. Event 2: Pension Reduction Since a second optionable event has now taken place in the same calendar year, the lump sum event that was previously not considered, will now be affected when calculating the current year option for this reduction; therefore you must remove it from the estimate. The current year option is calculated for July 2020 to November 2020. Estimated Income (2020) includes: reduced pension pro-rated (amount after reduction for 5 months) no lump sum Event 3: Pension Terminated The current year option is calculated for December 2020 to June 2021. Estimated Income (2020) includes: no pension no lump sum The previous year option is calculated for July 2021 to June 2022. Estimated Income (2021) includes: no pension no lump sum Example 2—Lump sum payment received after another Optionable Event The pension was reduced in February 2021. The pension ended effective August 2021 (the final payment was received in July 2021). The lump sum was received in October 2021. The current and previous year options are processed together in June 2022. The following table shows the events and their options: Table 4. Estimated Income (2021) includes: reduced pension pro-rated (reduced rate for 6 months, no pension for 5 months) the lump sum The current year option is recalculated for the new payment year, for July 2021 using the estimated income above. Event 2: Pension Terminated The current year option is calculated for August 2021 to October 2021. Estimated Income (2021) includes: lump sum no pension income Event 3: Lump Sum Payment The current year option is calculated for November 2021 to June 2022. The following examples describe how to prorate income with various payment frequencies in a current year option situation, where the income must be included in the estimate.

topic_title: Foreign pension income received monthly with additional payments
text: Certain countries (e.g. Portugal and the Philippines) issue their pension payments monthly but with an additional one or two payments issued per year, for a total of 13 or 14 payments received annually. Review the applicable country in the list of International Social Security Agreements Countries to determine if there are any irregularities in the foreign pension payments that need to be considered. International Social Security Agreements Countries Formula When the client is in receipt of a foreign pension that is paid in 13 or 14 monthly payments and reports the monthly pension amount in Canadian dollars on the ISP3041 form, multiply the Canadian dollar monthly amount by 13 or 14, then divide by 12 to arrive at a monthly average. If it is reported in anything other than the Canadian dollar, multiply the monthly amount of the foreign pension by the payment frequency (13 or 14) and then multiply that by the exchange rate and divide by 12 to obtain the monthly Canadian dollar equivalent. For information on obtaining current exchange rates, Foreign Currency Conversion Information Requests Multiply the monthly average by the number of months the benefit was received from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year, divided by the number of months from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year and multiplied by 12.

topic_title: Monthly pension rate varies during the year
text: Formula The monthly amount of the benefit rate #1 multiplied by the number of months the benefit was received at that rate from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year, plus the monthly amount of the benefit rate #2 multiplied by the number of months the benefit was received at that rate from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year, divided by the number of months from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year and multiplied by 12.

Before you prorate the income using the formula, you must convert the annual payment into a calculated monthly amount. Formula The calculated monthly amount of the payment multiplied by the number of months the benefit is received from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year, divided by the number of months from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year and multiplied by 12.

topic_title: Pension income received bi-weekly (every two weeks for a maximum of 26 payments per year)
text: Before you prorate the income using the formula, you must convert the bi-weekly payments into a calculated monthly amount. Formula The calculated monthly amount of the benefit multiplied by the number of months the benefit is received from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year, divided by the number of months from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year and multiplied by 12.

Before you prorate the income using the formula, you must convert the irregular payments into a calculated monthly amount. Formula The calculated monthly amount of the payments multiplied by the number of months the benefit is received from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year, divided by the number of months from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year and multiplied by 12.

Formula The monthly amount of the benefit multiplied by the number of months the benefit was received from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year, divided by the number of months from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year and multiplied by 12.

Before you prorate the income using the formula, you must convert the quarterly payments into a calculated monthly amount. Formula The calculated monthly amount of the benefit multiplied by the number of months the benefit is received from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year, divided by the number of months from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year and multiplied by 12.

Before you prorate the income using the formula, you must convert the semi-annual payments into a calculated monthly amount. Formula The calculated monthly amount of the benefit multiplied by the number of months the benefit is received from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year, divided by the number of months from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year and multiplied by 12.

topic_title: Pension income received semi-monthly (for a maximum of 24 payments per year)
text: Formula The semi-monthly amount of the benefit multiplied by 2, multiplied by the number of months the benefit is received from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year, divided by the number of months from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year and multiplied by 12.

Formula The weekly amount of the benefit multiplied by the number of weeks the benefit is received from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year, divided by the number of months from the effective month of the option until the end of the calendar year and multiplied by 12. Calculate the estimated amount of the pension or benefit according to the above formula. Calculate the amount that could be received if the client was paid this amount for all 52 weeks of the year. Compare Step 1 and Step 2. You must always use the lesser amount.

topic_title: Adding a CPP Record of Earnings update lump sum event to a Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form
text: If it is determined that a CPP Record of Earnings (ROE) update lump sum payment was received, you may add the payment as an event to a previously received statement of estimated income for the same year without calling the client or requesting a new Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form in certain situations.

topic_title: Adding an event to the Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form
text: If a Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form has been received and there is an indication that an event has occurred or will occur for the same calendar year, but has not been recorded on the form, confirm the details of the event over the phone and add them to the form even if the event is in the future.

topic_title: Adding an event to the Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form
text: When you are processing a Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form and you have identified or have been informed of an event for the same calendar year as the option, but the event is not recorded on the form, proceed as follows: If the event has already occurred: Call the client to confirm the details of the event. If CPP is the source, details can be confirmed through ITRDS and CPMS . Confirm with the client that the remaining income reported on the form has not changed and advise them that you will be adding this event to the statement. Add the details of the event to ITRDS Notes. Complete and retain a detailed Telephone Call (ISP-0112) form; and Process the option including the event as confirmed by the client. Refer to Estimated Income (Options) (Scenario) . Estimated Income (Options) (Scenario) If the event has not yet occurred: Call the client to confirm the details of the event. Add the details of the event to ITRDS Notes. Complete and retain a detailed ISP-0112 form. If the client has received a notification letter outlining the event details of their pension, ask the client to send a copy of the notification letter to the Department. Defer the option in Cúram until the event date so it can be calculated and added to the system at that time. Refer to Bring Forward (BF) (Action) . Bring Forward (BF) (Action) At the BF date, review Cúram and ITRDS notes to determine if the notification letter was received (if requested). If the notification letter has been received, confirm the details of the event and process the option. If the notification letter has not been received or the client did not receive a notification letter for their event (i.e. retirement), call the client to confirm that the event details and all other information on the statement have not changed. Process the option. Refer to Estimated Income (Options) (Scenario) . Estimated Income (Options) (Scenario) Update ITRDS notes and complete the tasks in Cúram.

topic_title: Moving income from one block to another on the Statement of Income
text: If you suspect that the client or applicant reported income in an incorrect block on an Application for the Guaranteed Income Supplement with Statement of Income (ISP-3025B) form or a Statement of income for the Guaranteed Income Supplement, the Allowance or Allowance for the Survivor for payment period of July (20XX) to June (20XX) with Information Sheet (ISP-3026) form, the income can be moved to the correct block if: It is clear when comparing with the income information provided by the CRA or another reliable source that the applicant or client reported the income in the wrong block on the form; and There is no change to the GIS, ALW or ALWS entitlement.

topic_title: Moving income from one block to another on the Statement of Income
text: When you are processing an Application for the Guaranteed Income Supplement with Statement of Income ( ISP-3025B) form or a Statement of income for the Guaranteed Income Supplement, the Allowance or Allowance for the Survivor for payment period of July (20XX) to June (20XX) with Information Sheet (ISP-3026) form and you identify that the client has reported their income on an incorrect line in the income section, proceed as follows: Review the income breakdown from the CRA to confirm the income. If the CRA income is unavailable or unclear, review Cúram and ITRDS notes to determine if there is information from another reliable source on file to confirm the income. If the income is clearly identified as being on an incorrect line and there is no change to the client’s entitlement by making the correction, make the amendment in Cúram by manually entering the income on the correct line. Add the details of the change to ITRDS Notes. Refer to Manually Entered Income Evidence—Add, Edit, View and Delete in Cúram (Action) . Manually Entered Income Evidence—Add, Edit, View and Delete in Cúram (Action) If the income cannot be confirmed with the CRA income, the information on file or in the systems, or there would be a change to the entitlement, go to Step 2 . Step 2 Contact the client to clarify the discrepancy before making any changes to the income.

topic_title: Options and a CPP Record of Earnings update lump sum
text: If you determine that the client received a lump sum CPP payment due to an update to the Record of Earnings, proceed as follows: Access ITRDS and CPMS to review the details of the lump sum payment. Confirm that the Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form you are processing is for the same year that the CPP lump sum payment was received by the client. If yes, include the lump sum payment as an additional event on the form without calling the client or obtaining a new form. If no, go to Step 3 . Step 3 Check to see if the event date is still within the timeframes prescribed under the OAS Act to send an ISP-3041 form. Refer to Time Limit Tables for Submission of Statement of Estimated Income . If yes, send a new ISP-3041 form for the appropriate estimate year. If no, no further action is required, as it is too late to calculate the client's entitlement on an estimate. Time Limit Tables for Submission of Statement of Estimated Income Continue processing the ISP-3041 form. Refer to Estimated Income (Options) (Scenario) . Estimated Income (Options) (Scenario)

The person who elected to split their pension will have a deduction on line 21000 and the person who received the pension will have the corresponding amount displayed on line 116000. topic_title: Waiving the requirement for a current year Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form
text: Where a current year option could be considered, the Department will waive the requirement for a Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form when: an ISP-3041 form for the previous year option has been received by the Department within the timeframes prescribed under the OAS Act for both the current and previous year option. Refer to Time Limit Tables for Submission of a Statement of Estimated Income ; Time Limit Tables for Submission of a Statement of Estimated Income the CRA income or a statement of income for that year has already been received by the Department; and the details of the event can be confirmed over the phone and they match the income information provided by the CRA .

topic_title: Waiving the requirement for a current year option
text: When you process a Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form for a previous year option and there is entitlement to a current year option for the same event, proceed as follows: Review Cúram to determine if the applicable ISP-3041 form for the current year option has been received by the Department. If it has been received, retrieve it and process as usual. If it has not been received, confirm that the previous year option form was received by the Department within the timeframes prescribed under the OAS Act for both the current and previous year option. If yes, go to Step 2 . Step 2 If no, the requirement for an ISP-3041 form for the current year option cannot be waived. Review Cúram and ITRDS notes to determine if the CRA income or a statement of income has been received by the Department for the required taxation years. If yes, go to Step 3 . Step 3 If no, the requirement for an ISP-3041 form for the current year option cannot be waived. Review the income required for the current year option calculation. For more information, refer to Estimated Income (Options) (Scenario) . If you have all the required information to perform an accurate proration calculation on all pension income (before or after event monthly rate breakdown, event date, etc.), calculate the current year estimate and make any necessary adjustments to the client's account, then go to Step 6 . Step 6 If you do not have the required information to perform an accurate proration calculation on all pension income, contact the client by phone to obtain the following details, then go to Step 4 : The gross amount of the pension or benefit after the event; The gross amount of the pension or benefit prior to the event; and The start and end date or date of reduction of the pension or benefit. Step 4 Estimated Income (Options) (Scenario) Ensure these details align with the total income for that pension or benefit as provided by the CRA or from a Statement of Income for that year. Complete and retain a detailed Telephone Call (ISP-0112) form. Indicate the following in ITRDS Notes: “The requirement for a current year ISP3041 form for YYYY was waived in accordance with the Simplification Improvement Strategies—Options and Income (KA-05021)” Send the appropriate letter.

topic_title: Waiving the requirement for a GIS or ALWS (Pension Income Splitting - Change in Marital Status situation - Consent to remove a transferred amount) (ISP-3032) form or a GIS or ALW (Pension Income Splitting - Option situation - Consent to remove a transferred amount) (ISP-3034) form
text: Where it has been determined that a beneficiary has been disadvantaged by the Pension Income Split provision, the Department will not require a new statement of income or a GIS or ALWS (Pension Income Splitting - Change in Marital Status situation - Consent to remove a transferred amount) (ISP-3032) form or a GIS or ALW (Pension Income Splitting - Option situation - Consent to remove a transferred amount) (ISP-3034) form if: the applicable CRA income has been received by the Department; and the pension income split amounts can be easily identified. The client must be notified in writing of the changes to their entitlement. This simplification improvement strategy applies to situations when: a client’s spouse or common-law partner has died; a couple separates or divorces; and a pension income split has a negative impact in relation to estimated income for an option.

topic_title: Waiving the requirement for a previous year option
text: When you process a Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form for a current year option and there is entitlement to a previous year option for the same event, proceed as follows: Review Cúram to determine if the applicable ISP-3041 form for the previous year option has been received by the Department. If it has been received, retrieve it and process as usual. If it has not been received, confirm that the current year option form was received by the Department within the timeframes prescribed under the OAS Act for both the current and previous year option. If yes, go to Step 2 . Step 2 If no, the requirement for an ISP-3041 form for the previous year option cannot be waived. Review Cúram and ITRDS Notes to determine if the CRA income or a statement of income has been received by the Department for the required taxation year. If yes, go to Step 3 . Step 3 If no, the requirement for an ISP-3041 form for the previous year option cannot be waived. With the available income information, calculate the previous year estimate using the event details found on the current year option form and make any necessary adjustments to the client's account. Refer to Estimated Income (Options) (Scenario) . Estimated Income (Options) (Scenario) Indicate the following in ITRDS Notes: "The requirement for a previous year ISP-3041 form for YYYY was waived in accordance with the Simplification Improvement Strategies—Options and Income (KA-05021)." Send the appropriate letter.

text: Where a previous year option could be considered, the Department will waive the requirement for a Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form when: an ISP-3041 form for the current year option has been received by the Department within the timeframes prescribed under the OAS Act for both the current and previous year option. Simplification improvement strategies have been developed to simplify processing options and income statements where information about past income may no longer be readily available to clients or where information may already be available to the Department. Where all conditions have been met, the following simplification improvement strategies can be applied at the time of processing the option. Where the simplification measure cannot be applied, or further information is required for processing, you must consult and apply the respective procedure. For more information, Options (Policy)

The optionable event is a reduction in pension income in March 2021. Current year option form The Department must receive the current year option form (estimating the 2021 income) by June 30, 2023 . The event occurs in the July 2020 to June 2021 payment period, therefore July 2021 to June 2022 is the first payment period after the event and July 2022 to June 2023 is the second payment period after the event. Previous year option form The Department must receive the previous year option form (estimating the 2022 income) by June 30, 2024 . The event occurs in the July 2020 to June 2021 payment period. The effective date of the previous year option is July 2022, which is during the July 2022 to June 2023 payment year and July 2023 to June 2024 is the following payment period.

The optionable event is the retirement in October 2020. Current year option form The Department must receive the current year option form (estimating the 2020 income) by June 30, 2023 . The event occurs in the July 2020 to June 2021 payment period, therefore July 2021 to June 2022 is the first payment period after the event and July 2022 to June 2023 is the second payment period after the event. Previous year option form The Department must receive the previous year option form (estimating the 2021 income) by June 30, 2023 . The event occurs in the July 2020 to June 2021 payment period. The effective date of the previous year option is July 2021, which is during the July 2021 to June 2022 payment year and July 2022 to June 2023 is the following payment period.

The optionable event is the retirement in December 2021. Since the effective date for this option is January 2022, the full estimate calculation is completed using the 2022 estimated income. A second form is not required. The Department must receive the option form (estimating the 2022 income) by June 30, 2024 . The event occurs in the July 2021 to June 2022 payment period and is recalculated effective July 2022. Therefore the payment period effective July 2022 is July 2022 to June 2023 and the payment period following that effective date is July 2023 to June 2024.

topic_title: Example 4—Termination of pension income in January
text: The optionable event is the termination of pension income in January 2021. The client received their last payment in December 2020. Since the effective date for this option is January 2021, the full estimate calculation is completed using the 2021 estimated income. A second form is not required. The Department must receive the option form (estimating the 2021 income) by June 30, 2023 . The event occurs in the July 2020 to June 2021 payment period, and is recalculated effective July 2021. Therefore, the payment period effective July 2021 is July 2021 to June 2022 and the payment period following that effective date is July 2022 to June 2023.

topic_title: Example 5—Current year option form received too late
text: The optionable event is a reduction in pension income in April 2019. The received date of the current year option form (estimating the 2019 income) is February 17, 2022. Current year option form The Department must receive the current year option form (estimating the 2019 income) by June 30, 2021 . The event occurs in the July 2018 to June 2019 payment period, therefore July 2019 to June 2020 is the first payment period after the event and July 2020 to June 2021 is the second payment period after the event. This option form is received too late and must be denied. Previous year option form The Department must receive the previous year option form (estimating the 2020 income) by June 30, 2022 . The event occurs in the July 2018 to June 2019 payment period. The effective date of the previous year option is July 2020, which is during the July 2020 to June 2021 payment year and July 2021 to June 2022 is the following payment period. If the Department receives the previous year option form (estimating the 2020 income) by June 30, 2022, it can be processed.

As part of the Economic and Fiscal Update 2021 , the Government announced it would provide a one-time, non-taxable grant to alleviate financial hardship of Guaranteed Income Supplement ( GIS ) and Allowance ( ALW ) recipients who received pandemic benefits in 2020. Economic and Fiscal Update 2021 In July 2021, some GIS and ALW /Allowance for the Survivor recipients experienced a reduction or loss of benefits because of receiving pandemic payments in 2020. The amount of an individual's grant payment varied and corresponded to the annualized amount of their reduction or loss in GIS / ALW benefits. The recipient's monthly benefit loss was determined by comparing the maximum monthly reduction of GIS / ALW payments between June 2021 and July 2021 using March 2022 data. Once the maximum monthly reduction was established, the amount was multiplied by 12. The one-time grant was equal to the total 12-month reduction or loss of the GIS or ALW monthly payment amount. The grant payment was issued automatically in April 2022, and without the need for an application. Some grant payments were issued manually for dire need situations in March 2022 and some grant payments were issued between May 2022 and March 2023 for individuals who would become retroactively entitled to it. The one-time grant was not an OAS payment; it was issued under separate authorities. Eligibility To be entitled for the grant payment, individuals must have been eligible for the GIS or an GIS / ALW as of March 2022. These individuals must also have: received (or had a spouse/common-law partner who received) a "pandemic benefit" in 2020. A pandemic benefit is defined as one of the following benefits: the Canada Emergency Response Benefit; the Employment Insurance Emergency Response Benefit; the Canada Recovery Benefit; the Canada Recovery Sickness Benefit; or the Canada Recovery Caregiving Benefit. been in receipt of GIS and ALW benefits in June 2021 (or received a GIS and an ALW benefit in respect of June 2021); and experienced a reduction or loss in GIS and ALW benefits in July 2021. One-time grant details Overpayments Any overpaid grant payments may be reviewed under existing departmental collection policies. The Department will not attempt to recover the one-time grant payment from an estate when the GIS and ALW recipient dies before March 2022, but the Department is only notified after issuing the one-time grant payment. Agents are not required to calculate the amount of the grant payment, nor to validate the amount. If you come across a situation where you believe an overpayment may have occurred because you have reason to believe the client did not meet the eligibility criteria, send an enquiry via the Business Expertise Request Tool by following normal channels for next steps. Business Expertise Request Tool Return of payment If a GIS and ALW recipient does not wish to receive the grant payment, they may be directed to write a cheque payable to the Receiver General for Canada, or donate it to a charity of their choice. The pensioner must include a covering note, which should include their Social Insurance Number, name, contact information and the reason for returning the payment. A disclosure is the act of an individual or third party voluntarily notifying the Department that they have knowingly withheld information or misrepresented information provided to the CPP or OAS program.

The CPP and OAS Acts are separate pieces of legislation and each program must be treated individually, therefore, the disclosure is program-specific. Unless the individual informs the Department that they provided the same false information to both programs and now wish to correct this, any information they disclose regarding one program cannot automatically be considered as a disclosure to correct the same information under the other program. If you receive a written or verbal disclosure where the individual comes forward with information that they did not divulge during previous dealings with the Department, you must refer it to the Integrity Services Branch (ISB). If the client makes a verbal disclosure during the course of regular processing, you must clearly document the information provided. Use neutral and objective language to report the issue exactly as it has been described by the individual. You must not use words such as "fraud" or "abuse" unless the individual specifically uses these words. You may also receive a disclosure that the client provided to a Service Canada Centre, Call Centre or via correspondence. ISB will review the details of the disclosure, determine if it is valid and then conduct an investigation. Earnings attributed after a Credit Split may help an individual meet the MQP for a DTH benefit, SVR pension or Surviving Child's benefit. A Credit Split is approved effective the last day of the month the request or application was received. This is the effective date of the division of pensionable earnings. The attribution of pensionable earnings is effective the first day of the month following the month the division takes place. Therefore, when considering the earnings attributed after a Credit Split, the MQP cannot be met in the same month the division takes place. Earnings attributed as a result of a Credit Split can be used to meet the MQP the month following the month the Credit Split is approved. For the DTH benefit, the applicant must submit a new DTH benefit application with a receipt date after the date of attribution, unless they have requested a reconsideration of the initial DTH benefit application.

topic_title: Earnings not posted on the Record of Earnings
text: Interim earnings are earnings that have not yet been posted by the CRA but are needed for an applicant to qualify for a DTH benefit, SVR pension or Surviving Child's benefit. Interim earnings are included in the manual calculation of the MQP once they have been verified. Evidence of the contributor's earnings and contributions for the effective year of the benefit and the previous year is mandatory if such evidence is required to establish the MQP provided under the legislation for a DTH benefit, SVR pension or Surviving Child's benefit. Additional earnings that are not posted to the applicant's Record of Earnings could potentially impact the MQP. These employment earnings not related to wages or salary could include, but are not limited to: paid vacation leave; self-employed earnings; or shareholdings. For more information, CPP Earnings and Contributions (Policy)

Foreign creditable periods under a valid ISSA can be used to meet the MQP when determining eligibility to a CPP benefit. When totalizing CPP contributions or Dual CPP and QPP contributions with foreign creditable periods under an ISSA, the contributions are added to the foreign creditable periods. The ISSA must allow for totalizing the DTH benefit, SVR pension or Surviving Child's benefit. For the DTH benefit, the date of death must occur after the date the ISSA came into force. The foreign institution is the primary source for the individual's foreign creditable periods being totalized under the ISSA. If a client provides evidence of their foreign creditable periods, you can accept the evidence under certain circumstances. In all cases, International Operations must receive an acceptable breakdown of foreign creditable periods to determine eligibility under an ISSA.

All CPP benefits end the month following the client's death. Payments are made for the month in which the client dies, regardless of the day of the month on which the death occurs. When the Department is informed about a client's death, a Death Notification work item is created on a deceased client's account in PWS .

Call Centre, In-Person, and processing centre staff create a Death Notification work item in PWS . National Headquarters has undertaken a National Time Study to update the timings used for resource allocation to the regions. Previous real-time timing methods did not distinguish various complexities and age of many work items. Many regions identified gaps or inconsistencies in traditional timings. In an effort to bridge these gaps and ensure a more comprehensive overview of the work accomplished within all regions, the National Time Study used a new In Progress status in PWS between April 4 and August 31, 2022 to capture timings to support the Resource Determination Model. During the National Time Study, 82% of the target sample size was reached as some work items have a longer than average processing timeframe, are cyclical in nature or are more complex and take many months to complete. Re-enabling the PWS In Progress status until the full implementation of Cúram will enable the National Time Study team to: increase the accuracy of the timings; capture data on work items with larger processing timeframes; and capture timings for the work items that were missed during the initial National Time Study that was undertaken from April 4 to August 31, 2022.

Effective Date: April 3, 2023 Effective April 3, 2023, the In Progress status will be available for all work types in the Status field of PWS . The objective of this status is to assist in the development of the Resource Determination Model by establishing processing times for all PWS work items.

When you are ready to begin processing a work item, complete the following steps in PWS : View the main work item activity you will be processing (application, appeal or a stand-alone maintenance item). Change the status from Active to In Progress . Save. Locate and retrieve any related and/or supporting work items to be matched to the main work item per current PWS Guidelines. All related and/or supporting work items should be changed to status Completed in accordance with PWS Guidelines. The main work item will remain status In Progress until you can no longer continue processing (examples below). The work item status must be changed to Active , On Hold or Completed when you are not actively processing the work item. All related and/or supporting work items will be included in the processing time; this means all effort is captured with the main work item set to In Progress . The work item will remain In Progress during the period of processing until the processing must stop. The following status must be used when processing starts: Table 1. What you need to do when process begins PWS Status Definition In Progress Processing: Work item processing begins as soon as there is intention to apply rules/policy/regulations and/or capture and gather information with the end goal of completing the work item. It includes all the work required for processing including but not limited to: Processing of related work items that were matched and completed. Review work item for process readiness. Request any supporting information or data. Writing letters. ITRDS notes. Calling clients. Reviewing Policy and Procedure. Discussion with co-worker regarding your work item. Processing may expand over several periods where the work item changes status representing the complexity of a work item. Normally processing is actioned by the Medical Adjudicator or Benefit Officers (PM-01, PM-02) and the Program Clerks (CR-03 and CR-04), depending on the Delegation of Authority and the work item. Any stand-alone work items are considered for processing. Example: change of address, disposition of a returned T4, applications or appeals. The work item will remain In Progress during the period of processing until the processing must stop for the following reasons: Breaks (includes lunch and/or regular breaks) ( Active ). The workday is ending and processing cannot continue ( Active ). Other work duties, work items, etc. become a priority ( Active ). Awaiting system updates, client information, etc. ( On Hold ). Item no longer requires processing ( Completed ). The following status must be used when processing stops: Table 2. What you need to do when processing stops PWS Status Definition Active Work Items that are assigned or unassigned that cannot be in status Complete or On Hold and cannot remain In Progress . On Hold Work Items where a client or a third party reply is requested, a BF date should always be set to ensure that work items are reviewed in a timely fashion. Completed Work items where all necessary actions have been taken and processing is finished. Examples using the new PWS status In Progress Application work item A client submits an application (main work item) to the Department with a receipt date of January 22, 2022. The work item in PWS for this application is created in Active status. The status remains Active until the processing employee is ready to review. The same client also submits correspondence with a receipt date of January 28, 2022, and direct deposit information with a receipt date of February 1, 2022. Once the main work item (application, appeal or a stand-alone maintenance item) is ready to be processed, the processing employee will set the status of the application to In Progress and save. The processing employee will then check PWS for any outstanding work that is matched and will be processed with the main work item. The processing employee will change the status for the correspondence or matched maintenance work item to Completed and perform all actions to process (including create any letters, system updates, ITRDS notes, etc.) The actions taken to process the correspondence will be captured as part of the main work item (application, appeal or a stand-alone maintenance item). Once processing is completed in its entirety, the processing employees will change the status to Completed . If additional information is required from the client, the processing employee will change the status to On Hold . If processing is stopped for one of the reasons identified above ( in section Reasons to change work items out of In Progress status ) , the processing employee will change the status to Active , save and then back into In Progress and save once the processing resumes. Maintenance work item A client submits direct deposit information to the Department with a receipt date of March 8, 2022. A PWS work item is created in Active status. The status remains Active until processing employee review. Once this work is ready to be processed, the processing employee will set the status of this work item to In Progress and perform all actions to process (including create any letters, system updates, ITRDS notes, etc.).
