Unlike the medical adjudication for a DSB , the Latest Possible Date of Onset for the medical adjudication for a PRDB will either be the month of the applicant’s 65th birthday, or May 4, 2023, which is the day prior to the amended legislation coming into force. For the PRDB , medical adjudication is to: determine if the applicant has a severe and prolonged disability as per the CPP; and establish a date on which the individual became disabled. The DOO for a PRDB cannot be earlier than: 15 months prior to the date of application; the effective date of the early CPP RTR pension; or January 2019. It is not necessary for the DOO or established DOO to be within the Minimum Qualifying Period (MQP) and can be outside of the MQP.

The purpose of medical adjudication is to: determine if the applicant has a severe and prolonged disability as per the CPP; and determine a Date of Onset (DOO). Regular PRDB applications To be eligible for the PRDB , the applicant must be found to be disabled on or before their Latest Possible Date of Onset (LPDOO) and their ERTR pension effective date must fall on or before their LPDOO. The DOO for the PRDB : must be on or before their LPDOO; cannot be earlier than the month of the applicant's ERTR pension effective date; can be up to 15 months before the receipt date of the DSB or PRDB application; and cannot be earlier than May 2023. Late PRDB applications The 3 following criteria must be met before a determination of severe and prolonged can occur: the applicant must have sufficient CPP contributions to establish an LPDOO; the LPDOO must be after April 30, 2023; and the effective date of the applicant's ERTR pension must fall before the LPDOO. Regardless of when their disability began, the applicant must be found to be disabled on or before their LPDOO and continue to meet the severe and prolonged CPPD criteria into the future. The applicant's established DOO must be: on or after the month of the effective date of their ERTR pension; after April 30, 2023; and on or before their LPDOO. The DOO for the PRDB cannot be: more than 15 months before the receipt date of the PRDB application; and earlier than May 2023 .

If the DOO or established DOO falls in May 2023, send these cases to National Headquarters via the Business Expertise Request Tool. In order to be eligible for the PRDB , the applicant must: be in receipt of their Early Retirement (ERTR) pension; have a contributory period; and be determined to be disabled as per the CPP. Refer to Non-Medical Eligibility—CPPD Benefits (Policy) January 2019. Non-Medical Eligibility—CPPD Benefits (Policy)

If the DOO or established DOO falls in May 2023, send these cases to National Headquarters via the Business Expertise Request Tool. The purpose of the PRDB is to provide protection to CPP RTR pensioners who have: been in pay for an Early Retirement (ERTR) pension for 15 months or more and have become disabled; or become disabled after starting to receive their ERTR pension. To be eligible for the PRDB , the applicant must: be in receipt of their ERTR; meet the contributory requirements; and be determined to be disabled within the meaning of the CPP. Refer to Non-Medical Eligibility—CPPD Benefits (Policy) May 5, 2023. Non-Medical Eligibility—CPPD Benefits (Policy)

The DSB and the PRDB are distinct benefits that require separate decisions at each level of adjudication. If the initial decision is only regarding eligibility for a DSB , the reconsideration request only applies to the DSB determination. In the case where both benefits are denied, the applicant can decide to request one or both decisions to be reconsidered together or separately. It is important to understand which decision the reconsideration request is related to, either the DSB , PRDB or both. If the applicant was not in pay for an ERTR pension at the time of the initial decision but is in pay at the time of the reconsideration, an Application for a Canada Pension Plan Post-Retirement Disability Benefit (ISP1170) form is required from the applicant before the adjudication of a PRDB at the initial level can occur. This decision will have its own reconsideration rights. It is possible in some cases that the DSB and PRDB applications may be at different appeal levels. Reconsideration (Policy)

The DSB and the PRDB are distinct benefits that require separate decisions at each level of adjudication. If the initial decision is only regarding eligibility for a DSB , the reconsideration request only applies to the DSB determination. In cases where both benefits are denied, the applicant can decide to request a reconsideration of one or both decisions together or separately. It is important to understand which decision the applicant's reconsideration request is related to: the DSB ; the PRDB ; or both. If the applicant was not in pay for an Early Retirement (ERTR) pension at the time of the initial decision, but the ERTR pension is in pay at the time of the reconsideration, the applicant must provide a completed, signed and dated Application for a Canada Pension Plan Post-Retirement Disability Benefit (ISP1170) form before the adjudication of a PRDB at the initial level can occur. The PRDB application decision will have its own reconsideration rights. It is possible that in some cases, the DSB and the PRDB applications may be at different appeal levels. Reconsideration (Policy)

The SST has no authority to hear a case on either DSB or PRDB unless the Minister has already made both an initial and reconsideration decision on the benefits. Following a reconsideration decision, individuals may request an appeal to the Social Security Tribunal—general division ( SST —GD). When an applicant files separate appeals to the SST —GD for the PRDB and DSB decisions, it is recommended the appeals be heard simultaneously.

The SST has no authority to hear a case on either the DSB nor the PRDB unless the Minister has already made both initial and reconsideration decisions on the benefits. Following a reconsideration decision, applicants may appeal to the SST —General Division ( SST —GD). When an applicant files separate appeals to the SST -GD for the PRDB and DSB decisions, it is recommended the appeals be heard by the SST at the same time.

Creditable periods under the legislation of Bulgaria consist of periods of insurance, which are linked to contributions to the Bulgarian social security system based on employment, as well as equivalent periods. topic_title: Application for an Estonian Incapacity for work Pension (CAN/EST 204)
text: Incapacity for work Pension—Application review Requirement Direction Completeness of application The applicant must complete the following sections: Section 2; Sections 3 to 11. Documentation The date and place of birth of the applicant must be verified on the liaison form based on information in ITRDS or documentation submitted by the applicant or on file. The applicant must submit originals or certified copies of the following documents to be sent to Estonia with the application: Birth certificate; For periods in Estonia before January 1, 1999: employment record books; when employment record books do not exist, other documents containing information about the working period (e.g. employment contract, letter of employment); diploma from a trade school, vocational secondary school or institute of higher learning; employment service certificate indicating receipt of unemployment benefits; employment service certificate indicating periods of participation in employment training; and military identity card. If before January 1, 1999, the insured cared for a category 1 disabled person, a disabled child or a person under 18 years of age who is disabled since childhood, a medical report and a statutory declaration signed by witnesses, indicating that the insured and disabled person or child lived together or other document supporting their living together; If before January 1, 1999, the insured cared for a child under age 3, a statutory declaration signed by witnesses, indicating that they lived together or other document supporting their living together; If before January 1, 1999, the insured raised a child for at least 8 years, a statutory declaration signed by witnesses indicating that they lived together or other document supporting their living together; Proof of legal representation, if applicable; Marriage certificate, if there was a change in surname; and Birth certificates for children born in Estonia. If the applicant has applied for a DSB, a copy of the medical documentation on file must accompany the application to Estonia. Canadian residence Not required Protective date A protective date is required in cases where the applicant has applied for the corresponding Canadian benefit (intent is required). CPP contributions and/or periods when a DSB was paid Yes, all valid CPP contributions and all periods where a DSB was paid to the applicant must be provided. Canadian pensions and benefits in pay Yes, the current CPP and OAS pension and benefit amounts payable to the applicant must be provided. Signing off the application In Section 13, complete the following fields to certify that the vital data provided by the applicant has been verified: Name; Address; Stamp; Date; and Signature.

topic_title: Application for a Japanese Disability Pension (CAN/J1)
text: Disability Pension—Application review Requirement Direction Completeness of application The applicant must complete the following sections: Japanese Basic Pension Number or Number on Pension Handbook; Canadian Social Insurance Number; Type of benefits claimed; and Sections 1 to 8. Documentation The following must be verified on the liaison form based on information available in ITRDS or based on documentation submitted by the applicant or on file: Name (surname, given, name at birth); Birth (date and place); and Canadian SIN. The applicant must submit originals or certified copies of the following documents to be sent to Japan with the application: Proof of birth (e.g. birth certificate, extract copy of the Family Registry, any valid document to prove the date of birth); Pension Handbook, notice of Basic Pension Number or certificate of coverage under the Japanese pension scheme (if not available, a note stating the reason); A photocopy of banking information document containing the name of the financial institution and account number or an original of a void cheque; Certificates of benefits received under the Japanese pension schemes (if the applicant answered "yes" to section 5 of the CAN/J1 form); Pension Handbook, notice of Basic Pension Number or certificate of coverage under the Japanese Scheme for the spouse (if the applicant declared a spouse in section 2 of the CAN/J1 form); Birth certificate of the spouse and/or child(ren) and certificate of their relationship to the applicant (if the applicant declared a spouse and/or children in section 2 and/or 3 of the CAN/J1 form); A document attesting that the applicant is living with their spouse and/or child(ren) and is providing financial assistance (if the applicant declared a spouse "de facto" (common-law) in section 2 of the CAN/J1 form). If the applicant does not live with their spouse and/or child(ren), documents attesting that they are providing financial assistance; Certificate of income or tax assessment of the spouse and/or children (if the applicant declared a spouse and/or children in section 2 and/or 3 of the CAN/J1 form). Canadian residence Not required Protective date Not required CPP contributions and/or periods when a DSB was paid Yes, all valid CPP contributions and all periods where a DSB was paid to the applicant must be provided. Canadian pensions and benefits in pay Not required Signing off the application Not required

topic_title: Application for a Japanese Survivors Pension (CAN/J2)
text: Survivors Pension—Application review Requirement Direction Completeness of application The applicant must complete the following sections: Deceased person's Japanese Basic Pension Number or Number on Pension Handbook; Deceased person's Canadian Social Insurance Number; Sections 1 to 7; Section 8, if applicable; and Section 9. Documentation The following must be verified on the liaison form based on information available in ITRDS or based on documentation submitted by the applicant or on file: Name (family, given, name at birth) for the deceased, applicant and child(ren); Birth (date and place) for the deceased and applicant; Date of birth for the child(ren); Canadian SIN for the deceased and applicant; Date of marriage, if applicable; Death (date and place). The applicant must submit originals or certified copies of the following documents to be sent to Japan with the application: Proof of birth of the deceased, applicant and children (e.g. birth certificate, extract copy of the Family Registry, any valid substitute to prove the date of birth); Proof of death (e.g. death certificate, post-mortem certificate, autopsy report, extract copy of the Family Registry, any valid substitute such as certificate from the Mayor of a city, town or village in Japan regarding the contents of the death certificate or autopsy report); Proof of marriage, if legally married (e.g. marriage certificate, extract copy of the Family Registry, any valid substitute); Pension Handbook, notice of Basic Pension Number or certificate of coverage under the Japanese pension scheme for the deceased and the applicant (if not available, a note stating the reason); A document attesting that the applicant was living with the deceased contributor and that the deceased contributor was providing financial assistance such as proof issued by a third party (e.g. social worker) or a proof of legal status of the residence. If the applicant did not live with the deceased contributor, a note stating the reason is required; Certificate of income, earnings or taxation for the applicant for the 2 fiscal years before the death of the deceased contributor; Certificate of student registration (if the applicant declared children in section 3 of the CAN/J2 form); A document attesting the date when the deceased person’s disappearance was officially declared (in case the person was presumed dead after disappearance), if applicable; Certificates of benefits received under the Japanese pension schemes for the applicant (if the applicant answered "yes" to section 5 of the CAN/J2 form); A photocopy of banking information document containing the name of the financial institution and account number or an original of a void cheque; Pension certificates for the deceased (if the applicant answered "yes" to question 9 of section 7 of the CAN/J2 form). Canadian residence Not required Protective date Not required CPP contributions and/or periods when a DSB was paid Yes, all valid CPP contributions made by the deceased and all periods where a DSB was paid to the deceased must be provided. Canadian pensions and benefits in pay Not required Signing off the application Not required

topic_title: Application for Lithuanian Benefits (CAN - LT 1B)—Orphan's pension
text: Orphan's pension—Application review Requirement Direction Completeness of application The applicant must check Orphan's pension . The applicant must complete the following: Sections 1 to 3; Sections 6 to 10; Section 11, if the applicant wants their benefit to be paid directly to their financial institution; and Signature of the Applicant field. Documentation The following must be verified on the liaison form based on information available in ITRDS or based on documentation submitted by the applicant or on file: Name (family, given, name at birth) for the deceased; Birth (date and place) for the deceased; and Death (date and place). The applicant must submit originals or certified copies of the following documents to be sent to Lithuania with the application: Birth certificate for dependent children; Lithuanian workbooks for periods until December 31, 1993, for the deceased ; Statements from the deceased's former employers or archives for periods until December 31, 1993, in cases where Lithuanian workbooks are not submitted (if the employer’s business is liquidated); Lithuanian State Social Insurance Certificate issued as of January 1, 1992 for the deceased; Certificate of income in Lithuania from January 1, 1984, to December 31, 1993, for the deceased; Records of military service in Lithuania for deceased; Disability certificate, if the child is over 18 and disabled and became disabled before reaching age 18; and In cases where , before January 1, 1995, the insured raised or nursed a disabled family member of the first category or a disabled child under 16 years of age (for the mother only): the decision of the head of the local office of the State Social Insurance Fund Board on "inclusion of the nursing time into the insurance period"; and the certificate of disability of the family member or child, issued by the State Medical and Social Examination Commission of the Republic of Lithuania; or a medical report . The applicant must submit an original copy of evidence of school attendance or a Declaration of attendance at school or university (ISP1401) form for children between the ages of 18 and 24 who are attending school to be sent to Lithuania with the application. Canadian residence Not required Protective date A protective date is required in cases where the applicant has applied for the corresponding Canadian benefit (intent is required). CPP contributions and/or periods when a DSB was paid Yes, all valid CPP contributions made by the deceased and all periods where a DSB was paid to the deceased must be provided. Canadian pensions and benefits in pay Yes, the current CPP and OAS pension and benefit amounts payable to the applicant must be provided. Signing off the application You must sign and stamp the application form in the Canadian liaison agency receiving an application section.

Canadian residence Not required Protective date A protective date is required in cases where the applicant has applied for the corresponding Canadian benefit (intent is required). CPP contributions and/or periods when a DSB was paid Yes, all valid CPP contributions made by the deceased and all periods where a DSB was paid to the deceased must be provided. text: Lost working capacity (Disability) pension—Application review Requirement Direction Completeness of application The applicant must check Lost working capacity (Disability) pension . The applicant must complete the following: Sections 1 to 5; Section 6, if the applicant wants their benefit to be paid directly to their financial institution; and Signature of the applicant field. Documentation The following must be verified on the liaison form based on information available in ITRDS or based on documentation submitted by the applicant or on file: Name (family, given, name at birth); and Birth (date and place). topic_title: Application for Moroccan Benefits (CAN-MAR 1)—Survivors' pension and Death benefit
text: Survivors' pension and Death benefit—Application review Requirement Direction Completeness of application The applicant must select the benefit they are applying for and complete the following sections: Sections 1 and 2; and Sections 3 and 4. Documentation The following must be verified on the liaison form based on information available in ITRDS or based on documentation submitted by the applicant or on file: Name (surname, given, name at birth) for the deceased and applicant; Birth (date and place) for the deceased and applicant; Canadian SIN for the deceased and applicant; and Death (date and place). The applicant must submit originals or certified copies of the following documents to be sent to Morocco with the application: Birth certificate for the deceased, the applicant and any children declared in section 4; Marriage certificate; Death certificate; Registration card issued by the competent authority in Morocco for the deceased; Certificate of existence–Declaration on the honour of the applicant form completed within 3 months of the foreign benefit application receipt date and certified by a Service Canada Centre or the Consulate of the Kingdom of Morocco; National identity card or identification page of passport for the deceased; Applicant’s personal bank account statement; Certificate of monogamy or polygamy, if applicable; and Applicant’s certificate of name change, if applicable. Canadian residence All Canadian residence after age 18 for the deceased must be provided only for those periods of residence which are not a part of a creditable period under the CPP. Protective date A protective date is required in cases where the applicant has applied for the corresponding Canadian benefit (intent is required). CPP contributions and/or periods when a DSB was paid Yes, all valid CPP contributions made by the deceased and all periods where a DSB was paid to the deceased must be provided. Canadian pensions and benefits in pay Yes, the current CPP and OAS pension and benefit amounts payable to the applicant must be provided. Signing off the application On the first page of the application, you must indicate the date of receipt of the application in the Date application received ( Day/Month/Year ) field. In section 5, you must sign and stamp the application form and complete the Date application submitted ( day/month/year ) field by indicating the earlier of: the date of receipt of the corresponding benefit only where the application for the Canadian benefit was received on or after March 1, 2010, and: only where the applicant specifically requested the pension or benefit application to be considered an application for a Moroccan benefit; or indicated creditable periods in Morocco; the receipt date of the foreign benefit application; or the receipt date of the interim application.

topic_title: Application for Uruguayan Benefits (UR-CA 01)—Retirement due to advanced old age benefit
text: Retirement due to advanced old age benefit—Application review Requirement Direction Completeness of application The applicant must complete the following sections: Section 2.7; Section 7; Section 8, only if documentation attesting to the periods of work of the insured in Uruguay is not provided; and Section 9. Documentation The following must be verified on the liaison form based on information available in ITRDS or based on documentation (originals or certified copies) submitted by the applicant or on file: Name (family, given, name at birth); Birth (date and place); and Canadian SIN. The applicant must submit originals or certified copies of documentation attesting to periods of employment in Uruguay to be sent to Uruguay with the application. Canadian residence All Canadian residence after age 18 must be provided. Protective date Not required CPP contributions and/or periods when a DSB was paid Yes, all valid CPP contributions and all periods where a DSB was paid to the applicant must be provided. Canadian pensions and benefits in pay Yes, the current CPP and OAS pension and benefit amounts payable to the applicant must be provided. Signing off the application You must sign, date and stamp Section 11 of the application form to certify that the vital data provided by the applicant has been verified.

Survivors' benefit—Application review Requirement Direction Completeness of application The applicant must complete the following sections: Section 2.7; Section 3.9; Section 7; Section 8, only if documentation attesting to the deceased's periods of work in Uruguay is not provided; and Section 9. Protective date Not required CPP contributions and/or periods when a DSB was paid Yes, all valid CPP contributions made by the deceased and all periods where a DSB was paid to the deceased must be provided. Canadian pensions and benefits in pay Yes, the current CPP and OAS pension and benefit amounts payable to the applicant must be provided. Signing off the application You must sign, date and stamp Section 11 of the application form to certify that the vital data provided by the applicant has been verified.

As a Department, we are committed to meeting the highest standards of respect for the privacy rights of Canadians and the protection of their personal information. This commitment is critical to maintain the trust of Canadians. Every employee has a role to play in the proper handling, protection and Stewardship of Information.

All employees must follow the Values and Ethics Code for the Public Sector and the ESDC Code of Conduct . Employees must understand the importance of Stewardship and protecting the confidentiality of client information. All employees are responsible for understanding and complying with policies, procedures and practices for the collection, retention, use, disclosure and disposal of personal information. Values and Ethics Code for the Public Sector ESDC Code of Conduct Personal and sensitive departmental information must be accessed on a need to know and need to access basis. This means that you must only access information pertaining to the file you are working on as part of your workload or assigned duties. Access to information within internal databases is restricted to information required to perform your job only . Note that Corporate Security and Internal Investigations regularly monitor departmental databases for misuse, inappropriate or deliberate access, and disclosure, disposal or compromise of information. You are not permitted to view, process or handle any application, file or account for yourself, co-workers, relatives by blood or marriage (including common-law relationships), friends, acquaintances for convenience, curiosity or personal interest. These actions go against the ESDC Code of Conduct and employees must not provide preferential treatment or place themselves in a conflict of interest situation. You must not : access your own information or file using your own SIN; access files of family, friends or public figures; provide family or friends with status updates on their accounts; or process transactions for family or friends. Note this is not an exhaustive list. For more information, please Applications, Files and Accounts of Employees, Relatives and Friends In addition, you can review Unauthorized access and disclosure of Information on iService to ensure you fully understand access permissions. topic_title: Application for Peruvian Benefits (PE-CAN 01)—Old Age Pension/Retirement
text: Old Age Pension/Retirement—Application review Requirement Direction Completeness of application The applicant must indicate the type of benefit they are applying for. The applicant must complete the following: Section I; and Signature of the applicant field. Documentation The following must be verified on the liaison form based on information available in ITRDS or based on documentation submitted by the applicant or on file: Name (family, given, name at birth); and Birth (date and place). The applicant must submit certified copies of the following documents to be sent to Peru with the application in all cases: Marriage certificate or document that certifies a common-law union, if applicable; Identity documents (e.g. Peruvian Identification Document, current passport, alien identity card); Documents proving all employment in Peru (if documents are not available, an affidavit confirming working periods is acceptable); and Void cheque or document issued by the bank providing direct deposit information. If the applicant contributed to the Peruvian National Pension System, certified copies of the following documents must also be sent to Peru with the application: Certificates of employment in Peru; Periods in receipt of Peruvian social benefits; Peruvian pay stubs; Proof of contributions issued by ORCINEA (IPSS) or ESSALUD; Documents issued by a public entity (e.g. Resolution for Cessation, Resolution of Acknowledgement of years of service); and Affidavit including employer contact information and dates of employment periods, if employment documents are not available. Canadian residence All Canadian residence after age 18 must be provided only for those periods of residence which are not a part of a creditable period under the CPP. Protective date A protective date is required in cases where the applicant has applied for the corresponding Canadian benefit (intent is required). CPP contributions and/or periods when a DSB was paid Yes, all valid CPP contributions and all periods where a DSB was paid to the applicant must be provided. Canadian pensions and benefits in pay Yes, the current CPP and OAS pension and benefit amounts payable to the applicant must be provided. Signing off the application Not required

Survivorship Pension—Application review Requirement Direction Completeness of application The applicant must indicate the type of benefit they are applying for. The applicant must complete the following: Sections I and III; and Signature of the applicant field. Documentation The following must be verified on the liaison form based on information in ITRDS or documentation submitted by the applicant or on file: Name (family, given, name at birth) for the deceased and applicant; Birth (date and place) for the deceased and applicant; and Date of death. The applicant must submit certified copies of the following documents to be sent to Peru with the application in all cases: Birth certificate for dependants, if applicable; Death certificate; Marriage certificate or document that certifies a common-law union, if applicable; Identity documents (e.g. Peruvian Identity Document, current passport, alien identity card) for the deceased and applicant; Documents proving all employment in Peru (if documents are not available, an affidavit confirming working periods is acceptable) for the deceased; Document confirming that the applicant is in receipt of a Peruvian pension or an affidavit confirming non-receipt of the pension; Documents proving that the dependents are disabled and the Medical Report Form (PE-CAN 04) completed by a physician providing information about the disability, if applicable; and Void cheque or document issued by the bank providing direct deposit information. If the deceased contributed to the Peruvian National Pension System, certified copies of the following documents must also be sent to Peru with the application: Certificates of employment in Peru for the deceased; Periods in receipt of Peruvian social benefits for the deceased; Peruvian pay stubs for the deceased; Proof of contributions issued by ORCINEA (IPSS) or ESSALUD for the deceased; Documents issued by a public entity (e.g. Resolution for Cessation, Resolution of Acknowledgement of years of service) for the deceased; If employment documents are not available, an affidavit including employers’ contact information and dates of employment periods for the deceased; and Certificate of studies issued by the educational institution for the dependent children. If the deceased contributed to the Peruvian Private Pension Fund System, certified copies of the following documents must also be sent to Peru with the application: Identity documents (e.g. Peruvian Identity Document, current passport, alien identity card) for the dependants; Affidavit confirming current school program and career goals for the dependent children; and Document from an educational institution confirming course plan or enrolment for the dependent children. As part of the broader efforts to streamline the CPPD application process, a list of 32 Grave Medical Conditions, or severe and rapidly progressive conditions, was implemented in 2011. As of January 17, 2022, 9 new medical conditions and their corresponding ICD codes were added to the list of grave medical conditions. In addition, many of the previously listed conditions have been renamed and shortened, or both. Two medical conditions, breast and bladder cancer, were eligible for expedited processing if specific medical criteria were met. Twelve medical conditions are now only eligible for expedited processing if specific medical criteria are met. These medical conditions are considered grave only if the staging descriptors are identified. Files where these conditions are present may only be processed as terminal where a 6-month life expectancy is indicated on the file otherwise they are deemed grave condition. The indicator must be identified manually in ITRDS and PWS. To address the inability to identify all grave medical conditions based on ICD alone, the Terminally Ill/Gravely Ill (TI/GI) indicator must be set to Gravely Ill for all grave medical conditions . Starting in the August 2022 accounting month, only files that are identified by the Terminally Ill/Gravely Ill (TI/GI) indicator in ITRDS will be included in the grave medical condition service standard. If only an ICD is used without the ITRDS Terminally Ill/Gravely Ill (TI/GI) indicator, the file will be considered a regular file. Additionally, grave medical condition files will no longer be validated at headquarters, through ‘not met’ review, prior to being reported within the service standard.
If additional guidance is required, send an enquiry via the Business Expertise Request Tool by following normal channels. Business Expertise Request Tool

There are 12 medical conditions that are only eligible for expedited processing if the applicant’s condition meets specific medical criteria. Files that don’t meet the medical criteria are processed as a regular file. This means that for the 12 medical conditions outlined below, the same International Classification of Disease Codes (ICD) code could be regular, terminal illness, or a grave medical condition, depending on the stage of the applicant’s illness. For this reason, the Terminally Ill/Gravely Ill (TI/GI) indicator in ITRDS data capture must be selected for inclusion in the grave medical condition service standard.
Effective July 18, 2022, the Grave Medical Condition Policy has been updated.

Calling the client is essential to good client service as it allows you to gather information from the client and to provide information to them about their application or benefits. This procedure was created to prepare you for a potentially difficult telephone call and to guide you if the client has a crisis incident when you are speaking to them. A discrepancy report is generated to compare clients' marital status on file with the Department against their marital status reported to the CRA and identifies accounts with discrepancies. In June 2022, the Benefits and Integrated Services Branch (BISB) collaborated with the Integrity Services Branch (ISB) to review the discrepancy report that originally identified nearly 26,000 clients with a marital status discrepancy. In October 2022, the review concluded that 16,000 clients who receive GIS self-reported changes in marital status to the Department between June and October. ISB has been reviewing a selected group of accounts. During the week of March 20, 2023, a Marital Status Questionnaire (ISP-3152) letter was sent to clients included on this report. These accounts are identified by the following automated ITRDS notes: For accounts under review with ISB: ISB CRA/GIS Marital Status Review – account under review with ISB For accounts included in the mail-out by BISB: Client included in the BISB CRA marital status discrepancy mailing. Refer to KA-05166 Clients who receive the ISP-3152 letter must complete the Marital Status Questionnaire section and return it to the Department. The marital status on file with the Department is listed on the first page of the ISP-3152 letter. If the client is indicating a marital status that is different from what is currently on file with the Department, they must include a copy of any supporting documentation, such as a marriage certificate or death certificate. If a response was not received, a Marital Status Questionnaire - reminder letter (ISP-3152B) was automatically sent in June 2023 and an additional Marital Status Questionnaire - reminder letter (ISP-3152C) was sent on January 12, 2024. Both letters advised the clients their benefits may be suspended if no response is received. If the client fails to respond to the requests, National Headquarters will create an Account Verification work item in PWS with the barcode NHQ-OASMSD23-REMIND for processing. If a client has not responded to written requests for information, you must make reasonable efforts to contact them. When all attempts to contact them and obtain the required information have failed, determine if the client has failed to respond, is non-compliant or if their whereabouts are unknown and suspend the applicable benefits. Whereabouts unknown New A client's whereabouts are unknown if: they have not responded to written requests for information or attempts to contact them by phone; and there is no indication on file that the current address has changed; or correspondence has been returned by Canada Post as undeliverable. If a client's whereabouts are unknown, you must suspend their OAS and income-tested benefits and notify CPP and International Operations. Failure to Respond and Non-compliance New A client fails to respond if: they received correspondence from the Department but did not respond; you determine there is an indication on file (other correspondence, recent contact by phone, or cashed cheques) that the current address is correct; and their whereabouts are not in question. A client is non-compliant if: they respond but refuse to provide the requested information. If a client fails to respond or is non-compliant, you must suspend their income tested benefits until the requested information is received. For more information regarding the suspension of benefits, Suspension (Policy) It is important to add the required notes to ITRDS exactly as described so that these accounts can be identified for future review.

topic_title: Marital Status and Rate Tables for Income-Tested Benefits
text: There are 5 rate tables used to determine the monthly benefit entitlement for the GIS and the ALW and ALWS benefits. The monthly rates of entitlement to income-tested benefits are based on both marital status and level of income. The marital status determines the rate table that the benefit is based on. The income threshold for each rate table depends on the number of years of residence the pension or benefit is based on. If changes to the marital status occur during the payment period, the entitlement must be adjusted according to the corresponding rate table. Every year in January, April, July and October, rate tables are prepared for the OAS pension, the GIS and the ALW and ALWS benefits. Refer to the applicable rate tables under OAS Benefit Rates in the Benefits Toolbox : Benefits Toolbox Table 1. Rates Table and Details Rate Table Details All Benefit Rates Tables These rates apply when the OAS pension is in pay based on 40 or more years of residence in Canada. All Partial Rates Tables These rates apply when the OAS pension is in pay with less than 40 years of residence in Canada.

topic_title: Marital status codes and corresponding rate tables
text: The Marital Status ( MS ) code is entered into OAS Online and the International Agreements systems to correctly calculate a client's benefit entitlement based on their marital status. The table below outlines the MS code used in conjunction with the corresponding rate tables: Table 2. When to use MS Codes MS Code Rate Table When to use MS1 1 A GIS client who is single, widowed, separated or divorced. MS2 2 A GIS client who is married to or living common-law with another pensioner. MS3 3 A GIS client who is married to or living common-law with a non-pensioner. MS4 1 A GIS client who is married to or living common-law with another pensioner, who are living apart for reasons beyond their control and would normally be entitled to benefits as MS2 using rate table 2. The system will calculate the GIS for both clients based on individual income as MS4 using rate table 1. A GIS client who is married to or living common-law with a non-pensioner, who are living apart for reasons beyond their control and would normally be entitled to benefits as MS3 using rate table 3 . The system will calculate the GIS based on individual income as MS4 using rate table 1. A GIS client who is married to or living common-law with an ALW benefit client, who are living apart for reasons beyond their control and would normally be entitled to benefits as MS5 using rate table 4. A manual calculation is required for the ALW benefit to be paid as MS5 using rate table 4, based on individual income and issued by priority payment. The system will calculate the GIS based on individual income as MS4 using rate table 1. MS5 4 A GIS client who is married to or living common-law with an ALW benefit client. MS6 4 The MS6 code is no longer used. This code was previously used for a GIS client who is married to or living common-law with an ALW benefit client and who are living apart for reasons beyond their control. Currently, for this situation, refer to MS4 , rate table 1 above. MS8 5 An ALWS benefit client. MS9 5 An ALWS benefit client whose benefit has been converted from the ALW benefit to the ALWS benefit after their spouse or common-law partner died. The following table describes situations you may encounter while processing income-tested benefits and how to apply the correct rate table and MS code: Table 3. Situation and MS code and rate table to use Situation MS code and rate table to use The spouse or common-law partner is eligible for the ALW benefit but has not applied. The pensioner’s GIS will be calculated as MS3 using rate table 3, based on the couple's combined income. The spouse or common-law partner is eligible for the ALW benefit but has applied late. The pensioner's GIS is calculated as MS3 using rate table 3, based on the couple's combined income until the spouse or common-law partner is approved for the ALW benefit. At that time, the GIS will be recalculated retroactively as MS5 using rate table 4 for the period of the ALW benefit entitlement. The spouse or common-law partner is in pay for the OAS pension but does not apply for the GIS . The pensioner’s GIS will be calculated as MS2 using rate table 2, based on the couple's combined income. The spouse or common-law partner’s GIS must be suspended. The spouse or common-law partner does not apply for the OAS pension at age 65. The pensioner’s GIS will be calculated as MS3 using rate table 3, based on the couple’s combined income until the spouse or common-law partner is approved for the OAS pension. At that time, the pensioner's GIS must be recalculated as MS2 using rate table 2 for the period of the spouse or common-law partner’s retroactive entitlement. In some cases, it is advantageous to the couple to remain as MS3 using rate table 3. However, the Department can calculate benefits based on 2 separate rate tables. For more information, refer to the Paying 2 Pensioner Spouses or Common-Law Partners at One Pensioner Rate section below. The applicant has reported that they are separated on an initial application for the GIS . The applicant is considered separated after 3 months of separation. This requirement still applies when the date of separation is before the applicant's effective date. Example The date of separation is January 5, 2024, and the GIS effective date is March 2024. The applicant is considered married for March and April 2024 and the GIS is calculated at the applicable married rate based on the couple's combined income. Effective May 2024, they are considered separated and the GIS is calculated as MS1 using rate table 1, based on the individual income. The couple separates on the last day of the month. The date of separation is the first full day that the couple lives apart. If the couple continues to live apart for 3 months after the month of separation, they will be considered separated in the fourth month following the month of separation. The income-tested benefits will be based on the applicable married rate until the couple has met the 3-month requirement. Example The Department received a notification that a married couple receiving the GIS separated on April 30th, 2023. Their first full day of living apart was May 1, 2023, which is considered the day of separation. The couple is considered separated effective September 2023. The following is a breakdown of the 3-month requirement: The last day that the couple resided together is April 30th. Their first day of living apart is May 1st, which is the month of separation. The 3 months following the month of separation are June, July and August 2023. The couple is considered separated effective September 2023. For more information on various marital status situations, Marital Status—Income-Tested Benefits Entitlement (Policy)

topic_title: Paying 2 pensioner spouses or common-law partners at one pensioner rate
text: Under most circumstances, a couple, where both are OAS pensioners, will receive more GIS between them when they are paid on rate table 2 than they would if only one of them is a pensioner paid on rate table 3. However, there are situations where the combination of income levels and years of entitlement results in a lower combined amount. When this happens, the Department can pay married or common-law OAS pensioners using separate rate tables (rate tables 2 and 3) and pay one pensioner an adjustment amount to ensure that their total benefits are no less than they would have received as MS3 using rate table 3. For more information on when and how this protection is applied, Paying Two Pensioners at One Pensioner Rate (Policy) When the combined income is first added to the system, it will not be apparent which pensioner will receive the adjustment until after the weekly system update. An account that has been paid with the adjustment at any time in the past will show the following message at the bottom of the OAS Re-Calculation (CAL) Screen: WARNING* BILL C31 ACCOUNT – Manual recalculation will be required. After the weekly update, these accounts can be identified as Calc Tbl 2A and Calc Tbl 2B . The account being paid on the 2A table always receives the adjustment. The account that is being paid the adjustment will always be out of balance by the amount of the adjustment. This amount will accumulate each month. When it is necessary to balance the account, OAS Online—Out of Balance Account Data Clean-Up (Scenario) If you are processing an application for the GIS where there is retroactive entitlement or if you are performing a retroactive adjustment to a GIS account where the couple is being paid on separate rate tables, you must determine the advantage and the adjustment manually for the retroactive period. Example An OAS pension and GIS application is approved for Spouse B, effective February 2023. Spouse A has been in pay for the OAS pension and the GIS at the MS3 rate since June 2016. The following steps are followed to determine if the couple would benefit by having this protection applied and how to calculate the adjustment: Using their combined income of $38,476.00, determine what the couple’s entitlement would be at the MS2 and MS3 rates: Table 4. Example, OAS pension rates, MS3 rate and MS2 rate OAS Pension rates MS3 rate MS2 rate Spouse A (17/40ths) OAS pension: $242.47 GIS : $390.20 OAS pension: $242.47 GIS : $2.60 Spouse B (24/40ths) OAS pension: $0.00 GIS : $0.00 OAS pension: $342.31 GIS : $0.00 Combined entitlement $632.67 $587.38 Compare the couple’s combined entitlement at the MS2 and MS3 rates to determine which rate results in a higher combined entitlement. In this case, the couple would receive $45.29 less at the MS2 rate than they would receive at the MS3 rate ($632.67 - $587.38 = $45.29). Therefore, they would benefit from having the protection applied. Each pensioner will receive their OAS pension and the GIS at the MS2 rate. However, an adjustment amount of $45.29 will be added to one pensioner’s entitlement, resulting in the couple receiving a combined total of $632.67. This is the same combined entitlement they would receive at the MS3 rate.

Some situations where you might require information from a foreign institution include, but are not limited to: paying an income-tested benefit and requiring verification of foreign pension rates (for the client or their spouse) in an International Social Security Agreement (ISSA) country; confirmation of an exact date of death to process a DTH benefit or SVR pension; deeming a period abroad as Canadian residence under a specified circumstance, but requiring confirmation of foreign creditable periods to remove any overlap from your calculation validating a date of birth when conflicting information exists on file; requesting a protective date of application when the effective date is later than the earliest possible effective date, and when the client has requested this on the application; and requesting additional contributions granting an earlier Minimum Qualifying Period for a DSB . You must ensure that you are only requesting information when it has the possibility to affect entitlement or eligibility to a benefit. Do not initiate a request for foreign information simply to have a complete record. Before sending a request to IO, review the client's file for any mention of an ISSA country other than Jamaica, Japan or the United States. Some examples of this include: The client declared a period of residence or work in an ISSA country and on an application. The client is in receipt of a foreign pension from an ISSA country. There is documentation originating from an ISSA country's government. The client has a previous or current residential or mailing address in an ISSA country. There has been previous IO activity with an ISSA country in ITRDS or PWS . Any other information that indicates the client might have pension activity in an ISSA country. Once you determine that information is required from an ISSA partner country and that this country has been mentioned on the client's file, you must follow these steps to request the information: Verify in all applicable systems whether IO has received this information in the past. This includes: checking the ITRDS client profile for data with an IA source reading the notes on the ITRDS account, and checking PWS for activity with that country. If there is any indication that IO has received this information previously, request the information from IO using the Telecentre Request Portal External link . You must include the completed Verification Checklist letter (which can be accessed from the KMT EReference Library page, under Work Tools, General External link ) with your request to IO. Telecentre Request Portal KMT EReference Library If there is no indication that IO could have received this information, you must request this information directly from the client. You must request the client's foreign social insurance or identification numbers for all countries in question at this stage. Follow the standard Bring Forward (BF) time frames for your program. For more information refer to National Bring Forward Guidelines . National Bring Forward Guidelines If the client does not provide the requested information, follow regular procedures for non-compliance to a request for information. If the client responds to your request but additional information is required from the ISSA country: complete the Telecentre Request Portal External link enquiry form and send it to the appropriate IO site's generic email box. Refer to Transfer a Client's File to International Operations (Action) to determine to which IO processing site the request must be sent. Telecentre Request Portal Transfer a Client's File to International Operations (Action) When completing the Telecentre Request Portal External link enquiry form, you must include any relevant information such as the foreign social insurance number and the exact periods for which the information is required. For example, when requesting foreign pension amounts, specify the exact years that are required. Telecentre Request Portal You must also add the following note to the form: This information is required to [purpose of request]. Please request this information from [country name] if it is not already available. You must also send the Request for information under an international agreement letter to the client to advise them of this action. In processing the request for information under an ISSA, IO processors will follow the National Bring Forward Guidelines when sending a liaison to a foreign institution. Do not follow up with IO before these time frames have elapsed, except in urgent circumstances or cases of dire needs . National Bring Forward Guidelines If IO does not receive a response from the foreign institution after sufficient attempts, they will complete the Telecentre Request Portal External link enquiry form to advise you of this. If this is the case, you must make a decision using the information already on file. If IO receives the required information from the foreign institution later, they will subsequently advise you of this. Telecentre Request Portal

Information-sharing restrictions have now been largely removed. Certain information acquired under an International Social Security Agreement (ISSA) can be shared by International Operations (IO) staff if it is required to administer the OAS and CPP legislation for pension processing purposes. While the information sharing restrictions have been removed for most countries, IO remains unable to share information received from: Jamaica Japan United States Prior to the release of this article, IO staff was restricted from sharing information obtained under an ISSA. This included sharing information received from foreign partners on liaison forms (e.g. foreign pension information, date of death, current address, etc.) with non-IO processing regions or Integrity Services Branch, for example. You can apply information obtained from an ISSA partner country, even if a client does not have previous activity under an ISSA. If a client has applied for or is receiving benefits exclusively under Canadian legislation, but information under a non-restrictive ISSA could support the administration of those benefits, IO can request and share information obtained under that ISSA. There are no restrictions on the type of information that can be requested, as long as it is required for the administration of the file. There is no limit to retroactivity in sharing ISSA information. If you identify that ISSA information is required for the administration of a pension or benefit for a period prior to the publication of this article, you can still obtain the information from IO.

The change to IO is centered around the naming protocols within PWS. Before February 6, 2023 IO work was identified 2 ways: by virtue of the processing centre location (IO WT or IO ATL) and as well, by the Program or Category choices. This required all work involving IO to have changes made to the Program or Category in addition to the Location . As of February 6, 2023, the following changes specifically related to International Operations (IO) will be implemented in PWS. The IO program will no longer exist; rather IO inventory will be represented by outstanding work items in the processing location International Operations – ATL (IO ATL) or International Operations – WT (IO WT). The Program and Category will match the domestic fields within IO WT and IO ATL locations. The Foreign Benefit program will exist for all Foreign Benefit work, with the Category of Applications or Maintenance. The Country of Agreement field will appear on all work types, both domestic and international, and should continue to be used when work is moved to the IO ATL and IO WT processing locations. An IO Service Standard and age counter will be available on the Work Item details screen.

All current IO work items will use the same naming protocols that exist for domestic inventory, and no adjustments to Program or Category will be required when work moves to and from IO. Overall, this simplifies the PWS entries for work movement. As such, it is critical for IO work to be created in or moved to the correct processing location, being IO WT or IO ATL. In addition, all outstanding IO work items (excluding completed or deleted work items) will change to the existing domestic program and category. All new work received on or after February 6 , 2023 will be loaded using the new naming protocols. The PWS processing location will determine if the work item is within domestic inventories or IO inventory. A new program has been created for Foreign Benefits related work with matching categories of Applications and Maintenance. The location on these work items should be one of the 2 IO locations, i.e. IO WT or IO ATL. Because the domestic and international naming aligns, the Country of Agreement field appears on all work items and is no longer a mandatory PWS field. For work moving to IO, the Country of Agreement needs to be completed as this field determines the correct IO location. Once completed, the Country of Agreement remains on the work item even if moved back to a domestic processing location. An IO service standard and age counter (days spent in an IO location) will appear on the Work Item details screen in addition to the domestic service standard and age counter. This will appear when a work item is created in or moved to an IO location. The IO clock remains on the Work Item details screen even if the work item moves back to a domestic location, and the IO age counter stops when the work item is in a domestic location. This change supports call centres and in-person with a more fulsome understanding of the client’s submission and where they are situated in terms of processing timeframes. Search for a client in the Corporate Correspondence Tool (CCT) Archive to view and print exact copies of all system-generated letters sent to the client.

Open the Corporate Correspondence Tool (CCT) application in your web browser. Corporate Correspondence Tool Click Archive from the CCT’s menu bar. The Search Archive page opens. To perform a search in the CCT Archive, complete the fields as follows: Table 1 Field Direction Database Select the appropriate database from the dropdown. Key Field Select the appropriate key field from the dropdown. Search for Enter the search term. The Client ID can be the client’s ITDRS client ID number, SIN or name. You can use a partial search term in the Search For field. For example, searching for either "diener" or "LUCIANO" with the Client Name key field would find the account "DIENER, LUCIANO". Click Search . A table of related client accounts that match your search criteria appears below the Search For field. Each row is a single client account. Select a client from the search result list to load the archived correspondence for that client. The Archive Search Results page opens and displays a list of the documents previously sent to the selected client. By default, the documents are sorted from the most recent to the oldest document sent to the client. In the Documents pane on the left side, select a folder to see which documents it contains and then select a document to view. To open the document as a PDF in a separate browser tab or window, click Open in external reader or Save . Once the PDF opens, navigate the document pages using the scrollbar or the arrows. To print a copy of the document, open it as a PDF and then click Print .

The CCT Archive allows you to search for a client and view an exact copy of each system-generated letter sent to the client. This feature is useful when you must verify details in documents previously sent to clients, or when you must manually print and mail another copy of a document lost in transit. Client correspondence is considered Protected B information. Staff should only access the CCT Archive as required. To retrieve a client’s documents from the CCT Archive, you will need to search the database for the client using a unique identifier (a key field). You can search for a client using the following key fields: Social Insurance Number —search using the client’s SIN; OAS Account Number —search using the client’s OAS account number; IA Account Number —search using the client’s International Operations account number; Client Name —search using the client’s first and/or last name; and Client ID —search using the client’s identification number. If you know which Service Canada staff member created the client document you are searching for, then you can use the following key field to see all the documents created by that staff member: Document Author —search using the first and/or last name of the Service Canada staff member who created the document.

topic_title: Authenticating a client or their authorized representative
text: Suggested scripts when calling a client or their authorized representative Type of script Suggested script Introduction Use the following introduction when calling a client or their authorized representative: "Hello, my name is [employee's first name] and I am calling from Service Canada—[Canada Pension Plan , Old Age Security or International Operations]. May I speak with [first and last name of client or authorized representative]?" Initiate Security Check—Part I Once the individual confirms they are the client or authorized representative you are calling, inform them of the general reason for your call, and that a security check is required before proceeding, using one of the following scripts: If the client provided information to the Department and you are calling them for additional information or clarification: "We received the [information, documentation or request] you submitted on [date or general time frame], and I need more information to proceed. To discuss protected information, I need to ask you a few questions first to make sure that I am speaking with the right person." If you are calling the client for other reasons (e.g. a discrepancy found in the client's file that you are calling to clarify): "We are currently reviewing our records to ensure we have the most up-to-date information. To discuss protected information, I need to ask you a few questions first to make sure that I am speaking with the right person." Initiate Security Check—Part II Once the client or authorized representative has successfully completed the first part of the security check, initiate the second part by asking: "Would you be so kind as to answer a few more security questions so that I could make sure that I am speaking with the right person?" Client or authorized representative is reluctant to provide requested information for authentication The client or their authorized representative may be hesitant to provide the information required to validate their identity. Reassure them that the call is legitimate by saying: "I understand your concerns and we take our clients' privacy very seriously, which is why we only ask for the last 3 digits rather than the full account number to validate your identity." Refer the client or authorized representative to the Service Canada Call Centre or to a Service Canada Centre. If the client or their authorized representative is still hesitant to provide information, provide the following options: Suggest that the client or their authorized representative call the Service Canada Call Centre by saying: "I understand that you may feel hesitant to provide your personal information. As an alternative, you can call our Service Canada Call Centre to speak with a staff member, who will then verify that I work for Service Canada and confirm my name and telephone number. Once that staff member confirms this and you are comfortable with the information received, please give me a call back." Suggest that the client or their authorized representative visit a Service Canada Centre by saying: "I understand that you may feel hesitant to provide your personal information. As an alternative, you can visit a Service Canada Centre near you. Once the Service Canada Centre staff has verified that I work for Service Canada, confirmed my name and telephone number, and you are comfortable with the information received, please give me a call back." Service Canada Centre Service Canada Centre Client or authorized representative refuses to provide any information If the client or authorized representative refuses all options, advise them that you will request the required information by mail, saying: "I understand your concerns for your privacy and the security of your information. To obtain the required information, we will contact you by mail." Individual fails to answer the security questions correctly Do not tell the individual what information they have given wrong, and do not provide any information regarding the client, the existence of a CPP or OAS file or an application in progress. You can say: "The information you provided does not match the information available in our systems. We will contact the [client, or authorized representative] by mail."

topic_title: New Suspected fraudulent bank account—Authenticating a client or their authorized representative
text: Suggested scripts when contacting a client or their authorized representative in situations where banking details added to an account are flagged as suspicious activity Type of script Suggested script Introduction Use the following introduction when calling a client or their authorized representative: "Hello, my name is [your first name], and I work at Service Canada. I would like to speak to [client's name]. Hello, [client’s name]. Before we begin, I need to ask you a few questions to ensure I am speaking to the right person. You have the right to refuse to provide information over the phone. If you refuse, we will provide an alternative form of communication, such as referring you to a call centre. Are you willing to continue over the phone?" If the client refuses to continue the call "Service Canada has encountered suspicious activity on your account which could impact your [OAS, CPP or OAS and CPP benefits]. We will be sending you a letter to confirm this information. We strongly recommend checking all your Service Canada accounts for any suspicious activity. You can verify my identity by calling the Service Canada call centre at 1-800-277-9914. If you prefer, you can go to the Service Canada Centre and bring the letter that I will be sending along with proof of your identity and your banking information." Optional : Ask client whether they would like for us to suspend their account until we receive confirmation. If the client agrees to continue the call Propose to continue the call by asking for additional information to authenticate the client via the Security check portions of Authenticate a Client or an Authorized Representative During a Phone Call (Action) . If a password has been added to the ITRDS notes, it must be provided by the client or their authorized representative during Part I of the security check. If both parts of the security check have passed, proceed as follows: "As mentioned, my name is [your first name], and I am a Service Canada Benefit’s Officer for (OAS, CPP or OAS and CPP benefits). Have you recently changed or added bank account information related to your OAS/CPP benefits? (excluding the current call)." Authenticate a Client or an Authorized Representative During a Phone Call (Action) If the client confirms that they did not initiate the bank account change Inform the client that there was an attempt to change their bank account information but Service Canada has prevented this change from happening. "Service Canada has prevented an unauthorised attempt to change your bank account information. Your payments will continue to be made to your existing bank account. No action is needed by you at this time." If the client confirms that they did initiate the bank account change Inform the client that there has been a modification in bank account information on their account(s), hence the need to gather additional information. "Service Canada has measures in place to ensure your benefits are deposited into the correct account. Therefore, can you confirm your bank account information to ensure it matches what we have on file?" "Thank you. You will need to send us proof of your bank account information such as a void cheque or direct deposit authorization form from your bank. I will be sending you a letter to advise you how to do so. In the meantime, we will continue to issue your benefit payments to the current method of payment." If the client is unable to answer your questions Regardless of the situation, exercise judgment . The client may be nervous or skeptical of your call. Evaluate the situation and suggest alternatives, try rephrasing questions differently, ask if someone such as a family member can assist. Exercise vigilance to protect our programs while considering our clients. If they are still unable to answer your questions, send the OAS, Direct Deposit incorrect or incomplete, ask client to provide proof of account ownership (ISS-8574) letter. "Since you are unable to answer my questions, you will need to send us proof of your bank account information such as a void cheque or direct deposit authorization form from your bank. I will be sending you a letter to advise you how to do so. In the meantime, we will continue to issue your benefit payments to the current method of payment." Only if the client expresses concerns "Due to the nature of this incident, it is essential that you be informed about potential suspicious activities on any of your government accounts. You should verify your banking history including Service Canada payments or other government benefits. We take this situation seriously and are here to help. If you have concerns about privacy, you can file a complaint with the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada . For more information, you can contact them at 1-800-282-1376 or visit their website at www.priv.gc.ca External link . Also, you can contact either of Canada’s two major credit bureaus to verify their file. They can be reached at: 1-800-465-7166 (Equifax) and 1-800-663-9980 (TransUnion)." www.priv.gc.ca Offensive, threatening or violent behavior or language You may encounter a distressed, angry, or threatening clients. Make every effort to resolve the situation with the client, but it is important not to tolerate abusive behavior affecting your mental well-being. At all times, you can inform the client that you will end the call as deemed necessary. Refer to Respond to Telephone Crisis Incidents (Action) . Respond to Telephone Crisis Incidents (Action)

topic_title: What you need to look for
text: Ready to Process PWS Functionality—Processing Procedures Complete Application Definition An application is considered complete once the client provides the minimum documentation required as specified on the application form and information sheet. The client is not expected to provide more than what is asked for. Agents may need to request other documentation based on the specificities of a client’s application and as such may not cover all documentation needed to process the application. Internal procedures, such as the 60-day wait period for the executor to apply for the DTH benefit, might result in over standard processing for an application. That being said, the target of 80% provides coverage for those types of situations. Based on the application and information sheet, the minimum documentation requirements for the DTH benefit application are as follows: A certified true copy of the death certificate or equivalent acceptable documents for proof of death. The deceased’s SIN or if unavailable, certified true copy of the deceased’s birth certificate. Where the applicant is the person responsible for the funeral expenses, the funeral contract or the funeral receipts. The applicant's signature, unless the application is submitted online through a My Service Canada Account (MSCA). Based on the application and information sheet, the minimum documentation requirements for the SVR pension and children's benefit application are as follows: A certified true copy of the death certificate or equivalent acceptable documents for proof of death. A certified true copy of the Marriage Certificate or a Statutory Declaration of Legal Marriage for married couples, or a Statutory Declaration of Common-Law Union for common-law couples. The deceased’s SIN or if unavailable, a certified true copy of the deceased’s birth certificate. The child’s SIN or if unavailable, a certified true copy of the child’s birth certificate. The applicant's signature, unless the application is submitted online through a MSCA. The date the application is complete will be the date the final documents are received in a Government of Canada location. The date the application is complete begins the measurement timeframe, while the date the decision is made completes the measurement timeframe. The target remains at 80% of these work item types completed within 45 calendar days.

Prospect Person An individual who falls into the following categories: Someone who has not supplied sufficient information to be registered as a person; An organization that does not want to register as a person; Someone who wants to remain anonymous to screen for potential eligibility. The system will automatically register a client as a Prospect Person if: The Foreign Engagement Case country is one of the 3 restricted countries (the United States, Japan and Jamaica), and The liaison or supporting documents are received from a foreign country. Effective June 12, 2023, the portion of the IA system used for foreign benefits processing will be replaced by Cúram. All new foreign benefit applications, liaisons and all transactions associated to these will now be entered in Cúram. All existing foreign benefit and liaison records in the IA system will be loaded into Cúram using ITRDS EDB Source data. All foreign benefit applications and liaisons that are currently in in progress were converted as tasks in Cúram.

In preparation for the implementation of Cúram, 4 data quality issues were identified. When reviewing a foreign benefit client account that has one of these issues, you must refer to the physical client file to determine the exact nature of the transaction. You must also verify the address in ITRDS before sending out any correspondence. Issue 1: Invalid Foreign Benefit Code/Liaison Type—Codes 7-16 On June 5th, 2023, a data cleanup script was run prior to the Release 1 data load to Cúram to correct the following: Where an invalid Foreign Benefit Code/Liaison type was entered in the IA Legacy system as codes 7 to 16 , the type changed in ITRDS to General Inquiry ( type 98 ). These were loaded into Cúram with a Liaison Type " Other " with a description of "general inquiry". An automated note was not added to the affected client accounts. Issue 2: Invalid Foreign Liaison type codes 17 to 29 with a decision code 72 or 73 On June 5th, 2023, a data cleanup script was run prior to the Release 1 data load to Cúram to correct the following: Where invalid Foreign Liaison type codes 17 to 29 was entered in the IA Legacy system with a decision code 72 ( foreign benefit approved ) or 73 ( foreign benefit denied ), the Review code was changed to 71 ( date application sent to the foreign country, liaison replied to, or file closed ). If more than one liaison or foreign benefit record existed for the same Liaison type and Country code , the 72/73 were loaded into Cúram as Liaison Type " Other ". Once the automated system fix was performed, the following system automated notes were entered in ITRDS on each affected client account: Note 1 "Liaison with an invalid foreign benefit review code 72 or 73 has been systematically changed to review code 71 for the same Liaison type. Reference KMT KA-05218" « Liaison pour prestation étrangère avec un code de revue erroné 72 ou 73 a été systématiquement changé au code 71 pour le même type de liaison. Référence OGS KA-05218 » Note 2 "Liaison with an invalid foreign benefit review code of 72 or 73 has been systematically changed to review code 71 with liaison Other as a 71 application approved is already present on the account. Reference KMT KA-05218" « Liaison pour prestation étrangère avec un code de revue erroné 72 ou 73 a été systématiquement changé au code 71 avec type de liaison autre car le code 71 est déjà présent au dossier. Référence OGS KA-05218 » Issue 3: Address Changes in ITRDS for International Operations accounts It was identified that when address changes are made in ITRDS for an International Operations account, it is only sent to the IA system if there is domestic benefit activity. On May 6, 2023, all information for clients in the IA system was loaded into ITRDS to ensure the data was accurate and complete before the load into Cúram. This load replaced the newer ITRDS address with the older address in the IA system. On June 9, 2023, a script was run to revert approximately 98,000 ITRDS Home or Mailing addresses so the most recent address could be loaded into Cúram. To correct this issue, the address must be reviewed, and the current address must be entered in Cúram. An automated note was not added to the affected client accounts. Issue 4: Foreign Application Review codes with invalid IA Category code 30 to 98 There were 1,447 Foreign Application Review (FAR) records with an invalid IA Category code 30 to 98 that were incorrectly encoded in the IA system. In May 2023, a full load of the IA masterfile was loaded into ITRDS and these accounts were loaded into ITRDS as Liaison type invalid . These were migrated to Cúram as a Liaison Type " Other with description Code invalid ". An automated note was not added to the affected client accounts. The long-awaited day has finally come—the first Release of the Department's Benefits Delivery Modernization (BDM) system went live on June 12, 2023! This is the first major milestone for the OAS on BDM project and it will influence the way we deliver OAS services for decades to come. OAS on BDM is the first benefit program to use the Department's Cúram Social Program Management, a computer system that will modernize and standardize the delivery of Canada’s 3 major benefit programs, OAS, CPP and Employment Insurance. Release 1, which focuses on "case management" support, represents the first effort to transition more than 600,000 foreign benefits clients to the updated system. These foreign benefits clients were selected to be the first group to adopt the Cúram technology since they represent a smaller group when compared with other targeted groups in future releases. After Release 1 is successfully deployed and potential areas of improvement are addressed, Release 2 and 3 will continue to pave the way in ensuring that all 7 million OAS clients are moved to the updated system. Both releases are set to deploy in December 2024. Release 2 targets another 150,000 International Agreement clients and introduces complete end-to-end OAS processing. Release 3 will be the final stage, migrating data to transition the remaining 6.9 million existing OAS clients onto the updated system, while also welcoming new clients. For more information, Old Age Security on Benefits Delivery Modernization
