Effective immediately, the Operational Policy has been updated to clarify the Canada Pension Plan and Old Age Security Act do not impose any limitations on reimbursement to provincial social services, workers' compensation agencies or private insurers in the event an applicant passes away during the application process. The Department reimburses a provincial social services, workers' compensation agency or private insurer if valid consent to deduct forms are received. The forms must be signed before the applicant's death, and received before a payment has been released. The date of receipt can be before or after the applicant's death and does not negate the validity of the form, as long as all other conditions are met.

In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, a series of interim measures were introduced in the beginning of March 2020 to facilitate the continued timely delivery of CPP and OAS programs and to process a client's applications for benefits. It was decided that certain interim COVID-19 measures would be implemented as a permanent part of regular CPP and OAS benefit processing.

When an application is valid All valid applications require a decision to be made and communicated to the client. The two interim measures to become permanent are: You can accept an application submitted through a General Delivery box (email/scanned/photo), fax, or uncertified copies as a valid application without a wet signature. You can accept a Statement of Income for the Guaranteed Income Supplement, the Allowance or Allowance for the Survivor for payment period of July (20XX) to June (20XX) with Information Sheet form (ISP-3026) as an Application for the Guaranteed Income Supplement (ISP-3025). When an application is not valid When an application is deemed not valid, the request is processed as correspondence and not an application. The procedure to administratively close the correspondence is accessible through the article Determine if an Application is Valid (Scenario).

The implementation of the policy and procedures will provide you with the guidance necessary to determine what constitutes a valid application for CPP and OAS pensions and benefits. This procedure provides you with the steps to follow when adding and activating a Contribution Period or a Residence Period . It also provides you with the steps to view, edit or delete the periods.

In Cúram, foreign creditable periods are entered on the Residence Periods and Contribution Periods screens. These 2 periods, along with Canadian Residence Periods, are available under the Evidence tab in any Foreign Engagement Case (FEC). You can add, access, modify or delete foreign creditable periods under the Evidence tab in the FEC for the country. Cúram will only accept foreign contribution and residence periods that are in a standard date format (YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD). If creditable periods are not provided by the foreign institution in a standard format, complete years for which a creditable period is present (or potentially present) must be entered. The Comments field must be used to state the actual periods as reported by the foreign institution. If applicable, you must also add the type of contribution (e.g. voluntary or mandatory). Residence example The foreign institution states that the client had 27 weeks of residence in 1994 and 32 weeks in 1995. The periods must be captured as January 1, 1994 to December 31, 1994, and January 1, 1995 to December 31, 1995, with entering "27 weeks in 1994 and 32 weeks in 1995" into the Comments field. Contribution example The foreign institution states that the client had 83 months of contributions from 1980 to 1990. The period must be captured as January 1, 1980, to December 31, 1990, with entering "83 months of contributions from 1980-1990" into the Comments field. There are no limits to how many entries you can make and how many gaps in residence periods are allowed. If a Canadian residence period overlaps with a foreign contribution period, an issue will be raised on the Evidence Dashboard . This must be resolved before the evidence can be activated. Resolve Issues for Foreign Contribution and Canadian Residence Periods in Cúram Each foreign creditable period can have multiple statuses, as indicated by the icons below. Table 1—Foreign creditable period statuses Status Description In Edit Evidence The evidence has been saved but has not been activated. Items to Verify The evidence requires verification before it can be activated. Issues The evidence contains incomplete or incorrect information. Evidence with an issue cannot be activated until the issue is resolved. Active Evidence Once you activate an evidence record (by clicking Apply Changes... in Cúram), the evidence can be used by the system and, in the case of Canadian Residence Period, shared across other FECs.

This procedure demonstrates how to data capture a benefit or provision using the Program Exception Process (PEP) functionality in ITRDS . It shows you how to override individual eligibility and entitlement criteria for a pension or benefit (e.g. how to change the Retirement For Benefit Calculation ( RTR -FBC) or benefit start date).

PEP functionality allows you to manually enter account information required to adjudicate CPP benefits. This process allows you to bypass certain programming issues and legislative limitations found in ITRDS . Before data capturing the PEP block, you must review the client's account to ensure it is complete and correct. You must also manually calculate the client's RTR -FBC and entitlement period using the Canada Pension Plan Calculation Module or the ITRDS Simulation functionality. It takes 2 users to request and approve a PEP data capture: the Requester who creates a new PEP request and sends it for approval; and the Approver who verifies information captured in the PEP block. Once verified, they will either approve the request or return the request to the Requester for modification.

This procedure provides you with the steps to search for tasks, manage tasks forwarded or reserved to you, and create a manual task in Cúram.

A task is an instruction to carry out an item of work. A task can either be an automatic task created by Cúram or a manual task created by a team member. All task-related information is under the Inbox tab in Cúram. All tasks are assigned to a specific work queue in Cúram, and tasks reserved to you will be available to view under My Open Tasks . All tasks have 3 statuses: Open Deferred Closed All ongoing reserved tasks are under My Open Tasks , and all your deferred tasks are under My Deferred Tasks . When you defer an open task, you will record a restart date and the status of the task is updated from Open to Deferred . After the restart date, the deferred task will automatically reopen and move from My Deferred Tasks to My Open Tasks . You must review all ongoing tasks under My Open Tasks to determine if it is a new task or a previously deferred task that requires attention. Tasks will disappear from the list of tasks once they are closed. In each task, you will be able to: Close the task if it is completed. Add a comment to the task for additional notes. Defer the task to a later date if you are waiting for a client’s missing information and cannot proceed with the open task. Forward the task to another colleague. This procedure provides you with the steps to follow to create, access, modify and close a Foreign Engagement Case (FEC) under a Person’s profile in Cúram.

A Foreign Engagement Case (FEC) captures all information relating to a Person’s relationship with a foreign country. An FEC stores documentation and communication related to a Person’s foreign benefits for a foreign country and interactions between the department and the foreign country relating to the person’s eligibility for Canadian benefits. A Person can have multiple FECs under the profile and each FEC is dedicated to one specific country. When a Person requests a foreign benefit from a different country, or when the department receives a foreign liaison requesting information, an FEC must be created under the Person’s profile. If an FEC for a specific country already exists, you can update the record under the specific FEC. If the Person does not exist in Cúram yet, you must create a Person profile first. Register a Client and Create a Foreign Engagement Case in Cúram In Cúram, you cannot delete an FEC in a Person’s record. You can however choose to close the FEC when it is created in error and the status of the specific FEC will change from Open to Closed . When an FEC is created, the system will automatically assign the case to a processing queue as the case owner. In order to close an FEC, you must be the case owner of the FEC. To view the owners of an FEC, go to the User Roles page under the Administration tab. The page lists all the case owners. When the new case owner is assigned, the previous case owner will be updated with an end date. This procedure provides you with the steps to follow when you are registering a Person or a Prospect Person, and creating a Foreign Engagement Case (FEC) in Cúram.

When a liaison, a foreign benefit application, foreign benefit decisions or documentation from a foreign institution or a client is received, you will process the information based on one of the following scenarios: If the client does not exist in Cúram, you should register the client and creates an FEC based on the information. If the client exists in the system but does not have an FEC related to the required country, you must create an FEC based on the country information. If the client exists in the system and has the specific FEC in their profile, you must update the existing FEC. You must also register the client and create the FEC if an enquiry is received for a country with which Canada does not have an International Social Security Agreement in force (e.g. a kit request for a non-agreement country). Do not register the client or create an FEC when: the account has a Country of Agreement code of 099 or 61 ; or the work item received is not related to a foreign benefit application or liaison. If the client does not exist in Cúram, they can be registered as a Person or Prospect Person. The client will be registered as a Prospect Person if: the FEC Country is one of the 3 restricted countries (the United States, Japan and Jamaica); and liaisons, foreign benefit decisions and/or documentations are received directly from one of those country's foreign institutions. When the system is registering a Prospect Person, Cúram will hide the fields related to gender and phone number. Before registering a client, you must search and verify if the client already exists in Cúram. Modifying a person’s address includes correcting a mistake in the existing address or adding a new address when a person moves to a different location.

You can modify a person’s address or add a new residential and/or mailing address in the person’s profile in Cúram. Once you save a new address, Cúram will automatically assign an end date to the old address. The end date of an old address in Cúram cannot overlap with the start date of a new address. When the client has moved to a new location but does not want to change the mailing address, you can add the new address to the residential address and leave the mailing address unchanged. If you just need to add a new mailing address, you can add the new mailing address and leave the residential address as is. PO Box used as residential address For clients using a PO box as their actual residential addresses in Canada, you must enter the address of the closest Service Canada office as the residential address and the client’s PO Box address as their mailing address. When using a Service Canada office as a residential address, add the following Important Note to ITRDS: "SCC address used for residential in lieu of PO Box". Service Canada For clients who live abroad with a PO Box as an actual residential address, you must enter the PO Box to address line 1 of the 2 Address Details tab. Address Guidelines In order to reduce the cost and the volume of returned correspondence for CPP and OAS operations, it is important that you review and record/enter the person's address accurately. In addition, to avoid surcharges from Canada Post, ensure that you follow the address formatting outlined in the Addressing Guidelines when you are recording/entering a person's address. The most common error in address formatting is the apartment or suite number. The correct format for a Canadian address with an apartment or suite number requires it to appear before the civic address number, with a hyphen in between, without spaces and without the word “Suite” or the “#” symbol. This procedure provides you with the steps to follow when processing an enquiry related to a Person or a Foreign Engagement Case (FEC) and how to view urgent flags on a case.

The process begins when a client contacts the Department. It starts with an incoming request, but the processing agent can capture their outgoing response as well. If you receive a client enquiry from a Call Centre or Citizen Services Branch’s general delivery email box related to foreign benefit application, the incoming enquiry must be captured on the appropriate FEC. If no Person record exists, you must create one along with the relevant FEC (if one is not already present) and then capture the incoming enquiry. Register a Person in Cúram (Action) Client enquiries related to anything other than foreign benefit applications must be recorded on the Person's profile. Enquiries are only to be captured in Cúram when: the client is enquiring about foreign benefit applications (e.g. status of processing, questions about document requirements, kit requests); or the client is updating personal information (e.g. change of address, contact information) and they have a Cúram profile but no Canadian pension or benefit activity. All other enquiries must be captured in PWS as per normal procedures. If the enquiry is from a third party, you must confirm that the Person is verified by accessing the third party evidence. Third Party Contacts—Add, Access, Modify, and Delete in Cúram (Action) An automatic task will be generated according to the Type , Direction and Correspondent Type indicated. For instance: Member of Parliament (MP) and Ministerial offices are considered a high priority and a reply is required within 2 days. A task is generated, and an urgent flag is added to the communication. The urgent flag is not raised on the Person’s profile; it is only raised when it is recorded at the case level. To create an urgent flag related to a dire need or National Headquarters refer to Urgent Flags—Add, Access, Close, Delete in Cúram (Action) . To create an urgent flag related to MP and Ministerial offices, go to the steps below under Process an Enquiry Related to a Foreign Engagement Case . The urgent flag ends once all tasks associated to the FEC are closed. To manually close an urgent flag, Urgent Flags—Add, Access, Close, Delete in Cúram (Action) Urgent Flags—Add, Access, Close, Delete in Cúram (Action) There are 2 types of privacy requests: Table 1—Type of Privacy Request and Details Type of Privacy Request Details Privacy Request Tier 1 If the Direction is Incoming , an automatic task is triggered. Privacy Request Tier 2 If you receive a request, forward it directly to the Access to Information and Privacy (ATIP) group, follow normal processing guidelines. No task is created. Capture the communication as Incoming and select the client as the correspondent. If the ATIP group responds and requires more information, capture the communication as Incoming and the Correspondent Type as ATIP Group . A task is automatically generated. You can validate that the task has been created by accessing the Task tab on the Person or FEC. If you capture a communication with the same Type as a previous one, it triggers an increase in the escalation level of the related task (ascending), rather than creating a second task. Escalation levels are visible in most task lists and within the task itself. There are 8 levels of esca lation. Refer to Manage Tasks in Cúram (Action) . If the following types of communication are selected, an escalation is triggered: Manage Tasks in Cúram (Action) Enquiry Foreign Benefits—Requires Attention Enquiry—Address Change, Enquiry—Other Enquiry—Processing Status Editing the Type or Direction of an existing communication to correct an error may trigger Cúram to generate a new task. The previous task will automatically close and will disappear from the list in the Task tab.

This procedure provides you with the steps to follow when creating and reprinting correspondence.

Cúram connects with the Corporate Correspondence Tool (CCT) to create and reprint correspondence. Create Correspondence This process begins when you need to create correspondence, a letter, to communicate with a client or a third party. The letter is generated based on a template in the CCT. When creating correspondence in Cúram, the system will automatically open CCT in your browser. Creating correspondence can be done on a Person’s profile or on a Foreign Engagement Case (FEC). When correspondence is specific to an FEC, you must add it to the case. All the correspondence will display on the Person’s profile, but only the correspondence specific to an FEC will display on the case. The system automatically retrieves communication details for correspondence previously registered in Cúram (e.g. mailing address and preferred language). These must already have been created on the Person’s profile for the correspondence to be created. Cúram assigns a unique Correspondence Tracking Number for every correspondence created. The Correspondence Tracking Number hyperlink will only be enabled if the Communication Status is Sent , Returned or Void . Once enabled, the hyperlink will allow you to view the CCT letter. Unverified Contact for A Deceased Person You must remove a deceased person’s information in the Date of Death , Date Notified of Death and Country of Death fields under Birth and Death Details in the Evidence tab before adding an unverified contact if you are required to send correspondence to the unverified contact. Once the correspondence is sent, you must add back the information you removed. You must mark a record as a duplicate before you can perform a merge. Once marked as a duplicate, both records remain visible, but one is marked as a duplicate in the Context Panel. The record will no longer be used in case processing, and you cannot make changes to it. You must decide which of the records is the master Person and which is the secondary before marking it as a duplicate. To determine which Person record should be the master, consider: The account that has the most amount of accurate information; The information on the IA system and ITRDS; If one record has a SIN and the other does not; If a record has several Foreign Engagement Cases (FEC) compared to one that has one FEC. Since the multiple FECs will need to be entered manually when merging, it is best to make this one a master Person record. You can mark a record as a duplicate and complete the merge at another time or you can mark the record as duplicate and then proceed to merge the records. Merge Records and Access Merged Foreign Engagement Cases to Update a Master Person’s Record in Cúram You can unmark a record that was previously marked as a duplicate if there has been an error and the record should not be a duplicate. This will unmerge the records if they have been previously merged. Once a duplicate record is unmarked, it can be used in case processing again. Unmarking does not remove any of the merged data that was copied into the original record if a merge was already performed. You must manually delete any evidence brought over from the secondary account. Under the evidence record there is a comment that indicates if the evidence is from the duplicate account. If there are conflicting overlaps in the evidence periods, you will not be able to mark a record as a duplicate. Before marking a record as a duplicate, it is important to verify that the evidence periods do not overlap. For example, if each record has a marital status and they overlap you will receive an error message.

Recent banking changes for payments made to Australian clients require that we have their full home address on file. If a payment is made to a client with a P.O. Box as their main address, the Receiver General will return the payment.

If additional guidance is required, send an enquiry via the Business Expertise Request Tool (BERT) and select Canada Pension Plan & Old Age Security (access is required). Business Expertise Request Tool

For clients that currently have a home address in ITRDS notes: Lists of clients who already have an address on file have been share to the network by creating PWS items for processing agents to make the change. For clients who were sent a letter requesting their home address: When a client returns the Declaration form or calls to update their home address For call center agents: You must ask the clients for both their home and their mailing address. Call center agents must escalate the request for the address change to processing agents by creating an item in PWS . Call centre staff can refer to the Common Reference Tool (CRT) for procedures relating to this initiative. Common Reference Tool For processing agents: When you receive a returned Declaration form from the client or a PWS item, processing agents must make the change of address to reflect the home address as the main one on file. Please refer to the Request to Change an Address or Direct Deposit (Scenario) . The procedure will be updated to reflect this new requirement. Request to Change an Address or Direct Deposit (Scenario) With the exception of IO accounts, you must put an Important Note on the client’s account as follows: Client’s mailing address is different than home address. For all correspondence, please send to: (write full mailing address). For IO accounts, it is sufficient to ensure that the home and mailing addresses are recorded accurately in the IA system. For clients requesting new Foreign Direct Deposit for Australia only: When clients request a new FDD, you must ensure that we have their home address as the main address in ITRDS . All payments made to a client with a P.O. Box as their home address will be rejected and returned to us. Do not send the FDD form to be encoded if the home address on file is a P.O. Box. You need to contact the client to request their home address. For new clients: For all new clients living in Australia, when processing their application for CPP or OAS benefits, you must have their full home address on the application. If their home address is different than their mailing address, the home address must be the main one in ITRDS . With the exception of IO accounts, you must put an Important Note on the client’s account as follows: Client’s mailing address is different than home address. For all correspondence, please send to: (write full mailing address). For IO accounts, it is sufficient to ensure that the home and mailing addresses are recorded accurately in the IA system. When sending the Notice of Entitlement letter, this action must be done manually as the mailing address is not the same as the home address. For Returned Payments: If you receive a Payment Advice Notice (PAN) for a returned/rejected payment for clients residing in Australia with a P.O. Box as their main address, you must suspend the benefits and contact the client to obtain their home address. If the address has been updated to reflect the home address, you can reissue the payment.

A recent legislative change in Australia requires a home address for every OAS and CPP client in order for them to continue to receive benefits. Home addresses are transmitted to Australia via the Standard Payment System (SPS). This new home address requirement means a change to how addresses are recorded for Australian residents that have a home and mailing address in ITRDS and OAS online. For Australia only , the home address must be recorded in ITRDS / OAS online, while the P.O. box must be entered into ITRDS notes. This is due to the limitation in the number of addresses that can be entered in both systems. The IA system is not affected as it can record a home address, mailing address, and direct deposit details simultaneously. However, IO staff must still verify that the home address has been received and entered in the Home Address field in the IA system. A process is being developed to ensure that future mailings such as NR4, NRT successfully reach the clients. A letter was sent in April to clients currently receiving payments who have a P.O. Box on file, and no home address, requesting that they provide their home address to continue to receive their payments.

topic_title: CPP Enhancement and Triennial Review Reforms—Child Rearing Drop-In and Disability Drop-In Provisions
text: Effective Date: May 29, 2023

The Child Rearing Drop-In ( CRDI ) only applies to the enhanced component of the CPP , while the Child Rearing Drop-Out ( CRDO ) will continue to apply to the base CPP . The CRDI protects individuals from reduced wages due to providing care for a child under age 7 and will increase the amount of DSB benefit, RTR and SVR pensions paid by the CPP enhancement. In each year while a child is under age 7, a credit equal to the average of the primary caregiver’s earnings in the 5 years prior to the birth or adoption of a child will be “dropped-in” if that amount is higher than their actual earnings. The CRDI does not help individuals meet the Minimum Qualifying Period eligibility requirement for benefits. Clients are not required to submit a separate application for CRDI . The department will leverage the information provided in the Request for a Child Rearing Provision (ISP1640) form. When the client applies for the Child Rearing Provision they are applying for both the CRDO and CRDI .

The Disability Drop-In ( DDI ) only applies to the enhanced component of the CPP , while the Disability Exclusion will continue to apply to the base CPP . The DDI is provided to individuals with disabilities. It is equal to 70% of their average earnings in the six years prior to the onset of the disability. The DDI protects the value of their RTR pension and any subsequent survivor’s pension they may leave to their families. Earnings will be “dropped in" or credited for the years when individuals received the CPP DSB , increasing the amount of their RTR pensions (as well as their SVR pension). The DDI does not help individuals meet eligibility and Minimum Qualifying Period for benefits. Clients are not required to submit a separate application for DDI . The Department will leverage the information it has to calculate or apply the DDI . Additional system changes related to the calculation of the second additional component of the CPP will be implemented at a later date.

As the CRDI and DDI provisions impact the way some CPP benefits are calculated, changes to systems are being introduced and knowledge or communication products have been developed or updated. Background The CPP enhancement legislative changes are being phased-in over seven years, from 2019 to 2025. In January 2019, the Canada Revenue Agency began collecting enhanced contributions from working Canadians. System updates required to accommodate the CPP enhancement legislative changes are being implemented gradually through the CPP enhancement project. The project is also responsible for implementing system functionalities to accommodate the legislative changes stemming from the 2016-2018 CPP Triennial Review, i.e. flat-rate DTH benefit, removal of the age-based reduction to the SVR pension, CRDI , DDI and the PRDB . On November 23, 2019, system functionalities to split earnings and contributions in ITRDS (base CPP and first additional) were implemented. On May 21, 2022, system functionalities to pay the first additional component of the CPP were implemented. The system release in May 2022 also included the introduction of system functionalities for 2 of the Triennial Review reforms (flat-rate DTH benefit and removal of the age-based reduction to the SVR pension). On May 27, 2023, system functionalities were introduced to "drop in" credits into the calculation of the first additional component of CPP benefits. The Child Rearing Drop-In ( CRDI ) and Disability Drop-In ( DDI ) provisions were introduced on January 1, 2019, to help protect the value of CPP benefits during periods of low or no earnings. The drop-in provisions only apply to the enhanced component (first additional and second additional) of the CPP . The CRDI protects the enhanced component of CPP benefits of individuals who reduce their earnings to be the primary caregiver of young children. It has the same eligibility criteria as the Child Rearing Drop-Out ( CRDO ) provision in the base CPP but is calculated differently. The DDI protects the enhanced component of CPP benefits for individuals with severe and prolonged disabilities and is calculated differently from the disability exclusion, which will continue in the base CPP . On May 27, 2023, system functionalities were introduced to calculate drop-in credits for the first additional component of the CPP . For clients who begin receiving a CPP benefit in June 2023 or later and who are eligible for CRDI and/or DDI , drop-in credits will be calculated as part of the adjudication process. Accounts in pay with a Child Rearing Provision that include a period between January 2019 and May 2023 will require re-adjudication to calculate the CRDI component of the provision. Accounts in pay for a CPP RTR pension and/or SVR pension that had a previous period of disability with a date of onset on or after January 2019, will require re-adjudication to calculate the DDI . The re-adjudication process is currently scheduled to begin in June 2023 and will calculate the CRDI and DDI credits and pay any retroactive amount to the client. For more information, refer to CPP Enhancement and Triennial Review Reforms—Child-Rearing Drop-In and Disability Drop-In Provisions (Implementation Bulletin) . The CRDI protects individuals with low or no earnings, who are the primary caregiver of a child under age 7, and increases the amount of the benefit paid by the CPP enhancement. A contributor who is eligible for the CRDI will receive earnings dropped into the calculation of the enhanced component of their CPP benefit for the time when the child was under age 7, for a period that includes 2019 or later. Each year that a child is under age 7, credits equal the average of the primary caregiver's earnings in the 5 years prior to the birth or adoption of a child. These credits will be dropped in if that amount is higher than their actual earnings. These credits become 1st Additional Unadjusted Pensionable Earnings ( UPE ) on the individual's Record of Earnings. The first UPE dropped in as a result of the CRDI are eligible for a Credit Split provision. The CRDI only applies to the enhanced component of the CPP , while the Child-Rearing Drop-Out ( CRDO ) will continue to apply to the base CPP . Clients are not required to submit a separate request for the CRDI ; information submitted on the Request for a Child Rearing Provision (ISP1640) form will be used to determine eligibility to both the CRDO and CRDI .

It is only applied when calculating the individual's CPP RTR or SVR pensions. The DDI provision protects the value of their RTR pension and any subsequent SVR pension owed to the survivor. The DDI only applies to the enhanced component of the CPP , while the Disability Exclusion will continue to apply to the base CPP .

The PRDB legislation enacted in 2019 did not align with the contributory requirements of the DSB . It did not have a reference to “wholly or partly within a contributory period” which meant proration could not be considered. The 2019 legislation did not provide for exclusions (i.e. Child Rearing Provision and previous periods of disability) when determining the MQP. The recent legislative change on May 5, 2023, now aligns the contributory requirements for the PRDB with those of the DSB .

topic_title: Appendix A (CPP & CPPD): Program Exception Process Status
text: Review the Client Profile screen to determine the account notifications. This is where you will see if the account has any benefits in Program Exception Process (PEP) status. If the account has the PEP indicator, we need to determine if it is a triennial PEP for special handling. On the Benefits screen, we will see which benefits are in PEP status. If it is only the DTH benefit, check the notes to confirm that it is a Triennial DTH benefit. These need to be handled separately as they cannot be archived with regular non-triennial files. If the account is a PEP (not triennial DTH benefit) account or if any of the interrelated accounts are PEP accounts, the file cannot be destroyed. Update PWS accordingly.

Refer to the various file sort types Sort type Definition Active file The client is in receipt of a benefit and the last administration action has not been completed. Archive - Offsite retention The account is closed. There are no active benefits being paid and there are no outstanding monetary transactions. The last action on the account is less than the full retention period of 6 years. These files should be boxed and sent to secure storage. Closed file The client is not receiving a benefit. Their file is administratively closed. The last administration action has taken place, and there are no outstanding overpayments or underpayments. When the last administration action happens, the retention period begins. Destroy/Dispose The account is closed. There are no active benefits being paid and there are no outstanding monetary transactions. The last action on the account from the full retention period is more than 6 years. Dormant The account is closed. There are no active benefits being paid and there are no outstanding monetary transactions. The last action on the account is less than 2 years. These files are retained onsite for 2 full years, then should be boxed and sent to secure storage. Put away There is an active benefit being paid from the account. The file cannot be archived and must be returned to the file bay. PEP Program Exceptions Process. These files cannot be disposed of. They must be moved to the PEP location for storage. RCMP/Fraud These files have indicators either in the file itself, on the file jacket or in ITRDS notes that they are under RMCP review or review for fraud. These files cannot be disposed of and should be kept in a separate section of the file bay. The file jacket must clearly state "Do Not Destroy".

The following procedures provide information on the disposition of documents and outlines when to retain or destroy CPP, CPPD and OAS client files. Consult Appendix B: File Lifecycle Stages .

Find a Client. Use the SIN from the disposition list to locate the physical file in the file bay. Compare the SIN and family name on the file jacket against those on the disposition list. If the correct file has been located, place a checkmark next to the item on the disposition list. If the file is not found, make a note on your disposition list. Expand your search for the missing file once you have exhausted the list. Verify the Client File– ITRDS . In ITRDS , enter the client's SIN and select Search. The Client Profile screen opens. Determine if the file must be permanently retained. Review the file jacket, its contents, and the ITRDS notes to determine if there is an indicator that the file must be permanently retained (not eligible for disposal). These indicators can include the following: RCMP investigation/fraud; For CPP & CPPD only: Program Exception Process Status; and Do Not Destroy (for reasons such as class action lawsuits, Charter challenges, vocational rehabilitation, and survivors under 35 years of age). If yes , the file cannot be destroyed or sent to storage. The file must be retained in a separate location. If no , proceed to Step 3 . Step 3 Verify Date of Death (DOD) – ITRDS . Refer to the Date of Death field to verify if the client is deceased: Accounts for clients who are older than any known Canadian (115 years or age or older) that have no DOD in ITRDS should be kept separate. If the client is over 115 years of age and still in pay, refer to the Referral Process for Administrative Investigations (Scenario). If the client is deceased, write the DOD across the front of the client's physical file (e.g., DOD: 2008-05-27). If the client is not deceased, return the file to the file bay. Review Benefit Status. Review the benefits screen to determine if the account is in pay. All benefits other than the Death benefit should display a Terminated , Withdrawn , or Denied status. If yes , proceed to Step 5 . Step 5 If no , return the file to the file bay. Review Account Status: Select CPMS from the institutional bar. The Account Overview screen opens. Confirm if there are any outstanding payables or receivables. If yes , return to the file bay. If no , proceed to Step 6 . Step 6 Review the identifiers screen to determine if the account has been removed from OAS Online. If yes , proceed to Step 6 . Step 6 If no : confirm DOD is shown and account is status 03; confirm the Re-Calculated Net amount is NIL; and confirm there are no outstanding amounts owing for any overpayment listed. If all have been confirmed, proceed to Step 6 . Step 6 If any are not confirmed, return the file to the file bay. Review Interrelated Accounts: Is there an SVR pension in pay or suspended? If yes , the contributor file and any other interrelated files to the deceased contributor file cannot be destroyed or sent to storage as the SVR pension keeps it active. The file must be returned to the file bay. If no , proceed to Step 7 . Step 7 Is there a child's benefit in pay or suspended? If yes , the contributor file cannot be destroyed or sent to storage as the child benefit keeps it active. The file must be returned to the file bay. If no , proceed to Step 7 . Step 7 Is there an ALW / ALWS in pay or suspended? If yes , the control file cannot be destroyed or sent to storage as the ALW / ALWS pension keeps it active. The file must be returned to the file bay. If no , proceed to Step 7 . Step 7 Review the contents of the file. Ensure that all contents belong to the client and are for the correct program area (CPP, CPPD or OAS). If the contents belong to a different client or are related to a different program, remove the unrelated documents and PA them to the appropriate client file. Now that the file has been reviewed, the file can be destroyed, sent to storage, or stored onsite as applicable. Next Steps. Update ITRDS notes and the Disposition Tracking Tool with actions taken and obtain appropriate approval in the Disposition Tracking Tool for destroying files.

Client files must be retained for 7 years from the date of the account closure or cancellation. Refer to Retention and Disposition Schedule at ESDC – PLACER Project Internal link to locate the Guide for Archival Assessment and Retention of Information (GAARI) extended retention schedule. Retention and Disposition Schedule at ESDC – PLACER Project The number of retention years will increase if: there is an SVR pension in pay: the related contributor's file must be kept for 7 years from the date of the related survivor's account closure/cancellation; there is a surviving child's benefit related to the contributor's account in pay. The related contributor's file should be kept for 7 years from the date of the account closure or cancellation of the surviving child's +/-18 benefit; or the client's benefits were terminated as the client ceased to be disabled or returned to work. These files can only be destroyed after 15 years. A client's file cannot be destroyed if it: has any outstanding monetary actions; was referred to the RCMP for fraud; has a PEP status; is marked as “Do Not Destroy” (for reasons such as class action lawsuits, Charter challenges, vocational rehabilitation, and survivors under 35 years of age). For accounts interrelated to a triennial death benefit with a PEP status, the death benefit does not extend the retention period of the interrelated account unless there is an SVR benefit in pay. The number of retention years will increase if: The spouse is in pay for ALW / ALWS : the related control file must be kept for 7 years from the date of the account closure/cancellation of the spouse's ALW / ALWS benefit. A client's file cannot be destroyed if it: has any outstanding monetary actions; was referred to the RCMP for fraud; is marked as “Do Not Destroy” or for reasons such as class action lawsuits or Charter challenges.

The CPMS functionality allows the user to override the receivable recovery rate or amount on a supplementary payable. When the user would override the receivable recovery rate or amount, only the override rate or amount was withheld from the payable. The existing monthly recovery withhold rate or amount was not applied in addition to the override rate or amount.

When the functionality to override the receivable recovery rate or amount is applied, the rate or amount selected will be applied to the existing receivable. In addition, for any existing receivables with no overridden rate or amount, the recurring recovery rate is applied against all supplementary payables included in the weekly payment.

Changes made to the CPMS net pay process to align with the financial rules in SAP started to be effective on May 27, 2023. When the user applies the functionality to override the receivable recovery rate or amount on a supplementary payable, and there is at least one other payable on the account and at least two receivables present, the recovery rules have changed resulting in a different net amount. The procedures to override the receivable recovery rate or amount on a supplementary payable have not changed .

The CPP Program Compliance Review is a national integrity review initiated by the Integrity Services Branch (ISB), focusing on the RTR , SVR and Proactive enrolment benefits at age 70 or older. ISB regularly conducts Program Compliance Reviews on departmental programs and services to: assist in identifying risks; identify the nature and extent of incorrect payments due to internal or external program compliance errors, abuse and/or fraud; and inform mitigation and prevention strategies. Program Compliance Reviews support the Integrity by Design approach, which aims to embed integrity interventions and controls throughout the benefit and service life cycle in support of the continuous improvement of departmental programs and services.

Where a credit split has occurred and the date of attribution is prior to an eligibility determination, the divided pension credits are applied in the same manner for the PRDB as for the DSB . In the case of the PRDB , the credit split would have already been considered in the calculation of the Early Retirement (ERTR) pension. The CPP contributory period ends the month before the ERTR effective date. A credit split is not permitted for any months during which one of the former spouses was a beneficiary of an RTR pension under the CPP or the QPP. The credit split is based on the cohabitation period and cannot be extended past the end of the CPP contributory period (i.e. the month before the effective date of the ERTR) and excludes months where the contributor is in receipt of a DSB or an ERTR. If a credit split occurs after benefits are in pay, the monthly benefit rate will be recalculated as of the date of attribution where pensionable earnings are gained or lost. In the case of the PRDB , only the RTR payment amount may be affected.

Effective Date: May 2023 The Child Rearing Provision (CRP) applies in the same manner for PRDB as it does for DSB when determining the latest possible date of onset (LPDOO). The CRP for potentially increasing the benefit payment amount does not apply to the PRDB as PRDB is a flat rate. When the PRDB was first introduced in January 2019, the CPP contributory period ended with the month before the Early Retirement (ERTR) pension effective date, and the CRP drop-out period could not be extended past the end of the CPP contributory period. Effective May 5, 2023, legislative amendments introduced a contributory period for the PRDB . For the purpose of PRDB , its contributory period ends the month before the date of onset (DOO). CRP months and/or years can be dropped out of the PRDB contributory period, even if those years are after the ERTR pension effective date. These years can be dropped out to improve the LPDOO. Sliding the LPDOO The LPDOO can slide to the child’s 7th birthday when determining an LPDOO for a regular or late application, if the DOO falls in the same year before the child’s 7th birthday. This is because only full calendar years can be dropped out. If the first part of the year can be dropped out due to family allowance and exclude the remainder of the year due to disability, this fulfills the “whole calendar year” requirement.

text: The CPP enhancement legislative changes were phased-in over 7 years, from 2019 to 2025. The CPP enhancement legislative changes are being phased-in over 7 years, from 2019 to 2025. The enhancement components (i.e. first and second additional components) are not a separate benefit, but rather a top-up to the base CPP. The enhancement increases the CPP RTR pension, PRB , DSB and SVR pension. Eligibility for CPP benefits is not affected. In January 2019, the Canada Revenue Agency began collecting enhanced contributions from working Canadians. System updates required to accommodate the CPP enhancement legislative changes are being implemented gradually through the CPP enhancement project. On November 23, 2019, system functionalities to split earnings and contributions in ITRDS (base CPP and first additional) were implemented. On May 21, 2022, system functionalities were introduced in ITRDS and CPMS to pay the first additional component of the CPP. The system release in May 2022 also included the introduction of system functionalities for 2 of the Triennial Review reforms (flat-rate DTH benefit and removal of the age-based reduction to the SVR pension). On May 27, 2023, system functionalities were introduced in ITRDS to "drop in" credits (i.e. the Child Rearing Drop-In (CRDI) and Disability Drop-In (DDI) provisions) into the calculation of the first additional component of CPP benefits. On September 1, 2023, an updated version (9.10.12) of the Canada Pension Plan Calculation Module (CPPCM) (also referred to as Krystal) was released to enable the manual calculation of the first additional component of the CPP.

Pandemic relief benefits (e.g. the Canada Emergency Response Benefit) were issued during the pandemic to provide temporary income support to individuals. Such benefits received by low-income seniors in 2020 were considered taxable income and used in the calculation of income-tested benefits. The increase in taxable income led to a reduction or loss of income-tested benefits for many seniors. As a result, a one-time grant for GIS recipients who received pandemic benefits in 2020 was issued to impacted clients in April 2022. The grant was to compensate GIS and ALW recipients who saw a reduction or loss of benefits since July 2021 due to the receipt of pandemic payments in 2020. In order to ensure that this issue would not recur, the Government amended the Old Age Security Act through Bill C-12 to exempt any amount of most pandemic benefits received in 2021 or later from the calculation of income for the GIS and ALW . The CRA and Service Canada worked together to exclude these pandemic benefits from the 2021 data feed that provides income information between departments.
Effective Date: September 29, 2023

If additional guidance is required, send an enquiry via the Business Expertise Request Tool (BERT) External link and select Canada Pension Plan & Old Age Security (access is required). Business Expertise Request Tool

Since the issue was initially identified, work has been undertaken to determine the full extent of the issue, including running scans and analyzing potential impacts on client and their spouse's accounts. Most clients did not meet the eligibility criteria for income-tested benefits, with or without the 2020 pandemic benefit income. Therefore, the clients would not be impacted (e.g. have an overpayment) once the correct income was input on their file. However, for approximately 15,800 clients, the correct income would create an overpayment once the correct income was received. In order to correct this income issue, the automated process for the CRA Reassessment report (ISP-3017-REA) has been adapted to: recalculate the GIS or ALW benefit; remit the overpayment; add a note in ITRDS ; and inform the client of the outcome by manner of a centrally printed letter. These procedures may affect all processing staff supporting domestic pension programs. Accounts that are identified as exceptions to the automated process require manual intervention. In the event that this is required, work items will be created in PWS under the barcode: NHQ-2WAYCRAUPDATE-23 . For procedures to provide OAS staff with guidance for correcting accounts, 2020 Income Issue (Action)

Between March and August 2022, approximately 39,000 GIS and ALW accounts had discrepancies in their 2020 income information provided by the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). Specifically, the income mistakenly excluded pandemic benefits received in 2020, which affected certain clients' GIS or ALW entitlements for the July 2021 to June 2022 period. There are approximately 15,800 clients that had an overpayment as a result of the income issue. Using the remission provision under a blanket remission authority, these overpayments will be remitted due to Erroneous Advice/Administrative Error once the 2020 income has been corrected.

If the correspondence indicator is set to Y , the cheque has been returned. SPS will update the return reason to Returned foreign cheque, and you will receive a Payment Advice Notice (PAN). If the correspondence indicator is N , the cheque has not been returned and the client can cash the cheque at any time. The Bank of America will honour the cheque regardless of how long it has been in circulation and will reclaim the funds from PSPC. In this situation, SPS does not generate a PAN. If there is no entitlement to the payment, you must submit the CRCD Cancellation Without RG Cheque (SPS Issue) (PWGSC-TPSGC-5495) form to IRGOD before you cancel the cheque in the SPS. IRGOD will send a PAN to confirm the cheque is cancelled in SPS. If there is entitlement to the payment, you can issue a duplicate payment after the client completes and returns a signed UNDERTAKING AND INDEMNITY - For Cheques issued by the Receiver General (PWGSC-TPSGC-535) form. Once the duplicate payment has been issued, the original and duplicate cheques will appear on the SPS as two separate payments with the same Payment Reference Number. Due to system limitations, only one payment is set to Redeemed status in the SPS even if both the original cheque and the duplicate have been cashed. In this situation, the first attempt appears in SPS as Returned - reclaimed foreign cheque and the second attempt appears as Redeemed . If a client redeems both the original (reclaimed foreign) cheque and the duplicate cheque, IRGOD will automatically investigate and send a Journal Voucher to the Department. text: Access the Standard Payment System (SPS) to view the status of the payment. Refer to the Standard Payment System user guide External link . Standard Payment System user guide Select Payment Enquiry from main menu, then select Payment Information Enquiry from the screen. Enter the client's Payee Account Number : To view CPP payments: enter the 12-digit Client Identifier number of the payee from CPMS . To view OAS payments: enter the client's 9-digit SIN, OAS account number, IA account number or the Client ID. Identify the specific payment and select the Payment Reference Number . A cheque issued to a foreign country that is in circulation for more than 6 months and not redeemed by the client is considered a reclaimed foreign cheque. When the cheque remains outstanding, the Bank of America returns the funds to the Imaging and Receiver General Operations Directorate (IRGOD) within Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC). IRGOD records the cheque in the Standard Payment System (SPS) with the Payment Information Status as Outstanding and the Payment Attempt Status as Returned , with the reason code Reclaimed Foreign Cheque . The Correspondence Indicator identifies if the cheque has been returned or not.

The operational policy Eligibility Requirements—GIS New Business (Policy) , Eligibility Requirements— ALW Benefit New Business (Policy) and Eligibility Requirements— ALWS Benefit New Business (Policy) have been updated to be better aligned, remove duplication and provide clarification where necessary. Here is a summary of the updates: Eligibility Requirements—GIS New Business (Policy) Eligibility Requirements— ALW Benefit New Business (Policy) Eligibility Requirements— ALWS Benefit New Business (Policy) Eligibility requirements for the GIS —Before, the applicant had to be “in receipt of” an OAS pension; now, the applicant must be “eligible for”. Applying from outside Canada and the departure from Canada is more than 6 months before the effective date for the GIS —Information about OAS pension portability has been removed. When the applicant’s departure date is more than 6 months before effective date of the GIS, the application must be denied. OAS pension portability and the ALW benefit eligibility —This section title has been changed to: “Entitlement to the ALW after the GIS pensioner departs Canada.” Information about portability has been removed. In cases where the GIS pensioner is absent from Canada and their GIS is suspended in the 7th month after their departure from Canada, the ALW is also suspended. Legislative requirements to approve a new business application for the GIS, ALW or ALWS Eligibility for the GIS—This was changed from: the individual must be “receiving” to “eligible for” an OAS pension. Entitlement for GIS or ALW —Information was added regarding an individual applying for the GIS or ALW online through My Service Canada Account and their spouse or common-law partner’s signature requirements and when it may be waived. In December 2020, an overpayment working group was formed to address various issues raised by the Department and Income Security and Social Development (ISSD) branch. Its mandate was to address any overpayment policy issues and to recommend proposed policy amendments common to both the CPP and OAS programs. Based on these recommendations, ISSD developed a policy framework to provide updated direction on: reduced recovery rates for active accounts or undue hardship claims; recovery from arrears; remissions; and erroneous advice/administrative error. A new Contribution Details screen has been created to display the data elements for the base, first additional and second additional components for each contributory year. The new screen will be accessible from a link at the bottom of the Earning Details screen. Only users with access to the Earnings Details screen will have access to this new screen. Users will be able to view the paid versus required contribution amounts for the base, first and second additional components of CPP and QPP. The amounts displayed on the Paid columns refers to the withheld salary contributions transmitted from CRA and Retraite Québec. This is the total T4 contributions amount withheld by the employer(s) for each base, first and second additional total contributions for CPP and QPP (paid by the contributor) for the tax year. The amounts displayed on the Required columns refers to the required salary contributions. This is the total contributions required for base and first additional components. The required contributions for the second additional component are based on T4 salary earnings in excess of the Year's Maximum Pensionable Earnings, but not exceeding the Year's Additional Maximum Pensionable Earnings for the year. One row per tax year will be displayed on the Contribution Details screen once ESDC receives the contributions data elements from CRA or Retraite Québec. Should the amounts be revised and updated by CRA or Retraite Québec, the new values will overwrite the previous values. The Paid and Required columns under 2nd Additional T4 Contributions column will be populated with 0.00 until CRA or Retraite Québec transfer the earnings and contributions data for the second additional component to ESDC. Figure 2. Contribution Details screen

T4 and T1 File T4 files (known as L6001 and L6003) and T1 file (known as L7001) that are transmitted to ESDC from CRA have been updated to accommodate the second additional contributions data (i.e., employee contributions on T4 file, self-employed contributions on T1 file). Given that the second additional contributions are calculated on a different range of earnings than the base and first additional components, data fields have been added to the T4 and T1 files to capture the CPP or QPP second additional contributions. The base and first additional CPP contributions will continue to appear on the T4 and T1 files as one contribution amount when transmitted to ESDC. As such, ESDC will continue dividing this amount by applying a ratio in real-time when required. T4 Tax Slip The T4 tax slip has been modified to add two boxes displaying the second additional contributions, one for each plan (CPP/QPP) under the existing fields (i.e. fields 16 and 17). Refunds and Benefit Payment Updated The CRA will continue to send to ESDC a single annual T1 refund of excess contributions paid to the client. The refund (reimbursement amount) may apply to the base and enhanced contributions (first and second additional components) for the CPP and/or QPP plans in the case of a dual year. System functionalities were implemented in February 2024 to enable the transmitting of additional T4 information for CPP and QPP, which may allow ESDC to calculate excess contributions amounts (refund) for the base, first additional and second additional components. The additional T4 information will be displayed on the new Contribution Details screen in ITRDS , which is accessible to the users who currently have access to the Earnings Details screen. As Canadians have until the end of April of each year to report their previous year's income to CRA , ESDC is expecting to start receiving the additional information in 2025. Columns to display the breakdown of base, first and second additional refund amounts will also be added to the Contribution screen in ITRDS in 2025. For clients with multiple T4s and no second additional contributions, but have total earnings within the second additional range, ESDC will calculate their benefits based on T4 contributions calculated from T4 earnings instead of net T4 contributions after a T1 refund. Benefits would be recalculated when T1 refund data is received from CRA .

text: Once a benefit has been adjudicated using Super PEP, anything that would normally trigger a readjudication in ITRDS (e.g. update to the record of earnings, change in interrelationship) does not change the Benefit Entitlement Amount, Start Date or End Date without manual intervention. To readjudicate a benefit, you must recalculate the benefit by using the Canada Pension Plan Calculation Module, enter the benefit amount into the Super PEP block and re-submit the data capture to update the benefit and override the adjudication system. However, the yearly benefit escalation process and entering a date of death for the client are exceptions to the above. This article provides information on Super Program Exception Process (Super PEP), which is used for accounts that cannot be processed by the Program Exception Process (PEP) in ITRDS .

Some scenarios prevent a CPP pension or benefit from being paid using the PEP functionality. If an account cannot be paid using the PEP functionality, you must use the Super PEP functionality, determine a client's CPP pension or benefit eligibility and perform manual calculations to determine a client's monthly entitlement amount. When you enter the amount in the Super PEP Data Capture block, the Super PEP functionality completely bypasses the ITRDS adjudication process. Super PEP functionality is used to: pay the correct benefit amounts when calculation errors exist and cannot be corrected; manually override continuing benefit entitlement for a specific benefit under the CPP; issue the 1st additional components of enhanced benefits in some circumstances; and pay CPP benefits with an International Social Security Agreement (ISSA) activity. The Super PEP user profile for non-ISSA accounts is only accessible to staff in St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador. The Super PEP user profile for ISSA accounts is only accessible to staff in International Operations (IO) processing centres. Super PEP accounts are identified by a message displayed in the Messages block on the Client Profile screen or the Data Capture Session Screen. The Super PEP block is available to Super PEP users below the PEP block(s) at the bottom of the data capture screens for each CPP benefit and pension ( RTR Pension, DSB , Death Benefit, SVR Pension, Surviving Child's benefit, and Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit). Super PEP functionality does not apply to the Child Rearing Provision, the Credit Splitting provision or the Pension Sharing provision. Once a benefit is adjudicated in ITRDS using the Super PEP block, the resulting pay pattern displayed on the current Benefits screen will indicate YES in the PEP indicator field. If an ISSA was used to determine eligibility, YES will be indicated in the ISSA field. All non-ISSA Super PEP enquiries, maintenance work items or other work items (i.e. dual accounts with Super PEP status) must be moved to the Program Exception Processing Unit. All ISSA Super PEP enquiries, maintenance work items or other work items for IO Super PEP accounts must be moved to the responsible IO Processing Unit. The Start Date entered in a PEP or Super PEP block cannot be the same Start Date as another Super PEP block for the same benefit. If a benefit requires adjudication using Super PEP and has the same Start Date and Effective Date as an existing PEP or Super PEP block, you must delete the existing PEP or Super PEP block before requesting the new Super PEP adjudication override. Super PEP requires one user to request the adjudication override, and a different user to approve the adjudication override. The Requester completes the Super PEP data capture block by entering the Start Date , End Date (if applicable), Amount at Start Date , Reason and Requester fields. Then the request is sent to another user for approval. The Approver reviews the Super PEP benefit and ensures the Data Capture block is complete before completing the Approver field. ITRDS puts the benefit in pay and a new pay pattern is created. The Start Date of the new pay pattern is equal to the Start Date entered in the Super PEP block. ITRDS automatically escalates the benefit amount if the year entered in the Start Date field of the Super PEP block is before the current year. When the Super PEP block is submitted and approved, a Benefit Entitlement Reason (e.g. Cancelled for Super PEP ) will appear on the ended pay pattern, if applicable. You can review the information captured in the Super PEP block by selecting Complete in the Application Status field on the Data Capture Selection screen.

The CPP enhancement legislative changes are being phased-in over seven years (from 2019 to 2025), starting in January 2019. The enhancement components (first and second additional) are not a separate benefit, but rather a top-up to the base CPP. The enhancement increases the CPP RTR pension, Post-Retirement Benefit ( PRB ), DSB and SVR pension. Eligibility for CPP benefits is not affected. In January 2019, the Canada Revenue Agency began collecting enhanced contributions from working Canadians. System updates required to accommodate the CPP enhancement legislative changes are being implemented gradually through the CPP enhancement project. On November 23, 2019, system functionalities to split earnings and contributions in ITRDS (base CPP and first additional component) were implemented. On May 21, 2022, system functionalities were introduced in ITRDS and CPMS to pay the first additional component of the CPP. On May 27, 2023, system functionalities were introduced in ITRDS to “drop in” credits (CRDI and DDI) into the calculation of the first additional component of CPP benefits. On September 1, 2023, an updated version (9.10.12) of the CPPCM tool was released to enable the manual calculation of the first additional component of the CPP.

Updates have been made to the CPPCM tool. For a description of changes (including screenshots), Updates to Canada Pension Plan Calculation Module—CPP Enhancement and Triennial Review Reforms (Implementation Bulletin)

A JVAN is a notification received from the Imaging and Receiver General Operations Directorate (IRGOD) after 2 CPP or OAS payments with the same Payment Reference Number (PRN) have been redeemed in the Standard Payment System (SPS). IRGOD will notify the Department via a JVAN after a minimum of 2 attempts are redeemed. However, there can be up to a maximum of 8 attempts made on each PRN. If a payment in SPS has more than one payment attempt number with a Redeemed status, IRGOD will conduct an investigation. Their investigation may involve several actions, including: sending a Declaration (PWGSC-TPSGC 548-1) form to the payee; examining the cheques; or communicating with a financial institution. When IRGOD completes their investigation, it will be closed. If the client claims they did not receive the PWGSC-TPSGC 548-1 form (e.g. due to a recent address change), you can contact IRGOD and request they resend the form. Depending on the outcome of the investigation, a work item or task will be created in the applicable system for each JVAN. JVANs are sent to the Department for many reasons, including situations where: the payee requested a duplicate payment claiming the original payment attempt was lost, then redeemed both attempts; one or more of the payment attempts were fraudulently redeemed (e.g. forged endorsement, altered cheque amount or unendorsed); or the payment attempt was deemed to be counterfeit.

Administrative Penalties were implemented on July 21, 2011. Misrepresentations that occurred before that date are not subject to a penalty. An administrative penalty on a misrepresentation is an amount that is charged to a client or third party who knowingly misrepresented in relation to CPP or OAS benefits or pensions. A penalty is intended to be a deterrent to discourage individuals from committing further misrepresentations and protect the integrity of the programs. ISB is responsible for making a recommendation to the Benefits Delivery Services (BDS) Branch to impose an administrative penalty when it is determined during an administrative investigation that an individual knowingly misrepresented themselves. BDS is responsible for making the final decision to apply a penalty or not.

text: The repayment amount consists of all monies paid to date that are related to the cancellation request, less any intercepted or returned payments and some tax withholds in the current or the previous year. For examples of calculating the repayment amount, refer to KA-0XXXX Examples—Cancellation of OAS Benefits (article not available). Review the Payment Correction Case on the Financials tab for the client and their spouse or common-law partner, if applicable, to view the repayment amount. Determine if there are deductions that the Department will seek reimbursement for from the CRA (i.e. Federal Voluntary Tax and Recovery Tax withheld in the previous year). If yes, proceed as follows: Manually calculate the amount of deductions that will be requested from the CRA . Do not include this amount in the repayment amount when requesting reimbursement from the client. Go to Step 3 . Step 3 If no, go to Step 3 . topic_title: Repayment of the OAS pension and related benefits
text: When a request to cancel benefits is granted, the full amount of all affected benefits received from the effective date must be repaid within 6 months of the date the request is granted. This includes: all OAS pension and GIS payments received by the client requesting the cancellation; and all ALW benefit payments received by the spouse or common-law partner of the client who has requested the cancellation of their OAS pension. The 6-month timeframe for repayment begins on the date the letter is sent by the Department advising the client and their spouse or common-law partner that the cancellation request has been granted and the repayment amount that is required. Although the request for cancellation must be received within 6 months of the issue date of the first affected pension or benefit payment, th e request can be granted after the 6 months have passed. Generally, the client and their spouse or common-law partner, if applicable, are responsible to repay 100% of the repayment amount. However, there are some monies that the Department can recover that will reduce the amount of repayment, such as: intercepted payments; returned payments; and some tax withholds. A client may request to have their repayment of benefits recovered from a CPP pension or benefit through a cross-program recovery. If this is the case, you must ensure that the entire amount will be recovered within the 6 months after the date on which the cancellation request is granted. If additional funds are required, the pensioner or ALW benefit client must repay the difference within the 6-month timeframe. If the full repayment of all benefits is received within the 6-month timeframe, the OAS pension and the GIS are cancelled retroactively to the initial effective date. This results in the recalculation of their spouse or common-law partner's GIS or their non-eligibility to the ALW benefit, as applicable. If the full repayment of all benefits is not received within the 6-month timeframe: the OAS pension and any related benefits are reinstated; and any recovered amounts are returned to the pensioner and to the ALW benefit client, as applicable. The repayment amount is not considered a debt to the Crown as the client and their spouse or common-law partner, if applicable, are entitled to receive the OAS pension and related benefits. However, for financial record keeping purposes , th e repayment amount will be established in Cúram as an overpayment. The corresponding overpayment created in Cúram when the request is granted will be sent to the Public Sector Collections and Disbursements system once activated, but will have a 10-month collection deferral date to prevent the debt from being sent to the CRA for collection. The cancellation process must be finalized within this timeframe as the overpayment created for the purpose of cancelling a pension or benefit must not be sent to the CRA for collection. Repayment of withholds Until the final year tax remittance has been sent to the CRA in Janua ry of e ach year, some current calendar year tax withhold amounts can be reversed. Since January 15, 2018, the Department seeks rei mbursement from th e CRA for certai n taxes that were withheld in a previous calendar year. For other deductions, the amounts are forwarded to the applicable government author ity on a monthly basis and cannot be recovered by the Department. The following table lists the various withholds and whether the Department can recover them, or if they must be include d in the repayment amount for the client and their spouse or common-law partner, if applicable: Table 1. Withhold type and direction Withhold type Direction OAS Recovery Tax Amounts withheld in the current calendar year The Department can recover OAS Recovery Tax amounts withheld in the current calendar year. The total amount recovered is not included in the repayment amount. Amounts withheld in a previous calendar year OAS Recovery tax withheld in a previous calendar year can be recovered. The Department will seek reimbursement from the CRA for the amount withheld. The total amount to be recovered is not included in the repayment amount. This reimbursement will only be requested from the CRA once the client has reimbursed the full repayment amount. Federal Voluntary Tax Amounts withheld in the current calendar year The Department can recover Federal Voluntary Tax amounts withheld in the current calendar year. The total amount recovered is not included in the repayment amount. Amounts withheld in a previous calendar year Federal Voluntary Tax withheld in a previous calendar year can be recovered. The Department will seek reimbursement from the CRA for the amount withheld. The total amount to be recovered is not included in the repayment amount. This reimbursement will only be requested from the CRA once the client has reimbursed the full repayment amount. Provincial Voluntary Tax (Quebec) Amounts withheld in the current calendar year As the amount withheld is forwarded to Revenu Québec on a monthly basis, the Department cannot recover Provincial Voluntary Tax amounts withheld in the current calendar year. The total amount recovered must be included in the repayment amount. Clients will have to claim the withholds amount from Revenu Québec. Amounts withheld in a previous calendar year As the Department does not have a process in place with Revenu Québec to seek reimbursement of Provincial Voluntary Tax amounts withheld in a previous calendar year, the total amount must be included in the repayment amount. Clients will have to claim the withholds amount from Revenu Québec. Non-Resident Tax Amounts withheld in the current calendar year The Department can recover Non-Resident Tax amounts withheld in the current calendar year. topic_title: Requesting the reimbursement of deductions from the CRA
text: You may be able to request a reimbursement of OAS Recovery Tax and Federal Voluntary Tax withheld during the previous calendar year from the CRA using the Request for manual adjustment of OAS recovery Tax / Federal Voluntary Tax Withhold (VTW) for cancellation of OAS pension (ISP-3091) form. You must only submit the request for reimbursement once the following conditions are met: The pensioner and the ALW benefit client, if applicable, have fully repaid the amount requested from them by the Department; and The repayment was made within 6 months from the date that the pensioner's request for cancellation was granted. If these conditions are met, the request for reimbursement can be completed and sent to the CRA for the pensioner and the ALW benefit client, if applicable. A separate request is required for each account and for each year. Each request must include: a completed and approved ISP-3091 form; and an amended or cancelled tax slip (i.e. a T4A (OAS) Statement of Old Age Security (ISP-0137) or NR4 (OAS) Statement of Old Age Security Pension paid or credited to non-residents of Canada (ISP-0138) form, as required) for the applicable year. Recording the submission of the ISP-3091 form in Cúram When the ISP-3091 form has been sent to the CRA , you must record in Cúram that this action has been completed by updating the status of the applicable deductions. Although this status does not affect any year-to-date values, it provides the Chief Financial Officer Branch the ability to reconcile the payments when they are received from the CRA . This status can be found on the Transactions screen on the Financials tab of the Product Delivery Case. The ability to modify this status is available when: there is Federal Voluntary Tax or OAS Recovery Tax withheld; and there is active Benefit Cancellation Request evidence on the Integrated Case. Once the ISP-3091 form is sent to the CRA , access each payment that corresponds to the deductions being requested and click on Set as Refunded for each payment's Federal Voluntary Tax or Recovery Tax Withhold. If this status is set to Refunded in error, click on Reset Status to reset it.

topic_title: Spouse or common-law partner in receipt of the GIS or an ALW benefit
text: If the client has a spouse or common-law partner in receipt of the ALW benefit, the cancellation of the client's OAS pension will result in their spouse or common-law partner's non-eligibility to the ALW benefit and the loss of the lifetime renewal designation. The ALW benefit application will be considered to have never been made. All ALW benefit payments received must be repaid within the 6-month timeframe. If these benefits are not repaid in time, the cancellation request will not be finalized and all OAS benefits will be reinstated, even if the full OA S pension and GIS repayment is made. If the spouse or common-law partner of an individual whose OAS pension was cancelled is in receipt of the GIS at a table 2 rate (i.e. a client who is married to or living in a common-law relationship with another pensioner), a recalculation of their GIS will be performed for the period affected by the cancellation and any payments issued up until the cancellation is finalized. They would now be entitled to the GIS at the table 3 rate (i.e. a client who is married to or living in a common-law relationship with a non-pensioner) as their spouse or common-law partner is no longer an OAS pensioner. The recalculation of the spouse or common-law partner's benefits is performed only once the cancellation has been finalized (i.e. after the required repayment of benefits is confirmed). Under most circumstances, a couple where both are OAS pensioners will receive a higher combined GIS amount between them when they are paid on rate table 2 than they would if only one of them is a pensioner paid on rate table 3. However, there are situations where the combination of income levels and years of entitlement results in a lower combined amount. When this happens, the Department can pay married or common-law OAS pensioners using separate rate tables (rate tables 2 and 3) and pay one pensioner an adjustment amount to ensure that their total benefits are no less than they would have received using rate table 3. This adjustment would be included in the repayment amount. For more information on this provision, refer to: Paying Two Pensioners at One Pensioner Rate (Policy) ; and Paying Two Pensioners at One Pensioner Rate (Policy) Marital Status and Rate Tables for Income-Tested Benefits .
