Provide the CRA with taxable income breakdown information for notional tax purposes

The purpose of providing a breakdown of the total taxable income reported on the current tax slip to the CRA is to inform them how much of that total can be attributed to previous income years. When you receive a CRA breakdown request, you must provide the notional tax breakdown to the CRA within 30 days of receiving the request. If the CRA does not receive the breakdown within 30 days, they will assess the client's tax return without applying the notional tax provision. If the CRA does not apply the notional tax provision, a client can request to have it applied to their tax return and to have their taxes adjusted. The CRA sends the requests by email to the CPP notional tax contact at each regional processing centre. Processing centres must provide the breakdowns for the lump sum payments generated by an initial payment within their Office of Control. Validating the CRA breakdown request You must identify the reason for the notional tax request to accurately respond to the CRA 's enquiry. Situations when retroactive or arrears payments can result in notional tax include: applying the Child Rearing Provision to an existing benefit in pay; approving a new benefit with an effective date in a previous year; or a Record of Earnings update resulting in a payable of $300.00 or more for a previous year. Notional tax may not always be from a lump sum retroactive or arrears payment. The notional tax breakdown can be falsely generated on a tax slip due to a user or system error within CPMS or the IA system before the 2025 tax year. For example, applying an invalid payable (underpayment) to an invalid departmental receivable (overpayment) produces an incorrect notional tax breakdown, which results in a notional tax breakdown request from the CRA . Other examples that can result in a CRA notional tax break down request are: data capture errors; and manual priority payments. In these examples, it can be necessary to also issue an amended tax slip to correct the errors. For more information regarding the reasons to issue an amended tax slip and instructions on how to correct it, refer to T4 and NR4 Tax Slips Mail-out for 2023—Cyclical (Knowledge) to access the Annual CPP Taxation Instructional Bulletin – Taxation Year 20XX for the current taxation year. The notional tax provision applies when a retroactive CPP or QPP lump sum payment or the total of multiple lump sum payments: was or were paid in the base calendar year; and includes a total amount of $300.00 or more that relates to a previous calendar year. When determining entitlement for income-tested benefits, the notional tax provision is applied for all clients who meet the above criteria, regardless of whether there is a tax benefit. The income removed from the current year is not retroactively applied to previous years and is not considered income for the previous years. For more Information, Calculating Income (Policy) In most cases, the base calendar year portion can be calculated by taking the December gross CPP or QPP rate and multiplying it by 12. Any retroactive CPP or QPP lump sum payments that do not extend to a previous calendar year, or any amount for the previous year that is less than $300.00, must be included in the base calendar year income in which the underpayment was issued. Although this adjustment is automatically applied by OAS Online and the IA system, the following situations may require manual adjustment: The income information is reported on an application or a statement of income and the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) income information is not available. The client may not be aware of the notional tax provision and may include the full amount of CPP or QPP benefits received, including the full arrears portion; At reversion time (end of June), if both CRA income and client-reported income exist in the system, the system compares the income provided by the CRA to the client-reported income and retains the higher of the 2 amounts. If the client-reported income contains the full retroactive payment, the system will not retain the CRA income where the notional tax provision was applied; The notional tax provision was not applied by the CRA as it did not benefit the client for income tax purposes; The client did not file a federal Income Tax and Benefit Return; and An information link with the CRA has not been established for the account. To identify situations where the notional tax provision must be applied manually, verify the CPP and QPP amounts reported on all applications and statements of income.

On April 2, 2024, Service Canada will launch the CPPD Return to Work (RTW) Pilot Project. They will benefit from personalized case management by the newly introduced role of RTW Navigator, who will be the primary point of contact for RTW clients. After the client reports their RTW, an Enquiry-RTW PWS work item is created and sent to processing. At this point, the RTW pilot team will randomly select participants (750 per year) before the work gets assigned to regular workflows. RTW Navigators will use GC Notify External link to send outgoing (i.e. one-way) emails and text messages to pilot participants. Effective May 2, 2024, the following clarifications of the notional tax provision must be followed: Notional tax considerations may only be applied to retroactive lump sum payments of CPP or QPP when portions from the previous years of the payment are $300 or more. This means that any portions of the lump sum payment from previous years are subtracted from the base calendar year amount. The Program Exception Process (PEP) system is used to bypass certain calculations that would normally be done in ITRDS, specifically the calculation of the Retirement For Benefit Calculation (RTR-FBC). Authorized users can enter a manually calculated RTR-FBC into the PEP block. PEP then uses the manually entered RTR-FBC and other benefit information to calculate the benefit amount. PEP has built in rules that prevent the user from entering an amount free of benefit adjudication rules. In other words, the user cannot enter any amount to be paid. The Canada Pension Plan Calculation Module (CPPCM) is primarily used to calculate the RTR-FBC amount. The reasons for which a user would enter a manually calculated RTR-FBC (to override the automatically calculated one) would include but not limited to: ITRDS system bugs or a ministerial decision. While PEP is a suitable platform to pay most accounts that can’t be paid in ITRDS, it does have certain limitations. If there is a system bug that affects both ITRDS and PEP, the agent must issue a manual priority payment to pay the benefit.

Super PEP will be implemented on May 25, 2024. Super PEP functionality allows the user to override the PEP block to support CPP benefits that cannot be paid in regular PEP. As a result, authorized users have the option to bypass eligibility and entitlement rules that are present in regular PEP. The user can enter a monthly amount to be paid rather than entering an RTR-FBC to calculate the monthly amount. The CPPCM is primarily used to calculate the monthly amount. Super PEP users will be the same users currently using regular PEP. When Super PEP is implemented, there will be no accounts present in Super PEP. When accounts require Super PEP, the scenario(s) must be updated in the Super PEP section of the Special Handling Bulletin. Super PEP can only be used for exceptional situations, its primary purpose being to pay CPP International Agreements (IA) accounts. CPP IA accounts are scheduled to be onboarded in Super PEP in December 2024. From a workload and workflow perspective, the same process applied to regular PEP is to be applied to Super PEP accounts. When an account no longer needs to be maintained using the PEP functionality, it can be converted to a regular account in ITRDS by using the Remove PEP Status screen. Only one user is required to remove the PEP status. When PEP accounts are converted to a regular account in ITRDS , the regional staff can process these accounts as they would other accounts. The Remove PEP Status screen removes all PEP blocks on an account and triggers the ITRDS adjudication system to re-adjudicate all benefits. Removing the PEP status does not result in a new pay pattern on the Benefit screen as it causes a re-calculation of the entire benefit. All benefits and provisions on all interrelated accounts are also re-adjudicated. Once the PEP status is removed, the Client Profile screen no longer displays the PEP icon. topic_title: System operations—Changes to pension systems, applications, and tools
text: CPMS The new periodic payment functionality in CPMS allows users to modify the frequency of CPP benefit payments for an eligible client. It eliminates the need for suspending a client's account to manipulate the frequency of their payment. CPMS changes have been implemented and are detailed below. CPMS Online Help The CPMS Online Help has been updated to include help pages for the new Payment Frequency functionality and to ensure that all the links point to the correct location. Additional CPMS fixes Also included in this release are fixes to high priority outstanding issues that have been identified by Operations, as well as system performance corrections to improve the efficiency of CPMS : Table 1. Issue Description Fix Supplementary Payable remains in Pending status after split When CPMS received a change in payee to a bulk payee, where the account's payee was not being updated for any outstanding unpaid split payables, leaving the payables in Pending status. As a result, users had to issue manual priority payments and modify tax slips. The system now correctly updates the account's payee and supplementary payable status. Thus, automatically paying the outstanding supplementary payable and producing an accurate tax slip. Net pay - one-time recovery creating duplicate deductions When a one-time recovery/deduction was created on a payable, CPMS was creating a duplicate deduction. No payment was displayed in the payment history and no payment was sent to the Standard Payment System. As a result, users were required to open a ticket with the National Service Desk — Production Support to have the account corrected. The system no long creates duplicate deductions. Users no longer need to open a ticket with the National Service Desk to have the account corrected. Receivable status blank (impacts CRA set-off) When the Status Reason on the Departmental Receivable screen was blank the user was unable to update the receivable. As a result, users had to manually suspend the benefit in ITRDS and create priority payments outside of CPMS requiring modifications to tax slips. The system displays the receivable Status Reason and users are able to action as required. More than one third party receivable created CPMS was incorrectly allowing users to add another active third party receivable for the same department (e.g. Canada Revenue Agency, Department of Veterans Affairs). Only one third party receivable for each department can be active at one time in CPMS . Public Trustee Payment History error When viewing the Payment History Details screen for a bulk payee, an error was displayed “An unexpected error occurred. Please try again Message ID: 100.”. The user was unable to view the details of payment. This only impacted accounts where there was a change in the payee. For example, the client's monthly payment was being issued to them directly and then was changed to a bulk payee. Users can now view the payment details for payments paid to public trustees. Active/Inactive Entitlements after Escalation When a first additional benefit went from $0 to >$0 through the escalation process, the Entitlements statuses were not syncing. The CPMS Status went to Active displaying the Entitlement and paying the client, but the Client Status remained Inactive. The correct escalation rate is now being applied to a client's first additional benefit. Consolidate Recovered Amount Adjustment Details On the Departmental Receivables Details screen, CPMS was displaying every myEMS (SAP) transaction for a receivable. The Departmental Receivables Details screen now displays one deduction which represents the sum of the SAP transactions. Non-Resident Tax (NRT) not applied to Arrears Payable NRT was not being applied to payments on foreign accounts, which means that the CRA was not receiving the NRT. As a result, clients were receiving a T4A(P) instead of an NR4 slip. An NRT deduction is applied to the payment when it is released. This is displayed on both the Preview Payment Details screen, and the Payment History Details screen within CPMS . Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit ( DCCB ) or Surviving Child's Benefit for which the recovery of an overpayment includes a payee's monthly entitlement for a child under the age of 18 (-18 child) When a DCCB or Surviving Child's Benefit overpayment existed for –18 child, the payee's monthly entitlement, if one exists, was not being factored in when determining the recovery amount. The net pay process was impacted as the incorrect amount was not being recovered. Agents no longer need to determine if the correct overpayment recovery has been applied. Instead of only referring to monthly entitlements, the indications for clients are more general, referring to payment amount regardless of its frequency. Effective immediately , the SCBO and MA will use the following guidance: Repayment of Refunded Contributions for Late Applicant Provision using proration Late applicants who meet the Minimum Qualifying Period (MQP) with a prorate date are no longer required to repay refunded contributions for the year of the established Date of Onset (DOO). All LAP prorate files must be sent to the Program Exception Processing Unit to be paid using the Program Exception Process (PEP) functionality. When referring the file to PEP, provide the prorated year and the earnings and contributions for that year in the email. This will allow PEP to accurately determine the monthly entitlement amount. There is no requirement for late applicants to repay refunded contributions in the prorated year to establish an MQP. LAP prorate accounts that have been in pay, readjudicated and are now denied must be sent to the Program Exception Processing Unit to be paid using the PEP functionality. The overpayment created because of the denial will be adjusted. Any LAP prorate accounts that were identified on the LAP prorate scan that are still in pay do not need to be sent to the Program Exception Processing Unit. If the DSB is denied later due to refunded contributions in the established DOO, the account must be sent to the Program Exception Processing Unit to be paid using the PEP functionality. National Business Expertise Tool Interpretation of "Triggering Event" The words “commenced,” and “triggering event” are not intended to be interpreted in a literal sense as reflected in the previous policy. In order to qualify for CPPD benefits, the individual must demonstrate that they are disabled on or before the end of their MQP, which ends with a prorated period. If there was a specific disabling event, it does not need to occur within the prorated period, as was the previous direction. If the disabling event occurred prior to the prorated period, the benefit can still be granted provided the applicant continues to be disabled in the future. The date of the disabling event, for CPPD benefits purposes, is the DOO or for late applicants, the established DOO. The previously used language “within the prorate period, by the prorate month” should not be used in decision rationales. When making a decision for the prorated MQP, the rationale should clearly state whether the applicant meets the severe and prolonged criteria by the end of the prorated MQP, instead of “within the prorate year, by the prorate month.” Interim modified letters with updated language for this change can be found from the KMT EReference Library page, under Work Tools, CPPD, Interim denial letters for proration. Accounts will appear on this report when any of the following exclusions are detected at age 65: One of the addresses is outside of Canada; The address is invalid; There is a SIR Warning Flag; There is a fraudulent SIN; The client deceased. The process begins by selecting a template, entering the client's SIN or the ITRDS Client Identification Number and editing the letter in the Interactive Editor . The draft template can be saved for later or submitted to Awaiting Delivery for printing/mailing to the client and archiving.

Log in to the CCT. For the link to the CCT, refer to Corporate Correspondence Tool (CCT) . Corporate Correspondence Tool (CCT) Select Template . Click Next . Enter Customer Keys : enter the client's SIN and select the appropriate Client Information Source . Click Next . Verify customer details: verify the client's information and address are correct. Click Next . Edit communication: launch the Interactive Editor by clicking on Edit Communication and proceed with entering the letter details and making the appropriate selections. All prompts must be completed. Close the Interactive Editor . If the letter requires an attachment, click on Attach File in the Attachments window to include additional documents or forms, then click on Submit if you are ready to locally print and mail the letter to the client.

When creating a letter in the CCT, the letter must be submitted to Awaiting Delivery before it can be printed and mailed locally. Once the letter is submitted, you will need to retrieve it from the Awaiting Delivery screen to access the PDF of the letter to print and mail it to the client. Letters submitted in the CCT cannot be modified. If a mistake is found in a letter after it has been submitted to Awaiting Delivery , it must be deleted on the same day as it will be archived to the CCT vault overnight. To delete a letter from the CCT Vault, you will need to submit a service ticket with the National Service Desk.

Retrieve the letter from the Awaiting Delivery screen. Click on the View and Confirm Manual Delivery hyperlink to open a preview of the letter. Click Open in External Reader to save the letter in a central folder location to be printed locally. Close the external reader and return to the Awaiting Delivery screen. Click on the View and Confirm Manual Delivery hyperlink. Click on Confirm Delivery to change the CCT status from Pending Delivery to Finished . This informs the CCT that the letter is printed locally and mailed to the client.

As a result of the Migration OAS Overpayment Review project led by National Headquarters (NHQ), processing staff will see a noticeable decrease in overpayment work items in their workload. At the conclusion of the Migration OAS Overpayment Review project, there may still be overpayment work items that meet the criteria but will require manual review. Further guidance for the manual review for the remaining overpayment work items is currently being developed.

The Migration OAS Overpayment Review project will clean up uncollectible overpayments associated with inactive accounts. Beginning in July 2024, a series of automated clean-up process activities on inactive accounts will take place to remit or write-off overpayments based on the below approved criteria. Remit criteria Accounts with an overpayment amount equal to or less than $100.00 (further action would not be cost effective). Accounts where the debtor’s date of death occurred 2 years or more before the current accounting month in OAS Online (cannot be collected in the foreseeable future). Write-off criterion Inactive files with no Date of Death (DOD) and no activity for 7 years from the current accounting month in OAS online (cannot be collected in the foreseeable future).

This procedure provides guidance on the lifetime renewal designation and how to view a client's income-tested benefits for life status (i.e. ITB for Life status) in Cúram.

View the ITB for Life status In Cúram, go to the person's profile. Refer to Search for a Person in Cúram (Action) . Search for a Person in Cúram (Action) Click the Cases and Application tab on the navigation bar. Click Applications on the page group navigation bar on the left. Click the Reference number hyperlink of the Old Age Security Program Benefits case under the Reference column. The Old Age Security Program Benefits product delivery case opens in a new tab. Click the Determinations tab on the navigation bar. Click the Coverage Period hyperlink for the applicable date range under the Coverage Period column. The ITB for Life status is displayed in the context panel.

As of May 3, 2007, when an income-tested benefit application is approved, the client qualifies for a lifetime renewal designation. Once the client has a lifetime renewal designation, the ITB for Life status in Cúram will be set to Yes . Any subsequent income received from the CRA will automatically be used to calculate the client's benefit entitlement for the renewal of their income-tested benefits. As a result, a client who files their annual income tax return will never have to submit a statement of income. This designation remains on the account until the client is no longer eligible for the benefit. If the designation is lost, the client will have to submit a new application to have it reinstated. Following the eligibility assessment in Cúram, the ITB for Life status will be updated to reflect the client’s eligibility to the yearly renewal of income-tested benefits. The ITB for Life status cannot be manually modified. The designation and effective date are set automatically based on actions performed in the system. There are situations where the client can be eligible for the benefit, but not in pay. In these cases, the lifetime renewal designation remains on the account. Here are some examples where the client is not entitled to income-tested benefits, but they retain their lifetime renewal designation: the income is in excess; no income was received for a payment year; the client or their spouse or common-law partner is temporarily outside of Canada longer than 6 months and entitlement is affected; or the client or their spouse or common-law partner is under a sponsorship agreement and entitlement is limited. Once the client becomes entitled again (e.g. income is received, client returns to Canada, sponsorship ends), the benefit can be reinstated without having to reapply, as long as the required income has been received from the client or the CRA. For more information, Reinstatement (Policy) For more information about the requirements for a lifetime renewal designation, Lifetime Renewal Designation (Policy) For examples of how the lifetime renewal designation is affected in various situations, Situations Affecting the Lifetime Renewal Designation (Work Tool)

text: This Service Canada form is found in E-Forms. You can complete it online and then print or save it. Table 2. Section A Field Direction Type of request: Check the applicable box to indicate the type of request you are submitting and complete the sections as directed on the form. Table 3. Section B – New cross program recovery request Field Direction Total overpayment amount Indicate the total dollar amount of the overpayment that the debtor owes under your program. Overpayment amount to be recovered Enter the total dollar amount that you want the other program to recover. For example, if your program has an overpayment of $10,000.00 and: you are requesting a monthly withhold to recover the entire overpayment, indicate $10,000.00; or you are requesting a recovery from a Death ( DTH ) benefit payable, indicate $2,500.00. Type of recovery requested: Check the applicable box or boxes to indicate if you want to request a monthly recovery, lump sum recovery or both. Proceed as follows: If you are requesting a monthly recovery, complete section i) ; If you are requesting a lump sum recovery, complete section ii) ; or If you are requesting both, complete sections i) and ii) . i) Monthly recovery rate requested: Access the Benefits screen in ITRDS . Determine the benefit types and the debtor's current monthly entitlement for each benefit type under the other program. Calculate the total dollar amount of the debtor's current monthly entitlement under the other program. Determine the recovery rate to request. Refer to Recovery Guidelines (Work Tool) . Recovery Guidelines (Work Tool) Enter the: dollar amount of the recovery rate in the Amount field; or percentage in the Percentage field. Recovery Guidelines (Work Tool) ii) Lump Sum amount requested: Indicate the lump sum amount that you are requesting as directed below: Amount to recover from a DTH benefit: To request a recovery from a DTH benefit, indicate the lesser of: the total amount of the overpayment owing under your program; the amount indicated by the CPP program in the Notes field of the Overpayment - cross program recovery work item you received, if applicable; or $2,500.00. Amount to recover from an underpayment (i.e. other than DTH benefit payable): To request a recovery from an underpayment, indicate the lesser of the: amount of the overpayment owing under your program; or amount indicated by the other program in the Notes field of the Overpayment - cross program recovery work item you received, if applicable. Additional information If there is any additional information or direction that you want to provide, enter it in this field. Go to Section F – Requestor signature . Table 4. Go to Section E . Table 6. Section E Field Direction Reason for modification, suspension, deferral or cancellation Proceed as applicable below: For a modification, provide the reason for the modification. For a cancellation of a cross program recovery provide: the reason for the cancellation; and the amount that the recovering program must refund to the debtor or their legal representative, if applicable (e.g. if the overpayment was over-recovered as debtor sent in a full repayment or decision on a reconsideration resulted in the overpayment no longer being valid). Go to Section F . Table 7. Section F - Requestor signature Field Direction Requestor name Enter your full name. Telephone number (include area code) Enter your telephone number. Requestor signature Sign the form using your digital signature. Date (YYYY-MM-DD) Select the current date from the calendar. P/A check boxes (i.e. found below the Response section) Leave the check boxes blank if you are initiating the request (e.g. new cross program or a modification) to the other program area. Once you receive the form back with the other program's response, then check the applicable box to have a copy of the form put away to your program's file.

Table 8. Section A – New cross program recovery request – Monthly payments Field Direction i) Monthly recovery accepted: Proceed as applicable: If a monthly cross program recovery was requested: check Yes if you are accepting the request. Table 9. Legislative changes brought about by the Jobs, Growth and Long-Term Prosperity Act received Royal Assent on June 29, 2012, to amalgamate the privacy codes found in 5 separate Departmental Acts, including those in the CPP and OAS Act, into Part 4 of the DESDA. Consolidation of the privacy codes allows for better management of risks of accidental or unauthorized release of personal information to others, such as individuals, Federal and Provincial departments. On March 1, 2013, the privacy provisions common to the CPP and OAS Act were repealed, while those specific to each Act remained within the respective Acts: Sections 33 to 33.13 of the OAS Act and 104 to 105 of the CPP were removed and amalgamated into Part 4 of the DESDA. Sections 60 and 60.1 of the CPP Regulations and Sections 28.2 and 28.3 of the OAS Regulations were repealed so that the 1-year expiration date on written consent forms was no longer legislated but would continue to be the limit set by Departmental policy.

This knowledge article provides you with information regarding the Pensions Trusted Digital Repository (PTDR), a new digital document storage solution that will provide pension programs with a secure and sustainable repository based on SharePoint Online architecture to help digitize, view, and manage pension documents and files in an efficient and effective manner.

Effective August 26, 2024, the PTDR will be launched using a phased implementation approach in the regional processing network and integrated with the PWS . The PTDR phased implementation dates are as follows: Phase 1: Quebec (August 26) Phase 2: Atlantic (September 9) Phase 3: Western Territories (September 23) Phase 4: Ontario (October 7) Dedicated support will be provided to the regions during the monitoring and stabilization phase. All documents scanned into the PTDR will have a corresponding work item in the PWS , and Optical Character Recognition technology will be used to pre-populate metadata fields and simplify work item creation. The documents in the PTDR will be accessible through hyperlinks contained within the PWS work item. The introduction of the PTDR allows for the destruction and disposition of paper sources 120 days after digitization, provided : There is no litigation on the file where the paper document is relevant; The image enters the system “as is,” so the record can be used and submitted as evidence, and that the quality of that image is sufficient for business needs; and Disposition of the paper sources becomes part of Pensions' regular business practice and must be observed consistently across all regions and all programs.

To enable work from home during the COVID-19 pandemic, ESDC Pensions Programs shifted to digitizing incoming applications for the CPP and the OAS programs. These documents are currently saved to regional shared drives, a procedure that was meant to be temporary given storage limitations and data management risks. The Pensions Trusted Digital Repository (PTDR) modernizes the existing digital Pensions document storage solution – shared drives – with a permanent, digital trusted document repository based on a SharePoint Online architecture. Effective August 26, 2024, the PTDR will be launched using a phased implementation approach in the regional processing network and integrated with the PWS . Dedicated support will be provided to the regions throughout implementation. The PTDR will provide secure storage for the digitized applications and supporting documents which will ultimately allow pensions programs to destroy the paper copies and reduce file management storage challenges and costs.

Implementation of the PTDR will involve new national scanning and validation processes. New processes will include a document naming convention (to support the PWS automation) and a two-step quality validation process that enables the conditions required to create the environment necessary to allow the Department to shred paper after it has been digitized. Once scanned, documents will initially be saved in a temporary folder in SharePoint Online. Once the two-step quality control is complete in the SharePoint Online temporary folder, the scanned item will automatically move to the trusted repository. The PWS polls the PTDR once every hour to collect information for all new scanned images and uses this information to automatically create new work items. Each work item contains a hyperlink to the associated image in the PTDR, and all images in the PTDR are viewed through the PWS . The introduction of the PTDR also allows for the destruction and disposition of paper sources 120 days after digitization. Disposition of the paper can only occur if: There are security and audit system processes to ensure the integrity of the image. This means that the system can keep a log of when and who accessed the image, and what was done to the image (such as downloading or editing); There are business processes in place to ensure the image gets into that system “as is” so that the record can be used and submitted as evidence, and that the quality of that image is sufficient for the business needs; and Disposition of the paper becomes part of the regular business practice (this means it needs to be observed consistently across all regions and all programs). Documents must be scanned “as is” with no alterations made to the documentation to provide a level of confidence that the electronic image within the PTDR can be trusted as an original. The two-step verification ensures that the electronic image is readable, with no pages missing, or obstructions, so that the paper source can be disposed with confidence that the electronic image can be used by adjudicators. The electronic record must be the record used for all adjudication and decision making. The PTDR Procedures Manual Internal link located on the PTDR SharePoint Library outlines the business processes and steps (from intake to accessing the image) to ensure that the documents are scanned into the PTDR “as is” and of sufficient quality to meet adjudication needs while allowing for the destruction of the paper source. Absences from Canada can affect eligibility and entitlement to the following OAS pension and benefits: A non-portable OAS pension; The GIS ; The ALW benefit; and The ALWS benefit. Effective January 1, 2025, the eligibility to the DCCB can be extended for the child of a disabled contributor who was in receipt of a DSB or PRDB when they turned 65 years of age. Their 65th birthday must be in January 2025 or later, and the DCCB must be in pay at the time of the event to be identified on the monthly ITRDS report. A manual process is required for the DCCB to receive payments after a disabled contributor reaches the age of 65. The ITRDS report identifies accounts (including accounts with Program Exception Processing (PEP) and Super PEP status) that require this manual process. The responsible International Operations (IO) centres and the Specialized Processing Centres in Chatham, Ontario and St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador, will monitor their respective PRDB beneficiaries for when they reach age 65 and there is a DCCB in pay at the time of the event. For all identified accounts, the Specialized Processing Centres ( PRDB or IO) are responsible for issuing the monthly manual priority payments for the DCCB after the DSB converts to RTR pension or PRDB ends at age 65. Eligibility For the child to be eligible to receive the DCCB after the contributor reaches age 65, the following criteria must be met at the time the CPPD beneficiary turns 65 years of age: A DCCB is in pay at the time of the event; The established child-contributor relationship continues; and For a child over the age of 18, they continue to be in full-time or part-time attendance at school or university. Postal Disruption Process As of October 11, 2025, Canada Post has resumed regular mail delivery on a rotating basis. The full disruption lasted 16 days, from September 25 to October 10, 2025. During the postal disruption, mailed documents submitted by applicants, beneficiaries and third parties may be delayed until the disruption has ended. The extension for protected date will be equal to the number of days of the full postal disruption (16 days) plus an additional 21 days. Therefore, the Department must date protect applications and all other correspondence received by mail to September 25, 2025, if received before October 31, 2025. For clarification purposes, the following methods are considered “mail" submissions: Regular mail Drop off at Service Canada Centre Courier Services (e.g. UPS, Purolator) The following methods are considered “digital" submissions and are not subject to protected date for the purpose of the postal disruption: MSCA (e.g. Online applications, reconsideration requests) Document Upload Solution (DUS) Faxed documents Common CPPD OAS SST At the Social Security Tribunal General Division ( SST — GD), documents submitted by Appellants and third parties by mail may not be received by Service Canada until after the disruption has ended. When a new Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form is received for an estimate year, you must add a new Statement of Estimated Income evidence to capture the details of the event and income. This will create the applicable Estimated Income and Estimated Income Data evidences. If a subsequent form for the same year is received or if changes are needed once the Statement of Estimated Income evidence has been created for a given year, you must edit, add or delete the existing evidences as required. Statement of estimated income evidence Estimated income evidence Estimated income data evidence

When a Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form is received, you will use the Statement of Estimated Income wizard to create a new statement of estimated income evidence record based on the relevant details on the form. The wizard will guide you through adding the required information to create Estimated Income evidence and Estimated Income Data evidence. The information found in these 3 evidences are as follows: Table 1. Evidence types and information Evidence Information Statement of Estimated Income evidence This evidence captures the general information about the statement (e.g. estimate year, receipt date) and the event (e.g. event type, event date, reconciliation status). Only one Statement of Estimated Income evidence should exist for each estimate year. If a subsequent ISP-3041 form is received for the same estimate year, you must amend the existing statement for that year rather than create a new one. Estimated Income evidence This evidence captures the income types and frequencies of payments. A separate estimated income evidence is created for each income type. Estimated Income Data evidence This evidence captures the details of each income type (e.g. benefit rates before and after the event). A separate estimated income data evidence is created for each pension or income change in the estimate year. For example, if a client’s Registered Retirement Income Fund payments reduced twice during the estimate year, 3 estimated income data evidences are required: one for the start date and initial payment amount; and one for each payment rate reduction. Before activating the evidence in Cúram, you must review and analyze the information to ensure it is as complete and accurate as possible to avoid overpayments when the estimated income is reconciled with the actual income in the following year. For more information on analyzing the information provided on the ISP-3041, Estimated Income (Options) (Scenario) Once all updates have been applied and the evidences have been activated, Cúram will perform the option calculation based on the estimated income details that have been data captured. Cúram will use the estimated income evidences to calculate blocks 1, 2, 3, 7, 8 and 9. You must capture all income from these blocks as estimated income evidence, including non-optionable income (e.g. base calendar year) from Block 9. This income is automatically combined with the base calendar year income for blocks 4, 5 and 6 to determine the total estimated income. This total estimated income is compared to the total base year income and the most advantageous income is used to calculate entitlement for the income-tested benefit during the option period. Estimated income can be entered retroactively when the applicable base year income has been received. The statement of estimated income, estimated income and estimated income data evidences exist in both Integrated Cases and Application Cases. If an income-tested benefit is not approved, the evidences are maintained in the Application Case. If the benefit is approved, the evidences are maintained in the Integrated Case. Application Case, Integrated Case and Product Delivery Case in Cúram (Knowledge) When the evidences are activated, even if they are not being used directly in the calculation (e.g. not to the client's advantage), the capture of this information allows the system to implement all downstream functions (e.g. creating tasks to trigger reconciliation and sending of options). Reconciliation In some cases, Cúram will perform the option reconciliation automatically. If you are processing an "Estimated Income Reconciliation" task or you are processing an option and the actual income is available, you must manually reconcile the estimated and actual incomes and record the result in Cúram. For more information on option reconciliation, refer to KA-01448 Reconcile Options (Scenario) (article not available). To reflect the results of the manual reconciliation, update the Reconciled field by selecting: Not Applicable if at the time of processing the option, the actual income is not available for the estimate year to perform the reconciliation and : it is before renewal following the year of the estimate. It is not expected that the actual income would be received yet; or it is after renewal following the year of the estimate, but before October. It is expected that the actual income would be received. You must wait until the actual income is received to process the option and perform the reconciliation. Yes if the actual income has been received for the estimate year and you have successfully reconciled the estimated and actual incomes. This includes situations where the reconciled income is no longer to the client`s advantage. No if: it is October or later and the actual income should have been received but is not available, and the client has not responded to requests sent to submit the income information; or the actual income has been received for the estimate year but you were unable to reconcile discrepancies (e.g. the client did not respond to requests for clarification).

OAS clients will not receive OAS pension or income-tested benefit payments during a period of incarceration: of 2 years or more to be served in a federal penitentiary; or exceeding 90 days to be served in a provincial correctional facility in a province or territory where an Information Sharing Agreement has been negotiated. Refer to: Incarceration—OAS Pension and Benefits (Policy) ; and Incarceration—OAS Pension and Benefits (Policy) Incarceration – Limiting OAS Pension and Benefits (Scenario) . Incarceration – Limiting OAS Pension and Benefits (Scenario) The Correctional Service of Canada started transferring information to the Department as of January 2011, identifying incarcerated individuals aged 60 and over. The Incarceration team, a specialized team in the Timmins processing office, is responsible for managing the exchange of information between the Department and the Correctional Service of Canada, and may request that an incomplete application is processed. The Incarceration team does not have the required access to the International Agreements systems to perform necessary system actions (e.g. suspensions, calculating advantage, releasing payments). Therefore, the Incarceration team will communicate with the IO processing office to advise of the system actions required. While the individual is incarcerated, the regional and IO processing offices are responsible for determining eligibility and entitlement to benefits. However, the Incarceration team in Timmins is responsible for: administering the benefits; managing the account; and communicating with the incarcerated individual and their spouse or common-law partner, if applicable.

topic_title: Determine the most advantageous entitlement rate
text: When a notification of incarceration is received for a client and they or their spouse or common-law partner is in pay for or has applied for the GIS or ALW benefit, you must determine whether it is more advantageous for the spouse or common-law partner’s entitlement to be calculated: at a couple’s rate using their combined income; or at a single rate using their own individual income. If it is more advantageous, the benefit can be calculated based on their individual income for the duration of the incarceration, excluding the month of incarceration and the month of release. For more information on marital status and rate tables, Marital Status and Rate Tables for Income-Tested Benefits For examples of determining the most advantageous rate, Examples—Incarceration—Limiting Payment of OAS Benefits GIS entitlement for the spouse or common-law partner of an incarcerated GIS client (MS2 (rate table 2)) When the couple is being paid for or has applied and been approved for the GIS at the MS2 (rate table 2) rate, you must review the entitlement for the spouse or common-law partner of the incarcerated client and determine which rate is to their advantage. Compare the GIS entitlement at the following rates to determine which is most advantageous: MS2 (rate table 2) using the couple’s combined income; or MS4 (rate table 1) using their own individual income. If it is not advantageous to calculate the GIS entitlement based on their individual income, the GIS will remain based on the couple’s combined income at the MS2 (rate table 2) rate as usual. GIS entitlement for the spouse or common-law partner of an incarcerated ALW client (MS5 (rate table 4)) When the couple is being paid for or has applied and been approved for the GIS and ALW benefit at the MS5 (rate table 4) rate, you must review the GIS entitlement for the spouse or common-law partner of the incarcerated ALW client and determine which rate is to their advantage. Compare the GIS entitlement at the following rates to determine which is most advantageous: MS5 (rate table 4) using the couple’s combined income; MS3 (rate table 3) using the couple’s combined income; or MS4 (rate table 1) using their own individual income. If it is not advantageous to calculate the GIS entitlement based on their individual income, the GIS will remain based on the couple’s combined income at the MS5 (rate table 4) rate as usual. ALW entitlement for the spouse or common-law partner of an incarcerated GIS client (MS5 (rate table 4)) When the couple is being paid for or has applied and been approved for the GIS and ALW benefit at the MS5 (rate table 4) rate, you must review the ALW entitlement for the spouse or common-law partner of the incarcerated GIS client and determine which rate is to their advantage. Compare the ALW entitlement at the following rates to determine which is most advantageous: MS5 (rate table 4) using the couple’s combined income; or MS5 (rate table 4) using their own individual income. If it is not advantageous to calculate the ALW entitlement based on their individual income, the ALW will remain based on the couple’s combined income at the MS5 (rate table 4) rate as usual. GIS entitlement for the spouse or common-law partner of an incarcerated non-pensioner spouse (MS3 (rate table 3)) Since the non-pensioner spouse or common-law partner is not in receipt of any benefits, no action is necessary as the couple is not disadvantaged by one member’s entitlement being limited. The GIS will continue to be calculated based on the couple’s combined income at the MS3 (rate table 3) rate. System limitations OAS Online cannot pay a benefit in the following situations and, therefore, a monthly manual priority payment is required: An ALW benefit cannot be issued by the system when the OAS pensioner’s account is suspended; and The GIS cannot by issued by the system at the MS5 rate when the ALW benefit is suspended. When a couple’s accounts are linked to each other in the International Agreements systems, the system is designed to determine entitlement and issue the appropriate benefits to a couple. When one account is suspended, the system cannot automatically pay a benefit for the other account in the following situations and, therefore, the monthly payment must be issued online manually: at rate table 3 using the couple’s combined income; at rate table 1 using their own individual income; or at rate table 4 using combined income or their own individual income.

topic_title: Notification of incarceration from the Correctional Service of Canada or the province or territory
text: On a monthly basis, the Correctional Service of Canada or the province or territory provides the Department with a report that lists newly incarcerated and released individuals over the age of 60. The report includes the following information: Offender identification number Individual’s first, middle and last name Aliases and nicknames Gender Date of birth Home address or any other known addresses Institution name and address Offender status: Incarcerated UAL (unlawfully at large) SENT. COMP/SATIS (Sentence completed / satisfied) Supervised On Bail Deported Deceased Date of death (if applicable) Admission date Release date Release type Release revocation date (the incarcerated person was released on parole but violated their parole and has been returned to the penitentiary) Using the information on the report, you must attempt to match the individual to a client SIN on a Departmental system. If a match is confirmed, take the necessary actions on the account and, if applicable, adjust the spouse or common-law partner’s account. If there is an incomplete application in a regional or International Operations (IO) processing office for an individual on the report or for their spouse or common-law partner, contact the regional or IO processing office to request that the application be reviewed to determine eligibility and entitlement and to notify the Incarceration team of the outcome. The actions required on each account will depend on the offender status according to the table below: Table 1. Offender Status and Action Offender Status Action Incarcerated or UAL The incarcerated client’s account must be suspended. If there is a spouse or common-law partner in pay for OAS benefits, their account remains in pay and must be reviewed to determine the most beneficial entitlement rate. Temporarily Detained This offender status is not specifically identified on the report. These individuals are included with the Incarcerated status. However, if you notice that the client is a repeat offender or if the client submits an enquiry or a reconsideration regarding their status and suspension, it may be possible that they are temporarily detained. Send a verification to the Correctional Service of Canada to confirm their current offender status. If the status is confirmed with the Correctional Service of Canada as Temporarily Detained , the client is still entitled to receive their benefits. If the client becomes incarcerated at a later date, the benefits must be suspended. SENT. COMP/SATIS The incarcerated client’s account must be released back into pay once written confirmation is received from the client that they have been released. If there is a spouse or common-law partner in pay for OAS benefits, their account must be reviewed immediately to ensure their entitlement is returned to the appropriate entitlement rate, if applicable, even if written confirmation has not been received from the client who was incarcerated. topic_title: Suspending the account of an incarcerated individual
text: There must be an exact match in the individual’s name and date of birth before you take any action to suspend an account. If there is any doubt or there are multiple potential matches, do not suspend the benefits until you have confirmed that the account belongs to the individual on the report. It is the sentence of imprisonment that makes the determination for the suspension of benefits, not where the individual is incarcerated. For example, an individual may be temporarily incarcerated in a provincial facility, but their sentence is for 2 years or more to be served in a federal penitentiary. Therefore, the individual is considered incarcerated under the Old Age Security Act . The suspension of benefits begins the month following the first month of incarceration. The last month of suspension is the month before the month the individual is released. Before you suspend the account, ensure the incarceration date and the system accounting month are not the same. You may need to bring forward (BF) the account to suspend it in the next accounting month. For examples of situations where benefit suspensions are required, Examples—Incarceration—Limiting Payment of OAS Benefits

OAS clients will not receive OAS pension or income-tested benefit payments during a period of incarceration: of 2 years or more to be served in a federal penitentiary; or exceeding 90 days to be served in a provincial correctional facility in a province or territory where an Information Sharing Agreement has been negotiated. Incarceration – Limiting OAS Pension and Benefits (Scenario) The Correctional Service of Canada started transferring information to the Department as of January 2011, identifying incarcerated individuals aged 60 and over. A specialized team in the Timmins processing office, the Incarceration team, is responsible for handling the exchange of information between the Department and the Correctional Service of Canada and may request that an incomplete application be processed as a priority. The Incarceration team does not have the required access to the International Agreements systems to perform necessary system actions (e.g. suspensions, calculating advantage, releasing payments). Therefore, the Incarceration team will communicate with the IO processing office to advise of the system actions required. While the individual is incarcerated, regional and International Operations (IO) processing offices are responsible for determining eligibility and entitlement to benefits. However, the Incarceration team in Timmins is responsible for: administering the benefits; managing the account; and communicating with the incarcerated individual and their spouse or common-law partner, if applicable.

Non-resident clients receiving OAS payments, who live in a country that the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) requires an OAS return of income form from must file the form each year. In June of every year, the CRA provides information to Cúram about clients who have not filed their OAS return of income for the preceding year (i.e. the current tax year).If Cúram is unable to create OAS return of income evidence, staff from the Department will manually create and modify the OAS return of income non-filer evidence. OAS return of income non-filer evidence is created when: a client has not filed their OAS return of income for the current tax year before the end of June. In this case, their benefit is suspended. Refer to Add OAS Return of Income non-filer evidence section in the What you need to do section of the Step by Step tab ; or a client has filed their OAS return of income for a previous tax year or has filed their OAS return of income after the deadline for the current tax year. In this case, the OAS return of income non-filer evidence must be updated. Once the client's filer status is updated, their benefit is reinstated and/or their payments are released for the tax year that they have filed for. Refer to Edit OAS Return of Income non-filer evidence section in the What you need to do section of the Step by Step tab . The evidence exists in both Application Cases and Integrated Cases. If the OAS benefit is not approved, the non-filer evidence is maintained in the Application Case. If the benefit is authorized, the non-filer evidence is maintained in the Integrated Case. The Application Details evidence in Cúram represents: a client's request for a specific benefit type; the dates that would affect that benefit's start date; and the ongoing status of the application for a benefit. This evidence can be found at the Application Case and Integrated Case level. Application Details is the header record for the application life cycle evidence. It is the evidence that governs the lifecycle of a client's application for an OAS pension or benefit in Cúram. This evidence is generated by Cúram when an application for any OAS benefit is submitted by a client through the Client Portal, or manually added in Cúram. It cannot be created or deleted by a user. The Application Details evidence is found on the Evidence tab, which is the primary workspace for managing all OAS pension or benefit associated evidence.

A client can request to stop receiving an OAS pension or benefit that is in pay by submitting a cessation request if it has been more than 6 months from the date the first payment was issued. If there are less than 6 months from the date the first payment was issued, a cancellation request is required. If a request is received late, you must still input the date received. The payments will only stop the next accounting month. The client can reinstate a ceased OAS pension via a written request. The receipt date of a written request is the effective date, and no retroactivity is paid. The GIS and the ALW and ALWS benefits cannot be reinstated without a new application. When an OAS pension application is added to Cúram, the system will populate the World Income Evidence of the Application Case based on the information entered from the paper or online application. However, if the over threshold information was not entered when the paper application was added to Cúram (i.e. the client did not answer the question or the question on the application is for an income year prior to 2020), the system will automatically populate the evidence based on other information provided on the application. This prevents an evidence issue and the Evidence Correction – OAS task from being generated, allowing Cúram to apply the automatic determination criteria. A benefit suspension evidence is used to temporarily pause payments of a benefit on the Integrated Case Evidence. The evidence allows the suspension of individual benefits or all benefits. A suspension may be completely lifted or partially lifted. You cannot initiate a retroactive suspension as it is simply stopping the entitlement from going out. Retroactively, it is already gone. To suspend moving forward - add suspension evidence with a Suspension Status of Suspended . To Unsuspend moving forward but leave the period (from the suspension start date) suspended - add an end date to the evidence. To unsuspend and release all entitlements previously blocked - change the Suspension status to Unsuspended . A benefit suspension evidence will cause the current determination to display entitlement amount to be $0.00, suspension reason being lack of entitlement. When unsuspending a benefit, you must determine if the client is underpaid or overpaid. This will be transmitted in the notification letter that is manually sent out. When unsuspending all benefits in the integrated case or suspending a specific benefit, you must apply changes to both benefits at the same time, regardless of which benefits are involved. This is necessary to stop a payment from accidentally being issued on the benefit you would want to remain suspended.

You can review a client's approved benefit eligibility and entitlement information to assist when you are making decisions about a client's benefits and when supporting client enquiries. You can determine eligibility by using the Check Eligibility or Check Potential Eligibility functionality, if required. Eligibility and entitlement information in Cúram is available in: the Person Record; the Integrated Case; and the Product Delivery Case. A summary of all benefits will display in the context panel of both the Person Record and the Integrated Case. The following information will be included: Benefit ALW ALWS OAS GIS All benefits will be displayed, regardless of what benefit(s) the client has applied for. If the client has an active benefit, the start date will be displayed in brackets beside the benefit name. The start date is determined by the earliest coverage period where the client was determined to be eligible, even if there is no entitlement. Details The details will include the benefit status and current monthly amount, if applicable. The benefit status will be displayed as: Blank, if no application has been received for the benefit, or the Application Case is closed and the benefit was not authorized. Pending , if the application is pending on the Application Case and no determination has been made. Suspended , if the benefit is currently suspended. The reason for suspension will be displayed in brackets. Future/Pending , if the benefit has been authorized and the benefit start date is in the future. The Graph View is accessed from the Eligibility tab of the Integrated Case (i.e., Old Age Security case). It is a high-level graphical view of a client's eligibility and entitlement for an OAS pension, GIS, an ALW benefit and an ALWS benefit for a single calendar year. The Graph View displays coloured timelines for each benefit the client has applied for and for which the client satisfies the age requirement. The timelines are labelled with the benefit name and the entitlement amount, or Not Eligible , Not Entitled or Suspended , if applicable. When you click a timeline interval, a pop-up window displays eligibility and entitlement information specific to the benefit. Key events that affect a client's eligibility and entitlement are indicated on the timeline by a black dot on a month. When you click the black dot, a pop-up window displays that month's events. Possible key events for OAS program benefits include: Application date Requested pension start date 65th birthday 70th birthday 75th birthday 20 years' totalized residence 7th month outside Canada Returned to Canada Incarceration admission date Incarceration release date Special Qualifying Factor anniversary date Living apart for reasons beyond control start date Living apart for reasons beyond control end date Marital status change date Sponsorship start date Sponsorship end date Sponsorship breakdown date Detailed information about determination is also available in the Product Delivery Case (i.e., Old Age Security Program Benefits case). Available information includes: eligibility and entitlement criteria results; client income information; and the calculations used to determine benefit amounts. These calculations also provide insight into information, such as Rate Table. You can also view the history of determinations about the client's benefits. Determination information is shown in 5 tabs: Table 1. Determinations tab descriptions Tab Description Summary The Summary tab shows high-level details about a client's: Entitlement Amount Eligibility Entitlement Eligibility Criteria The Eligibility Criteria tab shows the criteria used to determine the client's eligibility. This includes: Application Details Age OAS Historical / Initial Residency GIS Initial Residency Legal Status GIS Ongoing Residency OAS Pension Status for GIS Entitlement Criteria The Entitlement Criteria tab shows the criteria used to determine the client's entitlement. This includes: Deferral Sponsorship Status Incarceration Status Country of Residence and Portability Spouse/Partner GIS Entitlement Requirement Income The Income tab details information about the client's income and the client's spouse or common-law partner's income. Calculations The Calculations tab shows details about a client's entitlement amount calculation, including the Calculation Used , and any alternate calculations and entitlement overrides. If the client receives the OAS pension and GIS, the Calculations tab includes 2 sections in the group navigation bar on the left (OAS and GIS).

Marking a person record as duplicate You must mark a record as a duplicate before you can merge records. Before marking a record as a duplicate, you must decide which of the records is the master and which is the secondary. To determine which person record should be the master, consider the following: which account has the most amount of accurate information. if one record has a permanent SIN (100-899 series) and the other does not: Person merge is not allowed when the master record has a temporary SIN and duplicate person record has a non-SIN Identifier or no SIN. In this case, by making the non-SIN identifier or no SIN the master, you will be able to perform the merge using the Merge Person wizard. Person merge is not allowed when both the master and duplicate records have a temporary SIN. In this case, you will not be able to use the Merge Person wizard. However, you can still mark one of the records as a duplicate using the steps outlined in the What You Need to do section. You can then manually recreate the evidence on the master record. if either profile has any applications: If neither profile has any applications, the profile with the earliest record should be the master record. If one profile has applications and the other does not, the profile with applications should be the master record. if both profiles have applications, the profile with the earliest record should be the master record. if there are two records where one is a registered person and the other is a prospect person, the record where one is a registered person must always be the master record. Tasks assigned from the work queue will be directly reserved in your My Open Tasks . However, if a task has been forwarded to you by another staff member, it will be sent to your Available Tasks and must be reserved. You can reserve unassigned tasks (i.e. tasks that are not assigned to anyone) under the Tasks tab in the person's profile or in the case level to yourself by using the Add to My Tasks function. The reserved task will be displayed under My Open Tasks . This function provides a convenient way for you to quickly take on related tasks for a person or a case you are working on, without the requirement of having the tasks assigned to you beforehand. In addition to being able to reserve tasks to yourself, those with workload management access can reserve unassigned tasks to staff members directly from the person's profile or in the case level. You can reserve the tasks to others using the Reserve Tasks function. This function provides a fast way to reserve relevant tasks to a staff member who works on the same case.

First Entry Into Canada Details evidence is used to record an applicant's arrival details in Canada. A case will only have one First Entry Into Canada Details evidence. If the applicant does not provide their initial date of arrival into Canada, Cúram will review the applicant's Residence Period evidence and create the First Entry Into Canada Details evidence as follows: Table 1. This procedure provides you with the steps to self assign a next task from the Inbox or a work queue in Cúram when you no longer have tasks in your Open Tasks Folder.

After a task is created by Cúram, it is automatically allocated to a work queue where it can be reserved to a user if: the user has the required skills to complete the new task. OR the user has one or more reserved tasks for the same client; and the user has the required skills to complete the new task. You can use the Get Next Task... function to add tasks to your Open Tasks list from your Inbox or from a Manual Work Queue: From the Inbox If you are usually assigned work through automatic allocation and have no open tasks assigned, you can contact the team lead to assign more work or use the Get Next Task... function from your Inbox. Cúram will prioritize the tasks in the automatic work queue that correspond to your region and reserve the next priority task that matches your location, language, and skill type. Tasks are prioritized as High, Medium and Low and sorted within the priority group as follows: If more than one automated work queue is applicable, Cúram sorts across all applicable automated work queues as one. Receipt Date (oldest to newest) Creation Date (oldest to newest) Due Date (oldest to newest) From a Manual Work Queue If you are usually required to add tasks to your Open Tasks list from a manual work queue, you can use Get Next Task… from the selected manual work queue to prompt Cúram to allocate the next priority task. Cúram will prioritize the tasks in the manual work queue that match your language and reserve the most prioritized task. Tasks are grouped by High, Medium and Low priority and sorted within the priority group as follows: Receipt Date (oldest to newest) Creation Date (oldest to newest) Due Date (oldest to newest) When the automatic allocation batch has assigned a task to a user, it will scan the remaining unreserved tasks for the same client to see which can be bundled to the same user provided they have the skillset to complete the task. Bundling rules do not validate against the max task threshold (30 tasks), meaning that a user can still receive a task via bundling if they are at their max task limit (30 tasks).

A person's residential and/or mailing address needs to be captured upon registration. Once on file, the address can be viewed, edited, or removed. An address must always remain on a Person or Prospect Person's profile. Mailing and residential addresses can be adjusted separately. If a client wants to add a new mailing address only, the residential address can remain as is. Current mailing addresses are mandatory in Cúram. However, future dated addresses can be edited. When editing current addresses, Cúram will require activation to make the address effective, but activation is not required upon registration. Once you save a new address, Cúram automatically assigns an end date to the old address. The end date of an old address in Cúram cannot overlap with the start date of a new address. When receiving an address change request, use the current date as the start date, not the date of receipt (if earlier). Post Office box used as residential address When updating or capturing an address, start by searching with the postal code provided by the client. The system will display the results. If a client or applicant provides a PO Box address as their home address, you must request confirmation of their address their civic address or physical location. Refer to Post Office Boxes (Action) . Once the confirmation has been received, instead of selecting one of the search results after entering the postal code, click on Add New Address . This will display a second page where you can capture the address manually in the below format: Post Office Boxes (Action) Civic Number: LOT 40 Street Name: Concession 1 City, Town, or Village: Bight Province, Territory, State or Region: Newfoundland Postal Code: A0E1B0 For clients using a Postal Office box as their residential address in the United States, you may capture the Postal Office box as a residential address too. For clients living in countries outside of Canada and the United States, addresses will be captured as Address Line 1, Address Line 2, and Address Line 3, with PO box addresses being captured under Address Line 1. Address guidelines To reduce the cost and the volume of returned correspondence for CPP and OAS operations, it is important that you review and record and/or enter the person's address accurately. The most common error in address formatting is the apartment or suite number. The correct format for a Canadian address with an apartment or suite number requires it to appear before the civic address number, with a hyphen in between, without spaces and without the word "suite" or the "#" symbol. Non-resident tax is a deduction in Cúram and is applied to OAS benefits. The non-resident tax default varies between 10% and 25% of the OAS benefits, depending on whether there is a tax treaty with the applicable country in place or in cases where there is an approved request for a non-resident tax reduction. A non-resident tax withhold deduction is automatically created when an OAS benefits product delivery case is created for a client whose current and/or future residential address is not within Canada, United States or the United Kingdom. Cúram automatically creates or updates the deduction based on trigger events. The default non-resident tax withhold deduction will be configured as a third-party variable deduction on the OAS product delivery case. The residential address evidence or the non-residential tax correction evidence provides the start date, end date and percentage of the non-resident tax withhold deduction. The trigger events that update the non-resident tax withhold deduction are: Table 1—Trigger events that update the non-resident tax withhold deductions, event and description Trigger event Description Deemed non-resident Non-resident clients can request a reduction in the amount of non-resident tax required to be withheld from the CRA . On approval of the request, the CRA informs the Department of the non-resident tax rate reduction. Deemed resident A deemed resident is not subjected to the non-resident tax. The CRA identifies deemed residents each year and sends a list of these clients to the Department. Retroactive recovery of the non-resident tax (current year only) This is required in situations where: The client's foreign residential address is entered retroactively. Past payments are already processed. The agent determines that a higher non-resident tax deduction rate is required for this client to recover what was previously not deducted. The CRA requests an increase of the rate of the non-resident tax withhold of a specific client. Such an increase may occur because the CRA has received additional income information following an original decision to reduce the withhold rate. Tax treaty non-resident tax rate change In the event of the change in the non-resident tax rate, Cúram sets the end date for the current non-resident tax and creates new non-resident tax withhold deductions through a batch process. The batch is manually triggered to create or update deductions. Once the batch is run, Cúram updates the existing non-resident tax withhold deduction based on the values provided in the evidence.

The OAS recovery tax is a tax on higher-income OAS pensioners whose individual net income, for a given base taxation year, is above the threshold determined by the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). This procedure provides you with the steps to reallocate an overpayment due to misrepresentation or fraud and write it off from a client's account in Cúram when an investigation by the Integrity Services Branch (ISB) determined that it occurred due to misrepresentation or fraud by a third party.

Overpayments made to a client receiving an OAS pension or benefits are processed as liabilities against the client and are considered debts that must be repaid. An investigation by ISB may determine that an overpayment assigned to a client is a result of a misrepresentation or fraud by a third party. In this case the person who committed the fraud or misrepresentation is liable for the debt, not the client. When a notification of misrepresentation or fraud is received, you must reallocate the overpayment to the account of the person who committed the fraud or misrepresentation and write-off (i.e. reduce) the overpayment on the original client's account in Cúram.

The Pension Trusted Digital Repository (PTDR) is the document repository system where documents are saved. When the mailroom receives documents, the Mailroom clerk will upload the documents in the PTDR. Once the documents are saved in the PTDR, the repository will send the information to Cúram. Cúram will run batch process to retrieve the documents scanned to the PTDR and attempt to match the document to a person in Cúram and a Document Type . If Cúram is successful, it will upload the documents in the Attachments page under the Contacts tab in the Person Record. If Cúram is unsuccessful at identifying the person or the Document Type , a task will be created for the mailroom clerk to resolve the issue and update the type of the document appropriately. Subsequently, Cúram will generate a task for processing staff to review the attachments. For more information on the intake process, OAS and Foreign Benefits Initial Intake (Action) When reviewing an attachment, processing staff may have to move the attachment to the correct location (e.g. a specific case, verification and appeal). When a document is uploaded into Cúram, the document will be sent to PTDR for storage and an attachment is created to represent the document in Cúram. The attachment links to the document in PTDR so that it can be viewed if needed. However, attachments added to Cúram (without a document uploaded) will not be transmitted to the PTDR as records.

In January 2014, changes were made to the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations . This increased the length of the Parents and Grandparents (PGP) sponsorship agreement period from 10 years to 20 years, which affects all provinces and territories except Québec. To align the OAS program with these changes, the Old Age Security Act (OAS Act) was amended in 2014 to limit the payment of income-tested benefits (i.e. GIS, ALW benefit and ALWS benefit). This limited the payment to sponsored individuals for the entire period of their sponsorship agreement, regardless of the type of sponsorship agreement or their years of residence. Individuals began entering Canada (in all provinces and territories except for Québec) under a 20-year PGP sponsorship agreement around January 2016. This means that the OAS Act amendments will begin impacting these individuals in 2026 when they attain 10 years of residence in Canada. Effective October 1, 2025, these amendments came into force through an Order in Council. This will affect income-tested benefit applications with an effective date on or after October 1, 2025. Sponsored individuals who are eligible for income-tested benefits with an effective date prior to October 1, 2025, will be grandfathered using the old sponsorship agreement rules.
