Cúram creates an overpayment case when an individual has received more OAS benefits than they were entitled to. Staff members can also manually create overpayments. There are 2 types of overpayment cases in Cúram: Table 1—Types and Descriptions of Cúram overpayment cases Type Description Benefit Overpayment cases A Benefit Overpayment case is created automatically when a recalculation is completed on previously-paid benefits in Cúram. Manual overpayment Manual overpayment cases are created by staff members. Refer to Overpayment (Manual) Case—Add, View, Edit, Suspend and Delete in Cúram (Action) . Overpayment (Manual) Case—Add, View, Edit, Suspend and Delete in Cúram (Action) After each recalculation of a client's eligibility and entitlement, Cúram creates a Benefit Overpayment case if the benefits the client received at a given time were determined to be too high. If a client was receiving different benefit types during the period affected by that recalculation, a case will be created for each benefit type. For example, if the client has both the OAS pension and the GIS, and both are overpaid, then two Benefit Overpayment cases will be created: one for the OAS pension and another for the GIS. If the same client is determined to be overpaid for the same period after a future recalculation, then another Benefit Overpayment case will be created. Separate Benefit Overpayment cases will also be created if the client is overpaid for different periods. You can suspend and unsuspend Benefit Overpayment cases. When a case is suspended, any related deduction will be deactivated, and the maximum deduction amount will be recalculated. When a suspended Benefit Overpayment case is unsuspended, Cúram recalculates the maximum deduction amount and reactivates any applicable deduction. Overpayment cases migrated from the legacy systems will not be combined with Benefit Overpayment cases. You must continue to follow previous guidance for overpayment recovery, especially for cases involving deceased clients. For more information, Departmental Receivables (Overpayments) (Scenario) Benefit Overpayment cases contain the following tabs: Table 2—Tab Names and Details in a Benefit Overpayment Case Tab Name Detail Home The Home tab consists of 3 sections: Case Details Comments Recent Transactions The Case Details section provides a summary of the client, benefits, owner, certification frequency, status, overpayment reason, maximum deduction amount, fraud or misrepresentation, billing pattern and creation date. The Comments section displays any comments entered in this case. The Recent Transactions section documents all the actions that were taken on this case. Tasks The Tasks tab displays the tasks related to the Benefit Overpayment case. Contacts The Contacts tab consists of the following pages: Communications Attachments The Communications page contains recorded enquiries and letters sent to the clients related to the Benefit Overpayment case. The Attachments page contains all the links to the documentation stored in the Pension Trusted Digital Repository (e.g. application, supporting documents) associated with the Benefit Overpayment case. Financials The Financials tab consists of the following pages: Transactions Deductions The Transactions page lists the information of liabilities, cash receipts and benefit deduction made on the Benefit Overpayment case. The Deductions page lists deductions applied against the client's benefits to settle the overpayment. Participants The Participants tab displays the information of all parties to the Benefit Overpayment case. This includes their name, type, as well as the start date and end date for their involvement in the case. Administration The Administration tab consists of the following pages: Transaction History Status History Related Cases User Roles The Transaction History page documents all the detailed actions that were taken in the Benefit Overpayment case. The Status History page documents all updates to the status of the Benefit Overpayment case. The Related Cases page lists the product delivery case associated with the Benefit Overpayment case. The User Roles page lists the case owner and case supervisor assigned to the Benefit Overpayment case. Benefit Overpayment case created in error New System-generated overpayments should not be reversed if they were created in error. If a Benefit Overpayment case was created in error, you must: correct the evidence or overrides applied incorrectly; and use the Liability Offset function to void the system-generated overpayment. Refer to Liability Offset—Create, Complete and Delete in Cúram (Action) . Liability Offset—Create, Complete and Delete in Cúram (Action) If, after correcting the evidence and overrides, it appears the system-generated overpayment is still incorrect, submit a National Service Desk Internal link technical ticket to investigate the problem. You must suspend the Benefit Overpayment case to prevent recovery while waiting on the National Service Desk resolution. National Service Desk

Updates have been made to operational policies, procedures, work tools, letters, questionnaires and application forms to reflect the 2022-2024 CPP Triennial changes.

The Canada Pension Plan legislation requires a review every 3 years. The following 6 CPP Triennial changes are being implemented on January 1, 2025: Top-up to the CPP Death ( DTH ) benefit. This change adds a top-up to the CPP DTH benefit for eligible contributors who die on or after January 1, 2025, do not have an SVR pension payable and have never received a CPP or QPP disability or retirement pension. New child's benefit for part-time attendance at a school or university. Effective January 1, 2025, children of disabled or deceased contributors aged 18 to 25 who attend a recognized institution on a part-time basis will be eligible to receive 50% of the CPP benefit currently paid to full-time students. Extension of eligibility for the Disabled Contributor's Child's Benefit ( DCCB ) when the disabled contributor reaches the age of 65. This change extends the child's eligibility for the DCCB when their disabled parent reaches the age of 65 on or after January 1, 2025, provided all other eligibility criteria are met. Disentitlement to a CPP SVR pension following a CPP Credit Split. Contributors who are separated from their legal spouse with an approved credit split on or after January 1, 2025, are no longer eligible to receive a CPP SVR pension for that same separated spouse. Extension of the CPP incapacity provisions to DCCB applications. Effective June 20, 2024, if a disabled contributor is found to have been incapacitated and their CPPD benefits application is deemed to have been received at an earlier date, the same deemed date of application would also apply to any children listed on that application. Determination of the payee for CPP children's benefits (i.e. DCCB and Surviving Child's benefit). Effective June 20, 2024, the DCCB and Surviving Child's benefit is paid on behalf of a minor child to the disabled contributor or surviving spouse if they have decision-making responsibility for the child.

This procedure provides you with the steps to create, complete and delete a liability offset in Cúram.

A void offset is used to fix financial errors caused by mistakes when entering and applying evidence, or for internal balancing. Void offsets do not appear on client records or tax slips. Instead of deductions, they are reported to the Public Sector Collections and Disbursements (PSCD) system as debt adjustments and reduces the overpayment amount that was originally sent. They must match the benefit type and coverage period. The void offset is found in the Liability Offset wizard. You can also check the Void Offset box for Underpayment Liability Offset records. In cases where a Payment Correction-Overpaid case is created due to an error and an underpayment is generated after correcting the error, you can offset the underpayment using the Payment Correction-Overpaid liability and check the Void Offset box. This creates a liability offset item to void the mistakenly generated underpayment amount. If the Void Offset box is checked, you can only offset Payment Correction-Overpaid and Manual Overpayment liabilities for the Underpayment Liability Offset for the same coverage period.

When a client has an overpayment or liability related to OAS (e.g. an interest or penalty debt), it is important to prioritize reducing the outstanding balance for these debts using any underpayment or arrears owing to the client. Only after this reduction should the remaining underpayment or arrears funds be paid to the client. The following tasks are automatically generated to identify opportunities to reduce an overpayment by applying an underpayment or arrears: Table 1. Automatically generated tasks and description Task Description Underpayment activation This task is triggered when an underpayment is created and there is an existing overpayment. Overpayment activation This task is triggered when an overpayment is created and there is an existing underpayment. The Liability Offset section of the Financials tab of the Person's record displays records for liability offsets related to underpayment and arrears components of each benefit type in a product delivery case. Each record has 3 action items: Approve ; Complete ; and Delete . The Liability Offset wizard is the mechanism used to apply any underpayment or retroactive amounts to reduce the outstanding amount of departmental overpayments (e.g. penalty, interest, manual overpayment, payment correction-overpaid liabilities). It allows you to enter an offset amount that will be deducted from the liability. The first page of the Liability Offset wizard is used to input offset details. You must input the approved offset amount, which represents the maximum amount of the underpayment that can be applied to the overpayment. You can apply one underpayment or arrears owing to a client to multiple overpayments and they can be void and non-void, as required. The second page of the Liability Offset wizard is used to specify the offset amount to be applied to each departmental overpayment (e.g. penalty, interest, manual overpayment, payment correction-overpaid liabilities), as applicable. You cannot enter an offset amount that exceeds the outstanding amount of the liability. Additionally, you cannot enter a total offset amount that exceeds the outstanding amount of the offset entered on the first page of the Liability Offset wizard. Clicking Save on this page creates a Liability Offset Item. The available statuses of the liability offset records on the Liability Offset list screen are: Table 2–—Statuses of Liability Offset Records Status Details Pending Approval The Pending Approval status is displayed when the Delegation of Authority has completed a batch run for the liability offset record, which creates arrears and underpayment records on the Liability Offset List screen for the corresponding arrear coverage period. In this case, you may approve the liability offset record. Pending Offset The Pending Offset status is displayed: when there are liabilities to offset, and you click the Approved action in the liability record's menu. while awaiting the Offset Delegation of Authority process. during a Delegation of Authority and Offset batch, when Delegation of Authority approval is not needed and there are liabilities that must be offset, the pending Offset status will be displayed. Completed The Completed status is displayed: when the offset is approved. when you click Save on the Offset wizard and the offset amount available is 0. when you click the Complete action menu. Processed The Processed status is displayed when the offset has been processed. Cancelled The Cancelled status is displayed when a new entitlement has been determined for this arrears period. If there is an overpayment in both Cúram and CPMS and a cross program recovery is required, do not complete the liability offset until the cross program recovery is finalized. Cross Program Recovery (Scenario) Ensure to close the associated task once you have completed all the required actions.

text: Clients can apply for the following pension and benefits through the Client Portal: OAS pension; GIS; and ALW or ALWS benefit. A Person Record and an Application Case are created in Cúram when a client applies for any pension or benefit through the Client Portal. The pension or benefit application then triggers a task in Cúram for staff to review and process the Application Case. Depending on the information provided on the application, there may be evidence that requires verification and activation if automated processes fail or if information provided differs from the evidence in Cúram. Tasks may also be generated to identify evidence issues or additional actions that are required. For guidance on processing an online application, Online Applications—OAS Pension and Benefits (Scenario)

Effective April 29, 2026, OAS clients can make changes to their address and direct deposit information through the Client Portal. To access the Client Portal, OAS clients must first register and sign in to their My Service Canada Account (MSCA). After a client signs into MSCA, they must select Canada Pension Plan or Old Age Security to access the available services. Access to CPP services remains in MSCA, while access to OAS services is redirected to the Client Portal. For information about MSCA, My Service Canada Account (Knowledge) Clients can use the Client Portal to: apply for, update and track the status of their application for the OAS pension and benefits; access their correspondence sent from OAS and receive notifications; submit required information during the initial benefit application process; update life events information; submit requests for reconsideration; submit an appeal to the SST ; and upload and submit documents. Third parties cannot use online services to access or update client accounts, even if the client provides verbal consent.

Cash Receipts refer to money received in Employment and Social Development Canada to apply towards departmental debts that are managed in Public Sector Collections and Disbursements (PSCD). Normally this money is received either via online banking, cheques or through cross program deductions. Cash receipts are stored under the Financials tab under a person profile or overpayment case in Cúram. When PSCD receives payments to apply against a client's liability, the payment details are sent to Cúram to be stored as a cash receipt. This is the same process involved when PSCD receives cross program liability payments from CPP towards an OAS debt. Cash receipts are generated by the system, and Cúram will record the cash receipt under the user's profile while automatically reducing the outstanding balance of the liability. Additionally, PSCD can send a Cash Receipt Reversal to Cúram to reverse a previously sent cash receipt. Cúram will process this information and add the cash receipt amount back to the outstanding balance of the liability. The cash receipt table displays specific details about the payment. The Method column indicates the source from which the amount was received. The Amount column shows the total payment received. The PSCD Details and Allocations sections are located below the main table. These sections can be expanded by clicking the ( > ) toggle icon next to each section. The Allocations section displays the liability to which the payment was allocated towards, along with the respective dollar amount.

In Cúram, you can add third party contacts as either an Individual or an External Party organization. In either case, a profile is created to manage the third party contact information (e.g. direct deposit information, address, phone number). To add or modify a third party representative's financial information, Third Party Direct Deposit Information—Add, View and Edit in Cúram (Action) To modify a third party representative's contact information, Register a Third-Party Organization, Office and Office Member in Cúram (Action) All External Third Party organizations must be registered before they can be added as a third party contact. If they are not registered, refer to Register a Third-Party Organization, Office and Office Member in Cúram (Action) before proceeding. Register a Third-Party Organization, Office and Office Member in Cúram (Action) Table 1—Third party roles and their definitions Role Direction Trustee Non-Accounting Select this role when a trustee accounting report is not required (e.g. court appointed, committee or provincially appointed). Trustee Accounting Select this role when a trustee accounting report is required (i.e. Department appointed trustees). Bulk Payee/Public Trustee Select this role when an individual is acting for a client who has no family or other representative to act on their behalf. The public trustees work under legislation specific to the province or territory where the client resides. A trustee accounting report is not required. Trustee Supporting Select this role when there is a second trustee of a joint trustee agreement. This role is for information purposes only. Tutor Select this role when the third party is a court-appointed individual that has the authority and responsibility to make financial decisions on an individual's behalf when they no longer have the capability to manage their affairs. This role is used only in Quebec. Power of Attorney Select this role when the client authorizes another individual or agency to act on their behalf. The client must be mentally capable of making their own decisions at the time the Power of Attorney (POA) is executed. Power of Attorney Supporting Select this role when a client designates more than one primary POA. Representative Select this role when a client authorizes another person or organization to communicate with the Department. This role is used only as a consent to communicate information related to the client, and the representative can check the application status, the client’s information or their benefits or pensions. However, they cannot make any changes or updates to their information. Representative records are only created for unverified contacts for correspondence. Authorization to Deduct Social Services Select this role to allow for a one-time reimbursement of social assistance benefits to a provincial agency. Authorization to Disclose Information Do not select this role. If a client submits an authorization to disclose information request, select Representative . Barrister/Solicitor Select this role when the client authorizes a barrister or solicitor to receive specific information on their behalf. Social Worker Select this role when the client authorizes a social worker to receive specific information on their behalf. Accountant Select this role when the client authorizes an accountant to receive specific information on their behalf. Estate Representative Select this role when the client authorizes an estate representative. You must have received a legal will to use this role. Witness of Application Select this role when an application is signed by a witness on behalf of the client. Executor Select this role when a legal representative is: an executor for the estate named in the individual's will after their death; or an estate administrator appointed by a court when there is no will and no named executor. An executor or court-appointed administrator's role is to act and communicate on behalf of the estate. Legal Representative of the Estate Select this role when the third party is the legal representative of a deceased client's estate. Administrator Appointed by the Courts Select this role when an administrator is appointed by the courts and is responsible for submitting a trustee's accounting report. Personal Select this role when a client authorizes a friend to receive information on their behalf. International Select this role when a client, living in or outside of Canada, authorizes official individuals or agencies, located in or outside of Canada, to liaise with International Operations and foreign pension organizations. Individuals or agencies can only exchange the information allowed under each applicable International Social Security Agreement. Mandatary Select this role when an individual is legally designated for the client in the province of Québec. They are equivalent to power of attorneys. Post Mortem Business Select this role when the client is deceased and an individual or organization submits a post-mortem benefit application for the client, as well as when payments or correspondence needs to be sent on behalf of the deceased client and there is no estate representative. Person Confirming Canadian Residence Select this role when the client indicates a name and contact information for a person who can confirm their residence in Canada. Notified department of death Select this role for the name and contact information of the person who contacted the Department to advise of a client's death (it may be a next of kin or another person). Patronato Select this role to allow an authorized agency to communicate personal information concerning OAS or CPP benefits, payments, income, contributions and changes to address (excluding the address where the cheque is mailed or the bank account where the payment is deposited). For the Estate of Select this role when an individual, other than the estate representative, applies for the DTH benefit for the client. If they are eligible, these applicants cannot receive any post-mortem benefits and correspondence for the client, only that related to the DTH benefit. Mandatory supporting Select this role when a client designates more than one primary mandatary. Tutor supporting Select this role when a client designates more than one primary tutor. Assistant Select this role when someone living with a difficulty chooses someone to help with the administration of their property or the exercise of their rights. Although assistants are not court-appointed, they are recognized by the public curator and are publicly registered to act as an intermediary between the individual living with a difficulty and third parties, including government departments. Temporary Representative Select this role when a client is incapable and the court authorizes an individual as a temporary representative. Liquidator Do not select this role. Instead, refer to the Executor role above. Certain role types are eligible to be assigned as the case nominee. For more information, Manage Payment Destination for Nominees—Add, Edit and View in Cúram (Action) Once you add a verified third party contact, Cúram allows you to send correspondence to them directly. When you add verified third party contacts, you must always ensure that proper documentation is received. In rare cases, a client can have an unverified third party contact. For example, if a client dies or becomes incapable, insufficient documentation may be received by an unverified third party. In such cases where further documentation is required to verify the contact or additional communication is necessary, you must create an unverified contact to communicate with the unverified individual. An overpayment case is typically used to rectify a situation where a pension or benefit has been recalculated. In the case of penalties, they are monetary amounts imposed on an individual who has knowingly misrepresented information in relation to CPP or OAS benefits or pensions. The amount of the imposed penalty is determined by the Department, considering factors related to the individual case. Interest is continuously calculated on unpaid penalties and their related overpayments. The Department treats penalties and interest as liabilities that must be repaid by the client. In terms of collecting the money owed for penalties and interest, the Department follows the same procedures as they would for other departmental receivables (e.g. overpayments). There are certain transactions that will result in updates to any penalties and/or interest being made to the Public Sector Collections and Disbursements (PSCD) system. Penalties and Interest: All deductions applied to penalties and interest will be sent to PSCD. Liability deactivation will not transmit to PSCD and will require staff members to manually apply locks to the debt in PSCD to ensure that no further collections occur while it is deactivated. Penalties only Any delete transactions will send PSCD a debt adjustment transaction. Any changes made to the penalty amount not related to remissions, recissions, and write-offs under the Financial Administration Act , will be sent to PSCD as a debt adjustment. Edits related to remissions, recissions and write-offs under the Financial Administration Act will not be transmitted to PSCD as they are expected to originate in PSCD and be transmitted to Cúram. Interest only Any changes made to the interest will not be sent to PSCD and care must be given to ensure that PSCD and Cúram stay in balance. In addition, recovery rates for penalties and interest will be calculated using the maximum deduction amount functionality.

A manual payment is made outside of Cúram when the system cannot issue a payment for a client, and an immediate payment is required. If the Department issues a payment manually to the client outside of Cúram, the record of the manual payment must be recorded in Cúram through the Manual Payment wizard under the Financials tab at the person level. Once recorded, Cúram compares the gross amount of the manual payment with the system calculated entitlement amount for the coverage period. If a discrepancy exists, Cúram automatically generates an overpayment or underpayment. When deductions exist on the manual payment, Cúram will automatically update the applicable deduction record to reflect the amount withheld from the payment. Not all payments issued outside of Cúram need to be recorded. There will be some exceptions (e.g. refunding deductions to clients). When a client requests a retroactive payment be issued immediately, you can issue the priority payment through the Issue Retro Pending Payments function in the product delivery case.

topic_title: Manual reversals of write-offs or remissions
text: Manual reversals of remissions or write-offs under the Financial Administration Act are only done in Cúram in exceptional cases when the Public Sector Collections and Disbursements system interface is unable to transmit or receive data. When you reverse a write-off or remission, the initial liability amount or outstanding debt balance is increased by the amount of the reversal in the Person record. As a result, the debt becomes collectible again. The write-off may or may not be able to be reversed in the future depending on the write-off reason. For example, a compromise settlement or a discharged bankruptcy cannot be reversed. However, write-offs coded as Benefit Cancellation Deductions , Reconciliation – RD and Other can be reversed.

The following write-off reason codes are available in Cúram: Table 1. Write-off reason codes and description Write-off reason code Description Cancelled Legacy Payment This code is used in situations when updated evidence created an overpayment based on previously migrated data, and a cancelled legacy payment exists for the same period; the amount of the cancelled legacy payment can then be applied towards the client's debt. This will trigger a debt adjustment in the Public Sector Collections and Disbursements (PSCD) system making it possible to collect the actual recoverable amount. Benefit Cancellation Deductions This code is used to write-off a portion of the overpayment when there are deductions (e.g. voluntary tax, OAS recovery tax) associated with a benefit cancellation that have been systematically or manually reversed or requested from the CRA . This ensures that the overpayment balance in PSCD accurately reflects the client's actual liability. Reconciliation – RD This code is used when a client receives a payment that includes a reversible deduction (e.g. non-resident tax, federal voluntary tax, OAS recovery tax deducted in the current year), and a subsequent reassessment for that period results in an entitlement of $0. In these cases, you must manually reverse the deduction and use this write-off reason to reduce the total overpayment amount for the client. For more information, refer to Manual Reversal of Deductions in Cúram (Action) . This will ensure that PSCD will have the correct overpayment amount, if any, resulting from the reconciliation of reversible deductions and ensures corporate accounting will have the correct information to adjust their interdepartmental settlements for the month and year. This write-off reason is reversible in Cúram. If a debt adjustment is reversed, the trigger will automatically increase the liability in PSCD. Manual Reversal of Deductions in Cúram (Action) Reconciliation – NRD This code is used to write-off non-reversible deduction overpayments that were created as part of the payment cancellation process. This code is not tracked by PSCD, but it is tracked by corporate accounting for balancing departmental funds. Non-reversible deductions include: department of justice arrears and fees; provincial voluntary tax withholds; CRA set-off; and taxes deducted in the previous year (non-resident tax, federal voluntary tax and OAS recovery tax). Other This code is used to partially or fully write-off an overpayment amount when the other codes do not fit the situation or when directed to through enquiries or guidance. An event is triggered for the PSCD to reduce the liability amount. The write-off can be reversed, which will increase the liability amount in PSCD. UT-over 12 months Under the Financial Administration Act , the Department does not issue payments that are less than $1.00. Cúram will automatically write-off any unpaid under threshold amounts of $1.00 that remain in the system for more than 12 months using this write-off code. This will ensure these payments will not be included in any future entitlement calculations.

There are 2 different types of write-offs: write-offs under the Financial Administration Act ; and write-offs in Cúram. A write-off under the Financial Administration Act is the removal of an overpayment, in whole or in part, from the accounts receivable records. Depending on the write-off reason, it may be a permanent or temporary forgiveness of the debt. For more information, refer to Write-Off an Overpayment (Scenario) . You will not manually add this type of write-off to Cúram unless you are directed to do so by the Chief Financial Officer Branch (CFOB). Once the recommendation has been approved by the CFOB, it will be added to Cúram automatically. Write-Off an Overpayment (Scenario) A write-off in Cúram is an adjustment that reduces the initial liability amount of a debt. It is not an actual forgiveness of the debt, and it could be recovered at some point in the future.

The ISB is responsible for completing investigations where unexplained discrepancies have been identified or misrepresentation or fraud is suspected. If a third party debtor incurs an overpayment due to misrepresentation or is convicted of fraud in court, all the OAS-related overpayments of misused accounts will be merged under the third party debtor’s account as follows: Table 1. Situation and guidance on how OAS-related overpayments of misused accounts will be merged under the third party debtor’s account Situation Guidance The third party debtor receives an OAS pension or benefits in OAS Online. All OAS overpayments that the third party is responsible for on the misused account (s) will be merged under the third party debtor’s account in OAS Online. The third party debtor: is not in receipt of an OAS pension or benefits in OAS Online; and has an account in the International Agreements (IA) system. All OAS overpayments that the third party is responsible for on the misused account(s) will be merged under the third party debtor’s account in the IA system. A request will be sent to International Operations (IO) to have the overpayment(s) created on the third party debtors account. The third party debtor does not have an account in OAS Online or the IA system. A request will be sent to IO to have an account created for the third party debtor in the IA system. The account will be created under the third party debtor’s SIN, if one is available, or IO staff will assign an IA account number to the third party debtor and create the account if no SIN is available. All OAS overpayments incurred under the fraudulent account(s) will be merged under the third party debtor’s account in the IA system. Once the accounts have been identified or created and the overpayments have been merged, the Chief Financial Officers Branch will need to be informed of the following: modifications made on the misused accounts; modifications made on the third party debtor’s account; and the overpayment type and amount that is related to misrepresentation or fraud which have been added to the third party debtor’s account. You must determine if tax slips need to be amended and issued or cancelled for both the third party debtor and for the misused account(s). You must handle the tax slips based on a number of factors (e.g. the misused account belongs to the third party debtor or to another individual, the other individual is in pay, or the other individual is deceased).

topic_title: Timelines for any Business Expertise Request Tool response
text: For first level regional enquiries, the standard processing timeframe is 24 hours; For second level regional enquiries, the standard processing timeframe is 48 hours; For NHQ responses, the standard processing timeframe is 3 days for urgent enquiries and 10 days for non-urgent enquiries.

topic_title: Was National Headquarters guidance provided and there are unresolved questions or concerns?
text: If National Headquarters (NHQ) responds to a Business Expertise Request Tool response was provided by, and there are unresolved questions or concerns, Regional Business Expertise can contact the NHQ responder, before submitting a new enquiry.

BERT is a customized SharePoint tool for staff across Service Canada that facilitates access to Business Expertise support for advice and guidance for Citizen Services and Program Delivery Branch. BERT is the preferred method for submitting enquiries, and allows for tracking and escalation to National Headquarters (NHQ), if required. An enquiry can be submitted whether it is client-specific or general. OAS processing staff requiring additional guidance must use the National Business Expertise Tool (NEXO). For detailed instructions on submitting an enquiry, refer to NEXO End User Guide Share Point link . NEXO End User Guide When submitting an enquiry, pertinent information is summarized in concise sentences and includes: relevant sources and dates the main issue(s) approved acronyms One enquiry and one account number/SIN are used for any client-specific enquiry. Before submitting an enquiry, any conflicting medical or non-medical information must be addressed with a description on how it was considered. The enquiry must be free of spelling errors. General enquiries may require additional time and are not to be marked as urgent. Examples of urgent enquiries may be those with files identified as terminal illness, grave or for a client with a dire financial need. Once a BERT enquiry has been submitted, a regional Business Expertise Advisor or Consultant, or a Medical Adjudicator Consultant will review the enquiry and will determine if it requires escalation to NHQ. A regional review must be completed prior to escalation.

The automated process will review the beneficiary's account and confirm there is a DSB in pay and there is no: Open Reassessment; Active Vocational Rehabilitation, Vocational Rehabilitation - Correspondence, Enquiry – RTW, Enquiry – Voc. Rehab work items in PWS ; Active Reconsideration or Appeal under Program: Disability in PWS ; Active Integrity work item under Program: Disability in PWS ; Date of Death (DOD) in ITRDS ; Date of Birth (DOB) discrepancy in ITRDS ; and Account notifications in ITRDS ( PEP, Fraud Indicator ). If the above criteria are met, the automated process will review the Case Folder data in Rules Based Reassessment System ( RBRS ) to determine if there are past RA or Vocational Rehabilitation (VR) decisions. If the automated process does not find active cases, it will go to the ROE History screen in RBRS to determine if there are uninvestigated earnings. It will also determine if the total earnings are above the Substantially Gainful Occupation (SGO) amount for each year. The process will log a business exception if: the total earnings for each year present are below the SGO amount for that year; and the uninvestigated earnings are from the same year as the Date of Onset. The PWS work item will be moved to Unassigned and Active status for regional processing staff to review and determine if further action is required. The automated process will complete the Reassessment Trigger work item in PWS ( Reassessment Required: No ) and add notes in PWS and ITRDS indicating the reason it was closed if: there is an open Reassessment; there is a DOD on the file; or there are no uninvestigated earnings in ROE History screen of the RBRS . If there are no uninvestigated earnings in the ROE History screen of the RBRS , a request will also be submitted to the National Service Desk (NSD) for the Reassessment Trigger to be purged from RBRS . If there are uninvestigated earnings above the SGO amount, the automated process will process the following steps: Open a Reassessment in RBRS based on the ROE Trigger. Generate and send the ISP-2580 letter with an ISP-2502 form. Select Reassessment Required: Yes within the Reassessment Trigger work item in PWS , which will close the Reassessment Trigger work item and create a Reassessment work item. Put the new PWS Reassessment work item in Auto status. Calculate and add a BF date in the Reassessment work item based on the National Bring Forward Guidelines (Work Tool) . National Bring Forward Guidelines (Work Tool) Add a note in ITRDS indicating the actions that were taken. After the first BF period expires In PWS , the automated process will: retrieve the PWS Reassessment work item that is On Hold ; and look for new work items under Disability in the Program field that are one of the following work item types: Correspondence Enquiry Undeliverable Mail Death Notification Medical Report (2519) Medical Information If new correspondence has been received in PWS , the automated process will: log a business exception; and set the work item to Unassigned and Active status for review by a reassessment regional processing staff. If no new work item has been received in PWS , the automated process will review ITRDS notes to determine: if there are new notes since the ISP-2580 letter was sent, and if any contact has been made by the beneficiary by searching for key words: if the beneficiary has contacted the department by telephone or in-person; and the work item will be moved to Unassigned and Active status in PWS for review by a reassessment regional processing staff. If no correspondence has been received or no contact has been made by the beneficiary, the beneficiary's address will be verified in ITRDS to ensure if any address change occurred since the ISP-2580 letter was sent. If the address remains the same: a reminder letter ISP-2581 will be generated and mailed to the beneficiary along with the ISP-2502 form, advising them that their benefit will be suspended if no response is received by the date specified, based on the National Bring Forward Guidelines (Work Tool) . National Bring Forward Guidelines (Work Tool) If a new address is found in the Address block from any source: a business exception will be logged; and the work item will be moved to Unassigned and Active status for review by regional processing staff. After the second BF period expires If new correspondence has been received in PWS or if ITRDS notes indicate that the beneficiary made contact by telephone or in-person: A business exception will be logged; and The work item will be moved to Unassigned and Active status for review by reassessment regional processing staff. If no new work item has been received or no contact has been made by the beneficiary after both BF periods have expired, the automated process will then go to the client's Benefit screen in ITRDS and verify that the DSB is still In Pay . If there is no DSB with In Pay status, the automated process will: log a business exception ; and the work item will be moved to Unassigned and Active status for review by a reassessment regional processing staff. If there is a DSB with In Pay status, the automated process will: check for other CPP benefits in pay, including RTR and SVR pensions; and look for the ICD Codes between 290 and 336, 348 and 349 in the ITRDS Data Capture screen (Primary and Secondary). If any of the above criteria are met: the DSB will not be suspended; a business exception will be logged; and the work item will be moved to Unassigned and Active status for review by reassessment regional Medical Adjudicator. If there are no other CPP benefits in pay and the Primary and Secondary ICD Codes are not between 290 and 336 , 348 and 349 , the automated process will: go to the client's Benefits screen, expand the DSB with status In Pay, and suspend the DSB ; use the last day of the current accounting month as the end date and will select Pending Eligibility in the Reason of the drop-down menu; verify that the benefit status is Suspended after the benefit has been modified; and add an ITRDS note; change the PWS work item to Unassigned and Active status for review by reassessment regional processing staff. A Record of Earnings (ROE) Reassessment is conducted to determine a beneficiary's work capacity based on earnings information provided to Service Canada by the CRA during the time a beneficiary is receiving CPPD benefits. This earnings information is called a Reassessment Trigger. Reassessment Triggers are loaded to the PWS with the appropriate descriptor (i.e. Record of earnings ). Regional processing employees from the Reassessment Unit are required to contact the beneficiary or authorized third party to request an explanation of the nature of the income, along with supporting documentation. A beneficiary's benefit may be stopped or suspended based on the following: the information on their account; the explanation or documentation submitted by the beneficiary; or the beneficiary does not respond to requests for information.

The ROE Reassessment Trigger work item will be loaded to PWS in Auto status. The automated process will determine if the earnings were previously investigated. If not, the process will generate and send the ROE Triggers Earnings Verification (ISP-2580) letter to the beneficiary with the Consent for Service Canada to Collect Personal Information (ISP-2502) form, notifying the beneficiary that their benefit may be suspended if no response is received within the appropriate timeframe. The automated process will also send a ROE Triggers Earnings Verification Reminder (ISP-2581) letter with a suspension notice if required and suspend the DSB in ITRDS if no response is received from the beneficiary after the Bring Forward (BF) periods have expired.

An OAS / GIS Application Case is automatically created once an OAS and GIS application form is added in Cúram. Add an OAS and GIS Application Form in Cúram (Action) An OAS / GIS Application Case can be accessed from the person's profile. You can view the OAS / GIS application for more information associated with a client's Application before starting the authorizing process. If a client's OAS application was approved before the cutover (i.e. before March 1, 2025) but their GIS application was not, you must submit a standalone “Application for Guaranteed Income Supplement” to authorize the GIS . However, if you submit a new “Application for Old Age Security Pension and Guaranteed Income Supplement” instead, you must proceed with completing all necessary case work in the Application Case, including adding evidences, completing verifications, and resolving any outstanding tasks. The OAS benefit should then be authorized. Cúram will copy the relevant evidence to the migrated Integrated Case. You must then review the Integrated Case to ensure all evidence has been carried over to the Integrated Case and determine whether any overrides need to the updated or removed based on the information available. You can now authorize the GIS . After the OAS pension has been authorized, the Benefits page refreshes automatically and updates the status of the Benefit from Pending to Approved , and Completed On date is populated. The application case status is changed to Closed. Before authorizing your application case you can click Check Eligibility, Cúram runs eligibility checks and updates the eligibility decision on the eligibility check screen. You can view the details of the unmet criteria (e.g. residency, age) on the potential eligibility screen. If any evidence is missing or requires verification, you must manually send the correspondence associated with the tasks based on the information required to process the application. Once all the verifications and issues or flags have been resolved, an application can be authorized. When you select Authorize , a potential eligibility check record is created on the application case. Viewing details of decisions The following screens can be used to view details of decisions for each criterion: Approved: Approval tab on Benefit line item can be expanded to view the criteria assessed. Closure: Closure tab on Benefit line item can be expanded to view the criteria assessed. Evidence: If an evidence issue exists, you can navigate to the evidence issue screen and view all the evidence which have an issue. Each individual evidence can be accessed to learn more about the issues. All client registered: If this criterion is not met, the user can check all the applicants on the application case to confirm which user is not registered. Identity confirmed: If this criterion is not met, the user can validate if there is outstanding verification on Name and SIN evidence. If there is a duplicate application during the authorization, the user will have to close one of them before authorizing the other. If the client is already receiving benefits, you will need to manually close the duplicate application. After the benefit has been authorized, the Old Age Security Integrated Case and Product Delivery Case are created. The Integrated Case will also be used for the GIS . If the client already has an Integrated Case or a Product Delivery Case, the cases will be updated with any new evidence information. Clients can receive OAS and GIS benefits together. However, they cannot receive ALW / ALWS Benefits along with OAS/ GIS . In some cases, an application may be added in Cúram and later denied. You must deny these applications in Cúram and the associated task should be closed. You can manually reopen a closed or withdrawn OAS or GIS benefit on the OAS GIS combined application case. This is possible when an Administrative Error , Appeal Decision , Request for Reconsideration, and/or a Response Received from SSA Country reopening reasons are met. Spouse and Non-Pensioner Spouse Non-Pensioner spouses are required to be registered as a Person to authorize GIS Benefit. Relevant tasks must be resolved. If there is a non-pensioner spouse on the application case, the benefit still needs to be authorized to close the application case. However, since the spouse is a non-pensioner, they will not be eligible for GIS . When an application is submitted with a spouse, you will need to deny their GIS benefit. If a spouse’s address differs from the primary applicant’s address, the provided address must be reviewed to ensure it matches the one listed on the application. In cases where the system has not automatically updated the spouse’s address, a manual update must be performed to reflect the correct address. GIS When a client qualifies for GIS , a single Old Age Security Benefit case is created and maintained to handle renewals on an annual basis. If the income is missing, it can be manually added. Active Application Details evidence with GIS must exist for the client before performing an override. If there are two applicants on a GIS application, both applicants must have Application Details evidence recorded. Failure to capture Application Details for both applicants will prevent the system from proceeding with GIS authorization. Marital Relationship The full period of the marital relationship must be provided to determine entitlement for income tested benefits. When a spouse’s date of death is added, the application case is automatically updated with this information, along with the marital status. If there is period of entitlement when the spouse was alive then you will add the spouse and their income to the application case. It is still possible to confirm a client’s marital status without requiring a date of marriage. You can contact the client to obtain the start date of the marriage. Ideally, the start date of the marriage should align with the start date of the benefit. If the marriage start date is provided within the same month as the benefit effective date, the benefit calculation can include the marital status from the benefit start date. When a person’s marital status is not aligned with the system’s record, Cúram will prevent the application from being processed. Marital status at the Person level cannot be updated directly. Instead, users must navigate to the application case and update the marital relationship evidence. Once the marital relationship evidence is activated, the marital status at the Person level will automatically update. Eligibility and Future Effective Date An application may have a future effective date, which can be found on the Client’s Application Case or their Integrated Case. The future effective date is located within the Application Details evidence under the Evidence tab. If all required criteria are met, a benefit can be authorized with a future effective date. On the eligibility check records, the user can view a detailed summary of all the criteria assessed to determine eligibility. Ensure correct application date is entered to ensure eligibility is properly calculated. The initial period of eligibility is determined based on the date of application, not the processing date. Eligibility for benefits is assessed from when the application was submitted. For Clients where earliest date of eligibility is more than 11 months after the application receipt date (For example, a 63-year-old Client submitting an OAS application), a user may add the "Initial Eligibility Period" Override to the case prior to authorization. This will not result in the Client meeting the Eligibility & Entitlement criteria earlier than under normal circumstances, but will allow for the application to be approved even if the calculated earliest date of eligibility is beyond the 11 months following the receipt date of the application. The initial eligibility period override does not extend the retroactive period for applications submitted after the earliest date of eligibility. The system will calculate retroactive benefits, including underpayments, automatically. When a client requests a retroactive payment or underpayment be issued immediately, you can issue the priority payment through the Issue Retro Pending Payments function in the product delivery case. Manual Payment and Priority Payment—Record and Issue in Cúram (Action) Documents During a triage task, the processor may be unsure about where to move the document. A document should be reviewed to determine where it should be moved to by the processing agent. If the document is related to or in support of an application, then it should be moved to the Application Case. If the document is about the individual and not specific to a benefit, then it can reside at the person level. The user needs to determine why the document was provided and then move it to the appropriate location to action. There will be cases that a document has to go to the Person (e.g. paper application received and there is no Application Case) and then the document can be moved afterwards if required. A document received for a verification cannot be moved from a Task directly to the verification. Documents for verifications must be moved to the location where the verification exists (e.g. Person) and then can be moved to the verification. This process applies to all document types, as there are no rules that prevent a user from moving a document type to a Case or a Person.

Voluntary Tax Withhold (VTW) evidence captures the details of the monthly federal and/or provincial tax amount a client requested to have withheld from their OAS benefits. A client can request VTW using the Request for Voluntary Federal Income Tax Deductions CPP and OAS (ISP-3520) or section D3 Taxes of the Old Age Security and Guaranteed Income Supplement (ISP-3550) forms, or through their My Service Canada account. The evidence exists in both Integrated Cases and Application Cases. If the benefit is not authorized, the VTW evidence is maintained in the Application Case. If the benefit is authorized, the VTW evidence is maintained in the Integrated Case. VTW evidence can be added for a client at the Application Case level or Integrated Case level when their application is processed and after their case is active. If VTW evidence needs to be updated (i.e. if the VTW evidence was 10% and is increased to 15%), the End Date should be entered for the existing VTW evidence and a new VTW evidence should be created with the new deduction value. This allows for traceability of evidence that were used in gross to net calculations. There are several cases in which a user would edit an existing voluntary tax withhold evidence: To correct incorrectly added information To update a client’s percentage or dollar amount based on a client’s request To stop the voluntary tax withhold based on a client’s request The cover period on a payment (i.e, transaction) provides the date range in which the voluntary tax withhold evidence was used. The earliest End Date that can be entered is the day after the cover period.

OAS and CPP payments issued by cheque were delivered by Canada Post on December 18, 2024. The production schedule and delivery dates remain unchanged for the month of January 2025. For more information, Benefits Toolbox Applications for benefits Applications for benefits were delayed in the mail and were not received by the Department until after the postal disruption ended. Applicants may also have delayed applying for benefits until the postal disruption ended. Applications and all forms of documentation received within 21 days (January 9, 2025) of the end postal disruption period will be deemed to have been received by the Department on the day the postal disruption began (November 15, 2024). The date indicated on these letters will be the date the letter was generated. Letters created during the postal strike and held in the regions will carry the date that the letter was originally generated. Regions have been advised to prepare the mail to facilitate pick-up by Canada Post. Resumption strategies for mail received in processing centres Resumption strategies on incoming mail and work prioritization was provided to the regional workload teams and will continue to be provided until volumes are stable. An ALW / ALWS application case is created when a new application for ALW and/or ALWS benefits is submitted in Cúram. An ALW / ALWS Application Case can be accessed from the person's profile. If a prospect person record exists due to the client information being received from a restricted country, you must register the Prospect Person as a Person before you proceed to authorize the ALW / ALWS benefit. Refer to Register a Prospect Person as a Person in Cúram (Action) . Cúram will determine the earliest eligibility date based on the eligibility criteria according to the information entered. Register a Prospect Person as a Person in Cúram (Action) All evidence must be active before authorizing an Application Case. This is to ensure the current eligibility determination is made regardless of the actual outcome. If there is a duplicate application with Open status, you must close one before you authorize the benefit. If an application is closed by mistake, you can also reopen the application manually. You will manually send the correspondence associated with the tasks based on the information required to process the application. When you select Authorize , a potential eligibility check record is created on the application case. On the eligibility check records, the user can view a detailed summary of all the criteria assessed to determine eligibility. The following screens can be used to view details of decisions for each criterion: Table 1—Decision and Detail for Each Criterion Decision Detail Approved The Approval tab on the Benefit line item can be expanded to view the criteria assessed. Closure The Closure tab on the Benefit line item can be expanded to view the criteria assessed. Evidence If an evidence issue exists, you can navigate to the evidence issue screen and view all the evidence which have an issue. Each individual evidence can be accessed to learn more about the issues. The details of the unmet criteria can be viewed by the client on the potential eligibility screen. This will confirm if there is any outstanding verification on the evidence. You can manually reopen a closed or withdrawn ALW / ALWS benefit on the Application Case. This is possible when an Administrative Error , Appeal Decision , Request for Reconsideration, and/or a Response Received from SSA Country reopening reasons are met. Consent required from spouse on ALW / ALWS cases Applications for OAS program benefits cannot be approved without a valid consent to the terms of the application and declaration of the truth of the information provided by all parties to the application. The Consent and Declaration evidence type captures this data for each participant on an Application Case. If the Application submitted for a client does not include the Consent for a participant, Cùram will generate a task stating that the Consent is required. This can be viewed from the Tasks tab on the application case. You must add the Consent and Declaration evidence and close this task prior to Authorization. If the task is not Closed, system will prevent the Authorization of the Application Case. Steps to follow when the ALW / ALWS is not showing up for a retroactive period The retroactive information is automatically calculated by Cùram. If an ALWS client was ineligible for the retroactive period, a separate application for ALW is not required. You can review the display rules for the retroactive period, to determine why the client is not eligible or not entitled. Guidance for processing ALW / ALWS applications if received simultaneously When processing ALW and ALWS applications received simultaneously, the following conditions should be verified: Was the client married on the Application Date ? If yes, an application for ALW must be added. Was the client a Surviving Spouse on the Application Date ? If yes, an application for ALWS must be added. If the conditions above are not met, there is no further processing required. topic_title: Residence period start and end dates New
text: The start and end date of the residence periods within the Residence Period evidence cannot overlap. When a client provides residence periods that overlap on their application, Cúram will update the Residence Period evidence as follows: If the periods overlap by one day between Canada and another country, Cúram will create the residence periods without the overlap by reducing the start date or end date of the residence period in the other country by one day. If the periods overlap by one day between countries other than Canada, Cúram will create the residence periods without the overlap by reducing the end date of the earliest residence period by one day. If the periods overlap by more than one day, Cúram will create the residence periods as provided by the client. An Issue displays on the Application Case and an Evidence Issue(s) task is created to indicate that the overlapping residence periods require review. If a client's Residence Period evidence is added manually, the start and end date of each validated residence period are determined as follows: Table 2. Start and End Dates of the Residence Period Evidence Situation Start date End date The client currently resides in Canada. The residence period in Canada begins the latest of: the applicant's 18th birthday; or the date the applicant meets the definition of resident in Canada (e.g. the date the applicant made Canada their home). Leave the End Date field of the residence period blank to indicate the Canadian residence is ongoing. The client is currently not a resident of Canada. The residence period in Canada begins the latest of: the applicant's 18th birthday; or the date the applicant meets the definition of resident in Canada (e.g. the date the applicant made Canada their home). The residence period in Canada ends on the latest of: the day the applicant left Canada; or the day before the date when the applicant no longer met the definition of resident. There are absences that interrupt Canadian residence. The absence period begins the day after the departure from Canada. The absence period ends the day before the date of return to Canada. There are periods of residence in another country before the client initially entered Canada. The foreign period begins on the client's 18th birthday. The foreign period ends the day before the client meets the definition of resident in Canada (e.g. the date the applicant made Canada their home).

The Residence Period evidence registered in Cúram captures a client's periods of residence in and outside of Canada since the age of 18. If any residence period is missing, a task will be generated that will prevent the authorization of the Application Case, and you will then need to add the missing periods to continue processing the application. The Residence Period evidence exists in both integrated cases and application cases. If the benefit is not approved, the Residence Period evidence is maintained in the Application Case. If the benefit is approved, the Residence Period evidence is maintained in the Integrated Case. Application Case, Integrated Case and Product Delivery Case in Cúram (Knowledge) In an Application Case, the evidence is considered during the eligibility check and/or authorization process. Once the evidence is activated in the Integrated Case, it triggers the Eligibility and Entitlement rules and a recalculation occurs.

An Application Case is created when the client applies for an OAS pension and/or income-tested benefits (i.e. GIS, ALW and ALWS benefits) by submitting the application form either via paper or the client portal in Cúram. You can find an Application Case by clicking Applications on the page group navigation bar under the Cases and Applications tab of the Person Record. There are 2 types of Application Cases: OAS/GIS Application Case ALW / ALWS Application Case It is important to accurately record all details provided by the client as appropriate evidences, prior to authorizing an Application Case. You can verify the client's potential eligibility using the Check Eligibility function prior to authorization. When you initiate the authorization process, Cúram conducts an eligibility check as the first step. An Application Case can be authorized once all information is gathered. If the authorization is approved and successful, the client is eligible for a benefit and will have their entitlement determined. A correspondence letter will be sent out automatically through Cúram to inform the client. If the required information is not received, the application case must be closed and could result in the client not being eligible for or entitled to benefits. A correspondence letter will be sent out automatically through Cúram to inform the client of the decision as well. You can manually reopen a closed or withdrawn Application Case when the situation allows. For example, if the client requests reconsideration of a decision, and the Department changes the decision after processing the reconsideration or if the Department receives the agreement information from another country. Both the OAS pension and GIS applications can exist in one Application Case. If that is the case, Cúram requires separate authorization for each benefit. After the benefit authorization results in Approval, Cúram automatically creates the Integrated Case and Product Delivery Case to manage and deliver the benefit. If the Application Case has 2 benefits, Cúram still creates one Integrated Case and one Product Delivery Case after the first benefit is authorized and approved. The Previous Participants page lists all the participants that are removed from the Current Participants page before the Application Case is authorized and the benefit was approved. A Product Delivery Case stores the financial information required to pay benefit to a client. It contains the decision(s), including eligibility, entitlement, financial information and payment amounts. If there is a reassessment that spans across multiple benefit types, benefits can be managed with a single Product Delivery Case. You can find a Product Delivery Case by clicking Cases on the page group navigation bar under the Cases and Applications tab of the Person Record. The Product Delivery Case is referred as Old Age Security Program Benefits case in the Name column. Once a Product Delivery Case is created, benefits are paid until one of the following situations occur: the client is deceased; or the benefit is ceased or cancelled. An overpayment case is used to make a correction to a benefit when it has been recalculated. When an overpayment deduction is added, the client is given a 60-day notice period to respond. There are 2 types of overpayment cases: a Department employee manually creates an overpayment case; and payment correction cases created by Cúram when a recalculation is completed on previously paid benefits. You can view manual overpayment information by navigating to the Transactions tab under the Financials tab on the Person level or the Transactions tab under the Financial tab on the Benefit Overpayment case. Liability reversals Manual overpayments should only be reversed if they were created in error. Before reversing a manual overpayment transaction, investigate the source and always verify if the overpayment should remain on the account. Third party debtors New When the Integrity Services Branch determines that a third party is responsible for an overpayment, a manual overpayment case is used to create the overpayment on their account. If a third party debtor was not receiving benefits at the time a manual overpayment was originally created on their account but later begins to receive benefits while an overpayment balance remains, proceed as follows: Write off the Overpayment – OAS Non-Beneficiary ; and Create a new Reallocation overpayment for the remaining balance.

Recipients of an OAS pension or the GIS can request the cancellation of these benefits within the first 6 months of payment. When a request for cancellation is granted, all issued payments must be recovered. The pension or benefit may be cancelled provided the client repays the repayment amount no later than 6 months after the day on which their request for a cancellation is granted. For more information on the cancellation of OAS benefits, Cancellation—OAS Pension and Benefits (Scenario) Once you have reviewed and validated the client’s request and it is confirmed that they are requesting a cancellation of the OAS pension and/or the GIS, you must create the Benefit Cancellation Request evidence. After the evidence is added and activated, Cúram will create a Cancel Benefits task. Once this task is created, close the original task that was created when the client’s request was received. This new task will be used to track the progress of the request in Cúram. The following table describes the different statuses of the Benefit Cancellation Request evidence and when to use them. For more information on other actions that must be performed before and after editing the Cancellation Status of the evidence, Cancellation—OAS Pension and Benefits (Scenario) Table 1. Different statuses of the Benefit Cancellation Request evidence Cancellation status Description Requested This is the initial status of the request once the evidence is created. The evidence will remain in Requested status until it is confirmed whether the request is granted or not. If, at the time this evidence is created, it has been confirmed that the request is either granted or denied, the Cancellation Status can be set accordingly. Granted When the request for cancellation is granted, edit the Cancellation Status to Granted . Once the evidence is activated, Cúram will: reassess entitlement to income-tested benefits for the client and their spouse or common-law partner, if applicable; create a liability for the gross benefit entitlement of the affected benefits from the effective date to present. This includes the ALW benefit of the spouse or common-law partner, if applicable; and stop the payment of the affected benefits as there is no entitlement. Denied If the request for cancellation is denied (e.g. the request was received after the first 6 months of payment), edit the Cancellation Status to Denied . Rescinded If at any time during the cancellation process, and before a final decision of Repaid or Delinquent is made, the client no longer wishes to cancel their benefits, edit the Cancellation Status to Rescinded . If the previous status was Requested , there will be no changes to the client's entitlement as benefits are still in pay and will resume. If the previous status was Granted , once the evidence is activated, Cúram will: reinstate the benefits back to the original effective date; create an underpayment for the period that the client was originally paid for when the request was granted; and create an arrears for the period after the benefits were stopped. Repaid Once it is confirmed that all affected benefits have been repaid within the 6-month timeframe, and all other required actions have been performed, edit the Cancellation Status to Repaid . Once the evidence is activated, Cúram will: edit the application status of the OAS pension and/or the GIS to Cancelled ; edit the application status of the ALW benefit to Not Eligible , if applicable; and reassess the spouse or common-law partner’s GIS entitlement using rate table 3 (rather than rate table 2), from the effective date of the client’s cancelled OAS pension to present. Delinquent If the client does not repay the repayment amount within the 6-month timeframe, edit the Cancellation Status to Delinquent after all other required actions are performed. Once the evidence is activated, Cúram will: reinstate the benefits back to the original effective date; create an underpayment for the period that the client was originally paid for when the request was granted; and create an arrears for the period after the benefits were stopped. The corresponding overpayment that is created when the Cancellation Status is updated to Granted will be sent to PSCD once activated but will have a 10-month collection deferral date so the debt will not be sent to the CRA for collection. The cancellation process must be finalized within this timeframe as the overpayment created for the purpose of cancelling a pension or benefit must not be sent to the CRA for collection.

A Person Record in Cúram contains all the client's information that will not change from program to program. If a client has a Product Delivery Case with a current determination, Cúram will display their total Canadian residence years, marital status or current rate table on the context panel of the Person Record, below the client's date of birth and age. If a 40ths override exists, Cúram will use that information to populate the residence years. If the client's current determination includes: An OAS pension and the GIS: Cúram will display the rate table on the context panel but it will not display the Marital Status (e.g. Currently Married PS). For more information on rate tables in Cúram, refer to Marital Status and Rate Tables for Income-Tested Benefits . Marital Status and Rate Tables for Income-Tested Benefits An OAS pension only: Cúram will only display the marital status if there is active Marital Status evidence on the Person Record. The ALW benefit: Cúram will display the marital status. In cases where an ALW recipient is living apart for reasons beyond their control (including if their spouse or common-law partner is incarcerated), the Marital Status will be followed by LA (e.g. Currently Married – LA). The ALWS benefit: Cúram will display the marital status as Widowed. If the information is not available in the current determination or there is no current determination, nothing will be displayed. The context panel on the Person Record also displays a summary of all benefits in the upper right corner. For more information, View Eligibility and Entitlement Results in Cúram (Action) You can add evidence, correct errors and update information on a Person Record, as necessary. This procedure provides you with the steps to view a client's tax slips in Cúram.

View tax slip information In Cúram, go to the client's profile. Refer to Search for a Person in Cúram (Action) . Search for a Person in Cúram (Action) Click the Financials tab. Click Tax Slips in the page group navigation bar on the left. The Tax Slips page opens and displays rows of tax slips that have been generated for the client, regardless of the status. Navigate to the tax slip you want to view. Click the ( > ) toggle icon to expand the row and view the tax slip information.

There are 2 types of tax slips that can be viewed in Cúram: The T4A (OAS) is generated for clients who received any payment in Canada or deemed residents. It is used for reporting OAS pension income. It shows the amount of OAS pension received during the year. The NR4 (OAS) is generated for clients who received any OAS pension payment outside of Canada. It reports amounts paid or credited to non-residents of Canada, including pensions, annuities and other income. It indicates the type of income paid, the total amount, and the amount of Canadian tax withheld. It is used to assist in claiming a refund for overpaid taxes or in paying additional taxes owed. There are 3 categories of tax slips within each type: Original Amended Cancelled Tax slips have one of the following Issuance Status : Submitted – the tax slip has been generated but not yet processed or released Issued – the tax slip has been already processed or released to CRA and/or Revenu Québec Draft – the tax slip data has been generated but not yet ready to be processed or released Deleted – the tax slip version has been deleted Tax slips have one of the following Printing Status : Submitted – the tax slip is ready to be printed but has not yet been sent to the print provider Sent – the tax slip has been sent to the print provider Intercepted – the tax slip with Submitted or Sent status is intercepted by an agent from the Correspondence tab Draft – the tax slip is saved but not issued Deleted – the tax slip is deleted and should not be picked by the printing batch to be processed Error – an error occurred while processing the tax slip The Tax Slips list shows the latest version of each tax slip for a given client, tax year and tax slip form type, regardless of whether the status is Submitted, Issued, Draft or Deleted . The following table provides descriptions of the information shown on a tax slip: Table 1—Information shown on the Tax Slip window Field Description Taxation Year The Taxation Year field shows the year in which the tax slip was issued. Type of Slip The Type of Slip field shows the type of tax slip for beneficiaries of the OAS pension program. Types of slips include: T4A (OAS) NR4 (OAS) Category The Category field shows the status of this tax slip version from the perspective of CRA and Revenu Québec . Category types include: Original Amended Cancelled Issuance Status The Issuance Status field shows whether this tax slip version has been issued or not. The issuance status types include: Submitted Draft Issued Deleted Printing Status The Printing Status field shows whether this tax slip version has been released or processed. The tax slip printing status types include: Submitted Sent Intercepted Draft Deleted Error Creation Method The Creation Method field shows whether the tax slip data was entirely system-generated or was modified by a user. The creation method types include: System Manual Status Date The Status Date field shows the date the status was set. The default sort order is descending, by date. You can view and sort the tax slips using the following columns: Taxation Year Type of slip Category Issuance Status Processing Status Creation Method Status Date You can expand a tax slip in the main list to see the tax slip details: If you expand the latest version of a tax slip, Cúram displays the following information: recipient details for the selected tax slip (e.g. name, SIN and mailing address) the Box Name and Box Value details for each Box Number listed for the selected tax slip a list of prior versions of the tax slip If you expand the prior version of a tax slip, Cúram displays the following information: recipient details for the selected tax slip the Box Name and Box Value details for each Box Number listed for the selected tax slip If you expand a NR4 (OAS) tax slip, Cúram displays the following information: Table 2—Fields and Description for NR4 (OAS) Tax Slips Field Description Last Name The Last Name field shows the client's last name. First Name The First Name field shows the client's first name. Initials The Initials field shows the client's initials. Social Insurance Number The Social Insurance Number field shows the client's SIN. Mailing Address The Mailing Address field shows the client's mailing address. Box Number The Box Number field shows the number included in a particular box on the client's tax slip (e.g. 018). Box Name The Box Name field shows the name included in a particular box on the client's tax slip (e.g. SIN or OAS number). Box Value The Box Value field shows the amount being paid or deducted (e.g. 2,110.20).
