topic_title: Living Apart for Reasons Beyond Control and Consent to be Disadvantaged evidence
text: The Living Apart for Reasons Beyond Control evidence exists on the Application Case and Integrated Case and impacts entitlement for income-tested benefits. It captures the reason why a client and their spouse or common-law partner are living apart when this living arrangement is beyond their control. A client can have multiple periods of living apart for reasons beyond their control resulting in multiple evidence records. If the client indicates on their paper application that they are living apart for reasons beyond their control, the Living Apart for Reasons Beyond Control evidence is automatically created when the application is captured in Cúram. The Reason for Living Apart field will indicate Unknown since this question is not included on paper benefit applications. However, as the Reason for Living Apart field is mandatory, Cúram will automatically generate an Evidence Issue(s) task which must be manually resolved before authorizing the application. Further documentation may be required. When a couple is living apart for reasons beyond their control, if it is to the overall advantage of the couple but to the disadvantage of one member to be paid on individual income, the client who is disadvantaged must give consent to receive a lower entitlement amount. Cúram will generate an Evidence Verification Request task and a request for consent to be disadvantaged must be manually sent to the client. Cúram will continue to pay the couple on combined income until consent is received. If it is received, the consent is manually captured in the Consent to be Disadvantaged evidence and Cúram will then apply the provision. If a client has multiple separate time periods of living apart for reasons beyond their control in the same marital relationship, they must give consent for each period. Each Living Apart for Reasons Beyond Control evidence can only have a single related Consent to be Disadvantaged evidence. A client can change their consent at any point during a period when they are living apart for a reason beyond their control. Consent for each new payment period is not required if the time period that the couple lives apart for reasons beyond their control is uninterrupted. As long as the period of living apart for reasons beyond their control is ongoing, the consent remains valid unless revoked by the disadvantaged client. For more information, Couples Living Apart for Reasons Beyond Their Control (Scenario)

The Marital Relationship evidence is captured on the Application Case and the Integrated Case. It links a couple's accounts and records the relationship details for the client, including the relationship status, duration, and the name of the spouse or common-law partner. When an application is captured in Cúram for a client who is married or in a common-law relationship and all the required spouse or common-law partner's details are provided, the Marital Relationship evidence is automatically created on the Application Case. An Evidence Issue(s) task is automatically created in the following scenarios: The Marital Status evidence on the Application Case is Married or Common-Law , and the Marital Relationship evidence was not created automatically as the required information about the spouse or common-law partner is missing. The Marital Relationship evidence was automatically created but is incomplete and requires review. When an Evidence Issue(s) task related to the Marital Relationship evidence is present, the Application Case cannot be authorized and approved until the evidence is manually added or edited, as applicable. If there is a change in marital status to Married or Common-Law after the client is in pay, a Marital Relationship evidence must be created on the Integrated Case. Do not manually update the Marital Status evidence on the Person Record. Adding or editing the Marital Relationship evidence details on the Application Case will automatically update the Marital Status evidence on the Application Case and the Person Record. Adding or editing the Marital Relationship evidence details on Integrated Case will automatically update the Marital Status evidence on the Person Record. The Marital Status evidence will be updated on both the client and their spouse and common-law partner's account, if applicable. If there is no Marital Relationship evidence, Cúram will calculate entitlement to income-tested benefits based on single income. For married or common-law clients, updates to the Marital Relationship evidence may be required on both accounts, depending on the types of cases each member of the couple has in Cúram. For more information on marital changes, Marital Status (Scenario)

The Marital Status evidence is captured on the Person Record and the Application Case, if applicable, and is used to determine eligibility and entitlement to income-tested benefits. If the Marital Status evidence is Single, Separated, Divorced or Surviving Spouse (Widow/Widower) or Common Law Partner and there were no changes to the client's marital status during the retroactive period, Marital Relationship evidence is not required. If the client is married or in a common-law relationship, the Marital Relationship evidence, which creates a link to the spouse or common-law partner, must be added. The Marital Status evidence does not identify the spouse or common-law partner and does not link a client's account to their spouse or common-law partner's account. When a client is registered in Cúram, the Marital Status evidence is added as Unknown . This evidence is automatically updated on both the Person Record and the Application Case, if applicable, for the client and their spouse or common-law partner in the following situations: When an Application Case is created for an income-tested benefit. The Marital Status evidence on the Application Case and the Person Record is updated based on the marital status declared on the application. When the Marital Relationship evidence is added or edited on the Application Case. When a new or updated Marital Relationship evidence is activated on the Integrated Case. The Marital Status evidence cannot be modified if the Marital Relationship evidence exists on an open Application Case or on the Integrated Case. All changes to the marital status must be made by updating the Marital Relationship evidence once it exists.

topic_title: Migrated accounts for married or common-law clients
text: For migrated accounts, the marital relationship start date is set to the month before the 1st month of entitlement in Cúram. As a result, all accounts for married and common-law couples that were in pay during migration have a marital relationship start date of March 1, 2025. This has 2 implications: For any retroactive marital changes before the implementation of Cúram, the Marital Relationship evidence must be updated to the actual start date of the initial relationship to accurately capture the subsequent change. This includes adding periods where the client and their spouse or common-law partner are living apart for reasons beyond control and periods where one spouse or common-law partner gives consent to receive a lower entitlement amount for periods of living apart for reasons beyond their control. Income is shared across couple's accounts for periods where the client is in an active marital relationship. If there are any income evidences that need to be shared to the spouse or common-law partner's case, the Marital Relationship evidence must be updated to indicate that there was an active relationship during the period for which income must be shared. When you authorize an initial Application Case for a new client whose spouse or common-law partner has a migrated account, you must add the actual date of marriage to the initial Marital Relationship evidence and review any Eligibility and Entitlement Override evidence on the spouse or common-law partner's Integrated Case. Under the Financial Administration Act , payments under $1.00 are not required to be paid to clients. Therefore, Cúram only releases these payments once they total at least $1.00. Any unpaid amounts under this threshold that remain in the system for more than 12 months will be automatically written off and will have a Payment status of UT – over 12 months in Cúram. This ensures these payments won't be included in any future entitlement calculations because the amount owing has been cleared.

Cúram will automatically recalculate a client's entitlement when new information is added or when existing information is updated and activated. If this automatic recalculation does not go through, staff can start the reassessment manually. For more information, Manually Reassess Entitlement in Cúram (Action)

You may need to add direct deposit information to a third-party's profile so that they can receive payment on behalf of the client. There are various third-party roles that can be designated as nominees in Cúram so they can receive a payment on behalf of the client. When you add a third party with their banking information for the first time, you must first add the third party's bank account using the Financials tab on their profile. Refer to Third Party Contacts—Add, View, Edit, and Delete in Cúram (Action) . Next, you go to the client's product delivery case and add the third party as a nominee. This changes the nominee on the case from the client to the third party and the direct deposit information to that of the third party. Third Party Contacts—Add, View, Edit, and Delete in Cúram (Action) When the third party reports a new bank account, you must use the New function to add new banking information, not Edit . However, you must use the Edit function to end the previous bank account information. Otherwise, the Edit function should only be used to correct information previously entered incorrectly when payments have not been made to that account. Once the bank account information has been added, you use the Transfer function to automatically update the product delivery case. When the direct deposit for a third party is to take effect in the future, you must create a manual task. This task should be deferred and added to the third party's profile at that future date. The reason why a manual task is needed is because the system cannot capture a future dated direct deposit information for a third party. You must use the Transfer function to update product delivery case nominee details at that time. Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) receives data from Canadian financial institutions regarding changes to a client’s direct deposit information. Once PSPC verifies the Standard Payment System and performs updates, they will then create a Notice of Change File which is sent to the Department. When the Notice of Change is received from PSPC to update direct deposit information, Cúram attempts to automatically update the direct deposit information for clients. If Cúram is unable to automatically update the direct deposit information based on the Notice of Change, a task will be generated. You must review the client's information and manually add the direct deposit information. This will ensure that payment goes to the correct bank account.

Eligibility and entitlement override evidence is used when the actual detailed evidence in Cúram is insufficient to achieve the intended determination of a client's eligibility and entitlement for OAS benefits. Overrides are rarely used. Circumstances when you would add an override include: when a ministerial request is received (e.g. the Minister states that the client is eligible for a pension or benefit or meets the legal status criterion.) to comply with the determination of a court case (e.g. if the Social Security Tribunal rules that a client should be paid $300.00 a month regardless of what is on the client's file, an override would be created to reflect that judgement.) The evidence exists in both Application Cases and Integrated Cases. If the OAS benefit is not approved, the eligibility and entitlement override evidence is maintained in the Application Case. If the benefit is authorized, the eligibility and entitlement override evidence is maintained in the Integrated Case.

When a domestic bank account is added or edited, Cúram automatically reviews the details and compares them against the Bank Account Fraud List. The client will still receive payment, which will be issued by cheque.

topic_title: Establishing payment method and frequency for nominees
text: You must select a delivery pattern for the payment before saving the nominee. The delivery pattern specifies the type of payment (i.e. cheque or direct deposit) and the frequency at which the nominee will receive the payment (monthly, semi-annually, etc.). When the delivery pattern payment type is set to Cheque , a mailing address must be on file. When you assign a new case nominee, you must also assign the dedicated delivery pattern. You can select and change between the available nominees. When a Public Trustee is initially set up, a method of payment is already specified. Therefore, when you add a Public Trustee as a nominee for a client, you must first review the Public Trustee profile to verify the specified method of payment and frequency and ensure you select it as the Delivery Pattern .

The Incarceration evidence captures information about a client's period of incarceration. It is used by Eligibility and Entitlement to assess entitlement to benefits for both the incarcerated individual and their spouse or common-law partner. Since a person may be incarcerated multiple times, you can add multiple incarceration records. During the period of incarceration, the circumstances of incarceration may change (e.g. a different institution or offender status). The Effective Date of Change field is used to track changes of information during an incarceration period. The client's incarceration institution is linked in the evidence as a case participant. When you create a new incarceration evidence, you add an institution by searching for a service supplier and selecting it. This associates the institution with the evidence. If the client has previously been incarcerated, those institutions are listed in the related drop-down menu, allowing you to select that institution if the client has re-entered it. When you modify incarceration evidence, the institution drop-down menu is populated with the current institution name. The evidence exists in both Application Cases and Integrated Cases. If the OAS benefit is not approved, the incarceration evidence is maintained in the Application Case. If the benefit is authorized and approved, the incarceration evidence is maintained in the Integrated Case.

The consent to deduction and payments evidence captures the client's consent to reimburse benefits to the Social Assistance Agency. Additionally, there is a sub-evidence called "social assistance payment." The social assistance payments evidence captures the payment amounts that were paid by the Social Assistance Agency to the client. This amount may be reimbursed from the OAS pension payments and/or income tested benefits (i.e. GIS or ALW and ALWS benefits). Clients who are eligible for income tested benefit or pension payments (i.e. OAS pension, GIS , ALW and ALWS benefits) may receive payments from a Social Assistance Agency (municipal or provincial) for the same period. The Social Assistance Agency can request reimbursement for the payments by submitting a valid Consent to Deduction and Payment - Old Age Security (ISP-3010) form to recover all or part of the amount paid to the individual when pension and/or income tested benefit payments (OAS pension, GIS , ALW and ALWS benefits) are issued. Upon receiving the ISP-3010 form from the Social Assistance Agency, you must make sure it is registered as an external party in Cúram before updating the evidence. In Cúram, the consent to deduction and payment evidence is the parent evidence of the social assistance payments. You must ensure the consent to deduction and payment evidence is active before making any changes to the social assistance payments evidence. The evidence exists in Application Cases and Integrated Cases and can also exist in the Person / Prospect Person profile. If the benefit is not approved, the consent to deduction and payments evidence is maintained in the Application Case. If the benefit is approved, the consent to deduction and payments evidence is automatically brokered to and maintained in the Integrated Case. If the client is found to be ineligible within 12 months of receiving the ISP-3010 form, then a Department's representative must manually send a rejection letter to the Social Assistance Agency.

The CRA income evidence contains income information shared by the CRA . This evidence may impact a client's eligibility and entitlement for income-tested benefits. Cúram will request CRA income data: when an application for an income-tested benefit is submitted; and/or when the request to add a client to the CRA Lifetime List is sent. As a result of the request, the CRA will automatically return the income information for the base calendar year and the following years. You only need to perform a manual request if there is no available income data and you have determined that this information is required to assess eligibility. In those cases, you can manually request a person’s CRA income data by using the New CRA Request wizard in the Interfaces tab in an Application Case or an Integrated Case. Regardless of how Cúram receives CRA income data, the data may need to be reviewed and validated. Refer to Validate Income for Income-Tested Benefits (Action) . The CRA income evidence cannot be edited, discarded or deleted. If you find any discrepancies or if you need to amend a client's income information, you must create a Manually Entered Income evidence for the appropriate tax year. Validate Income for Income-Tested Benefits (Action) Manually Entered Income Evidence—Add, Edit, View and Delete in Cúram (Action) Historical data migrated from CRA income records can be viewed from an Integrated Case in the CRA Income Data section of the Interfaces tab in an Integrated Case. These records are migrated with the line-by-line income information and are identified by the Request Type set to Migration . If the Request Type is set to Migration , no evidence will be created. If the migrated historical CRA data includes Block 7 – Net Employment Income or Block 8 – Net Self-Employment Income , there may be a discrepancy with the Manually Entered Income evidence and the CRA Income evidence as the earnings exemption is not applied to historical migrated data. If there are negative amounts in Block 7 , these should be considered nil. When migrated historical income is required to determine eligibility, you must create a Manually Entered Income evidence for the appropriate tax year. topic_title: Handle tasks with no linked person or prospect person
text: If an agent receives a task that is not linked to a Person or Prospect Person in Cúram, and the Person or Prospect Person cannot be identified using the supporting information, links, and attachments in the task, a ticket must be raised to Operations to retrieve the original PWS task for the agent. Based on the detailed instructions in the original PWS task, the agent must navigate Cúram to identify the client and continue the related workload, or if the work is no longer applicable, update the task status to complete. If an agent must stop, defer, bring forward, reallocate, forward, or make the work available, they can add a comment with additional information to the unlinked task.

A user's Inbox is the centralized location where tasks are received and managed. At any given time, a user can navigate to their inbox and review their workload. Tasks are allocated to the users based on a user's location, language, skill type (virtual skills group), and availability. At the start of a shift, and throughout the workday, users should navigate to their inbox to review their existing workload and workload that has newly been assigned. Under Inbox is the My Tasks tab that displays all tasks reserved to the logged in user. The My Tasks tab is divided in two pages: My Open Tasks ; and My Deferred Tasks . In My Open Tasks , a user can view tasks that have been started, are ongoing, have not yet been started, or stopped. In My Deferred Tasks , a user can view all tasks that have been deferred. In both task spaces, the full details of each task is displayed. All tasks in a user's Inbox are sorted by default based on their importance in being completed. While this sorting is used to indicate where a user should start, it does not prevent a user from completing other tasks in their Inbox. All tasks have 4 statuses: Open On Hold Deferred Closed The status of a task is Open when it is created.

In Cúram, click the Inbox tab. Under My Open Tasks , click the task's hyperlink under Subject . The task details open in a new tab. Click the 3-dots (…) action menu at the top right of the detailed task tab and select Make Available… . The Make Tasks Available window opens. Enter comments to explain why the task is deferred in the Comment field. Click Save .

In all other cases, create an OAS– Maintenance – Manual-Account Verification task. This procedure provides you with the steps to search for tasks, manage tasks forwarded or reserved to you, and create a manual task in Cúram.

Tasks can be modified based on the task actions. This includes: Table 1. Task types and descriptions Task action Description Start Work This task action allows a user to initiate the time-worked timer when they are ready to start working on a reserved task. Selecting Start Work begins the timer and moves the task from the Stopped Work / Work Not Started list to the Started Work list. You can only use Start Work on one task at a time. Selecting Stop Work on the existing task, or Start Work on a new task, stops the timer on the existing task and automatically moves it back to the Stopped Work / Work Not Started list. Stop Work This task action allows a user to pause the time-worked timer until they are ready to resume work on the task. Selecting Stop Work on a task stops the timer and moves the task from the Started Work list to the Stopped Work / Work Not Started list. The time worked is calculated and stored. The timer will resume once you start work again on the task. Add Comment This task action allows a user to add comments to a task. Edit Task This task action allows a user to update the category, type, skill type, priority level and income year of a task. However, only team leaders can edit the Category field and Type field of a system-generated task. Edit the task to correct or update if needed. Edit Due / Receipt Date This task action allows a user to update the due date and receipt date of a task. Edit the due date or receipt date to correct or update the task information if needed. Bring Forward This task action allows a user to set a task to On Hold status until a Bring Forward (BF) date. You may want to BF a task when a future action is required and can be completed by another user with the required skill. The task will be allocated to the assigned work queue until the BF date and will not show in your My Tasks list. The time-worked timer automatically stops when the task status is changed to Bring Forward . Once the BF date arrives, the system will set the task status back to Open . Make Available This task action makes the task available to the previous assignee. The user will no longer see the task in their My Open Tasks list. Make a task available when you identify that you are unable to complete the task and that it should be allocated to the previous assignee to complete. A task that is made available will be unreserved from the current user and be allocated to the previous assignee (individual or work queue). A key difference between Make Available and Reallocate is the destination of the task. When you use the Make Available action, the task will be allocated to the previous assignee. When you use the Reallocate action, the task will be allocated to the initial work queue. Forward This task action allows a user to forward a task assigned to them, to another user or work queue. Team leads can forward tasks that are not assigned to them. These tasks can be viewed in the Open Tasks page of the processing user's workspace or in the work queue workspace. Forward a task when you: identify another user who is working on tasks associated with a common prospect person, person, or case and determine that the task should be forwarded to them. are unable to work on the task and must forward it to your team lead to appropriately reassign. are unable to work on the task and must forward it to a work queue so it can be picked up by another user. When forwarding tasks to an automated work queue, ensure that Virtual Skills Group is listed and that the Virtual Skills Group program and the work queue program match (e.g. OAS VSG will be set for tasks in OAS work queues). Reallocate This task action allows a user to remove the task from their inbox and reassign it using the same allocation rules that were used when the task was first created. Reallocate a task when you determine that you cannot complete it and that it should be reassigned using the same allocation rules used at the time of the task's creation. A key difference between Make Available and Reallocate is the destination of the task. When you use the Make Available action, the task will be allocated to the previous assignee. When you use the Reallocate action, the task will be allocated to the initial work queue. Defer This task action allows a user to set the task to Deferred status. This status is used in cases where you are waiting for information, or a specific action needs to be completed before you can action the task. The task remains in the user's inbox and moves into the My Deferred Tasks page. The time-worked timer automatically stops when the task is deferred. When you defer an open task, you must record a restart date and the status of the task is updated from Open to Deferred . At the restart date, the task remains in Deferred status. To resume work on a deferred task, you must restart the task manually to Open status and initiate the time-worked timer by selecting Start Work on the task. Restart This task action allows a user to manually restart a deferred task and return it to the user's My Open Tasks list. When you are ready to resume work on the task, initiate the time-worked timer by selecting Start Work . Restart a task when you need to work on it prior to the restart date or when the restart date arrives. Only a task that has been deferred can be restarted. This task action does not apply to tasks that use the Bring Forward functionality. Reserve When a user is working on one or more existing tasks associated with a prospect person, person, or case, the user may identify additional tasks on the target. In this case, the user should consider reserving the task with the following guidelines: Is the task currently available to reserve? Do I have the required skill confirmed under the Skill Type(s) field to complete the task? If a user recognizes that the task is available and they have the required skill confirmed under the Skill Type(s) field to complete the task, the user should reserve the task if their availability and language (oral and written) permit it. Complete (commonly referred to as Close) This task action allows a user to update the status of a task to Completed. To complete or close a task, it must be reserved to you and in your My Open Tasks . Tasks will disappear from the list of tasks once they are completed or closed.

A task refers to a specific unit of work that needs to be completed as part of a larger process, or workflow. It represents an individual or collection of actions or activities that are assigned to a user within the system. These actions or activities could include reviewing documentation, collecting information, and updating evidence. Tasks are often associated with a prospect person, person, or a type of case. These tasks are used to manage and track the progress of work related to the associated target. In Cúram, tasks are created in two ways. Primarily, tasks are generated automatically by the system based on predefined rules and workflows. However, Cúram also allows the manual creation of tasks by users. Manual task creation is only to be used in specific scenarios. Each task contains attributes, history and comments, assignments, time worked, and relevant links to supporting pages based on the prospect person, person, application, or type of case. Task attributes are a set of details used to capture a task's name, status, priority, category, urgency, and more. The combination of task attributes provides key insight as to what the task is about, what information is available, what work has been previously done on the task, and what is the relevant priority for the task.

A work queue is a central repository that organizes, holds, and tracks the tasks that need to be completed within the system. Work queues are used to manage and monitor user-created, or system-generated workload. There are two types of work queues: automatic work queues and manual work queues. Team members will only be subscribed to manual work queues. Team leads will be subscribed to both automatic and manual work queues to monitor workload, however, team leads will only subscribe team members to manual queues. Automatic work queues are used to hold tasks that can be automatically assigned by the system to users. Manual work queues are used to manage specific tasks that require manual intervention for allocation. A campaign work queue is a work queue created a result of an organization-planned activity or an event. It is organized with the purpose to complete an identified set of tasks by a specific group of staff members. Work queues have been configured specifically for OAS. In addition to automatic and manual work queue configurations, work queues are defined by region and purpose. Each region has a respective automatic and manual work queue Additionally, there are different work queues based on region (region or national), type of workload (migrated from legacy or generated in Cúram), and work queues by business units. A deduction is an amount withheld from a payment. The maximum deduction amount is the amount that can be deducted to recover overpayments, penalties, and interest from a pay-run (gross to net). The maximum deduction amount will be stored on the Product Delivery Case and displayed on the Overpayment Case for reference. The maximum deduction amount is not associated to a single deduction. It is the common deduction amount that is linked to all active overpayment, penalty, and interest deductions. The maximum deduction amount is equal to the recovery rate that will be withheld from benefit payments to repay monies owed to the Department. If the Auto Calculate box is checked, Cúram will auto calculate and create the maximum deduction amount after the following trigger events: Overpayment update triggers An Overpayment Case (manual Overpayment Case or Payment Correction Case) is activated. There is a change in future OAS eligibility and entitlement. An Overpayment Case is suspended or unsuspended. Penalty and interest triggers A new penalty or interest is added and there is no existing maximum deduction amount. A new penalty or interest is added for a current and future existing maximum deduction amount. A new penalty or interest initial liability amount is updated, and the new amount is more than the running outstanding liability balance, the current and future maximum deduction amount. Manually triggers You manually edit a maximum deduction amount line item (recovery amount or recovery percentage) and the Auto Calculate box is unchecked. The deduction will start 60 days after the activation of debt or the maximum deduction amount.

When a death notification is received, the DOD must be added to the Birth and Death Details evidence as soon as possible because it will impact any OAS pension and benefits that the client is currently receiving. Once the DOD is added or updated on the Birth and Death Details evidence and activated, Cúram will run a reassessment to ensure that the account is in balance. A task will be generated for manual review if, at any time during the reassessment process: the account is not in balance; or the system cannot perform actions automatically. As part of the reassessment process, Cúram will automatically: Update the spouse's Marital Relationship evidence to Surviving Spouse/Common Law Partner , if applicable. If the system is unable to update the Marital Relationship evidence of the spouse, it will create a task for the processing centre to review the account; Send the Surviving Spouse OAS Rate Change (ISP-3393) letter outlining the new monthly benefit, if monetary changes are detected for the spouse; Send the Client has died outside of Canada (ISS-2388) letter, if the death occurred outside of Canada; and Generate a task to review the account if there are any existing overpayment or underpayment and/or any new overpayment or underpayment generated because of the DOD (e.g. the DOD was reported late). DOD received via ITRDS Updated When a DOD is received in ITRDS with a CPP source or SIR-PRV-C source, the ITRDS interface will send the DOD to Cúram. In most cases, the DOD evidence is automatically activated and a reassessment is performed. There are certain scenarios where the DOD evidence received from ITRDS will remain in an In Edit status and/or additional actions must be taken on the account. Table 1. Development Scenarios and Results Scenario Result Prior to the DOD being received, the client's OAS pension or benefit was suspended in Cúram for the following reasons: Cannot locate ISB Request OAS-RI Non-Filer Other Presumed or potentially Deceased Non-compliance The DOD evidence will remain in an In Edit status, and a task will be generated for staff to review the account. The DOD evidence will be activated in Cúram, and a task will be generated for staff to review the account. Contact the Integrity Services Branch (ISB) investigator assigned to the file to determine next steps before taking any action on the account. The client is incarcerated. The DOD evidence will remain in an In Edit status, and a task will be generated for staff to review the account. There is an existing DOD in Cúram, and the DOD is removed in ITRDS . Clients can submit a request for reconsideration anytime they disagree with a decision made on their case. The client must submit a request for reconsideration within 90 days of the date of the decision letter from Service Canada. The request for reconsideration can be submitted using the Request for Reconsideration of an Old Age Security Decision (ISP-3134) form or online through the client portal. When a client submits a request for reconsideration from the client portal, a request for reconsideration task is created in the appropriate work queue. Cúram automatically displays a corresponding reconsideration flag on the context panel for the Person or Prospect Person and associated case for the client. When a written request for reconsideration is processed, a task is created in Cúram that shows the client's SIN or Cúram Reference Number, the client's name, and Request for Reconsideration for the Type. The request is also listed as an attachment under the Contacts tab. You must manually add a flag to the client's profile to indicate it is under reconsideration. When the reconsideration is closed, you must remove the flag. When there is a reconsideration on an account with an overpayment that resulted from the decision the client is requesting the reconsideration for, recovery action must be deferred if it has not been initiated. If recovery has already been initiated, then it must be suspended until the outcome of the reconsideration, or the appeal is known. You should manually de-activate a payment correction or overpayment (manual) case deduction for a departmental liability.

Central Printing is where the bulk printing occurs, where manual letters would be produced in a nightly batch. This is the default method unless the letter does not meet the requirements for bulk printing. The process of centrally printing correspondence is available for most scenarios. A letter must not be greater than 5 physical pages (shows as 10 pages in a PDF due to double sided (duplex) printing) including pages from attachments added to the letter. The letter and attachment must be the same page size (i.e. 8.5x11 inches and 8.5x14 inches are distinct sizes and cannot be combined for central printing). The size is based on the page size of the template, not the size of the attachment. Once this letter has been submitted for printing, Cúram will change the communication status from Submitted to Sent , when the print file is sent to the print provider.

Cúram will change the Communication Status to Sent for any central printing letters. Some of the following statuses can be changed manually. The following status are available in Cúram: Table 2—Available Communication status Status Description Draft The Draft status is displayed once the template has been selected and all mandatory data is populated and Edit after Submit has been selected to open the template. This will create the hyperlink to the letter in Cúram, along with the Correspondence Tracking Number for this letter. Submitted The Submitted status is a transition state that indicates a letter has been submitted for printing and is awaiting the delivery options that are associated with the letter to complete. For central printing, it will show in this state until the nightly batch is completed. For local printing, this status will show before Confirm Delivery has been selected. Sent The Sent status is displayed automatically by Cúram when a manual or system-generated correspondence has successfully been bulk printed, or when a manual correspondence has been locally printed (once the user confirms delivery). Submitted Oversized The Submitted Oversized status is displayed by Cúram when the manual nightly print job has failed because a letter is over the 5-page maximum allowed by Central Print (manual only). A task will be generated and assigned back to the processing work queue for task assignment. Misdirected The Misdirected status is manually updated in Cúram when correspondence is sent to a wrong recipient and is potentially a privacy breach. This status removes access to the correspondence in the vault by removing the hyperlink to the letter. This status can be manually changed. Returned The Returned status is used when the correspondence is returned. This status is updated manually in Cúram. Once the status is updated, a task ("TASK-07 Review nature of absence evidence") will be generated. This status can be manually changed. Void The Void status is used when the correspondence has been identified as incorrect. This status removes access to the correspondence in the vault by removing the hyperlink to the letter. This status can be manually changed. Intercepted The Intercepted status will display in Cúram when the request to pull a letter from a bulk or nightly batch file was successfully pulled before it was mailed to the client. Only Central Print can change this status.

Correspondence (i.e. letters) are created in Cúram to communicate with a client or a verified third party on a Person record, Application Case, Integrated Case and/or a Foreign Engagement Case. If you cannot find the correspondence template in Cúram, updated versions are available on the Forms and Letters page of the KMT. You must search for NATS letters temporarily stored on the KMT before searching in NATS. There are 3 types of letters being generated out of Cúram with the Corporate Correspondence Tool (CCT): bulk letters; on demand letters; and manual letters. Table 1—Types of letters in the CCT Type of letter Description Bulk letters Bulk correspondence (also known as "bulk letters") are high volume letters sent to clients on a set schedule. This schedule can be daily, weekly, monthly or yearly, depending on the type of letter. Client data in Cúram determines who will be scheduled to receive each type of scheduled bulk letter. Bulk correspondence is generated automatically by the CCT with a data file created by Cúram through a system process and is sent to the CCT to produce the correspondence. Clients are selected to receive each type of scheduled bulk letter based on changes made to their personal or case record. The list of clients who meet the criteria for each bulk letter is created by Cúram and sent to the CCT to create the letters. Each type of bulk correspondence has a specific template. Cúram will automatically prevent the generation of bulk letters for clients marked as duplicates. On demand letters On demand letters include 5 specific letters: Application for the Allowance or Allowance for the Survivor (ISS-3008) Application for the Guaranteed Income Supplement with Statement of Income (ISS-3025B/ISB-3026) Statement of Income for the GIS , the ALW or ALWS (ISS-3026) OAS Cancellation of Waiver of Application by Minister (ISS-8418B/ISP3550) Client has died outside of Canada (ISS-2388) These system-generated letters are printed in the manual nightly batch printing process. Manual correspondence Manual correspondence generation can be submitted for nightly bulk printing. This allows the system to generate bulk correspondence for a targeted group of clients or recipients when required. For every letter created (bulk, on demand or manual), a correspondence tracking number and a communication record is created in Cúram. All correspondence is displayed on the Person record, but only the correspondence specific to a case are created and displayed on the Case record. To create a letter, you must specify the recipients of the correspondence, select a template to use, and complete all mandatory data/selections and/or all required options. A pop-up interface with the CCT is used to complete the template and generate the correspondence. A user's working pattern refers to the specific working hours set for an individual user over a 14-day period. This period starts on a Monday and ends on the 2nd Sunday. The 14-day period will repeat when an end date is not set for a working pattern. A working pattern could be added for a user when their working pattern does not align with the organizations default working pattern. For example, if a user works 3 days per week or works part time. This ensures work is assigned limited to their availability. There are several types of working patterns: 14-Day Cycle: Each working pattern covers a 14-day period, which can repeat indefinitely if no end date is set. Standard and Non-Standard Hours: Standard working hours might be set (e.g. 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.). Non-standard hours can be defined for specific days (e.g. a half-day on a Friday from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.). Non-Working Hours: These can be specified for one or more days and can automatically apply to a full day to indicate a non-working day. A team lead can manage working pattern for users to ensure the allocation of new tasks based on their availability. The Working Patterns tab allows a team lead to see the user-specific working patterns that have been created. The team lead can select the New menu option to add a new working pattern for the user. A work queue is a central repository that organizes, holds, and tracks the tasks that need to be completed within the system. Work queues are used to manage and monitor user-created or system-generated workload. There are 2 types of work queues: automatic work queues and manual work queues. Team members will only be subscribed to manual work queues. Team leads will be subscribed to both automatic and manual work queues to monitor workload, however, team leads will only subscribe team members to manual queues. Automatic work queues are used to hold tasks that can be automatically assigned by the system to users. Manual work queues are used to manage specific tasks that require manual intervention for allocation. A campaign work queue is a work queue created a result of an organization-planned activity or an event. It is organized with the purpose to complete an identified set of tasks by a specific group of staff members. Work queues have been configured specifically for OAS. In addition to automatic and manual work queue configurations, work queues are defined by region and purpose. Each region has a respective automatic and manual work queue Additionally, there are different work queues based on region (region or national), type of workload (migrated from legacy or generated in Cúram), and work queues by business units. topic_title: Cancelling Nil or under threshold payments
text: You can manually cancel a payment record in Cúram if it is within your delegation of authority in the following situations: the payment is created after an Eligibility and Entitlement re-assessment occurs and there is no longer entitlement to that payment; to correct the payment if an incorrect deduction was applied, rather than manually reversing the deduction and paying as a priority payment. The manual cancellation function can be used under the following conditions: The net payment amount is $0 ( Nil Payment ); or The net payment is under the $1 threshold ( UT ) and remains in that status, indicating it has not yet been included in a subsequent payment. If you cancel a payment that includes a reversible deduction, you must apply the gross entitlement to the overpayment to void the overpayment to $0. If you cancel a payment that included a non-reversible deduction, the amount available to offset should already be reduced by the amount of the non-reversible deduction which would leave an outstanding overpayment equal to the amount of the non-reversible deduction.

topic_title: Liability offset deductions on cancelled payments New
text: Depending on how and when the payment was issued or re-issued, and subsequently cancelled, a liability offset deduction may be considered reversible or non-reversible. If a liability offset deduction was created to offset penalty, interest and overpayment liabilities: when reconciling and reissuing a payment, the date the deduction was created will determine whether the deduction is reversible or not. during the offset of an arrears or underpayment, the date the payment was cancelled will determine whether the deduction is reversible or not. The same process will follow as usual to update the Public Sector Collections and Disbursements (PSCD): When a non-void liability offset is reversed, the system triggers an update to PSCD using existing deduction triggers. When a void liability offset is reversed, the system triggers an account debt adjustment to PSCD using existing triggers. The following table provides details of when the liability offset deduction will be considered reversible or non-reversible under each payment process. Table 2. Reversible or non-reversible liability offset deductions Payment Process Before March 27, 2026 On or after March 27, 2026 The liability offset deduction was created during the offset of an arrears or underpayment. If the payment was cancelled before March 27, 2026, the deduction is non-reversible . If the payment was cancelled on or after March 27, 2026, the deduction is reversible . The liability offset deduction was created when reconciling and reissuing a payment. If the liability offset deduction on the cancelled payment was created before March 27, 2026, the deduction is non-reversible . If the liability offset deduction on the cancelled payment was created on or after March 27, 2026, the deduction is reversible .

text: If the payment is cancelled after reassessment, you must determine if the cancelled payment should be applied to any existing overpayment. If yes , you must use the Reconcile & Reissue Payment functionality. If no , reissue the payment.

topic_title: Reconciling and Reissuing a Payment Updated
text: The Reconcile & Reissue Payment feature is only enabled for Cúram-generated payments, payments with pending Penalty, Interest, or Overpayment liabilities. The Reconcile & Reissue Payment feature is not enabled for cancelled legacy payments and cancelled manual payments. It is used to apply a cancelled payment to an outstanding overpayment, penalty, or interest either as a deduction or an internal reconciliation process. When submitted, the liability amount of the overpayment, interest, or penalty will be reduced. All other deductions will only be withheld, according to the priority of withholds, if any amount is owing after the liability offset deduction and non-reversible deduction overpayments deductions have been applied. If any non-reversible deductions were withheld from the original payment, they will not be deducted a second time. Any reversible deductions (including 'Program Specific Overpayments', Penalties, Interests, CPP deductions) that were part of the original payment may be deducted again at their current rate with any remaining amount after reconciliation should there still be an outstanding balance. If you want to withhold an amount for an overpayment that is different than the current maximum deduction amount, you must manually adjust the offset amount. The current maximum deduction amount will not be deducted from the payment if you perform this adjustment. For example, the client's original payment for $400 ($500 for the OAS pension with $100 recovered for an existing OAS overpayment) was cancelled. Instead of deducting the current liability offset deduction amount of $100 for the overpayment, you want to withhold a lump sum amount of $300. After you manually adjust the Offset Amount to $300 and reconcile and reissue the payment, the remaining balance of $200 will be issued. Once you submit the reconciling and reissuing of a payment, Cúram does the following: It creates a Liability Offset deduction in the amount equal to the sum of the liability offset amounts. When the payment is reissued, Cúram will end-date the liability offset deduction and its status will be changed to Inactive . It reduces the liability amount of the overpayment, interest, or penalty. For overpayments, a write-off is created; for a penalty or interest, the outstanding balance amount is reduced. It sends a trigger to Public Sector Collections and Disbursements as a void offset. If there are any other current, active deductions on the client's account, they will be applied to the reconciled and reissued payment, if there is a sufficient balance remaining. If there is a reason the deduction should not be applied to the payment (e.g. the client does not want a Voluntary Tax Withhold deducted) you must add an end-date to the deduction before reconciling and reissuing the payment. You will have to start the deduction again for the next monthly payment, if it is a recurring deduction. The remaining amount, if any exists once all deductions have been applied, can be issued to the original nominee or to an alternative nominee. The reissued payment will be picked up by the Standard Payment System batch process for further processing if the remaining balance after reconciliation is greater than $1.

This procedure provides you with the steps to manage cancelled payments in Cúram.

When a payment that was issued in Cúram is cancelled in the Standard Payment System (SPS), the status automatically changes from Issued to Cancelled , and the status for all instruction line items within the payment change from Processed to Cancelled . This will take 1 to 2 business days. These transactions can be found in the Financials tab at the Person level or in the Product Delivery Case. The SPS communicates both the successful and unsuccessful disbursement of payments back to Cúram, including the reasons for cancellations for traceability purposes. In some instances, you may cancel a payment in SPS before it is redeemed, and this cancellation is communicated to Cúram for further resolution. When a payment is cancelled, Cúram: identifies the non-reversible and reversible deductions: Invisible: Table 1—Deduction types Deduction Type Employment Insurance Non-reversible CRA Set Off Non-reversible Veterans Affairs Canada Non-reversible Social Assistance Agency Reimbursement Non-reversible Department of Justice Arrears Non-reversible Department of Justice Fees Non-reversible Provincial Voluntary Tax Non-reversible Liability Offset Conditional Interest Reversible Penalties Reversible Departmental (Overpayments) Reversible Canada Pension Plan overpayments Reversible Non-Resident Tax Conditional OAS Recovery Tax Conditional Federal Voluntary Tax Conditional creates a corresponding Overpayment Case for each non-reversible deduction regardless of if the client's eligibility and entitlements during the cancelled payment period was reassessed or not and creates a corresponding deduction against each liability. reverses the reversible deductions and: updates (increases) the liability amount back to amount that was reversed; and updates (decreases) the year-to-date totals by the amount that was reversed. records the cancellation reason for accountability and traceability purposes. updates the status of: the payment from Issued to Cancelled . any instruction line items from Processed to Cancelled . Once Cúram receives a cancellation notice from the SPS, a task will be created to manage the cancelled payment. There are 2 possible paths you can choose for payment reissuance following a cancelled payment: reissue the payment; or reconcile and reissue the payment. If you want to reissue the payment with the current, active deductions, use the Reissue function. If you want to withhold an amount for an overpayment that is different than the current maximum deduction amount, use the Reconcile & Reissue Payment function.

PSCD creates interest automatically on liabilities when penalties are imposed on a client. When this happens, PSCD issues a report requiring you to create or modify an interest record on a client's penalty liability or overpayment case. Interest is a liability owed by a client to the Department. It is a separate liability from a penalty liability or overpayment that the interest is owed on. Interest can only be charged if a penalty is imposed, even if the amount imposed is 0. The amount of interest charged will be based on many factors including the collection status, the amount of the penalty and/or any associated overpayments. Liabilities, including interest records, can only be deleted in the pre-payment period which occurs before gross to net has been calculated.

text: In Cúram, go to the client's profile. Refer to Search for a Person in Cúram (Action) . Special caution(s) are concerns and issues on a client account. The Department uses special caution(s) to alert staff of the issues and concerns. A red exclamation mark in the top-left of the Profile Home Screen identifies a person with a special caution. Special cautions do not stop processing on a client account. All processes currently in place with the client should proceed while special cautions are present on a client account. A special caution indicates the Department needs to pay attention to the account to ensure correct business processes are followed. A client can have more than one special caution applied to their profile. For example, if the client has a risk of inaccurate migrated data and their whereabouts are unknown. Special cautions may be added in the following instances: Special Caution Type Description Whereabouts Unknown An Employment and Social Development Canada Department representative can create a Whereabouts Unknown special caution when the client cannot be located. Based on the established procedures, once certain duration has elapsed and the client still cannot be located, the client may be referred to the Integrity Services Branch (ISB) for investigation and another special caution can be created to capture Under Investigation with ISB . If the ISB is not able to locate the client, you must leave the flag on the account even after the investigation has been concluded. Under Appeal A Department representative can create an Under Appeal special caution to indicate that the client has submitted an appeal to Social Security Tribunal (SST). Under Reconsideration A Department representative can create an Under Reconsideration special caution to indicate that a paper-based Request for Reconsideration document was uploaded for a client. Additional Security Criteria When the ISB has identified that a specific client requires additional security criteria for authentication, an Additional Security Criteria flag can be set and maintained for the Client. Risk of Inaccurate Migrated Data The migration process has identified that some clients may have inaccurate data migrated from the pay pattern file. Under Investigation with ISB A Department representative has referred the client to the ISB for investigation and captures the flag for the client. Special cautions should be removed in the following situations: The Department has located a client whose location was previously not known. The ISB has concluded their investigation. The Under ISB Investigation flag can only be removed by a SCBO and only after the adjustments have been applied. The client's appeal to the SST has been finalized. All paper-based reconsideration documents for the client have been captured in Cúram and all the client's reconsideration requests have been resolved. The ISB has determined that the additional security criteria is no longer required on the client's account. Additional security criteria can be added by other channels as well in addition to ISB. All inaccurate migrated data previously identified in the client's record has been resolved. All special cautions that have been removed will be display in the Previous tab of the Special Cautions tab. The special caution is placed in the wrong record. The wrong type of special caution was placed in the record. The special caution was placed with the wrong date. In any of these situations, the special caution should subsequently be added to the correct account, with the correct type and date.

topic_title: Determine when to intercept a payment
text: A payment may be intercepted for any of the following reasons; although not an exhaustive list: there is no entitlement (e.g. payment after death, change in marital status or residence); the amount of the entitlement is incorrect; the payee cannot be located; the name of the payee has changed; the payee has changed (e.g. a trustee dies); the payee has a new address; the payee is deceased and the payment must be issued to the estate or legal representative; there is a garnishment related to the Family Orders and Agreements Enforcement Assistance Act ; or automatic intercepts (Autopulls) where SPS automatically intercepts payments that are: under or over the allowable amounts (under $1.00 or $40,000 or more); or issued to the same third party address or direct deposit account as 3 previous payments that were returned because the information within the payee's file is incorrect. Do not intercept any payments where there is still partial entitlement. Do not intercept any payments for the month of death to apply towards an overpayment. This procedure provides guidance on when and how to: intercept a payment in the Standard Payment System (SPS); and redirect or reissue the payment, if applicable.

When you determine that a payment should not be delivered to a payee, you can access the SPS and intercept it. This prevents the issuing of a payment. The intercepted payment can be cancelled, remailed or reissued to the payee, if applicable. Previously, the same user had the delegated authority to intercept a payment, modify the payment destination and reissue the same payment. Since October 26, 2017, SPS does not allow you to intercept and redirect the same payment. The additional security measure allows you to: intercept a payment and have another user modify the payment destination or reissue the payment; and modify a payment destination or reissue a payment after a payment has been intercepted by another user. This additional security measure is similar to the current segregation of duties for inputting and authorizing a priority payment. For more information, refer to the Delegation of Authorities (PDF, 313 KB) Download link . Delegation of Authorities There is a limited timeframe to intercept a payment after it is loaded into the SPS and before it is extracted. The payment must have a Payment Status of Ready for Extract . The OAS benefit payment date is the same for every region, but the schedule of production of payments may vary by region. You will follow the production schedule to obtain specific information on when CPP and OAS payments are loaded into the SPS and the final intercept dates. To view current and past production schedules, refer to the Benefits Toolbox . In some cases, you may need to keep track of or hold a file until the payment appears in SPS and is ready for extract. Benefits Toolbox Intercepting payments reduces the need to pull cheques or recall direct deposit payments after the extract date. In emergency situations, such as when a payment is determined to be fraudulent or when issuing a payment will result in a substantial overpayment, cheque pulls and direct deposit recalls may still be requested. If a new address or new banking information is required to issue a payment, and SPS shows the Payment Status as Ready for Extract , this must be actioned immediately. SPS only allows a payment to be reissued the same day it has been intercepted. If you intercept a payment without reissuing it the same day, SPS will extract the payment and cancel it automatically. SPS will update the payment with the return reason Intercepted at the extract date .

This procedure provides you with the steps to action and record re-issued cancelled legacy payments in Cúram for OAS client accounts migrated from both the OAS Online and International Agreement (IA) legacy systems.

Payments are issued, returned, and cancelled through the Standard Payment System (SPS) on behalf of the government of Canada. When a payment is cancelled in SPS, Cúram will receive a cancelled payment file and create a task to review the cancelled legacy payment. Unlike Cúram-issued cancelled payments, when the payment is issued before migration to Cúram, it cannot be resolved systematically. OAS clients from the OAS Online and IA legacy systems will be migrated into Cúram. For clients migrating from OAS Online, Cúram generates a lump sum legacy payment of all the client’s historical entitlements during the cutover process. The legacy payment is based on the first eligibility and entitlement reassessment upon the migration of historical evidence. Historical eligibility and entitlement information from 2010 onwards will be migrated. During migration, the following items will be created: an OAS Integrated Case; a Product Delivery Case; financial components; and a payment record based on the created financial components. For clients migrating from the IA system, no historical entitlement data will be migrated for IA clients and no financial information will be generated for periods prior to migration. This means that Cúram will assume that it has not paid any amount to the client. An FEC captures all information relating to a Person’s relationship with a foreign country. An FEC stores documentation and communication related to a Person’s foreign benefits for a foreign country as well as interactions between the Department and the foreign country relating to the person’s eligibility for Canadian benefits. A Person can have multiple FECs under their profile and each FEC is dedicated to one specific country. An FEC must be created under the Person’s profile when a person requests a foreign benefit from a different country, or when the Department sends or receives a foreign liaison requesting information. If an FEC for a specific country already exists, you can update the details within the specific FEC. If the Person does not exist in Cúram, you must add a Person profile. Register a Person in Cúram (Action) You cannot delete an FEC in a Person’s record. However, you can choose to close the FEC when it is added in error. The status of the specific FEC will change from Open to Closed . When an FEC is created, the system automatically assigns the case to a processing work queue as the case owner. To close an FEC, you must be a supervisor. To view the owners of an FEC, go to the User Roles page under the Administration tab. The page lists all the case owners. When the new case owner is assigned, the previous case owner will be updated with an end date. The information in each FEC is categorized into 7 tabs: Table 1 — Tab Name and Detail Tab Name Details Home The Home tab consists of 2 pages: Home Urgent Flags The Home page shows the overview of the FEC. The Urgent Flags page lists the tasks with urgent flags. Tasks The Tasks tab displays the tasks related to the specific FEC. Foreign Benefits The Foreign Benefits tab consists of the following pages: Foreign Applications Foreign Liaisons Attachments The Foreign Applications page lists the foreign benefit applications in the FEC. To view the details of each application, click the toggle icon ( > ) to expand the item. You can also create a Foreign Benefit Application from this page. Foreign Benefit Application—Add, View, Modify, and Delete in Cúram (Action) The Foreign Liaisons page lists the records of all incoming and outgoing liaisons in the FEC. This page also lists the cross reference to any related foreign benefit applications to the outgoing liaison. To view the details of each liaison, click the arrow icon to expand the item. You can also add a liaison record from this page. Liaison—Add, Modify, Access and Delete in Cúram (Action) The Attachments page lists all the attachments associated with the FEC. To view the details of each attachment, click on the arrow icon to expand the item. You can also add an attachment from this page. In January 2014, changes were made to the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations which increased the length of the Parent and Grandparents (PGP) sponsorship period from 10 years to 20 years, affecting all provinces except Quebec. For individuals who landed in Quebec, the sponsorship period remains at 10 years, regardless of where they live in Canada now. Around January 2016, individuals began landing in Canada under 20-year PGP sponsorship agreements (except in Quebec). However, for a period of time after January 2016, some individuals still landed in Canada under 10-year PGP sponsorship agreements. Effective October 1, 2025, sponsored individuals will not be entitled to receive income-tested benefits for the entire period of their sponsorship agreement, regardless of the type or length of sponsorship agreement. Income-tested benefits with an effective date before October 1, 2025, will be grandfathered and processed under the old sponsorship agreement rules even if the application is received after this date. The interim guidance in this procedure must be followed until the updated policy, procedures and related forms and letters are published. Applications affected by the new sponsorship agreement rules must be placed on hold until an announcement is published to advise that all affected policy and procedures have been updated. When an application for income-tested benefits is received, you must determine if the applicant is under a sponsorship agreement, if the following conditions apply: The applicant was not born in Canada; The effective date of the initial income-tested benefit is October 1, 2025, or later; and The applicant has less than 20 years of residence in Canada from the date they became a permanent resident. If the application form does not allow for the applicant to provide this information or the applicant does not answer the sponsorship agreement question, and there is no supporting documentation on the file to confirm the sponsorship agreement, you must request it by phone or mail. The following sponsorship agreement details must be requested: The category of the sponsorship agreement; If the sponsorship agreement was with the province of Quebec; The length of the sponsorship agreement in months or years; The date the applicant became a permanent resident in Canada; and The applicant's Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) Unique Client Identifier (UCI) number. The applicant may not be able to provide all of the above information; however, they must provide enough information for you to confirm whether they are under a sponsorship agreement and the length of the sponsorship. All of the required information can be obtained over the phone, and a note must be added in ITRDS to record the sponsorship agreement details. Documentation Documentation to support the sponsorship agreement details may not be required; however, the Department can request it at any time. Some documents supporting an applicant’s legal status may include the sponsorship agreement details. Review the sponsorship agreement details provided by the applicant and any immigration documentation regarding the sponsorship agreement to ensure there are no discrepancies or situations that require confirmation, such as: The applicant indicated that they did not enter Canada under a sponsorship agreement. However, identifiers exist on any IRCC records that suggest a sponsorship undertaking (e.g. "FC" (Family Class) notations, completion of any fields related to sponsorship). The applicant’s permanent resident date is in January 2016 or later, and they indicate they are under a 10-year sponsorship agreement (except where they landed in Quebec). Although this situation may not be a discrepancy, it requires documentation before it is accepted. There is a discrepancy between the application and previously submitted information (e.g. a duplicate or previous application, documentation). If there is a discrepancy or situation that requires confirmation, request supporting documentation to confirm the sponsorship agreement details. Acceptable documentary evidence The following documents can be accepted to support the sponsorship agreement details: Confirmation from IRCC; Confirmation of Permanent Residence (IMM 5292) (older version); Confirmation of Permanent Residence (IMM 5688); Verification of Status (VOS) or replacement of Immigration Document (IMM 5716); Record of Landing (IMM 1000); Verification of Landing (IMM5617); Any official immigration documents that confirm the details of the sponsorship agreement; and Formulaire Demande d’engagement (A-0546-GF).

This procedure provides you with the steps to manage tax slips in Cúram. This includes how to view, create, edit, delete, amend, issue, cancel, and reverse the cancellation of T4A or NR4 tax slips for an OAS pension, the GIS, and ALW and ALWS benefits in Cúram.

You can manage the tax slips through several action items. Each action item is enabled based on the current Issuance Status and Printing Status of the tax slip for a specific client, tax slip form type, and tax year. Action items available include the following: Table 8. Action Items Action Item Description Create This action allows you to start a new tax slip after the original one has been deleted or cancelled. This action is only available when: the Issuance Status is Deleted or Cancelled ; the tax slip is created for a tax year after the last business day of that tax year; and no tax slip of the same type already exists for that year. Tax Slips (Scenario) Edit This action allows you to make changes to the financial data of an existing tax slip that has not been issued yet. This action is only available when the Issuance Status is Submitted or Draft . It is not available if the Printing Status is Sent . Delete This action allows you to remove a tax slip that is not in its final state. This action is only available when the Issuance Status is Submitted or Draft . It is not available if the Printing Status is Sent . Amend This action allows you to make changes to the financial data of a tax slip that has been officially issued. This action is only available when the Issuance Status is Issued . Cancel This action allows you to invalidate a tax slip that has been issued (e.g. the tax slip was sent to the wrong person, a confirmation is received that a person previously identified as deceased is not truly deceased, OAS benefits were cancelled). This action is only available when the Issuance Status is Issued . To ensure that the information is sent to the CRA and Revenu Québec, you must send an enquiry to the National Business Expertise Tool (NEXO) Internal link (access is required) when a tax slip is cancelled in Cúram. National Business Expertise Tool National Business Expertise Tool Issue This action allows you to issue the drafted version of a tax slip that was saved but not yet issued. This action is only available when the Issuance Status is Draft . Duplicate and Issue This action allows you to reissue a tax slip to the client. This can only happen if the financial data has not changed. This action is only available when the Issuance Status is Issued . Reverse Cancellation This action allows you to reverse the cancellation of a tax slip that was done in error. This action is only available when: the Category is Cancelled ; the Issuance Status is Submitted ; and the Printing Status is Submitted . This action is not available if: the Printing Status is Sent or Deleted ; the Issuance Status is Issued ; or a new tax slip has been created for the same year after cancellation.

There are 3 categories within each type of slip: Table 3. Tax slip categories Tax Slip Category Description Original Original tax slips indicate that a specific tax slip form type and tax year was generated for a given client (e.g. T4A (OAS) 2025). Amended Amended tax slips indicate that changes were made to the financial data generated for a specific client, tax slip form type, and tax year after the original tax slip has been issued. Cancelled Cancelled tax slips indicate that the tax slip was invalidated because it was sent in error (e.g. tax slip was sent to the wrong person, confirmation is received that a person previously identified as deceased is not truly deceased). It could also indicate that the benefits were cancelled.

The Creation Method indicates how the financial data was generated for the latest version of the tax slip for that specific client, tax form type, and tax year. There are two types of Creation Method for tax slips in Cúram: Table 6. Tax Slip Creation Method Tax Slip Creation Method Description Auto create through batch The tax slip data was entirely system generated. Create manually Some or all the box content of this tax slip was manually modified.

Tax slip progress can be tracked through the Issuance Status . The Issuance Status indicates whether a particular version of the tax slip has been picked up for processing by the CRA and/or Revenu Québec interface batch jobs. This is the process through which the financial data is forwarded to the CRA and Revenu Québec for tax purposes. Tax slips have one of the following Issuance Status : Table 4. Tax Slip Issuance Status Tax Slip Issuance Status Description Submitted This status indicates that tax slip data has been generated but has not yet been processed or released. The tax slip is ready to be picked up for processing by the CRA and/or Revenu Québec interface batch job. When the Issuance Status of the tax slip is Submitted , you can: view the tax slip; edit the tax slip; and delete the tax slip. Issued This status indicates that the tax slip has been processed and released to the CRA and/or Revenu Québec and to the print provider or the Client Portal, depending on the client’s preferences and system settings. When the Issuance Status of the tax slip is Issued , you can: view the tax slip; amend the tax slip; cancel the tax slip; duplicate the tax slip; and create a new tax slip, if the Issuance Status is Issued (Cancelled) . Draft This status indicates that the tax slip data has been generated but is not yet ready to be processed or released. When the Issuance Status of a tax slip is Draft , you can: view the tax slip; edit the tax slip; issue the tax slip; and delete the tax slip. Deleted This status indicates that this tax slip version has been deleted. Deleted tax slip versions will no longer be visible. When the Issuance Status of a tax slip is Deleted , the only action allowed is to create a new manual tax slip for that specific client, tax slip form type, and tax year.

Tax slip progress can also be tracked through the Printing Status . The Printing Status indicates whether a particular version of a tax slip has been released or processed by the printing batch job. This is the process through which the tax slips are forwarded to the print provider or to the Client Portal, depending on the client’s preferences and system settings. Tax slips have one of the following Printing Status : Table 5. Tax Slip Issuance Status Tax Slip Printing Status Description Submitted This status indicates that the tax slip is ready to be printed but has not yet been sent to the print provider or to the Client Portal, depending on the client’s preferences and system settings. Sent This status indicates that the tax slip has been sent to the print provider or to the Client Portal, depending on the client’s preferences and system settings. Intercepted This status indicates that the tax slip was intercepted during the printing process. Draft This status indicates that the tax slip is saved but not submitted. The tax slip was amended, edited, or created and the option selected was Save rather than Save and Issue . Deleted This status indicates that this tax slip version has been deleted. Deleted tax slip versions will no longer be visible. Error This is an interim status that indicates that an error occurred while processing this tax slip (e.g. it may have been successfully sent to the CRA and/or Revenu Québec, but not to the print provider). No manual intervention is required.

You can view 3 types of tax slips in Cúram: Table 2. Types of tax slips and their description Type of slip Description T4A (OAS) This tax slip is generated for clients who received any OAS pension or benefits in Canada or to deemed residents. NR4 (OAS) This tax slip is generated for clients who received any OAS pension outside of Canada. This will show up in Cúram as an NR4 (OAS) form. NR4 (ITB) This tax slip is generated for clients who received any income-tested benefits outside of Canada. This will show up in Cúram as an NR4 (ITB) form. However, the client will receive an NR4 (OAS) (ISP-0138).
