As individuals may apply for income-tested benefits up to 11 months before their effective date, an interim procedure has been created to identify applicants under a sponsorship agreement. These applications must be put on hold until all affected policy and procedures have been updated. An announcement will be published to advise when the affected policy and procedures have been updated and when these applications can be processed. To determine if an initial income-tested benefit application is affected by the upcoming sponsorship agreement amendments, Interim Guidance for Upcoming Sponsorship Agreement Amendments (Action) Initial income-tested benefit applications are being enhanced with detailed questions regarding an individual’s sponsorship agreement.

In January 2014, changes were made to the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations which increased the length of the parent and grandparent (PGP) sponsorship agreement period from 10 years to 20 years, affecting all provinces except Quebec. To align the OAS program with these changes, the OAS Act was amended in 2014 to limit the payment of income-tested benefits (i.e. GIS, ALW benefit and ALWS benefit) to sponsored individuals for the entire length of their sponsorship agreement, regardless of the type of sponsorship agreement or their years of residence in Canada. However, these amendments were not immediately brought into force. Individuals began landing in Canada (in all provinces except for Quebec) under 20-year parent and grandparent (PGP) sponsorship undertakings around January 2016. This means that the OAS Act amendments will begin impacting these individuals in 2026, when they will have attained 10 years of residence in Canada. These amendments will be brought into force through an Order in Council effective October 1, 2025, affecting income-tested benefit applications with an effective date of October 2025 or later. Sponsored individuals who are eligible for income-tested benefits with an effective date prior to October 2025 will be grandfathered using the old sponsorship agreement rules.

topic_title: Disclosure—Prepare and send a referral to the Integrity Services Branch
text: If an individual discloses, either verbally or in writing, that they may have provided potentially misleading information to the Department, proceed as follows: If the disclosure is received verbally from an individual during regular processing, you must document the information provided. Use neutral and objective language to report the issue as it has been described by the individual when documenting the disclosure. An informant lead (also known as a third party complaint) is a notification from an individual that, in their opinion, an investigation should be made into a client's eligibility or entitlement to an OAS pension or benefit. An informant lead can be received by letter, telephone or any other means to OAS. All informant leads must be sent to Integrity Services Branch (ISB) for a potential administrative investigation. It is the Department’s obligation to review each lead received to determine if it is valid or has an impact on an applicant or a beneficiary’s eligibility or entitlement. You must never indicate receipt of an informant lead on an individual's file or in ITRDS notes, as this could reveal an informant's identity. You must protect the informant, even if they do not indicate they want to remain anonymous. Information that might reveal the identity of an informant must not be divulged or disclosed. A verbal or written disclosure is when an individual or third party voluntarily admits to knowingly making a misrepresentation to the OAS program. If you receive a verbal or written disclosure where the individual comes forward to correct inaccurate or incomplete information, or to provide information they did not divulge during previous dealings with the Department, you must refer it to the Integrity Services Branch (ISB). ISB will: review the details of the disclosure and determine if the disclosure is voluntary; and complete the disclosure investigation. If a disclosure is made for any reason, it can lead ISB to review the client’s eligibility and entitlement for benefits, under the same program, even if the file was not previously flagged for review. For more information, Disclosure (Knowledge)

An administrative investigation is an impartial process conducted by ISB when there is a concern, suspected fraud or potential misrepresentation regarding eligibility or entitlement to the OAS pensions and benefits. A file can be sent for an administrative investigation for a number of reasons, including: anomalies, discrepancies or suspected fraud discovered by departmental officials; informant leads (third party complaints); or verbal or written disclosures. While reviewing a file or processing an application, you may discover an anomaly or discrepancy that warrants further review. You should thoroughly review the client's OAS and CPP files, ITRDS and notes, Cúram and PWS for historical data. If you cannot determine a reasonable explanation, before making a decision on the account, the file and all relevant documentation must be referred to ISB immediately. Only a SCBO or a Medical Adjudicator, can refer a file for an administrative investigation. Under the OAS Act, you are not authorized to collect and use publicly available personal information in the administration, review and determination of initial and continuing eligibility to pensions, benefits or provisions. However, you are authorized to access an individual’s publicly available personal information only to obtain their address and contact information to locate and re-establish communication with the individual (e.g. by using Canada411.ca). For more information, Privacy and Personal Information (Scenario) When referring a file for an administrative investigation it is important that any action you take does not interfere or obstruct a future investigation. You must exercise discretion when: contacting the client; suspending or cancelling the account; or requesting reimbursement for an overpayment. On January 27, 2025, the Simplified CPPD Client Engagement National Pilot was launched and officially became permanent on April 1, 2026. The goal of the pilot was to evaluate the effectiveness of reducing client engagement calls, maintaining client satisfaction, and improving the speed of service. The pilot confirmed that the number of mandatory client engagement calls could be reduced while maintaining client satisfaction and improving speed of service. Results demonstrated reduced call volumes, sustained client satisfaction, and faster service delivery. Based on these outcomes, the pilot measures were implemented as standard operational procedures effective April 1, 2026.

Individuals can apply for an OAS pension or income-tested benefit (i.e. GIS, ALW and ALWS benefits) online through the Client Portal on their My Service Canada Account (MSCA) portal if the following conditions are met: Table 1. Criteria required to apply online Pension or benefit Eligibility criteria to apply online The OAS pension alone, or the OAS pension with the GIS The applicant: is aged 64+1 month or older; is not already in pay or pending for an OAS pension; is a Canadian resident; and does not have a third-party representative (trustee or power of attorney) on file. The GIS alone The applicant: is aged 64+1 month or older; is in pay or pending for the OAS pension; is not already in pay or pending for the GIS; is a Canadian resident; and does not have a third-party representative (i.e. trustee or power of attorney) on file. The ALW benefit The applicant: is aged between 59+1 month to 65+11 months; is not already in pay or pending for the ALW benefit; is a Canadian resident; and does not have a third-party representative (i.e. trustee or power of attorney) on file. The ALWS benefit The applicant: is aged between 59+1 month to 65+11 months; is not already in pay or pending for the ALWS benefit; is a Canadian resident; and does not have a third-party representative (i.e. trustee or power of attorney) on file. When the applicant logs into MSCA and applies for an OAS pension or benefit, the system verifies if a Cúram user account exists. If the system cannot find a match in Cúram, a Prospect Person is created along with a task for the Application Case. If the applicant has an application started in the Client Portal, they can save and exit the application at any time before submitting it. If they attempt to begin another application for the same pension or benefit, they will be prompted to complete the application that is currently in progress. If any of the above criteria are not met for the pension or benefit being applied for, the applicant will be unable to continue and the Apply button will be greyed out. If all of the above criteria are met for the application being applied for, the applicant can complete and submit their application online. Completing and submitting an online application The applicant’s residential and mailing addresses are pre-populated based on information available through MSCA. Any address and telephone number updates made through the online application are captured directly into Cúram and will transfer over to ITRDS . When the applicant submits the application, the information is captured in a date stamped PDF file and the applicant is presented with a confirmation page. The confirmation page contains the following information: a confirmation number; the applicant's name; the date and time stamp; a list of Service Canada phone numbers and the address of the mail processing centre where supporting documents can be sent; a list of documents that the applicant is required to submit as supporting evidence based on answers they provided on the application (e.g. legal status, marital status, immigration); a link to upload documents online; a phone number for foreign residents to provide direct deposit information and a link to the applicable direct deposit form; and a list of other benefits or provisions the applicant may be eligible for or entitled to.
There are no exceptions or special cases. (KA-01098 Snippet 12.0 content. Do not modify or delete.)

When an individual is married or in a common-law relationship and is applying online for the GIS or ALW benefit, their spouse or common-law partner must provide consent to obtain their information from the CRA and declare that the information provided about them is true. The spouse or common-law partner's consent and declaration are considered obtained through their GIS or ALW benefit application process if: the details of their marital status match the information provided on the online GIS or ALW benefit application you are processing; the marital status and spouse or common-law partner details provided by the CRA match the information provided, if available; and one of the following conditions are met: both spouses or common-law partners have signed a previously submitted paper OAS pension/GIS or paper GIS application; the spouse or common-law partner previously submitted an online OAS pension/GIS or online GIS application and a signed Spousal Consent and Declaration (ISS-0954) letter or a Spousal Consent and Declaration GIS (ISS-0954A) letter was received; the spouse or common-law partner has been approved for automatic enrolment of the GIS (i.e. the process is not in Pending status); or the spouse or common-law partner has also submitted an online OAS pension/GIS , online GIS or online ALW benefit application that is being processed at the same time as the applicant's online GIS or ALW benefit application. If there are any discrepancies between the information provided in the spouse or common-law partner's GIS or ALW benefit application process, the CRA spouse information, and the information provided in the online GIS or ALW benefit application you are processing that affects eligibility and entitlement, a task is generated in Cúram. You must resolve the discrepancy according to regular procedures before authorizing the online GIS or ALW benefit application. Mismatches on the case record occur when there are discrepancies between the information stored in Cúram and ITRDS . These mismatches can happen for any information in the case record (e.g. bank account details, phone records, third-party contact evidence for representatives). If there is an error in matching data, the system sends an error response code. Subsequently, the error code may generate a task in Cúram. This information will assist you to validate mismatched case records with ITRDS . The following are examples of mismatch tasks: Example 1: Mismatched bank account details A mismatch may occur when a future-dated bank account exists for a client in Cúram and the system receives an event update from ITRDS . The client account will need to be reviewed when there is a transactional event update from ITRDS to delete future-dated bank account or if there is a mismatch with existing future-dated bank account (i.e. financial institution number, branch transit number and account number). You must review the client's account information before manually closing the task. Example 2: Mismatched phone records There may be a mismatch when the system cannot match an existing current or future-dated phone record in Cúram with a transactional event update from ITRDS to delete phone record. A mismatch task would be created when the matching criteria (i.e. type, start date, phone number) do not match between Cúram and the ITRDS update. Based on this review you must decide whether to add, modify or delete the correct phone number to resolve the mismatch. Table 1 — Cúram to ITRDS Telephone mapping Cúram ITRDS Personal Landline 1 – Home Personal Mobile 3 – Cell Business Landline 2 – Business Personal Teletypewriter (TTY) 7 – Device for the Deaf Business Mobile 8 – Other Business Teletypewriter 8 – Other Example 3: Mismatched third-party representative evidence When Cúram cannot match a third-party representative evidence record with the transactional event update from ITRDS , a task will be created to update the third-party contact information. You must review and update the relevant contact details to ensure the case record is accurate. Note that only the representative role is shared between Cúram and ITRDS . No other third-party representative role is shared or can be mismatched. However, it is possible to have 2 separate third party contacts for a single client in Cúram (i.e. Trustee and Power of Attorney). Also, there are no mismatch tasks surrounding Third Party Contacts between ITRDS and Cúram. A mismatch on this would likely be a system-based mismatch because Cúram was not sending the correct or enough information for ITRDS to retrieve the correct record. Example 4: Mismatched future-dated addresses A mismatch for future-dated addresses may occur when an ITRDS update is received but there is a difference in the effective date of the address change or there are multiple future-dated addresses. The client account must be reviewed, and information must be evaluated to determine if ITRDS updates must be applied or identify the correct future-dated address to be deleted. Example 5: Mismatched death match If there is a mismatch of date of death with ITRDS or if there's no date of death in Cúram, the date of death must be reviewed. The date of death evidence record on the person profile must be updated based on the event update from ITRDS . Example 6: Mismatched marital status A CRA Marital Status Mismatch task is created for verification when a mismatch with CRA Marital Status and Marital Relationship evidence do not match. If Cúram receives marital status information from the CRA and the details do not match with the existing CRA marital status evidence in the client’s profile, Cúram will update the CRA marital status evidence with the new details from the CRA.

This procedure provides you with the steps to apply a cash receipt reversal in Cúram.

Apply a cash receipt reversal In Cúram, do one of the following: Go to the person’s profile. Refer to Search for a Person in Cúram (Action) . Click the Cases and Applications tab. Click Cases in the left navigation bar. Click the reference number for the Benefit Overpayment case. The overpayment case opens in a new tab. Search for a Person in Cúram (Action) Go to the Overpayment case. Click the Financial tab. Click Transactions in the left navigation bar. Click the ( > ) toggle icon to expand the transaction. Click the ( > ) toggle icon to expand the liability. Click the 3-dots ( … ) action menu to display the action menu, and select Reverse Cash Receipts… . Enter the information in the Reverse Cash Receipts wizard as follows: Table 1 — Fields and Directions under the Reverse Cash Receipts wizard Field Direction PSCD Document Number Mandatory Enter the PSCD document number for the reversal. Document Received Date Mandatory Today’s date is automatically filled. If the date is not correct, select the correct date. Click Save . A new Payment Received (Reversed) transaction will appear on the Overpayment case under the Transactions list on the Financials tab.

The Public Sector Collections and Disbursements (PSCD) system can send a reversal of a cash payment to Cúram. When this happens, Cúram uses a Payment Received Reversal functionality to record and display the reversal. This cancels the corresponding received payment and creates a reversal record for tracking purposes. A cash receipt reversal also updates the outstanding balances on the overpayment that was updated by that payment when it was initially created. The Cash Received amount previously received is added back to the Departmental Liability outstanding balance. Cash receipt reversal is automatic. The procedure in this document is only necessary when the automated procedure fails. The cash receipt reversal received from PSCD and applied to the applicable overpayment in Cúram will generate a task containing the following information: Client SIN or Cúram reference number Client name Total overpayment amount Date Product delivery case type Product delivery case reference number Overpayment authorization requirement In addition, the task may indicate one of the following: That overpayment letters will be sent That the case needs to be reviewed That the overpayment penalties or interests can be applied to offset an underpayment PSCD will only send one reversal for a cash receipt. The cash receipt will be indicated by its SAP document number. Cúram will reverse all transactions associated with the document number. The principal amount and the interest owed initially communicated by PSCD may be different at the time the reversal is sent. Cúram will reverse both the principal and the interest amounts. For example, if the principal and interest amounts sent for the cash receipt received were different, PSCD will send a reversal of the cash receipt received. Based on the SAP document number, Cúram will reverse both the principal (overpayment) and interest amounts.

text: In Cúram, go to the client's profile. Refer to Search for a Person in Cúram (Action) . Search for a Person in Cúram (Action) Click the Cases and Applications tab. There are 3 International Social Security Agreement (ISSA) countries (United States, Japan, and Jamaica) with information sharing restriction that do not allow any information, including the date of death that is received on a Foreign Liaison form to be shared outside of International Operations (IO). Refer to International Operations — Sharing information obtained under an International Social Security Agreement (Knowledge) for more information if needed. Due to the restrictions that do not allow the information to be shared outside of IO, this evidence is to be created on the Foreign Engagement Case (FEC) so that the date of death received remains restricted. Once the evidence is created on the FEC, it only applies to Canadian benefits processed under an ISSA. If the date of death is reported or verified by a non-restricted source in the future (e.g. confirmed or reported by NOK, death certificate, or other) the date of death can then be updated on the person record. International Operations — Sharing information obtained under an International Social Security Agreement (Knowledge) Before entering a date of death on the Restricted FEC, you must verify that a date of death is not already recorded on the person. If the date of death on the person and the date of death on the liaison is different, you must verify the date of death prior to entering the date of death on the Restricted FEC. Cúram does not restrict you from adding a date of death on the Person’s profile and on the FEC. If a “Birth or Death details” evidence or “Restricted Date of Death” evidence is activated and date of death on the 2 evidence does not match, then a task will be generated to review the date of death. This task will be sent to the IO User as they have access to both the Person level Date of Death and the Restricted Date of Death. Different dates of death received from restricted countries Different dates of death may be received from restricted countries. In such cases, only the correct date of death must be captured in the system as evidence. If any previously captured date is incorrect, the evidence must be deleted, and a new restricted date of death evidence should be created. For example, you initially capture and activate the first received restricted date of death evidence. Later, the department receives another restricted date of death from one of the other two restricted countries. If the date matches the previously captured one, no further action is needed. However, if the date differs, you must conduct research to determine the correct date of death. If the previously captured date is confirmed to be correct, no further steps are required. If the new date is determined as correct, you must delete the existing Restricted Date of Death evidence and apply changes. After applying changes, you must capture the new ‘Restricted Date of Death’ evidence with the correct date of death and apply changes.

The ALW / ALWS Conversion page displays the conversion status for accounts where the ALW benefit or ALWS benefit may be converted to an OAS pension and the GIS when the client reaches the age of 65. This status can be modified manually to allow or prevent conversion. The ALW / ALWS Conversion page is created automatically by Cúram. Once created, this page will appear on the Administration tab of the client's Integrated Case. Every month, Cúram will identify clients who need an ALW / ALWS Conversion page created based on the following criteria: The client has an OAS/GIS Integrated Case with an Open status. The client does not have OAS/GIS Application Details with Auto-Enrolment as the Method of Application . The client is turning the age of 64 and 1 month in the processing month, or has turned the age of 64 and 1 month in the past (includes age overrides, which take precedence). The client does not have an ALW / ALWS Conversion page. If the above criteria are met, Cúram will: create the ALW / ALWS Conversion page; and set the Automated Conversion status to Yes if the client: has 40 years of residence in Canada as of their most recent ALW benefit or ALWS benefit application (including overrides); is eligible and entitled to receive an amount greater than $0 for the ALW benefit or ALWS benefit in the current calendar month; and does not have their ALW benefit or ALWS benefit suspended. The following tasks will be created in Cúram to indicate that the account may be eligible for the conversion of benefits: At the start of every month, the system will create an OAS-Applications-Conversion Review task if: the client will turn the age of 64 and 9 months or the age of 65; their Automated Conversion status is set to No ; and their Conversion Status is set to Pending . When the Department receives a Conversion Application (OAS/GIS) (ISP-3045) form, an OAS Intake - Conversion 3045 task is created. These accounts must be reviewed as a priority to determine if the benefits can be converted and set the Conversion Status accordingly. For more information about processing these tasks, Conversion of OAS Benefits (Scenario)

text: When the OAS program communicates with the CPP or CPPD program, complete the following steps: Review the client's ITRDS notes. OAS processors must complete the ISP-0435 form and send it to the regional GD inbox indicated on the form. Upon receipt of the completed ISP-0435 form, Program Support Clerks will scan the form into the Pension Trusted Digital Repository (PTDR) and create work items in PWS . Add the work items under the Benefit Review work type. For more information, refer to PTDR Procedures Manual Internal link . PTDR Procedures Manual When a Benefit Review work item is assigned to a CPP processor, the processor must verify if the work item is related to their program. If yes , the processor must update the information on the client's file in ITRDS . If no , the processor must update the work item with one of the following two options: If the review needs to be done by the CPPD program, the CPP processor must change the work item program to DSB and select the Benefit Review work type. If the review needs to be done by the Program Exception Processing Unit, International Operations or the Dual Unit, the CPP processor must change the location on the work item accordingly but maintain the same program and work type.
The Communication between programs (ISP-0435) form was developed to facilitate the exchange of client information between the CPP, CPPD and OAS programs.
The following actions are required when the CPP and OAS programs communicate through a Communication between programs (ISP-0435) form.

Use the ISP-0435 form in the following situations: The client wishes to discuss their benefits from the other program or initiate a change on their account while on a call (e.g. update their language preference, Federal Voluntary Tax Withhold, country of birth and telephone number). An action to suspend or release benefits is needed on a client's account and the processor becomes aware of an impact on the other program (e.g. returned mail is received for the OAS program but no action has yet been taken for the CPP program). A processor receives an enquiry addressed to their program only or a document that was only scanned to one program (e.g. email, Power of Attorney document, third-party contact, name changes), and they identify that there may be an impact on the other program. The OAS program must communicate with the CPPD program when awaiting a decision on a Declaration of Incapacity - Physician's Report (ISP-1800) form. Enquiries related to the date of death, direct deposit, change of address, consent or authorization to communicate that cannot be actioned by one program due to system limitations and require manual intervention by the other program. Do not use the ISP-0435 form in the following situations: A cross program recovery is required for overpayments. CPP, CPPD and OAS processors must use the Cross Program Recovery – Set-Off Memorandum (Request) (ISP0434-B) and Cross Program Recovery – Set-Off Memorandum (Response) (ISP0434-C) forms. A death notification is received. Information can be shared between the CPP and OAS programs by selecting the other program in ITRDS or Cúram, including: direct deposit updates; address changes; and consent or authorization to communicate information. A processor receives a document or application that needs to be shared with the other program. Follow regional procedures to have the document rescanned to the Pension Trusted Digital Repository and a work item or task created for the other program.

The CPP enhancement legislative changes were phased-in over seven years (from 2019 to 2025), starting in January 2019. The enhanced components (first and second additional components) are not a separate benefit, but rather a top-up to the base CPP. The enhancement increases the CPP RTR pension, Post-Retirement Benefit ( PRB ), DSB and SVR pension. The increase a client will receive depends on how much and for how long they have made enhanced contributions (and/or enhanced contributions made by their late spouse or common-law partner). Eligibility for CPP benefits is still based on the contributions to the base component and is not affected by the enhancement. The CRA began collecting first additional contributions in January 2019 and second additional contributions in January 2024. System updates required to accommodate the CPP enhancement legislative changes have been implemented gradually through the CPP enhancement project. The project was also responsible for implementing system functionalities to accommodate the legislative changes resulting from the 2016-2018 CPP Triennial Review, such as: a flat-rate Death ( DTH ) benefit; the removal of the age-based reduction to the SVR pension; the Child Rearing Drop-In (CRDI) provision; and the Disability Drop-In (DDI) provision. The CRDI and DDI only apply to the first and second additional components of CPP benefits. On November 23, 2019, system functionalities required to split earnings and contributions in ITRDS (between the base CPP and first additional component) were implemented. Certain products such as the Statement of Contributions (SOC), My Service Canada Account (MSCA) and the Canadian Retirement Income Calculator were updated to accommodate the CPP enhancement and Triennial Review legislative changes. On May 21, 2022, system functionalities were introduced in ITRDS and CPMS to pay the first additional component of the CPP. The system release in May 2022 also included the introduction of system functionalities for two of the Triennial Review legislative changes: a flat-rate DTH benefit; and the removal of the age-based reduction to the SVR pension. On May 27, 2023, system functionalities were introduced in ITRDS to attribute or “drop in” credits (Child Rearing Drop-In and the Disability Drop-In provisions) into the calculation of the first additional component of CPP benefits. On February 10, 2024, system functionalities were introduced to allow ESDC to receive second additional contribution data from the CRA . Data transmission between Retraite Québec and ESDC was also updated to accommodate the second additional component.

topic_title: View OAS and GIS automatic enrolment details
text: In Cúram, go to the person's profile. Refer to Search for a Person in Cúram (Action) . Search for a Person in Cúram (Action) Click the Cases and Applications tab. Click Application on the page group navigation bar on the left. The list of available applications opens. Click the hyperlink for the application under the Reference column. On the Home tab of the application case, click the Automatic Enrolment link. The Automatic Enrolment screen displays the following information: Table 1 — Automatic Enrolment Screen Fields Field Description OAS Auto-Enrolment Cluster Header OAS Automatic Enrolment Displays Yes when OAS AE Status = Auto Enrolled . Displays No when OAS AE Status = Excluded , otherwise it is blank. Eligibility Process Date The date the client is deemed eligible for OAS auto-enrolment in ITRDS /EDB. This date is provided in the OAS auto-enrolment file from ITRDS /EDB. OAS AE Completion Date The date the OAS auto-enrolment process completes (after authorization). OAS AE Status The current OAS auto-enrolment status for the client. Change… link: This link opens the screen to manually change the OAS AE Status . The link is only displayed if there is an OAS auto-enrolment status. OAS AE Exclusion Reason The reason that the client is excluded from OAS auto-enrolment. This field only displays when the status is Excluded . GIS Auto-Enrolment Cluster Header GIS Automatic Enrolment Displays Yes when GIS AE Status = Auto Enrolled . Displays No when GIS AE Status = Excluded , otherwise it is blank. GIS AE Completion Date The date the GIS auto-enrolment process completes (after authorization). GIS AE status The current GIS AE status for the client. Change… link: This link opens the screen to manually change the GIS AE status. The link is only displayed if there is a GIS AE status. GIS AE Exclusion Reason The reason that the client is excluded from GIS auto-enrolment. This field only displays when the status is Excluded . Auto-Enrolment Status History Cluster Header Pension Identifies which pension or benefit the status record is related to. AE Status The status that was in effect based on the effective date and time. Effective Date Time The date and time that the auto-enrolment status came into effect. Updated By The system or individual that updated the status. If the status was updated manually, the username will be displayed. Table 2 — Automatic Enrolment Statuses Status Description Ready for Intake Only used by OAS auto-enrolment to indicate that the client is ready to be picked up by the OAS auto-enrolment intake process. This is the first step in the OAS auto-enrolment process after the file has been received. Intake in progress Only used by OAS auto-enrolment to indicate that the OAS auto-enrolment intake process has started for the client. The intake process is used to match or register a client as a Person in Cúram, create the application case, and create the evidence on the application case. Ready for GIS AE Only used by GIS auto-enrolment to indicate that the client is ready to be auto enrolled. This is the first step in the GIS auto-enrolment process after the GIS auto-enrolment file is received. GIS AE Initiated Only used by GIS auto-enrolment to indicate that the GIS auto-enrolment process has been initiated for the client. During this step there is a check to confirm the client is still auto enrolled for OAS, and to ensure the client has not already applied for GIS (e.g. a paper application). Add to lifetime list Only used by GIS auto-enrolment to indicate that the client has been added to the CRA lifetime list. The status remains at this status until the CRA has provided a response with the client’s income information. This step is skipped if the client is already on the CRA lifetime list. Validate CRA response Only used by GIS auto-enrolment to check the response from the CRA (income information), and validate the information provided. Validation includes steps such as checking that income information was provided successfully for the tax year, death code, bankruptcy status, and marital status. Check for Spouse Only used by GIS auto-enrolment to check if the client has a spouse, based on the response from the CRA, and to compare it with the Marital status in Cúram. If the client has a spouse, then the system checks if the spouse is already in Cúram. During this stage, the status may be set to Manual Intervention if the system finds the spouse in Cúram but is not able to create marital relationship evidence automatically. Request Spouse profile Only used by GIS auto-enrolment to retrieve the spousal information from ITRDS /EDB if the spouse is not found in Cúram. During this stage, the status may be set to Manual Intervention if the system encounters an error when attempting to send the spousal information from ITRDS /EDB to Cúram. Spouse profile received Only used by GIS auto-enrolment to indicate that the spousal information was received from ITRDS /EDB. Spouse Added to Application Only used by GIS auto-enrolment to indicate that the client’s spouse was successfully added to the Application Case and the marital relationship evidence was created successfully. Add Spouse to lifetime list Only used by GIS auto-enrolment when the spouse is added to the CRA lifetime list to receive their income information from the CRA. This step is skipped if the spouse is already on the CRA lifetime list. Validate Spouse CRA response Only used by GIS auto-enrolment to check the response from the CRA (income information), and validate the information provided. Validation includes steps such as checking that income information was provided successfully for the tax year, bankruptcy status, and death code. Manual Intervention Used by OAS auto-enrolment and GIS auto-enrolment to indicate that the remaining auto-enrolment steps need to be completed manually. Once all the remaining steps are completed, including sending correspondence manually, then the status should be set to Waiting for Authorization . The authorization process should not be done manually. Setting the status to Waiting for Authorization will ensure that the authorization process will complete the process in the month that the client turns 65. Waiting for authorization Used by OAS auto-enrolment and GIS auto-enrolment to indicate that the client has almost completed all the auto-enrolment steps. The only remaining step is the authorization process, which occurs at the beginning of the month that the client turns 65 years old. Auto Enrolled Used by OAS auto-enrolment and GIS auto-enrolment to indicate that the client has been successfully auto enrolled. This is the last step of the auto-enrolment process after the Application Case has been authorized. Excluded Used by OAS auto-enrolment and GIS auto-enrolment to indicate that the client has been excluded from the OAS or GIS auto-enrolment process. An exclusion reason is provided to indicate why the client was excluded.

An OAS / GIS Application Case is automatically created during the auto-enrolment process and a separate OAS / GIS Application Case is created for the GIS auto-enrolment process. The evidence required to support each auto-enrolment process is also created automatically. An OAS / GIS Application Case can be accessed from the person's profile. OAS/ GIS Application Case—View, Authorize, Reopen and Print in Cúram (Action) You can view a client’s OAS and GIS auto-enrolment status on the automatic enrolment screen that is accessed from the OAS / GIS Application Case. The auto-enrolment screen is only accessible from the Application Case for clients that are auto enrolled. The link will not display if a client is not auto enrolled. The Automatic Enrolment screen displays the OAS auto-enrolment status and GIS auto-enrolment status, current and historical, so that you can see where the client is in each auto-enrolment process. You can also manually update either auto-enrolment status from the screen. The OAS / GIS Application Case created by each auto-enrolment process is automatically authorized at the beginning of the month that the client turns 65 years old. The auto-enrolment authorization process will send the entitlement award letter (ISP-3092) automatically. A client may be excluded from the auto-enrolment process automatically if an issue (e.g. evidence issue) is encountered, or if certain information changes (e.g. date of birth month or year changes) during automatic enrolment. You can also exclude a client from auto-enrolment manually if needed using the Edit OAS auto-enrolment status or GIS auto-enrolment status process. A client may decide to opt out of auto-enrolment before the authorization process. You can see if a client has opted out by checking the status on the Application Details evidence. If a client has opted out via Client Portal, there are no steps required for processing until an application is received. If the client opts out via a letter, you will need to make this update before the month the client turns 65 to reflect the client has opted out of auto-enrolment. Identity Confirmed When a client is selected for OAS auto-enrolment or GIS auto-enrolment, their identity is confirmed and verified in ITRDS /EDB before the auto-enrolment process starts in Cúram. As a result, a client that is auto-enrolment for OAS or GIS is considered verified so none of the evidence requires verification during auto-enrolment. Any changes to the evidence (e.g. manually or a life event) will trigger a verification, if applicable, as per the standard process. Manual Intervention If a client’s auto-enrolment status is set to Manual Intervention , manually or automatically, then the remaining steps of the auto-enrolment process must be completed manually up until authorization. When doing this, set the client’s auto-enrolment status to Waiting for Authorization as the last step in the process. After this, the auto-enrolment authorization process will complete the process. You must generate correspondence manually for all the steps you complete during manual intervention.

Bank account information contains the details of a client's bank accounts. Bank accounts can be used to set up electronic fund transfers to or from the Department. direct deposit information for all clients must be recorded as a Joint Account and the Account Name must be entered as or changed to alphabetical characters that reflect the clients' name. You must use the following formatting for the Account Name field for joint accounts: Use the first letter of the client’s first name, followed by a space and their full last name. Then, use the word "and", followed by the first letter of the linked client’s first name, a space, and their full last name. Example E Bennet and F Darcy If a middle name is provided, it can be abbreviated to an initial and placed between the first initial and the last name, separated by spaces. Example E J Bennet and F Darcy The Account Name field in Cúram has a character limit of 60. However, when sharing the new direct deposit information with CPP, the Account Name entered in Cúram must be limited to 30 characters to comply with Account Holder name input requirements for ITRDS . For joint accounts exceeding this limit only , you must follow the instructions below: In Cúram: Update the direct deposit information for OAS, ensuring the above account name formatting is followed. Do not check the Use for CPP checkbox. In ITRDS , provide detailed notes indicating that due to character limits, the direct deposit was only updated in Cúram. Fill out the Communication between programs (ISP-0435) form, noting that the direct deposit information has been updated for OAS and requires review by CPP. Refer to Communication Between Programs (ISP-0435) Form (Action) . Joint accounts As Cúram does not allow more than one client to receive pension payments in the same bank account unless the Bank Accounts Details are the same across these clients, you will receive an error message when you try to update or add bank account details if the information does not match. If you receive this error message, you must review the account to determine if the client has a spouse, common-law partner or a third party registered in Cúram. If this spouse, common-law partner or third party is receiving payments in the same account, their Bank Accounts evidence must be updated to match. When a payment has not been processed, refer to the Payments not issued section in the What you need to do section of the Step by Step tab. When a payment has been processed, the direct deposit information must not be edited for evidence preservation purposes. Refer to the Payments Issued section in the What you need to do section of the Step by Step tab. If the client has no spouse, or there is no third-party evidence recorded on the account, you must call the client to obtain information about the party who may be using the identical bank account. If you are unable to determine who may be using the same banking information as the client, send an enquiry via the NEXO Tool Internal link . NEXO Tool If a task was received from the Call Centre with a request to update the direct deposit information, review the date of the request then intercept and redirect pending payments, as needed, to avoid returned payments. Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) receives data from Canadian financial institutions regarding changes to a client’s direct deposit information. Once PSPC verifies the Standard Payment System and performs updates, they will then create a Notice of Change File which is sent to the Department. When the Notice of Change is received from PSPC to update direct deposit information, Cúram attempts to automatically update the direct deposit information for clients. If Cúram is unable to automatically update the direct deposit information based on the Notice of Change, a task will be generated. You must review the client's information and manually add the direct deposit information. This will ensure that payment goes to the correct bank account. This article explains how the renewal of income-tested benefits occurs in Cúram.

The renewal of income-tested benefits is an annual process that occurs in July, which is the start of a new benefit payment period. If a client is eligible for an income-tested benefit and their income information from the previous calendar year has been received, Cúram will automatically process the renewal of the benefit. In addition to the renewal of benefits, several supporting activities are performed around the same time in Cúram. These activities include: reviewing existing overrides; sending appropriate correspondence (e.g. renewal notices, decision letters); reviewing income variances that may indicate inconsistencies between reported and actual income; and reconciling estimated income that was used for the prior benefit period with the actual income now received. Some clients may need to fill out a Statement of Income for the Guaranteed Income Supplement, the Allowance or Allowance for the Survivor for payment period of July (20XX) to June (20XX) with Information Sheet (ISP-3026) form to keep receiving their benefits. This usually happens when their income information is missing, because they have not filed a tax return, or they don't meet the eligibility rules for automatic renewal based on the information available (e.g. there is a bankruptcy reported by the CRA ). The ISP-3026 form is mailed in March to the address the client has on file at the end of the March accounting month. If the ISP-3026 form is not returned by late June, Cúram automatically sends a second form. If the ISP-3026 form is still not returned in time, benefit payments may be delayed starting in July. Before income-tested benefits are paid for the new payment period, Cúram goes through a process called "reversion", which takes place in June. This process includes: moving all new income information into the current income fields; deleting any data that is no longer needed from the previous payment period; calculating eligibility for the GIS, the ALW benefit, and the ALWS benefit based on the updated income; and capturing information for issuing entitlement correspondence. As part of the supporting activities during the renewal process, Cúram will automatically generate tasks based on pre-defined trigger conditions. These tasks are applied to the client profile which are assigned to processing agents to review and resolve. Below is a list of tasks that Cúram generates along with their associated trigger conditions: Situation Task Subject Task Type Client's total payment income for the June accounting month is $0; No base income for the most recent calendar year. <SIN or Curam Reference Number> - <First Name> < Last Name> - No renewal received and income was nil for the previous payment period. Review case and resolve. Renewal Reassessment Incomplete The CRA indicates the Client reported pre/post bankruptcy. Declared CPP/QPP amount is above CRA Amount for <Tax Year> CRA – Income Validation(s) Total amount exceeds the year over year threshold between the provided tax year and the prior tax year. Year over year income variance threshold exceeded for <Tax Year> CRA – Income Validation(s) The total OAS Program Benefit Amount issued to the Client for the tax year equals any line or block amount. Override Determination Once a client meets all the necessary requirements (e.g. having pending tasks resolved or overrides cleared) Cúram will automatically proceed with renewing the benefits. The system continuously checks for these conditions and benefit renewal is triggered once the conditions are satisfied. If a client does not meet the eligibility requirements for renewal, Cúram will create a task for an agent to review and resolve. Once the task is completed and the eligibility requirements are met, Cúram will automatically renew the benefit. Tasks that are not part of the eligibility rules do not stop the renewal of income-tested benefits. The ITB For Life status is automatically updated to Yes as a result of the eligibility determination process. Correspondence plays an important role in the renewal process. Cúram automatically sends letters to clients to ensure they have the information they need and that renewals are completed on time. Below is a list of correspondence generated by Cúram in July regarding the result of the renewal process: Correspondence Description GIS/ ALW / ALWS Entitlement Letter (ISP-3057) Renewal award letter for all income-tested benefits informing the client of their new entitlement amount and the payment income used to calculate the entitlement. GIS Suspension Letter (ISP-3067) Letter to inform clients that their new payment income puts them above the income threshold for GIS, thus making them not entitled for the benefit. ALW / ALWS Suspension Letter (ISP-3068) Letter to inform clients that their new payment income puts them above the income threshold for ALW or ALWS , making them not entitled for the benefit. GIS/ ALW / ALWS Non-Entitlement Letter (ISP-3056) Letter to inform clients that they are still not entitled to the income-tested benefit.

The Special Qualifying Factor (SQF) determines how much income-tested benefits a client can receive when they have not reached 10 full years of Canadian residence after age 18. Since April 1996, clients may receive 1/10th of the full benefit for each full year of residence in Canada, up to a maximum of 10 years (i.e. the full benefit means an SQF of 1.0). How the SQF works Table 1. Client value and SQF value Client Type SQF Value OAS approved without an International Social Security Agreement (ISSA) with 10 years or more of Canadian residence 1.0 OAS approved with an ISSA with less than 10 years of Canadian residence 0.1 x each full year of residence (to a maximum of 1.0) The SQF increases by 0.1 each year as the client reaches their next anniversary date of residence. For example, a client that entered Canada on March 15 would reach a year of residence the next year on March 14. Therefore, March would be the anniversary month and the SQF would increase effective April. Cúram uses the Residence Period evidence to calculate the SQF. In the absence of a complete Residence Period evidence, an SQF override equal to the client's total years of Canadian residence up to a maximum of 10 years can be entered. Residence Period evidence considerations for migrated accounts Updated The GIS New Business application only asks for the applicant's residence history in the last 2 years. If that period is the only Residence Period evidence in Cúram, the system assumes that is the total residence for the SQF calculation. Table 2. Application, information entered and how the system calculates the SQF Application Information entered System-calculated SQF GIS New Business Residence in Canada for the last 2 years 0.2 This underrepresents a client’s full residence history, leading to incorrect GIS entitlement. The client’s complete residence history should be added to Cúram to ensure an accurate client record and avoid the need for overrides when possible. The residence history can be obtained through the client file (e.g. residence calculation sheet, validated residence histories) and the system (e.g. ITRDS notes, address history). How to fix the SQF Updated Access the client file to determine if client’s residence from age 18 to the OAS effective date is present. If yes, add the client’s complete residence period history in Cúram. Refer to Residence Period—Add, View and Edit in Cúram (Action) . Residence Period—Add, View and Edit in Cúram (Action) If no, go to Step 2 . Step 2 Add an entitlement override for the SQF. Refer to Eligibility and Entitlement Override Evidence—Add, Edit, View, and Delete in Cúram (Action) . For OAS approved without an ISSA, enter an SQF of 10. For OAS approved under an ISSA, enter an SQF of 1 to 10 based on the number of full years of Canadian residence at the start date of the override. Create an OAS - Maintenance/Override Determination task in Cúram and: Add "SQF review related" as a comment in the task. Bring forward for follow-up to review at the residence anniversary date. If no match is found and the BF date: has expired, the automation will follow the Review the BF steps section below. has not expired, the automation moves on to the next work item On Hold. If the date is after the BF date, the automation will follow the Review of the BF steps section below. If a match is found, the automation will ensure the Program is Canada Pension Plan . If the new work item is Active and Unassigned , the automation will determine if the following situations apply: The Source is Reports. The work Type is either: Report Follow-Up ; Address Change/Direct Deposit ; Foreign Direct Deposit ; Payment Advice Notice – FDD ; SST Appeal ; SST Appeals Payment ; Integrity Case (0415) ; or Integrity- Investigation Request (0414) . If the Type or Source of the new work item matches one of the above, the automation actions depend on the current date: If the date is prior to the BF date of the On Hold work item, the automation takes no further action. If the date is on or after the BF date, the automation follows the Review of the BF steps section below. If the Type or Source of the new work item does not match one of the above and there are no other new Active and Unassigned work items, the automation actions depend on the current date: If the date is prior to the BF date of the On Hold work item, the automation takes no further action. If the date is on or after the BF date, the automation follows the Review of the BF steps section below. If the Type or Source of the new work item does not match one of the above and there is a new Active and Unassigned work item, the automation follows the Match the BF steps section below. Match the BF steps The automation reviews the work item history to determine if the Bin was previously updated to either BFNoResponse or BFReturned . If the Bin was updated and the current date is before the BF date, the automation takes no further action. If the Bin was not updated or if it was updated and the current date is equal to or passed the BF date, the automation depends on that the Category is Application or work Type is not one of the following: The automation will then: Correspondence Deem Person to Rep Clt (1202) Post Retirement Benefit PRB Correspondence PRB Method of Payment (1019-2) PRB Other Separation of Spouses/Common-law partners (1811) Statutory Declaration (1809/1896/1898/1899/3004/3104) Undeliverable Mail remove the BF date, change the status to Active , update the BIN to BFReturned , and add the following note in PWS : Work item matched to WI XXXXXXXXX/ Article de travail jumelé à ID XXXXXXXXX. If the On Hold work item was assigned to someone, the automation assigns the matched work item to the same person. If the Bin was not updated or if it was updated and the current date is equal to or passed the BF date, the automation depends on that the Category is not Application or work Type and is not listed in previous step, the automation will then: remove the BF date, change the status to Active, update the BIN to BFReturned , and add the following note in PWS : Work item matched to WI XXXXXXXXX/ Article de travail jumelé à ID XXXXXXXXX. For the On Hold work item, the automation changes the status to Completed and adds the following note in PWS : Work item completed by Automation and matched to WI XXXXXXXXX / Article de travail complété par automatisation et jumelé à ID XXXXXXXXX for the matched work item. Review of the BF steps The automation reviews the BF date and takes the following actions: If the BF date is after the current date (the BF date is in the future), the automation will take no further action. Awaiting Client Info Awaiting Third party Other Awaiting Program Support Waiting on Investigation Awaiting Translation If the work item was placed On Hold once, the automation will then: remove the BF date; change the status to Active ; update the Bin to BFNoResponse ; and add the following note in PWS : Reminder letter may be required as BF date has passed/ Une lettre de rappel est peut-être nécessaire vue que la date AR est passée. Review is required/ Date AR est passée. Une révision est nécessaire. A key policy change extends certain work incentives to beneficiaries regardless of whether they self-reported a return to work or not. Automatic reinstatement and fast-track reapplication process Automatic Reinstatement (AR) and the fast-track reapplication process will be extended to all beneficiaries whose benefits ceased due to a return to work or participation in educational or volunteer activities, regardless of whether they self-reported or not. AR and the fast-track reapplication process are not offered or available when a former beneficiary's benefit ceased due to non-compliance. However, if a former beneficiary's benefit ceased due to evidence of a return to work, rather than ceasing on the date of non-compliance, the AR and fast-track reapplication process may be offered. Educational or volunteer activities Beneficiaries who participate in educational or volunteer activities are currently required to report these activities to the Department after 4 months of participation at 15 hours or more per week. The policy change allows these beneficiaries an additional observation period of 4 months . This aligns with the observation month and 3-month work trial provided to those with paid employment. Substantially gainful occupation A beneficiary is no longer required to meet the monthly Substantially Gainful Occupation (SGO) benchmark before starting the 3-month work trial. The beneficiary is also no longer required to meet the SGO benchmark during each month of the work trial. This change aims to ensure only eligible individuals continue to receive CPPD benefits. RA files with up to one calendar year of earnings at or above SGO, followed by no earnings in subsequent years, may be treated as a failed attempt to return to work. An assessment of the factors is still required (e.g. earnings, work activity, predictability). In cases of non-compliance, files may be transferred to Integrity Services Branch to confirm the source of earnings, when required. Ensure all types of reassessments including prescheduled return to work are completed. Send an enquiry in the following situations: You are considering ceasing benefits on regained capacity alone. A previous beneficiary's benefit ceased due to regained capacity alone and they submit a new application for CPPD benefits or an AR request within AR timeframes. The volunteer activity participation is greater than 30 hours per week. Prior to offering an observation period.

When an applicant applies online for the OAS pension and benefits, they must provide their declaration and signature electronically before the application can be submitted through the Client Portal. If an applicant is married or in a common-law relationship and is applying online for the GIS or ALW benefit, the spouse or common-law partner's consent and declaration is not obtained when the applicant applies online. If the spouse or common-law partner's consent and declaration has not been previously obtained through their GIS or ALW benefit application process, the Consent and Declaration evidence for the spouse or common-law partner must be manually added to the Application Case after obtaining their consent.

If the applicant or their spouse or common-law partner is not one of the individuals who signed the paper application, the legal representative who signed on behalf of the individual is recorded in the evidence as Signing on Behalf . Cúram will generate an Evidence Review task to flag that review of the legal representative is required to verify they are authorized to act on the individual's behalf. The legal representative must submit documentation to support that they are authorized to act on the individual's behalf, if it has not already been provided. For more information, Third Party Requests (Scenario) If the applicant or their spouse or common-law partner signed the paper application with a mark (e.g. an “X”, thumbprint or other symbol), the individual that witnessed the mark is recorded in the evidence as Acting as Witness .

When an OAS pension, GIS, ALW benefit or ALWS benefit application is added to Cúram, the system will populate the Consent and Declaration evidence of the Application Case based on information entered from the paper application. If the signature details were not entered when the paper application was added to Cúram, the system will automatically populate the evidence to ensure the Application Case is created with a status set to Open . If signature details are missing when the paper application was added to Cúram, Cúram populates the Consent and Declaration evidence as follows: Situation The fields on the Declaration and Signature page in the New Application Form Wizard were not completed when the application was added to Cúram. Result Cúram: populates: the Signature Type field with Not Signed ; the Date Signed field with 1900-01-01 ; and creates an Evidence Issue(s) task to flag that a review and validation of the signature details is required. Situation The signature date is missing for the applicant or their spouse or common-law partner. Result Cúram: populates the Date Signed field with 1900-01-01 ; and creates an Evidence Issue(s) task to flag that a review and validation of the signature details is required. Situation The applicant or their spouse or common-law partner signed the application with a mark and there was no witness information provided on the application. Result Cúram: populates the Date Witness or Authorized Person Signed field with 1900-01-01 ; and creates an Evidence Issue(s) task to flag that a review and validation of the signature details is required.

The Foreign Bank Details evidence captures a client’s detailed foreign banking information when they request payment to a financial institution outside of Canada. The evidence is captured in Cúram by the Foreign Direct Deposit unit or by the client via the Client Portal. The evidence is stored on the Person record and does not affect the payment destination of a benefit until: the foreign direct deposit information is entered in the Standard Payment System; a Bank Accounts evidence is added with the generic direct deposit encoding; and a corresponding direct deposit link is added.

If a client is determined to be eligible and entitled for an OAS pension or benefit for a past period when no payment was previously issued, the payments will be processed as arrears rather than as underpayments. An arrears payment is a retroactive payment for a period that has not previously been assessed. For example, if an application is approved in December 2025 and the benefit's effective date is June 2025, the arrears payment will cover the period from June to December 2025.

The Delegation of Authorities ensures that arrears and underpayments are reviewed and approved by the appropriate level of authority before being issued. This maintains financial control and ensures compliance with policy.​ Cúram will confirm the Delegation of Authorities for the underpayment and/or arrears amount overnight. If the total combined arrears and underpayments created on that day are over $15,000, Cúram will create a task to manually request the required approvals. Once the approvals are completed, Cúram will include the payment in the next scheduled payment cycle. If the combined total is under $14,999.99, Cúram will issue the underpayment and/or arrears payment with the next weekly payment cycle, or the next scheduled payment if the frequency in non-standard (e.g. quarterly, semi-annual, annual). Under the Financial Administration Act , payments under $1.00 are not required to be paid to clients. Therefore, Cúram only releases these payments once they total at least $1.00. Any unpaid amounts under this threshold that remain in the system for more than 12 months will be automatically written off and will have a Payment Status of UT – over 12 months . This ensures that these payments will not be included in any future entitlement calculations because the amount has been cleared.

When Cúram reassesses a client's entitlement and determines a new amount for a past period, the system compares the revised entitlement to the previously issued amount to determine if an underpayment exists. Cúram creates an underpayment when it determines that a client was paid less for a past period than they were entitled to. Cúram reassesses entitlement to the OAS pension or benefits when new evidence or existing evidence is updated and activated. If the new entitlement amount is higher than the previously issued amount, the individual is determined to have been underpaid and Cúram automatically creates a Payment Correction – Underpaid case. This case can be found under the Cases and Applications tab. For example, if a client who receives the ALWS benefit reports a correction to their 2024 renewal income in December 2025 that results in lower total income amount, the underpayment will cover the period from July to December 2025. Underpayments can only be created in Cúram via system-generated reassessments. You must manually calculate and issue the entitlement outside of Cúram in all situations where the system is unable to reassess the entitlement.

Review all systems and documents related to the application. Refer to CPPD Benefits Application (Scenario) . CPPD Benefits Application (Scenario) Review the earnings investigation worksheet: Date of Application (DOA); Latest Possible Date of Onset (LPDOO) without the credit split; LPDOO with the credit splitting applied, if applicable; Earliest Possible Date of Onset (EPDOO); and Date of attribution, if applicable. Determine which LPDOO(s) to adjudicate: If the date of attribution is 11 months or more before the DOA , adjudicate the LPDOO with credit split and implement the decision. The applicant’s own LPDOO is not adjudicated. Refer to Medical Adjudication (Scenario) . Medical Adjudication (Scenario) If the date of attribution is less than 11 months before the DOA , adjudicate using the LPDOO without credit split first. Refer to Late Applicant Provision (Scenario) . If the severe and prolonged criteria was met before the LPDOO without credit split, implement the decision. Refer to Medical Adjudication (Scenario) . Medical Adjudication (Scenario) If the severe and prolonged criteria was not met before the LPDOO without credit split, assess if it was met by the LPDOO with credit split. If the severe and prolonged criteria was met by the LPDOO with credit split, implement the decision and include an explanation in the rationale for each LPDOO. Refer to Medical Adjudication (Scenario) . Medical Adjudication (Scenario) If the severe and prolonged criteria was not met by either LPDOO, implement the decision and include an explanation in the rationale why the severe and prolonged criteria was not met by either LPDOO. Send the letter to the applicant and use the LPDOO calculated from the credit split. Refer to Medical Adjudication (Scenario) . Medical Adjudication (Scenario) Late Applicant Provision (Scenario)

Credit splitting is a provision that allows Unadjusted Pensionable Earnings (UPE) or pension credits, earned by both spouses during the marriage or common-law union, to be divided equally between the 2 persons. The division can only take place after a divorce, legal annulment or separation from a legal marriage or common-law union. The effective date of the credit split approval is the last day of the month in which the request or application is received. Any benefits requiring a credit split cannot be paid in the month the credit split was approved or any month before. Benefits may begin on the date of attribution (i.e. the month following the month in which the credit split is approved). For example, if a request or application is received in March, the earnings resulting from the credit split approval will be accredited to the record of earnings effective April. For CPPD, if the applicant had a qualifying period without credit splitting and the date of attribution is within the 11 months before the date of application, it is more beneficial to the applicant if they are found disabled by the Latest Possible Date of Onset (LPDOO) from their own credits than it would be if they were found disabled by the LPDOO with the credit split. When medically adjudicating a CPPD benefit application and a credit split is applied, it is important that you consider both LPDOOs, if applicable, in determining when severe and prolonged criteria was met. This ensures that the applicant receives all the benefits to which they are entitled. Examples when the date of attribution is less than 11 months before the date of application An applicant applies for CPPD benefits in August 2026 with an Earliest Possible Date of Onset (EPDOO) in May 2025. The applicant previously applied for a credit split in September 2025 and has a date of attribution of October 2025. With the credit split, the LPDOO is December 2027. Without the credit split, the LPDOO is December 2023. If this applicant met the severe and prolonged criteria by December 2023, they will be entitled to a benefit for the full retroactive period. If they became disabled after December 2023 but before December 2027, the effective date for payment of their benefit would be the same date as the later of: the date of attribution; 4 months after the Date of Onset (DOO); or for subsequent applications, the month after the DOO if the DOO is within 5 years after the cessation date of a previous CPPD benefit. Example when the date of attribution is 11 months or more before the date of application An applicant applies for CPPD benefits in July 2025 with an EPDOO in April 2024. The applicant previously applied for a credit split in August 2023 and has a date of attribution of September 2023. With a credit split, the LPDOO is December 2022. As this date is before the maximum retroactivity the LPDOO without credit split should not be considered as the date of attribution is before any possible effective date. If the applicant is found disabled, the effective date would be August 2024, the full retroactive period. Automated mail out of the ISP-1402-A form and the ISP-1365 letter To comply with the new +18 children's benefits policy framework, the Department must provide clients with appropriate notification when their benefits are ending, including reminders and an ISP-1365 cancellation letter, with reconsideration rights. Additional processes have been added to the existing automation to provide clients with reminders and benefit cease letters. Children turning 18 years old An automated ISP-1402-A form (formerly the ISP-1401-A form) is sent to the custodial parent 3 months before the child turns 18 years old (i.e. the existing process). An automated ISP-1365 cancellation letter with reconsideration rights and an ISP-1402-A form is sent to the custodial parent the month the benefit is going to end. +18 Children An automated ISP-1402-A form (formerly the ISP-1401-A form) is sent to the +18 child one month before the current school period ends, inviting them to renew or submit a new ISP-1402-A form (i.e. the existing process). An automated ISP-1365 cancellation letter with reconsideration rights is sent to the +18 child if the child does not submit an ISP-1402-A form within 60 days following the first letter. School period overlapping the child's 25th birthday An automated ISP-1365 cancellation letter with reconsideration rights is sent to the child the month of their 25th birthday. This letter is similar to the Notice of Entitlement - CPP Disability benefit converted to a Retirement pension (ISP-1021) letter which is system generated when a disabled contributor turns 65. Following this release, enhancements and improvements have been made to the following: Digital tax slips A new evidence type was created in Cúram that feeds client’s digital tax slip preferences from Tax Information Slips Online (TISO). This new feature is used solely to correctly flag clients who have opted for the digital-only delivery of their 2025 tax slips. Users do not need to action this evidence manually. Beginning in June 2026, clients will also be able to select their digital tax slip preference through the portal in addition to TISO. This evidence will not be used operationally outside of the annual tax slip file until the Universal Access portal integration is live in June 2026. Tax slip functionality Call centre users can now delete a client's tax slip that has a Draft or Submitted status. Previously, these users could not delete tax slips with these statuses. This feature removes the ability for call centre users to intercept a tax slip, as it is no longer required. Intercepting tax slips should only be accessible by Central Print and the Innovation, Information and Technology Branch. Cúram search tools Workload managers can now: search Cúram tasks by a client’s date of birth; and identify tasks in key areas such as Intake , OAS Case , and Evidence Corrections based on a potential entitlement date that may prevent clients from being paid on time. OAS benefit cancellation Users can now set a non-reversible deduction to status as part of the OAS benefit cancellation process. This feature enables the system to accurately reflect the reversal of Federal Voluntary Tax Withholds (FVTW) and recovery tax deductions that were previously flagged as non-reversible, specifically during benefit cancellations that span 2 calendar years. This improvement will help users who are processing a benefit cancellation in a subsequent calendar year. Users can now update the system to show that the FVTW and the recovery tax deductions on impacted payments have been refunded. A person receiving an OAS pension or benefits may offer to pay back another client's debt (i.e. overpayment, penalty or interest) on their behalf. This does not result in the debt being reallocated to the volunteer offering to pay it, as they are not deemed responsible for the debt. This person can: choose a dollar amount (fixed) or percentage (variable) of the payment; change the amount of the payments; or stop payments at any time. These deductions will not be reflected on the volunteer's tax slip. The debtor will receive credit as if they had made the payments themselves. You must ensure the non-debtor volunteer is receiving an OAS pension or benefits before setting up a non-debtor volunteer deduction. The deduction will display as Overpayment Non-Debtor , Penalty Non-Debtor or Interest Non-Debtor deductions in the non-debtor volunteer's product delivery case.

The GIS Automatic Enrolment Program Compliance Review (PCR) is a national integrity review initiated by the Integrity Services Branch (ISB), focusing on the automatic enrolment of GIS clients. ISB routinely performs PCRs on departmental programs and services to identify potential integrity risks, assess the effectiveness of existing controls, and determine the extent of incorrect payments resulting from compliance errors, abuse, or fraud.
