Effective Date: April 29, 2026 As of April 29, 2026, existing OAS clients can update their personal information online. This includes changing their bank accounts and updating their mailing and residential addresses (i.e. Canadian or foreign addresses and payment information). Clients can make these updates through the Profile tab in the OAS Client Portal. When clients initiate a change to their payment destination or addresses, the system will prompt those who are not already authorized for alerts and notifications to register for a one-time security verification. Additional security measures are in place to identify bank accounts known to Service Canada as potentially fraudulent. These accounts will be sent to Cúram for account review and possible investigation. Clients can log into their My Service Canada Account (MSCA) to make these updates in their OAS dashboard. While the View and Update Personal Information (VUPI) self-service functionality under the CPP tab in MSCA is not yet active, Cúram will continue to share address changes and updated Canadian bank account information with ITRDS . This implementation bulletin provides a detailed overview of the enhancements related to the activation of the online self-service life event changes. As part of these enhancements, clients can change: their Canadian or foreign residential and mailing addresses. their Canadian or foreign banking information.
There is no reference material. (KA-01423 Snippet 14.0 content. Do not modify or delete.)

The following sections outline the improvements that clients and Cúram users will experience with the activation of the online self-service life event changes in the OAS Client Portal. Each section details what has changed, how it functions within the system, and what users can expect. Additionally, KMT articles will be updated to support users with their everyday activities related to changes in addresses and banking information. Client facing components If clients are not registered for alerts and notifications, they will initially see an Unable to Continue message in their OAS Dashboard when attempting to update their banking information or addresses. This message prompts the client to call Service Canada to subscribe to alerts and report life events. This one-time security measure added to the Client Portal only, ensures that only clients can make updates to their personal information. Once clients subscribe to alerts, they can report life events through their online account. OAS clients who update their personal information via the Client Portal can also apply those changes to their CPP file. Updating the Manage Email Addresses tab in the OAS Profile tab does not automatically subscribe clients to alerts. Clients must call Service Canada to authenticate their account and register for notifications and alerts. For more information, refer to Adding or Updating Cúram OAS Portal Alerts Internal link . Adding or Updating Cúram OAS Portal Alerts Clients will receive alerts at their registered phone number or email address. A notification will also appear on their dashboard so clients can be certain the alert is from Service Canada. When clients update their addresses or bank account information online, the system captures the data as evidence in Cúram and records the reason for the change as Reported by client via Life Event . Address changes Once clients are registered for alerts and notifications, they can update their address information, including residential and mailing addresses, under the Manage My Address Information tab in the OAS Dashboard. They can change their address from one Canadian address to another, switch from a Canadian address to a foreign address, or vice versa. Cúram will generate tasks if the Office of Control or residential periods need to be reviewed manually. Residential address updates Clients can change their residential addresses to Canadian or foreign addresses through the OAS Client Portal. When clients have a Canadian address on file and add a new foreign address, they must indicate if they intend to return to Canada and, if so, when. They will also need to provide a reason for their absence (e.g. vacation or permanent move). Cúram will generate tasks for mandatory review if the intended absence is more than 6 months. All updates to residential addresses are automatically shared from Cúram to ITRDS and recorded as an update to the Home Address field in ITRDS . Mailing address updates When clients indicate that their update is for their mailing address, they will be prompted to confirm if they are receiving CPP pensions or benefits and if they want to share this update with CPP. Updates to the client's mailing address are automatically shared from Cúram to ITRDS and recorded as an update to the Correspondence Address field in ITRDS . All correspondence, including paper cheques, will be issued to the updated mailing address unless evidence tasks prevent the evidence from being finalized. Residential and mailing addresses updates Clients can update both their residential and mailing addresses at the same time. The system will ask the client to confirm if their mailing address is different from their residential address. If the client selects that their residential and mailing address are the same, the system prompts them to confirm if they are in receipt of CPP pensions or benefits and if the updated mailing address must be applied to their CPP mailing address. If yes, Cúram shares the update with ITRDS and it is recorded as an update to the Correspondence Address field in ITRDS . If the client selects that their residential address is different from their mailing address, the system prompts them to enter their mailing address. The system then asks if the updated mailing address should also be shared with CPP. If yes, Cúram shares the update with ITRDS . Effective date of residential address updates Clients are prompted to confirm the start date of their residential address change. They can select the current date or a future date up to one year from the current date. If the residential period requires a review, Cúram will generate tasks for the manual review. Clients cannot request address changes retroactively. Changes to payment destination Once clients register for alerts and notifications, they will be able to update their Canadian or foreign banking information under the Manage My Payment Destination tab in their OAS dashboard. Clients will receive alerts at their registered phone number or email address. A notification will also appear on their dashboard so clients can be certain the alert is from Service Canada. Client has a Canadian address on their OAS dashboard When clients have a Canadian address on their account, the system prompts them to update their Canadian bank account information only. The system will also ask if they are in receipt of CPP pensions or benefits and if the new banking information should apply to both CPP and OAS. If yes, Cúram will share the new banking information with ITRDS . Client has a foreign address on their OAS dashboard When clients have a foreign address on their account, they can choose to update either a Canadian or a foreign bank account. Only updates to a new Canadian bank account will prompt the system to ask if their new banking information should also apply to CPP. At this time, clients cannot indicate that their new foreign direct deposit must be shared with CPP. Clients will see a note informing them that they must contact Service Canada to update their CPP payment destination. For OAS (manual review needed) The system will generate tasks for manual review or further action in the following situations: If a new added bank account in the Client Portal appears on the list of fraudulent bank accounts. If a client updates a joint bank account and the joint account holder names do not match. If a client updates their Canadian residential address to a foreign residential address and the change may affect benefit eligibility or entitlement. If a client updates their banking information to a foreign bank account and a review by the Foreign Direct Deposit unit in the Atlantic region is required. For CPP Clients cannot yet update their address or banking information for CPP in MSCA through the VUPI service. This functionality is not currently being restored. Updates to clients' residential and mailing addresses, as well as Canadian banking information, are shared in real time from Cúram to ITRDS . Under/Overpayment This column indicates the result of the recalculation: underpayments are displayed as positive amounts; overpayments are displayed as negative amounts; and no changes in entitlement are displayed as $ 0.00. Title required in this format Field Description Non-Joint Code This value indicates the non-joint code on the client's account in OAS Online. Below the general information, there is a list of accounting months. The data is displayed in a table with columns replicating the OAS Online CAL screen fields. Aside from the Accounting Date column, the others display two values which are separated by a vertical line: On the left is the original system value. On the right is the recalculated value if this information was updated for this accounting month. When no value exists, Cúram will display the data as two hyphens ( - - ). The list contains the following: Table 1. Title required in this format Column Description Accounting Date This value indicates a given period. The value will display as: a date in the YYYYMM format (e.g. 202501); T4/NR ; or a total value. The NR indicator next to the accounting date shows that the client was a non-resident for that given period. Payment Income This value indicates the income used for the determination of the entitlement. Modifying the Payment Income column in the CAL screen could have triggered a reassessment of benefits. Account Status This value is a numeric indicator providing the following information on the status of the client's account in the system: 1 – The account is active, in pay 2 – The account is suspended (e.g. the client's whereabouts are unknown) 3 – The account is cancelled (e.g. the client has died) 4 – The account is pending (i.e. the benefits are approved, but not effective yet) 5 – The account is incomplete (i.e. the account was created in the system, but is not approved yet) 6 – The account is active, last pay 7 – The account is terminated ( ALW or ALWS not converted in time) Modifying the Account Status column in the CAL screen could have triggered a reassessment of benefits. Account Type This value provides information on the benefits and how they are issued. The Account Type is a numeric value made up of two subfields. The first digit indicates the type of benefit paid and the second digit indicates the reason for control being exercised on the account. The first digit of the Account Type means the following: 1 – Domestic OAS 2 – Domestic GIS/ ALW / ALWS (maximum entitlement) 3 – Domestic GIS/ ALW / ALWS (partial entitlement) 4 – Foreign OAS 5 – Foreign GIS/ ALW / ALWS (maximum entitlement) 6 – Foreign GIS/ ALW / ALWS (partial entitlement) The second digit of the Account Type means the following: 0 – Regular 1 – Trustee 2 – C/O Bank 3 – Foreign Unlimited 4 – Foreign Limited 5 – P.O. Box 6 – Bulk Payment 7 – Direct Deposit (Regular) 8 – Direct Deposit (Trustee) For example, an Account Type indicator of 37 means that the client is paid a partial GIS, ALW benefit or ALWS benefit by direct deposit. Modifying the Account Type field in the CAL screen could have triggered a reassessment of benefits. Account Indicator This value provides the following information on the client's link to another account: Blank ( - - ) – This is a stand-alone account (e.g. no spouse or common-law partner) Control ( C ) – This client's account is linked to another one and they came in to pay first Subordinate ( S ) – This client's account is linked to another one, but they were the second to come in to pay The Account Indicator field was for informational purposes only and did not trigger a reassessment of benefits. Marital Status This value indicates the client's marital status for GIS, ALW benefit and ALWS benefit calculation purposes. The values mean the following: 1 – Single pensioner 2 – Couple, married or common law, both are pensioners 3 – Couple, married or common law, one is a pensioner and the other receives no benefits 4 – Couple, married or common law, both are pensioners living apart for reasons beyond their control 5 – Couple, married or common law, one is a pensioner and the other receives an ALW benefit 6 – Couple, married or common law, one is a pensioner and the other is receiving an ALW benefit, but they are living apart for reasons beyond their control 7 – Client's ALWS benefit is suspended 8 – Client receives an ALWS benefit 9 – Client's ALW benefit converted to an ALWS benefit (extended ALW benefit) Modifying the Marital Status field in the CAL screen could have triggered a reassessment of benefits. Eligible Years This value indicates the number of 40ths to which the client is eligible. Modifying the Eligible Years field in the CAL screen could have triggered a reassessment of benefits.

This procedure provides you with the steps to view the migrated historical monthly data from the OAS Online Re-calculation Input (CAL) screen in Cúram.

In Cúram, go to the client's Person Record. Refer to Search for a Person in Cúram (Action) . Search for a Person in Cúram (Action) Click the Cases and Applications tab. Click Cases on the page group navigation bar on the left. Click the hyperlink in front of the Old Age Security Program Benefits case in the Reference column. The case opens in a new tab. Click on the Historical Recalculation tab. Navigate to the accounting month you want to view. Click the (>) toggle icon to expand the row and view the detailed information.

Prior to the migration to Cúram, the CAL screen in OAS Online was used to display monthly information for the client's benefits. Changes to the eligibility and entitlement calculations could be performed in that screen to determine underpayments or overpayments. The data from the CAL screen has been added to Cúram to help with the determination of eligibility and entitlement when reviewing migrated accounts. This data cannot be edited and is available in read-only mode for awareness and processing purposes. Cúram will display what was on the screen at the time of migration and will go back as far as January 1998, when applicable. Data migrated from the OAS Online CAL screen is displayed in Cúram using the same rules as the legacy system. As OAS Online used numerical and alphabetical values to provide information on the client's account, these same values will be transferred to Cúram. The Historical Recalculation tab contains the historical CAL screen data. It can be accessed on the Old Age Security Program Benefits case (Product Delivery Case) and will only be displayed when migrated data is available, otherwise the tab will not appear. The Historical Recalculation tab contains one page, also titled Historical Recalculation. The page contains: a header with general data that is not associated to a specific month (e.g. non-joint code, record type); and a toggleable list of the accounting months for every month that was available in OAS Online. Once expanded, the section displays detailed information on the selected accounting month, including entitlement amounts for each benefit (i.e. OAS pension, GIS, ALW benefit and ALWS benefit).

Effective Date: March 26, 2026 On March 26, 2026, OAS Release 3.5 went live. This implementation bulletin provides a detailed overview of the improvements included in OAS Release 3.5 and highlights: the changes made to the system; the functionality of the changes; and what officers can expect when processing cases after the implementation. The design improvements will: reduce the manual workload; improve processing accuracy; and streamline end-to-end operations across intake, financials, workload management, and user experience.

Design improvements have been divided into the following categories: Automatic enrollment improvements Automatic enrollment improvements Automation improvements Automation improvements Financial improvements Financial improvements User experience improvements User experience improvements Client experience improvements Client experience improvements Workload improvements Workload improvements Return to Automatic enrollment improvements Person-matching logic improvements The automatic enrolment matching logic has been simplified to consider a match when a verified SIN and date of birth (year and month only) match that of an existing registered or prospect person. In the case of the prospect person, the system will convert the prospect to registered. The same logic will be applied to the GIS automatic enrolment spousal matching. This will significantly reduce the exclusions from automatic enrolment. Exclusion reasons have been updated for better clarity. Daily authorization for automatic enrolment Application Cases (OAS pension and GIS) The automatic enrolment authorization job now runs daily from the 1st to the 15th day of the month and only authorizes the Application Cases on the day the client turns 65. This will significantly reduce the number of manual interventions necessary when a client opts out of automatic enrolment before their birthday after the 1st day of the month. Return to Automation improvements Management of ALW benefit and ALWS benefit conversions Conversions no longer require manual investigation in most cases. Benefits of clients who meet the 40‑year residency requirement will convert more quickly, improving client service and legislative compliance. Only exceptional cases will generate follow‑up tasks, while the majority of cases will be handled seamlessly through automated processing. Automated death notification process Officers will receive exception workloads automatically. Manual reports or ad hoc tasks will no longer be created. This automation ensures: faster, consistent handling of Date of Death (DOD) cases; clear auditability; the proactive mailing of correct correspondence; improved client service for surviving spouses; and a reduced risk of missed actions when DOD changes are received from ITRDS. Return to Financial improvements Prevention of the payment of aged and low-value amounts Officers no longer need to track or cancel small and aged underpayments. The system will automatically accrue these amounts and include them in the next payment once they exceed the payment threshold. If the threshold is not reached, the amounts will continue to accrue for up to 12 months, after which they will be paid to the client. Clients will not see outdated, low‑value amounts merged into future payments, which will reduce incorrect payments and improve accuracy. This automation: ensures compliance with legislative requirements; improves client service; and improves financial integrity across programs. Inbound garnishment from the Department of Justice This improvement eliminates the creation of duplicate garnishment deductions on a client's file, reducing the number of financial inaccuracies that require manual intervention by officers. This fix will ensure that modified Department of Justice instructions replace existing deductions, instead of duplicating them. Liability offsets coded as a reversible deduction Officers no longer need to fix incorrect offsets or reconcile unwanted non‑reversible deductions after cancellations. Financial records, Year to Date amounts, and tax slip data will remain accurate because the system will correctly categorize and reprocess cancelled offsets. This improvement: reduces financial reporting errors; prevents incorrect recoveries from clients; and supports correct handling during reissue or reconcile‑and‑reissue workflows. In support of this release, the Integrated Expertise Network has developed a Liability Offset job aid that explains how: to apply a liability offset; to understand system generated activation tasks; offsets are reversed when a payment is cancelled in the Standard Payment System (SPS); and to manage cancelled payments with a liability offset previously applied. For additional information, refer to the Job Aids SharePoint link section of the ESDC’s Cúram SharePoint site. Historic Recalculation Data from the Recalculation (CAL) screen Officers can now: reference historical entitlement information to assist them in resolving client enquiries using complete legacy account data; access monthly details which will reduce errors, prevent payment delays, and support accurate manual recalculations; and immediately access the information they need, without triggering system rules or unintended changes. Return to Client experience improvements Client portal style guidelines improvements Clients will experience a more consistent, accessible, and user‑friendly interface throughout the online application process. Pages will look and behave predictably across the portal, reducing confusion and helping clients complete applications more easily. These improvements strengthen usability, accessibility, and overall trust in the digital experience. Client portal application improvements Clients will experience a smoother, more intuitive application flow with related questions grouped together and presented in a logical order. The process is easier to understand, reducing confusion and improving completion success. Behind the scenes, the system will use newly collected data to support accurate application intake and eligibility and entitlement decisions. Return to Workload improvements General task changes Tasks are now easier to read, locate, and manage. The tasks have clearer information, new tasks fields and enhanced search capabilities which improves allocation, monitoring, and overall workflow efficiency. There are 11 new on hold reasons and 12 new deferred reasons available for users to select for tasks. Each new task has its own reason and a Bring Forward date assigned to it. When users: change a task’s status to On-Hold , they must also select the appropriate work queue that the on hold task must be assigned to. select a new deferred task, they must keep it in their own work queue for further action. The On Hold and Deferred Reason Code Descriptions SharePoint link list is available on the ESDC's Cúram SharePoint site. These improvements optimize workload management and streamline daily operations across all programs. Capture communications for deceased records Officers can now accurately capture communications from clients who incorrectly appear deceased in the system and who present themselves in person to correct the record. The validation error will no longer prevent communication entry, improving accuracy and client service. This ensures smoother correction of erroneous death notifications and supports proper case management. Evidence corrections A change will be introduced that impacts how Evidence Correction tasks on Application Cases that have an Awaiting Resolution status are processed when the evidence issue relates to: residence period; legal status; marital status; and the first date of entry into Canada. Application Case Evidence accuracy In many cases, Cúram will automatically approve applications based solely on the information gathered from the application. It is essential that application information is entered correctly. Typos or inaccurate evidence may lead to incorrect payments or determinations. When manually entering application details into Cúram, do not enter the information if you are uncertain of its accuracy (e.g. the client includes a handwritten statement to explain their residence period). Reassign the application task to another Virtual Skill Group level with the appropriate level of authority and training to validate the information. OAS and Foreign Benefits Initial Intake (Action) Once data captured, online applications will be analyzed by the system to determine if the evidence requires validation. Manual intervention is only required when the system triggers a task. When you manually capture data from paper applications or manually review an application, apply the same methodology used by the system (i.e. evidence should be accepted at face value). If the system triggers a task to review the evidence, follow regular procedures to validate the issue. Impacted procedures will be updated accordingly soon. The system generates the required evidence verification tasks when the Application Case is created. If the system has automated the benefit authorization, tasks related to evidence verification, issues or exceptions were previously closed and the review of the benefit application is considered complete. No further review of potential discrepancies is required at this stage. This approach to automating benefit applications is based on sound risk management principles and on the reliance on information provided by clients. The examples below show situations where no further review is necessary, because the system identifies and flags any required verification that affects eligibility: The client indicates they are single, and there is no conflicting information within the application. The data is captured as single, even if previously received marital status evidence on file suggests otherwise. The marital status does not need to be investigated unless a task is triggered to verify this information. The client indicates they are single, but information on the application indicates they may be married or common law. This must be investigated before the information is entered in the system as evidence when actioning the GIS Application Case. All evidence verification tasks must be reviewed before manually authorizing benefits. The client indicates they were a resident of Canada for 12 months in 2005, followed by a 3-year gap and re-entry to Canada without further absences. The initial residence period does not need to be investigated unless a task is triggered to verify this information. Tasks Various tasks related to evidence anomalies will prevent the account from being selected for automated authorization. It is essential that all tasks remain open until the evidence in question is verified and updated in Cúram. Inaccurate evidence may result in incorrect payments or decisions that may be communicated to the client. OAS Maintenance tasks are created whenever benefits are authorized, whether automatically or manually. Even when an application is approved by the system, the task for validating the payments will be created when required.

CRA interface reassessment enhancements This feature improves how Cúram receives and processes CRA reassessment data. What's changed CRA reassessment records are no longer processed immediately when they arrive. Instead, Cúram first saves each record and then processes it step-by-step in a controlled sequence. This approach ensures that no records are lost and every reassessment can be fully tracked. Why it matters As a result of this feature, Cúram can now clearly show: what CRA sent; what Cúram received; how processing progressed; where processing stopped, if applicable; and why a reassessment could not be completed. This eliminates reconciliation gaps and prevents undetected errors. Benefits This feature offers the following benefits: Reliability, auditability, and transparency is improved. Support teams are given clear visibility into each CRA reassessment. Reporting is more precise, monitoring is better, and issue resolutions is faster. Errors are reduced by ensuring the system reviews and validates each step before moving forward. Financial integrity is strengthened and confidence in system processing is increased. Overall, by saving and processing CRA reassessment data in clear, traceable steps, the system improves reliability, strengthens oversight, and enables faster problem resolution for high-volume reassessments.

Sharing application information from the Person Record to the Application Case This enhancement makes it easier to share application information from the Person Record to the Application Case. What's changed Evidence that was only previously on the Person Record is now shared to the Application Case. If there is a problem with the evidence, the system pauses the Application Case and creates a task for review. The evidence remains editable to allow for correction. When a Person Record is first created, only basic details are mandatory. These include the client's: name; SIN; address; and date of birth. All other evidence collected from the application stays linked to the Person Record and is shared to the Application Case. Why it matters As a result of this feature, evidence that was previously only on the Person Record is now: shared automatically from the Person Record to the Application Case; available immediately on the Application Case; and applied by Cúram to where it is needed, without manual steps. Benefits This enhancement offers the following benefits: The processes are simpler and more reliable. Errors are reduced and intakes are faster. Data consistency is improved. The risk of duplicate or incorrect client information is reduced. Important details are not overwritten. Visibility for staff is improved. All submitted evidence displays on the Application Case right away. Evidence is applied automatically once the Application Case is approved, with no manual intervention needed. Clear tracking and accountability is provided. Every step of how information is added and activated is recorded. It is easy to see when and how data is entered into Cúram. Overall, this approach is more reliable, reduces manual work, and gives staff clearer and more consistent information.

Recalculating gross to net amounts using current deductions and the current maximum deduction amounts This feature improves how the system handles deductions when it reissues a cancelled payment. What's changed When Cúram reissues a cancelled payment, it uses a new gross to net amount calculation. The existing controls still prevent double deductions for prior-year payments and ensures the system does not apply deductions when there is no outstanding balance. Why it matters As a result of this feature, Cúram applies the most current deductions and the current maximum deduction amount in effect at the time of reissue. It no longer reuses outdated deductions from the original payment. Benefits This feature offers the following benefits: Over collection or under-collection of departmental receivables is prevented. Processing staff no longer needs to manually deduct adjustments. Errors, rework, and audit risks are reduced. Clients receive the correct payment without delay. Payments are reissued faster and debt recovery is more reliable by aligning deductions with current account conditions. Overall, reissued payments now automatically apply current deduction rules, improving accuracy, efficiency, and financial integrity while reducing manual effort.

Reducing the number of GIS auto-enrolment accounts requiring manual intervention This enhancement builds on the application authorization automation introduced in March 2026 and reduces unnecessary GIS auto enrolment failures by improving how the system handles spousal address information in the ITRDS —Cúram interface. For more information, OAS Pension and GIS Application Automation What's changed Previously, GIS auto-enrolment could not proceed if the client's mailing or residential address was missing or incomplete. However, with the new enhancements, Cúram now checks for a valid address from the client's spouse or common-law partner. If an address is available, Cúram will allow the GIS auto-enrolment to proceed, reducing the need for manual invention. Why it matters As a result of this enhancement, Cúram can now look for a valid address from the client's spouse or common-law partner, when applicable. The system will only raise an error if no valid address exists in any eligible source. The following steps are an example of the order to follow when selecting an address for a GIS automatic enrolment client: Use the client's mailing address if it is complete. If the mailing address is not complete, use the client's residential address if it is complete and not a PO box. If neither of the client's addresses work, use the residential address of the older spouse or common-law partner who was previously approved for the GIS (a PO box is allowed). If their address is not available, use the mailing address of the older spouse or common-law partner who was approved for the GIS. If none of these addresses are usable, send the case for manual review. Impact on processing These enhancements change how processing works by limiting manual intervention tasks to cases where address data is invalid or not available. As a result, most auto-enrolment cases can now proceed without interruption, even when correctable address gaps exist. Benefits This enhancement offers the following benefits: Up to 30% more GIS auto-enrolment cases can stay in automated processing. Unnecessary workloads are reduced as processing officers work on cases only when needed. The auto-enrolment completion rates increase. The speed to which eligible clients receive benefits increases. Privacy, data integrity, and program compliance are maintained at all times in the system. Overall, Cúram now corrects common address gaps automatically. This allows GIS auto enrolment to complete cases in most situations while reserving manual review for cases where the address is invalid or missing data.

Interactive Voice Response interface alignment for OAS information This feature improves the client experience when phoning into the Interactive Voice Response system to obtain information about OAS benefits. Clients who call the Interactive Voice Response system can use menu options to: verify their identity (i.e. authenticate); check their payment status; and check the status of their benefit applications. Why it matters As a result of this feature, clients can now: access OAS benefit information easily through self-serve options; be redirected to the call centre only if the Interactive Voice Response system cannot provide the information; and spend less time waiting to speak with an officer. Impact on call centre officers This feature reduces the number of calls officers receive about OAS payment amounts, allowing them to focus more on complex client issues. Benefits for call centre officers This feature reduces the overall call volumes for payment amount enquiries, which helps improve client satisfaction. Benefits for clients This feature makes it easier for clients to access their payment information through self-serve options, while reducing wait times and helping resolve enquiries quickly.

Increase in task maximum limit for bulk forwards and reserves This feature improves bulk task management in Cúram, making it easier for team leads and workload managers to manage work. Team leaders and workload managers can now move up to 300 tasks at once in real time. For requests over 300 tasks, they must submit a ticket to the National Service Desk to schedule a batch job. Tasks included in a batch job cannot be manually forwarded while they are waiting for processing. Why this was needed While Cúram's default bulk features met initial go live needs, operational feedback identified limitations with bulk forwards and bulk reserves. Why it matters Bulk actions are now more flexible and easier to use. The maximum number of tasks that can be forwarded or reserved immediately has increased from 100 to 300. Cúram also shows how many tasks are selected, making it easier for users to confirm their actions. Benefits This feature helps team leaders and workload managers: respond to changing priorities; address emerging backlogs; support planned operational shifts; and move work in bulk between officers and work queues in real time. This feature also improves the system by making workload management more responsive and flexible across all channels. Overall, these improvements give team leaders and workload managers better control over workload distribution, allowing for faster adjustments, smoother operations, and more efficient use of time. Update to the Office of Control determination rules This feature improves the Office of Control (OCON) determination rules to ensure cases are routed correctly and only when appropriate. What's changed Curam now completes additional checks before routing a case to International Operations (IO). It first confirms that the applicant's residence history is complete from age 18 to the application date. If the residence history is incomplete, Cúram does not assess whether the applicant meets the 10-year Canadian residence requirement (20 years for foreign applicants). Instead, it determines the OCON based on the applicant's current residential address or the last province of residence if they are applying from outside of Canada. Why it matters This change prevents cases from being sent to IO simply because Canadian residence periods are missing or not reported, ensuring that only cases that clearly require an International Agreement (IA) assessment are forwarded to IO. Benefits This feature: reduces the number of domestic cases sent to IO when an IA has not been established; increases the speed of domestic processing; prevents cases from sitting idle in IO queues waiting to be returned; improves workload management; creates a more accurate IO queue; improves visibility into performance; and focuses specialized IO resources on applications that require an IA to qualify for a benefit.
